# AI Adoption and Literacy Plan

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-adoption-and-literacy --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-adoption-and-literacy`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`curriculum.csv`, `training-load.csv`, `adoption-plan.md`, `adoption.json`). `--verify` recomputes every hour and seat total from `adoption.json`.

## Starting points
- **New** — no AI training yet: bring the population by role (and waves, targets if set); the skill builds the curriculum from its own default catalogue and sizes the training load.
- **Existing** — bring the population and the training catalogue you already run; the skill maps every role to your modules, sizes the load and names the roles and oversight duties your catalogue does not cover.

## When to use
- ADLC strategy stage: before an AI system (or AI tools in general) reaches staff, to plan who learns what, when, and how adoption is measured.
- "Which roles need which AI training, and how many hours is that per wave?"
- Evidence of EU AI Act Article 4 literacy measures (a record of measures, not a certificate).
- NOT for: the AI strategy or CoE operating model (`ai-strategy-coe`), the staged release of the system itself (`ai-release-plan`), legal determinations of provider/deployer status or high-risk scope (route to counsel).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `population` — role, headcount, exposure, proficiency, business_unit | yes | HR / Change lead (copy `assets/population-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `catalog` — module_id, title, hours, audience, level, format, mandatory_for | no | L&D lead | default `assets/literacy-modules.csv` (the skill's own design, labelled so in the plan) |
| `waves` — wave, business_unit, start_date | no | Change lead (copy `assets/waves-template.csv`) | wave and start date are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]` |
| `targets` — key,value,source | no | Change lead / product owner (copy `assets/adoption-targets.csv`) | each KPI target is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]` |
| `strict` — true/false | no | Change lead | false: gaps reported, exit 0 |

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Fill the population: one row per role and business unit; set exposure and proficiency per `references/method.md`.
3. Review the default catalog with the L&D lead or supply your own; keep a `mandatory_for` overseer module.
4. Run the agent. A role needs a module when the module audience includes its exposure and the module level exceeds its proficiency; overseer-mandatory modules are always required.
5. Read the gaps: operator/overseer roles with no module and business units without a wave.
6. With `strict=true`, any operator/overseer role without a module fails the run (exit 1) — use it before go-live.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `curriculum.csv` — `business_unit, role, module_id, title, hours, reason`.
- `training-load.csv` — `wave, business_unit, start_date, people, learners, hours`.
- `adoption-plan.md` — **Summary**, **Who needs what**, **Curriculum** (seats, seat-hours), **Rollout**, **Adoption KPIs**, **Art. 4 note**, **Method**.
- `adoption.json` — roles, modules, seats, totals, load, KPIs, gaps, gate.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every overseer has the human-oversight module; every operator/overseer has at least one module
- [ ] Hours and seats pass `--verify`
- [ ] KPI targets came from `targets` or are TBD for the Change lead; none invented
- [ ] The plan says when the default catalog (skill design) was used
- [ ] Art. 4 note uses the amended wording and says it is not a legal determination

## References
- `references/method.md` — exposure levels, proficiency scale, rules, gate, limits
- `references/sources.md` — EU AI Act Art. 4 (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), Art. 3(56), Art. 26(2), Art. 113, with URLs and date checked
- `assets/literacy-modules.csv` — default curriculum (skill design)
- `assets/population-template.csv`, `assets/waves-template.csv`, `assets/adoption-targets.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/adoption_plan.py` — planner and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AI adoption and literacy plan: population x module catalog -> curriculum, training load, KPIs.

Rules (references/method.md):
  * A role needs a module when the module's `audience` includes the role's exposure AND the
    module's `level` is above the role's current proficiency (0-3).
  * A module whose `mandatory_for` includes the role's exposure is always required, whatever the
    proficiency (the default catalog makes the human-oversight module mandatory for overseers).
  * hours per person = sum of the role's module hours; role hours = headcount x hours per person;
    seats per module = sum of headcount of the roles that need it.
  * Training load is summed per business unit and mapped to rollout waves; a business unit with
    no wave is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]`.
  * Adoption KPI targets come only from --targets; every missing target is
    `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]`.

Usage:
  python3 -I adoption_plan.py --population population.csv [--catalog modules.csv]
      [--waves waves.csv] [--targets targets.csv] [--strict] --out-dir OUT
  python3 -I adoption_plan.py --verify OUT/adoption.json     (any file in OUT works)

Inputs:
  population  CSV role,headcount,exposure,proficiency,business_unit
              exposure in none|user|operator|builder|overseer; proficiency integer 0-3.
  catalog     CSV module_id,title,hours,audience,level,format[,mandatory_for]
              audience / mandatory_for are '|'-separated exposure levels; level integer 1-3.
              Default: ../assets/literacy-modules.csv (the skill's own curriculum design).
  waves       CSV wave,business_unit,start_date (YYYY-MM-DD).
  targets     CSV key,value[,source] for adoption KPIs.
  Lines starting with '#' are comments.

Outputs (in --out-dir): curriculum.csv, training-load.csv, adoption-plan.md, adoption.json.
Exit codes: 0 written · 1 --strict and an overseer/operator role has no module (outputs still
written) · 2 missing or invalid input. Stdlib only; no network; writes only inside --out-dir.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import io
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEFAULT_CATALOG = SKILL_DIR / "assets" / "literacy-modules.csv"
EXPOSURES = ("none", "user", "operator", "builder", "overseer")
GATED = ("operator", "overseer")
TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]"
TBD_LD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: L&D lead]"
# Adoption KPIs the plan always shows (the skill's own measurement design; targets are never defaulted).
KPIS = [
    ("training_completion_rate", "Share of in-scope people who completed every required module", "LMS completion records"),
    ("weekly_active_rate", "Share of licensed users who used the AI system in the last 7 days", "product telemetry"),
    ("task_success_rate", "Share of AI-assisted tasks accepted without rework", "workflow / QA sampling"),
    ("satisfaction", "Average user rating of the AI system (scale stated in the target source)", "in-product or pulse survey"),
    ("time_saved_hours_per_user_week", "Self-reported or measured hours saved per active user per week", "time study or survey"),
]


class InputError(Exception):
    """Missing or invalid input -> exit 2."""


def fmt(x: float) -> str:
    s = f"{x:.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    return s if s not in ("", "-0") else "0"


def read_csv(path: Path, label: str, required_cols: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        raise InputError(f"{label} file not found: {path}")
    lines = [ln for ln in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").splitlines()
             if ln.strip() and not ln.lstrip().startswith("#")]
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO("\n".join(lines))))
    header = [h.strip() for h in (csv.reader(io.StringIO(lines[0])).__next__() if lines else [])]
    missing = [c for c in required_cols if c not in header]
    if missing:
        raise InputError(f"{label} CSV needs columns {','.join(required_cols)} (missing {','.join(missing)})")
    return [{(k or "").strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items()} for r in rows]


def to_int(v: str, label: str, lo: int, hi: int | None = None) -> int:
    try:
        n = int(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise InputError(f"{label}: expected an integer, got {v!r}") from None
    if n < lo or (hi is not None and n > hi):
        raise InputError(f"{label}: {n} out of range {lo}-{hi if hi is not None else 'inf'}")
    return n


def levels(v: str, label: str) -> list[str]:
    out = [x.strip().lower() for x in v.split("|") if x.strip()]
    bad = [x for x in out if x not in EXPOSURES]
    if bad:
        raise InputError(f"{label}: unknown exposure level(s) {bad}; allowed {EXPOSURES}")
    return out


def load_population(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    rows = read_csv(path, "population", ("role", "headcount", "exposure", "proficiency", "business_unit"))
    if not rows:
        raise InputError("population CSV has no rows")
    seen, out = set(), []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        if not r["role"] or not r["business_unit"]:
            raise InputError(f"population row {i}: role and business_unit are required")
        key = (r["role"], r["business_unit"])
        if key in seen:
            raise InputError(f"population row {i}: duplicate role {r['role']!r} in {r['business_unit']!r}")
        seen.add(key)
        exp = r["exposure"].lower()
        if exp not in EXPOSURES:
            raise InputError(f"population row {i}: exposure {r['exposure']!r} not in {EXPOSURES}")
        out.append({"role": r["role"], "business_unit": r["business_unit"], "exposure": exp,
                    "headcount": to_int(r["headcount"], f"population row {i} headcount", 0),
                    "proficiency": to_int(r["proficiency"], f"population row {i} proficiency", 0, 3)})
    return out


def load_catalog(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    rows = read_csv(path, "catalog", ("module_id", "title", "hours", "audience", "level", "format"))
    if not rows:
        raise InputError("catalog CSV has no modules")
    out, ids = [], set()
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        if not r["module_id"] or r["module_id"] in ids:
            raise InputError(f"catalog row {i}: module_id missing or duplicated")
        ids.add(r["module_id"])
        try:
            hours = float(r["hours"])
        except ValueError:
            raise InputError(f"catalog row {i}: hours must be a number, got {r['hours']!r}") from None
        if hours <= 0:
            raise InputError(f"catalog row {i}: hours must be > 0")
        out.append({"module_id": r["module_id"], "title": r["title"], "hours": hours, "format": r["format"],
                    "audience": levels(r["audience"], f"catalog row {i} audience"),
                    "level": to_int(r["level"], f"catalog row {i} level", 1, 3),
                    "mandatory_for": levels(r.get("mandatory_for", ""), f"catalog row {i} mandatory_for")})
    return sorted(out, key=lambda m: m["module_id"])


def load_waves(path: Path | None) -> dict[str, dict]:
    if path is None:
        return {}
    out = {}
    for i, r in enumerate(read_csv(path, "waves", ("wave", "business_unit", "start_date")), start=2):
        try:
            dt.date.fromisoformat(r["start_date"])
        except ValueError:
            raise InputError(f"waves row {i}: start_date must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {r['start_date']!r}") from None
        if r["business_unit"] in out:
            raise InputError(f"waves row {i}: business_unit {r['business_unit']!r} appears in two waves")
        out[r["business_unit"]] = {"wave": r["wave"], "start_date": r["start_date"]}
    return out


def load_targets(path: Path | None) -> dict[str, dict]:
    if path is None:
        return {}
    return {r["key"]: {"value": r["value"], "source": r.get("source", "")}
            for r in read_csv(path, "targets", ("key", "value")) if r["key"] and r["value"]}


def build(pop, catalog, waves, targets, catalog_label: str) -> dict:
    roles, curriculum = [], []
    seats = {m["module_id"]: 0 for m in catalog}
    for p in sorted(pop, key=lambda r: (r["business_unit"], r["role"])):
        mods = []
        for m in catalog:
            if p["exposure"] in m["mandatory_for"]:
                reason = f"mandatory for {p['exposure']} (rule), regardless of proficiency"
            elif p["exposure"] in m["audience"] and m["level"] > p["proficiency"]:
                reason = f"exposure {p['exposure']}; module level {m['level']} > proficiency {p['proficiency']}"
            else:
                continue
            mods.append(m)
            seats[m["module_id"]] += p["headcount"]
            curriculum.append({"business_unit": p["business_unit"], "role": p["role"], "module_id": m["module_id"],
                               "title": m["title"], "hours": fmt(m["hours"]), "reason": reason})
        hpp = sum(m["hours"] for m in mods)
        roles.append({**p, "modules": [m["module_id"] for m in mods], "hours_per_person": round(hpp, 2),
                      "total_hours": round(hpp * p["headcount"], 2)})
    gaps = [r for r in roles if r["exposure"] in GATED and not r["modules"]]
    has_oversight = any("overseer" in m["mandatory_for"] for m in catalog)
    overseer_rule_gap = (not has_oversight) and any(r["exposure"] == "overseer" for r in roles)
    load: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for r in roles:
        bu = r["business_unit"]
        w = waves.get(bu, {"wave": TBD, "start_date": TBD})
        e = load.setdefault(bu, {"wave": w["wave"], "business_unit": bu, "start_date": w["start_date"],
                                 "people": 0, "learners": 0, "hours": 0.0})
        e["people"] += r["headcount"]
        e["learners"] += r["headcount"] if r["modules"] else 0
        e["hours"] = round(e["hours"] + r["total_hours"], 2)
    load_rows = sorted(load.values(), key=lambda e: (e["wave"] == TBD, e["start_date"], e["wave"], e["business_unit"]))
    kpis = []
    for key, definition, source in KPIS:
        t = targets.get(key)
        kpis.append({"kpi": key, "definition": definition, "measured_from": source,
                     "target": t["value"] if t else TBD, "target_source": (t["source"] or "targets input") if t else ""})
    for key in sorted(set(targets) - {k for k, _, _ in KPIS}):
        kpis.append({"kpi": key, "definition": "owner-supplied KPI", "measured_from": TBD,
                     "target": targets[key]["value"], "target_source": targets[key]["source"] or "targets input"})
    total_people = sum(r["headcount"] for r in roles)
    return {
        "catalog": catalog_label,
        "totals": {"roles": len(roles), "people": total_people,
                   "learners": sum(r["headcount"] for r in roles if r["modules"]),
                   "training_hours": round(sum(r["total_hours"] for r in roles), 2),
                   "modules_in_catalog": len(catalog),
                   "modules_used": sum(1 for v in seats.values() if v > 0)},
        "roles": roles,
        "modules": [{"module_id": m["module_id"], "title": m["title"], "hours": m["hours"], "level": m["level"],
                     "format": m["format"], "audience": m["audience"], "mandatory_for": m["mandatory_for"],
                     "seats": seats[m["module_id"]], "seat_hours": round(seats[m["module_id"]] * m["hours"], 2)}
                    for m in catalog],
        "curriculum": curriculum,
        "training_load": load_rows,
        "kpis": kpis,
        "gaps": {"unmapped_operator_overseer_roles": [f"{r['role']} ({r['business_unit']})" for r in gaps],
                 "overseer_rule_unmet": overseer_rule_gap,
                 "business_units_without_wave": [e["business_unit"] for e in load_rows if e["wave"] == TBD]},
    }


def render(plan: dict, strict: bool) -> str:
    t, g = plan["totals"], plan["gaps"]
    L = ["# AI adoption and literacy plan", "",
         "## Summary", "",
         f"- {t['people']} people in {t['roles']} roles; {t['learners']} need at least one module.",
         f"- Total training load: {fmt(t['training_hours'])} hours across {t['modules_used']} of "
         f"{t['modules_in_catalog']} catalog modules.",
         f"- Catalog: {plan['catalog']}."]
    if g["unmapped_operator_overseer_roles"]:
        L.append(f"- Gap: operator/overseer roles with no module: {', '.join(g['unmapped_operator_overseer_roles'])} "
                 f"— {TBD_LD}.")
    else:
        L.append("- Every operator and overseer role has at least one module mapped.")
    if g["overseer_rule_unmet"]:
        L.append(f"- Gap: the catalog has no module mandatory for overseers (human-oversight rule) — {TBD_LD}.")
    if strict:
        failed = bool(g["unmapped_operator_overseer_roles"]) or g["overseer_rule_unmet"]
        L.append(f"- `--strict` was set: {'the run fails (exit 1).' if failed else 'gate passed.'}")
    L += ["", "## Who needs what", "",
          "| Business unit | Role | Exposure | Proficiency | Headcount | Modules | Hours / person | Total hours |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in plan["roles"]:
        L.append(f"| {r['business_unit']} | {r['role']} | {r['exposure']} | {r['proficiency']} | {r['headcount']} | "
                 f"{', '.join(r['modules']) or 'none'} | {fmt(r['hours_per_person'])} | {fmt(r['total_hours'])} |")
    L += ["", "## Curriculum", "",
          "| Module | Title | Level | Hours | Format | Audience | Mandatory for | Seats | Seat-hours |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for m in plan["modules"]:
        L.append(f"| {m['module_id']} | {m['title']} | {m['level']} | {fmt(m['hours'])} | {m['format']} | "
                 f"{'/'.join(m['audience'])} | {'/'.join(m['mandatory_for']) or '—'} | {m['seats']} | {fmt(m['seat_hours'])} |")
    L += ["", "## Rollout", "",
          "| Wave | Business unit | Start date | People | Learners | Training hours |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for e in plan["training_load"]:
        L.append(f"| {e['wave']} | {e['business_unit']} | {e['start_date']} | {e['people']} | {e['learners']} | {fmt(e['hours'])} |")
    L += ["", "Sequence: train the wave before its go-live; overseers and operators complete their modules before "
          "they take on oversight or operation duties.",
          "", "## Adoption KPIs", "",
          "| KPI | Definition | Measured from | Target | Target source |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for k in plan["kpis"]:
        L.append(f"| {k['kpi']} | {k['definition']} | {k['measured_from']} | {k['target']} | {k['target_source'] or '—'} |")
    L += ["", "Targets come only from the targets input; none is defaulted.",
          "", "## Art. 4 note", "",
          "EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Article 4 has applied since 2 February 2025 (Art. 113(a)). As amended by "
          "the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since July 2026), providers and deployers "
          "\"shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing "
          "with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf\", taking into account their technical knowledge, "
          "experience, education and training and the context of use; the obligation \"does not require providers or "
          "deployers to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of any individual.\" Deployers of high-risk systems "
          "must still assign human oversight to people with the necessary competence, training and authority "
          "(Art. 26(2)). This plan is evidence of measures taken; keep completion records. Not a legal determination — "
          "confirm scope with counsel. Sources: `references/sources.md`.",
          "", "## Method", "",
          "- A role needs a module when the module's audience includes the role's exposure and the module level "
          "is above the role's proficiency; modules marked mandatory for an exposure are always required.",
          "- Hours per person = sum of module hours; total = headcount × hours per person; seats = sum of headcount.",
          "- Business units without a wave are " + TBD + ".",
          "- Limits: proficiency is self- or manager-assessed; hours exclude travel and backfill; the default catalog "
          "is this skill's own design, not a regulatory syllabus."]
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def write_csv(path: Path, cols: list[str], rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=cols, extrasaction="ignore", lineterminator="\n")
    w.writeheader()
    for r in rows:
        w.writerow(r)
    path.write_text(buf.getvalue(), encoding="utf-8")


def verify(path: Path) -> int:
    """Recompute every total in adoption.json and cross-check curriculum.csv / training-load.csv."""
    d = path if path.name == "adoption.json" else path.parent / "adoption.json"
    errs = []
    try:
        plan = json.loads(d.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"verify: cannot read {d}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    mods = {m["module_id"]: m for m in plan["modules"]}
    seats = {k: 0 for k in mods}
    for r in plan["roles"]:
        hpp = round(sum(mods[m]["hours"] for m in r["modules"]), 2)
        if abs(hpp - r["hours_per_person"]) > 1e-6 or abs(round(hpp * r["headcount"], 2) - r["total_hours"]) > 1e-6:
            errs.append(f"role {r['role']}: hours do not recompute")
        for m in r["modules"]:
            seats[m] += r["headcount"]
            if r["exposure"] not in mods[m]["mandatory_for"] and not (
                    r["exposure"] in mods[m]["audience"] and mods[m]["level"] > r["proficiency"]):
                errs.append(f"role {r['role']}: module {m} not justified by the rule")
    for k, m in mods.items():
        if seats[k] != m["seats"]:
            errs.append(f"module {k}: seats {m['seats']} != {seats[k]}")
    total = round(sum(r["total_hours"] for r in plan["roles"]), 2)
    if abs(total - plan["totals"]["training_hours"]) > 1e-6:
        errs.append("total training hours do not recompute")
    if abs(round(sum(e["hours"] for e in plan["training_load"]), 2) - total) > 1e-6:
        errs.append("training load does not sum to total hours")
    cur = d.parent / "curriculum.csv"
    if cur.exists():
        n = sum(1 for _ in csv.DictReader(cur.open(encoding="utf-8")))
        if n != sum(len(r["modules"]) for r in plan["roles"]):
            errs.append("curriculum.csv row count does not match role modules")
    tl = d.parent / "training-load.csv"
    if tl.exists():
        h = round(sum(float(r["hours"]) for r in csv.DictReader(tl.open(encoding="utf-8"))), 2)
        if abs(h - total) > 1e-6:
            errs.append("training-load.csv hours do not sum to total")
    for e in errs:
        print(f"verify: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    if not errs:
        print(f"verify: ok ({len(plan['roles'])} roles, {fmt(total)} hours)")
    return 1 if errs else 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--population", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--catalog", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--waves", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--targets", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="exit 1 if an operator/overseer role has no module")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--verify", type=Path, help="re-verify an output directory's adoption.json and exit")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.verify:
        return verify(args.verify)
    if not args.population or not args.out_dir:
        print("error: --population and --out-dir are required", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        catalog_path = args.catalog or DEFAULT_CATALOG
        label = (f"supplied catalog `{catalog_path.name}`" if args.catalog else
                 "default `assets/literacy-modules.csv` (this skill's own curriculum design)")
        plan = build(load_population(args.population), load_catalog(catalog_path),
                     load_waves(args.waves), load_targets(args.targets), label)
    except InputError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    out = args.out_dir
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    write_csv(out / "curriculum.csv", ["business_unit", "role", "module_id", "title", "hours", "reason"], plan["curriculum"])
    write_csv(out / "training-load.csv", ["wave", "business_unit", "start_date", "people", "learners", "hours"],
              [{**e, "hours": fmt(e["hours"])} for e in plan["training_load"]])
    plan["strict"] = bool(args.strict)
    failed = bool(plan["gaps"]["unmapped_operator_overseer_roles"]) or plan["gaps"]["overseer_rule_unmet"]
    plan["gate"] = "fail" if (args.strict and failed) else ("pass" if args.strict else "not run")
    (out / "adoption.json").write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "adoption-plan.md").write_text(render(plan, args.strict), encoding="utf-8")
    if args.strict and failed:
        print("strict gate failed: " + (", ".join(plan["gaps"]["unmapped_operator_overseer_roles"])
                                        or "no human-oversight module for overseers"), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    t = plan["totals"]
    print(f"adoption plan written: {t['people']} people, {fmt(t['training_hours'])} training hours")
    return 0

# Method

## Exposure levels
| Exposure | Who | Typical need |
|---|---|---|
| none | Staff who do not use the AI system but work near it | Awareness |
| user | Uses AI outputs in daily tasks | Safe use, prompting, checking outputs |
| operator | Runs, monitors or supports the AI system | Monitoring, incidents, escalation |
| builder | Designs, builds, evaluates or changes the system | Evaluation, guardrails, data protection |
| overseer | Accountable for decisions the system supports; can override or stop it | Human oversight, risk and accountability |

## Proficiency (0-3)
0 none · 1 basic (has used AI tools) · 2 working (uses or runs AI in role with confidence) · 3 advanced (can teach others). Assessed by the manager or a short self-assessment; record which.

## Rules
1. Required when `exposure ∈ audience` and `level > proficiency`.
2. Always required when `exposure ∈ mandatory_for` (default catalog: AIL-06 human oversight for overseers).
3. Hours per person = Σ module hours; role hours = headcount × hours per person; seats per module = Σ headcount.
4. Training load per business unit is mapped to its wave; no wave → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]`.
5. Gate (`--strict`): exit 1 when an operator or overseer role has no module, or the catalog has no overseer-mandatory module while overseers exist.

## KPIs
Five adoption KPIs are always listed with a definition and data source (skill design). Targets are never defaulted: each comes from `targets` or is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Change lead]`.

## Limits
Proficiency is an estimate. Hours exclude travel, backfill and refresher cycles. The default catalog is this skill's own design, not a regulatory syllabus.

## Article 4 as it stands (S2, S3) — brief EU-law quotation
1. "Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf, taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education and training and the context the AI systems are to be used in, and considering the persons or groups of persons on whom the AI systems are to be used. This obligation does not require providers or deployers to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of any individual."
2. The Commission and Member States support providers and deployers (in particular SMEs) and the Commission publishes practical examples on the single information platform (Art. 62(3)(b)).
3. The AI Board adopts recommendations on AI literacy, taking into account European competence frameworks.

## What changed
The 2024 text required measures "to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy". The Digital Omnibus on AI replaced this with measures "to support the development of" AI literacy and added that no specific individual level must be guaranteed (S3, S7). The obligation still applies to providers and deployers. Briefs that cite the "sufficient level" wording are out of date.

## How the skill uses this
- The plan is a record of measures taken; the Commission says no certificate is needed (S7).
- Role-based modules reflect "technical knowledge, experience, education and training and the context" (S2).
- The overseer rule (human-oversight module always required) reflects Art. 26(2) for high-risk deployers (S6); the skill applies it to every overseer as a design choice.
- Not a legal determination. Whether the organisation is a provider or deployer, and whether a system is high-risk, is for counsel.

# AI-BOM Licence Check

## In a conversation: check the licences now
The reply **is the licence check**: its first line is `Gate: FAIL / PASS / PENDING — <the component(s) that decided it>`, never only a request for files. It is not legal advice; say so and name Legal counsel for every review and unknown.
- **The request names components** ("we fine-tuned Llama 3.1 and trained on a CC BY-NC dataset — can we ship commercially?"), or says a BOM or policy is attached but its contents are not in the conversation: give the check **in this reply** from the stated facts, in this order:
  1. **Gate line** — any deny, or commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence, is `FAIL`; otherwise `PENDING` until the BOM and policy are complete.
  2. **Components table** — `component | type (model/dataset/library/service) | licence as stated | spdx_id | use | decision | reason | flags`. Normalise only to ids in `assets/license-catalog.csv` (e.g. `CC-BY-NC-4.0`, `LicenseRef-Llama-3.1-Community`); an unrecognised string stays `unknown` and goes to Legal counsel. Use rules decide what policy cannot override: a **CC BY-NC** dataset in commercial use is **deny** (non-commercial licence, commercial use). **Llama 3.1** is **review / conditional**, never a plain allow: licence from Meta needed above 700M monthly active users, display "Built with Llama", Acceptable Use Policy, ship the agreement and Notice file, derived model names begin with "Llama".
  3. **Blocked** — each deny with the fix: replace the component, relicense it, or change the use.
  4. **Needs review** — conditional and unknown licences, routed to Legal counsel.
  5. **Obligations** — notices, attribution and flow-down terms to ship with the release.
  6. **What I need to finish** — ask once for the full BOM (`component,type,version,license,source_url,use`, every model, dataset, library and hosted service) and the organisation's licence policy (`license,decision,notes`). Without a policy, every other decision is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Legal counsel]`; blank versions or licences are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Engineering lead]`.
- **No components named** ("check our AI licences"): ask once for the BOM in the CSV layout above and the licence policy; do not decide any licence from memory.
- **Asked to approve without a policy or skip the gate** ("just approve the usual permissive ones", "it's only NC, ship it"): decline in one line — decisions come only from Legal counsel's policy and the documented use rules. Still normalise each licence, show every decision as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Legal counsel]`, and keep a non-commercial licence in commercial use as deny / gate FAIL.

## Starting points
- **New** — a system heading to its first release: list the components in the CSV layout; the skill normalises each licence, applies your policy and writes the AI-BOM.
- **Existing** — bring the CycloneDX AI-BOM kept from the last release (this skill's `aibom.json`, or an SBOM export with a `giri-skills:use` property per entry); every entry is re-checked against today's policy and catalog. An entry without a use, or of a type outside model/data/library/framework/service, stops the run rather than being guessed or dropped.

## When to use
- ADLC govern stage: before an AI release, or when a model, dataset, library or API is added or upgraded.
- "Can we ship this?" — every component's licence against the organisation's licence policy, with the use it will be put to.
- Producing an AI bill of materials in a CycloneDX-shaped JSON for a release record.
- NOT for: vulnerability or dependency CVE scanning (`security-review`), finding personal data (`pii-data-inventory`), choosing a model (`model-selection`), a legal opinion on a licence (route to Legal counsel).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bom` — `component,type,version,license,source_url,use` CSV, or an existing CycloneDX JSON BOM (`giri-skills:use` property per entry) | yes | engineering lead; model cards, dataset cards, package metadata | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `policy` — `license,decision,notes` | no | Legal counsel (start from `assets/license-policy.example.csv`) | every decision is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Legal counsel]` |
| `system` — AI system name | no | product owner | report title TBD (owner: Engineering lead); JSON omits `metadata` |

`type`: model | dataset | library | service. `use`: internal | commercial | redistribution. Other values stop the run (exit 2). Blank version or licence → TBD (owner: Engineering lead); a blank licence counts as unknown.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. List every model, dataset, library and hosted service the AI system depends on, with the licence string exactly as published and the intended use.
3. Run the skill. `scripts/aibom.py` normalises each licence through `assets/license-catalog.csv` (`references/method.md`); unknown strings stay `unknown` and go to review.
4. Decisions come only from the policy. Commercial or redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied; Llama's conditional commercial terms turn an allow into a review.
5. Any deny fails the gate (exit 1). Resolve each Blocked row (replace, relicense, or change use), then re-run.
6. Send Needs review rows to Legal counsel; ship the Obligations (notices, attribution, flow-down terms) with the release.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `aibom.csv` — `component, type, version, license_raw, spdx_id, decision, reason, flags, use`.
- `aibom.json` — CycloneDX-shaped subset (specVersion 1.6): `components` typed `machine-learning-model` / `data` / `library`, `services`, `licenses` (SPDX `id` or `expression`; `name` for unknown), `externalReferences`, decision/flags in `properties`.
- `license-report.md` — **Summary** (gate), **Components**, **Blocked**, **Needs review**, **Obligations**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every `spdx_id` is from the catalog or `unknown`; no licence guessed
- [ ] Every decision came from the policy, a documented use rule, or is TBD for Legal counsel
- [ ] Commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied and the run exits 1
- [ ] `aibom.json` passes `--verify`; it is described as a CycloneDX-shaped subset, not a validated SBOM
- [ ] Obligations listed for every shipped component; limits and "not legal advice" stated

## References
- `references/sources.md` — SPDX list 3.29.0, publisher licence pages, CycloneDX 1.6 schema, with dates checked
- `references/method.md` — normalisation, expressions, decision and use rules, gate
- `assets/license-catalog.csv` — SPDX/LicenseRef catalog with flags, obligations and source URL per row
- `assets/license-policy.example.csv` — example policy for Legal counsel to replace
- `scripts/aibom.py` — checker, CycloneDX writer and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`aibom.csv`, `aibom.json`, `license-report.md`). **Gate:** any denied component fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; all three outputs are still written. Not legal advice.

# Method

1. **Normalise.** Each `license` string is lower-cased, "licence" → "license", and stripped of everything but letters, digits, `.` and `+`; it is then looked up against every catalog row's `spdx_id`, `name` and `aliases`. No match → `unknown` (never guessed).
2. **Expressions.** `A OR B`: each part resolved; the part with the best policy decision is chosen (allow < TBD < review < deny), ties to the first. `A AND B`: the strictest decision; flags are the union. Parentheses, `WITH`, or a mix of AND and OR → `unknown`.
3. **Decide.** Policy decision for the id; id not in the policy → `review`; no policy at all → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Legal counsel]`; unknown licence → `review` (TBD when no policy).
4. **Use rules.** `use` commercial or redistribution with `commercial_use_restricted=yes` → `deny`. With `conditional` (Llama MAU clause) an `allow` becomes `review`.
5. **Gate.** Any `deny` → exit 1; all outputs are still written.
6. **Obligations.** Catalog obligations are listed for every component that is not denied; unknown licences get a Legal-counsel TBD.

Policy rows must name a catalog id (SPDX or LicenseRef, or an alias); an unrecognised policy licence stops the run (exit 2) so the policy cannot silently miss.

# AI Controls Mapping (NIST AI RMF 1.0)

## In a conversation: map the controls now
The reply **is the controls mapping**: first line `Coverage: <overall, or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]> against NIST AI RMF 1.0 (72 subcategories) — self-assessment, not an audit`. It corresponds to `python3 -I scripts/map_controls.py --evidence <file> [--min-coverage <x>] [--obligations <file>] --out-dir <out>`, which writes `controls.csv`, `coverage.json` and `controls-report.md`; name that command (with the case's flags) and those files.

**Never**
- Never assign an owner the user names for unowned gaps ("put the product manager on them"): every gap with a blank owner shows `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`; say how many gaps lack an owner.
- Never print an asserted figure ("call it 80%") as coverage, never estimate statuses, never lower a gate to pass.
- Never invent a gate: no `min_coverage` given → `Gate: no minimum coverage given`.
- Never count a blank or absent row as implemented: it is `missing`.

**Procedure — compute row by row from the supplied file, never estimate**
1. Catalogue (72): GOVERN 1.1-1.7, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.2, 6.1-6.2 (19) · MAP 1.1-1.6, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.5, 4.1-4.2, 5.1-5.2 (18) · MEASURE 1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.13, 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.3 (22) · MANAGE 1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3 (13). Function = the word before the number.
2. Read each data row (skip `#` lines). Status blank **and** evidence blank → unfilled template row = `missing`. Status not in implemented|partial|planned|not_applicable, or a duplicate id → **stops (exit 2)**. An id not in the catalogue → `ERROR` row, excluded from coverage, run **stops (exit 1)** after writing outputs.
3. Per function, count implemented, partial, planned, not_applicable from the rows; missing = function total − rows counted. applicable = total − not_applicable.
4. coverage = (implemented + 0.5 × partial) ÷ applicable, 3 decimals. Same for ALL (72).
5. Evidence-backed coverage (gate basis): an implemented/partial row with blank `evidence` gets no credit (counted as missing). Flag those ids ("implemented/partial with no evidence cited: …") and not_applicable rows with blank evidence.
6. Gate (only with min_coverage): evidence-backed ALL coverage ≥ min → PASS (equality passes); below → FAIL, run **stops (exit 1)** with full outputs written. Say "stops (exit 1)" explicitly.
7. Gaps = partial, planned, missing. Owner blank → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`. Count gaps without a named owner.
8. Obligations (only if given): skip status done/not_applicable. Look up `assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv` (trailing `*` = prefix match, e.g. TR-50-* → MEASURE 2.8). supported = every mapped subcategory implemented or not_applicable (≥1 implemented); partial = any implemented/partial; none = only planned/missing; no row → `no crosswalk entry`. Label it "the skill's own crosswalk, not an official NIST or EU mapping".

**Reply layout**
1. Working table first: `function | total | implemented | partial | planned | not_applicable | missing | applicable | coverage | evidence-backed`, rows GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE, ALL, with the formula `(implemented + 0.5 × partial) ÷ applicable` stated above it. Then the gate verdict.
2. Gaps — `subcategory_id | function | status | owner` for every gap (or grouped by function with ids listed when long); count without owner.
3. Flags, AI Act obligations (if given), outputs written.
4. Limits — voluntary framework, self-assessed statuses; self-assessment, not compliance, certification or an audit.

**No register rows in the conversation** (a spreadsheet is mentioned but not attached, or "call it 80%"): still give the layout — the function table with formula and every cell `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`, gaps "all subcategories without a row are missing; owner [TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]", the self-assessment line — and ask once for the evidence register as `subcategory_id,status,evidence,owner` (ids as in NIST AI 100-1, e.g. `GOVERN 1.1`; template `assets/evidence-template.csv`). Without evidence the run stops (exit 2). Do not estimate coverage.

## Starting points
- **New** — starting a controls programme: fill `assets/evidence-template.csv` with what exists today; blank rows count as missing and the report gives the baseline coverage and the full gap list.
- **Existing** — bring the evidence register you maintain (and `obligations.csv` from `eu-ai-act-classifier`); the skill re-scores coverage, withholds credit from uncited claims, tracks the open obligations and applies your minimum-coverage gate.

## When to use
- ADLC govern stage: before a release review, an audit or a customer assurance questionnaire that asks for NIST AI RMF alignment.
- "Where are our gaps across GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE, and who owns them?"
- After `eu-ai-act-classifier`: pass its `obligations.csv` to see which open AI Act obligations lack supporting evidence.
- NOT for: AI Act tiering (`eu-ai-act-classifier`), risk registers and likelihood/impact scoring (`ai-governance-risk`), evaluating the AI system itself (`llm-eval-harness`, `red-team-suite`), certification or audit opinions.

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evidence` — `subcategory_id,status,evidence,owner` | yes | AI risk lead with control owners (copy `assets/evidence-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| owner blank on a row | — | control owner | `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]` |
| subcategory absent from `evidence` | — | — | counted as `missing` (a gap) |
| `min_coverage` — fraction 0-1 | no | AI risk lead | no gate; coverage reported only |
| `obligations` — classifier `obligations.csv` | no | `eu-ai-act-classifier` run | AI Act section omitted |

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Copy `assets/evidence-template.csv` (all 72 ids). Owners fill status, evidence (document id or link) and owner. Mark `not_applicable` only with a justification in `evidence`.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/map_controls.py` joins the evidence to `assets/nist-ai-rmf-1.0.csv` and computes coverage per `references/crosswalk-method.md`.
4. With `obligations`, it looks up each open obligation in `assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv` (the skill's own mapping) and reports supported, partial or none.
5. Exit 1 means coverage is below `min_coverage` or there are unknown ids. Fix the evidence; do not lower the threshold to pass.
6. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `controls.csv` — `subcategory_id, function, category, status, evidence, owner, gap, note`: 72 rows in catalogue order, plus `ERROR` rows for unknown ids.
- `coverage.json` — per-function and overall counts (implemented, partial, planned, not_applicable, missing, applicable) and coverage; gate; gaps; flags; input errors; AI Act obligation support.
- `controls-report.md` — **Summary**, **Coverage by function**, **Gaps** (with the AI Act sub-section when given), **Evidence register**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] All 72 subcategories present; counts per function are 19/18/22/13
- [ ] Coverage recomputes from controls.csv (`--verify` passes)
- [ ] Every gap has an owner or the AI risk lead TBD marker
- [ ] Claims without evidence and unjustified not_applicable rows are flagged
- [ ] The crosswalk is labelled the skill's own mapping wherever it is shown
- [ ] Limits stated: voluntary framework, self-assessed statuses, not compliance or an audit

## References
- `references/sources.md` — NIST AI 100-1, Playbook, crosswalk list; URLs and check date
- `references/crosswalk-method.md` — coverage formula, gap rules, crosswalk rules and limits
- `assets/nist-ai-rmf-1.0.csv` — 72 subcategories with function, category and paraphrase
- `assets/evidence-template.csv` — input template
- `assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv` — AI Act obligation → subcategory mapping (skill's own)
- `scripts/map_controls.py` — mapper and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-controls-mapping --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-controls-mapping`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`controls.csv`, `coverage.json`, `controls-report.md`). With `min_coverage`, the skill is a gate: evidence-backed coverage (claims with no evidence cited get no credit) below the minimum fails the run (exit 1) and the outputs are still written. Unknown subcategory ids also fail the run until they are fixed.

# Coverage and crosswalk method

## Coverage
| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Statuses | `implemented`, `partial`, `planned`, `not_applicable` (from the input). A subcategory absent from the input is `missing`. |
| Applicable | total − not_applicable |
| Coverage | (implemented + 0.5 × partial) ÷ applicable, rounded to 3 decimals. `n/a` when nothing is applicable. |
| Gate | Overall evidence-backed coverage (`coverage_evidenced`: as coverage, but implemented/partial claims with no evidence cited get no credit) < `min_coverage` → exit 1, with full outputs. |
| CSV safety | Text cells in controls.csv that start with = + - @ tab or CR get a leading `'` (CSV-injection guard). |
| Gap | partial, planned or missing. A blank owner becomes `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`. |
| Flags | implemented or partial with no evidence cited; not_applicable with no justification. Flagged, not downgraded. |
| Input errors | Ids not in the 72-id catalogue are listed as `ERROR` rows in controls.csv, excluded from coverage, and fail the run (exit 1). A duplicate id or a bad status is invalid input (exit 2). |

## Crosswalk (skill's own mapping)
- **Scope:** links each `eu-ai-act-classifier` obligation id to 1-3 NIST AI RMF subcategories whose stated outcome would produce evidence for that obligation. A trailing `*` matches an id prefix (`TR-50-*`).
- **Conservative by design:** a mapping shows that evidence is *relevant*, not that the obligation is met. `supported` requires every mapped subcategory to be implemented (or not applicable). `partial` means some evidence exists. `none` means only planned or missing.
- **Not authoritative:** neither NIST nor the EU publishes a subcategory-level crosswalk to the final AI Act (sources.md S4). Counsel and the AI compliance lead own the final judgement.
- **Closed obligations** (`done`, `not_applicable`) are skipped. An obligation id with no crosswalk row is reported as `no crosswalk entry`.

# Sources — AI controls mapping

All checked **2026-10-18** with WebSearch/WebFetch. NIST publications are US-government works in the public domain. `assets/nist-ai-rmf-1.0.csv` holds short paraphrases, not the full text.

| # | Source | URL | What it confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | NIST AI 100-1, *Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)*, Jan 2023 — Tables 1-4 | https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf | GOVERN: 6 categories, 19 subcategories (1.1-1.7, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.2, 6.1-6.2). MAP: 5 categories, 18 (1.1-1.6, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.5, 4.1-4.2, 5.1-5.2). MEASURE: 4 categories, 22 (1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.13, 3.1-3.3, 4.1-4.3). MANAGE: 4 categories, 13 (1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.3). **Total 19 categories, 72 subcategories.** |
| S2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook (page updated 18 Jun 2026) | https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/ | Suggested actions are aligned to each subcategory of the four functions. The Playbook will be updated after the AI RMF is revised. |
| S3 | NIST, AI Risk Management Framework page | https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework | The current version is AI RMF 1.0 (26 Jan 2023). It "is being revised as part of the White House AI Action Plan"; no draft revision was published at check date. AI 600-1 (GenAI profile) released 26 Jul 2024. |
| S4 | NIST AIRC, Crosswalk documents | https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/crosswalks/ | 12 crosswalks listed (ISO/IEC 23894, 42001, 42005, OECD, Singapore, Japan, Korea and others). The only EU-related one is NIST's "OECD/EU/EO13960" (26 Jan 2023), which maps AI RMF trustworthiness characteristics to the **proposed** AI Act. None maps subcategories to the final Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. |
| S5 | NIST crosswalk AI RMF 1.0 ↔ OECD / EO 13960 / proposed EU AI Act | https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/2023/01/26/crosswalk_AI_RMF_1_0_OECD_EO_AIA_BoR.pdf | Characteristic-level mapping, used as context only. |

## Why the crosswalk is the skill's own
No authoritative mapping from the final AI Act's obligations to AI RMF subcategories existed on the check date (S4). `assets/aiact-nist-crosswalk.csv` is therefore **the skill's own mapping**, and it is labelled that way in the asset, the report and here. See `crosswalk-method.md`.

# AI FinOps Chargeback (showback)

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-finops-chargeback --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-finops-chargeback`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`showback.csv`, `anomalies.csv`, `budget.csv`, `finops-report.md`). Every dollar figure in the report traces to the CSVs, and each output is re-verified against the inputs with `--verify`. With `strict=true` the run is a gate: a team forecast over budget exits 1, with complete outputs.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — you bring metered usage from the AI gateway, the dated price sheet and (optionally) team budgets; the skill allocates the spend, flags anomalies and forecasts each budget.
- Only for existing: chargeback allocates spend that has already been metered; pricing a workload before launch goes to `llm-cost-model`.

## When to use
- ADLC operate stage: monthly showback of AI spend to the teams and features that consume it, before Finance decides on chargeback.
- Unit economics: cost per 1k requests by feature and model, to target optimisation work.
- Budget tracking mid-month: run-rate forecast and variance per team, with a strict gate for alerts.
- Spend spike triage: which team-days broke the trailing-14-day pattern and which feature drove them.
- NOT for: pricing a planned workload before launch (`llm-cost-model`), GPU or self-hosting sizing (`infra-gpu-sizing`), provider invoice reconciliation or posting journal entries (Finance owns chargeback posting).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` — date, team, feature, model, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens[, cached_input_tokens] | yes | AI gateway / provider usage export, tagged by team and feature | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `prices` — model, input_per_1m, output_per_1m[, cached_input_per_1m], effective_from | yes | FinOps lead, from contract or vendor price page, dated | run stops (exit 2), asks once; never estimated |
| `budgets` — team, month, budget_usd | no | FinOps lead / budget owners | every budget reads `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead]`, status NO BUDGET |
| `as_of` — YYYY-MM-DD | no | run owner | latest usage date |
| `strict` — true/false | no | FinOps lead | false: over-budget reported, run exits 0 |

A usage row whose model has no price row, or no price in effect on its date, gets no cost: it is listed under Unpriced usage with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead]` and excluded from every total.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Export usage per day with team and feature tags; copy the layouts in `assets/`. Confirm `input_tokens` includes cached tokens.
3. Get the dated price sheet from the FinOps lead (one row per price change). Never fill a price from memory.
4. Run the agent. `scripts/chargeback.py` applies `references/method.md`.
5. Read Summary, then Budgets (OVER BUDGET rows first), Anomalies (send each to the team's engineering lead), Unpriced usage (FinOps lead adds price rows and re-runs).
6. Publish showback (team and team_feature rows). Chargeback posting is Finance's call once unpriced usage is priced and figures reconcile to the invoice.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `showback.csv` — `level, month, team, feature, model, requests, cost_usd, cost_per_1k_requests, share, mom_change_pct, input_tokens, output_tokens`; levels total, month, month_team, team, team_feature, model, detail.
- `anomalies.csv` — `date, team, cost_usd, trailing_mean_usd, trailing_sd_usd, threshold_usd, excess_usd, prior_days, top_feature`.
- `budget.csv` — `team, month, budget, actual, forecast, variance, status, basis, days_elapsed, days_in_month, unpriced_requests`.
- `finops-report.md` — **Summary**, **Spend by team**, **Unit economics**, **Anomalies**, **Budgets**, **Unpriced usage**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every price came from the supplied sheet; unpriced usage is TBD for the FinOps lead, never estimated
- [ ] Totals reconcile to the cent across levels (total = months = teams)
- [ ] Every $ figure in the report appears in a CSV (`numbers_trace_to` passes)
- [ ] The as-of month is flagged as partial; forecasts use the stated as-of date, never today
- [ ] Anomaly rule and forecast method are stated in Method; they are this skill's method, not a standard
- [ ] Fixture or fictional prices are never presented as real vendor prices

## References
- `references/method.md` — formulas, levels, worked example (the eval fixture, hand-checked), how showback feeds chargeback
- `references/sources.md` — FinOps Foundation showback / chargeback definitions, checked 2026-10-18
- `assets/usage-template.csv`, `assets/prices-template.csv`, `assets/budgets-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/chargeback.py` — calculator and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 strict over budget / 2 input)

# Method — AI showback / chargeback

## Inputs
| File | Columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| usage | date, team, feature, model, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens[, cached_input_tokens] | one row per day × team × feature × model (finer rows are summed); `input_tokens` includes cached tokens |
| prices | model, input_per_1m, output_per_1m[, cached_input_per_1m], effective_from[, source] | several rows per model allowed; the latest `effective_from` on or before the usage date applies |
| budgets | team, month (YYYY-MM), budget_usd | optional; a team-month with usage and no row reads `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead]` |

## Formulas
| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| Row cost | ((input − cached) × input_per_1m + cached × cached rate + output × output_per_1m) ÷ 1M; cached rate = `cached_input_per_1m`, else the full input price (noted in the report) |
| Unpriced row | model absent from the sheet, or no row in effect on the date → no cost, `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead]`, excluded from every total, anomaly and forecast |
| Cost per 1k requests | spend ÷ priced requests × 1k, 4 decimals |
| Share | detail and month_team rows: % of that month's priced spend; other rows: % of all priced spend; 2 decimals |
| Month-over-month | (month − prior calendar month) ÷ prior month × 100; `n/a` without a prior month |
| Anomaly | team-day spend > mean + 3 × sample sd of the team's previous 14 calendar days (no-usage days = 0; days before the team's first usage excluded); evaluated only with ≥ 7 prior days |
| Forecast | closed month = actual; as-of month = actual ÷ days elapsed × days in month; later month = not started |
| Variance | budget − forecast (negative = over budget); status OVER BUDGET when forecast > budget |

Precision: `decimal.Decimal` throughout; money rounded half-up to cents only when written; rollup rows are rounded from their full-precision sums. `--as-of` defaults to the latest usage date (never today).

## showback.csv levels
`total`, `month`, `month_team`, `team`, `team_feature`, `model`, `detail` (month × team × feature × model). Unused dimensions read `*`. Sum only one level at a time.

## Worked example (the eval fixture — fictional prices, hand-checked)
Prices per 1M tokens: fict-large 3.00 in / 15.00 out / 0.30 cached from 2026-08-01, then 2.50 / 15.00 / 0.25 from 2026-09-15; fict-small 0.25 / 1.25, no cached price.

| Line | Daily usage | Daily cost |
|---|---|---|
| billing-support · invoice-qa · fict-large | 1,000 req; 2.0M in (0.5M cached); 0.3M out | to 09-14: 1.5 × 3 + 0.5 × 0.30 + 0.3 × 15 = 9.15; from 09-15: 3.75 + 0.125 + 4.50 = 8.375 |
| billing-support · dispute-summary · fict-small | 333 req; 777,777 in (100,000 cached, full price); 111,111 out | 0.19444425 + 0.13888875 = 0.333333 |
| collections · dunning-email · fict-small | 500 req (odd days) / 520 (even); 800 in and 200 out per request; 5,000 req on 09-25 | 450 × req ÷ 1M: 0.225 / 0.234; 2.25 on 09-25 |
| billing-support · invoice-qa · fict-legacy | 200 req on 10-01..10-03 | unpriced (no price row) |

- September: invoice-qa 14 × 9.15 + 16 × 8.375 = 262.10; dispute-summary 30 × 0.333333 = 9.99999 → 10.00; billing-support 272.09999 → **272.10**; collections 15 × 0.225 + 15 × 0.234 + 2.025 = **8.91**; month **281.01**.
- October 1–10: billing-support 83.75 + 3.33333 = 87.08333 → 87.08, forecast 87.08333 ÷ 10 × 31 = **269.96** vs budget 250.00 → variance **−19.96, OVER BUDGET**; collections 2.295 → 2.30, forecast **7.11**, variance 2.89.
- Total **370.39** = 281.01 + 89.38 = 359.18 + 11.21 (reconciles to the cent).
- Anomaly 2026-09-25 collections: trailing 14 days mean 0.2295, sample sd 0.0047, threshold 0.2435; spend 2.25, excess 2.01.

## Input hygiene
- Inputs must be UTF-8 CSV (a BOM is accepted); any other encoding or a binary file stops the run (exit 2) — bytes are never silently replaced.
- A row with more fields than the header (a ragged row) stops the run (exit 2) with its line number, so no value is dropped silently.
- Exact-duplicate usage rows are summed as supplied but listed in the Summary and on stderr (possible double count from a re-export); the FinOps lead confirms.
- Text cells written to the CSV outputs (team, feature, model, reasons) that start with = + - @ tab or CR get a leading `'` (OWASP CSV-injection guard); numbers such as -19.96 are left as they are.

## Using the output
- Showback: publish `showback.csv` (team and team_feature levels) to each team monthly.
- Chargeback: Finance posts the `month_team` amounts only once unpriced usage is priced and the figures are reconciled to the provider invoice; this skill does not reconcile invoices.
- Anomalies go to the team's engineering lead to confirm cause before any adjustment.

# Sources (checked 2026-10-18)

| Id | Source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | FinOps Foundation, FinOps Framework capability "Invoicing & Chargeback" — https://www.finops.org/framework/capabilities/invoicing-chargeback/ (CC BY 4.0) | Showback = reporting each group the cost of the scope it owns, at any granularity; chargeback = the formal step of posting those costs to the accounting records, governed by the organisation's accounting policy |

No price, rate or threshold comes from a source: every price is the user's dated price sheet, and the anomaly rule (mean + 3 sd over 14 days, ≥ 7 prior days) and the linear run-rate forecast are this skill's documented method, not a standard.

# AI Governance & Risk Review

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-governance-risk --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-governance-risk`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`risk-register.csv`, `register-diff.csv`, `model-card.md`). Scores the canvas cannot support stay `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; a High risk with no mapped control fails the run (exit 1) on purpose.

## Starting points
- **New** — a new AI use case: bring the filled use-case canvas; the register is scored only where the canvas supports it and everything else is TBD for the AI risk lead.
- **Existing** — bring the updated canvas and last quarter's risk register; risk IDs stay stable, the canvas wins where it supports a value, reviewed scores, owners and still-valid controls carry forward (labelled for re-confirmation), and `register-diff.csv` lists every change, including rows that could not be carried.

## When to use
- Pre-launch risk review of an AI use case; building or refreshing the AI risk register; model documentation; regulatory mapping at summary level.
- NOT for: legal opinions (state this; route to counsel), strategy/CoE (`ai-strategy-coe`), eval mechanics (`llm-eval-harness`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Use-case description: purpose, users, decisions influenced, autonomy level | yes | user / design doc |
| Data: categories (PII, special categories, minors, financial, health, education records), sources, jurisdictions | yes | user |
| Model(s): provider/open-weights, version, fine-tuned?, hosting location | yes | user |
| Deployment context: internal / employee-facing / customer-facing / regulated decision | yes | user |
| Existing controls and policies | no | user |
| Existing risk register (e.g. last quarter's `risk-register.csv`) | no | AI risk lead; carried forward by category, changes in `register-diff.csv` |
| Applicable regulations the org already tracks | no | user; otherwise summary mapping only |

If the use case, data categories, or deployment context are missing, ask once.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. **Classify the use case.** Determine the internal risk tier (low / medium / high) using `references/risk-taxonomy.md` §Tiering, and the summary EU AI Act tier using `references/regulatory-mapping.md`. State both with the criteria met.
3. **Identify risks.** Walk the taxonomy (bias, privacy, hallucination, IP, security, misuse, operational, transparency). For each applicable risk: scenario, likelihood (1–5), impact (1–5), inherent score, in `assets/risk-register.csv`.
4. **Select controls** from `references/controls-catalog.md` per risk; record control owner, status (in place / planned / gap), evidence, and residual score. Gaps become next steps with owner and date.
5. **Write the model card** from `assets/model-card.md`: intended use, out-of-scope use, data, evaluation results (from `llm-eval-harness` where available), limitations, monitoring, contacts.
6. **Map to frameworks** at summary level with `references/regulatory-mapping.md`: NIST AI RMF Govern/Map/Measure/Manage coverage table; EU AI Act tier and headline obligations; note other regimes the org names. Add the line: "Summary mapping for planning; legal review required for obligations."
7. **Decide.** Launch recommendation: go / go with conditions / no-go, with the conditions listed as owner + date.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `ai-risk-review-<use-case>.md`: tiering, risk register table, controls, model card, framework mapping, decision, next steps.
- `risk-register.csv` filled.
- `register-diff.csv` — every carry-forward and change against the existing register (header only when none was given).

## Self-check
- [ ] Both internal tier and EU AI Act summary tier stated with criteria
- [ ] Every risk has likelihood, impact, control, owner, residual score
- [ ] Zero gaps without an owner and date
- [ ] Model card has out-of-scope uses and limitations, not only intended use
- [ ] Framework mapping is labeled summary-level; legal review line present
- [ ] No fabricated regulatory citations; cite article/section only when provided by a source
- [ ] Decision line is first

## References
- `references/risk-taxonomy.md` — risk categories, scenarios, tiering
- `references/controls-catalog.md` — controls by risk with evidence expectations
- `references/regulatory-mapping.md` — NIST AI RMF functions, EU AI Act tiers (summary)
- `scripts/risk_register.py` — canvas + controls catalog (+ optional existing register) → `risk-register.csv` + `register-diff.csv` + `model-card.md`; exit 1 if a High risk has no control
