#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Risk register + model card from a filled use-case canvas and the controls catalog.

    python3 -I scripts/risk_register.py use-case-canvas.md --out-dir runs/x \
        [--controls references/controls-catalog.md] [--template assets/model-card.md] [--name "Ticket triage"] \
        [--existing last-quarter/risk-register.csv]

Canvas (ai-use-case-canvas assets/use-case-canvas.md layout): the nine-box table
`| # | Box | Content |` is parsed by box name; `key: value;` pairs inside a box are read
(Tier, autonomy, sensitivity, owner, Sources, top risks ...). Headings and the Verdict line are
read when present.

Register rules (references/risk-taxonomy.md): one row per taxonomy category. Impact comes from
the canvas tier (low=2, medium=3, high=5 per the taxonomy's impact scale; basis cited) and likelihood is 3 only when the canvas
names that category among its top risks — anything the canvas does not support stays
`[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`, and the rating is TBD until both scores exist.
Rating = L x I: >= 15 High, 8-14 Medium, < 8 Low. Controls are mapped per category from the
catalog's `| ID | Control | Addresses | ... |` table ("All" matches every category).

Existing register (--existing, e.g. last quarter's risk-register.csv; this script's columns, or the
assets/risk-register.csv layout with likelihood_1_5 / impact_1_5 / control_ids / control_owner): rows
are matched by category. The canvas still wins wherever it supports a value; where it gives none, a
reviewed 1-5 score and a named owner are carried forward (basis says so, to be re-confirmed), the
previous risk_id is kept so IDs stay stable, and previously accepted control ids that are still in
the catalog stay mapped. Every carry-forward and every change is listed in register-diff.csv;
existing rows whose category is not in the taxonomy are listed there, never dropped silently.

Writes risk-register.csv (risk_id, category, description, likelihood, impact, rating, control_id,
control, owner, basis), register-diff.csv (risk_id, category, field, previous, current, change;
header only when no existing register is given) and model-card.md (assets/model-card.md with the canvas facts filled; the
tier's minimum control set listed in §7). Exit 1 when any High-rated risk has no mapped control,
or on a missing/unparseable canvas or catalog. Stdlib only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILL = HERE.parent
TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]"
CATEGORIES = [("bias", "Bias / fairness"), ("privacy", "Privacy"), ("hallucination", "Hallucination / accuracy"),
              ("ip", "IP / copyright"), ("security", "Security"), ("misuse", "Misuse"),
              ("operational", "Operational"), ("transparency", "Transparency / accountability"),
              ("safety", "Safety (physical / wellbeing)")]
SYNONYMS = {"bias": ["bias", "fairness"], "privacy": ["privacy", "pii", "personal data"],
            "hallucination": ["hallucination", "accuracy", "fabricat"], "ip": ["ip ", "ip)", "ip,", "copyright", "licen"],
            "security": ["security", "injection", "exfiltrat"], "misuse": ["misuse", "out-of-scope use", "out of scope use"],
            "operational": ["operational", "drift", "vendor", "outage"], "transparency": ["transparency", "disclos", "contest", "appeal"],
            "safety": ["safety", "wellbeing", "harm"]}
TIER_IMPACT = {"low": 2, "medium": 3, "high": 5}


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def parse_canvas(path: Path) -> dict:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    boxes: dict[str, str] = {}
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"^\|\s*\d+\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*(.*?)\s*\|\s*$", ln)
        if m:
            boxes[m.group(1).lower()] = m.group(2)
    if not boxes:
        die(f"{path.name}: no canvas box table found (expected `| # | Box | Content |` rows)")
    fields: dict[str, str] = {}
    for content in boxes.values():
        for part in content.split(";"):
            if ":" in part:
                k, _, v = part.partition(":")
                k, v = k.strip().lower(), v.strip()
                if k and v and not v.startswith("<") and k not in fields:
                    fields[k] = v
    m = re.search(r"^\*\*Verdict:\*\*\s*(.+)$", text, re.M)
    title = re.search(r"^#\s+AI Use-Case Canvas\s+[—-]\s+(.+?)\s+[—-]", text, re.M)
    return {"boxes": boxes, "fields": fields, "verdict": (m.group(1).strip() if m else ""),
            "name": (title.group(1).strip() if title else "")}


def box(c: dict, key: str) -> str:
    for k, v in c["boxes"].items():
        if key in k:
            return v.strip()
    return ""


def is_filled(v: str) -> bool:
    return bool(v) and not v.startswith("<") and "[TO BE BASELINED" not in v


def parse_catalog(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, list[str]]]:
    if not path.is_file():
        die(f"controls catalog not found: {path}")
    controls, tiers = [], {}
    for ln in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        cells = [x.strip() for x in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")] if ln.startswith("|") else []
        if len(cells) >= 3 and re.fullmatch(r"C\d+", cells[0]):
            controls.append({"id": cells[0], "control": cells[1], "addresses": cells[2].lower()})
        elif len(cells) == 2 and cells[0].lower() in TIER_IMPACT:
            tiers[cells[0].lower()] = re.findall(r"C\d+", cells[1]) + (["(see lower tiers)"] if "+" in cells[1] else [])
    if not controls:
        die(f"{path.name}: no controls table found (`| C01 | ... | Addresses | ... |`)")
    return controls, tiers


def controls_for(cat: str, controls: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    label = dict(CATEGORIES)[cat].split(" ")[0].lower()
    return [c for c in controls if c["addresses"] == "all" or label in c["addresses"]]


def tier_controls(tier: str, tiers: dict) -> list[str]:
    order = ["low", "medium", "high"]
    if tier not in order:
        return []
    ids = []
    for t in order[: order.index(tier) + 1]:
        ids += [i for i in tiers.get(t, []) if i.startswith("C") and i not in ids]
    return ids


DIFF_COLS = ["risk_id", "category", "field", "previous", "current", "change"]
EXISTING_ALIASES = {"likelihood": ("likelihood", "likelihood_1_5"), "impact": ("impact", "impact_1_5"),
                    "owner": ("owner", "control_owner"), "control_id": ("control_id", "control_ids")}


def unset(v) -> bool:
    s = str(v if v is not None else "").strip()
    return not s or s.upper() == "TBD" or s.startswith("[TO BE BASELINED") or s.startswith("<")


def score(v) -> int | None:
    s = str(v or "").strip()
    return int(s) if s.isdigit() and 1 <= int(s) <= 5 else None


def load_existing(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        die(f"existing register not found: {path}")
    lines = [ln for ln in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").splitlines() if not ln.lstrip().startswith("#")]
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(lines))
    if not rows or "category" not in rows[0]:
        die(f"{path.name}: existing register needs a category column and at least one row")
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        r = {(k or "").strip().lower(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k is not None}
        rec = {"risk_id": r.get("risk_id", ""), "category": r.get("category", "").lower()}
        for field, names in EXISTING_ALIASES.items():
            rec[field] = next((r[n] for n in names if r.get(n)), "")
        out.append(rec)
    return out


def rating_of(likelihood, impact) -> str:
    if isinstance(likelihood, int) and isinstance(impact, int):
        s = likelihood * impact
        return "High" if s >= 15 else "Medium" if s >= 8 else "Low"
    return "TBD"


def merge_existing(rows: list[dict], existing: list[dict], controls: list[dict], src: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Carry reviewed values forward from an existing register; return the diff rows."""
    byid = {c["id"]: c for c in controls}
    known = {cat for cat, _ in CATEGORIES}
    prev = {}
    diff = []
    for e in existing:
        if e["category"] in known and e["category"] not in prev:
            prev[e["category"]] = e
        else:
            why = "category not in the taxonomy" if e["category"] not in known else "duplicate category"
            diff.append({"risk_id": e["risk_id"], "category": e["category"], "field": "row", "previous": e["risk_id"],
                         "current": "", "change": f"not carried: {why} — review with {TBD}"})
    used = {e["risk_id"] for e in existing if e["risk_id"]}
    nums = [int(m.group(1)) for i in used if (m := re.fullmatch(r"R-(\d+)", i))]
    nxt = max(nums, default=0) + 1
    for r in rows:
        e = prev.get(r["category"])
        if e is not None and e["risk_id"]:
            r["risk_id"] = e["risk_id"]  # IDs stay stable across reviews
        elif r["risk_id"] in used:
            r["risk_id"] = f"R-{nxt:03d}"
            nxt += 1
        if e is None:
            diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": "row", "previous": "",
                         "current": r["risk_id"], "change": "new: category not in the existing register"})
            continue
        basis = [r["basis"]] if r["basis"] != "canvas gives no basis for scores" else []
        for field in ("likelihood", "impact"):
            old = score(e[field])
            cur = r[field] if isinstance(r[field], int) else None
            if cur is None and old is not None:
                r[field] = old
                basis.append(f"{field} {old} carried forward from {src} {e['risk_id'] or r['category']} (re-confirm)")
                diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": field, "previous": str(old),
                             "current": str(old), "change": "carried forward: canvas gives no basis"})
            elif cur is not None and old is not None and cur != old:
                diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": field, "previous": str(old),
                             "current": str(cur), "change": "updated from the canvas"})
            elif cur is not None and old is None:
                diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": field,
                             "previous": e[field] or "blank", "current": str(cur), "change": "newly scored from the canvas"})
        if unset(r["owner"]) and not unset(e["owner"]):
            r["owner"] = e["owner"]
            diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": "owner", "previous": e["owner"],
                         "current": e["owner"], "change": "carried forward: canvas names no owner"})
        elif not unset(r["owner"]) and not unset(e["owner"]) and r["owner"] != e["owner"]:
            diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": "owner", "previous": e["owner"],
                         "current": r["owner"], "change": "updated from the canvas"})
        ids = [i for i in r["control_id"].split("; ") if i]
        old_ids = re.findall(r"C\d+", e["control_id"])
        kept = [i for i in old_ids if i in byid and i not in ids]
        gone = [i for i in old_ids if i not in byid]
        if kept:
            ids += kept
            r["control_id"] = "; ".join(ids)
            r["control"] = "; ".join(byid[i]["control"] for i in ids)
            diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": "control_id",
                         "previous": "; ".join(old_ids), "current": r["control_id"],
                         "change": "carried forward: previously accepted controls still in the catalog"})
        if gone:
            diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": "control_id",
                         "previous": "; ".join(gone), "current": "", "change": f"not carried: not in the controls catalog — review with {TBD}"})
        old_rating = rating_of(score(e["likelihood"]), score(e["impact"]))
        r["rating"] = rating_of(r["likelihood"] if isinstance(r["likelihood"], int) else None,
                                r["impact"] if isinstance(r["impact"], int) else None)
        if old_rating != r["rating"]:
            diff.append({"risk_id": r["risk_id"], "category": r["category"], "field": "rating", "previous": old_rating,
                         "current": r["rating"], "change": "re-rated"})
        r["basis"] = "; ".join(basis) or "canvas gives no basis for scores"
    return diff


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="use-case canvas + controls catalog -> risk-register.csv + model-card.md")
    ap.add_argument("canvas")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--controls", default=str(SKILL / "references" / "controls-catalog.md"))
    ap.add_argument("--template", default=str(SKILL / "assets" / "model-card.md"))
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--existing", default="", help="existing risk register CSV (e.g. last quarter's) to carry forward")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cp = Path(a.canvas)
    if not cp.is_file():
        die(f"canvas not found: {cp}")
    c = parse_canvas(cp)
    controls, tiers = parse_catalog(Path(a.controls))
    name = a.name or c["name"] or "<system name>"
    f = c["fields"]
    tier = next((t for t in TIER_IMPACT if t in f.get("tier", "").lower()), "")
    top_risks = box(c, "risks and tier").lower()
    autonomy = f.get("autonomy", "")
    sensitivity = f.get("sensitivity", "")
    data_owner = f.get("owner", "")
    users = box(c, "problem and user")
    decision = box(c, "decision or task")

    rows, unmapped_high = [], []
    for i, (cat, label) in enumerate(CATEGORIES, 1):
        basis = []
        impact = TIER_IMPACT.get(tier)
        if impact:
            basis.append(f"impact from tier={tier} (canvas box 8)")
        named = any(s in top_risks for s in SYNONYMS[cat]) and is_filled(top_risks)
        likelihood = 3 if named else None
        if named:
            basis.append("likelihood 3: named as a top risk in canvas box 8")
        if likelihood and impact:
            score = likelihood * impact
            rating = "High" if score >= 15 else "Medium" if score >= 8 else "Low"
        else:
            rating = "TBD"
        desc = {
            "bias": f"Outputs systematically disadvantage a group in: {decision or TBD}",
            "privacy": f"Personal data exposed or retained beyond purpose; sensitivity: {sensitivity or TBD}",
            "hallucination": f"Confident false output acted on by: {users or TBD}",
            "ip": "Protected content leaks into or out of the system (training/retrieval provenance)",
            "security": f"Prompt injection or tool abuse; autonomy: {autonomy or TBD}",
            "misuse": "System used outside the canvas's intended decision or task",
            "operational": "Model/vendor change, drift, cost or outage breaks the workflow",
            "transparency": "Users unaware of AI involvement or unable to contest the outcome",
            "safety": "Advice or action harms people (vulnerable users, action-taking)",
        }[cat]
        mapped = controls_for(cat, controls)
        if rating == "High" and not mapped:
            unmapped_high.append(cat)
        rows.append({"risk_id": f"R-{i:03d}", "category": cat, "description": desc,
                     "likelihood": likelihood if likelihood else TBD, "impact": impact if impact else TBD,
                     "rating": rating, "control_id": "; ".join(m["id"] for m in mapped),
                     "control": "; ".join(m["control"] for m in mapped),
                     "owner": data_owner if (cat == "privacy" and data_owner) else TBD,
                     "basis": "; ".join(basis) or "canvas gives no basis for scores"})

    diff = []
    if a.existing:
        ep = Path(a.existing)
        diff = merge_existing(rows, load_existing(ep), controls, f"existing register `{ep.name}`")
        unmapped_high = [r["category"] for r in rows if r["rating"] == "High" and not r["control_id"]]

    out = Path(a.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (out / "register-diff.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=DIFF_COLS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(diff)
    with (out / "risk-register.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["risk_id", "category", "description", "likelihood", "impact", "rating",
                                           "control_id", "control", "owner", "basis"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

    tpl_path = Path(a.template)
    if not tpl_path.is_file():
        die(f"template not found: {tpl_path}")
    t = tpl_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    t = t.replace("<system name>", name).replace("<version>", "0.1").replace("<date>", TBD)
    t = t.replace("| Risk tier (internal / EU AI Act summary) | |",
                  f"| Risk tier (internal / EU AI Act summary) | {tier or TBD} / {TBD} |")
    t = t.replace("| Owner (business) | |", f"| Owner (business) | {f.get('baseline signed by', '') or TBD} |")
    t = t.replace("| Owner (technical) | |", f"| Owner (technical) | {TBD} |")
    t = t.replace("- Purpose:", f"- Purpose: {users or TBD}")
    t = t.replace("- Users:", f"- Users: {f.get('users', '') or TBD}")
    t = t.replace("- Decisions or actions influenced:", f"- Decisions or actions influenced: {decision or TBD}")
    t = t.replace("- Autonomy level and human oversight:", f"- Autonomy level and human oversight: {autonomy or TBD}")
    t = t.replace("## 2. Out-of-scope uses (explicit)\n- \n- ", f"## 2. Out-of-scope uses (explicit)\n- {TBD}\n- {TBD}")
    t = t.replace("| Retrieval sources | |", f"| Retrieval sources | {f.get('sources', '') or TBD} |")
    t = t.replace("| Tools and side effects | |", f"| Tools and side effects | {('autonomy: ' + autonomy) if autonomy else TBD} |")
    t = t.replace("| Data entering prompts (categories; PII handling) | |",
                  f"| Data entering prompts (categories; PII handling) | sensitivity: {sensitivity or TBD}; owner: {data_owner or TBD} |")
    t = t.replace("| Retrieval corpus (owner, ACL, refresh) | |",
                  f"| Retrieval corpus (owner, ACL, refresh) | {f.get('sources', '') or TBD}; access: {f.get('access', '') or TBD}; freshness: {f.get('freshness', '') or TBD} |")
    t = t.replace("## 6. Limitations and known failure modes\n- \n- ",
                  "## 6. Limitations and known failure modes\n- " + "\n- ".join(
                      f"{r['category']}: {r['description']} (rating {r['rating']})" for r in rows if r["rating"] in ("High", "Medium"))
                  + (f"\n- {TBD}" if not any(r["rating"] in ("High", "Medium") for r in rows) else ""))
    req = tier_controls(tier, tiers)
    byid = {x["id"]: x for x in controls}
    ctl_rows = [f"| {i} — {byid[i]['control'] if i in byid else ''} | planned — {TBD} | {TBD} |" for i in req] \
        or [f"| {TBD} (tier not stated in canvas) | | |"]
    t = t.replace("| Control (ID) | Status | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|",
                  "| Control (ID) | Status | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|\n" + "\n".join(ctl_rows))
    t = re.sub(r"^(\| [^|]+ \|) \|$", lambda m: f"{m.group(1)} {TBD} |", t, flags=re.M)
    t = re.sub(r"^(- [^:\n]+:)\s*$", lambda m: f"{m.group(1)} {TBD}", t, flags=re.M)
    t += ("\nSummary mapping for planning; legal review required for obligations. "
          f"Facts above come from the canvas `{cp.name}`; everything else is marked {TBD}.\n")
    (out / "model-card.md").write_text(t, encoding="utf-8")

    n_tbd = sum(r["rating"] == "TBD" for r in rows)
    print(f"risk register: {len(rows)} risks ({n_tbd} unscored), tier={tier or 'TBD'}, {len(req)} required controls -> {out}"
          + (f"; {len(diff)} change(s) against `{Path(a.existing).name}` in register-diff.csv" if a.existing else ""))
    if unmapped_high:
        print(f"error: High-rated risk(s) without a mapped control: {unmapped_high}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Regulatory and Framework Mapping (summary level)

This is a planning aid. It is not legal advice. Obligations, tiers, and timelines must be confirmed by counsel against the current text of each regulation.

## NIST AI Risk Management Framework — four functions
| Function | Purpose | What to show in the review | Controls (catalog) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Govern | Policies, roles, accountability, culture | AI policy; inventory; tiering; roles (owner, reviewer, risk lead); training | C01, C18, C19, C21 |
| Map | Context, intended use, impacts, stakeholders | Use-case description; users and affected parties; data flows; out-of-scope uses; tier rationale | C02, C13, C20 |
| Measure | Evaluate and track risks with metrics | Eval harness results; bias tests; security tests; monitoring metrics | C06, C07, C08, C10, C16, C22 |
| Manage | Prioritize, respond, and recover | Controls with owners; HITL; incident process; rollback; vendor fallback; periodic review | C04, C05, C09, C11, C12, C14, C15, C17 |

Coverage table for the deliverable: Function | Evidence present | Gaps | Owner.

## EU AI Act — risk tiers (summary)
| Tier | Summary description | Typical examples (illustrative) | Headline implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unacceptable | Practices prohibited outright | Social scoring by public authorities; manipulative techniques causing harm; certain biometric categorization | Do not build |
| High-risk | Systems in listed domains or safety components of regulated products | Employment decisions (recruitment, promotion), access to education and student assessment, credit scoring, essential services, law enforcement, critical infrastructure | Risk management system, data governance, technical documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy/robustness/security, conformity assessment, registration |
| Limited risk (transparency) | Systems with specific transparency duties | Chatbots interacting with people; AI-generated or manipulated content; emotion recognition in some contexts | Disclose AI interaction; label synthetic content |
| Minimal risk | Everything else | Spam filters, internal drafting aids | Voluntary codes; general law still applies |
| General-purpose AI models | Separate obligations for model providers; additional for systemic-risk models | Foundation model providers | Mostly provider-side; deployers inherit documentation needs |

Deployer vs provider: an organization that builds on a vendor model and puts a system into service in its own name may carry deployer obligations and, in some configurations, provider obligations. Flag this for counsel when the system is customized substantially or re-branded.

Tiering questions for the review:
1. Does the system make or materially influence decisions in employment, education, credit, essential services, or law enforcement? → likely high-risk.
2. Do people interact with it without knowing it is AI? → transparency duty.
3. Does it generate content presented to the public? → labeling duty.
4. Is it purely internal productivity with human review? → minimal, with general data-protection law still applying.

## Other regimes to name when applicable (confirm with counsel)
| Regime | Trigger |
|---|---|
| GDPR / UK GDPR and other data-protection laws | Personal data of residents; automated decision-making provisions; DPIA triggers |
| US state privacy and AI laws (e.g., Colorado AI Act, state consumer privacy laws) | Consumer-facing consequential decisions; state residents |
| Sector rules: FERPA (education records), HIPAA (health), GLBA/ECOA/FCRA (finance, credit), EEOC guidance (employment) | Sector data or decisions |
| ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system) | When the organization wants certifiable governance |
| Contractual and procurement requirements | Client or vendor obligations on AI use |

Deliverable line (mandatory): "Summary mapping for planning purposes; legal review required to confirm obligations."

# AI Risk Taxonomy and Tiering

## Categories
| Category | Definition | Example scenarios | Typical signals |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bias / fairness | Outputs systematically disadvantage a group | Résumé screening favors one demographic; loan pre-qualification differs by zip code; tutoring assistant gives lower-quality help in one language | Protected attributes or proxies in data; decisions about people |
| Privacy | Personal data collected, exposed, inferred, or retained beyond purpose | PII in prompts logged to a vendor; RAG surfaces another employee's record; model infers health status | PII, special categories, minors, cross-border transfer |
| Hallucination / accuracy | Confident false or unsupported output | Invented policy clause; wrong dosage; fabricated citation | No grounding; no abstention path; high-stakes facts |
| IP / copyright | Infringement or leakage of protected content | Training data provenance unclear; output reproduces licensed text; employee pastes source code into a public model | Generative output published externally; proprietary inputs |
| Security | Prompt injection, data exfiltration, tool abuse, model theft | Agent follows instructions embedded in an email; over-privileged tools; secrets in prompts | Agents with tools; untrusted content; external communications |
| Misuse | System used outside intended purpose | Internal drafting tool used for customer legal advice; chatbot used to generate harassment | Broad access; no scope controls |
| Operational | Reliability, drift, cost, vendor dependency | Model version change breaks workflow; cost spike; vendor outage | No eval gate; no fallbacks; single vendor |
| Transparency / accountability | Users unaware they interact with AI or cannot contest outcomes | No disclosure; no human appeal; decisions unexplained | Customer-facing; consequential decisions |
| Safety (physical / wellbeing) | Harm to people from advice or action | Health, safety, or financial guidance to vulnerable users | Vulnerable users; action-taking agents |

## Scoring
| Scale | Likelihood | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rare; strong preventive controls | Negligible; internal, reversible |
| 2 | Unlikely | Minor; limited users; reversible with effort |
| 3 | Possible | Moderate; customer or employee harm; regulatory inquiry possible |
| 4 | Likely | Major; legal exposure; material financial or reputational impact |
| 5 | Almost certain without controls | Severe; safety, rights, or regulatory breach |

Inherent score = likelihood × impact (1–25). Residual score re-scored after controls. Treat ≥ 15 as requiring executive sign-off; 8–14 as requiring named mitigations before launch; < 8 monitor.

## Internal tiering
| Tier | Criteria (any) | Review path |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Internal users; no personal data beyond business contact; human reviews every output; reversible | Self-certification; register entry |
| Medium | Employee-facing or customer-facing with human in the loop; personal data present; outputs influence but do not decide | CoE review; controls checklist; model card |
| High | Autonomous actions on people or money; decisions about employment, credit, education, health, legal status; minors or vulnerable users; special-category data; likely EU AI Act high-risk | Risk committee; full register; DPIA/equivalent; legal review; executive sign-off |

## Elicitation questions
1. What decision or action does the output influence, and who bears the consequence?
2. What is the worst plausible output, and who sees it before harm occurs?
3. What data enters the prompt, what is logged, and where does it go?
4. Can a user contest or correct an outcome?
5. What happens when the model is unavailable or wrong 5% of the time?

---
name: ai-incident-runbook
description: Use when something has gone wrong with a live AI system and the user needs to respond — "the bot leaked customer data", "we have a prompt injection incident", "the assistant gave harmful answers", "LLM costs spiked overnight", "how severe is this AI incident", "write the runbook and postmortem". Produces runbook.md (Severity, Immediate actions, Containment, Recovery, Communications, Postmortem) and incident.json from an incident facts CSV - severity SEV1-SEV4 with the matrix rows that fired, the bundled per-category playbook (contain, eradicate, recover, verify), a timeline anchored on started_at, a comms checklist with a regulator track only when regulated data is yes or unknown, and a postmortem skeleton. Not legal advice; not for monitoring (llm-observability) or general software incidents without an AI failure mode.
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: ai-platform
  adlc_stage: operate
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    inputs:
      - {name: incident, type: csv, required: true, from: "incident facts key,value (layout: assets/incident-template.csv) - category, started_at required; unknowns stay unknown"}
      - {name: matrix, type: csv, required: false, from: "your severity matrix rule_id,conditions,severity,reason; without it the skill's documented default (references/severity-matrix.md) is used and stated"}
    run:
      - {step: runbook, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/runbook.py --incident {incident} [--matrix {matrix}] --out-dir {out}"}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/runbook.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Severity","Immediate actions","Containment","Recovery","Communications","Postmortem"], no_unowned_tbd, numbers_trace_to:"{out}/incident.json"]}
      - {path: "{out}/incident.json", checks: [exists, json, contains:"\"fired_rules\"", contains:"\"matrix_source\""]}

      existing: {case: agent-mode-existing, bring: "the incident facts plus your team's own severity matrix"}

# AI Incident Runbook

## In a conversation: write the runbook now
The reply **is the runbook**: its first line is `Severity: SEV<n> (provisional) — <rule ids that fired> — <the facts and unknowns that drove it>`, never only a request for a CSV. Contain first; questions go after the actions.
- **The request describes the incident** ("our assistant showed one member another member's claim details; started about an hour ago"), or says facts are attached but they are not in the conversation: write the runbook **in this reply** from the stated facts, in this order:
  1. **Severity** — classify with the skill's default matrix (`references/severity-matrix.md`) and say so; list every fired row. Missing `users_affected`, `data_exposed`, `regulated_data` are **unknown, and unknown escalates** (D02: exposure confirmed, regulated status unknown → SEV1; D03: exposure not ruled out, regulated data possible → SEV2; D12: users unknown → SEV3). Severity goes down only with evidence.
  2. **Immediate actions** — contain first, from `assets/playbooks/<category>.md`. For a data leak: disable the leaking path now (feature flag off, tool or connector revoked, retrieval source detached), preserve evidence (traces, logs, outputs) while restricting access to them, revoke and rotate any credentials that appeared. **Timeline** holds only the times the user gave (e.g. "started ~1 hour ago" as stated); every other time is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Incident commander]`.
  3. **Containment** and **Recovery** — the playbook's contain, eradicate, recover and verify steps.
  4. **Communications** — internal always; customer unless users_affected = 0; **regulator track** when regulated data is yes or unknown, flagged for Legal / privacy to confirm obligations and deadlines — no deadline is set or invented.
  5. **Postmortem** skeleton — fields and action items, including a regression eval case and the missing alert.
  6. **Owners** — incident commander, engineering lead, comms lead, legal/privacy, security lead: named only if the user named them, else `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`.
  7. **Facts I need** — ask once, in one list: users affected, whether data was exposed and whether it is regulated, exact start and detection times, system name; until answered they stay unknown and escalate.
- **No incident facts at all** ("we had an AI incident, give me the runbook"): ask once for category, start time, users affected, data exposed, regulated data (yes/no/unknown) and owners; do not guess a severity.
- **Asked to assume it's fine or keep severity low**: decline in one line — unknown regulated status or exposure escalates. Show the severity the matrix gives (e.g. prompt injection with regulated status unknown → SEV2 via D03), keep the regulator track, and leave users, detection time and owners as TBD markers. A supplied matrix in which no row fires is rejected; ask for a baseline row rather than guessing a severity.

## Starting points
- **New** — no runbook or severity policy yet: bring the incident facts; the skill classifies with its documented default matrix (and says so) and assembles the runbook.
- **Existing** — bring the incident facts and your team's own severity matrix; every row of your matrix is evaluated, the fired rules are listed, and a matrix with no baseline row fails the run instead of guessing.

## When to use
- A live AI incident: hallucination, data leak, prompt injection, outage, cost spike or harmful output.
- Classifying severity consistently and showing why; producing the comms checklist and the postmortem skeleton.
- NOT for: legal advice on notification duties (route to counsel), detection and SLO alerting (`llm-observability`), pre-launch risk review (`ai-governance-risk`), turning feedback into fixes (`feedback-improvement-loop`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `incident` CSV: `category`, `started_at` | yes | incident commander |
| `users_affected`, `data_exposed`, `regulated_data` (yes/no/unknown) | no — missing = unknown, and unknown escalates | incident commander, privacy |
| `detected_at`, `detected_by`, `system_name`, `summary` | no | alert or report |
| `owner_<role>`: incident_commander, engineering_lead, comms_lead, legal_privacy, security_lead | no — missing = TBD with the accountable role | on-call rota |
| `matrix` CSV (rule_id, conditions, severity, reason) | no | your incident policy; default = the skill's documented matrix |

If `incident` is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. No time, name or count is invented.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Fill `assets/incident-template.csv` with what is known now; leave unknowns as `unknown`.
3. Run the skill. The script evaluates every matrix row (`references/severity-matrix.md`), takes the most severe, and lists every fired row as reasoning.
4. It loads `assets/playbooks/<category>.md` into Containment (contain, eradicate) and Recovery (recover, verify).
5. It builds the timeline from `started_at` / `detected_at` only; later events are TBD for the Incident commander.
6. Communications: internal always; customer unless `users_affected = 0`; regulator only when `regulated_data` is yes or unknown, with Legal / privacy confirming obligations.
7. Re-run as facts change (unknown → yes/no); severity can go down only with evidence.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `runbook.md`: Severity (fired rules, facts, unknowns), Immediate actions (+ Timeline), Containment, Recovery, Communications (internal, customer, regulator), Postmortem (fields and action items).
- `incident.json`: the same record, machine-readable.

## Self-check
- [ ] Severity shows every fired row and the matrix source (supplied or the skill's default)
- [ ] Unknown data/regulated status escalated, not assumed away
- [ ] Regulator track present only for regulated yes/unknown; no deadlines invented
- [ ] Timeline holds only supplied times; the rest TBD with an owner role
- [ ] Every owner named or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`
- [ ] Postmortem action items include a regression eval case and the missing alert

## References
- `references/severity-matrix.md` — the default matrix, method, comms rule
- `references/severity-matrix.default.csv` — machine copy of the default matrix
- `assets/playbooks/` — per-category playbooks (contain, eradicate, recover, verify)
- `assets/incident-template.csv` — input layout
- `scripts/runbook.py` — the classifier and runbook builder (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-incident-runbook --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-incident-runbook`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`runbook.md`, `incident.json`). A severity matrix in which no row fires fails the run (exit 1) on purpose.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AI incident runbook: incident facts + severity matrix -> classified runbook and incident record.

Classifies severity (SEV1 highest .. SEV4) by evaluating every row of the severity matrix and
taking the most severe row that fires; every fired row is listed as reasoning. Without --matrix
the skill's documented default matrix is used (references/severity-matrix.default.csv; see
references/severity-matrix.md) and the output says so. Assembles the runbook from the bundled
per-category playbook (assets/playbooks/<category>.md: Contain, Eradicate, Recover, Verify), a
timeline skeleton anchored on started_at, a communications checklist (regulator track only when
regulated_data is yes or unknown — unknown escalates), and a postmortem skeleton.
Unknowns stay `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`; no time or name is invented.

Usage:
  python3 -I runbook.py --incident incident.csv [--matrix severity-matrix.csv] --out-dir OUT

Incident CSV key,value. Required: category (hallucination|data-leak|prompt-injection|outage|
cost-spike|harmful-output), started_at (ISO 8601). Optional: system_name, summary,
users_affected (integer or unknown), data_exposed (yes|no|unknown), regulated_data
(yes|no|unknown), detected_at, detected_by, owner_incident_commander, owner_engineering_lead,
owner_comms_lead, owner_legal_privacy, owner_security_lead. Missing yes/no fields are unknown.
Matrix CSV: rule_id,conditions,severity,reason. conditions = `always` or `;`-joined clauses
`field=value`, `field!=value`, `field>=n`, `field>n`, `field<=n`, `field<n`, `field in a|b`
(all must hold). Numeric clauses never fire on unknown.

Outputs (in --out-dir): runbook.md (Severity, Immediate actions, Containment, Recovery,
Communications, Postmortem), incident.json.
Exit codes: 0 written · 1 no matrix row fired (matrix lacks a baseline row) or playbook missing ·
2 missing/invalid required input. Stdlib only; no network; writes only inside --out-dir.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import io
import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEFAULT_MATRIX = SKILL_DIR / "references" / "severity-matrix.default.csv"
PLAYBOOKS = SKILL_DIR / "assets" / "playbooks"
CATEGORIES = ("hallucination", "data-leak", "prompt-injection", "outage", "cost-spike", "harmful-output")
TRISTATE = ("yes", "no", "unknown")
SEVERITIES = ("SEV1", "SEV2", "SEV3", "SEV4")
ROLES = {  # role key -> (display name, role accountable for naming the person when missing)
    "incident_commander": ("Incident commander", "On-call engineering manager"),
    "engineering_lead": ("Engineering lead", "Incident commander"),
    "comms_lead": ("Comms lead", "Incident commander"),
    "legal_privacy": ("Legal / privacy", "Incident commander"),
    "security_lead": ("Security lead", "Incident commander"),
}
CLAUSE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([a-z_]+)\s*(>=|<=|!=|=|>|<| in )\s*(.+?)\s*$")


class InputError(Exception):
    """Missing or invalid required input -> exit 2."""


def tbd(role: str) -> str:
    return f"[TO BE BASELINED — owner: {role}]"


def read_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        raise InputError(f"input file not found: {path}")
    lines = [ln for ln in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if not ln.lstrip().startswith("#")]
    return [{(k or "").strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items()} for r in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO("\n".join(lines)))]


def parse_ts(v: str) -> datetime:
    s = v.strip()
    if s.endswith("Z"):
        s = s[:-1] + "+00:00"
    dt = datetime.fromisoformat(s)
    return dt if dt.tzinfo else dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def load_incident(path: Path) -> dict:
    rows = read_rows(path)
    if rows and ("key" not in rows[0] or "value" not in rows[0]):
        raise InputError("incident CSV needs columns key,value")
    inc = {r["key"]: r["value"] for r in rows if r.get("key") and r.get("value", "") != ""}
    missing = [k for k in ("category", "started_at") if k not in inc]
    if missing:
        raise InputError(f"incident missing required keys: {', '.join(missing)}")
    inc["category"] = inc["category"].lower()
    if inc["category"] not in CATEGORIES:
        raise InputError(f"category must be one of {CATEGORIES}, got {inc['category']!r}")
    for k in ("data_exposed", "regulated_data"):
        inc[k] = inc.get(k, "unknown").lower()
        if inc[k] not in TRISTATE:
            raise InputError(f"{k} must be yes|no|unknown, got {inc[k]!r}")
    ua = inc.get("users_affected", "unknown").lower()
    if ua != "unknown" and not ua.isdigit():
        raise InputError(f"users_affected must be a whole number or unknown, got {ua!r}")
    inc["users_affected"] = ua
    for k in ("started_at", "detected_at"):
        if k in inc:
            try:
                parse_ts(inc[k])
            except ValueError:
                raise InputError(f"{k} is not an ISO 8601 timestamp: {inc[k]!r}") from None
    return inc


def load_matrix(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    rows = read_rows(path)
    if not rows:
        raise InputError(f"severity matrix has no rows: {path}")
    for col in ("rule_id", "conditions", "severity", "reason"):
        if col not in rows[0]:
            raise InputError(f"severity matrix needs columns rule_id,conditions,severity,reason (missing {col})")
    for r in rows:
        if r["severity"].upper() not in SEVERITIES:
            raise InputError(f"rule {r['rule_id']}: severity must be one of {SEVERITIES}")
        r["severity"] = r["severity"].upper()
        for clause in split_conditions(r["conditions"]):
            if clause != "always" and not CLAUSE_RE.match(clause):
                raise InputError(f"rule {r['rule_id']}: cannot parse condition {clause!r}")
    return rows


def split_conditions(cond: str) -> list[str]:
    return [c.strip() for c in cond.split(";") if c.strip()]


def clause_holds(clause: str, inc: dict) -> bool:
    if clause == "always":
        return True
    field, op, val = CLAUSE_RE.match(clause).groups()
    op = op.strip()
    actual = str(inc.get(field, "unknown")).lower()
    if op == "in":
        return actual in [v.strip().lower() for v in val.split("|")]
    if op in ("=", "!="):
        return (actual == val.lower()) == (op == "=")
    try:
        a, b = float(actual), float(val)
    except ValueError:
        return False  # numeric clause on unknown/non-numeric never fires
    return {">=": a >= b, ">": a > b, "<=": a <= b, "<": a < b}[op]


def classify(inc: dict, matrix: list[dict]) -> tuple[str | None, list[dict]]:
    fired = [r for r in matrix if all(clause_holds(c, inc) for c in split_conditions(r["conditions"]))]
    fired = [{"rule_id": r["rule_id"], "conditions": r["conditions"], "severity": r["severity"], "reason": r["reason"]}
             for r in fired]
    if not fired:
        return None, []
    return min((r["severity"] for r in fired), key=SEVERITIES.index), fired


def load_playbook(category: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    path = PLAYBOOKS / f"{category}.md"
    if not path.is_file():
        return {}
    sections: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    current = None
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("## "):
            current = line[3:].strip().lower()
            sections[current] = []
        elif current and line.strip().startswith(("- ", "1.", "2.", "3.", "4.", "5.", "6.", "7.", "8.", "9.")):
            sections[current].append(re.sub(r"^\s*(-|\d+\.)\s*", "", line).strip())
        elif current == "references" and line.strip():
            sections[current].append(line.strip())
    return sections


def owners(inc: dict) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {name: inc.get(f"owner_{key}") or tbd(fallback) for key, (name, fallback) in ROLES.items()}


def build(inc: dict, matrix: list[dict], matrix_source: str) -> dict:
    sev, fired = classify(inc, matrix)
    pb = load_playbook(inc["category"])
    own = owners(inc)
    ic = own["Incident commander"]
    started = parse_ts(inc["started_at"])
    timeline = [{"event": "Incident started (impact began)", "time": started.isoformat(), "source": "started_at"}]
    ttd = None
    if inc.get("detected_at"):
        det = parse_ts(inc["detected_at"])
        ttd = round((det - started).total_seconds() / 60.0, 1)
        timeline.append({"event": f"Detected by {inc.get('detected_by', tbd('Incident commander'))}",
                         "time": det.isoformat(), "source": "detected_at"})
    else:
        timeline.append({"event": f"Detected by {inc.get('detected_by', tbd('Incident commander'))}",
                         "time": tbd("Incident commander"), "source": "not supplied"})
    for ev in ("Incident commander assigned and acknowledged", "Containment in place", "Eradication complete",
               "Service recovered", "Verification passed; incident resolved", "Postmortem review held"):
        timeline.append({"event": ev, "time": tbd("Incident commander"), "source": "to record"})

    ua = inc["users_affected"]
    reg = inc["regulated_data"]
    comms = {
        "internal": [f"Open the incident channel and post severity {sev or 'unclassified'} with the fired rules",
                     "Notify the system owner and the engineering on-call"]
                    + (["Notify the executive sponsor (SEV1/SEV2)"] if sev in ("SEV1", "SEV2") else [])
                    + [f"Status updates on the cadence the Incident commander sets: {tbd('Incident commander')}"],
        "customer": ([] if ua == "0" else
                     ["Decide whether affected users/customers are notified; record the decision and who made it",
                      "Draft the customer message (what happened, what data, what we did, what they should do)",
                      f"Approver for customer messages: {own['Comms lead']}"]),
        "regulator": [],
        "regulator_basis": "",
    }
    if reg in ("yes", "unknown"):
        comms["regulator"] = [
            "Legal / privacy confirms which notification obligations apply (e.g. GDPR Article 33, sector or state "
            "breach rules) and their deadlines — the skill does not set them",
            "Preserve evidence: affected records, access logs, traces, prompts and outputs for the window",
            f"Regulator notification owner: {own['Legal / privacy']}",
        ]
        comms["regulator_basis"] = ("regulated_data = yes" if reg == "yes" else
                                    "regulated_data = unknown — unknown escalates: treat as regulated until Legal / privacy rules it out")
    else:
        comms["regulator_basis"] = "regulated_data = no — no regulator track"

    unknowns = [k for k in ("users_affected", "data_exposed", "regulated_data") if inc[k] == "unknown"]
    unknowns += [k for k in ("detected_at", "detected_by", "system_name") if not inc.get(k)]
    return {
        "incident": {k: v for k, v in inc.items() if not k.startswith("owner_")},
        "severity": sev,
        "fired_rules": fired,
        "matrix_source": matrix_source,
        "playbook": {"category": inc["category"], "sections": pb},
        "time_to_detect_min": ttd,
        "timeline": timeline,
        "communications": comms,
        "owners": own,
        "unknowns": unknowns,
        "incident_commander": ic,
    }


def bullets(items: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return [f"- [ ] {x}" for x in items] if items else ["- (none)"]


def render(rec: dict) -> str:
    inc, own, pb = rec["incident"], rec["owners"], rec["playbook"]["sections"]
    title = inc.get("system_name") or tbd("Incident commander")
    L = [f"# Incident runbook — {title} — {inc['category']}", "",
         f"Summary: {inc.get('summary') or tbd('Incident commander')}", "",
         "## Severity", "",
         f"**{rec['severity']}** — most severe of the rows that fired. Matrix: {rec['matrix_source']}.", "",
         "| Rule | Conditions | Severity | Reason |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in rec["fired_rules"]:
        L.append(f"| {r['rule_id']} | `{r['conditions']}` | {r['severity']} | {r['reason']} |")
    L += ["", "| Fact | Value |", "|---|---|"]
    for k in ("category", "users_affected", "data_exposed", "regulated_data", "started_at", "detected_at", "detected_by"):
        L.append(f"| {k} | {inc.get(k) or tbd('Incident commander')} |")
    if rec["unknowns"]:
        L += ["", "Unknown now (each resolves to a fact, not a guess): " + ", ".join(rec["unknowns"]) + "."]
    L += ["", "## Immediate actions", "",
          f"- [ ] Incident commander: {own['Incident commander']} — acknowledge and own the timeline",
          f"- [ ] Engineering lead: {own['Engineering lead']} — join and take the playbook below",
          "- [ ] Freeze deploys and prompt/config changes to the affected system except fixes for this incident",
          "- [ ] Preserve evidence: traces, prompts, outputs, retrieval logs and config versions for the window"]
    if rec["severity"] in ("SEV1", "SEV2"):
        L.append(f"- [ ] Security lead: {own['Security lead']} — engaged for {rec['severity']}")
    L += ["", "### Timeline", "", "| Event | Time | Source |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for t in rec["timeline"]:
        L.append(f"| {t['event']} | {t['time']} | {t['source']} |")
    if rec["time_to_detect_min"] is not None:
        L += ["", f"Time to detect (detected_at − started_at): {rec['time_to_detect_min']} minutes."]
    L += ["", "## Containment", "", "### Contain", ""] + bullets(pb.get("contain", []))
    L += ["", "### Eradicate", ""] + bullets(pb.get("eradicate", []))
    L += ["", "## Recovery", "", "### Recover", ""] + bullets(pb.get("recover", []))
    L += ["", "### Verify", ""] + bullets(pb.get("verify", []))
    c = rec["communications"]
    L += ["", "## Communications", "", "### Internal", ""] + bullets(c["internal"])
    L += ["", "### Customer", ""] + (bullets(c["customer"]) if c["customer"] else ["- Not required: users_affected = 0."])
    L += ["", "### Regulator", "", f"Basis: {c['regulator_basis']}.", ""]
    L += bullets(c["regulator"]) if c["regulator"] else ["- Not required."]
    L += ["", "## Postmortem", "",
          "Blameless; held after resolution. Fill from the timeline and evidence, not memory.", "",
          f"| Field | Value |", "|---|---|",
          f"| Owner | {own['Incident commander']} |",
          f"| Review date | {tbd('Incident commander')} |",
          f"| Severity (final) | {rec['severity']} (confirm or revise with evidence) |",
          f"| Impact (users, data, duration) | {tbd('Incident commander')} |",
          f"| Root cause | {tbd('Engineering lead')} |",
          f"| Contributing factors | {tbd('Engineering lead')} |",
          f"| Detection gap (time to detect) | {str(rec['time_to_detect_min']) + ' minutes' if rec['time_to_detect_min'] is not None else tbd('Incident commander')} |",
          "", "### Action items", "", "| Action | Type (prevent/detect/mitigate) | Owner | Due |", "|---|---|---|---|",
          f"| Add a regression eval case for this failure (feedback-improvement-loop / llm-eval-harness) | detect | {tbd('Engineering lead')} | {tbd('Engineering lead')} |",
          f"| Add or tighten the alert that should have fired (llm-observability SLO) | detect | {tbd('Engineering lead')} | {tbd('Engineering lead')} |"]
    if pb.get("references"):
        L += ["", "Playbook references: " + " ".join(pb["references"])]
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--incident", type=Path, required=True, help="incident facts CSV (key,value)")
    ap.add_argument("--matrix", type=Path, help="severity matrix CSV; default: the skill's documented default")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        inc = load_incident(args.incident)
        matrix_path = args.matrix or DEFAULT_MATRIX
        source = (f"supplied ({args.matrix.name})" if args.matrix else
                  "the skill's default matrix (references/severity-matrix.default.csv) — no matrix supplied")
        rec = build(inc, load_matrix(matrix_path), source)
    except InputError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (args.out_dir / "incident.json").write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (args.out_dir / "runbook.md").write_text(render(rec), encoding="utf-8")
    if rec["severity"] is None:
        print("no severity-matrix row fired; add a baseline row (conditions: always)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not rec["playbook"]["sections"]:
        print(f"no playbook for category {inc['category']}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"runbook written: {rec['severity']} ({len(rec['fired_rules'])} rule(s) fired)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Playbook — cost-spike (token or inference spend far above plan)

## Contain
- Identify the driver from traces: feature, tenant, model, tokens per request, request volume, retries or agent loops
- Apply caps: per-tenant and per-user rate limits, max tokens, max agent steps, budget alerts at the provider
- Route the driver to a cheaper model or disable the runaway path if caps are not enough

## Eradicate
- Fix the cause: loop or retry bug, prompt growth, context stuffing, abusive client, pricing or model change
- Add guards: step limits, timeouts, idempotent retries with backoff, context-size checks

## Recover
- Remove temporary caps that hurt legitimate users once the fix is live
- Reconcile the spend with the provider invoice; record the excess amount from billing data

## Verify
- Tokens per request and cost per request back within SLO (llm-observability)
- Budget alerts fire in a test before the incident is closed

## References
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025: LLM10 Unbounded Consumption.

# Playbook — data-leak (sensitive data disclosed through the AI system)

## Contain
- Disable the leaking path now: feature flag off, tool or connector revoked, or retrieval source detached
- Revoke and rotate any credentials, tokens or keys that appeared in prompts, outputs or logs
- Restrict access to traces and logs that now contain the leaked data; stop further replication (exports, analytics)

## Eradicate
- Determine the path: retrieval returned data outside the user's entitlement, memory/cache crossed sessions, training or fine-tune data, system prompt, tool output
- Enforce authorization at retrieval and tool level (per-user filters), not in the prompt
- Purge leaked data from caches, vector stores, conversation memory and logs per the retention policy

## Recover
- Restore the feature through a canary with an access-control test suite as a gate
- Complete the affected-records list (who, what data, when) for the notification decision

## Verify
- Access-control tests and red-team prompts for cross-user and cross-tenant retrieval pass
- No further occurrences in traces for the agreed observation window

## References
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025: LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses.

# Playbook — hallucination (incorrect or unsupported output reached users)

## Contain
- Identify the affected feature, prompt version, model version and retrieval index from traces
- Turn on the fallback: route the feature to human review, a safe canned answer, or disable it behind its flag
- Add a temporary output guardrail for the failing pattern (block or flag answers without citations)

## Eradicate
- Reproduce with the exact inputs from the traces; classify the cause: retrieval miss, stale source, prompt regression, model change
- Fix the cause (re-index or correct the source, revert or fix the prompt, pin the previous model version)
- Add the reproducing inputs as regression eval cases before re-enabling

## Recover
- Re-enable the feature through a canary (ai-release-plan) with the regression cases as a gate
- Correct or retract wrong answers already delivered where the product allows it

## Verify
- Regression cases pass and the full eval suite pass rate has not dropped
- Online eval score and negative feedback rate back within SLO for the agreed window (llm-observability)

## References
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025: LLM09 Misinformation.

# Playbook — harmful-output (toxic, unsafe, biased or policy-violating output reached users)

## Contain
- Disable or restrict the feature for the affected audience; enable the strictest moderation setting available
- Add an output filter for the specific harm pattern and route borderline outputs to human review
- Capture the full context (inputs, retrieved content, outputs) for review by Trust and Safety

## Eradicate
- Determine the cause: jailbreak input, poisoned retrieval content, prompt regression, model change, missing moderation step
- Fix the cause and add the harmful cases (and close variants) to the safety eval and red-team suites

## Recover
- Reach out to affected users where policy requires; remove or correct harmful content still visible
- Re-enable through a canary with the safety suite as a gate

## Verify
- Safety suite and red-team suite pass, including the new cases
- Moderation flags and negative feedback back within SLO for the agreed window

## References
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025: LLM01 Prompt Injection (jailbreaks), LLM05 Improper Output Handling. NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile).

# Playbook — outage (AI feature unavailable or degraded)

## Contain
- Confirm scope from traces: which features, models, providers and regions show errors or latency
- Fail over: secondary model or provider, cached answers, or graceful degradation message
- Shed load if needed: rate limits, queueing, disable non-critical AI features

## Eradicate
- Identify the cause: provider incident, quota or rate limit, expired credential, deploy, dependency (vector store, gateway)
- Fix or roll back (previous deploy, previous model version, restored quota or credential)

## Recover
- Restore primary routing gradually; watch error rate and p95 latency
- Drain queued requests and confirm no duplicate side effects

## Verify
- Error rate and latency within SLO for the agreed window (llm-observability)
- Synthetic checks across all affected features pass

## References
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025: LLM10 Unbounded Consumption (where load-driven).

# Playbook — prompt-injection (direct or indirect instructions hijacked the system)

## Contain
- Disable the injected channel: the tool, connector, document source or input type carrying the payload
- Reduce agency: switch tools with side effects (send, write, pay, delete) to require human approval
- Quarantine the poisoned content (documents, web pages, emails, tickets) from retrieval

## Eradicate
- Trace every action the agent took after the injection; list side effects to reverse
- Separate trusted instructions from untrusted content; enforce least-privilege tool scopes and output handling
- Add the payload and close variants to the red-team suite

## Recover
- Reverse side effects (revoke sent items, roll back writes) and record each reversal
- Re-enable tools one at a time behind a canary with the red-team suite as a gate

## Verify
- Red-team suite including the new payloads passes
- No tool calls outside the allowed scope in traces for the agreed window

## References
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025: LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM05 Improper Output Handling, LLM06 Excessive Agency.

# Severity matrix (the skill's default)

This is **the skill's default matrix**, used only when no `matrix` input is supplied; the runbook
then states "the skill's default matrix". It is a starting point, not an industry standard —
replace it with your organisation's incident policy by passing your own CSV in the same layout.

Machine copy: `references/severity-matrix.default.csv` (`rule_id,conditions,severity,reason`).

## Method
1. Missing `data_exposed` / `regulated_data` / `users_affected` are **unknown**.
2. Every row is evaluated; a row fires when all of its `;`-joined clauses hold.
3. Severity = the most severe fired row (SEV1 > SEV2 > SEV3 > SEV4). All fired rows are listed as the reasoning.
4. Numeric clauses (`users_affected>=100`) never fire on unknown; unknown is handled by explicit rows (D02, D03, D12) so **unknown escalates**.
5. A matrix where no row fires is invalid (exit 1): keep a baseline row with `always`.

# AI Postmortem (blameless, measured, owned)

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-postmortem --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-postmortem`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`postmortem.md`, `timings.json`, `actions.csv`, `eval-cases.csv`). With `strict=true` the run is a gate: it exits 1 when a factor has no action or an action has no owner, and still writes every output so the gaps are visible.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — you bring the facts and timeline of an incident that happened (plus factors and actions when known); the skill measures the timings, checks the actions cover every factor and turns the failure into eval cases.
- Only for existing: a postmortem always concerns an incident that has already happened; a live incident goes to `ai-incident-runbook`.

## When to use
- After an AI incident is mitigated: bad answers at scale, prompt-injection exploit, cost runaway, outage, harmful output, data leak.
- Measuring time to detect, acknowledge, mitigate and resolve from the real timeline, and showing which milestones are missing.
- Closing the loop: every contributing factor has an owned, dated action; failing inputs become regression evals.
- NOT for: responding while the incident is live — severity, containment, comms (`ai-incident-runbook`); alerts and SLOs (`llm-observability`); scoring the eval set (`llm-eval-harness`); legal or HR determinations.

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `incident` — `key,value,source,notes`: `id`, `title`, `started_at` (+ `severity`, `system`, `customer_impact`, `detection_source`, `went_well`) | yes | Incident commander; severity and start time from the `ai-incident-runbook` run | run stops (exit 2), asks once; optional keys become `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Incident commander]` |
| `timeline` — `timestamp,event,description,actor_role` | yes | incident channel, pager, deploy log | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `factors` — `factor,category,evidence` | no | postmortem review meeting | factors TBD for the Incident commander; strict gate fails |
| `actions` — `action,type,owner,due,factor` | no | postmortem review meeting | actions TBD for the Incident commander |
| `strict` — true/false | no | engineering lead | false: gaps reported, run exits 0 |

Write `actor_role` as a role, never a person's name. Mark a failing user input in any description or evidence as `input:"..."` and the bad reply as `output:"..."` so it can become a regression case.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Copy `assets/incident-template.csv`, `assets/timeline-template.csv`, `assets/factors-template.csv` and `assets/actions-template.csv`. Carry `started_at`, `detected_at` and severity over from the `ai-incident-runbook` output.
3. Pick each factor's category from `assets/factor-taxonomy.csv`. Describe systems and processes, not people.
4. Run the skill. `scripts/postmortem.py` computes timings per `references/method.md`, flags missing and out-of-order milestones, links actions to factors and scans for blame phrasing (`assets/blame-phrases.csv`).
5. Fix every flag in the inputs (rewrite blameful text, add owners, link uncovered factors) and re-run until the strict gate passes.
6. Hand `eval-cases.csv` to the Eval lead: fill `must_contain` / `must_not_contain`, then feed it to `llm-eval-harness`.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `postmortem.md` — **Summary**, **Impact**, **Timeline**, **Timings**, **Contributing factors**, **What went well**, **Actions**, **Lessons for the eval set**, **Method** (with the blameless language check).
- `timings.json` — milestones, minutes per measure with basis, flags, coverage and gate result.
- `actions.csv` — `action, type, owner, due, factor, status` (status `open | in-progress | done | blocked: no owner | blocked: no due date`).
- `eval-cases.csv` — proposed regression cases in the `llm-eval-harness` golden-set columns.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every timing traces to two timeline timestamps; missing milestones are flagged, not estimated
- [ ] An incident with no `resolved` event is reported OPEN
- [ ] Every factor has at least one action; every action has an owner and a due date, or a TBD naming the Incident commander
- [ ] Blame-phrase hits rewritten as system or process conditions
- [ ] Eval cases use only inputs quoted in the timeline or factors; scoring left to the Eval lead
- [ ] `--verify` passes on all four outputs
- [ ] Limits stated: word-list blame scan, timeline accuracy, not a legal determination

## References
- `references/method.md` — timing definitions, ordering rules, coverage, eval-case extraction, limits
- `references/sources.md` — blameless postmortem practice (Google SRE book ch. 15, SRE workbook ch. 10), checked 2026-10-18
- `assets/factor-taxonomy.csv` — AI contributing-factor categories
- `assets/blame-phrases.csv` — blame word list with rewrite hints
- `assets/incident-template.csv`, `assets/timeline-template.csv`, `assets/factors-template.csv`, `assets/actions-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/postmortem.py` — builder and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

# Method

## Timings (minutes, one decimal)
| Measure | From | To | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time to detect | incident `started_at` | first `detected` event | |
| Time to acknowledge | first `detected` | first `acknowledged` | |
| Time to mitigate | `started_at` | first `mitigated` | user impact contained |
| Time to resolve | `started_at` | first `resolved` | no `resolved` event = incident OPEN; never inferred |
| Impact duration | `started_at` | first `mitigated` (else first `resolved`) | basis written to `timings.json` |

Rules:
- Timestamps must be ISO 8601 with a timezone. `Z` is accepted.
- A milestone that is absent gives `null` for every measure that needs it, plus a flag. Nothing is estimated.
- Milestones must run `started_at ≤ detected ≤ acknowledged ≤ mitigated ≤ resolved`. Each violation is flagged; a negative interval is reported as `null`.
- Rows listed out of time order in the CSV are flagged and shown sorted. A duplicate milestone is flagged; the first one counts.
- `change` and `note` events may precede `started_at` (a change often causes the incident).

## Factors and coverage
- Factors get ids F1..Fn in row order. `category` must match an id or name in `assets/factor-taxonomy.csv`, or the run stops (exit 2).
- Actions link to factors by id or exact factor text (`;` for several). Coverage = each factor has ≥ 1 linked action.
- Missing owner or due date → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Incident commander]`; status becomes `blocked: no owner` / `blocked: no due date`. Otherwise status is the input `status` (open | in-progress | done) or `open`.

## Strict gate (`--strict`)
Exit 1 when any factor has no action, any action has no owner, or no factors were supplied (coverage cannot be shown). All outputs are still written.

## Regression eval cases (`eval-cases.csv`)
- Columns are exactly the `llm-eval-harness` golden-set columns (`id, category, difficulty, input, expected, must_contain, must_not_contain, expected_json_valid, weight, source, notes`), so the file feeds `build_golden.py` unchanged.
- An input is taken only from an `input:"..."` marker in timeline descriptions or factor text/evidence. An `output:"..."` marker is copied into `notes` as the observed bad output.
- An eval-relevant factor (taxonomy `eval_relevant = yes`) without a marker yields a row whose input is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval lead]`.
- Scoring columns are never invented: `must_contain` / `must_not_contain` stay blank with a TBD note for the Eval lead. `difficulty` is `adversarial` for prompt/guardrail-gap factors, else `medium`; `weight` is 1.

## Blameless language check
Case-insensitive regex scan of title, customer impact, went-well, timeline descriptions and actor roles, factors, evidence and actions against `assets/blame-phrases.csv`. Each hit lists where, the phrase, why it reads as blame and a rewrite hint. It is a word-list scan: it cannot detect personal names or tone, and it does not change the text.

## Limits
- Timings are only as good as the timeline timestamps.
- The skill does not decide root cause; it records the factors the review supplied.
- Not a legal, regulatory or HR determination.

# Sources

Checked 2026-10-18 (WebFetch of the primary pages; short paraphrases only).

| ID | Source | URL | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Google, *Site Reliability Engineering*, Chapter 15 "Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure" (J. Lunney, S. Lueder) | https://sre.google/sre-book/postmortem-culture/ | Blameless postmortems assume everyone acted with good intentions and focus on fixing systems and processes, not people; a blame atmosphere hides incidents. Postmortem triggers include user-visible degradation, data loss, on-call intervention (rollback), long resolution time and monitoring failure. |
| S2 | Google, *The Site Reliability Workbook*, Chapter 10 "Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure" | https://sre.google/workbook/postmortem-culture/ | Blameful language stifles collaboration; every action item has an owner and a tracking number; an action set that is mostly mitigative should add preventative items. |

## How the skill uses them
- **Blameless check** (S1, S2): `assets/blame-phrases.csv` is this skill's word list of phrasing that assigns fault to a person or uses hindsight judgement. The list is the skill's own; the principle comes from S1 and S2.
- **Owned actions** (S2): an action without an owner is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Incident commander]` and fails the `--strict` gate.
- **Prevent / detect / mitigate / process** (S2): the action mix is reported; zero prevent actions is called out.

# AI Release Plan (staged rollout)

## In a conversation: write the release plan now
The reply **is the release plan**: its first line is `Readiness: READY / NOT READY / PENDING GATES — <the gates or facts that decided it>`, never only a request for CSVs.
- **The request gives release facts** (scores, risk tier, traffic — e.g. "offline evals 93%, red-team 98%, medium risk, ~48k requests a day"), or says facts and gates are attached but they are not in the conversation: write the plan **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **Readiness** — gates come only from the owner; with none supplied, measured values are listed as "measured, gate threshold `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]`" and readiness is PENDING GATES. Never propose default thresholds.
  2. **Stages** — offline eval → shadow (100 % mirrored, not served) → canary steps → GA. Canary steps by risk tier are **the skill's policy** (`references/rollout-policy.md`), say so: low 10, 50 %; **medium 5, 25, 50 %**; high 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 % (owner may override with `canary_steps`). Table: `stage | traffic % | served | min hours | owner`.
  3. **Minimum durations** — `hours = ceil(min_observed_requests ÷ (daily_requests × traffic% ÷ 100 ÷ 24))`, using the stated daily_requests; `min_observed_requests` is the owner's confidence choice, so show the formula and per-stage requests/hour (48,000/day at 5 % = 100/hour) and keep hours `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]` until the owner sets it. Offline eval and GA have no duration.
  4. **Gates** — `stage | metric | min | max | actual now | status (met / NOT MET / not measured)`; not measured never counts as met.
  5. **Rollback** — every shadow/canary/GA gate becomes a trigger; owner SRE on-call; rollback time as stated or TBD.
  6. **Owners** — Eval lead (offline eval), SRE on-call (shadow, rollback), Release manager (canary), Product owner (GA); any not named is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]`.
  7. **What I need to finish** — ask once for the gates (`stage,metric,min,max` for offline_eval, shadow, canary, ga), `min_observed_requests`, `rollback_time_min` and owner names.
- **A rollout under way** (current stage plus live readings): decide the current stage — ROLL BACK if a gate is not met now, HOLD if a gate is not measured or too few requests were observed, else PROMOTE to the next step — with the Release manager as decision owner and the remaining rollback triggers kept.
- **No facts at all**: ask once for system name, risk tier, measured metrics, daily requests and the gates; do not invent any.
- **Asked to use "standard" gates or mark ready despite a failed gate** ("eval came in at 82% but mark us ready"): decline in one line — thresholds come only from the owner and a blocked first stage is NOT READY. Write the plan with the blocker (e.g. eval_pass_rate NOT MET) shown; never print the requested READY status or a made-up threshold.

## Starting points
- **New** — first rollout of a release: bring the release facts and the owner's gate thresholds; the skill builds offline eval → shadow → canary → GA, checks the first-stage gates now and sizes each stage.
- **Existing** — a rollout already under way: add `current_stage`, the requests observed there and the live metric readings; the plan shows where you are and decides PROMOTE, HOLD or ROLL BACK for the current stage against the same gates.

## When to use
- A model, prompt, agent or RAG change is about to reach users and needs shadow → canary → GA with explicit gates.
- "Are we ready?" — evaluate the owner's gates against the measured facts now.
- NOT for: building the eval set or scoring it (`llm-eval-harness`), risk tiering (`ai-governance-risk`), pipeline wiring (`ci-cd-vercel-github`), live monitoring after GA (`llm-observability`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `facts` CSV `key,value`: `system_name`, `risk_tier` (low/medium/high) | yes | release owner; tier from `ai-governance-risk` |
| Measured metrics named by gates (e.g. `eval_pass_rate`, `redteam_pass_rate`, `latency_p95_ms`, `error_rate`) | for gate status | eval run, red-team run, staging telemetry |
| `daily_requests`, `min_observed_requests` | for durations | traffic forecast; owner's confidence target |
| `rollback_time_min`, `owner_<role>` (eval_lead, sre_oncall, release_manager, product_owner) | no | owner; missing → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]` |
| `current_stage` (stage id, e.g. `canary_1`), `current_stage_observed_requests` | only for a rollout under way | release manager; live telemetry — metric facts are then the live readings |
| `gates` CSV `stage,metric,min,max` (stage ∈ offline_eval, shadow, canary, ga) | yes | release owner — the skill never supplies a threshold |

If `facts` or `gates` is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. Missing optional facts stay TBD with an owner role; nothing is invented.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Copy `assets/release-facts.csv` and `assets/release-gates.csv`; the owner fills measured values and thresholds (with sources).
3. Run the skill. The script builds the stage list from `references/rollout-policy.md` (canary steps by risk tier — the skill's policy, owner-overridable via `canary_steps`).
4. It evaluates every gate against the facts now (`references/gate-method.md`): met / NOT MET / not measured; `not measured` never counts as met.
5. It computes minimum shadow/canary durations: `ceil(min_observed_requests ÷ (daily_requests × traffic% ÷ 24))` hours.
6. It turns every live-stage gate into a rollback trigger and assigns an owner per step.
7. Exit 1 if any `offline_eval` gate is not met or none was supplied; report the blockers, do not soften them.
   With `current_stage` set it also decides the current stage: ROLL BACK (a gate not met now; exit 1), HOLD (a gate not measured, no gate, or too few requests observed) or PROMOTE to the next stage (COMPLETE at GA).
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `release-plan.md`: Readiness, Stages (traffic %, served, min hours, owner), Gates (threshold, actual now, status, source), Rollback (owner, time, triggers), Owners.
- `gates.json`: the same plan, machine-readable (`first_stage_ready`, `stages`, `gates`, `rollback_triggers`, `owners`, `current` — null unless a rollout is under way).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every gate threshold came from the gates CSV; none defaulted
- [ ] `not measured` gates are shown as such, never as met
- [ ] Canary steps state their basis (tier policy or owner override)
- [ ] Durations trace to `daily_requests` and `min_observed_requests`, or are TBD with an owner
- [ ] Every rollback trigger maps to a gate; rollback owner named or TBD with role
- [ ] Exit 1 when the first stage is blocked

## References
- `references/rollout-policy.md` — stage sequence, canary steps per risk tier (skill policy), owner per step
- `references/gate-method.md` — gate statuses, duration formula, rollback triggers
- `assets/release-facts.csv`, `assets/release-gates.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/release_plan.py` — the planner (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-release-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-release-plan`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`release-plan.md`, `gates.json`). A first-stage gate that is not met fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the plan is still written so the blockers are visible.
