# Gate evaluation and duration method

## Gates
Each gate row is `stage, metric, min, max`. A gate is **met** when the fact named by `metric` is
numeric and `min <= actual <= max` (an empty bound is not checked). Status values:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| met | fact present and within bounds |
| NOT MET | fact present and outside bounds |
| not measured | no numeric fact for the metric yet — never treated as met |

Gates are evaluated **now**, from the facts supplied. Only the first stage (`offline_eval`) blocks
the run: if any `offline_eval` gate is not met, or no `offline_eval` gate exists, the script still
writes the plan and exits 1. Later-stage gates are re-evaluated with live metrics during rollout.

## Minimum stage duration
```
hours = ceil( min_observed_requests / (daily_requests × traffic_pct / 100 / 24) )
```
Shadow uses 100 % (mirrored traffic). Offline eval and GA have no duration (sign-off gates).
Missing `daily_requests` or `min_observed_requests` → duration `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]`.
The request count is an owner input chosen for statistical confidence; the skill does not pick it.

Worked example (fictional fixture): 2,000 requests at 48,000/day on a 5 % canary →
48,000 × 0.05 / 24 = 100 requests/hour → 20 hours.

## Rollback triggers
Every gate on `shadow`, `canary` or `ga` becomes a trigger: `metric > max` or `metric < min` while
that stage is live → stop the stage (shadow) or roll back (served stages). `rollback_time_min` is
reported as stated; if absent it is TBD with the Release manager.

# Rollout policy (the skill's policy)

This is **the skill's policy**, not an industry standard. It fixes the *shape* of the rollout by
risk tier; the *thresholds* (gates) always come from the release owner's gates CSV and are never
defaulted.

## Stage sequence
| Order | Stage | Traffic | Served to users | Leaves the stage when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Offline eval | none (eval set) | no | every `offline_eval` gate is met and the Eval lead signs off |
| 2 | Shadow | 100 % mirrored | no | `min_observed_requests` observed and every `shadow` gate holds |
| 3..k | Canary steps | policy % below | yes | `min_observed_requests` observed at that % and every `canary` gate holds |
| last | GA | 100 % | yes | every `ga` gate holds; Product owner approves |

## Canary steps by risk tier
| risk_tier | Canary steps (% of live traffic) | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| low | 10, 50 | small blast radius; two observation points |
| medium | 5, 25, 50 | one low-exposure step before a quarter of traffic |
| high | 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 | exposure grows slowly; each step must observe the same request count |

Override: an owner may set the `canary_steps` fact (ascending percentages, e.g. `1;5;25`); the plan
then states "canary_steps fact (owner override)" as the basis.

## Owner per step
| Step | Accountable role | Fact key |
|---|---|---|
| Offline eval | Eval lead | `owner_eval_lead` |
| Shadow | SRE on-call | `owner_sre_oncall` |
| Canary steps | Release manager | `owner_release_manager` |
| GA | Product owner | `owner_product_owner` |
| Rollback | SRE on-call | `owner_sre_oncall` |

A missing owner is written `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Release manager]`: the Release manager is
accountable for naming one before the stage starts.

## Related public practice (by name)
- Google SRE Workbook, "Canarying Releases" — staged exposure and canary evaluation.
- NIST AI RMF 1.0, *Manage* function — deployment decisions tied to measured risk.

---
name: ai-slo-definition
description: Use when the user needs service-level objectives for an AI feature — "define SLOs for our assistant", "what should our latency and availability targets be", "are we inside our error budget", "set up burn-rate alerts", "quality and cost per request as SLOs". Produces slos.csv, slo-spec.md (Summary, SLIs and objectives, Error budgets, Alerting policy, Method) and slo.json from a request log - availability, latency under threshold, quality pass rate and cost under threshold as SLIs, nearest-rank p50/p95/p99, error budget, budget consumed and multiwindow burn rates per the Google SRE workbook (14.4x / 6x / 1x for 30 days). Without targets it proposes objectives from observed data, each marked to be baselined by the Product owner. Exit 1 when an agreed SLO is breached. Not for live dashboards or trace schemas (llm-observability), distribution drift (drift-monitor) or monthly API cost forecasts (llm-cost-model).
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: ai-platform
  adlc_stage: requirements
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    inputs:
      - {name: log, type: csv, required: true, from: "request log timestamp (ISO-8601), latency_ms, status ok|error, optional quality_pass 0/1, optional cost_usd (layout: assets/log-template.csv)"}
      - {name: targets, type: csv, required: false, from: "agreed targets sli,objective,threshold,window_days (layout: assets/targets-template.csv); without it every objective is a proposal for the Product owner"}
      - {name: system, type: string, required: false, from: "name of the AI feature for the report title"}
    run:
      - {step: slo, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/slo.py --log {log} [--targets {targets}] [--system {system}] --out-dir {out}"}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/slos.csv", checks: [exists, csv:[sli,objective,threshold,observed,budget_consumed,burn_rate,status], "csv_rows:status~^(met|at-risk|breached|proposed)$", "csv_rows:observed~^[01]\\.\\d{5}$", cmd:"python3 -I scripts/slo.py --verify {path}"]}
      - {path: "{out}/slo-spec.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Summary","SLIs and objectives","Error budgets","Alerting policy","Method"], no_unowned_tbd, cmd:"python3 -I scripts/slo.py --verify {path}"]}
      - {path: "{out}/slo.json", checks: [exists, json, contains:"\"verdict\""]}
    modes:
      new:      {case: agent-mode-new, bring: "a few days of request logs from your pilot"}
      existing: {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "the request log from production and your agreed targets"}
---

# AI SLO Definition

## In a conversation: draft the SLO spec now
The reply **is the SLO spec draft**, never only a request for the log. No log rows are in the conversation, so no observed value is printed; every number the log would give is a marker.
- **The request names the feature and says logs exist** ("a week of pilot logs", "here are two days of logs") but no rows are in the conversation: write the spec **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **Summary** — line 1: `Status: proposed — no objective is agreed until the Product owner signs it.` Then how the objectives are set: `scripts/slo.py` is run on the pilot log **without targets** (`python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input log=<pilot-log.csv> --input system="<feature>" --out <dir>`), and each objective is proposed from the observed data.
  2. **SLIs and objectives** — table `sli | good ÷ eligible | proposal rule | objective | threshold | status` for the four SLIs: availability (`status = ok` ÷ every request); latency (ok requests with `latency_ms <= threshold`; failed requests count against availability only); quality (`quality_pass = 1` ÷ labelled rows); cost (`cost_usd <= threshold` ÷ rows with a cost). Proposal rules from `references/method.md`: availability and quality take the highest ladder level not above the observed SLI (availability `0.9 / 0.95 / 0.99 / 0.995 / 0.999 / 0.9995 / 0.9999`; quality `0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.98 / 0.99`); latency threshold = observed nearest-rank p95 of ok requests rounded up to the next 100 ms at objective 0.95; cost threshold = observed p95 cost rounded up to the next 0.001 USD at objective 0.95. Every objective cell reads `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and every status `proposed`; none is called agreed. Without `quality_pass` or `cost_usd` in the log, that SLI is "not measured" with its owner.
  3. **Error budgets** — error budget = 1 − objective; budget consumed = (1 − SLI) ÷ (1 − objective); above 1 is breached. Proposals are never gated; only agreed targets are.
  4. **Alerting policy** — Google SRE workbook multiwindow burn-rate alerts at a 30-day window: fast-burn page 14.4x over 1 h with a 5 m short window (2% of budget); slow-burn page 6x over 6 h / 30 m (5%); ticket 1x over 3 d / 6 h (10%). An alert fires when both windows burn at or above the threshold. The SLO window is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]` until agreed; a pilot shorter than 3 days cannot show the ticket window.
  5. **Method & limits** — nearest-rank percentiles, the log must cover normal traffic, quality depends on labelling; then the next step: take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead, then re-run with the agreed `targets` file (`sli,objective,threshold,window_days`).
- **Agreed targets and a measurement are asked for** ("measure against our targets", "errors spiked — check the SLOs and alerts"): give the same sections with the stated targets as objectives, the observed / consumed / burn columns as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]` until the log is run, and state the gate: consumed above 1 on an agreed SLO is breached and the run exits 1 with every output written; a firing alert on an unbreached SLO is at-risk.
- **No feature and no log mentioned at all**: ask once, in one list, for the request log (`timestamp, latency_ms, status`, optional `quality_pass`, `cost_usd`), any agreed targets, and the feature name. Do not invent latency, availability or cost figures.
- **Asked to "just set sensible SLOs" or to lower an objective so a breach passes**: decline in one line — objectives come from observed data and the Product owner's agreement, not from typical industry numbers, and a breached objective is not lowered to pass the gate without the Product owner. Never print a suggested target number; show `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and the proposal rules above.
- **Distribution drift** ("have our confidence scores shifted since launch?"): that is `drift-monitor`; this skill measures SLIs against objectives.

## Starting points
- **New** — no SLOs yet: bring a pilot request log; every objective is proposed from the observed data and marked for the Product owner to agree.
- **Existing** — bring the production request log and the targets already agreed; the skill measures each SLI against them, computes budget burn and flags breaches.

## When to use
- ADLC requirements stage: turn "it should be fast and reliable" into measurable SLIs, objectives and error budgets before build sign-off.
- Drafting first objectives from a pilot or shadow log: the skill proposes them from observed data for the Product owner to accept or change.
- Checking a release or a week of traffic against agreed targets, and wiring the burn-rate alert policy.
- NOT for: dashboards, trace schemas and live monitoring (`llm-observability`); input or score drift (`drift-monitor`); monthly API spend forecasts (`llm-cost-model`); judging answer quality itself (`llm-eval-harness` produces the `quality_pass` labels).

2. Confirm the log covers normal traffic (ideally several days; the 6 h and 3 d alert windows need that much history).

skills/ai-platform/ai-slo-definition/ref:
# SLO method (what `scripts/slo.py` computes)

## Log
`timestamp, latency_ms, status[, quality_pass][, cost_usd]`. Rows are sorted by timestamp. Timestamps must all carry a UTC offset or all omit it. `status` is `ok` or `error`; `quality_pass` is `0`, `1` or blank; `cost_usd` is a number or blank.

## SLIs (good events ÷ eligible events)
| SLI | Eligible | Good |
|---|---|---|
| availability | every request | `status = ok` |
| latency | ok requests with a latency | `latency_ms <= threshold` |
| quality | rows with `quality_pass` | `quality_pass = 1` |
| cost | rows with `cost_usd` | `cost_usd <= threshold` |

Latency counts ok requests only: failed requests already count against availability, and fast failures would flatter latency.

## Error budget, consumption, burn rate
- Error budget `= 1 − objective`.
- Budget consumed `= (1 − SLI) / (1 − objective)` over the whole log — equal to the burn rate over the log span. It is the share of the window's budget used if the log is representative of the SLO window. `> 1` is **breached** (gate, exit 1).
- Budget spent to date `= consumed × log span ÷ SLO window` (shown when `window_days` is given).
- Window burn rate `= (bad ÷ eligible in the window) / (1 − objective)`, windows `(T − w, T]` ending at the last log timestamp `T`. A window the log does not cover (first timestamp later than `T − w`) or with no eligible events is `n/a`.
- `burn_rate` in `slos.csv` is the last-1 h window; every window is in `slo.json` and the Alerting policy section.
- All ratios are exact fractions (no float rounding at the `> 1` boundary); outputs round half-up (observed 5 dp, consumed and burn 3 dp).

## Alerting policy (SRE workbook table 5-8, see `references/sources.md`)
| Alert | Long / short window | Budget share | Threshold at 30 days |
|---|---|---|---|
| fast-burn page | 1 h / 5 m | 2% | 14.4 |
| slow-burn page | 6 h / 30 m | 5% | 6 |
| ticket | 3 d / 6 h | 10% | 1 |

Threshold = share × window_days × 24 ÷ long-window hours. An alert fires when both the long and the short window burn at or above it. Any firing alert on an agreed SLO that is not breached makes it **at-risk**. Without `window_days` the 30-day reference is used and the window is marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]`.

## Proposals (no target for an SLI)
- availability / quality: highest level on the ladder not above the observed SLI (availability `0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.995, 0.999, 0.9995, 0.9999`; quality `0.8, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95, 0.98, 0.99`). None fits → objective `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`.
- latency: threshold = observed nearest-rank p95 of ok requests rounded up to the next 100 ms; objective 0.95.
- cost: threshold = observed p95 cost rounded up to the next 0.001 USD; objective 0.95.
- Status `proposed`, note `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`. Proposals are never gated: they describe current behaviour, not an agreed commitment.

## Percentiles
Nearest-rank: sort ascending, take the value at rank `ceil(p/100 × n)` (1-based). No interpolation, so the result is always an observed value.

## Worked example (eval fixture, hand-checked)
480 requests one minute apart (00:00–07:59). Errors at i = 7, 207, 407; `quality_pass = 0` when i mod 25 = 3 (20 rows); latency = 800 + (37·i mod 900); cost = 0.0020 + 0.0001·(i mod 10).
- availability: 477/480 = **0.99375**; objective 0.99 → consumed 0.00625/0.01 = **0.625**; last hour (i ≥ 420) has no error → burn **0.000** → met.
- latency ≤ 1650 ms: 451 of 477 ok requests = **0.94549**; objective 0.9 → consumed (26/477)/0.1 = **0.545**.
- quality: 460/480 = **0.95833**; objective 0.95 → consumed **0.833**; last hour has 3 fails in 60 (i = 428, 453, 478) → burn 0.05/0.05 = **1.000**.
- cost ≤ 0.0028: 432/480 = **0.90000**; objective 0.8 → consumed **0.500**.
- Latency nearest-rank on 477 ok values: p50 rank 239 = **1238 ms**, p95 rank 454 = **1653 ms** → proposed threshold **1700 ms**.

# Sources (checked 2026-10-18)

| Item | Source | What it supports |
|---|---|---|
| Burn rate definition | Google SRE workbook, ch. 5 "Alerting on SLOs" — https://sre.google/workbook/alerting-on-slos/ | "Burn rate is how fast, relative to the SLO, the service consumes the error budget." A burn rate of 1 spends exactly the budget over the SLO window. |
| Multiwindow, multi-burn-rate thresholds | same page, Table 5-8 "Recommended parameters for a 99.9% SLO alerting configuration" | Page: 1 h long / 5 m short window, burn rate 14.4, 2% of budget consumed. Page: 6 h / 30 m, burn rate 6, 5%. Ticket: 3 d / 6 h, burn rate 1, 10%. |
| Short window length | same page | Guideline: the short window is 1/12 of the long window. |
| Threshold formula | same page (worked examples use a 30-day SLO period) | Budget consumed by the time an alert fires = burn rate × alert window ÷ SLO period; so 14.4 × 1 h ÷ 720 h = 2%. The script inverts this: threshold = budget share × window hours ÷ long-window hours, which reproduces 14.4 / 6 / 1 for 30 days and scales them for other `window_days`. |

Short paraphrases only; read the workbook for the full reasoning (precision, recall, detection and reset time).

Nearest-rank percentile and the error-budget arithmetic (budget = 1 − objective; consumed = (1 − SLI)/(1 − objective)) are standard definitions and need no external source. The proposal ladders (`0.9 … 0.9999`, `0.8 … 0.99`) and "p95 rounded up" rule are this skill's own convention for drafting objectives; they are labelled proposals and owned by the Product owner.

# AI Strategy & CoE Design

## In a conversation: write the strategy now
The reply **is the deliverable** (or one ask), never only a command. About 1,000 tokens; first line is the answer; tables, not prose.

**Never**
- Never infer maturity from industry averages or invent benchmark figures; a dimension without evidence is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
- Never weight the formula, never rank a row missing any of V, F, D, R, never carry over an earlier score.
- Never schedule scale before measurement exists.

**Which reply**
1. **No current-state evidence** (e.g. "write us an AI strategy, we are a retailer"): ask once, then stop — no scores. Offer this table to fill: `| Input | Your answer |` rows: data platforms · cloud · existing AI/ML in production · AI team and skills · AI policy/governance · strategic priorities (12 months) · executive sponsor and budget envelope · candidate use cases.
2. **Operating-model question only**: answer in tables (≤350 words). Apply `references/operating-models.md`: maturity 1–2 and talent in one team → Central CoE; maturity 2–3, 3+ business units, a platform exists → **Hub-and-spoke**; maturity 4+ with AI engineers in every BU → Federated. Give: `| Model | Verdict | Why |` (chosen + the two rejected); **design decisions** `| Decision | Recommendation |` — reporting line (where the data platform reports, never under one BU), funding (central for platform and lighthouses; chargeback once metered), intake (quarterly review + fast lane), risk gate (tiered: self-certify low, CoE medium, committee high), build vs buy/partner; **precondition: 1–3 AI-capable people per spoke** (talent per spoke) before the hub hands over; **transition triggers** (central → hub-and-spoke: 2+ spokes have trained builders and the platform has self-service onboarding and eval gates; hub-and-spoke → federated: value tracking at level 4, controls tested, spokes pass audits two quarters running).
3. **Full strategy from a description**, in this order: (a) **maturity table** `| Dimension | Score 1–5 | Evidence (from the user's words) |` for all five — data, platform, talent, governance, value — score only what the user's facts support, else `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; (b) **"Overall: Level N (= minimum of the evidenced scores); constraining dimension: X"**; (c) operating model chosen + two rejected with reasons; (d) **portfolio** — one row per idea the user counts (e.g. all 12), columns `V | F | D | R | priority = V×F×D÷R | band`; unnamed or unscored ideas keep their row with axes `[TBD at scoring workshop]` and band "unscored"; (e) governance minimum (intake gate, risk tiers, model inventory, review cadence); (f) **roadmap** `| Quarter | Focus | Exit criterion | Owner |` for Q1–Q4 from `references/roadmap-skeleton.md` (Q1 foundations + 1–2 lighthouses with baselines; Q4 operating-model transition decision); (g) ≤5-bullet executive summary.
4. **Use-case CSV attached but no maturity scorecard**: first line asks once for the **maturity scorecard** (`dimension, score_1_to_5, evidence, gap_to_next_level, owner`; `assets/maturity-scorecard.csv`) — `maturity.py` cannot run without it; maturity stays "pending", not inferred. The ranked portfolio may follow.
5. **Files attached**: name the commands — `python3 -I scripts/score_portfolio.py use-cases.csv --out-dir out --org <org> [--previous previous-portfolio.csv]` → `portfolio.csv`, `unscored.csv`, `portfolio.md`; `python3 -I scripts/maturity.py maturity-scorecard.csv --out-dir out --org <org> --target 3 --default-owner "AI CoE lead"` → `maturity.md`, `roadmap.md` — then show the computed result.

**Portfolio procedure — compute row by row from the CSV; show the working table** (`scripts/score_portfolio.py`)
1. A row with any blank V/F/D/R → **unscored** (`missing score(s): …`), not ranked.
2. score = V×F×D÷R (2 decimals). Sort by score desc, tie → lower id first. rank k = 1..n (n = ranked rows).
3. quartile = ceil(k×4÷n) (n = 9: ranks 1–2 → Q1, 3–4 → Q2, 5–6 → Q3, 7–9 → Q4).
4. Band, first match: **Stop** if V≤2 or F=1 or R=5; **Now** if quartile 1, R≤3, D≥3 and owner and baseline named (else Next, "no owner/baseline"); **Next** if quartile 1 with D≤2 or R>3, or quartile 2; else **Later**. Blank owner/baseline/evidence shows `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI CoE lead]`.
5. With a previous portfolio.csv: movement = previous rank − rank now (`up N` / `down N` / `same`; `new` if absent before); band before → now (e.g. "UC-003 Now → Next"); list ids ranked before that are now unscored or **no longer in the list**. Computed from the two files only.
Working table: `| rank | id | V | F | D | R | score | quartile | band | reason | prev rank/band | movement |`.

**Maturity procedure** (`scripts/maturity.py`): a score without evidence is not a score → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <owner, else AI CoE lead>]`; overall = minimum of the evidenced scores, name the constraining dimension (level names 1 Ad hoc, 2 Emerging, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimizing); gap = below target (default 3) or unevidenced; **one roadmap item per gap**, with owner.

## Starting points
- **New:** a first list of scored AI ideas and a maturity self-assessment give a ranked portfolio, maturity gaps and a quarter roadmap.
- **Existing:** add the `portfolio.csv` from your last review (`previous_portfolio`); the re-ranked portfolio shows each use case's rank and band movement, what is new and what dropped out or lost its scores.

## When to use
- "Build our AI strategy", "stand up an AI CoE", "where are we on AI maturity", "prioritize our AI backlog", "12-month AI roadmap".
- Executive audience: CIO, CDO, CTO, board.
- NOT for: qualifying one idea (`ai-use-case-canvas`), risk/compliance only (`ai-governance-risk`), agent design (`agent-architecture`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Organization context (industry, size, regulatory posture) | yes | user |
| Current-state evidence (data platforms, cloud, existing AI/ML, team) | yes | user / documents |
| Candidate use-case list (even rough) | no | user; skill elicits if missing |
| Executive sponsor and budget envelope | no | user; mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` if absent |
| Strategic priorities for the next 12 months | yes | user / annual plan |

If organization context or current-state evidence is missing, ask once. Do not infer maturity from industry averages.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. **Assess maturity.** Score each of the five dimensions 1–5 using `references/maturity-model.md`. Record evidence per score in `assets/maturity-scorecard.csv`. A score without evidence is `[TO BE BASELINED]`.
3. **Pick the operating model.** Apply the decision table in `references/operating-models.md`. State the chosen model, the two rejected ones, and why. Maturity level and organizational breadth drive this, not preference.
4. **Score the portfolio.** Score every candidate use case on value, feasibility, risk, data readiness (1–5 each) with `references/use-case-scoring.md`; fill `assets/use-case-scoring.csv`. Compute priority = value × feasibility × data readiness ÷ risk. Classify: Now / Next / Later / Stop.
5. **Define governance.** Minimum: intake gate, risk tiering, model inventory, review cadence. Point deeper controls to `ai-governance-risk`.
6. **Build the roadmap.** Use `assets/roadmap.md` with `references/roadmap-skeleton.md`. Q1 is foundations and 1–2 lighthouse use cases; never schedule scale before measurement exists.
7. **Write the executive summary** (≤5 bullets): maturity headline, model choice, top-3 use cases, investment envelope or `[TO BE BASELINED]`, first 90-day commitments.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `ai-strategy-<org>.md`: exec summary, maturity table, operating model, portfolio table, governance, roadmap, risks, next steps (owner + date).
- `maturity-scorecard.csv` and `use-case-scoring.csv` filled.
- Saved to the working directory unless the user names a path.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every maturity score has an evidence line or a `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` marker
- [ ] Operating model choice cites the decision criteria it satisfied
- [ ] Portfolio table has every candidate scored on all four axes; no "high/med/low" without the numeric score
- [ ] Roadmap quarters each have an exit criterion and an owner

- [ ] No invented benchmark figures; industry comparisons carry a source or are omitted

- `references/maturity-model.md` — 5-level model with criteria per dimension
- `references/operating-models.md` — central / hub-and-spoke / federated, when to choose
- `references/use-case-scoring.md` — rubric and formula

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Maturity assessment + roadmap skeleton from a scorecard CSV (assets/maturity-scorecard.csv layout).

    python3 -I scripts/maturity.py maturity-scorecard.csv --out-dir runs/x \
        [--target 3] [--org "Acme"] [--model references/maturity-model.md] [--template assets/roadmap.md]

Input columns: dimension, score_1_to_5|score, evidence, gap_to_next_level, owner, baseline_status.
The `overall_min` row in the asset layout is ignored and recomputed.

Rules (references/maturity-model.md): a score without an evidence line is NOT a score — the
dimension is reported as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <owner, else --default-owner>]`. Overall level = the
minimum of the evidenced scores; the constraining dimension is named. A gap = any dimension
below --target (default 3) or unevidenced. Each gap becomes one roadmap item citing the next
level's criteria from the maturity model.

Writes: maturity.md (level per dimension, overall, gaps) and roadmap.md (assets/roadmap.md with
the Maturity table filled and a "Gap closure items" table, one item per gap). Exit 1 on missing
columns, a score outside 1-5 or no dimension rows. Stdlib only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILL = HERE.parent
DIMS = ["data", "platform", "talent", "governance", "value"]
LEVEL_NAMES = {1: "Ad hoc", 2: "Emerging", 3: "Defined", 4: "Managed", 5: "Optimizing"}


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


# who owns a gap the scorecard leaves unassigned (--default-owner); never a blank owner
FALLBACK = {"owner": "AI CoE lead"}


def own(owner: str) -> str:
    return owner or FALLBACK["owner"]


def tbd(owner: str) -> str:
    return f"[TO BE BASELINED — owner: {own(owner)}]"


def read_scorecard(path: str) -> list[dict]:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    with p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        rows = [{k.strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k} for r in csv.DictReader(f)]
    if not rows:
        die(f"{p.name}: no data rows")
    header = rows[0].keys()
    if "dimension" not in header or not ("score_1_to_5" in header or "score" in header):
        die(f"{p.name}: needs columns dimension and score_1_to_5 (or score)")
    out = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 2):
        dim = r["dimension"].lower()
        if dim == "overall_min" or not dim:
            continue
        raw = r.get("score_1_to_5", r.get("score", ""))
        if raw and raw not in ("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"):
            die(f"row {i} ({dim}): score must be 1-5 or blank, got {raw!r}")
        out.append({"dimension": dim, "score": int(raw) if raw else None, "evidence": r.get("evidence", ""),
                    "gap": r.get("gap_to_next_level", ""), "owner": r.get("owner", "")})
    if not out:
        die("no dimension rows")
    return out


def criteria_from_model(model_path: Path) -> dict[str, dict[int, str]]:
    """{dimension: {level: criteria}} parsed from the '### <Dimension>' tables of the maturity model."""
    out: dict[str, dict[int, str]] = {}
    if not model_path.is_file():
        return out
    current = None
    for line in model_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"^###\s+(\w+)", line)
        if m:
            current = m.group(1).lower()
            out.setdefault(current, {})
            continue
        if current and line.startswith("|"):
            cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip("|").split("|")]
            if len(cells) >= 2 and cells[0].isdigit():
                out[current][int(cells[0])] = cells[1]
    return out


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="maturity scorecard -> maturity.md + roadmap.md skeleton")
    ap.add_argument("scorecard")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--target", type=int, default=3, help="target level; dimensions below it are gaps")
    ap.add_argument("--org", default="<Organization>")
    ap.add_argument("--default-owner", default="AI CoE lead", help="owner of gaps the scorecard leaves unassigned")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=str(SKILL / "references" / "maturity-model.md"))
    ap.add_argument("--template", default=str(SKILL / "assets" / "roadmap.md"))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    FALLBACK["owner"] = a.default_owner.strip() or FALLBACK["owner"]
    if not 1 <= a.target <= 5:
        die("--target must be 1-5")
    rows = read_scorecard(a.scorecard)
    crit = criteria_from_model(Path(a.model))

    for r in rows:
        r["evidenced"] = r["score"] is not None and bool(r["evidence"])
        if r["score"] is not None and not r["evidence"]:
            r["note"] = "score given without evidence — treated as unscored"
        elif r["score"] is None:
            r["note"] = "no score"
        else:
            r["note"] = ""
        r["level"] = f"{r['score']} ({LEVEL_NAMES[r['score']]})" if r["evidenced"] else tbd(r["owner"])
        r["is_gap"] = (not r["evidenced"]) or r["score"] < a.target
        nxt = (r["score"] + 1) if r["evidenced"] and r["score"] < 5 else None
        r["next_criteria"] = crit.get(r["dimension"], {}).get(nxt, "") if nxt else ""

    scored = [r for r in rows if r["evidenced"]]
    unscored = [r for r in rows if not r["evidenced"]]
    missing_dims = [d for d in DIMS if d not in {r["dimension"] for r in rows}]
    if scored:
        low = min(scored, key=lambda r: r["score"])
        overall = f"Level {low['score']} ({LEVEL_NAMES[low['score']]}) overall; constraining dimension: {low['dimension']}"
        if unscored:
            overall += f" — provisional: {len(unscored)} dimension(s) unscored"
    else:
        overall = f"Overall level {tbd('')} — no evidenced score"
    gaps = [r for r in rows if r["is_gap"]]

    L = [f"# AI maturity assessment — {a.org}", "", f"**{overall}.** Target level: {a.target}. "
         f"{len(gaps)} gap(s): {', '.join(r['dimension'] for r in gaps) or 'none'}.", "",
         "## Level per dimension", "| Dimension | Level | Evidence | Gap to next level | Owner | Note |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {r['dimension']} | {r['level']} | {r['evidence'] or tbd(r['owner'])} | "
          f"{r['gap'] or r['next_criteria'] or tbd(r['owner'])} | {own(r['owner'])} | {r['note']} |" for r in rows]
    L += [f"| {d} | {tbd('')} | not in scorecard | | {own('')} | missing row |" for d in missing_dims]
    L += ["", f"## Gaps (dimensions below target {a.target} or unscored)", "| Dimension | Current | Target | Next-level criteria | Owner |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {r['dimension']} | {r['level']} | {a.target} | {r['next_criteria'] or tbd(r['owner'])} | {own(r['owner'])} |"
          for r in gaps] or ["| none | | | | |"]
    L += ["", "Scores and evidence are taken from the scorecard as supplied; plans score at the current level (rule 2). "
          "Unevidenced scores are not counted toward the overall level."]
    out = Path(a.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "maturity.md").write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    tpl_path = Path(a.template)
    if not tpl_path.is_file():
        die(f"template not found: {tpl_path}")
    tpl = tpl_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("<Organization>", a.org)
    by_dim = {r["dimension"]: r for r in rows}
    for d in DIMS:
        r = by_dim.get(d)
        cell = (f"| {d.capitalize()} | {r['level']} | {r['evidence'] or tbd(r['owner'])} | "
                f"{r['gap'] or r['next_criteria'] or tbd(r['owner'])} | {own(r['owner'])} |") if r else \
            f"| {d.capitalize()} | {tbd('')} | not in scorecard | | {own('')} |"
        tpl = re.sub(rf"^\| {d.capitalize()} \|.*$", cell.replace("\\", "\\\\"), tpl, count=1, flags=re.M)
    tpl = tpl.replace("- Maturity: Level <n> overall; constraining dimension: <dimension> (evidence: <line>)",
                      f"- Maturity: {overall}")
    items = ["", "## Gap closure items (one per gap; sequence into the quarter plan)",
             "| # | Dimension | From | To | Exit criterion (next-level criteria) | Owner | Quarter |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for k, r in enumerate(gaps, 1):
        to = (r["score"] + 1) if r["evidenced"] else a.target
        exit_c = r["next_criteria"] or ("baseline the dimension with evidence" if not r["evidenced"] else tbd(r["owner"]))
        items.append(f"| {k} | {r['dimension']} | {r['level']} | {to} | {exit_c} | {own(r['owner'])} | {tbd(r['owner'])} |")
    if not gaps:
        items.append("| — | none | | | | | |")
    tpl = tpl.replace("\n## Assumptions", "\n".join(items) + "\n\n## Assumptions", 1)
    (out / "roadmap.md").write_text(tpl, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"maturity: {overall}; {len(gaps)} gap(s) -> {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rank an AI use-case portfolio from a scoring CSV (assets/use-case-scoring.csv layout).

    python3 -I scripts/score_portfolio.py use-cases.csv --out-dir runs/x [--org "Acme"]
                                          [--previous last-review/portfolio.csv]

Input columns (asset layout; short aliases accepted): id, use_case, business_owner,
value_V|value, feasibility_F|feasibility, data_readiness_D|data_readiness, risk_R|risk,
baseline_metric, evidence|notes. Scores are 1-5.

Formula (references/use-case-scoring.md): priority = V x F x D / R, unweighted unless the
sponsor states a weighting (not supported here on purpose; record it in the notes).
Bands: Stop (V<=2, F=1 or R=5) -> Now (top quartile, R<=3, D>=3, owner + baseline named)
-> Next (second quartile, or top quartile blocked by D<=2 / missing owner or baseline)
-> Later (rest). A row missing any of the four scores is NOT ranked: it goes to the
"unscored" bucket with the missing axes named. Nothing is invented.

Writes: portfolio.csv (ranked rows only, score always filled), unscored.csv (rows that
could not be ranked, with reason), portfolio.md (ranked table, quadrant summary, unscored
list). Exit 1 on missing columns, a score outside 1-5, or no data rows. Stdlib only.

Re-review (--previous): the portfolio.csv of an earlier run (rank, id, band at least). portfolio.csv then
gains previous_rank, previous_band and movement (new | up N | down N | same); portfolio.md gains "Changes since
last review", which also lists ids ranked last time that are now unscored or no longer in the list. Movement is
computed from the two files only; nothing is carried over from the earlier scores.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI CoE lead]"
AXES = {"V": ("value_V", "value"), "F": ("feasibility_F", "feasibility"),
        "D": ("data_readiness_D", "data_readiness"), "R": ("risk_R", "risk")}
OUT_COLS = ["rank", "id", "use_case", "business_owner", "value_V", "feasibility_F", "data_readiness_D",
            "risk_R", "score", "quartile", "band", "band_reason", "baseline_metric", "evidence"]


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def read_rows(path: str) -> list[dict]:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    with p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        rows = [{k.strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k} for r in csv.DictReader(f)]
    if not rows:
        die(f"{p.name}: no data rows")
    header = rows[0].keys()
    for ax, names in AXES.items():
        if not any(n in header for n in names):
            die(f"{p.name}: missing column for {ax} (one of {list(names)})")
    for col in ("id", "use_case"):
        if col not in header:
            die(f"{p.name}: missing column '{col}'")
    return rows


def axis(row: dict, ax: str) -> str:
    for n in AXES[ax]:
        if n in row:
            return row[n]
    return ""


PREV_COLS = ["previous_rank", "previous_band", "movement"]


def read_previous(path: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Earlier portfolio.csv -> {id: {rank, band, use_case}}."""
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"previous portfolio not found: {p}")
    with p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        rows = [{(k or "").strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items()} for r in csv.DictReader(f)]
    if not rows:
        die(f"{p.name}: previous portfolio has no rows")
    for col in ("rank", "id", "band"):
        if col not in rows[0]:
            die(f"{p.name}: previous portfolio needs columns rank,id,band (a portfolio.csv from this script)")
    prev: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 2):
        if not r["rank"].isdigit():
            die(f"{p.name} row {i}: rank must be a whole number, got {r['rank']!r}")
        if r["id"] in prev:
            die(f"{p.name} row {i}: duplicate id {r['id']!r}")
        prev[r["id"]] = {"rank": int(r["rank"]), "band": r["band"], "use_case": r.get("use_case", "")}
    return prev


def movement(now_rank: int, was: dict | None) -> str:
    if was is None:
        return "new"
    d = was["rank"] - now_rank
    return "same" if d == 0 else (f"up {d}" if d > 0 else f"down {-d}")


def quadrant(v: int, f: int) -> str:
    if v >= 3 and f >= 3:
        return "Quick win (V>=3, F>=3)"
    if v >= 3:
        return "Strategic bet (V>=3, F<3)"
    if f >= 3:
        return "Fill-in (V<3, F>=3)"
    return "Avoid (V<3, F<3)"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="use-case scoring CSV -> ranked portfolio (csv + md)")
    ap.add_argument("use_cases", help="CSV in assets/use-case-scoring.csv layout")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--org", default="<Organization>")
    ap.add_argument("--previous", help="portfolio.csv from the last review, to show movement")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    rows = read_rows(a.use_cases)
    prev = read_previous(a.previous) if a.previous else None

    ranked, unscored = [], []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 2):
        scores, missing = {}, []
        for ax in AXES:
            raw = axis(r, ax)
            if raw == "":
                missing.append(ax)
                continue
            if raw not in ("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"):
                die(f"row {i} ({r.get('id') or '?'}): {ax} must be 1-5, got {raw!r}")
            scores[ax] = int(raw)
        rec = {"id": r.get("id", ""), "use_case": r.get("use_case", ""),
               "business_owner": r.get("business_owner", ""),
               "baseline_metric": r.get("baseline_metric", ""),
               "evidence": r.get("evidence") or r.get("notes", "")}
        if missing:
            rec["reason"] = "missing score(s): " + ", ".join(missing)
            unscored.append(rec)
            continue
        rec.update({"value_V": scores["V"], "feasibility_F": scores["F"], "data_readiness_D": scores["D"],
                    "risk_R": scores["R"], "score": round(scores["V"] * scores["F"] * scores["D"] / scores["R"], 2)})
        ranked.append(rec)

    ranked.sort(key=lambda x: (-x["score"], x["id"]))
    n = len(ranked)
    for k, rec in enumerate(ranked, 1):
        rec["rank"] = k
        rec["quartile"] = math.ceil(k * 4 / n) if n else ""
        v, f, d, rr = rec["value_V"], rec["feasibility_F"], rec["data_readiness_D"], rec["risk_R"]
        if v <= 2 or f == 1 or rr == 5:
            rec["band"], rec["band_reason"] = "Stop", "V<=2, F=1 or R=5 (rubric Stop rule)"
        elif rec["quartile"] == 1 and rr <= 3 and d >= 3:
            if rec["business_owner"] and rec["baseline_metric"]:
                rec["band"], rec["band_reason"] = "Now", "top quartile, R<=3, D>=3, owner and baseline named"
            else:
                lack = [x for x, ok in (("owner", rec["business_owner"]), ("baseline", rec["baseline_metric"])) if not ok]
                rec["band"], rec["band_reason"] = "Next", "top quartile but no " + "/".join(lack) + " (rule 2: demote)"
        elif rec["quartile"] == 1 and d <= 2:
            rec["band"], rec["band_reason"] = "Next", "top quartile blocked by D<=2: fund data readiness first"
        elif rec["quartile"] == 1:
            rec["band"], rec["band_reason"] = "Next", "top quartile but R>3: mitigation plan before funding"
        elif rec["quartile"] == 2:
            rec["band"], rec["band_reason"] = "Next", "second quartile"
        else:
            rec["band"], rec["band_reason"] = "Later", f"quartile {rec['quartile']}"
        rec["evidence"] = rec["evidence"] or TBD
        rec["business_owner"] = rec["business_owner"] or TBD
        rec["baseline_metric"] = rec["baseline_metric"] or TBD
        if prev is not None:
            was = prev.get(rec["id"])
            rec["previous_rank"] = was["rank"] if was else ""
            rec["previous_band"] = was["band"] if was else ""
            rec["movement"] = movement(k, was)

    out = Path(a.out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (out / "portfolio.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=OUT_COLS + (PREV_COLS if prev is not None else []), extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(ranked)
    with (out / "unscored.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "use_case", "business_owner", "reason"], extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(unscored)

    L = [f"# AI use-case portfolio — {a.org}", "",
         f"{n} use case(s) ranked by priority = V x F x D / R; {len(unscored)} unscored (missing axes, not ranked)."
         + (" Fewer than 8 candidates scored: the backlog is not fully elicited yet (rubric rule 1)." if n < 8 else ""),
         "", "## Ranked portfolio",
         "| Rank | ID | Use case | Owner | V | F | D | R | Score | Band | Why |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {r['rank']} | {r['id']} | {r['use_case']} | {r['business_owner']} | {r['value_V']} | {r['feasibility_F']} | "
          f"{r['data_readiness_D']} | {r['risk_R']} | {r['score']} | {r['band']} | {r['band_reason']} |" for r in ranked]
    if not ranked:
        L.append("| — | none ranked | | | | | | | | | |")
    L += ["", "## Band summary", "| Band | Count | IDs |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for band in ("Now", "Next", "Later", "Stop"):
        ids = [r["id"] for r in ranked if r["band"] == band]
        L.append(f"| {band} | {len(ids)} | {', '.join(ids) or '—'} |")
    L += ["", "## Quadrant summary (value vs feasibility)", "| Quadrant | Count | IDs |", "|---|---|---|"]
    quads = {}
    for r in ranked:
        quads.setdefault(quadrant(r["value_V"], r["feasibility_F"]), []).append(r["id"])
    for q in ("Quick win (V>=3, F>=3)", "Strategic bet (V>=3, F<3)", "Fill-in (V<3, F>=3)", "Avoid (V<3, F<3)"):
        L.append(f"| {q} | {len(quads.get(q, []))} | {', '.join(quads.get(q, [])) or '—'} |")
    L += ["", "## Unscored (not ranked — score before the next review)", "| ID | Use case | Owner | Missing |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {u['id']} | {u['use_case']} | {u['business_owner'] or TBD} | {u['reason']} |" for u in unscored] \
        or ["| none | | | |"]
    if prev is not None:
        ranked_ids = {r["id"] for r in ranked}
        unscored_ids = {u["id"] for u in unscored}
        band_moves = [r for r in ranked if r["previous_band"] and r["previous_band"] != r["band"]]
        L += ["", "## Changes since last review",
              f"Compared with `{Path(a.previous).name}` ({len(prev)} ranked then, {n} ranked now). "
              f"{sum(1 for r in ranked if r['movement'] == 'new')} new, {len(band_moves)} changed band.", "",
              "| ID | Use case | Rank then | Rank now | Movement | Band then | Band now |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        L += [f"| {r['id']} | {r['use_case']} | {r['previous_rank'] or '—'} | {r['rank']} | {r['movement']} | "
              f"{r['previous_band'] or '—'} | {r['band']} |" for r in ranked]
        for pid, was in sorted(prev.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["rank"]):
            if pid not in ranked_ids:
                status = "now unscored (see Unscored)" if pid in unscored_ids else "no longer in the list"
                L.append(f"| {pid} | {was['use_case']} | {was['rank']} | — | {status} | {was['band']} | — |")
    L += ["", "Scores are taken from the input file as supplied; no axis was inferred. "
          f"Evidence gaps are marked {TBD}."]
    (out / "portfolio.md").write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"portfolio: {n} ranked, {len(unscored)} unscored -> {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# AI Maturity Model — 5 levels × 5 dimensions

Score each dimension independently. Overall maturity = the **lowest** dimension score, not the average; the weakest dimension is the constraint on everything else.

## Levels
| Level | Name | One-line test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ad hoc | Individuals experiment; nothing is repeatable or owned |
| 2 | Emerging | Pilots exist; some ownership; no shared platform or policy |
| 3 | Defined | Standard platform, intake, and policy exist and are used by most teams |
| 4 | Managed | Measured: value, risk, and cost tracked per use case; portfolio decisions are evidence-based |
| 5 | Optimizing | AI is in the operating rhythm; continuous improvement; business owns outcomes, CoE owns enablement |

## Criteria per dimension

### Data
| Level | Criteria (all must hold) |
|---|---|
| 1 | Data in silos; no catalog; access by personal request; quality unknown |
| 2 | Partial catalog; one or two curated domains; lineage absent; PII handling manual |
| 3 | Enterprise catalog with owners; documented quality rules for key domains; access via role; PII classified |
| 4 | Data products with SLAs; lineage automated; quality monitored with alerts; feature/vector stores governed |
| 5 | Data contracts enforced in CI; consumers self-serve; quality and freshness reported to business owners |

### Platform
| Level | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | Laptop notebooks; API keys in personal accounts |
| 2 | Shared cloud project; some model access through a gateway; no environments separation |
| 3 | Approved model gateway with logging; dev/test/prod; CI for AI apps; secret management; one orchestration framework standard |
| 4 | Observability (traces, cost per call, eval scores) in production; prompt/model versioning; canary releases; rate and spend limits per team |
| 5 | Platform as product: SLAs, self-service onboarding, automated eval gates, model routing by cost/quality policy |

### Talent
| Level | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | Enthusiasts only; no roles defined |
| 2 | Small data-science or innovation team; business users untrained |
| 3 | Defined roles (AI engineer, data engineer, product owner, risk reviewer); training path for builders and consumers; hiring plan |
| 4 | Communities of practice; career ladder; business "AI translators" in each major function; vendor/partner strategy |
| 5 | Capability measured and renewed; internal certifications; business leads own AI outcomes in their scorecards |

### Governance
| Level | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | No policy; shadow AI usage unknown |
| 2 | Acceptable-use policy published; no enforcement; no model inventory |
| 3 | Intake and risk tiering; model inventory; human-review rules for high-risk; vendor/data terms reviewed |
| 4 | Controls tested (bias, privacy, security, hallucination); incident process; regulatory mapping (NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act where applicable) |
| 5 | Continuous assurance; audit evidence automated; board-level reporting |

### Value
| Level | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | No business case; "innovation" budget |
| 2 | Pilots with anecdotal benefit; no baseline measured |
| 3 | Each use case has baseline, target, and owner; benefits tracked at portfolio level |
| 4 | Realized value reported quarterly to finance; kill decisions made on evidence; unit economics per use case |
| 5 | AI value embedded in business plans and P&L; portfolio rebalanced on return |

## Scoring rules
1. Score on evidence you were shown or told. Record the evidence line. No evidence → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
2. Do not round up for intent ("we plan to…"). Plans score at the current level.
3. Present as a table: Dimension | Score | Evidence | Gap to next level | Owner.
4. State the overall level as the minimum and name the constraining dimension in the headline.

## Typical gap patterns (diagnostic, not prescriptive)
| Pattern | Usual cause | First move |
|---|---|---|
| Platform 3+, Value 1–2 | Technology-led program | Install baselines and benefit owners before new builds |
| Data 1–2, everything else 3 | Vendor demos drove the roadmap | Pick two data domains and productize them; defer RAG at scale |
| Governance 1, Platform 2 | Shadow AI | Gateway + inventory in 60 days; policy follows |
| Talent 2, Platform 4 | Platform team outran adoption | Enablement, office hours, embedded engineers in two functions |

# AI Operating Models — central CoE, hub-and-spoke, federated

Pick the model from maturity and organizational breadth. The model is expected to change as maturity rises; say so in the roadmap.

## The three models
| Attribute | Central CoE | Hub-and-spoke | Federated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who builds | CoE team builds and runs everything | CoE builds platform, standards, lighthouse cases; business "spokes" build on it | Business units build and run; a thin enablement group sets standards |
| Who owns outcomes | CoE (initially) | Business, with CoE co-ownership for lighthouses | Business |
| Platform | Owned by CoE | Owned by CoE (hub) | Shared services or per-BU |
| Governance | CoE gate on everything | Hub sets policy, spokes self-certify; hub audits | Policy council; BU risk owners |
| Speed to first value | Fast (focused team) | Medium | Slow at first, fast at scale |
| Scale ceiling | Low — the CoE becomes the bottleneck | High | High |
| Talent requirement | 1 strong team | Hub team + 1–3 AI-capable people per spoke | AI-capable people in every BU |
| Risk of shadow AI | Highest (BUs route around the gate) | Medium | Low if standards are strong, high if weak |

## When to choose
| Signal | Choose |
|---|---|
| Overall maturity 1–2; fewer than ~5 live use cases; talent concentrated in one team | **Central CoE** for 6–12 months, with an explicit transition plan to hub-and-spoke |
| Maturity 2–3; 3+ business units with distinct data and use cases; a platform exists or is funded | **Hub-and-spoke** (default for most mid-to-large enterprises) |
| Maturity 4+; BUs already employ AI engineers; strong data governance; regulated BUs need local risk ownership | **Federated** with a standards council |
| Highly regulated single business (e.g., one product line under one regulator) | Central CoE longer; federate only the consumer-facing layer |
| Holding company / conglomerate with unrelated businesses | Federated from the start; the hub is a standards and procurement function |

## Design decisions to state explicitly (for any model)
| Decision | Options | Recommendation rule |
|---|---|---|
| Reporting line of the CoE | CIO / CDO / COO / CEO staff | Where the data platform reports, unless the sponsor is elsewhere; never under a single BU |
| Funding | Central budget / chargeback / BU-funded | Central for platform and lighthouses; chargeback once consumption is metered (Platform level 4) |
| Intake | Open backlog / quarterly portfolio review / continuous | Quarterly review with a continuous fast lane for sub-threshold cases |
| Risk gate | CoE approves / BU self-certifies / tiered | Tiered: self-certify low-risk, CoE review medium, risk committee high |
| Build vs partner | In-house / SI / vendor product | Build what differentiates; buy commodity (document OCR, transcription); partner for surge capacity |

## Minimum CoE roles (hub-and-spoke, lean)
| Role | FTE guide | Note |
|---|---|---|
| CoE lead / head of AI | 1 | Owns roadmap and portfolio |
| AI platform engineer | 2–3 | Gateway, observability, CI/eval, cost |
| AI/agent engineer | 2–4 | Lighthouse builds, patterns, code review for spokes |
| Data engineer (liaison to data platform) | 1–2 | Data products for AI |
| AI product manager | 1 | Portfolio, baselines, value tracking |
| Risk / governance lead | 0.5–1 | Inventory, tiering, reviews; may sit in risk function |
| Enablement / change lead | 0.5–1 | Training, communities, adoption metrics |

FTE guides are structural, not a benchmark; size to portfolio and label as assumption in the deliverable.

## Transition triggers
| From → To | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Central → Hub-and-spoke | 2+ spokes have trained builders and the platform has self-service onboarding and eval gates |
| Hub-and-spoke → Federated | Value tracking is at level 4; governance controls are tested; spokes pass audits two quarters running |
| Any → Central (regression) | Serious incident, regulatory finding, or shadow-AI sprawl; temporary and time-boxed |

# 12-Month AI Roadmap Skeleton

Four quarters, five workstreams. Each quarter has an exit criterion; do not advance a workstream whose exit criterion failed. Dates, headcount, and spend are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` until the sponsor confirms.

## Workstreams
| Workstream | Owner (role) | Measures |
|---|---|---|
| W1 Foundations (platform, gateway, observability, CI/eval) | AI platform lead | Gateway coverage %, eval gate in CI, cost per call visible |
| W2 Data readiness | Data platform lead | Domains productized, catalog coverage, PII classification % |
| W3 Use cases (lighthouse + fast lane) | AI product manager | Cases live, baseline vs realized value |
| W4 Governance & risk | Risk lead | Inventory complete, tiering applied, reviews on cadence |
| W5 Talent & adoption | Enablement lead | Builders trained, consumers active, communities running |

## Quarter plan
| Quarter | W1 Foundations | W2 Data | W3 Use cases | W4 Governance | W5 Talent | Exit criterion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Model gateway with logging; dev/test/prod; secrets; one orchestration standard | Pick 2 priority domains; assign owners; classify PII | Select 2 lighthouse + 2 fast-lane cases; baselines signed off | Policy v1; intake form; risk tiers; model inventory started | Role definitions; builder cohort 1 (10–20 people); exec briefing | Gateway live; 4 cases with baselines; policy published |
| Q2 | Tracing, cost per call, eval harness in CI; prompt/model versioning | Domain 1 productized (owner, quality rules, access by role) | Lighthouse 1 in production with HITL; fast-lane cases live | First risk reviews; incident process; vendor terms reviewed | Cohort 2; office hours; AI translators named per function | 1 lighthouse in prod with measured value; eval gate blocks regressions |
| Q3 | Canary/rollback; spend limits per team; self-service onboarding | Domain 2 productized; vector/feature store governed | Lighthouse 2 live; 3–5 further cases through fast lane; first kill decision | Controls tested (bias, privacy, security); NIST AI RMF mapping | Career ladder; community of practice; adoption metrics reported | Portfolio review with realized value; spokes onboarded self-service |
| Q4 | Model routing policy (cost/quality); platform SLA | Data contracts in CI for both domains | Scale lighthouse 1 to adjacent function; portfolio re-scored | Audit evidence automated for high-risk cases; board report | Internal certification; FY+1 capability plan | Operating-model transition decision (central → hub-and-spoke) with evidence |

## Rules
1. Nothing scales before it is measured: W3 scale items require W1 eval gate and W3 baselines.
2. One lighthouse per quarter at most until Platform maturity ≥ 3.
3. Each quarter ends with a portfolio review: realized value, cost, risk findings, kill/continue decisions.
4. Dependencies are stated per item: "requires Q1 gateway", "requires domain 1 productized".
5. Headcount and spend lines live in the roadmap's assumption table, not in the body.

## Roadmap risks (starter list)
| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lighthouse chosen for visibility, not data readiness | High | Slips 2 quarters | Enforce D ≥ 3 for Now cases | AI PM |
| Platform built before any consumer | Medium | Low adoption, cost overrun | Platform items gated by use-case pull | Platform lead |
| Governance perceived as blocker | Medium | Shadow AI | Tiered gate; self-certify low-risk in ≤5 days | Risk lead |
| Talent concentrated in CoE | High | Scale ceiling | Embedded engineers rotate to spokes in Q3 | CoE lead |
| Value not baselined | High | Program cannot defend budget at FY+1 | No baseline, no build | Sponsor |

# Use-Case Scoring Rubric — value × feasibility × data readiness ÷ risk

Score 1–5 on each axis. Score with evidence; mark unknowns. Record scores in `assets/use-case-scoring.csv`.

## Axes
### Value (V)
| Score | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | No quantified benefit; "nice to have" |
| 2 | Qualitative benefit; small user group |
| 3 | Quantified benefit with a baseline; single function; owner named |
| 4 | Quantified benefit material to a function's plan; multiple teams; revenue or cost line identified |
| 5 | Enterprise-level benefit tied to a strategic priority; sponsor at executive level; benefit baselined in finance |

### Feasibility (F)
| Score | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | Research-grade problem; no known pattern; unclear success definition |
| 2 | Known pattern but major integration or process change required; success definition fuzzy |
| 3 | Known pattern (RAG, classification, extraction, summarization, agentic workflow with bounded tools); integration points exist; success measurable |
| 4 | Pattern proven elsewhere in the organization; APIs and data accessible; team available |
| 5 | Near-configuration; vendor or platform feature; weeks not months |

### Data readiness (D)
| Score | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | Data does not exist or is not captured |
| 2 | Exists, but unstructured, unowned, or not accessible without legal review |
| 3 | Accessible with an owner; quality unknown or partly documented |
| 4 | Curated, documented, access via role; sufficient volume and freshness |
| 5 | Data product with SLA; already used by another production system |

### Risk (R) — higher is riskier
| Score | Criteria |
|---|---|
| 1 | Internal, low-stakes, human reviews every output |
| 2 | Internal, decision support, reversible outcomes |
| 3 | Customer-facing or employee-impacting, with human in the loop; moderate privacy exposure |
| 4 | Autonomous actions on customer/employee data; regulated domain (credit, employment, health, education records); IP exposure |
| 5 | Safety, legal, or regulatory outcome without reliable human oversight; likely "high-risk" under EU AI Act or equivalent |

## Formula
```
priority = (V × F × D) / R
```
Range: 0.2 (1×1×1/5) to 125 (5×5×5/1). Rank descending. Do not weight axes unless the sponsor states a weighting; if they do, record it.

## Classification
| Band | Rule | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Now | Top quartile by priority AND R ≤ 3 AND D ≥ 3 | Fund in Q1–Q2; lighthouse candidates |
| Next | Second quartile, or top quartile blocked by D ≤ 2 | Fund data readiness work first |
| Later | Third quartile | Revisit at next portfolio review |
| Stop | V ≤ 2, or R = 5 with no mitigation path, or F = 1 | Close with a one-line reason |

## Rules
1. Score at least 8 candidates before ranking; fewer means the backlog is not elicited yet.
2. Every "Now" case names a business owner and a measurable baseline. No owner → demote to Next.
3. Keep one "boring" high-D, high-F case in Now (document extraction, ticket triage) to prove the platform while a lighthouse matures.
4. Re-score quarterly; publish deltas.
5. Portfolio balance target (assumption, state it): 60% productivity/cost, 30% revenue/experience, 10% exploratory.

# AI Threat Model (STRIDE + OWASP LLM Top 10 2025)

## In a conversation: write the threat model now
- **The request names the architecture** (components such as web app, orchestrator, hosted LLM, vector store, refund API), even when the CSVs are not in the conversation: build the threat model **in this reply**, in this order. Never reply with only a request for the CSVs.
  1. **Components table** in the `assets/components-template.csv` columns: `id, name, kind, trust_zone, handles_pii, write_actions, internet_facing` (kinds: user, external_api, app, llm, retriever, tool, agent, vector_store, data_store). **Flows table**: `from, to, data, crosses_trust_boundary`. Attributes the user did not state are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Solution architect]`; ask the user to confirm the two tables in one list.
  2. The command that produces the files: `python3 -I scripts/threat_model.py` via the runner (see "How to run" below), giving `threats.csv`, `dfd.md`, `threat-report.md`.
  3. **Threats by severity** (high first), one row each: `threat_id` (stable: `<component>:<category>` or `<from>><to>:<category>`) | element | category (STRIDE letter or OWASP 2025 id LLM01–LLM10) | threat | likelihood | impact | severity | mitigation ids | status | owner. Apply `references/method.md`: STRIDE per element (external entity S, R; process S, T, R, I, D, E; data store T, I, D; flow T, I, D); OWASP rules (LLM01 on llm/agent reachable from an untrusted origin; LLM02 where PII is handled; LLM05 on anything receiving model output; LLM06 where write_actions = yes; LLM07, LLM09, LLM10 on the llm; LLM08 on vector store and retriever). Likelihood = 1 + exposed + boundary; impact = 1 + PII + write (cap 3; D and LLM10 fixed at 2); severity high ≥ 6, medium 3–4, low ≤ 2.
  4. **Mitigation ids** only from `assets/mitigations.csv`: S M01; T M02, M07; R M03; I M04; D M05 (stores also M08); E M06, M07; LLM01 M20–M23; LLM02 M24, M25; LLM03 M26, M27; LLM04 M28, M27; LLM05 M29, M30; LLM06 M31–M33; LLM07 M34, M35; LLM08 M36, M28; LLM09 M37, M38; LLM10 M39, M40.
  5. **Open high threats** with owner: status comes only from a control register; with none, every threat is `open` and owned by `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]`.
  6. **Data flow**: a mermaid flowchart, one subgraph per trust zone, boundary-crossing flows labelled.
  7. **Method & limits**: rule-based enumeration of the declared design; misses business-logic abuse and attack chains; not a penetration test or a security sign-off.
- **Components given, flows missing**: still show the components table and the threats the components alone imply, and ask once for the flows CSV; do not guess flows.
- **No control register, or asked to "assume the usual controls are in place"**: decline in one line (a control counts only with a register row and evidence); no threat is marked mitigated or planned; every threat is open, owner `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]`; offer `assets/controls-template.csv` for control owners to fill, then re-run.
- **Release gate** ("fail if more than N high threats remain open"): report open high vs the limit — more than N fails (exit 1), equal passes; all outputs are still written.
- **Live jailbreak or prompt-leak testing of a running app**: route to `red-team-suite`; offer this skill for the design-level threat model.

## Starting points
- **New:** components and flows of a design not yet built give every threat, all open and owned by the Security architect until controls exist.
- **Existing:** add the control register you already keep (`controls`); each in-place or planned control closes or downgrades its threats, and only the residual open threats count toward the gate.

## When to use
- ADLC architecture stage: the component and data-flow design of an LLM app, RAG pipeline or agent is drafted and needs a security review before build.
- Before a release review: re-run with the current control register to show residual (open) threats and gate on open highs.
- After a design change (new tool, new data store, new vendor model): re-run; threat ids are stable, so the control register carries over.
- NOT for: attacking a running app (`red-team-suite`), writing runtime input/output filters (`guardrails-config`), EU AI Act or NIST risk tiering (`ai-governance-risk`), or a penetration test or security sign-off.

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `components` — id, name, kind, trust_zone, handles_pii, write_actions, internet_facing | yes | solution architect (copy `assets/components-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `flows` — from, to, data, crosses_trust_boundary | yes | solution architect (copy `assets/flows-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `controls` — threat_id or mitigation_id, status, evidence, owner | no | security architect / control owners (copy `assets/controls-template.csv`) | every threat is `open`; owner `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]` |
| `max_open_high` — integer | no | CISO / release owner | no gate; report says "no gate set" |

Component ids are letters, digits and `_`. A flow whose ends sit in different trust zones is treated as crossing a boundary even if marked `no` (listed in `dfd.md`).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Build the components and flows CSVs from the architecture diagram; one row per component and per directed flow.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/threat_model.py` applies STRIDE per element and the OWASP LLM 2025 rules in `references/method.md`, scores likelihood × impact, and attaches mitigation ids from `assets/mitigations.csv`.
4. First run without controls: hand `threats.csv` to control owners; they record `in_place` / `planned` rows by `threat_id` or `mitigation_id` with evidence and owner.
5. Re-run with the controls file and, for a release gate, `max_open_high`.
6. Review the open high threats with the Security architect; add threats the rules cannot see (business-logic abuse, attack chains) by hand to the risk register.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `threats.csv` — `threat_id, element, element_type, category, threat, likelihood, impact, severity, mitigation, status, owner, evidence`; sorted by severity then id. `threat_id` = `<component>:<category>` or `<from>><to>:<category>`.
- `dfd.md` — mermaid flowchart: one subgraph per trust zone, boundary-crossing flows labelled and dashed red.
- `threat-report.md` — **Summary**, **Data flow**, **Threats by severity**, **Open high threats**, **Method & limits** (with the mitigation catalogue used).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every component and flow from the architecture is in the inputs (unlisted elements are not analysed)
- [ ] Every threat has a severity from the documented rule and at least one mitigation id
- [ ] Status comes only from the control register; no control is assumed
- [ ] Every owner is a named role or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]`
- [ ] Limits stated: rule-based enumeration, not a penetration test or sign-off

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-threat-model --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-threat-model`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`threats.csv`, `dfd.md`, `threat-report.md`). With `max_open_high` set, the run is a gate: more open high threats than the limit fails the run (exit 1) and all outputs are still written.

## References

# Method — ai-threat-model

## 1. Element types (STRIDE per element)
| Component kind | DFD element type | STRIDE categories |
|---|---|---|
| user, external_api | external entity | S, R |
| app, llm, retriever, tool, agent | process | S, T, R, I, D, E |
| vector_store, data_store | data store | T, I, D |
| every flow | data flow | T, I, D |

Source: Microsoft STRIDE-per-element table (Hernan, Lambert, Ostwald, Shostack, MSDN Magazine, Nov 2006, Figure 5). The table gives data stores no R; if a store is an audit log, add its repudiation threat by hand.

## 2. OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 rules
| Id | Applies to kinds | Extra condition |
|---|---|---|
| LLM01 Prompt Injection | llm, agent | reachable via flows from an untrusted origin: kind user, external_api, retriever or vector_store (indirect injection through stored content), or any internet_facing component |
| LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure | llm, agent, app, retriever, vector_store | handles_pii = yes |
| LLM03 Supply Chain | llm, agent, tool | — |
| LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning | llm, vector_store | — |
| LLM05 Improper Output Handling | app, agent, tool, data_store | has an incoming flow from an llm or agent |
| LLM06 Excessive Agency | llm, agent, tool, app | write_actions = yes |
| LLM07 System Prompt Leakage | llm, agent | — |
| LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses | vector_store, retriever | — |
| LLM09 Misinformation | llm | — |
| LLM10 Unbounded Consumption | llm, agent | — |

## 3. Severity
- Likelihood (1–3) = 1 + **exposed** + **boundary**.
  - Component: exposed = internet_facing; boundary = it is an end of any boundary-crossing flow.
  - Flow: exposed = either end internet_facing; boundary = the flow crosses a trust boundary (declared, or ends in different zones).
- Impact (1–3) = 1 + **PII** + **write**, capped at 3.
  - PII adds 1 for S, T, I, E, LLM01, LLM02, LLM03, LLM04, LLM07, LLM08 when handles_pii = yes (flow: either end).
  - Write adds 1 for S, T, R, E, LLM01, LLM03, LLM05, LLM06, LLM09 when write_actions = yes (flow: the receiving end).
  - D and LLM10 are fixed at 2 (availability and cost affect the whole service).
- Severity from L × I: **high** ≥ 6, **medium** 3–4, **low** ≤ 2 (5 cannot occur).

Worked example (Northwind fixture, fictional): `orchestrator` is not internet-facing but sends and receives boundary-crossing flows, so L = 2; it handles PII and has write actions, so LLM01 impact = 3; 2 × 3 = 6 → high.

## 4. Status and owner
- Control rows match by `threat_id`, or by `mitigation_id` (that row then covers every threat listing the mitigation).
- **mitigated**: a threat-level `in_place` row, or every mitigation id the threat lists has an `in_place` row.
- **planned**: any other matching row (planned, or only some mitigations in place).
- **open**: no matching row.
- Owner: the matched rows' owners (sorted, `;`-joined); none → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Security architect]`.
- Control rows that match nothing are listed in the report, not dropped silently.

## 5. Gate
`max_open_high` = N: the run exits 1 when open high threats > N. Exit 0 when equal.

## 6. Limits
Rule-based enumeration from the declared DFD. It does not find business-logic abuse, multi-step attack chains, implementation bugs or threats in elements missing from the inputs. Severity rules are a consistent triage, not a quantitative risk estimate. Not a penetration test or a security sign-off.

# Sources — ai-threat-model

| Source | URL | Used for | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| OWASP Gen AI Security Project — LLM Top 10 (2025 Top 10 Risk & Mitigations for LLMs and Gen AI Apps) | https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/ | Ids LLM01:2025–LLM10:2025 and names (Prompt Injection; Sensitive Information Disclosure; Supply Chain; Data and Model Poisoning; Improper Output Handling; Excessive Agency; System Prompt Leakage; Vector and Embedding Weaknesses; Misinformation; Unbounded Consumption) | 2026-10-18 |
| OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications — project page | https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/ | Confirms the project links "Version 2025" to https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-llm-applications-2025/ | 2026-10-18 |
| Hernan, Lambert, Ostwald, Shostack — "Uncover Security Design Flaws Using The STRIDE Approach", MSDN Magazine, Nov 2006 | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/msdn-magazine/2006/november/uncover-security-design-flaws-using-the-stride-approach | STRIDE-per-element table (Figure 5): data flows T,I,D; data stores T,I,D; processes S,T,R,I,D,E; interactors S,R | 2026-10-18 |

The OWASP paraphrases in `assets/owasp-llm-top10-2025.csv` are one-sentence summaries written for this skill; they are not OWASP text. Applicability rules, severity rules and the mitigation catalogue are this skill's own method (see `method.md`), not OWASP or Microsoft guidance.
