# Annotation Agreement (inter-annotator reliability)

## In a conversation: write the agreement assessment now
The reply **is the agreement assessment draft**, never only a request for the CSV. No label rows are in the conversation, so no alpha, kappa or count is printed; each is a marker until the run.
- **The request describes a labelling round** (annotators, items, label set, purpose) but the labels are not in the conversation: write the report skeleton **in this reply**, in the order of `agreement-report.md`:
  1. **Summary** — gate verdict first: `Gate: not set — the minimum alpha is the data owner's decision` (ask them for it; never choose one), or the stated minimum against `alpha [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run]`. Line 2: how it is computed — export one row per rating as `item_id, annotator, label` and run `scripts/agreement.py` (`python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input labels=<labels.csv> [--input guidelines=<guidelines.md>] [--input min_agreement=<alpha>] --out <dir>`).
  2. **Agreement** — Krippendorff's alpha (nominal) is the headline; then percent agreement, pairwise Cohen's kappa per annotator pair and Fleiss' kappa (n/a with the reason when items have different numbers of ratings). State the interpretation bands as **conventions, not tests**: Krippendorff ≥ 0.800 commonly relied on, 0.667–0.800 tentative conclusions only, < 0.667 discard; Landis & Koch for kappa (< 0 poor, 0.00–0.20 slight, 0.21–0.40 fair, 0.41–0.60 moderate, 0.61–0.80 substantial, 0.81–1.00 almost perfect).
  3. **Disputed items** — table `item_id | labels (label:count) | majority (or tie) | agreement`, lowest first, to send to an adjudicator.
  4. **Guideline gaps** — per-label agreement (`label | n | agreement | defined_in_guidelines`); a low-agreement label is one below overall percent agreement; a gap is such a label the guidelines do not define, plus boundary rules for the top confusion pairs. Without guidelines: `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]`.
  5. **Method & limits** — ratings must be independent; items with one rating are excluded and counted; nominal labels only; no confidence intervals; agreement measures consistency, not correctness.
- **Each item has only one annotator**: say agreement cannot be computed without two or more independent ratings per item, report no score, and recommend double-labelling a sample.
- **No labelling round described at all**: ask once for the labels export, the guidelines and the data owner's minimum alpha.
- **Asked to pick the threshold, declare labels defined without guidelines, or report a score anyway**: decline in one line (the threshold is the data owner's; definitions come from written guidelines; no score without paired ratings) and show the marker.

## Starting points
- **New:** labels from a pilot round (and draft guidelines) give alpha, disputed items and the label boundaries to sharpen before labelling at scale.
- **Existing:** add the `agreement.json` from the previous round (`previous`); the report adds alpha, percent agreement, disputed items and per-label agreement then vs now, and names labels whose agreement fell.

## When to use
- ADLC data stage: before human labels become an eval golden set, an LLM-as-judge calibration set or fine-tuning data.
- Pilot labelling round: find disputed items and the label boundaries the guidelines must sharpen before labelling at scale.
- Gate: labels may be used only when alpha meets the minimum the data owner set.
- NOT for: scoring model outputs against labels (`llm-eval-harness`), data quality or PII scans (`data-readiness-assessment`, `pii-data-inventory`), building the training file (`finetune-dataset-builder`), ordinal or interval scales (nominal labels only).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` — `item_id, annotator, label` | yes | labelling tool export (one row per rating) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `guidelines` — Markdown | no | Annotation lead | `defined_in_guidelines` and the gap list read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]` |
| `min_agreement` — alpha threshold | no | eval / data owner | no gate; the report says none was set |

A blank `label` means "not rated" and is skipped. Two ratings of the same item by the same annotator stop the run (exit 2).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Confirm ratings were independent (annotators did not see each other's labels); agreement on shared work is inflated.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/agreement.py` builds the coincidence matrix and computes alpha, Fleiss' kappa (equal ratings per item only), pairwise Cohen's kappa, per-label agreement and confusion pairs.
4. Read Disputed items worst-first; send them to an adjudicator.
5. Read Guideline gaps: define each low-agreement label the guidelines do not mention, and write a boundary rule for the top confusion pairs.
6. Re-label a fresh sample after the guideline change and re-run; compare alpha.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `agreement.json` — every statistic, per-item agreement, pairs, confusion pairs, gate result, settings for `--verify`.
- `disputed-items.csv` — `item_id, labels, majority, agreement` (labels as `label:count`; `majority` is the plurality label or `tie`), lowest agreement first.
- `label-agreement.csv` — `label, n, agreement, defined_in_guidelines`.
- `agreement-report.md` — **Summary** (gate verdict first), **Agreement**, **Disputed items**, **Guideline gaps**, **Method & limits**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Alpha is reported with its band labelled as a convention (Krippendorff 0.667 / 0.800); kappas with Landis & Koch bands, also a convention
- [ ] Fleiss' kappa is n/a (with the reason) when items have different numbers of ratings — alpha is the headline
- [ ] Items with one rating are excluded and counted, not scored
- [ ] Guideline gaps come from the supplied guidelines; without them the gap list is TBD for the Annotation lead
- [ ] Limits stated: nominal only, no confidence intervals, agreement is not correctness

## References
- `references/method.md` — formulas, the worked examples the tests reproduce, per-label agreement definition
- `references/sources.md` — Cohen 1960, Fleiss 1971, Krippendorff 2011, Landis & Koch 1977; verified URLs and dates
- `assets/labels-template.csv`, `assets/guidelines-template.md` — input layouts
- `scripts/agreement.py` — statistics and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/annotation-agreement`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`agreement.json`, `disputed-items.csv`, `label-agreement.csv`, `agreement-report.md`). Alpha below `min_agreement` fails the run (exit 1) with every output written. If no item has two or more ratings the run exits 1 and reports no score. Each output passes `--verify`, which re-derives it from the labels and the settings recorded in `agreement.json`.

# Method — annotation-agreement

All statistics are computed by `scripts/agreement.py` with the Python standard library. Sources: `sources.md`.

## Data model
Ratings `(item, annotator, label)`; blank labels are "not rated". An item is **pairable** when it has 2+ ratings. Items with one rating are excluded from every statistic and listed. With no pairable item the run exits 1 and reports no score.

## Percent agreement
Per item with m ratings and n_k ratings of label k: P_i = Σ_k n_k(n_k − 1) / (m(m − 1)) — the share of agreeing annotator pairs. Percent agreement = mean P_i. Not chance-corrected.

## Cohen's kappa (per annotator pair)
On items both annotators rated: p_o = share of identical labels; p_e = Σ_k p_A(k) p_B(k); κ = (p_o − p_e)/(1 − p_e). Undefined (n/a) when p_e = 1.
Worked check (Wikipedia, Cohen 1960 example): 20 yes/yes, 5 yes/no, 10 no/yes, 15 no/no → p_o 0.70, p_e 0.50, κ 0.40.

## Fleiss' kappa
Only when every pairable item has the same number of ratings m. p_j = share of all ratings in label j; P̄ = mean P_i; P̄_e = Σ p_j²; κ = (P̄ − P̄_e)/(1 − P̄_e). Otherwise n/a with the reason.
Worked check (Wikipedia example: 10 subjects, 14 raters, 5 categories): P̄ 0.378, P̄_e 0.213, κ 0.210.

## Krippendorff's alpha (nominal)
Coincidence matrix over pairable items: o_ck = Σ_u (number of ordered pairs of ratings (c, k) in u) / (m_u − 1); n_c = Σ_k o_ck; n = Σ_c n_c.
alpha = 1 − (n − 1) · Σ_{c≠k} o_ck / Σ_{c≠k} n_c n_k. Undefined (n/a) when only one label is used.
Worked checks (Krippendorff 2011): 4 observers × 12 units with missing values → 0.743; Meg/Owen binary 2 × 10 → 0.095.

## Per-label agreement
agreement(k) = o_kk / n_k: of the pairable ratings with label k, the share whose paired rating on the same item is also k. For two annotators this equals the specific agreement 2a/(2a + b + c) (yes: 2·20/(40 + 15) = 0.727 in the Cohen example). `n` in `label-agreement.csv` is the number of pairable ratings with that label.

## Confusion pairs
For each pairable item and each pair of annotators who rated it with different labels, count the unordered label pair. Sorted by count, then label.

## Disputed items and guideline gaps
- Disputed: pairable items with P_i < 1, lowest first; `majority` is the plurality label or `tie`.
- Low-agreement label: agreement(k) below the overall percent agreement (both are shares of agreeing pairs, so the comparison is like for like; no fixed threshold is assumed).
- Guideline gap: a low-agreement label whose name does not appear in the guidelines (case-insensitive word match; `_` and `-` also matched as spaces). Without guidelines: `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]`.

## Interpretation bands (conventions, not tests)
| Kappa (Landis & Koch 1977) | Band |
|---|---|
| < 0 | poor |
| 0.00–0.20 | slight |
| 0.21–0.40 | fair |
| 0.41–0.60 | moderate |
| 0.61–0.80 | substantial |
| 0.81–1.00 | almost perfect |

Alpha (Krippendorff): ≥ 0.800 commonly relied on; 0.667–0.800 tentative conclusions only; < 0.667 discard. The `min_agreement` gate is the data owner's choice; the skill never sets one.

## Limits
Nominal labels only (no ordinal / interval distance); point estimates without bootstrap CIs; agreement measures consistency, not correctness; multi-label items must be split into one binary label per item first.

---
name: bias-fairness-check
description: Use when the user asks whether a classifier or AI decision system treats groups fairly — "run a bias check on these predictions", "disparate impact / four-fifths rule", "equal opportunity or equalised odds gap", "fairness gate before launch", "per-group accuracy by gender/region/age band". Produces fairness.json and fairness-report.md from a labelled predictions CSV - per-group n, base rate, selection rate, accuracy, TPR, FPR, precision; demographic parity difference, disparate impact ratio, equal opportunity and equalised odds differences; small-group flags; a verdict against user-supplied thresholds (none built in; missing ones are to be baselined, never a pass). Exit 1 on any breach. Not for LLM output quality (llm-eval-harness), the risk register or model card (ai-governance-risk), or a legal compliance opinion.
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: ai-platform
  adlc_stage: evaluate
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    modes:
      new:      {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "labelled predictions from a model before launch, plus thresholds"}
      existing: {case: agent-mode-existing, bring: "this period's decisions plus your last fairness check"}
    inputs:
      - {name: predictions, type: csv, required: true, from: "labelled predictions, one row per decision (layout: assets/predictions-template.csv) with the sensitive-attribute column, label, prediction, optional score"}
      - {name: thresholds, type: csv, required: false, from: "metric,threshold set by the Responsible AI lead (layout: assets/thresholds-template.csv); absent or blank = to be baselined, never a pass"}
      - {name: sensitive_attr, type: string, required: false, default: "group", from: "name of the sensitive-attribute column"}
      - {name: reference_group, type: string, required: false, from: "reference group for the disparate impact ratio (default: highest selection rate, stated in the report)"}
      - {name: min_sample, type: string, required: false, from: "minimum n per group; smaller groups are flagged (absent = to be baselined)"}
      - {name: previous, type: json, required: false, from: "fairness.json from the last check of the same system and attribute; adds metric, selection-rate and breach changes"}
    run:
      - {step: fairness, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/fairness.py --predictions {predictions} [--thresholds {thresholds}] --sensitive-attr {sensitive_attr} [--reference-group {reference_group}] [--min-sample {min_sample}] [--previous {previous}] --out {out}"}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/fairness.json", checks: [exists, json, contains:"disparate_impact_ratio"]}
      - {path: "{out}/fairness-report.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Verdict","Metrics","Per-group","Small groups","Limits"], no_unowned_tbd, numbers_trace_to:"{out}/fairness.json"]}

# Bias & Fairness Check

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/bias-fairness-check --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/bias-fairness-check`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`fairness.json`, `fairness-report.md`). A metric that breaches a supplied threshold fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; a metric with no threshold is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Responsible AI lead]` and the verdict is INCOMPLETE, never PASS.

## Starting points
- **New:** labelled predictions from a validation set and the thresholds your Responsible AI lead set give the pre-launch gate.
- **Existing:** add the `fairness.json` from the last check (`previous`); the report adds each metric and group selection rate then vs now, and which breaches are new or resolved.

## When to use
- Pre-launch or periodic fairness gate on a binary classifier or a yes/no AI decision (approve/deny, flag/not flag, shortlist/reject).
- Answering "is there disparate impact", "is the error rate the same across groups", "which groups are too small to judge".
- NOT for: LLM answer quality or groundedness (`llm-eval-harness`); the risk register, controls and model card (`ai-governance-risk` — attach this report as evidence); legal advice on anti-discrimination law (route to counsel); multi-class or regression outputs (binarise first and say how).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `predictions` CSV: sensitive-attribute column (default `group`), `label`, `prediction` (0/1, true/false, yes/no), optional `score` | yes | model owner's labelled evaluation sample; fixture rows must be labelled fictional |
| `thresholds` CSV: `metric,threshold` for `demographic_parity_difference`, `disparate_impact_ratio`, `equal_opportunity_difference`, `equalized_odds_difference` | no | Responsible AI lead; policy decision, never invented by the skill |
| `sensitive_attr` | no (default `group`) | user |
| `reference_group` | no | user / policy (often the historically advantaged group) |
| `min_sample` | no | Responsible AI lead / statistician |

If `predictions` is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. Thresholds are never assumed: the four-fifths rule applies only when the user sets `disparate_impact_ratio` to 0.8.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Confirm the decision, the positive outcome (what `prediction = 1` means), the sensitive attribute and the evaluation sample's provenance. Copy `assets/predictions-template.csv` and `assets/thresholds-template.csv`.
3. Run the agent (above) or the script directly: `python3 -I scripts/fairness.py --predictions p.csv --thresholds t.csv --reference-group A --min-sample 30 --out <dir>`.
4. Read the verdict: FAIL (a breach, exit 1), INCOMPLETE (a threshold to be baselined or a metric undefined), PASS (every metric within its supplied threshold).
5. Interpret with `references/fairness-metrics.md`: which metric governs for this decision, why base rates differ, whether small groups drive the gap.
6. Hand the report to `ai-governance-risk` as bias-risk evidence; record mitigations (re-threshold per group only with legal sign-off, rebalance data, add human review).
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `fairness.json`: verdict, breaches, metrics (value, rule, threshold, status, owner when unbaselined), per-group stats, reference group and basis, small groups, notes.
- `fairness-report.md`: sections Verdict, Metrics, Per-group, Small groups, Limits. Every number traces to `fairness.json`.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every threshold came from the user; missing ones read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Responsible AI lead]`, never "pass"
- [ ] Reference group and its basis stated
- [ ] Small groups flagged and kept in the metrics (not silently dropped)
- [ ] Undefined rates (no positives / no negatives in a group) named, not shown as 0
- [ ] Limits section kept: no confidence intervals, metric conflict, label bias, no legal conclusion
- [ ] No fixture or fictional data presented as a real model's results

## References
- `references/fairness-metrics.md` — definitions, worked example (the eval fixture, hand-checked), choosing a metric, standards by name
- `scripts/fairness.py` — calculator (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 breach / 2 input)
- `assets/predictions-template.csv`, `assets/thresholds-template.csv` — input layouts

# Fairness metrics — definitions, worked example, choosing one

## Per-group rates (binary decision, positive = the outcome the decision grants or flags)
| Rate | Formula |
|---|---|
| Base rate | actual positives / n |
| Selection rate | predicted positives / n |
| Accuracy | (TP + TN) / n |
| TPR (recall) | TP / (TP + FN) — undefined when the group has no actual positives |
| FPR | FP / (FP + TN) — undefined when the group has no actual negatives |
| Precision | TP / (TP + FP) — undefined when the group has no predicted positives |

## Fairness metrics computed by `scripts/fairness.py`
| Metric | Formula | Better | Typical question |
|---|---|---|---|
| `demographic_parity_difference` | max − min selection rate | lower | Do groups receive the outcome at the same rate? |
| `disparate_impact_ratio` | min over groups of selection rate ÷ reference group's | higher | Does any group receive it at a fraction of the reference rate? |
| `equal_opportunity_difference` | max − min TPR | lower | Among those who qualify, are groups recognised equally? |
| `equalized_odds_difference` | max(TPR gap, FPR gap) | lower | Are both error types equal across groups? |

Gaps use every group with a defined rate (min-max across groups); per-group values versus the reference group are in the Per-group table. Undefined rates are excluded and named in the notes.

## Worked example (the eval fixture — fictional, hand-checked)
| Group | n | TP | FN | FP | TN | Selection | TPR | FPR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (ref) | 10 | 4 | 1 | 1 | 4 | 5/10 = 0.5 | 4/5 = 0.8 | 1/5 = 0.2 |
| B | 10 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 5 | 3/10 = 0.3 | 2/4 = 0.5 | 1/6 ≈ 0.1667 |
| C | 3 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 1/3 ≈ 0.3333 | 1/1 = 1.0 | 0/2 = 0 |

DPD = 0.5 − 0.3 = 0.2 · DIR = min(0.3/0.5, 0.3333/0.5) = 0.6 · EOD = 1.0 − 0.5 = 0.5 · FPR gap = 0.2 − 0 = 0.2 · EqOdds = max(0.5, 0.2) = 0.5. With `min_sample` 5, group C (n = 3) is flagged: its TPR of 1.0 rests on one positive and drives the EOD.

## Choosing the governing metric (a policy decision — owner: Responsible AI lead)
- Outcome is a benefit allocated by rate (hiring shortlist, credit approval): selection-rate metrics (DPD, DIR) are the usual first screen.
- Errors carry the harm (fraud flags, clinical triage): error-rate metrics (equal opportunity, equalised odds).
- When base rates differ between groups, equal selection rates and equal error rates generally cannot both hold; pick deliberately and record why.
- The four-fifths rule (DIR ≥ 0.8) comes from the US Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures; it is a screening heuristic in that context, not a universal standard. The skill applies it only when the user supplies 0.8.

## Standards (by name; read the source, the skill gives no legal opinion)
- NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) — MEASURE function: fairness and bias evaluated and documented.
- NIST SP 1270, Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence.
- EU AI Act — data and data governance obligations for high-risk systems include examining possible biases.
- US Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (1978) — origin of the four-fifths rule.

## What this check does not do
- No confidence intervals or significance tests; small groups are flagged instead.
- No intersectional analysis unless the user encodes it in the attribute column (e.g. `F|45-54`).
- No label-bias detection; labels are treated as ground truth.

---
name: conversation-design
description: Use when the user is designing or checking the conversation layer of an AI assistant or chatbot — "design the intents for our assistant", "how well do our intents cover what users actually say", "which intents get confused", "where is the fallback and human hand-off", "check our utterances against the intent list". Produces routing.csv (each utterance's best intent and score), intent-quality.csv (examples, precision, recall, confusable intents) and conversation-spec.md (Summary, Persona, Intents, Fallback and hand-off with a mermaid flowchart, Coverage, Gaps, Method) from an intent catalog and real user utterances, using a deterministic TF-IDF router. Exit 1 when labelled accuracy is below the supplied min_accuracy. Not for prompt wording (use prompt-spec), LLM answer quality (use llm-eval-harness) or agent topology (use agent-architecture).

---

# Conversation Design (intents, fallback, hand-off, coverage)

## In a conversation: route and report now
The reply **is the coverage report** (or one ask), never only a command. About 1,000 tokens, tables over prose. Line 1: `Run: python3 -I scripts/conversation_design.py --intents <intents.csv> --utterances <utterances.csv> [--persona <persona.csv>] [--min-accuracy <x>] --out-dir out` → `routing.csv`, `intent-quality.csv`, `conversation-spec.md` (use the case's flags). Line 2: the headline — `Coverage a/b · Accuracy c/d = 0.xxx (or "not measured — no labels") · Gate: met (exit 0) | FAILED (exit 1) | none (exit 0)`.

**Never**
- Never pick "sensible" persona values. Each of `name, tone, reading_level, escalation_channel, disallowed_topics` absent from the persona file is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Conversation designer]` — list each missing key by name (e.g. reading_level too), and say "not chosen: the Conversation designer's decision".
- Never invent utterances or intents: no utterance file → ask once for the utterance sample (`utterance[,expected_intent]`, `assets/utterances-template.csv`); the run **stops (exit 2)**. Same for a missing intent catalog.
- Never echo more than the first 80 characters of a user message (end with "…").
- Never state accuracy without counting labelled rows from the file.

**Procedure — row by row from the supplied CSVs** (`references/method.md`)
1. Tokenise: lower-case, `[a-z0-9]+`, drop tokens < 2 chars and stopwords (a an the and or but if of to in on at for from by with about as is are was were be been am do does did i me my we our you your it its this that these those there here can could would should will just so please hi hello hey), drop a trailing `s` on tokens > 3 chars not ending `ss`.
2. One document per intent = description + all examples; idf(t) = ln((1+N)/(1+df)) + 1 over the N intent documents; vectors = count × idf, L2-normalised; utterance terms in no intent document are ignored. Score = cosine; best intent wins (tie → intent name). **Best score < 0.25 → `fallback`** (uncovered). Long messages sharing one or two common terms usually fall below 0.25.
3. Coverage = utterances routed to an intent ÷ all utterances (blank-label rows count here).
4. Labelled = rows with a non-blank `expected_intent` (`fallback` is a label). Accuracy = correct ÷ labelled, 3 decimals. Precision = correct ÷ routed-to-intent; recall = correct ÷ labelled-as-intent; zero denominator → `n/a`.
5. Confusable: cosine of two intents' **example sets** ≥ **0.40** (shared example words such as "pay … bill" across two intents).
6. Gate: `--min-accuracy x` and accuracy < x (or no labels) → "**run exits 1; all outputs still written**" (e.g. "0.870 is below 0.900"); accuracy ≥ x → "gate met (exit 0)"; no min_accuracy → "no gate (exit 0)". Unknown label, bad response_type, handoff not yes/no, duplicate intent, an intent named `fallback`, or a missing required file → **stops (exit 2)** with the line.

**Reply layout after the two lines**
1. Working table, every utterance: `| # | utterance (≤80 chars) | predicted | score≈ | expected | ✓ |`, then the counts it gives.
2. Per-intent `| intent | examples | precision | recall | confusable_with | owner |`.
3. **Gaps** (each with the intent's owner): uncovered messages, recall/precision < 1.000, intents with < 5 examples, confusable pairs, missing persona keys.
4. **Fallback and hand-off**: below 0.25 → rephrase prompt → re-route; second miss → the persona's `escalation_channel` (or its TBD); `handoff=yes` intents go straight there. Short mermaid `flowchart`.
5. **Method** line: thresholds 0.25 route / 0.40 confusable; the router is **lexical (TF-IDF) and sample-based**, not a production NLU benchmark; hand-computed scores are approximate — `routing.csv` from the run is authoritative (`--verify` re-derives it).
No files in the conversation: give line 1, describe each metric above with its threshold, and ask once for the intent catalog and utterance sample.

## Starting points
- **New:** first-draft intents and unlabelled sample messages give a coverage figure, the messages nothing catches, thin and confusable intents, and the persona keys still to decide.
- **Existing:** your live intent catalog, persona and labelled real messages give per-intent precision and recall, misroutes and an accuracy gate for edits to the catalog.

## When to use
- ADLC requirements stage: before building an assistant, to agree the intent catalog, response types, fallback and the human hand-off path.
- "How much of what users actually say do our intents cover?" — route a sample of real messages and read coverage and gaps.
- Regression check after editing intents: run with labelled utterances and a `min_accuracy` gate.
- NOT for: prompt wording or system prompts (`prompt-spec`), grading LLM answers (`llm-eval-harness`), single- vs multi-agent design (`agent-architecture`), production NLU benchmarking (this router is lexical).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `intents` — `intent,description,examples,response_type,handoff,owner` | yes | Conversation designer (copy `assets/intents-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `utterances` — `utterance[,expected_intent]` | yes | chat logs, search logs, call-centre notes, sampled and de-identified | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `persona` — kv-csv `name, tone, reading_level, escalation_channel, disallowed_topics` | no | Conversation designer / brand voice guide | each missing key is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Conversation designer]` |
| `min_accuracy` — 0–1 | no | product owner | no gate; accuracy reported only |

`expected_intent` may be an intent name, `fallback` (out of scope on purpose) or blank (unlabelled; counts toward coverage only). An unknown label, a bad `response_type`, a `handoff` other than yes/no, a duplicate intent or an intent named `fallback` stops the run (exit 2) with the line number.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Strip personal data from the utterance sample. Outputs echo at most 80 characters of each utterance, but the run reads all of it.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/conversation_design.py` routes each utterance by TF-IDF cosine (`references/method.md`); below 0.25 it goes to `fallback`.
4. With labels it computes accuracy, per-intent precision/recall and confusion pairs; it flags intent pairs whose example sets reach cosine 0.40.
5. With `min_accuracy`, accuracy below it (or no labels to measure it) exits 1.
6. Work the Gaps list with each intent's owner: add missed phrasings, split or merge confusable intents, confirm out-of-scope messages.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `routing.csv` — `utterance` (≤ 80 chars), `predicted_intent`, `score`, `expected_intent`, `correct`, `nearest_intent`.
- `intent-quality.csv` — `intent, examples, precision, recall, confusable_with, response_type, handoff, routed, labelled, owner`.
- `conversation-spec.md` — **Summary**, **Persona**, **Intents**, **Fallback and hand-off** (mermaid flowchart), **Coverage** (uncovered utterances, confusion pairs), **Gaps** (each with an owner), **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] `routing.csv` re-derives exactly (`--verify`) and no output echoes more than 80 characters of an utterance (`--leak-check`)
- [ ] Every gap names an owner; missing persona keys are TBD for the Conversation designer
- [ ] The flowchart shows fallback and a path to a person
- [ ] Threshold values (0.25 route, 0.40 confusable) are stated in the report
- [ ] Limits stated: lexical router, sample-based, not a production NLU benchmark

## References
- `references/method.md` — tokenising, TF-IDF formula, thresholds, metrics, limits
- `assets/intents-template.csv`, `assets/utterances-template.csv`, `assets/persona-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/conversation_design.py` — router, metrics, spec writer, `--verify` and `--leak-check` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/conversation-design --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/conversation-design`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`routing.csv`, `intent-quality.csv`, `conversation-spec.md`). Accuracy below a supplied `min_accuracy` fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the outputs are still written so the misses are visible.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Conversation-layer design check: intents + real utterances -> routing, intent quality, spec.

Routes every utterance to its best intent with a TF-IDF cosine over each intent's
description + examples (references/method.md). A best score below CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD
(0.25) routes to `fallback` (uncovered). With expected_intent labels it computes accuracy,
per-intent precision/recall and confusion pairs. Intent pairs whose example sets have a
TF-IDF cosine at or above CONFUSABLE_THRESHOLD (0.40) are flagged as confusable.

Usage:
  python3 -I conversation_design.py --intents intents.csv --utterances utterances.csv \
      [--persona persona.csv] [--min-accuracy 0.8] --out-dir OUT
  python3 -I conversation_design.py --verify OUT/routing.csv --intents intents.csv --utterances utterances.csv
  python3 -I conversation_design.py --leak-check OUT/conversation-spec.md --utterances utterances.csv

Inputs:
  intents     CSV intent,description,examples,response_type,handoff,owner. examples are
              pipe-separated; response_type answer|action|handoff|clarify; handoff yes|no.
  utterances  CSV utterance[,expected_intent]. expected_intent is an intent name, `fallback`
              (out of scope on purpose) or blank (unlabelled).
  persona     kv-CSV key,value[,source,notes]: name, tone, reading_level, escalation_channel,
              disallowed_topics. Missing keys -> [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Conversation designer].
  min_accuracy  optional gate 0-1 on labelled accuracy.

Outputs (in --out-dir): routing.csv, intent-quality.csv, conversation-spec.md.
Utterances are user text: outputs never contain more than the first 80 characters of one.
Exit codes: 0 written (and gate met when set) · 1 accuracy below --min-accuracy (or no labels to
measure it) — outputs still written · 2 missing/invalid input.
Stdlib only; no network; writes only inside --out-dir.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import io
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.25   # best cosine below this -> fallback (uncovered)
CONFUSABLE_THRESHOLD = 0.40   # example-set cosine at/above this -> confusable pair
MIN_EXAMPLES = 5              # skill design guideline: fewer examples -> thin intent (gap)
MAX_ECHO = 80                 # never echo more than this many characters of an utterance
FALLBACK = "fallback"
TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Conversation designer]"
RESPONSE_TYPES = ("answer", "action", "clarify", "handoff")
PERSONA_KEYS = ("name", "tone", "reading_level", "escalation_channel", "disallowed_topics")
STOPWORDS = frozenset(
    "a an the and or but if of to in on at for from by with about as is are was were be been "
    "am do does did i me my we our you your it its this that these those there here can could "
    "would should will just so please hi hello hey".split()
)
TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")


class InputError(Exception):
    """Missing or invalid input -> exit 2."""


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ input
def read_csv(path: Path, what: str) -> list[dict]:
    if not path or not Path(path).is_file():
        raise InputError(f"{what} file not found: {path}")
    text = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    lines = [ln for ln in text.splitlines() if not ln.lstrip().startswith("#")]
    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO("\n".join(lines)))
    rows = [{(k or "").strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k is not None} for r in reader]
    return rows, [(c or "").strip() for c in (reader.fieldnames or [])]


def load_intents(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    rows, cols = read_csv(path, "intents")
    need = ("intent", "description", "examples", "response_type", "handoff", "owner")
    miss = [c for c in need if c not in cols]
    if miss:
        raise InputError(f"intents CSV missing column(s): {', '.join(miss)} (need {','.join(need)})")
    if not rows:
        raise InputError("intents CSV has no intent rows")
    out, seen = [], set()
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        name = r["intent"]
        if not name:
            raise InputError(f"intents line {i}: intent name is blank")
        if name.lower() == FALLBACK:
            raise InputError(f"intents line {i}: '{FALLBACK}' is reserved for uncovered utterances")
        if name in seen:
            raise InputError(f"intents line {i}: duplicate intent {name!r}")
        seen.add(name)
        rt = r["response_type"].lower()
        if rt not in RESPONSE_TYPES:
            raise InputError(f"intents line {i}: response_type {r['response_type']!r} not in {'|'.join(RESPONSE_TYPES)}")
        ho = r["handoff"].lower()
        if ho not in ("yes", "no"):
            raise InputError(f"intents line {i}: handoff {r['handoff']!r} must be yes or no")
        examples = [e.strip() for e in r["examples"].split("|") if e.strip()]
        out.append({"intent": name, "description": r["description"], "examples": examples,
                    "response_type": rt, "handoff": ho, "owner": r["owner"] or TBD})
    return out


def load_utterances(path: Path, intent_names: set[str]) -> list[dict]:
    rows, cols = read_csv(path, "utterances")
    if "utterance" not in cols:
        raise InputError("utterances CSV needs an 'utterance' column")
    out = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        if not r.get("utterance"):
            continue
        exp = r.get("expected_intent", "")
        if exp and exp != FALLBACK and exp not in intent_names:
            raise InputError(f"utterances line {i}: expected_intent {exp!r} is not an intent or '{FALLBACK}'")
        out.append({"utterance": r["utterance"], "expected": exp})
    if not out:
        raise InputError("utterances CSV has no non-empty utterances")
    return out


def load_persona(path: Path | None) -> dict[str, dict]:
    if not path:
        return {}
    rows, cols = read_csv(path, "persona")
    if "key" not in cols or "value" not in cols:
        raise InputError("persona CSV needs columns key,value[,source,notes]")
    return {r["key"]: {"value": r["value"], "source": r.get("source", "")}
            for r in rows if r.get("key") and r.get("value")}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ TF-IDF
def tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for t in TOKEN_RE.findall(text.lower()):
        if t in STOPWORDS or len(t) < 2:
            continue
        if len(t) > 3 and t.endswith("s") and not t.endswith("ss"):
            t = t[:-1]  # light plural folding: bills -> bill
        out.append(t)
    return out


def idf_table(docs: list[list[str]]) -> dict[str, float]:
    n = len(docs)
    df: dict[str, int] = {}
    for d in docs:
        for t in set(d):
            df[t] = df.get(t, 0) + 1
    return {t: math.log((1 + n) / (1 + c)) + 1.0 for t, c in df.items()}


def vector(toks: list[str], idf: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]:
    tf: dict[str, int] = {}
    for t in toks:
        if t in idf:
            tf[t] = tf.get(t, 0) + 1
    v = {t: c * idf[t] for t, c in tf.items()}
    norm = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in v.values()))
    return {t: x / norm for t, x in v.items()} if norm else {}


def cosine(a: dict[str, float], b: dict[str, float]) -> float:
    if len(a) > len(b):
        a, b = b, a
    return sum(x * b.get(t, 0.0) for t, x in a.items())


def echo(text: str) -> str:
    """User text as it may appear in outputs: at most MAX_ECHO characters, single line."""
    t = " ".join(text.split())
    return t if len(t) <= MAX_ECHO else t[:MAX_ECHO] + "…"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ analysis
def analyse(intents: list[dict], utterances: list[dict], persona: dict, min_accuracy: float | None) -> dict:
    docs = [tokens(it["description"] + " " + " ".join(it["examples"])) for it in intents]
    idf = idf_table(docs)
    ivecs = [vector(d, idf) for d in docs]
    names = [it["intent"] for it in intents]

    routing = []
    for u in utterances:
        uv = vector(tokens(u["utterance"]), idf)
        scored = sorted(((round(cosine(uv, iv), 6), n) for iv, n in zip(ivecs, names)), key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))
        best_score, best = scored[0] if scored else (0.0, FALLBACK)
        pred = best if best_score >= CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD else FALLBACK
        correct = "" if not u["expected"] else ("yes" if pred == u["expected"] else "no")
        routing.append({"utterance": u["utterance"], "predicted_intent": pred, "score": best_score,
                        "nearest_intent": best, "expected_intent": u["expected"], "correct": correct})

    labelled = [r for r in routing if r["expected_intent"]]
    n_correct = sum(1 for r in labelled if r["correct"] == "yes")
    accuracy = (n_correct / len(labelled)) if labelled else None
    covered = sum(1 for r in routing if r["predicted_intent"] != FALLBACK)

    # confusable intents: cosine between example-set vectors (examples only)
    evecs = [vector(tokens(" ".join(it["examples"])), idf) for it in intents]
    confusable: dict[str, list[tuple[str, float]]] = {n: [] for n in names}
    pairs = []
    for i in range(len(names)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(names)):
            s = round(cosine(evecs[i], evecs[j]), 6)
            if s >= CONFUSABLE_THRESHOLD:
                confusable[names[i]].append((names[j], s))
                confusable[names[j]].append((names[i], s))
                pairs.append((names[i], names[j], s))
    pairs.sort(key=lambda p: (-p[2], p[0], p[1]))

    quality = []
    for it in intents:
        n = it["intent"]
        tp = sum(1 for r in labelled if r["expected_intent"] == n and r["predicted_intent"] == n)
        pred_n = sum(1 for r in labelled if r["predicted_intent"] == n)
        exp_n = sum(1 for r in labelled if r["expected_intent"] == n)
        quality.append({
            "intent": n, "examples": len(it["examples"]),
            "precision": (tp / pred_n) if pred_n else None, "recall": (tp / exp_n) if exp_n else None,
            "confusable_with": ";".join(c for c, _ in sorted(confusable[n], key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))),
            "response_type": it["response_type"], "handoff": it["handoff"], "owner": it["owner"],
            "routed": sum(1 for r in routing if r["predicted_intent"] == n), "labelled": exp_n,
        })

    confusion: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
    for r in labelled:
        if r["correct"] == "no":
            k = (r["expected_intent"], r["predicted_intent"])
            confusion[k] = confusion.get(k, 0) + 1
    confusion_pairs = sorted(confusion.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))

    gate = None
    if min_accuracy is not None:
        gate = {"min_accuracy": min_accuracy, "met": accuracy is not None and accuracy >= min_accuracy}
    return {"routing": routing, "quality": quality, "pairs": pairs, "confusion": confusion_pairs,
            "labelled": len(labelled), "correct": n_correct, "accuracy": accuracy, "covered": covered,
            "total": len(routing), "intents": intents, "persona": persona, "gate": gate}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ rendering
def f3(x) -> str:
    return "n/a" if x is None else f"{x:.3f}"


def pct(num: int, den: int) -> str:
    return f"{num}/{den} ({100.0 * num / den:.1f}%)" if den else "0/0"


def routing_csv(res: dict) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(["utterance", "predicted_intent", "score", "expected_intent", "correct", "nearest_intent"])
    for r in res["routing"]:
        w.writerow([echo(r["utterance"]), r["predicted_intent"], f"{r['score']:.3f}", r["expected_intent"],
                    r["correct"], r["nearest_intent"]])
    return buf.getvalue()


def quality_csv(res: dict) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(["intent", "examples", "precision", "recall", "confusable_with", "response_type", "handoff",
                "routed", "labelled", "owner"])
    for q in res["quality"]:
        w.writerow([q["intent"], q["examples"], f3(q["precision"]), f3(q["recall"]), q["confusable_with"] or "none",
                    q["response_type"], q["handoff"], q["routed"], q["labelled"], q["owner"]])
    return buf.getvalue()


def md_cell(s: str) -> str:
    return str(s).replace("|", "\\|")


def mermaid_label(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[\[\]{}()\"<>|#;]", " ", s).strip() or "unnamed"


def mermaid(res: dict, channel: str) -> list[str]:
    groups = {rt: [it["intent"] for it in res["intents"] if it["response_type"] == rt] for rt in RESPONSE_TYPES}
    lines = ["```mermaid", "flowchart TD",
             '  U(["User message"]) --> R{"Best intent score >= ' + f"{CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD:.2f}" + '?"}']
    labels = {"answer": "Answer", "action": "Action", "clarify": "Clarify", "handoff": "Hand-off intents"}
    for rt in RESPONSE_TYPES:
        if groups[rt]:
            names = ", ".join(mermaid_label(n) for n in groups[rt])
            lines.append(f'  R -->|yes| {rt.upper()}["{labels[rt]}: {names}"]')
    lines.append('  R -->|no| FB["Fallback: rephrase prompt"]')
    lines.append('  FB -->|matched| R')
    lines.append(f'  FB -->|still unmatched| H["Human hand-off: {mermaid_label(channel)}"]')
    if groups["handoff"]:
        lines.append("  HANDOFF --> H")
    if groups["clarify"]:
        lines.append("  CLARIFY -->|answer given| R")
    lines.append("```")
    return lines


def spec_md(res: dict) -> str:
    persona, intents = res["persona"], res["intents"]
    L: list[str] = []
    total, covered = res["total"], res["covered"]
    acc = res["accuracy"]
    L.append("# Conversation spec")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Summary")
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"- Intents: {len(intents)}. Utterances routed: {total}.")
    L.append(f"- Coverage: {pct(covered, total)} reach an intent at score >= {CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD:.2f}; "
             f"{total - covered} go to fallback.")
    if acc is None:
        L.append("- Accuracy: not measured (no expected_intent labels).")
    else:
        L.append(f"- Accuracy: {pct(res['correct'], res['labelled'])} of labelled utterances routed correctly.")
    L.append(f"- Confusable intent pairs (example cosine >= {CONFUSABLE_THRESHOLD:.2f}): {len(res['pairs'])}.")
    if res["gate"]:
        g = res["gate"]
        if g["met"]:
            L.append(f"- Gate: accuracy {f3(acc)} meets min_accuracy {g['min_accuracy']:.3f}.")
        elif acc is None:
            L.append(f"- Gate: FAILED — min_accuracy {g['min_accuracy']:.3f} set but no labels to measure it (exit 1).")
        else:
            L.append(f"- Gate: FAILED — accuracy {f3(acc)} is below min_accuracy {g['min_accuracy']:.3f} (exit 1).")
    else:
        L.append("- Gate: none set (no min_accuracy).")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Persona")
    L.append("")
    L.append("| Key | Value | Source |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|")
    for k in PERSONA_KEYS:
        p = persona.get(k)
        L.append(f"| {k} | {md_cell(p['value']) if p else TBD} | {md_cell(p['source']) if p and p['source'] else '—'} |")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Intents")
    L.append("")
    L.append("| Intent | Response type | Hand-off | Examples | Routed | Precision | Recall | Confusable with | Owner |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for q in res["quality"]:
        L.append(f"| {md_cell(q['intent'])} | {q['response_type']} | {q['handoff']} | {q['examples']} | {q['routed']} | "
                 f"{f3(q['precision'])} | {f3(q['recall'])} | {md_cell(q['confusable_with']) or 'none'} | {md_cell(q['owner'])} |")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Fallback and hand-off")
    L.append("")
    channel = persona["escalation_channel"]["value"] if "escalation_channel" in persona else TBD
    handoff_intents = [it["intent"] for it in intents if it["handoff"] == "yes"]
    L.append(f"- Fallback: any utterance whose best intent score is below {CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD:.2f} gets a rephrase "
             "prompt; a second miss goes to a person.")
    L.append(f"- Escalation channel: {channel}.")
    L.append(f"- Intents that hand off to a person: {', '.join(handoff_intents) if handoff_intents else 'none'}.")
    if "disallowed_topics" in persona:
        L.append(f"- Disallowed topics (decline and route to fallback): {persona['disallowed_topics']['value']}.")
    else:
        L.append(f"- Disallowed topics: {TBD}.")
    L.append("")
    L.extend(mermaid(res, channel if "escalation_channel" in persona else "channel to be baselined"))
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Coverage")
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"Covered {pct(covered, total)}. Uncovered utterances (first {MAX_ECHO} characters only):")
    L.append("")
    uncovered = [r for r in res["routing"] if r["predicted_intent"] == FALLBACK]
    if uncovered:
        L.append("| Utterance | Nearest intent | Score | Expected |")
        L.append("|---|---|---|---|")
        for r in uncovered:
            L.append(f"| {md_cell(echo(r['utterance']))} | {r['nearest_intent']} | {r['score']:.3f} | "
                     f"{r['expected_intent'] or '—'} |")
    else:
        L.append("None: every utterance reached an intent.")
    L.append("")
    if res["confusion"]:
        L.append("Confusion pairs (expected → predicted, labelled utterances):")
        L.append("")
        L.append("| Expected | Predicted | Count |")
        L.append("|---|---|---|")
        for (e, p), c in res["confusion"]:
            L.append(f"| {e} | {p} | {c} |")
        L.append("")
    L.append("## Gaps")
    L.append("")
    gaps = []
    for q in res["quality"]:
        if q["examples"] < MIN_EXAMPLES:
            gaps.append(f"Thin intent `{q['intent']}`: {q['examples']} example(s), guideline is {MIN_EXAMPLES} "
                        f"(owner: {q['owner']}).")
        if q["routed"] == 0:
            gaps.append(f"No utterance routed to `{q['intent']}`: check it is needed or add real phrasings "
                        f"(owner: {q['owner']}).")
        if q["recall"] is not None and q["recall"] < 1.0:
            gaps.append(f"`{q['intent']}` recall {f3(q['recall'])}: add the missed phrasings as examples "
                        f"(owner: {q['owner']}).")
        if q["precision"] is not None and q["precision"] < 1.0:
            gaps.append(f"`{q['intent']}` precision {f3(q['precision'])}: other requests route here; tighten its "
                        f"examples or add the missing intent (owner: {q['owner']}).")
    for a, b, s in res["pairs"]:
        gaps.append(f"Confusable: `{a}` and `{b}` (example cosine {s:.3f}); sharpen examples or merge "
                    "(owner: Conversation designer).")
    for it in intents:
        if it["response_type"] == "handoff" and it["handoff"] != "yes":
            gaps.append(f"`{it['intent']}` has response_type handoff but handoff=no (owner: {it['owner']}).")
    if not handoff_intents:
        gaps.append("No intent hands off to a person; only fallback reaches one (owner: Conversation designer).")
    n_unc = total - covered
    if n_unc:
        gaps.append(f"{n_unc} uncovered utterance(s): add intents or examples, or confirm they are out of scope "
                    "(owner: Conversation designer).")
    missing_p = [k for k in PERSONA_KEYS if k not in persona]
    if missing_p:
        gaps.append(f"Persona keys missing: {', '.join(missing_p)} — {TBD}.")
    L.extend([f"- {g}" for g in gaps] if gaps else ["None found."])
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Method")
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"- Routing: TF-IDF cosine between the utterance and each intent's description + examples "
             f"(smoothed IDF over intent documents, L2-normalised term counts, stopwords removed, light plural "
             f"folding). Best score below {CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD:.2f} → `fallback`. Ties break by intent name.")
    L.append(f"- Confusable: TF-IDF cosine between two intents' example sets >= {CONFUSABLE_THRESHOLD:.2f}.")
    L.append("- Precision = correct / routed-to-intent; recall = correct / labelled-as-intent; labelled rows only.")
    L.append(f"- Coverage = utterances routed to an intent / all utterances. Utterances are echoed to {MAX_ECHO} "
             "characters at most.")
    L.append("- Limits: lexical matching only (no synonyms or embeddings); a production NLU model will score "
             "differently. Results describe this utterance sample, not all future traffic.")
    L.append("")
    return "\n".join(L)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ modes
def verify(routing_path: Path, intents_path: Path, utt_path: Path) -> int:
    intents = load_intents(intents_path)
    utt = load_utterances(utt_path, {i["intent"] for i in intents})
    expected = routing_csv(analyse(intents, utt, {}, None))
    actual = Path(routing_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8") if Path(routing_path).is_file() else ""
    if actual != expected:
        print(f"verify FAILED: {routing_path} does not match a fresh routing of the inputs")
        return 1
    print(f"verify ok: {len(utt)} routings reproduce")
    return 0


def leak_check(path: Path, utt_path: Path) -> int:
    rows, cols = read_csv(utt_path, "utterances")
    text = " ".join(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").split())
    leaks = 0
    for r in rows:
        u = " ".join(r.get("utterance", "").split())
        if len(u) > MAX_ECHO and u[:MAX_ECHO + 1] in text:
            leaks += 1
    if leaks:
        print(f"leak-check FAILED: {leaks} utterance(s) echoed beyond {MAX_ECHO} characters in {path}")
        return 1
    print(f"leak-check ok: no utterance echoed beyond {MAX_ECHO} characters")
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--intents", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--utterances", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--persona", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--min-accuracy", type=str)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--verify", type=Path, help="routing.csv to re-derive from --intents/--utterances")
    ap.add_argument("--leak-check", type=Path, help="output file to check against --utterances")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if args.leak_check:
            if not args.utterances:
                raise InputError("--leak-check needs --utterances")
            return leak_check(args.leak_check, args.utterances)
        if not args.intents or not args.utterances:
            raise InputError("--intents and --utterances are required")
        if args.verify:
            return verify(args.verify, args.intents, args.utterances)
        if not args.out_dir:
            raise InputError("--out-dir is required")
        min_acc = None
        if args.min_accuracy not in (None, ""):
            try:
                min_acc = float(args.min_accuracy)
            except ValueError:
                raise InputError(f"--min-accuracy must be a number 0-1, got {args.min_accuracy!r}")
            if not 0.0 <= min_acc <= 1.0:
                raise InputError(f"--min-accuracy must be between 0 and 1, got {min_acc}")
        intents = load_intents(args.intents)
        utt = load_utterances(args.utterances, {i["intent"] for i in intents})
        res = analyse(intents, utt, load_persona(args.persona), min_acc)
    except InputError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    out = args.out_dir
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "routing.csv").write_text(routing_csv(res), encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "intent-quality.csv").write_text(quality_csv(res), encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "conversation-spec.md").write_text(spec_md(res), encoding="utf-8")
    acc = "n/a" if res["accuracy"] is None else f"{res['accuracy']:.3f}"
    if res["gate"] and not res["gate"]["met"]:
        print(f"gate FAILED: accuracy {acc} below min_accuracy {res['gate']['min_accuracy']:.3f}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"conversation spec written: coverage {res['covered']}/{res['total']}, accuracy {acc}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Method: routing, quality and coverage

All steps are deterministic and stdlib-only (`scripts/conversation_design.py`). Same inputs give byte-identical outputs.

## Tokenising
Lower-case; tokens are `[a-z0-9]+`; tokens shorter than 2 characters and a fixed stopword list (articles, pronouns, auxiliaries, greetings, "please") are dropped; a trailing `s` is removed from tokens longer than 3 characters that do not end in `ss` (light plural folding: `bills` → `bill`). No stemming beyond that, no synonyms.

## Routing (TF-IDF cosine)
- One document per intent: its description plus all examples.
- IDF over the intent documents, smoothed: `idf(t) = ln((1 + N) / (1 + df(t))) + 1`.
- Vectors are raw term counts × IDF, L2-normalised. Utterance terms not in any intent document are ignored.
- Score = cosine(utterance, intent). The best intent wins; ties break by intent name.
- **Confidence threshold 0.25**: a best score below 0.25 routes to `fallback` (uncovered). The value is the skill's default, not a standard; tune it on your own labelled sample. The threshold is printed in every report.

## Accuracy and per-intent quality (labelled rows only)
- `correct` = predicted intent equals `expected_intent` (`fallback` is a valid expected value for out-of-scope messages).
- Accuracy = correct / labelled. Precision(intent) = correct / routed-to-intent. Recall(intent) = correct / labelled-as-intent. A zero denominator prints `n/a`.
- Confusion pairs: (expected, predicted) counts for wrong rows.

## Confusable intents
Cosine between two intents' **example sets** (examples only, same IDF) at or above **0.40** flags the pair. Shared vocabulary in examples is the main cause of lexical mis-routing; the fix is sharper examples or a merge.

## Coverage and gaps
- Coverage = utterances routed to an intent / all utterances.
- Gaps listed: recall or precision below 1.000, intents with fewer than **5 examples** (skill design guideline), intents no utterance reached, confusable pairs, a `handoff` response type without `handoff=yes`, no hand-off intent at all, uncovered utterances, missing persona keys.

## Fallback and hand-off pattern
The spec states the pattern the flowchart draws: below threshold → rephrase prompt → re-route; a second miss → the persona's `escalation_channel`. `handoff=yes` intents go straight to that channel.

## Limits
- Lexical only: paraphrases with no shared words score 0. A production NLU or embedding router will score differently; use this as a design-time check, not a production benchmark.
- Results describe the supplied sample, not all future traffic. Sample size is printed; small samples swing accuracy by several points per utterance.
- Utterances are user text. Outputs echo at most the first 80 characters (`--leak-check` enforces it). Strip personal data from samples before running.

skills/ai-platform/data-contract-validat:
---
name: data-contract-validator
description: Use when a dataset must be checked against its data contract before an AI system uses it for training, RAG ingestion or evaluation — "validate this extract against the contract", "does this data meet the contract", "gate the feed before ingestion", "check types, nulls, uniqueness and allowed values", "is this data fresh enough", "check updated_at is fresh against the load date and a max age", "our contract is an ODCS YAML file", "draft a contract from this first extract". Produces violations.csv (every violation with rule, severity, failing rows and rate, at most 3 truncated examples and the owner), profile.csv (inferred type, null rate, distinct, min/max per column) and contract-report.md with a PASS / PASS WITH WARNINGS / FAIL verdict; any error-severity violation exits 1. Contract as CSV, or an ODCS v3 YAML subset. Not for finding personal data (use pii-data-inventory), scoring overall data readiness (use data-readiness-assessment) or building training sets (use finetune-dataset-builder).
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: ai-platform
  adlc_stage: data
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    modes:
      new:      {case: agent-mode-new, bring: "a first extract of a new feed, no contract yet"}
      existing: {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "your agreed data contract and the latest extract"}
    inputs:
      - {name: contract, type: file, required: false, from: "data contract CSV (layout: assets/contract-template.csv) or ODCS v3 YAML subset (references/odcs-subset.md); from the data owner. Without it a DRAFT contract is inferred from the data to {out}/contract-draft.csv (warn severity, no owners) and the extract is checked against it"}
      - {name: data, type: csv, required: true, from: "dataset extract CSV with a header row (values are read; at most 3 truncated examples per violation are written)"}
      - {name: freshness_column, type: string, required: false, from: "date or datetime column whose newest value must be recent; without as_of and max_age_days freshness is TBD for the Data owner"}
      - {name: as_of, type: string, required: false, from: "as-of date YYYY-MM-DD for the freshness check (never defaults to today)"}
      - {name: max_age_days, type: string, required: false, from: "maximum age in days of the newest record (data owner's freshness SLA)"}
    run:
      - {step: validate, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/validate_contract.py [--contract {contract}] --draft-contract {out}/contract-draft.csv --data {data} [--freshness-column {freshness_column}] [--as-of {as_of}] [--max-age-days {max_age_days}] --out-dir {out}"}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/violations.csv", checks: [exists, csv:[column,rule,severity,failing_rows,failing_rate,examples,owner], cmd:"python3 -I scripts/validate_contract.py --verify {path} --contract '{contract}' --draft-contract {out}/contract-draft.csv --data {data} --freshness-column '{freshness_column}' --as-of '{as_of}' --max-age-days '{max_age_days}'"]}
      - {path: "{out}/profile.csv", checks: [exists, csv:[column,inferred_type,null_rate,distinct,min,max], "csv_rows:null_rate~^[01]\\.\\d{3}$", cmd:"python3 -I scripts/validate_contract.py --verify {path} --contract '{contract}' --draft-contract {out}/contract-draft.csv --data {data} --freshness-column '{freshness_column}' --as-of '{as_of}' --max-age-days '{max_age_days}'"]}
      - {path: "{out}/contract-report.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Summary","Verdict","Violations","Profile","Method"], no_unowned_tbd, cmd:"python3 -I scripts/validate_contract.py --verify {path} --contract '{contract}' --draft-contract {out}/contract-draft.csv --data {data} --freshness-column '{freshness_column}' --as-of '{as_of}' --max-age-days '{max_age_days}'"]}
---

# Data Contract Validator

## In a conversation: validate the extract now
The reply **is the contract report** (or its skeleton): line 1 is `Verdict: PASS | PASS WITH WARNINGS | FAIL | pending — <reason>`, never only a request for files. Error-severity violations block use (the run exits 1); warnings do not.
- **The request carries the contract rules and the data (or a description of them)**: write the report **in this reply** in the script's order — **Summary**; **Verdict** with counts of error- and warn-severity violations; **Violations** table `column, rule, severity, failing_rows, failing_rate, examples, owner, expectation` (errors first; rules from `references/rules.md`: missing_column, extra_column, ragged_row, type, required, null_rate, unique, min/max, allowed, regex, freshness; at most 3 examples per violation, each ≤ 40 characters; blank owner = `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`); **Profile** (`column, inferred_type, null_rate, distinct, min, max`); **Method**. Name the run that produces the files: `python3 -I scripts/validate_contract.py --contract … --data … [--freshness-column … --as-of … --max-age-days …] --out-dir …`.
- **Files said to be attached, or the extract/contract named but not shown** (e.g. "check this extract against the contract before RAG ingestion"): lay out every section above now with each value `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`, state the gate rule (any error-severity violation → FAIL, exit 1, outputs still written; examples truncated, at most 3 per violation), and ask once, in one list, for: the contract (CSV per `assets/contract-template.csv`, or ODCS v3 YAML), the extract CSV, and for freshness the column, load (as-of) date and max age. Never invent rules, thresholds or owners.
- **No contract yet / onboarding a feed**: the run drafts `contract-draft.csv` from the first extract (types, required, unique keys, enums, observed null limits, all at warn severity, owners left to the Data owner); the report marks the contract **DRAFT** and says the pass is by construction until the owner signs it off.
- **ODCS YAML contract**: map the supported subset (`references/odcs-subset.md`: primaryKey, pattern, minimum/maximum, validValues, format email, nullValues percent, duplicateValues); list anything else (e.g. `missingValues`) as not evaluated, never silently passed.
- **"Use today's date and a sensible max age" for freshness**: decline in one line (freshness must be measured from the load date and the owner's SLA); freshness reads `not checked: as_of and max_age_days [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`; today's date is never used and no max age is proposed.
- **"Which columns hold personal data / need masking?"**: line 1 routes it to `pii-data-inventory`; offer this skill for contract conformance afterwards.

## Starting points
- **New:** with only a first extract, the run drafts `contract-draft.csv` from it (types, required, keys, code lists, null limits, observed ranges in `notes`, all at warn severity with no owner invented) and checks the extract against the draft; the report marks the contract DRAFT until the Data owner signs it off.
- **Existing:** your agreed contract (CSV or ODCS YAML) and the latest extract give every breach with its owner and the error-severity gate.

## When to use
- ADLC data stage: before an extract is loaded into a vector store, a fine-tune set or an evaluation set.
- A recurring feed into an AI system needs a pass/fail gate on schema, types, nulls, keys, ranges, code lists and freshness.
- A data owner has a contract (CSV, or an ODCS v3 YAML file) and wants every breach listed with its owner.
- NOT for: finding personal data (`pii-data-inventory`), overall readiness scoring (`data-readiness-assessment`), building or cleaning training data (`finetune-dataset-builder`), cross-table or drift checks, fixing the data (this skill reports; it never edits the source).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contract` — CSV `column, type, required, unique, min, max, allowed, regex, max_null_rate, severity, owner` or ODCS v3 YAML | no | data owner (copy `assets/contract-template.csv`) | a DRAFT contract is inferred from the extract to `contract-draft.csv` (warn severity, owners TBD) and the report says the pass is by construction |
| `data` — extract CSV with header | yes | data engineering | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `freshness_column` | no | data owner | freshness not requested |
| `as_of` — YYYY-MM-DD | no | run owner (the load date) | freshness reads `not checked … [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`; never today's date |
| `max_age_days` | no | data owner's freshness SLA | as for `as_of` |

Contract types: `string, integer, number, boolean, date, datetime, email, enum`. `min`/`max` are numbers, dates or (for text types) character lengths. `allowed` is pipe-separated. Blank `severity` = error; blank `owner` = `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`. YAML: the subset in `references/odcs-subset.md` is parsed with the repo's YAML subset parser; anything outside it is listed as not evaluated, never silently passed.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Get the contract from the data owner; if none exists, start from `assets/contract-template.csv` and have the owner sign off each row (severity and owner especially).
3. If the extract may hold personal data, run `pii-data-inventory` first; examples here are truncated but still real values.
4. Run the agent. `scripts/validate_contract.py` checks every rule in `references/rules.md` and profiles every column.
5. Read the Verdict. FAIL (exit 1): send each error row to its owner; fix at source and re-run — never edit the outputs.
6. Review warnings and `extra_column` rows with the Data owner: add the column to the contract or drop it from the feed.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `violations.csv` — `column, rule, severity, failing_rows, failing_rate, examples, owner, expectation`; errors first.
- `profile.csv` — `column, inferred_type, null_rate, distinct, min, max` (min/max for numeric and date-like columns only).
- `contract-report.md` — **Summary**, **Verdict**, **Violations**, **Profile**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every violation names an owner or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`
- [ ] No more than 3 examples per violation, each ≤ 40 characters; no text values in the profile
- [ ] Freshness used the supplied as-of date, or is marked TBD — never today's date
- [ ] YAML terms outside the subset are listed as not evaluated
- [ ] Each output passes `--verify`; an error-severity violation exits 1
- [ ] Limits stated: one extract, not a statistical guarantee

## References
- `references/rules.md` — rules, denominators, type parsing, sensitivity handling, limits
- `references/odcs-subset.md` — ODCS v3 YAML mapping and what is not evaluated
- `references/sources.md` — ODCS sources checked 2026-10-18
- `assets/contract-template.csv` — contract layout for the data owner
- `scripts/validate_contract.py` — validator and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 gate / 2 input)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/data-contract-validator --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/data-contract-validator`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`violations.csv`, `profile.csv`, `contract-report.md`). This is a gate: any error-severity violation exits 1 with complete outputs. Each output is re-verified against the data and contract with the script's `--verify` mode.

# ODCS v3 YAML subset (what `--contract *.yaml` understands)

The YAML contract is parsed with the repo's YAML subset parser (`scripts/skillmeta.py`) after two clean-ups: block-scalar bodies (`key: |`, `key: >`) are dropped and inline `# comments` outside quotes are removed. Anchors, aliases and tags exit 2. Field names follow ODCS v3 ([S2], [S3] in `sources.md`).

## Mapping
| ODCS | Contract rule |
|---|---|
| `schema:` with exactly one object | the dataset (several objects exit 2 — one dataset per run) |
| `properties[].name` | `column` |
| `logicalType` string / integer / number / boolean / date / timestamp | `type` string / integer / number / boolean / date / datetime |
| `logicalType` time, object, array, map, vector | exit 2 (not checkable in a flat CSV) |
| `logicalTypeOptions.format: email` on a string | `type: email` |
| `logicalTypeOptions.pattern` | `regex` (full match) |
| `logicalTypeOptions.minimum` / `maximum` (numbers, dates) | `min` / `max` |
| `logicalTypeOptions.minLength` / `maxLength` (strings) | `min` / `max` (character length) |
| `enum` (property or `logicalTypeOptions`) | `allowed` (string becomes `enum`) |
| `required: true` | `required: yes` |
| `unique: true` | `unique: yes` |
| `primaryKey: true` | `required: yes` and `unique: yes` |
| quality `invalidValues` + `arguments.validValues` + `mustBe: 0` | `allowed` |
| quality `invalidValues` + `arguments.pattern` + `mustBe: 0` | `regex` |
| quality `duplicateValues` + `mustBe: 0` | `unique: yes` |
| quality `nullValues` + `unit: percent` + `mustBeLessOrEqualTo: N` | `max_null_rate = N / 100` |
| quality `severity` | `severity` (error / warn; blank = error) |

## Not evaluated (listed in the report under "Contract terms not evaluated")
Any other quality metric or operator (e.g. `missingValues`, `rowCount`, `mustBeBetween`, `unit: rows` thresholds above 0, SQL or custom rules), `exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `physicalType`. ODCS has no per-property owner, so every YAML rule's owner is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`; use the CSV layout to name owners.

# Rules, denominators and limits

| Rule | Fires when | failing_rows | failing_rate denominator |
|---|---|---|---|
| missing_column | contract column absent from the data | all rows | all rows |
| extra_column | data column absent from the contract (always `warn`, owner TBD Data owner) | all rows | all rows |
| ragged_row | a row has more or fewer fields than the header (`error`) | ragged rows | all rows |
| type | non-null value does not parse as the contract type | failing values | non-null values |
| required | `required=yes` and any null | null rows | all rows |
| null_rate | null rows ÷ rows > `max_null_rate` | null rows | all rows |
| unique | `unique=yes` and repeated values | rows beyond the first occurrence | non-null values |
| min / max | value (or text length) outside the bound | failing values | non-null values |
| allowed | value not in the pipe-separated list (exact, case-sensitive) | failing values | non-null values |
| regex | value does not full-match the regex | failing values | non-null values |
| freshness | newest date in the freshness column older than as-of − max_age_days, or any record dated after the as-of date (failing rows = future-dated rows) | all rows | all rows |

Type parsing: integer `^[+-]?\d+$`; number decimal or exponent, finite; boolean true/false/yes/no/y/n/t/f/1/0; date `YYYY-MM-DD` (real calendar date); datetime ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD[T ]HH:MM[:SS[.f]]` with optional `Z` or offset (compared in UTC; a date-only `max` on a datetime column covers the whole day, a date-only `min` starts at 00:00); email `local@domain.tld`. Values that fail the type rule are excluded from min/max (they are already reported).

Freshness is evaluated only when `freshness_column`, `as_of` and `max_age_days` are all supplied. A column with no as-of date or maximum age reads `not checked … [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]`; the script never uses today's date.

Input files must be UTF-8 (a BOM is accepted); any other encoding or a binary file stops the run (exit 2) — bytes are never silently replaced. Output CSV cells that start with = + - @ tab or CR are prefixed with `'` (OWASP CSV-injection guard); plain numbers such as -3.5 are left as they are.

Sensitive data: violations carry at most 3 distinct example values, each cut to 40 characters; profile min/max are shown only for numeric and date-like columns. Run `pii-data-inventory` first if the extract may hold personal data, and treat `violations.csv` as no more public than the data.

Limits: one CSV extract per run; no cross-column, referential or distribution-drift rules; results describe the extract, not the full table.

# Sources (checked 2026-10-18)

| Id | Source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Bitol, Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS), overview — https://bitol-io.github.io/open-data-contract-standard/latest/ (current version shown: v3.2.0) | Which standard the YAML subset follows |
| S2 | ODCS, Schema section — https://bitol-io.github.io/open-data-contract-standard/latest/schema/ | `logicalType` values (string, date, timestamp, time, number, integer, object, array, boolean, map, vector); `logicalTypeOptions` (string: format, minLength, maxLength, pattern; integer/number: minimum, maximum; date: format, minimum, maximum); `required`, `unique`; `enum` |
| S3 | ODCS, Data Quality section — https://bitol-io.github.io/open-data-contract-standard/latest/data-quality/ | Library metrics `nullValues`, `missingValues`, `invalidValues` (arguments `validValues` or `pattern`), `duplicateValues`, `rowCount`; operators `mustBe`, `mustBeLessOrEqualTo`, …; `unit: rows|percent` (rows is the default) |
| S4 | datacontract-cli documentation, "Define your Schema" — https://docs.datacontract.com/docs/schema.md | Cross-check: `primaryKey: true` implies not-null and unique; `logicalTypeOptions.enum` example |

Only field names and short paraphrases are recorded here; the standard's text is not reproduced. Re-check S2/S3 when ODCS publishes a new minor version.

apiVersion: v3.0.2
kind: DataContract

        required: true

      - name: question
        logicalType: string

          - metric: duplicateValues

              missingValues: ['n/a', '-']
