---
name: eval-engineering-runner
description: Use when the user has an eval dataset (or SME-written test cases in a spreadsheet) and wants to know whether it is fit to score with — "audit our eval set", "do we have enough cases per category", "we need N safety and M refund cases — are we covered?", "turn our SMEs' test cases into a clean eval set and check them against first-cut targets", "find duplicates and leakage in the golden set", "clean this eval file". Produces eval-audit.json and eval-audit.md (verdict, per-category coverage vs targets, duplicates and near-duplicates, empty references, conflicting references, split leakage, grader coverage, balance, recommendations per category) and a cleaned eval-clean.jsonl; optional LLM review against the upstream eval-engineering guidance. Not for running evals or LLM-as-judge scoring (llm-eval-harness) or retrieval metrics (rag-pipeline-design).
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: ai-platform
  adlc_stage: evaluate
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    modes:
      new:      {case: agent-mode-new, bring: "the first test cases your experts wrote in a spreadsheet"}
      existing: {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "your current eval set and its coverage targets"}
    inputs:
      - {name: dataset, type: file, required: true, from: "eval set JSONL or CSV: id, input, expected/reference, category or tags, optional grader, split, label (layout: assets/eval-dataset.example.jsonl)"}
      - {name: targets, type: csv, required: false, from: "coverage targets CSV: category, min_cases (layout: assets/coverage-targets.example.csv); without it coverage is reported, not gated"}
      - {name: near_dup_threshold, type: string, required: false, default: "0.9", from: "token Jaccard at or above which two inputs count as near-duplicates (method parameter)"}
      - {name: review, type: flag, required: false, flag: "--review", from: "yes to add an LLM review of the audit against the upstream eval-engineering guidance"}
    run:
      - {step: audit, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/audit_evals.py --dataset {dataset} [--targets {targets}] --near-dup-threshold {near_dup_threshold} --out-dir {out}", stdout: "{out}/audit.log"}
      - {step: upstream-review, kind: llm, template: assets/eval-review-template.md, context: ["../../../vendor/eval-engineering/SKILL.md", "../../../vendor/eval-engineering/references/verifier-design.md", "../../../vendor/eval-engineering/references/calibration.md", "{out}/eval-audit.md", "{out}/eval-audit.json"], out: "{out}/eval-review.md", skip_if_missing: [review]}
    outputs:

# Eval Engineering Runner

Wraps eval-engineering from langchain-ai/langchain-skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). The upstream skill designs Harbor tasks and verifiers by interview; this skill applies its dataset-level concerns (leakage, coverage, independent verifier evidence, fairness of the case mix) as a deterministic audit of a flat eval set. Upstream text is not copied: the optional review step reads `vendor/eval-engineering/SKILL.md` and two of its references directly.

## In a conversation: audit the set now
- **The request carries the set or the targets** (cases pasted, counts per category, or "here is our golden set and the minimum cases per category" with the file contents not in the conversation): write the audit **in this reply**, in this order. Never reply with only a request for the file.
  1. **Verdict** from the targets: PASS, FAIL (any category BELOW its `min_cases`, exit 1) or NOT GATED (no targets). Name the command that produces it: `python3 -I scripts/audit_evals.py` via the runner (see "How to run" below).
  2. **Coverage table per category**: category | min_cases | clean cases | gap | status (OK / BELOW). Counts on the cleaned set; a category with a target but no cases is BELOW. Counts not visible read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval owner]`.
  3. **Quality issues** by the `references/audit-method.md` rules with severity and action: empty input (high, dropped), empty reference for a reference-based grader (high, dropped), conflicting reference (high, later row dropped, domain owner resolves), split leakage (high, re-split), exact duplicate (medium, dropped), near-duplicate at token Jaccard ≥ 0.9 (medium, kept for review), missing grader (medium), missing category, duplicate id. Apply them to any cases shown; for an unseen file, list each check with its result `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval owner, from the audit run]`.
  4. **eval-clean.jsonl**: the cleaned cases, one JSON object per line with `id, input, expected, category, tags, grader, split` (written from the cases shown; for an unseen file, state it is written by the run). The original is kept for provenance.
  5. **Recommendations with exact counts**: "add 3 safety cases (3 of 6)", "replace 2 near-duplicates", "assign a grader to 4 cases" — counts, not adjectives.
  6. One line: this audits the dataset only; it does not run the evals or judge outputs (`llm-eval-harness` does that on `eval-clean.jsonl`).
- **Targets stated, counts stated** ("we need 6 safety, 5 refund, 2 escalation cases — are we covered?"): give the coverage table with the exact gap per category and the verdict; never write new cases to close a gap, name how many to add.
- **No targets agreed**: verdict NOT GATED; each category's `min_cases` is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval owner]`; still report counts, issues and balance (largest/smallest category ratio).
- **Nothing to audit** (no set, no counts): ask once for the dataset (JSONL or CSV with id, input, expected/reference, category; optional grader, split) and the per-category targets; say no cases or targets will be invented.

## Starting points
- **New:** a spreadsheet of first cases from subject experts becomes a clean JSONL eval set, with duplicates dropped and coverage measured against first-cut targets.
- **Existing:** your current eval set is audited for duplicates, near-duplicates, leakage, missing graders and coverage gaps against its targets, and a cleaned file is written.

## When to use
- Before trusting a score: is the eval set big enough per category, free of duplicates and leakage, and gradable?
- After merging cases from several sources (logs, SMEs, synthetic) into one golden set.
- NOT for: running the evals or judging outputs (`llm-eval-harness` runs them; this skill engineers the dataset), retrieval metrics (`rag-pipeline-design`), designing Harbor tasks (the upstream skill itself).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `dataset` — JSONL or CSV with id, input, expected/reference, category or tags; optional grader type, split, label | yes | eval owner; layout `assets/eval-dataset.example.jsonl` |
| `targets` — CSV category, min_cases | no (without it the verdict is NOT GATED) | eval owner + product owner; layout `assets/coverage-targets.example.csv` |
| `near_dup_threshold` — token Jaccard (default 0.9, a method parameter printed in the report) | no | eval owner |
| `review` — flag for the optional LLM review | no | user |

Targets are never invented: without a targets file each category's `min_cases` is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval owner]`.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Export the eval set to JSONL or CSV; set per-category `min_cases` with the product owner.
3. Run the skill. `scripts/audit_evals.py` applies `references/audit-method.md`: normalise inputs; drop empty inputs, empty references (unless the grader is reference-free), and exact duplicates; flag conflicting references, cross-split leakage, near-duplicates, missing or unknown graders, repeated ids; count cleaned cases per category against targets.
4. On exit 1 (FAIL) add the cases named in Recommendations, then re-run. Fix high-severity issues before scoring with `llm-eval-harness`.
5. Use `eval-clean.jsonl` as the scored set; keep the original for provenance.
6. Optional: pass `review=yes` for `eval-review.md` on `assets/eval-review-template.md`.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
| File | Content | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `eval-audit.json` | verdict, coverage per category, balance, label distribution, issues, issue counts, recommendations, columns used | json; has coverage |
| `eval-audit.md` | Verdict, Coverage, Quality issues, Recommendations | sections; no unowned TBD |
| `eval-clean.jsonl` | cleaned cases: id, input, expected, category, tags, grader, split (+ label) | every line JSON; id, input, category non-empty; ids unique (`scripts/check_jsonl.py`) |
| `eval-review.md` (optional) | Upstream alignment, Dataset gaps, Next actions | eval case `agent-with-review` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every category in scope has a target; none is below it
- [ ] No input appears in more than one split; conflicting references resolved
- [ ] Every case has a grader type; reference-based graders have references
- [ ] Near-duplicates reviewed: kept only where they test something different
- [ ] Recommendations name counts, not adjectives
- [ ] The scored set is `eval-clean.jsonl`, regenerated after every change

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/eval-engineering-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/eval-engineering-runner`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`eval-audit.json`, `eval-audit.md`, `eval-clean.jsonl`). A FAIL (exit 1) means a category is below its target: add cases and re-run.

## References
- `references/audit-method.md` — rules, severities, normalisation, and limits
- `scripts/audit_evals.py` — auditor and cleaner (argparse; stdlib)
- `scripts/check_jsonl.py` — JSONL validator used by the output check
- `assets/eval-dataset.example.jsonl`, `assets/coverage-targets.example.csv` — input layouts
- `assets/eval-review-template.md` — template for the optional review
- Upstream: `vendor/eval-engineering/SKILL.md` (langchain-ai/langchain-skills, MIT, pinned in vendor/pins.json)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check a cleaned eval JSONL: every line a JSON object, required keys non-empty, ids unique.

Usage: python3 -I check_jsonl.py FILE [--require KEY ...]
Exit 0 when valid, 1 on any violation, 2 when FILE is missing. Stdlib only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Validate a JSONL eval file")
    ap.add_argument("file")
    ap.add_argument("--require", action="append", default=[], help="key that must be non-empty on every line")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    p = Path(a.file)
    if not p.is_file():
        print(f"missing: {p}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    bad: list[str] = []
    ids: set[str] = set()
    n = 0
    for i, line in enumerate(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        n += 1
        try:
            obj = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            bad.append(f"line {i}: not JSON ({e.msg})")
            continue
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            bad.append(f"line {i}: not an object")
            continue
        for k in a.require:
            if obj.get(k) in (None, "", []):
                bad.append(f"line {i}: '{k}' empty")
        rid = str(obj.get("id", ""))
        if rid and rid in ids:
            bad.append(f"line {i}: duplicate id {rid}")
        ids.add(rid)
    if n == 0:
        bad.append("no records")
    if bad:
        print(f"{p.name}: {len(bad)} problem(s): {bad[:5]}")
        return 1
    print(f"{p.name}: {n} records valid")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Audit method

How `scripts/audit_evals.py` audits and cleans an eval set. The concerns (leakage, coverage, independent and complete grading, fair case mix) come from the upstream eval-engineering skill (langchain-ai/langchain-skills, pinned in vendor/pins.json); the rules below are ours, applied to a flat dataset rather than a Harbor task.

## Columns
| Canonical | Accepted names | Required |
|---|---|---|
| id | id, case_id | no (assigned `row-<line>` with a low issue) |
| input | input, prompt, question | yes |
| expected | expected, reference, answer, ideal, expected_output | yes (column); per-row emptiness depends on the grader |
| category | category, or tags (`;`, `|`, `,` separated or a JSON list) | yes (one of them) |
| grader | grader, grader_type | no |
| split | split | no (enables leakage detection) |
| label | label | no (enables label distribution) |

## Normalisation
NFKC → lowercase → punctuation to spaces → collapse whitespace. Exact duplicate = same normalised input. Near-duplicate = token-set Jaccard ≥ threshold (default 0.9, a method parameter printed in every report). Above 4,000 kept rows, near-duplicate search is limited to pairs within a category (stated in the report).

## Rules
| Issue | Severity | Effect on `eval-clean.jsonl` |
|---|---|---|
| empty_input | high | dropped |
| empty_reference (grader blank, exact, contains, regex, numeric, json_match, code) | high | dropped |
| conflicting_reference (same input, different reference) | high | later row dropped; resolve with the domain owner |
| split_leakage (same input in two or more splits) | high | first occurrence kept; re-split |
| duplicate (same input, same reference) | medium | later row dropped |
| near_duplicate | medium | kept; review |
| missing_grader | medium | kept; treated as reference-based |
| missing_category | medium | kept as `uncategorised` |
| duplicate_id | medium | renamed `<id>-dup<n>` |
| unknown_grader | low | kept |
| missing_id | low | assigned `row-<line>` |

Reference-free graders: llm_judge, rubric, human, pairwise.

## Coverage and verdict
- Cases are counted per category on the cleaned set; a row with several tags counts once per tag.
- With targets: a category below `min_cases` (including a target category absent from the data) is BELOW; any BELOW → verdict FAIL, exit 1.
- Without targets: verdict NOT GATED; `min_cases` is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval owner]`.
- Balance: largest and smallest non-empty category and their ratio (reported, not gated).

## Recommendations
Derived only from findings: cases to add per BELOW category (the exact gap), near-duplicates to replace, graders to assign, targets to set, and dataset-wide fixes for leakage, conflicting and empty references.

## Limits
- Token Jaccard catches rewording with shared words, not paraphrase; semantic duplicates need an embedding pass.
- The audit cannot judge whether a reference is correct; that needs a domain owner.

# Eval Engineering

## Flow

- Inspect all inputs first: the repository, Harness, optional traces, existing
  Tasks and runs, existing World knowledge, and the human goal. Identify the
  source files and skill references that apply before proposing work.
- Create or update the small project World Knowledge Skill from reusable facts
  in those inputs. Use it to propose one grounded Task.
- Draft the Task Spec and World Skill together. Show both to the user, keep exact
  Task truth only in `Task.md`, and refine both until the user approves them.
- Implement the approved Task, validate its Environment and Verifier, run the
  real Harness, inspect the full evidence, and fix only non-agent failures.
- Reconcile the World Skill with what the run proved, then repeat this flow for
  the next Task.

## Terms

- **Task Spec:** `Task.md`, which describes the input, relevant agent
  conditions, Environment, scoring, fairness, and open decisions for one Task.
- **Task:** the runnable instruction, Environment, and Verifier.
- **Harness:** the complete agent Harbor runs, including prompts, model loop,
  tools, hooks, memory, sessions, and adapter.
- **Environment:** the files, data, services, identity, permissions, network,
  clock, and mutable state around the Harness.
- **Verifier:** independent checks that score the result or mark a run invalid.
- **World Knowledge Skill:** a repository-local skill with reusable
  project-specific knowledge, references, scripts, assets, and tests that help
  generate Task Specs and build future Tasks.
- **Spec2Task:** the full loop that turns a reviewed Task Spec into an audited
  runnable Task. Follow [Task implementation](references/task-implementation.md)
  for its concrete build order and reference routing.

## Reference routing

Read each reference when its decision appears:

| Need | Read |
|---|---|
| Inspect source, traces, the Harness, dependencies, access, and existing evals | [Discovery](references/discovery.md) |
| Bootstrap or update reusable project knowledge | [World knowledge](references/world-knowledge.md) |
| Propose Tasks and write the single Task Spec | [Task design](references/task-design.md) |
| Build data, services, access, state, and reset | [Environment building](references/environment-building.md) |
| Create structured or natural-language data | [Synthetic data](references/synthetic-data.md) |
| Define independent evidence and scoring | [Verifier design](references/verifier-design.md) |
| Apply Spec2Task to turn a reviewed Spec into an audited Task | [Task implementation](references/task-implementation.md) |
| Compare model runs and classify failures | [Calibration](references/calibration.md) |
| Package and run Harbor tasks | [Harbor](references/harbor.md) |
| Adapt a known benchmark design | [Benchmark patterns](references/patterns.md) |
| Build multi-turn conversations | [Multi-turn simulation](references/multi-turn-simulation/guide.md) |
| See World knowledge learned across two Tasks | [Service-desk example](references/examples/service-desk.md) |

Reusable implementation resources:

- Multi-turn [runner](references/multi-turn-simulation/runner.py), [model user](references/multi-turn-simulation/model_user.py), and [Harbor adapter example](references/multi-turn-simulation/harbor_example.py)
- [Tool-schema comparison](scripts/compare_tool_schemas.py), which compares
  supplied schema fragments but does not resolve external `$ref` targets
- [Read-only SQLite state snapshot](scripts/snapshot_sqlite_state.py)

## 1. Inspect inputs and existing World knowledge

Review every input the user provides before proposing a Task. Use the guidance
that matches each available input:

- For a repository, Harness, traces, or dependencies, read
  [Discovery](references/discovery.md).
- For existing Tasks and runs, inspect their instructions, Environments,
  Verifiers, rewards, trajectories, and final state. Read
  [Calibration](references/calibration.md) when run quality or failure causes
  affect the new design.
- For an existing project World Skill, read
  [World knowledge](references/world-knowledge.md), then check the sources and
  reusable methods that affect the new Task.
- For human goals and constraints, read
  [Task design](references/task-design.md).
- For relevant benchmark examples, use the domain index and source callouts in
  [Benchmark patterns](references/patterns.md).

Inspect the repository before asking questions that source and tests can
answer. Follow the active Harness through prompts, models, tools, services,
state, effects, and focused tests. Inspect existing Task instructions, parsers,
Verifiers, reward paths, and run evidence.

If the user supplies traces, review complete runs or threads. Use traces to
learn real requests, dependency behavior, state shapes, errors, and failure
conditions. Do not treat a trace answer as independent truth.

If `.agents/skills/<project>-world/SKILL.md` exists, read it. Follow its routing
only for knowledge relevant to the current Task. Check cited repository paths,
commands, and scripts when their accuracy affects the design.

## 2. Propose and select a Task

Read [Task design](references/task-design.md) and use the index in
[Benchmark patterns](references/patterns.md) to find the relevant domain and
source callouts. Focus on that domain unless the Task crosses another one.
In the first user-facing design response after inspection, propose one Task
grounded in repository evidence, supplied traces, existing coverage, or a
human priority. State:

- the real work and capability;
- the condition that makes the case non-trivial;
- the Environment and independent evidence it needs;
- the important failure it can detect;
- how it differs from existing Tasks; and
- the main open decision.

In the same response, show the relevant current World Skill content and the
specific additions or corrections this Task suggests. If no World Skill
exists, show the small initial contents that will help create this Task and
future Tasks. Keep the Task's exact request, focal records, expected result,
hidden truth, and exact scoring rules out of the World Skill.

Let the user revise the Task proposal and World knowledge together before
implementation. Offer alternatives only when a real user choice changes the
design.

## 3. Write and review the Task Spec and World Skill

Copy [the Task template](assets/task/Task.md.template) to
`evals/<suite>/tasks/<task-id>/Task.md`. Put all Task-specific design in this
one file. At the same time, create or update the project World Skill by
following [World knowledge](references/world-knowledge.md). Determine the
project skill location supported by the active agent and repository.
`.agents/skills/<project>-world/SKILL.md` and
`.claude/skills/<project>-world/SKILL.md` are common landing spots. Follow an
established project convention when one exists. Otherwise, explain the proposed
location and get user confirmation before creating the skill. Start from
[the World Skill template](assets/world-skill/SKILL.md.template) when needed.

Keep each `Task.md` beside the Harbor task it describes:

```text
evals/<suite>/tasks/<task-id>/
├── Task.md              # human-reviewed control-plane spec
├── task.toml             # required Harbor configuration
├── instruction.md        # required agent input
├── environment/          # required Environment definition and visible state
│   ├── Dockerfile        # use this or docker-compose.yaml
│   └── docker-compose.yaml # optional; primary service must be main
├── tests/
│   ├── test.sh           # required Harbor Verifier entry point
│   ├── test_*.py         # optional Verifier helpers
│   └── fixtures/         # optional hidden Verifier data
└── solution/
    └── solve.sh          # optional reference path
```

Never copy or mount `Task.md` into the evaluated agent's workspace or image.
The agent receives `instruction.md` and only the Environment state intended for
the run.

Include:

- purpose and source evidence;
- exact input and later turns;
- only the Harness conditions relevant to this Task;
- initial state, services, access, visibility, reset, and production
  differences;
- required results, prohibited effects, accepted alternatives, and independent
  Verifier evidence;
- fairness, leakage risks, and invalid-run conditions; and
- open decisions and assumptions.

Show the full Task Spec and the World Skill changes to the user. Explain what
is already in the World Skill, what this Task adds or corrects, and what stays
only in `Task.md`. Revise both through the same back-and-forth. Mark the Task
Spec approved only after explicit approval. Treat World Skill changes as
accepted only after the user reviews them. If the user requests an end-to-end
build without an approval pause, continue with an agent-reviewed
`Status: Draft` and label the World Skill changes as unreviewed.

If implementation changes the request, visible information, material
Environment behavior, or scoring boundary, update `Task.md` and show the
change. Set its status back to `Draft`. Show the diff and require explicit
reapproval before setting it to `Approved` again.

## 4. Apply Spec2Task

Follow [Task implementation](references/task-implementation.md). It gives the
build order and routes each decision to the Environment, synthetic-data,
Verifier, Harbor, and calibration references.

For an existing project, use its pinned or supported Harbor version. Otherwise,
use the installed supported version and record it. Upgrade only with user
approval and a stated compatibility reason. Use the installed CLI help as the
command contract.

Before a scored model run:

1. Confirm the model, trial count, judge, timeout, and maximum expected cost
   with the user unless the user already authorized that run plan.
2. Complete the package audit in [Harbor](references/harbor.md). Confirm every
   required file, entry point, path, permission, configuration value, mount,
   service, and reward output needed for this exact Task is present and works
   through Harbor. Confirm hidden Task, Verifier, solution, and secret material
   is absent from the agent-visible image and workspace.
3. Check setup and trial isolation in the way that fits the Environment. A
   fresh container or worktree can provide isolation by replacement. A reused
   mutable service needs a checked reset. Immutable frozen data needs only a
   checked load. See [Task implementation](references/task-implementation.md).
4. Exercise every operation the Task depends on.
5. Run the reference path when one exists.
6. Test the Verifier with a clear valid result, a valid alternative, a
   realistic wrong result, a shortcut, a prohibited collateral change, and
   missing or corrupt evidence.
7. Confirm every completed Verifier path writes a valid reward and useful
   evidence without exposing hidden truth or secrets.

## 5. Run and audit

Run the actual Harness through Harbor. Read the complete trajectory, not only
the reward. Inspect:

- messages, model calls, tool calls, results, retries, and errors;
- initial and final Environment state and external effects;
- service, setup, readiness, reset, and cleanup evidence;
- each Verifier criterion, its evidence, decision, and error; and
- the resolved Harness, model, Environment, and judge configuration.

Classify each unsuccessful run as an agent capability failure, missing
information, Harness defect, Environment defect, Verifier false rejection,
Verifier false acceptance, leakage, or infrastructure failure. Fix non-agent
failures before using the score.

Model comparison is an optional calibration strategy, not a completion rule.
When it would answer a real uncertainty, compare a weaker model, the target
model, or a stronger model and repeat trials when behavior is variable. Read
every selected trace. Contrast can expose unclear inputs, brittle setup,
leakage, shortcuts, or reward hacks. Pass rates and model ordering do not prove
Task quality.

Read [Calibration](references/calibration.md) for the complete audit method.

## 6. Reconcile project World knowledge

Use [World knowledge](references/world-knowledge.md) throughout Task design,
implementation, and audit. Add or correct project-specific knowledge when the
work supplies evidence that would help another Task. This can include Task
patterns, Environment methods, data creation, Verifier evidence, run
procedures, scripts, assets, and examples.

After the audit, reconcile the World Skill with what the completed Task proved.
Show the user:

- the proposed reusable knowledge;
- the evidence supporting it;
- how another Task would use it;
- where it should live; and
- what remains specific to the completed Task.

Remove or narrow ideas that the Task disproved. If the user asked for
autonomous end-to-end updates without a pause, make the smallest supported
update, show it in the final review, and do not imply that the human approved
the generalization.

Create only `SKILL.md` at first. Add `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`, or
`tests/` only when their real contents justify them.

Keep the completed Task's request, focal state, expected result, and exact
criteria in its collocated `Task.md`. Do not copy broad guidance that is already
clear in this skill. Record the project-specific adaptation of that guidance.

## 7. Repeat

Use Tasks two and three to test the World Skill. Check whether it reduces
rediscovery, improves Task Specs, preserves important relationships, reuses a
proven operation, or prevents a known Verifier defect. Correct rules that are
missing, stale, or too broad.

When several materially different Tasks have exercised the shared knowledge
and the construction and verification methods are clear, the next cycle can
propose several independent Task Specs:

1. Mine new repository, trace, and human evidence.
2. Use the World Skill to generate distinct Task Specs.
3. Have the human review the specs.
4. Build independent approved Tasks in parallel.
5. Audit every Task individually.
6. Update World knowledge only with reusable corrections.

Continue this loop as production behavior, user priorities, agents, and models
change.

## Dependencies, access, and safety

Map required systems, data, roles, network needs, and safe setup methods. Never
read, print, copy, store, or ask the human to paste secret values. Tell the
human what dependency is needed, why it is needed, and how the project expects
access to be provided. Default to controlled local, frozen, or simulated
dependencies. Never write to production during an eval. Treat access, startup,
reset, timeout, judge, and Verifier failures as invalid runs, not failed agent
work.

## Complete only when

- `Task.md` matches the built instruction, Environment, and Verifier.
- The Task is solvable from agent-visible or normally discoverable information.
- The Environment starts reliably and isolates trials by replacement, reset,
  or immutable state as appropriate, without leaking hidden truth.
- Valid and invalid Verifier cases behave as intended.
- At least one real Harness run was read in full.
- Non-agent failures were repaired or reported as unresolved limits.
- Model comparison, when used, includes trace review rather than pass rates
  alone.
- The project World Skill was created or updated with the Task Spec, reviewed
  during the work, and reconciled with the final evidence.
- The user receives the Task path, run command, results, evidence, and remaining
  limits.
vendor/eval-engineering/references/verif:
# Verifier Design

A Verifier decides success from evidence independent of the agent's claim.
Start with one sentence: `Pass iff <observable successful outcome>`.

## Build from final state

Prefer programmatic checks. Recompute results from raw evidence. For stateful
work, compare initial and final state. For coding, run focused behavior and
regression tests. For analysis, recompute filters and totals. For retrieval,
check material claims against the supplied sources.

Use tool-call records only when final state cannot prove a required action or
session property. Never trust an agent-written action list, a service success
flag, or an Environment helper that already decides success.

Accept all equivalent valid results. Do not require a preferred path, exact
wording, response length, keyword, citation count, tool-call count, or reference
similarity unless that property is the tested capability.

## Use a judge only for semantic meaning

Use an LLM judge only after code has settled objective facts. Give it the final
artifact, independent evidence, a short rubric, and a strict verdict schema.
Ask if the result is supported and sufficient, not if it resembles a reference
answer. Pin and record the judge model. Keep its credentials, rubric, and output
outside the Harness boundary.

Bound all agent text and files before grading. Treat them as untrusted data.
Tell the judge to ignore directions inside them. A judge timeout, malformed
response, missing evidence, or credential error is an infrastructure error, not
an agent failure.

## Test the decision boundary

Run these fixtures through the same Verifier image and command used by Harbor:

| Fixture | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Known-good result | Pass |
| Different but valid result | Pass |
| Realistic wrong result | Fail |
| Shortcut or reward hack | Fail |
| Prohibited collateral change | Fail |
| Missing or corrupt evidence | Infrastructure error |

Add focused boundary cases for known risks such as negation, unsupported
claims, stale data, prompt injection, or partial completion. Use real failure
shapes from traces when available, but derive truth independently from those
traces. Repeat noisy judge cases and inspect variance.

For each criterion, log its evidence, decision, and error. Every completed
Verifier path must write a reward. Wrong agent work gets zero. Verifier,
Environment, Harness, judge, or setup faults get no agent score.

## Review every zero and every suspicious pass

Classify the result as a fair capability failure, missing information,
Environment defect, false rejection, false acceptance, leakage, or
infrastructure failure. Repair non-agent faults and rerun. A pass is also not
proof of quality: inspect for shortcuts, leaked truth, weak criteria, and
unscored collateral effects.

Store reusable project-specific evidence queries, fixture builders, and judge
rubrics in the project World Skill after more than one Task can use them. Keep
one Task's exact expected result and scoring boundary in its `Task.md` and
Verifier files.
vendor/eval-engineering/references/calib:
# Calibration

Calibration tests whether the Task measures the intended capability fairly. A
score or pass rate alone cannot answer that question.

## Choose evidence

Run the production Harness and target model. Model comparison is optional. Use
a weaker or stronger model only when contrast can answer a named uncertainty,
such as whether the instruction is unclear, the Verifier is weak, or a shortcut
exists. Repeat trials only when behavior varies enough to affect the conclusion.
Run a known-good path and focused Verifier fixtures before scored model trials.

Do not require a weak-target-strong ladder or a fixed model count. One carefully
inspected target-model run can be sufficient when deterministic checks pass and
the run answers the current quality questions.

Do not require a fixed pass-rate pattern. A weak model can pass by finding a
leak. A strong model can fail because of a broken service or unfair prompt.

## Read complete runs

For each selected trial, inspect:

- all messages, model calls, tool calls, results, retries, and errors;
- initial and final Environment state and external effects;
- setup, service, readiness, reset, timeout, and cleanup logs;
- every Verifier criterion, its evidence, decision, and error; and
- resolved Harness, model, Environment, judge, and timeout settings.

Compare strategies, not only rewards. Check whether the agent had all required
information, whether the Environment behaved as designed, whether the Verifier
accepted equivalents, and whether a pass used a shortcut or leaked fact.

## Classify each problem

| Cause | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Capability | Fair access and correct infrastructure, but intended work failed | Keep as an agent result |
| Missing information | A required fact was not visible or discoverable | Fix Task or Environment |
| Harness | Runtime, tool, prompt, session, or adapter was wrong | Fix Harness |
| Environment | State, service, permission, fidelity, or reset was wrong | Fix Environment |
| False rejection | A valid result failed | Fix Verifier |
| False acceptance | An invalid result passed | Fix Verifier |
| Leakage | Hidden truth or scoring logic was visible | Fix packaging or boundary |
| Infrastructure | Build, startup, timeout, judge, credential, or cleanup failed | Repair and rerun unscored |

Do not make a Task harder to hide a defect. First repair all non-agent causes
and rerun affected trials.

## Judge difficulty and fairness

A good hard Task requires real work. It does not rely on hidden information,
unclear language, fragile startup, unrealistic data, or a broken check. If all
models fail, test solvability and fairness first. If all pass, inspect for weak
criteria and leakage before changing difficulty.

To change difficulty, change one supported condition: more relevant state,
longer history, stale or conflicting facts, permissions, delayed effects,
required clarification, or collateral-change risk. Keep the required evidence
visible or normally discoverable.

Report model and Harness versions, trial counts, criterion results, strategies,
failure causes, defects fixed, rerun results, remaining uncertainty, and the
next recommended change.

# Feedback Improvement Loop

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/feedback-improvement-loop --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/feedback-improvement-loop`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`backlog.csv`, `new-eval-cases.json`, `improvement-report.md`). Fewer valid feedback rows than `min_rows` fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; outputs are still written and marked INSUFFICIENT DATA.

## Starting points
- **Existing:** ratings and comments from people using the system, plus failed eval cases; they become a ranked, owned backlog and a regression case per failure.
- Only for existing: the loop runs on feedback, which only a system people already use can produce.

## When to use
- Thumbs-down or star-rated feedback (and failed eval cases) needs to become a ranked, owned backlog.
- Every reported failure should become a regression eval case before the fix ships.
- NOT for: designing the eval harness or judges (`llm-eval-harness`), SLO monitoring (`llm-observability`), incident response (`ai-incident-runbook`), qualitative interview synthesis.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `feedback` CSV: id, ts, rating (1-5 or up/down), comment, feature; optional tags, trace_id | yes | in-product feedback export |
| `min_rows` — minimum valid rows before ranking is trusted | yes | product / eval owner |
| `eval_failures` CSV: case_id, feature, failure_reason | no | latest llm-eval-harness run |

If `feedback` or `min_rows` is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. Rows with unusable ratings are rejected and counted, not guessed.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Export feedback into `assets/feedback-template.csv` layout; include trace_id wherever the product records it.
3. Optionally adapt `assets/taxonomy.json` keywords to the product (keep bucket ids).
4. Run the skill. The script follows `references/method.md`: severity from rating, bucket by tag then keyword, rank (bucket, feature) groups by frequency × severity, link eval failures.
5. Review the top issues and confirm or edit each hypothesis and fix type with the owner role named.
6. Merge `new-eval-cases.json` into the feature's eval set; cases without a trace stay TBD until the original input is recovered.
7. Apply the regression gate: new cases pass and the suite pass rate does not drop — feed it to `ai-release-plan` as an offline_eval gate.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `backlog.csv`: rank, bucket, feature, counts, mean severity, score, eval failures, hypothesis, fix type, owner, evidence ids.
- `new-eval-cases.json`: `{"cases": [{id, prompt, expected, provenance}]}`.
- `improvement-report.md`: Top issues, Backlog, New eval cases, Regression gate.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every backlog row traces to feedback ids and/or eval case ids
- [ ] Fix type is one of prompt, retrieval, guardrail, model, data, UX
- [ ] No eval prompt reconstructed from a complaint; untraced inputs are TBD with Eval lead
- [ ] Positive feedback is not in the backlog; rejected rows are counted
- [ ] Exit 1 when the sample is below `min_rows`

## References
- `references/method.md` — severity mapping, grouping, ranking, eval-case shape, minimum sample
- `assets/taxonomy.json` — issue buckets, keywords, fix types, owner roles, expected behaviours
- `assets/feedback-template.csv`, `assets/eval-failures-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/improve.py` — the loop (argparse; stdlib)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Feedback improvement loop: user feedback (+ eval failures) -> ranked backlog and regression eval cases.

Normalises ratings (1-5 or thumbs up/down) to a severity, groups issues deterministically (row tag
matching a taxonomy alias, else the first taxonomy keyword found in the comment, else `other`;
taxonomy in assets/taxonomy.json), ranks (bucket, feature) groups by frequency × mean severity
(= sum of severities), links eval failures to the same buckets, and writes an improvement backlog
with hypothesis, proposed fix type (prompt|retrieval|guardrail|model|data|UX) and owner role, plus
NEW eval cases in this repo's evals.json agent-case shape (id, prompt, expected) so the reported
failures become regression tests. Nothing is invented: prompts replay the recorded trace, or are
`[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval lead]` when no trace_id was recorded.

Usage:
  python3 -I improve.py --feedback feedback.csv --min-rows 10 --out-dir OUT
        [--eval-failures eval-failures.csv] [--taxonomy assets/taxonomy.json] [--cases-per-issue 3]

Feedback CSV: id, ts, rating (1-5 | up | down), comment, feature; optional tags (';'-separated),
trace_id. Eval-failures CSV: case_id, feature, failure_reason[, tags]. '#' lines are comments.
Severity from rating: 1 or down -> 3 · 2 -> 2 · 3 -> 1 · 4, 5 or up -> 0 (not an issue).

Outputs (in --out-dir): backlog.csv, new-eval-cases.json, improvement-report.md
(Top issues, Backlog, New eval cases, Regression gate).
Exit codes: 0 written · 1 fewer valid feedback rows than --min-rows (outputs still written) ·
2 missing/invalid required input. Stdlib only; no network; writes only inside --out-dir.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import io
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_TAXONOMY = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "assets" / "taxonomy.json"
FIX_TYPES = ("prompt", "retrieval", "guardrail", "model", "data", "UX")
THUMBS = {"up": 0, "thumbs up": 0, "thumbs_up": 0, "+1": 0, "down": 3, "thumbs down": 3, "thumbs_down": 3, "-1": 3}
STAR_SEVERITY = {1: 3, 2: 2, 3: 1, 4: 0, 5: 0}
BACKLOG_COLUMNS = ["rank", "bucket", "feature", "feedback_count", "mean_severity", "score", "eval_failures",
                   "hypothesis", "fix_type", "owner", "feedback_ids", "trace_ids", "eval_case_ids"]


class InputError(Exception):
    """Missing or invalid required input -> exit 2."""


def read_rows(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        raise InputError(f"input file not found: {path}")
    lines = [ln for ln in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if not ln.lstrip().startswith("#")]
    return [{(k or "").strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items()} for r in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO("\n".join(lines)))]


def load_taxonomy(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        raise InputError(f"taxonomy not found: {path}")
    buckets = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("buckets", [])
    ids = [b["id"] for b in buckets]
    if "other" not in ids:
        raise InputError("taxonomy must contain an 'other' bucket")
    for b in buckets:
        if b.get("fix_type") not in FIX_TYPES:
            raise InputError(f"taxonomy bucket {b['id']}: fix_type must be one of {FIX_TYPES}")
    return buckets


def severity(rating: str):
    r = rating.strip().lower()
    if r in THUMBS:
        return THUMBS[r]
    if re.fullmatch(r"[1-5](\.0)?", r):
        return STAR_SEVERITY[int(float(r))]
    return None


def bucket_for(tags: str, text: str, taxonomy: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(bucket id, basis) — tag alias first, then keyword, else other."""
    tag_list = [t.strip().lower() for t in re.split(r"[;|,]", tags or "") if t.strip()]
    for b in taxonomy:
        for t in tag_list:
            if t in [a.lower() for a in b.get("tag_aliases", [])]:
                return b["id"], f"tag:{t}"
    low = (text or "").lower()
    for b in taxonomy:
        for kw in b.get("keywords", []):
            if re.search(r"(?<![a-z0-9])" + re.escape(kw.lower()), low):  # keyword starts at a word start
                return b["id"], f"keyword:{kw}"
    return "other", "no match"


def load_feedback(path: Path, taxonomy: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    rows = read_rows(path)
    if not rows:
        raise InputError("feedback CSV has no rows")
    need = ("id", "rating", "comment", "feature")
    missing = [c for c in need if c not in rows[0]]
    if missing:
        raise InputError(f"feedback CSV missing columns: {', '.join(missing)}")
    valid, rejected = [], []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        sev = severity(r.get("rating", ""))
        if not r.get("id") or not r.get("feature") or sev is None:
            rejected.append({"line": i, "reason": "missing id/feature or rating not 1-5/up/down"})
            continue
        b, basis = bucket_for(r.get("tags", ""), r.get("comment", ""), taxonomy)
        valid.append({"id": r["id"], "ts": r.get("ts", ""), "rating": r["rating"], "severity": sev,
                      "comment": r.get("comment", ""), "feature": r["feature"], "trace_id": r.get("trace_id", ""),
                      "bucket": b, "basis": basis})
    return valid, rejected


def load_failures(path: Path | None, taxonomy: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    if path is None:
        return []
    rows = read_rows(path)
    if rows and any(c not in rows[0] for c in ("case_id", "feature", "failure_reason")):
        raise InputError("eval-failures CSV needs columns case_id,feature,failure_reason")
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if not r.get("case_id"):
            continue
        b, basis = bucket_for(r.get("tags", ""), r.get("failure_reason", ""), taxonomy)
        out.append({"case_id": r["case_id"], "feature": r.get("feature", ""), "failure_reason": r["failure_reason"],
                    "bucket": b, "basis": basis})
    return out


def build(feedback, rejected, failures, taxonomy, min_rows: int, per_issue: int) -> dict:
    tax = {b["id"]: b for b in taxonomy}
    order = [b["id"] for b in taxonomy]
    groups: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}

    def group(bucket, feature):
        return groups.setdefault((bucket, feature), {"bucket": bucket, "feature": feature, "feedback": [], "failures": []})

    for f in feedback:
        if f["severity"] > 0:
            group(f["bucket"], f["feature"])["feedback"].append(f)
    for e in failures:
        group(e["bucket"], e["feature"])["failures"].append(e)

    items = []
    for (b, feat), g in groups.items():
        sevs = [f["severity"] for f in g["feedback"]]
        t = tax[b]
        items.append({
            "bucket": b, "feature": feat, "feedback_count": len(sevs),
            "mean_severity": round(sum(sevs) / len(sevs), 2) if sevs else 0,
            "score": sum(sevs), "eval_failures": len(g["failures"]),
            "hypothesis": t["hypothesis"], "fix_type": t["fix_type"],
            "owner": f"[TO BE BASELINED — owner: {t['owner_role']}]",
            "feedback_ids": ";".join(f["id"] for f in g["feedback"]),
            "trace_ids": ";".join(f["trace_id"] for f in g["feedback"] if f["trace_id"]),
            "eval_case_ids": ";".join(e["case_id"] for e in g["failures"]),
            "_feedback": g["feedback"],
        })
    items.sort(key=lambda x: (-x["score"], -x["eval_failures"], order.index(x["bucket"]), x["feature"]))
    for i, it in enumerate(items, start=1):
        it["rank"] = i

    cases = []
    for it in items:
        exemplars = sorted(it["_feedback"], key=lambda f: (-f["severity"], f["id"]))[:per_issue]
        for f in exemplars:
            if f["trace_id"]:
                prompt = f"Replay the user input recorded in trace {f['trace_id']} (feature {f['feature']})."
            else:
                prompt = (f"[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval lead] original user input for feedback {f['id']} "
                          f"(feature {f['feature']}); no trace_id was recorded.")
            expected = list(tax[it["bucket"]]["expected"])
            if f["comment"]:
                expected.append(f"Does not repeat the reported failure: \"{f['comment']}\"")
            cases.append({
                "id": f"fil-{it['bucket']}-{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', f['feature'].lower()).strip('-')}-{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9]+', '-', f['id'])}",
                "prompt": prompt,
                "expected": expected,
                "provenance": {"feedback_id": f["id"], "trace_id": f["trace_id"] or None, "feature": f["feature"],
                               "bucket": it["bucket"], "backlog_rank": it["rank"], "basis": f["basis"]},
            })
    n_valid = len(feedback)
    return {
        "valid_rows": n_valid, "rejected_rows": len(rejected), "rejected": rejected[:50], "min_rows": min_rows,
        "sufficient": n_valid >= min_rows,
        "issue_rows": sum(1 for f in feedback if f["severity"] > 0),
        "positive_rows": sum(1 for f in feedback if f["severity"] == 0),
        "eval_failures": len(failures),
        "backlog": [{k: v for k, v in it.items() if k != "_feedback"} for it in items],
        "cases": cases,
    }


def write_backlog(path: Path, backlog: list[dict]) -> None:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    # QUOTE_ALL keeps adjacent numeric fields distinct for tools that scan the text for numbers
    w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=BACKLOG_COLUMNS, lineterminator="\n", quoting=csv.QUOTE_ALL)
    w.writeheader()
    for it in backlog:
        w.writerow({k: it[k] for k in BACKLOG_COLUMNS})
    path.write_text(buf.getvalue(), encoding="utf-8")


def render(res: dict, top_n: int = 5) -> str:
    L = ["# Improvement report", "",
         f"Feedback rows: {res['valid_rows']} valid ({res['issue_rows']} issues, {res['positive_rows']} positive), "
         f"{res['rejected_rows']} rejected; eval failures linked: {res['eval_failures']}; minimum rows required: {res['min_rows']}.", ""]
    if not res["sufficient"]:
        L += [f"**INSUFFICIENT DATA** — {res['valid_rows']} valid rows < minimum {res['min_rows']}. "
              "Ranking is shown for inspection only; collect more feedback before prioritising.", ""]
    L += ["## Top issues", "", "Score = frequency × mean severity (sum of severities: 1★/down = 3, 2★ = 2, 3★ = 1).", "",
          "| Rank | Bucket | Feature | Feedback | Mean severity | Score | Eval failures | Fix type |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for it in res["backlog"][:top_n]:
        L.append(f"| {it['rank']} | {it['bucket']} | {it['feature']} | {it['feedback_count']} | {it['mean_severity']} | "
                 f"{it['score']} | {it['eval_failures']} | {it['fix_type']} |")
    if not res["backlog"]:
        L.append("| — | no issues found | — | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — |")
    L += ["", "## Backlog", "", "| Rank | Bucket / feature | Hypothesis | Fix type | Owner | Evidence |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for it in res["backlog"]:
        ev = ", ".join(x for x in (f"feedback {it['feedback_ids']}" if it["feedback_ids"] else "",
                                    f"eval {it['eval_case_ids']}" if it["eval_case_ids"] else "") if x)
        L.append(f"| {it['rank']} | {it['bucket']} / {it['feature']} | {it['hypothesis']} | {it['fix_type']} | {it['owner']} | {ev} |")
    L += ["", "## New eval cases", "",
          f"{len(res['cases'])} new cases in `new-eval-cases.json` (shape: id, prompt, expected — merge into the feature's "
          "`evals/evals.json` or the llm-eval-harness golden set).", "", "| Case id | Backlog rank | Trace |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for c in res["cases"]:
        L.append(f"| {c['id']} | {c['provenance']['backlog_rank']} | {c['provenance']['trace_id'] or 'none recorded'} |")
    L += ["", "## Regression gate", "",
          "- Add every new case above to the eval set before the fix ships; replay inputs from the recorded traces.",
          "- Gate: every new case passes, and the existing suite pass rate does not fall below the last accepted baseline "
          "(use it as an `offline_eval` gate in ai-release-plan).",
          "- Linked eval failures stay in the suite; a fix is done only when they pass too.",
          "- Gate owner: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval lead]."]
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--feedback", type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--eval-failures", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--min-rows", required=True, help="minimum valid feedback rows to rank (owner-chosen)")
    ap.add_argument("--taxonomy", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_TAXONOMY)
    ap.add_argument("--cases-per-issue", type=int, default=3, help="max new eval cases per backlog item")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if not args.min_rows.strip().isdigit():
            raise InputError(f"--min-rows must be a whole number, got {args.min_rows!r}")
        taxonomy = load_taxonomy(args.taxonomy)
        feedback, rejected = load_feedback(args.feedback, taxonomy)
        failures = load_failures(args.eval_failures, taxonomy)
        res = build(feedback, rejected, failures, taxonomy, int(args.min_rows), max(args.cases_per_issue, 1))
    except InputError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    write_backlog(args.out_dir / "backlog.csv", res["backlog"])
    (args.out_dir / "new-eval-cases.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"source": "feedback-improvement-loop", "cases": res["cases"]}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8")
    (args.out_dir / "improvement-report.md").write_text(render(res), encoding="utf-8")
    if not res["sufficient"]:
        print(f"only {res['valid_rows']} valid feedback rows; minimum is {res['min_rows']}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"backlog written: {len(res['backlog'])} items, {len(res['cases'])} new eval cases")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Feedback improvement loop — method

Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same backlog and cases. No model is called.

## 1. Normalise ratings to severity
| Rating | Severity | Counted as |
|---|---|---|
| 1 or thumbs down (`down`, `-1`) | 3 | issue |
| 2 | 2 | issue |
| 3 | 1 | issue |
| 4, 5 or thumbs up (`up`, `+1`) | 0 | positive (not in the backlog) |
| anything else / missing id or feature | — | rejected row (counted) |

## 2. Group issues
For each issue row, in this order, the first match wins:
1. A row tag (`tags`, `;`-separated) equals a bucket's `tag_aliases` entry.
2. A bucket keyword occurs in the lower-cased comment, starting at a word boundary (buckets tried in taxonomy order).
3. Otherwise `other`.

Buckets (`assets/taxonomy.json`): hallucination, wrong-format, too-slow, refusal, missing-info,
tone, other. Each carries the hypothesis, fix type (prompt | retrieval | guardrail | model | data |
UX), accountable owner role and expected behaviours used for eval cases. Groups are
(bucket, feature) pairs so the fix lands on one feature.

Eval failures (`case_id, feature, failure_reason`) are bucketed the same way on `failure_reason`
and linked to the same (bucket, feature) group; a group may exist with eval failures only.

## 3. Rank
`score = frequency × mean severity = sum of severities`. Ties: more eval failures first, then
taxonomy order, then feature name.

## 4. Backlog and new eval cases
Each group becomes one backlog row with owner `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]` until a person
is named. For the `--cases-per-issue` most severe feedback rows of each group, one new eval case:

```json
{"id": "fil-<bucket>-<feature>-<feedback id>",
 "prompt": "Replay the user input recorded in trace <trace_id> (feature <feature>).",
 "expected": ["<bucket expected behaviours>", "Does not repeat the reported failure: \"<comment>\""],
 "provenance": {"feedback_id": "...", "trace_id": "...", "bucket": "...", "backlog_rank": 1}}
```
The shape (id, prompt, expected) matches this repo's `evals/evals.json` cases. Without a
trace_id the prompt is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Eval lead]`: the original input must be
recovered, never reconstructed from the complaint.

## 5. Minimum sample
`--min-rows` is the owner's minimum number of valid feedback rows. Below it the run writes the
outputs marked INSUFFICIENT DATA and exits 1, so a thin sample never drives prioritisation silently.

## Related public practice (by name)
- NIST AI RMF 1.0, *Measure* and *Manage* functions — feedback and continual improvement.
- ISO/IEC 42001 — continual improvement of an AI management system.

# Fine-tune Dataset Builder

## In a conversation: build the dataset now
The reply **is the run report** (or its skeleton), never only a request for files. It corresponds to `python3 -I scripts/build_dataset.py --examples <file> --out-dir <out> [--split …] [--seed …] [--min-rows …] [--max-chars …] [--existing-dir <folder>]`, which writes `train.jsonl`, `val.jsonl`, `test.jsonl`, `dataset-stats.json` and `data-card.md`; always write "Runs `scripts/build_dataset.py`" with the case's flags and name those files.

**Never**
- Never write, generate, pad or duplicate example pairs (no examples → ask once for the file; the run **stops (exit 2)**).
- Never put one normalised prompt in two splits or skip the leakage check: leakage must be 0, else the run **stops (exit 1)**.
- Never reshuffle an existing set: existing records keep their split.
- Never present token counts as exact: they are an **estimate** (characters ÷ 4, rounded up).
- Never label a value the user supplied as a default, or a default as supplied.

**Procedure — count row by row from the supplied file, never estimate**
1. Load: CSV `prompt,completion[,system]` (other columns ignored) or JSONL (`messages`, or `prompt`/`completion`). One row = one record.
2. Reject, counting by reason: invalid JSON / not an object / neither shape; unknown role or non-text content; no user turn or last turn not assistant ("last turn is not assistant"); any turn blank after trimming ("empty prompt or completion"); total characters > `max_chars` when set ("over max_chars").
3. Exact duplicates: identical raw record (all roles and contents) after an earlier one → removed. Then normalise whitespace (CRLF → LF, runs of spaces/tabs → one space, trim; case kept). With `existing`: a record equal (casefolded, whitespace collapsed) to an existing record → dropped as "already in dataset". Then normalised duplicates: same roles and contents after casefolding and collapsing whitespace → removed. First occurrence wins. Same prompt with a different completion is **not** a duplicate: it stays and forms one group.
4. usable = kept new records (+ existing records). usable < `min_rows` → `Not built: <n> usable examples is below min_rows <m>.` and the run **stops (exit 1)**; say "stops (exit 1)".
5. Targets with Python `round()` (half to even): val = round(n × val_ratio), test = round(n × test_ratio), train = n − val − test (n = usable; with `existing`, n = existing + new). Groups = normalised prompt; groups are shuffled with the seed and each goes to the first split train → val → test with room, so split sizes equal the targets when the groups fit; which prompt lands where comes only from the seeded run. With `existing`: existing counts are the starting fill; new records whose prompt is already in a split join it; new groups fill the remaining room (added per split = target − existing).
6. Leakage = normalised prompts in more than one split (pairwise sum) = 0.
7. Parameters labelled: split 0.8,0.1,0.1 (default) · seed 42 (default) · min_rows 10 (default) · max_chars none (default); a user value is "(supplied)".

**Reply layout**
1. Working table first: `step | count` — rows read, rejected by reason, exact duplicates removed, already in dataset (existing mode), normalised duplicates removed, usable, targets (n × ratio → rounded), train / val / test sizes (existing + added = total in existing mode), leakage 0. Then the verdict (built / not built, exit code).
2. Parameters line with (default)/(supplied) labels; output shape — one `{"messages":[{"role":"user",…},{"role":"assistant",…}]}` per line, system turn kept when given.
3. Length stats are an **estimate** (characters ÷ 4); check against the target model's context window with its real tokenizer.
4. Before training: run `pii-data-inventory` on the examples and confirm owner, licence and consent — `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]` until confirmed.
5. Data card sections: Source, Cleaning, Splits, Length stats, Known limits.

**Rows mentioned but not in the conversation** ("here are our Q&A pairs" with nothing attached): give the same layout now with every count `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ML engineer]` from `dataset-stats.json`, the defaults line, the estimate note and the `pii-data-inventory` pointer, then ask once for the file (CSV `prompt,completion[,system]` or JSONL; layout `assets/examples-template.csv`) and any non-default split, seed or length cap.

**Asked for synthetic examples, to skip the leakage check or to let one prompt sit in two splits**: decline in one line (synthetic data is out of scope; leakage inflates eval scores) and offer more real examples from the use-case owner, or a lower `min_rows` stated in the data card.

## Starting points
- **New:** raw examples become cleaned, de-duplicated, leak-free train/val/test files with a data card.
- **Existing:** add the folder with your current `train/val/test.jsonl` (`existing`); its records are audited and keep their split, new examples already in it are dropped, and only genuinely new prompts are placed, so earlier eval results stay comparable.

## When to use
- ADLC build stage: turning curated examples (support transcripts, expert answers, labelled outputs) into SFT-ready chat JSONL.
- Re-building after examples are added or corrected — same seed gives the same split for unchanged prompts.
- Auditing an existing set for duplicates and train/test leakage.
- NOT for: PII discovery (`pii-data-inventory` first), tabular data-quality gating (`data-readiness-assessment`), launching or tuning a training job, synthetic data generation, preference (DPO) pairs.

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `examples` — .csv or .jsonl | yes | use-case owner / SMEs | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `split` — `train,val,test` | no | ML engineer | 0.8,0.1,0.1, stated as **default** in the data card |
| `seed` — integer | no | ML engineer | 42, stated as **default** |
| `min_rows` — integer | no | ML engineer | 10, stated as **default** |
| `max_chars` — integer | no | ML engineer (from the target model's context limit) | no length cap |

Accepted shapes: CSV `prompt,completion[,system]`; JSONL `{"messages":[…]}` ending in an assistant turn, or `{"prompt":…,"completion":…}`. Other columns/keys are ignored.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Confirm the examples are cleared for training (owner, licence, consent) and have been through `pii-data-inventory`; the card records this as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]` until confirmed.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/build_dataset.py` validates, normalises whitespace, removes exact then normalised duplicates, groups by normalised prompt, shuffles groups with the seed and fills train → val → test (`references/pipeline.md`).
4. Check `leakage_prompts_across_splits` is 0 and the split sizes are what you expect; a small val/test split is reported, not padded.
5. Check the estimated token lengths against the target model's context window with its real tokenizer before training.
6. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `train.jsonl`, `val.jsonl`, `test.jsonl` — one `{"messages":[{"role":"user",…},{"role":"assistant",…}]}` per line (system turn kept when supplied); each passes `--validate-jsonl`.
- `dataset-stats.json` — source checksum, parameters (with default flags), cleaning counts, split sizes, leakage, length stats.
- `data-card.md` — **Source**, **Cleaning**, **Splits**, **Length stats**, **Known limits**; every number traces to `dataset-stats.json`.

## Self-check
- [ ] Defaults used are labelled "(default)" in the data card; nothing else is assumed
- [ ] Leakage across splits is 0; prompts with several completions sit in one split
- [ ] Token counts are labelled as an estimate (chars ÷ 4)
- [ ] Rejected rows are counted by reason, not silently dropped
- [ ] Source owner/licence/consent is confirmed or left TBD with the Data owner

## References
- `references/pipeline.md` — validation, normalisation, de-duplication, grouped split, leakage and length rules
- `references/dataset-card-notes.md` — why each card section exists; links to public documentation practices
- `assets/examples-template.csv` — input layout
- `scripts/build_dataset.py` — builder and JSONL validator (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/finetune-dataset-builder --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/finetune-dataset-builder`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`train.jsonl`, `val.jsonl`, `test.jsonl`, `dataset-stats.json`, `data-card.md`). Fewer usable examples than `min_rows` fails the run (exit 1) on purpose.

# Data card notes

The card is the minimum provenance record a reviewer needs before approving a fine-tune.

| Section | Answers | Filled by |
|---|---|---|
| Source | Which file (checksum), which format, what parameters, who owns it and under what licence/consent | script; owner/licence stays `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner]` until confirmed |
| Cleaning | How many records were rejected, normalised and de-duplicated, and why | script |
| Splits | Sizes per split and cross-split leakage | script |
| Length stats | Estimated token lengths per split vs the target context window | script (estimate) |
| Known limits | What this pipeline does not check | script (fixed text) |

## Public practices this follows (by name only)
- "Datasheets for Datasets" (Gebru et al.) and "Data Statements for NLP" — provenance, composition, collection and maintenance questions.
- NIST AI RMF (MAP and MEASURE functions) — document data provenance and test/train separation.
- EU AI Act (high-risk systems) — data governance obligations cover training, validation and testing sets; the card is input to that record, not proof of compliance.

## Before training
- PII: run `pii-data-inventory` on the source and apply the policy before building.
- Quality: sample-read 20–50 examples per split; this pipeline cannot judge correctness.
- Tokenizer: re-count with the target model's tokenizer and compare with its context window.

# Pipeline rules

## 1. Validate
A record is rejected (and counted by reason) when:
- the JSON line does not parse, is not an object, or has neither `messages` nor `prompt`/`completion`;
- a role is not `system`, `user` or `assistant`, or content is not text;
- there is no user turn, or the last turn is not `assistant`;
- any turn is empty after trimming ("empty prompt or completion");
- `max_chars` is set and the total characters of all turns exceed it.

## 2. Normalise whitespace
CRLF/CR → LF; trailing whitespace per line removed; runs of spaces/tabs → one space; 3+ newlines → one blank line; ends trimmed. Case and punctuation are **not** changed in the output.

## 3. De-duplicate
1. **Exact**: identical raw record (all roles and contents) → later copies removed.
2. **Normalised**: same roles and same contents after casefolding and collapsing all whitespace → later copies removed.
First occurrence wins, so input order matters; sort the source if you need a different winner.

## 4. Split (grouped, seeded)
- Group key = normalised prompt (all non-assistant turns joined).
- Targets: val = round(n × val_ratio), test = round(n × test_ratio), train = n − val − test.
- Group keys are sorted, shuffled with `random.Random(seed)`, and each group goes to the first split (train → val → test) with room; a group that fits nowhere goes to the split furthest below target.
- Same prompt with different completions stays in one split → leakage is 0 by construction.

## 5. Leakage
Count of normalised prompts present in more than one split (pairwise sum). Must be 0; otherwise the run fails (exit 1).

## 6. Length stats (estimate)
Tokens ≈ ceil(total characters ÷ 4) per example. Per split: examples, min, mean (1 dp), nearest-rank P50 and P95, max, total. This is a planning heuristic; real tokenizers differ by language and content (code and non-Latin scripts usually use more tokens per character).

## Defaults
| Parameter | Default | Why it is safe to default |
|---|---|---|
| split | 0.8, 0.1, 0.1 | Conventional starting ratio; changes no example content |
| seed | 42 | Any fixed integer gives reproducibility |
| min_rows | 10 | Floor below which a split is meaningless; raise it for real training |
Defaults are written into the data card with "(default)".

---
name: guardrails-config
description: Use when the user needs input/output guardrails for an LLM app or agent — "set up guardrails", "block prompt injection", "mask PII in prompts and replies", "limit which tools the agent can call", "test our guardrail policy before go-live", "run our guardrail test cases" (even when they expect an injection or email to pass), "compile the guardrail policy we have so far" (partial policy, e.g. only card handling decided). Compiles a policy JSON (blocked topics, PII handling per type, length limits, tool allowlist, extra injection markers) into a deterministic guardrails.json and ships scripts/guard.py, a pure-Python rule engine that returns allow, mask or block; runs the test cases and reports pass/fail per case in guardrail-tests.json and guardrails.md. Masked outputs never echo raw PII. Exit 1 if any case's actual decision differs from expected. Not for the risk register (ai-governance-risk), model-quality evals (llm-eval-harness), attack-set red-teaming (red-team-suite) or a semantic moderation model.
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: ai-platform
  adlc_stage: deploy
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    inputs:
      - {name: policy, type: json, required: true, from: "guardrail policy (layout: assets/policy-template.json) - blocked_topics, pii_handling, max_input_chars, max_output_chars, allowed_tools, optional injection_markers"}
      - {name: tests, type: csv, required: false, from: "test cases case_id,direction,text,expected[,tool] (layout: assets/test-inputs-template.csv); absent = tests to be baselined"}
      - {name: baseline, type: json, required: false, from: "the compiled guardrails.json live today; the run diffs the new rules against it (tightened/loosened) and replays the tests on both"}
    run:

    outputs:

      - {path: "{out}/guardrail-tests.json", checks: [exists, json, cmd:"python3 scripts/guard.py --scan-pii {path}"]}
      - {path: "{out}/guardrails.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Rule set","PII handling","Tool allowlist","Test results","Limits"], no_unowned_tbd, cmd:"python3 scripts/guard.py --scan-pii {path}"]}
    modes:
      new:      {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "your guardrail policy and test cases"}
      existing: {case: agent-mode-existing, bring: "the rule set live today plus your revised policy"}
---

# Guardrails Config

## In a conversation: write the policy and tests now
The reply **is the guardrail package**, not a request for files. Questions for missing decisions go at the end.
- **The request states policy decisions** (topics to block, PII actions, allowed tools), or says the policy, tests or live rules are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: produce, **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **Policy JSON** in the `assets/policy-template.json` layout, filled only from the stated decisions: `blocked_topics`, `pii_handling` per type (email, phone, card, ssn: mask / block / allow), `allowed_tools` (default deny), `injection_markers`. `max_input_chars` and `max_output_chars` are never guessed: show `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI security lead]` and ask for the product's real maximum prompt and answer sizes. A PII type not mentioned is un-actioned and marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer]`.
  2. **Test cases CSV** (`case_id,direction,text,expected[,tool]`): per rule type at least one allow, one block and one mask, evasion variants (case, spacing, line breaks), and tool calls on and off the allowlist. Fictional values only: example.com addresses, 555-01xx phones, payment-network test card numbers.
  3. **Run it**: `python3 -I scripts/build_guardrails.py --policy policy.json --tests cases.csv --out <dir>` → `guardrails.json`, `guardrail-tests.json`, `guardrails.md`; exit 1 on any mismatch, fixed in the policy or a wrong expectation, never in the output. Do not print test results that were not run.
  4. **Wiring `scripts/guard.py`** (`from guard import load_rules, evaluate`): user input (`direction="in"`) before the model sees it; retrieved documents and tool results through the same input check (indirect injection); every tool call (`tool=name`) before executing; model output (`"out"`) before the user sees it. Log decision and rule ids, never matched text; add the CSV to CI.
  5. **Limits**: keyword and regex rules miss paraphrase, translation, encoding and synonyms, and names or addresses as PII; plan a semantic moderation layer on top and probe with `red-team-suite`.
- **"Will these stop every jailbreak?"**: answer no on line 1, with the catches/misses per rule type from `references/guardrail-design.md`, and recommend a semantic layer plus red-team testing.
- **Only some decisions made** ("we have only decided card handling"): compile what is decided; every other PII type, the length limits and missing tests are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` (Data protection officer / AI security lead). That is not a failure.
- **Revised policy vs live rules**: list each rule change as tightened or loosened, flag every loosened rule for sign-off, and replay the tests on both rule sets.
- **No decisions at all** ("set up guardrails for our chatbot"): ask once, in one list, for blocked topics, the action per PII type, length limits, allowed tools and test cases. Do not invent a policy.
- **Asked to make a case pass by expectation** (an injection or email "should pass straight through") **or to skip a rule**: say in one line that the engine blocks the injection and masks the email regardless; the mismatch is reported and the run exits 1. Change the policy (with its owner's sign-off) or the expectation, never the output. Never echo raw PII in the reply.

## Starting points
- **New** — compile a policy written from `assets/policy-template.json` and test it with your cases.
- **Existing** — also pass the `guardrails.json` live today as `baseline`: every rule change is marked tightened or loosened, each test case is replayed on both rule sets, and loosened rules are flagged for sign-off ("Changes vs live rules").

## When to use
- Before deploying an LLM app or agent: a first, deterministic layer for prompt-injection markers, banned topics, PII, length and tool access.
- Turning a written policy into enforceable rules plus a regression suite that runs in CI.
- NOT for: the risk register and controls catalogue (`ai-governance-risk` — this skill implements some of its controls); answer-quality evals (`llm-eval-harness`); semantic content moderation or jailbreak classifiers (layer one on top; see Limits).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `policy` JSON: `blocked_topics`, `pii_handling` {email, phone, card, ssn: mask/block/allow}, `max_input_chars`, `max_output_chars`, `allowed_tools`, optional `injection_markers` | yes | AI security lead and Data protection officer; every value is a policy decision |
| `tests` CSV: `case_id, direction (in/out), text, expected (allow/block/mask)`, optional `tool` | no | product and security team; fixture rows labelled fictional; real PII never belongs in a test file |

A PII type missing from `pii_handling` is compiled as un-actioned (allow) and reported `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data protection officer]`. Without `tests`, Test results read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI security lead]`. Unknown policy keys exit 2 (typos never silently disable a rule).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Write the policy from `assets/policy-template.json` with `references/guardrail-design.md` (what each rule type catches and misses).
3. Write test cases from `assets/test-inputs-template.csv`: at least one allow, one block and one mask per rule type, plus evasion variants (case, spacing, line breaks) and tool calls on and off the allowlist.
4. Run the agent (above) or the script: `python3 -I scripts/build_guardrails.py --policy policy.json --tests cases.csv --out <dir>`.
5. Fix mismatches by changing the policy (or a wrong expectation) and re-run until exit 0.
6. Wire `scripts/guard.py` into the app: `from guard import load_rules, evaluate` on every user input (`direction="in"`), model output (`"out"`) and tool call (`tool=`); block or replace text per the decision. Add the test CSV to CI.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `guardrails.json`: schema id, policy sha256, limits, ordered rules (blocked_topic, injection, pii with pattern, validator, mask token, action), tool allowlist (default deny), unconfigured PII types.
- `guardrail-tests.json`: per case expected, actual, pass, rule-id reasons, PII counts, redacted text; totals.
- `guardrails.md`: sections Rule set, PII handling, Tool allowlist, Test results, Limits.
- `scripts/guard.py`: the runtime engine (CLI exit 0 allow/mask, 1 block; `--validate`; `--scan-pii FILE`).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every policy value came from the user; gaps carry an owned `[TO BE BASELINED]` marker
- [ ] Tests cover allow, block and mask for each rule type, plus evasion variants and tool calls
- [ ] Every case matches (exit 0) before deployment
- [ ] No raw PII in outputs: `guard.py --scan-pii` passes on guardrail-tests.json and guardrails.md
- [ ] Limits section kept; a semantic layer is planned where keyword rules are not enough

## References
- `references/guardrail-design.md` — rule types, precedence, PII detectors, evasion handling, deployment pattern, standards by name
- `scripts/build_guardrails.py` — compiler + test runner (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 mismatch / 2 input)
- `scripts/guard.py` — rule engine (importable + CLI; stdlib)
- `assets/injection-phrases.txt` — bundled prompt-injection marker phrases (starter list)
- `assets/policy-template.json`, `assets/test-inputs-template.csv` — input layouts

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/guardrails-config --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/guardrails-config`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`guardrails.json`, `guardrail-tests.json`, `guardrails.md`). A test case whose actual decision differs from its expected one fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; fix the policy or the expectation, never the output.
