skills/build/ci-cd-vercel-github/referen:
# Environments, Secrets, Promotion

## Environment matrix
| Environment | Code | Vercel env | Supabase project | DB data | Who can reach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local | working tree | — | local (`supabase start`) | seed | developer |
| Preview (PR) | PR branch | Preview | **staging** project (shared) or branch DB (Supabase Branching) | seed / synthetic | team (Vercel Authentication on) |
| Staging | `main` | Preview (of main) | staging | synthetic, prod-shaped | team |
| Production | tag `vX.Y.Z` | Production | prod | real | public |

Rules: preview never points at prod DB; staging DB is reset from seed weekly or uses branching; prod env vars marked **Sensitive** in Vercel.

## Variables and secrets
| Name | Where | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | Vercel env | Dev / Preview / Prod, per-environment values | public |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Vercel env (Sensitive) | Preview / Prod | server only |
| `HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_DSN`, `LOG_LEVEL` | Vercel env | Preview / Prod | |
| `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_ORG_ID`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` | GitHub secrets | repo | deploy from Actions |
| `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET` | GitHub secret | repo | Playwright through preview protection |
| `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | GitHub secret | repo | CLI auth |
| `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF_STAGING`, `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD_STAGING` | GitHub Environment `staging` | | |
| `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF_PROD`, `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD_PROD` | GitHub Environment `production` | | required reviewers on this Environment |
| `E2E_USER_EMAIL/PASSWORD`, `E2E_VIEWER_EMAIL/PASSWORD` | GitHub secrets | repo | seeded staging accounts |
| `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` | GitHub secrets | repo | source maps |

Set with `gh secret set NAME` (prompts for value) or `gh secret set NAME --env production`.

## Vercel project settings
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Git integration | connected, but **Production Branch deploys disabled** ("Ignored Build Step" returns 1 for `main`, or disconnect prod auto-deploy) — prod ships only via `prod.yml` |
| Preview deployments | enabled for PR branches (Vercel's own) *or* via `preview.yml` — pick one to avoid double builds; the template uses Actions for control |
| Deployment protection | Vercel Authentication on Preview; Protection Bypass for Automation enabled |
| Environment variables | per environment as above; "Sensitive" for secrets |
| Functions region | same region as Supabase project |
| Instant Rollback | on (Pro) |

## Promotion flow
| Step | Actor | Command / action | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | dev | open PR | `ci`, `preview / e2e` green; review |
| 2 | reviewer | squash-merge to `main` | — |
| 3 | auto | preview of `main` = staging | smoke via e2e already ran on PR |
| 4 | release owner | `git tag v1.4.0 && git push origin v1.4.0` | tag on main |
| 5 | auto | migrate staging | success |
| 6 | reviewer | approve **production** Environment in GitHub | human gate |
| 7 | auto | migrate prod → deploy → smoke → GitHub Release | health ok |
| 8 | release owner | watch alerts 30 min; update HANDOFF | — |

## Versioning
Semver tags. `patch` = fixes, `minor` = features, `major` = breaking API/schema contract. Hotfix: branch from the tag, PR to main, tag `v1.4.1`.

# Pipeline Stages

## Overview
```
PR opened/updated ──► ci.yml ───────────────► preview.yml ──────────────► merge to main
                      lint → typecheck →       vercel preview → e2e           │
                      unit+coverage → build    (+ preview URL comment)        ▼
                      rls-lint, secrets-scan                           preview of main = staging
                                                                               │  tag vX.Y.Z
                                                                               ▼
                                        prod.yml: verify-tag → migrate-staging → [gate] migrate-prod → deploy-prod → smoke → release
```

## Stage table
| Stage | Workflow / job | Trigger | Required check name | Timeout | Fails when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lint + typecheck + unit + build | `ci.yml` / `lint-typecheck-test` | PR, push main | `ci / lint-typecheck-test` | 15 min | eslint error, tsc error, test fail, coverage < 80% on server/, build error |
| RLS lint | `ci.yml` / `rls-lint` | PR, push main | `ci / rls-lint` | 5 min | any RLS error finding |
| Secrets scan | `ci.yml` / `secrets-scan` | PR, push main | `ci / secrets-scan` | 5 min | `.env*` committed; `NEXT_PUBLIC_*SERVICE_ROLE*` |
| Preview deploy | `preview.yml` / `deploy-preview` | PR | — | 20 min | vercel build/deploy error |
| E2E | `preview.yml` / `e2e` | after preview | `preview / e2e` | 30 min | playwright failure after 2 retries |
| Verify tag | `prod.yml` / `verify-tag` | tag `v*.*.*` | — | 2 min | tag commit not on main |
| Migrate staging | `prod.yml` / `migrate-staging` | after verify | — | 15 min | `supabase db push` error |
| Migrate prod | `prod.yml` / `migrate-prod` | after staging; **production** Environment approval | — | 15 min | push error |
| Deploy prod | `prod.yml` / `deploy-prod` | after migrate | — | 20 min | build/deploy error |
| Smoke | `prod.yml` / `deploy-prod` step | after deploy | — | 2 min | `/api/health` or `/api/health/deep` not ok |
| Release | `prod.yml` / `deploy-prod` step | after smoke | — | 1 min | — |

## Conventions
| Topic | Rule |
|---|---|
| Check names | `<workflow name> / <job id>`; these exact strings go into branch protection |
| Concurrency | `ci-${{ github.ref }}` and `preview-${{ github.ref }}` cancel in progress; `prod` group never cancels |
| Permissions | `permissions:` block per workflow; least privilege (`contents: read` default) |
| Node | `actions/setup-node@v4` with `cache: npm`; version pinned via `NODE_VERSION` env (match `.nvmrc`) |
| Caching | npm cache via setup-node; Next build cache: `actions/cache` on `.next/cache` keyed by lockfile + source hash (optional) |
| Artifacts | coverage (7 days), playwright report on failure (7 days) |
| Timeouts | every job has `timeout-minutes` |
| Secrets in logs | never `echo $SECRET`; derived values masked with `echo "::add-mask::$VAL"` |
| Fork PRs | secrets unavailable → `preview.yml` skips deploy for forks (`if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`) |
| Integration tests in CI | optional job `integration` with `supabase/setup-cli` + `supabase start`; add when `tests/integration` exists (adds ~3 min) |

## Adding a stage (procedure)
1. Add the job to the right workflow with `needs:` wiring and `timeout-minutes`.
2. Make it required in branch protection only after it has passed on 3 PRs.
3. Document in `docs/ci-cd.md`.

## Optional integration job (`ci.yml`)
```yaml
  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: "20", cache: npm }
      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1
        with: { version: latest }
      - run: supabase start
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Export local keys
        run: |
          supabase status -o env >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - run: npm test -- --project integration
```

# Rollback Runbook

## Decision table
| Symptom after release | First action | Then |
|---|---|---|
| 5xx spike / health down, no migration in release | **Code rollback** (≤ 2 min) | investigate on preview |
| Same, release had an **additive** migration | Code rollback (old code ignores new columns/tables) | leave schema; fix forward |
| Same, release had a **destructive/contract** migration | Do NOT roll back code blindly (old code expects dropped columns) | fix forward or run revert migration first, then code rollback |
| Feature misbehaves, flag-gated | flip flag off | fix forward |
| Data corrupted by new code | stop writes (flag/maintenance), code rollback | restore from PITR to a side DB, repair via migration — never hand-edit prod rows |

## Code rollback (Vercel)
```bash
# Option A — instant: promote previous production deployment
vercel rollback --token=$VERCEL_TOKEN                 # interactive pick, or:
vercel rollback <previous-deployment-url> --token=$VERCEL_TOKEN

# Option B — rebuild previous tag through the pipeline (slower, auditable)
git tag v1.4.1 v1.3.0^{} -m "rollback to v1.3.0"      # new tag pointing at old commit
git push origin v1.4.1                                 # prod.yml runs; migrations are no-ops
```
Then: confirm `/api/health/deep` ok; post in channel; open incident note; HANDOFF entry.

## Migration rollback (Supabase)
1. Open the migration file; copy the `-- rollback:` block.
2. Create a new forward migration: `supabase migration new revert_<name>` with that SQL.
3. Test on staging: `supabase db push` (linked to staging).
4. Apply to prod via a tag release (`prod.yml`) or, in an emergency, `supabase db push` linked to prod from a trusted machine — record who/when.
5. Never delete the original migration file; never `supabase migration repair` to hide history unless the migration never ran.

## Pre-release checklist (makes rollback possible)
- [ ] Previous production deployment still exists (not deleted)
- [ ] Release notes list migrations and their type (additive / contract)
- [ ] Contract migrations are in a separate, later release from the code that stops using the old shape
- [ ] Feature flags default off for new risky paths
- [ ] PITR enabled on prod Supabase (Pro)
- [ ] Someone is watching alerts for 30 min post-release

## Drill
Quarterly: roll back staging to the previous deployment and apply a revert migration; time it; update this runbook.

# Troubleshooting CI/CD

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ci` passes locally, fails in CI on typecheck | CI uses `npm ci` with lockfile; local has newer deps | run `npm ci` locally; commit lockfile |
| Coverage gate fails right after adding tests | `coverage-summary.json` not generated (`json-summary` reporter missing) | add reporter in `vitest.config.ts` |
| `vercel pull` fails: "project not found" | `VERCEL_ORG_ID`/`VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` wrong or token scope | `vercel link` locally, copy ids from `.vercel/project.json` |
| Preview URL 401 in Playwright | protection bypass header missing | set `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET`; `extraHTTPHeaders` in config |
| E2E flaky only in CI | timing; shared test data | web-first assertions; unique data per worker; 2 retries |
| `supabase db push` "migration already applied with different checksum" | an applied migration was edited | revert the edit; add a new migration |
| `supabase link` asks for password interactively | `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` not exported | set env in the step |
| Prod job skipped | tag not on `main` or Environment approval pending | check `verify-tag` logs; approve in Actions UI |
| Two preview deployments per PR | Vercel git integration AND `preview.yml` both deploying | disable one (see env-promotion.md) |
| Secrets empty on fork PR | GitHub does not pass secrets to forks | gate deploy job on same-repo condition |
| Build fails: env var missing | `lib/env.ts` zod parse at build | add placeholder in `ci.yml` build step env, real value in Vercel |
| Playwright browsers not installed | cache restored without browsers | `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` every run |
| Smoke fails `/api/health/deep` 401 | `HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN` differs between Vercel and GitHub | align secrets |

# preview.yml — deploy a Vercel preview for the PR and run Playwright e2e against it.
# Required status check name: "preview / e2e"
name: preview

on:
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  deployments: write

env:
  VERCEL_ORG_ID: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
  VERCEL_PROJECT_ID: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }}

jobs:
  deploy-preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    outputs:
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm i -g vercel@latest
      - run: vercel pull --yes --environment=preview --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - run: vercel build --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - id: deploy
        run: |
          URL=$(vercel deploy --prebuilt --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }})
          echo "url=$URL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Comment preview URL
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const url = '${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}';
            const body = `Preview: ${url}`;
            const {data: comments} = await github.rest.issues.listComments({...context.repo, issue_number: context.issue.number});
            const prev = comments.find(c => c.body.startsWith('Preview: '));
            if (prev) await github.rest.issues.updateComment({...context.repo, comment_id: prev.id, body});
            else await github.rest.issues.createComment({...context.repo, issue_number: context.issue.number, body});

  e2e:
    needs: deploy-preview
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Playwright against preview
        env:
          BASE_URL: ${{ needs.deploy-preview.outputs.url }}
          VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET }}
          E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
          E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
        run: npm run test:e2e
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

      - run: vercel pull --yes --environment=production --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - run: vercel build --prod --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}

---

# code-review-runner

Wraps `code-review` from mattpocock/skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). Upstream reviews a change on two separate axes — Standards and Spec — with a Fowler smell baseline as judgement calls. This skill makes the deterministic part of the Standards axis executable and hands the upstream instructions to the optional narrative step by path (`../../../vendor/code-review/SKILL.md`), never by copy.

## In a conversation: review the change now
**Never**
- Never BLOCK for a warning or info finding: the verdict is **BLOCK only if at least one finding has severity `blocking`**; otherwise **PASS** (warnings and info are listed under Non-blocking). `console.log` is CR-DEBUG = **warning**; an owner-less TODO is CR-TODO = **info** (unless team rules override).
- Never flag removed (`-`) or context (` `) lines, and never flag CR-DEBUG inside a test file (`__tests__/`, `tests/`, `*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`, …).
- Never print a full secret: evidence keeps the first 4 characters + `[redacted]` (e.g. `AKIA[redacted]`).
- Never "just approve": a blocking finding fails the gate (exit 1) regardless of deadline.

**Procedure (from `scripts/review.py`; work line by line through the supplied diff)**
1. Parse: per file, status (added if `--- /dev/null`, else modified), hunks, added lines with new-file line numbers — the `@@ … +N` start is line N; each context or `+` line advances the counter, `-` lines do not.
2. Detect on added lines only — blocking: CR-SECRET (key/token literals, `password|secret|token|api_key = "<literal ≥8>"`, high-entropy literal ≥ 20 chars at ≥ 4.0 bits/char), CR-EVAL (`eval(`/`exec(`/`new Function(`), CR-TLS (`verify=False`, `rejectUnauthorized: false`, `CERT_NONE`, `curl -k`…), CR-SQL-CONCAT (SQL keyword text built with `+`, f-string, `${}`, `%`, `.format(`); warning: CR-SWALLOW (`except: pass`, empty `catch {}`), CR-DEBUG (non-test files: `console.log/debug/trace`, `debugger`, `print(` in .py, `pdb`, `System.out.println`); info: CR-TODO (TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK not followed by `(name)`, `@name`, `[ABC-12]`, `(#12)`), CR-DUP (same ≥3-line added block twice); warning: CR-NO-TESTS when source code files changed and **no** test file changed.
3. Team rules (`rules` CSV) after the built-ins: a built-in `rule_id` with empty pattern overrides its severity (`off` disables) — e.g. `CR-TODO,,warning` makes the TODO a warning, `CR-NO-TESTS,,blocking` only bites if no test changed; other rows are custom regex rules on added lines (filtered by `file_glob`).
4. Sort blocking → warning → info, then file, line; number F01, F02 …. Counts per severity.
5. Verdict: BLOCK if blocking count > 0 (script exits 1, outputs still written, `--gate review.json` fails); else PASS (exit 0).

**Reply layout**: first a working table — one row per added line that hits a detector (file:line, text, rule, severity) and the test check (source files changed, test files changed) — then `Verdict: **PASS**` or `Verdict: **BLOCK**` — "N blocking, N warning, N info.", then the `review.md` sections: **Summary** (files (source/test), hunks, lines added / removed, size vs 400, risky paths), **Blocking**, **Non-blocking**, **Tests** ("Test verdict: tests changed" / "MISSING" / "no source change", listing source and test files), **Files**. Each finding row: id, `file:line`, rule, severity, finding, evidence, fix.
- Name the run: `python3 -I scripts/review.py --diff <change.patch> [--rules <rules.csv>] --json review.json --md review.md`, then `python3 -I scripts/review.py --gate review.json`; outputs `review.json` and `review.md` (and `review-two-axis.md` only with `narrative=true`).
- **The request says a diff, PR, team rules or spec is here but its text is not in the conversation**: still write the review skeleton now — the five sections with their headings, the detector checklist above that will run on the added lines, the Tests line, and `Verdict: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: author, from the diff]`. With team rules: state they are applied after the built-ins (custom regex rules; a built-in id with empty pattern overrides its severity, e.g. CR-TODO raised to warning or CR-NO-TESTS made blocking) and record each override. With a narrative request: lay out the two-axis review (Standards from the findings, Spec from the issue/spec, kept separate, then Summary) per `assets/two-axis-review-template.md` and the upstream method. End with one line asking for the unified diff (`git diff <base>...HEAD > change.patch`). Never print a PASS verdict or invent findings for code you have not seen.
- **Nothing to review** ("review my PR" with no diff): ask once for the unified diff (and, optionally, the team rules CSV and the spec). Do not review an imagined change.
- **Asked to "just approve it" or skip the review to merge today**: decline in one line — approval without the review is not given, and a blocking finding (secret, eval, disabled TLS, SQL built by concatenation) fails the gate regardless of deadline. Run or lay out the review as above; offer the fastest defensible path: fix the blocking rows, re-run, merge on PASS.

## Starting points
- **New** — a diff that adds new files is reviewed on its added lines: standards findings, test verdict, verdict.
- **Existing** — a change to code that already exists is reviewed together with your team's own rules file (custom regex rules and severity overrides), so the verdict follows the team's bar, not only the built-in one.

## When to use
- Before merge: a quick, repeatable pass that catches the mechanical defects first.
- In CI: `review.py --gate review.json` as a required check.
- NOT for: threat modelling and authz reasoning (`security-review`), stack-specific conventions (`nextjs-enterprise-conventions`), fixing what it finds (`safe-fix`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `diff` | yes | Unified diff, three-dot against the merge base. Only added lines are scanned. |
| `rules` | no | Team rules CSV (`assets/rules-template.csv`): `rule_id,pattern,severity,message,file_glob`. A built-in id with empty pattern overrides its severity (`off` disables). |
| `spec` | no | Issue or spec text for the Spec axis of the narrative step. Without it the Spec axis reports "no spec available". |
| `narrative` | no | `true` runs the LLM step that writes the two-axis review. |

## Procedure
1. **Parse the diff** (`scripts/review.py`): files, status, hunks, added lines with new-file line numbers, removed-line counts.
2. **Stats**: files, hunks, +/-, size label (`--large-change`, default 400 changed lines), source vs test files, risky paths (auth, migrations, config, CI, env).
3. **Detect** on added lines: CR-SECRET, CR-EVAL, CR-TLS, CR-SQL-CONCAT (blocking); CR-SWALLOW, CR-DEBUG, CR-NO-TESTS (warning); CR-TODO, CR-DUP (info). See `references/review-rules.md`.
4. **Apply team rules** from the rules CSV; sort findings blocking → info, number F01….
5. **Write** `review.json` and `review.md`; exit 1 if anything is blocking.
6. **Gate**: `review.py --gate review.json` is the output check that fails the run on blocking findings.
7. Optional: with `narrative=true` the LLM fills `assets/two-axis-review-template.md` — Standards (from the findings) and Spec (from `spec`) kept separate, per the upstream method.

## Output
- `review.json` — stats, files, tests verdict, counts, verdict (PASS/BLOCK), findings `{id, rule, severity, file, line, evidence, message, fix}`; secrets redacted in evidence.
- `review.md` — Summary, Blocking, Non-blocking, Tests, Files.
- `review-two-axis.md` (only with `narrative=true`).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every finding has file:line, rule and severity; evidence never shows a full secret
- [ ] Only added lines were scanned; context and removed lines produce no findings
- [ ] Blocking findings fail the run through the gate check
- [ ] The Tests section states whether tests changed alongside source
- [ ] The Spec axis is not claimed by the script; it is the narrative step's job and needs a spec

## References
- `references/review-rules.md` — detector rules, severities, false-positive notes, overrides
- `assets/rules-template.csv` — team rules layout
- `assets/two-axis-review-template.md` — narrative template for the optional LLM step
- `scripts/review.py` — parser, detectors, renderer and gate (argparse; stdlib)
- Upstream method: `vendor/code-review/SKILL.md`

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/code-review-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/code-review-runner`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The script always writes both outputs; the gate check on `review.json` then fails the run (exit 1) when any blocking finding remains, so a blocking diff is reported, never waved through.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic first-pass code review of a unified diff (added lines only).

    python3 -I scripts/review.py --diff change.patch [--rules rules.csv] --json review.json --md review.md
    python3 -I scripts/review.py --gate review.json     # exit 1 if any blocking finding

The review covers the Standards axis of the vendored code-review method with fixed detectors;
the Spec axis needs a spec and judgement, so it is left to the optional LLM step.

Detectors (rule id · default severity), run on ADDED lines only:
  CR-SECRET      blocking  key/token literals (AWS, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, Google, private key, JWT,
                           `password|secret|token|api_key = "<literal>"`) and high-entropy string literals
  CR-EVAL        blocking  eval( / exec( / new Function(
  CR-TLS         blocking  disabled TLS verification (verify=False, rejectUnauthorized: false, CERT_NONE,
                           NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, curl -k/--insecure)
  CR-SQL-CONCAT  blocking  SQL text built by + concatenation, f-string, ${} template, % or .format()
  CR-SWALLOW     warning   broad exception swallowed (except: pass, except Exception: pass, empty catch {})
  CR-DEBUG       warning   console.log/debug, debugger, print( (non-test .py), pdb/breakpoint(),
                           System.out.println
  CR-TODO        info      TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK without an owner: TODO(name), TODO @name, TODO [ABC-12], TODO(#12)
  CR-DUP         info      the same block of >= 3 non-trivial added lines appears more than once
                           (the Duplicated Code smell from the upstream baseline, as a labelled heuristic)
  CR-NO-TESTS    warning   source files changed but no test file changed
Severities: blocking | warning | info. A rules CSV (rule_id,pattern,severity,message,file_glob) adds
custom regex rules; a row whose rule_id is a built-in id and whose pattern is empty overrides that
rule's severity (`off` disables it). Thresholds are CLI options, not facts: --entropy (bits/char,
default 4.0) and --min-secret-len (default 20) tune the high-entropy detector; --large-change
(default 400 changed lines) only labels the size.

Exit codes: 0 no blocking finding · 1 blocking finding(s) (outputs still written) or --gate failed ·
2 missing/invalid input. Stdlib only; writes only --json / --md.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import fnmatch
import json
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SEVERITIES = ("blocking", "warning", "info")
SEV_ORDER = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(SEVERITIES)}

CODE_EXT = {".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".java", ".kt", ".go", ".rb", ".php", ".cs",
            ".scala", ".rs", ".swift", ".sql", ".sh"}
TEST_PATH = re.compile(r"(^|/)(tests?|__tests__|spec|specs)/|(^|/)test_[^/]+\.py$|_test\.(py|go)$|"
                       r"\.(test|spec)\.[jt]sx?$|Tests?\.(java|kt|cs)$|(^|/)conftest\.py$")
RISKY_PATH = re.compile(r"auth|login|session|permission|rbac|policy|migration|security|crypto|payment|"
                        r"(^|/)\.env|Dockerfile|\.github/workflows|terraform|\.tf$|settings\.py$|config", re.I)

SECRET_PATTERNS = [
    ("AWS access key id", re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")),
    ("GitHub token", re.compile(r"\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}\b")),
    ("Slack token", re.compile(r"\bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}")),
    ("Stripe live key", re.compile(r"\b[sr]k_live_[0-9A-Za-z]{16,}")),
    ("Google API key", re.compile(r"\bAIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{35}\b")),
    ("private key block", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |DSA |OPENSSH |PGP )?PRIVATE KEY-----")),
    ("JWT", re.compile(r"\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}")),
    ("credential assignment", re.compile(
        r"(?i)\b\w*(?:password|passwd|pwd|secret|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|token)"
        r"\w*\s*[:=]\s*[\"']([^\"'\s]{8,})[\"']")),
]
PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"(?i)^(?:<[^>]+>|\$\{[^}]+\}|x{4,}|\*{4,}|your[_-]|example|placeholder|changeme$|dummy|"
                         r"process\.env|os\.environ|getenv)")
STRING_LIT = re.compile(r"[\"']([A-Za-z0-9+/=_\-]{16,})[\"']")
EVAL = re.compile(r"(?<![.\w])(?:eval|exec)\s*\(|\bnew\s+Function\s*\(")
TLS = re.compile(r"verify\s*=\s*False|rejectUnauthorized\s*:\s*false|NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED\s*=?\s*[\"']?0|"
                 r"InsecureSkipVerify\s*:\s*true|CERT_NONE|_create_unverified_context|\bcurl\b[^\n]*\s(?:-k|--insecure)\b|"
                 r"setHostnameVerifier\([^)]*ALLOW_ALL|TrustAllCerts|check_hostname\s*=\s*False", re.I)
SQL_KW = re.compile(r"(?i)[\"'`f][^\"'`]*\b(?:select\b[^\"'`]*\bfrom|insert\s+into|update\s+\w+\s+set|delete\s+from)\b")
SQL_BUILD = re.compile(r"(?:[\"'`]\s*\+\s*[A-Za-z_(])|(?:[A-Za-z_)\]]\s*\+\s*[\"'`])|(?<![\w])f[\"']|\$\{|"
                       r"[\"']\s*%\s*[\w(]|\.format\(")
SWALLOW_INLINE = re.compile(r"^\s*except(?:\s+(?:Exception|BaseException)(?:\s+as\s+\w+)?)?\s*:\s*(?:pass|\.\.\.)\s*(?:#.*)?$|"
                            r"catch\s*(?:\(\s*\w*(?:\s*:\s*\w+)?\s*\))?\s*\{\s*\}|"
                            r"catch\s*\(\s*(?:final\s+)?(?:Exception|Throwable|RuntimeException)\s+\w+\s*\)\s*\{\s*\}")
SWALLOW_HEAD = re.compile(r"^\s*except(?:\s+(?:Exception|BaseException)(?:\s+as\s+\w+)?)?\s*:\s*(?:#.*)?$")
SWALLOW_BODY = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:pass|\.\.\.)\s*(?:#.*)?$")
DEBUG_JS = re.compile(r"\bconsole\.(?:log|debug|trace)\s*\(|^\s*debugger\s*;?\s*$")
DEBUG_PY = re.compile(r"^\s*print\s*\(|\bpdb\.set_trace\s*\(|^\s*breakpoint\s*\(\s*\)|\bimport\s+pdb\b")
DEBUG_JAVA = re.compile(r"\bSystem\.(?:out|err)\.print(?:ln)?\s*\(|\.printStackTrace\s*\(\s*\)")
TODO = re.compile(r"\b(TODO|FIXME|XXX|HACK)\b(?!\s*(?:\(\s*[@#]?[\w.-]+\s*\)|@\w|\[\s*[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+\s*\]|:\s*@\w))")

BUILTIN = {
    "CR-SECRET": ("blocking", "Hard-coded secret or high-entropy literal", "Move it to a secret store / env var and rotate it; it is now in history."),
    "CR-EVAL": ("blocking", "Dynamic code execution (eval/exec/new Function)", "Replace with an explicit parser or dispatch table."),
    "CR-TLS": ("blocking", "TLS certificate verification disabled", "Keep verification on; pin or install the CA instead."),
    "CR-SQL-CONCAT": ("blocking", "SQL built by string concatenation/interpolation", "Use parameterised queries / bound parameters."),
    "CR-SWALLOW": ("warning", "Broad exception swallowed", "Catch the specific exception and log or re-raise it."),
    "CR-DEBUG": ("warning", "Debug leftover", "Remove it or route through the project logger."),
    "CR-TODO": ("info", "TODO/FIXME without an owner", "Add an owner or ticket: TODO(name) or TODO [ABC-123]."),
    "CR-DUP": ("info", "Possible Duplicated Code (judgement call)", "Extract the shared block if the duplication is real."),
    "CR-NO-TESTS": ("warning", "Source changed with no test changes", "Add or update tests covering the change."),
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ diff parsing

def parse_diff(text: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Return [{path, old_path, status, hunks, added:[(line, text)], removed:int}]."""
    files, cur, new_line = [], None, 0
    old_path = None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if raw.startswith("diff --git"):
            cur = None
            old_path = None
            continue
        if raw.startswith("--- "):
            old_path = re.sub(r"^[ab]/", "", raw[4:].strip().split("\t")[0])
            continue
        if raw.startswith("+++ "):
            p = re.sub(r"^[ab]/", "", raw[4:].strip().split("\t")[0])
            status = "added" if old_path == "/dev/null" else ("deleted" if p == "/dev/null" else "modified")
            cur = {"path": old_path if p == "/dev/null" else p, "status": status, "hunks": 0, "added": [], "removed": 0}
            files.append(cur)
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,\d+)? @@", raw)
        if m and cur is not None:
            cur["hunks"] += 1
            new_line = int(m[1])
            continue
        if cur is None or cur["hunks"] == 0:
            continue
        if raw.startswith("+"):
            cur["added"].append((new_line, raw[1:]))
            new_line += 1
        elif raw.startswith("-"):
            cur["removed"] += 1
        elif raw.startswith(" ") or raw == "":
            new_line += 1
    return files


def shannon(s: str) -> float:
    if not s:
        return 0.0
    counts = {c: s.count(c) for c in set(s)}
    return -sum(n / len(s) * math.log2(n / len(s)) for n in counts.values())


def redact(text: str, secret: str) -> str:
    keep = secret[:4] if len(secret) > 8 else ""
    return text.replace(secret, f"{keep}[redacted]").strip()[:160]


def is_test(path: str) -> bool:
    return bool(TEST_PATH.search(path))


def is_code(path: str) -> bool:
    return Path(path).suffix.lower() in CODE_EXT


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ detectors

def detect(files: list[dict], entropy: float, min_len: int) -> list[dict]:
    out = []

    def add(rule, f, line, evidence, detail=""):
        out.append({"rule": rule, "file": f["path"], "line": line, "evidence": evidence.strip()[:160],
                    "detail": detail})

    for f in files:
        path, ext, test = f["path"], Path(f["path"]).suffix.lower(), is_test(f["path"])
        added = f["added"]
        for idx, (ln, text) in enumerate(added):
            hit_secret = False
            for label, rx in SECRET_PATTERNS:
                m = rx.search(text)
                if not m:
                    continue
                val = m.group(1) if m.groups() else m.group(0)
                if label == "credential assignment" and PLACEHOLDER.search(val):
                    continue
                add("CR-SECRET", f, ln, redact(text, val), label)
                hit_secret = True
                break
            if not hit_secret:
                for m in STRING_LIT.finditer(text):
                    s = m.group(1)
                    if len(s) >= min_len and shannon(s) >= entropy and not PLACEHOLDER.search(s) \
                            and not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z_\-/.]+|[A-Z_\-]+", s):
                        add("CR-SECRET", f, ln, redact(text, s), f"high-entropy literal ({shannon(s):.2f} bits/char)")
                        break
            if EVAL.search(text) and ext not in (".md", ".txt"):
                add("CR-EVAL", f, ln, text)
            if TLS.search(text):
                add("CR-TLS", f, ln, text)
            if SQL_KW.search(text) and SQL_BUILD.search(text):
                add("CR-SQL-CONCAT", f, ln, text)
            if SWALLOW_INLINE.search(text):
                add("CR-SWALLOW", f, ln, text)
            elif SWALLOW_HEAD.match(text) and idx + 1 < len(added) and added[idx + 1][0] == ln + 1 \
                    and SWALLOW_BODY.match(added[idx + 1][1]):
                add("CR-SWALLOW", f, ln, text + " " + added[idx + 1][1].strip())
            if not test:
                if ext in (".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".mjs", ".cjs") and DEBUG_JS.search(text):
                    add("CR-DEBUG", f, ln, text)
                elif ext == ".py" and DEBUG_PY.search(text):
                    add("CR-DEBUG", f, ln, text)
                elif ext in (".java", ".kt") and DEBUG_JAVA.search(text):
                    add("CR-DEBUG", f, ln, text)
            m = TODO.search(text)
            if m:
                add("CR-TODO", f, ln, text, m.group(1))
    out += detect_duplicates(files)
    src = [f for f in files if is_code(f["path"]) and not is_test(f["path"]) and f["status"] != "deleted"]
    if src and not any(is_test(f["path"]) for f in files):
        first = src[0]
        line = first["added"][0][0] if first["added"] else 0
        out.append({"rule": "CR-NO-TESTS", "file": first["path"], "line": line,
                    "evidence": f"{len(src)} source file(s) changed: " + ", ".join(f["path"] for f in src[:5]),
                    "detail": ""})
    return out


def detect_duplicates(files: list[dict], window: int = 3) -> list[dict]:
    seen: dict[tuple, tuple] = {}
    out, reported = [], set()
    for f in files:
        lines = [(ln, t.strip()) for ln, t in f["added"]]
        for i in range(len(lines) - window + 1):
            chunk = lines[i:i + window]
            if any(chunk[k + 1][0] != chunk[k][0] + 1 for k in range(window - 1)):
                continue
            key = tuple(t for _, t in chunk)
            if sum(len(t) for t in key) < 40 or any(len(t) < 4 for t in key):
                continue
            if key in seen and seen[key] != (f["path"], chunk[0][0]):
                if key not in reported:
                    first = seen[key]
                    out.append({"rule": "CR-DUP", "file": f["path"], "line": chunk[0][0],
                                "evidence": key[0], "detail": f"same {window}-line block as {first[0]}:{first[1]}"})
                    reported.add(key)
            else:
                seen.setdefault(key, (f["path"], chunk[0][0]))
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ rules CSV

def load_rules(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], dict, list[str]]:
    """Return (custom_rules, severity_overrides, errors)."""
    custom, overrides, errors = [], {}, []
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="")))
    need = {"rule_id", "pattern", "severity", "message"}
    if rows and not need <= set(rows[0].keys()):
        return [], {}, [f"rules CSV needs columns {sorted(need)} (file_glob optional)"]
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 2):
        rid = (r.get("rule_id") or "").strip()
        sev = (r.get("severity") or "").strip().lower()
        pat = (r.get("pattern") or "").strip()
        if not rid or rid.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if sev not in SEVERITIES + ("off",):
            errors.append(f"rules line {i}: severity {sev!r} not in {SEVERITIES + ('off',)}")
            continue
        if rid in BUILTIN and not pat:
            overrides[rid] = sev
            continue
        try:
            rx = re.compile(pat)
        except re.error as e:
            errors.append(f"rules line {i}: bad regex {pat!r}: {e}")
            continue
        if not pat:
            errors.append(f"rules line {i}: custom rule {rid} has no pattern")
            continue
        custom.append({"id": rid, "rx": rx, "severity": sev, "message": (r.get("message") or rid).strip(),
                       "glob": (r.get("file_glob") or "").strip()})
    return custom, overrides, errors


def apply_custom(files, custom) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for rule in custom:
        if rule["severity"] == "off":
            continue
        for f in files:
            if rule["glob"] and not fnmatch.fnmatch(f["path"], rule["glob"]):
                continue
            for ln, text in f["added"]:
                if rule["rx"].search(text):
                    out.append({"rule": rule["id"], "file": f["path"], "line": ln, "evidence": text.strip()[:160],
                                "detail": "", "severity": rule["severity"], "message": rule["message"],
                                "fix": "See the team rule."})
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ review

def review(diff_text: str, rules_path: Path | None, entropy: float, min_len: int, large: int, source: str) -> dict:
    files = parse_diff(diff_text)
    if not files:
        raise ValueError("no file changes found in the diff (expected unified diff with ---/+++ headers)")
    custom, overrides, rule_errors = (load_rules(rules_path) if rules_path else ([], {}, []))
    if rule_errors:
        raise ValueError("; ".join(rule_errors))
    findings = []
    for f in detect(files, entropy, min_len):
        sev, msg, fix = BUILTIN[f["rule"]]
        sev = overrides.get(f["rule"], sev)
        if sev == "off":
            continue
        findings.append({**f, "severity": sev, "message": msg + (f" — {f['detail']}" if f["detail"] else ""), "fix": fix})
    findings += apply_custom(files, custom)
    findings.sort(key=lambda x: (SEV_ORDER[x["severity"]], x["file"], x["line"], x["rule"]))
    for i, x in enumerate(findings, 1):
        x["id"] = f"F{i:02d}"
        x.pop("detail", None)
    added = sum(len(f["added"]) for f in files)
    removed = sum(f["removed"] for f in files)
    tests = [f["path"] for f in files if is_test(f["path"])]
    src = [f["path"] for f in files if is_code(f["path"]) and not is_test(f["path"])]
    risky = [f["path"] for f in files if RISKY_PATH.search(f["path"])]
    counts = {s: sum(1 for x in findings if x["severity"] == s) for s in SEVERITIES}
    size = "large" if added + removed > large else "normal"
    return {
        "skill": "code-review-runner", "source": source,
        "stats": {"files": len(files), "hunks": sum(f["hunks"] for f in files), "added": added, "removed": removed,
                  "changed": added + removed, "size": size, "large_change_threshold": large,
                  "source_files": len(src), "test_files": len(tests), "risky_paths": risky},
        "files": [{"path": f["path"], "status": f["status"], "hunks": f["hunks"], "added": len(f["added"]),
                   "removed": f["removed"], "kind": "test" if is_test(f["path"]) else ("source" if is_code(f["path"]) else "other"),
                   "findings": sum(1 for x in findings if x["file"] == f["path"])} for f in files],
        "tests": {"source_changed": src, "tests_changed": tests,
                  "verdict": "tests changed" if tests else ("no source change" if not src else "MISSING")},
        "counts": counts,
        "verdict": "BLOCK" if counts["blocking"] else "PASS",
        "findings": findings,
        "rules": {"custom": [r["id"] for r in custom], "overrides": overrides,
                  "entropy_bits_per_char": entropy, "min_secret_len": min_len},
        "scope_note": "Deterministic Standards baseline on added lines. The Spec axis (does it do what the "
                      "issue asked) is not checked by this script.",
    }


def _cell(s) -> str:
    return str(s).replace("|", "\\|").replace("`", "'")


def render_md(r: dict) -> str:
    s, c = r["stats"], r["counts"]
    out = ["# Code review", "", f"_Generated by code-review-runner from {_cell(r['source'])}. {r['scope_note']}_", "",
           "## Summary", "",
           f"Verdict: **{r['verdict']}** — {c['blocking']} blocking, {c['warning']} warning, {c['info']} info.", "",
           "| Metric | Value |", "|---|---|",
           f"| Files changed | {s['files']} ({s['source_files']} source, {s['test_files']} test) |",
           f"| Hunks | {s['hunks']} |", f"| Lines added / removed | {s['added']} / {s['removed']} |",
           f"| Size | {s['size']} (threshold {s['large_change_threshold']} changed lines) |",
           f"| Risky paths | {', '.join(f'`{p}`' for p in s['risky_paths']) or 'none'} |", ""]

    def table(rows):
        if not rows:
            return ["None.", ""]
        t = ["| ID | File:line | Rule | Severity | Finding | Evidence | Fix |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for x in rows:
            t.append(f"| {x['id']} | `{_cell(x['file'])}:{x['line']}` | {x['rule']} | {x['severity']} | "
                     f"{_cell(x['message'])} | `{_cell(x['evidence'])}` | {_cell(x['fix'])} |")
        return t + [""]

    fs = r["findings"]
    out += ["## Blocking", ""] + table([x for x in fs if x["severity"] == "blocking"])
    out += ["## Non-blocking", ""] + table([x for x in fs if x["severity"] != "blocking" and x["rule"] != "CR-NO-TESTS"])
    t = r["tests"]
    out += ["## Tests", "", f"Test verdict: **{t['verdict']}**", "",
            f"- Source files changed: {', '.join(f'`{p}`' for p in t['source_changed']) or 'none'}",
            f"- Test files changed: {', '.join(f'`{p}`' for p in t['tests_changed']) or 'none'}", ""]
    nt = [x for x in fs if x["rule"] == "CR-NO-TESTS"]
    if nt:
        out += table(nt)
    out += ["## Files", "", "| File | Status | Kind | Hunks | +/- | Findings |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for f in r["files"]:
        out.append(f"| `{_cell(f['path'])}` | {f['status']} | {f['kind']} | {f['hunks']} | +{f['added']}/-{f['removed']} | "
                   f"{f['findings']} |")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def gate(path: Path) -> int:
    try:
        r = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"gate: cannot read {path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    n = sum(1 for x in r.get("findings", []) if x.get("severity") == "blocking")
    if n:
        print(f"gate: BLOCK — {n} blocking finding(s)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print("gate: PASS — no blocking findings")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Deterministic code review of a unified diff (added lines only)")
    ap.add_argument("--diff", help="unified diff (git diff <base>...HEAD)")
    ap.add_argument("--rules", help="optional rules CSV: rule_id,pattern,severity,message,file_glob")
    ap.add_argument("--json", dest="json_out", help="write review.json here")
    ap.add_argument("--md", dest="md_out", help="write review.md here")
    ap.add_argument("--gate", metavar="REVIEW_JSON", help="exit 1 if the review has blocking findings")
    ap.add_argument("--entropy", type=float, default=4.0, help="high-entropy threshold, bits/char (default 4.0)")
    ap.add_argument("--min-secret-len", type=int, default=20, help="min literal length for the entropy check")
    ap.add_argument("--large-change", type=int, default=400, help="changed-line count labelled 'large'")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.gate:
        return gate(Path(a.gate))
    if not a.diff or not Path(a.diff).is_file():
        print(f"error: --diff is required and must exist (got {a.diff!r})", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if a.rules and not Path(a.rules).is_file():
        print(f"error: --rules file not found: {a.rules}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not a.json_out and not a.md_out:
        print("error: give --json and/or --md", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        r = review(Path(a.diff).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), Path(a.rules) if a.rules else None,
                   a.entropy, a.min_secret_len, a.large_change, Path(a.diff).name)
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if a.json_out:
        Path(a.json_out).write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if a.md_out:
        Path(a.md_out).write_text(render_md(r), encoding="utf-8")
    c = r["counts"]
    print(f"review: {r['verdict']} — {c['blocking']} blocking, {c['warning']} warning, {c['info']} info "
          f"across {r['stats']['files']} files")
    return 1 if c["blocking"] else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Review rules — what the runner flags and why

The vendored `code-review` method (mattpocock/skills, pinned in `vendor/pins.json`) reviews a change on two axes, Standards and Spec, and keeps them separate. This runner automates only the mechanical part of the Standards axis. Read `vendor/code-review/SKILL.md` for the method; this note documents the detectors.

## Scope
- Only **added** lines are scanned (`+` lines of the new file). Context and removed lines never produce findings.
- Line numbers are new-file line numbers from the hunk headers.

## Detectors
| Rule | Severity | Flags | Common false positive → what to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| CR-SECRET | blocking | AWS key ids, GitHub/Slack/Stripe/Google tokens, private-key blocks, JWTs, `password/secret/token/api_key = "<literal>"`, high-entropy string literals (`--entropy` bits/char, `--min-secret-len`) | Test fixtures with fake keys, hashes → keep fakes obviously fake or override severity for the fixture path via a team rule |
| CR-EVAL | blocking | `eval(`, `exec(`, `new Function(` (not `.exec(` method calls) | Sandboxed expression engines → document and override |
| CR-TLS | blocking | `verify=False`, `rejectUnauthorized: false`, `CERT_NONE`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`, `InsecureSkipVerify: true`, `curl -k`, trust-all verifiers | Local-only dev tooling → still fix; use a local CA |
| CR-SQL-CONCAT | blocking | SQL text (`select … from`, `insert into`, `update … set`, `delete from`) built with `+`, f-strings, `${}`, `%` or `.format()` | Identifiers from a fixed allow-list → document; values must be bound parameters |
| CR-SWALLOW | warning | `except:` / `except Exception:` followed by `pass`/`...`, empty `catch {}`, `catch (Exception e) {}` | Deliberate best-effort cleanup → log at debug level instead of silence |
| CR-DEBUG | warning | `console.log/debug/trace`, `debugger`, `print(` in non-test `.py`, `pdb`, `breakpoint()`, `System.out.println`, `printStackTrace()` | CLI scripts whose job is to print → override for that path |
| CR-TODO | info | TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK without `(owner)`, `@owner`, `[ABC-123]` or `(#123)` | — |
| CR-DUP | info | the same 3 consecutive non-trivial added lines appear twice | Generated code → ignore; it is a labelled judgement call, like the upstream smell baseline |
| CR-NO-TESTS | warning | code files changed and no test file changed | Pure refactors with existing coverage → say so in the PR |

Test files: `tests/`, `__tests__/`, `spec/`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py|go`, `*.test|spec.[jt]sx?`, `*Test.java`. Debug detectors skip test files.

## Severities and the gate
`blocking` fails the run (`review.py --gate review.json` exits 1). `warning` and `info` are reported under Non-blocking (missing tests under Tests). Team rules may raise or lower any built-in severity; the change is recorded in `review.json` → `rules.overrides`.

## Thresholds are parameters
The entropy threshold, minimum literal length and the large-change label are CLI options with documented defaults, not facts about your codebase. Tune them per repository and record the values (they are echoed in `review.json`).

vendor/code-review/SKILL.md:
---
name: code-review
description: "Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\"."
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Search the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Issue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).
- The brief: "Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

# domain-modeling-runner

Wraps `domain-modeling` from mattpocock/skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). Upstream is a conversational discipline — challenge terms against the glossary, sharpen fuzzy language, stress-test relationships with scenarios, record hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs. This skill makes the checkable part deterministic (structure, identifiers, cardinalities, glossary gaps, invariants) and passes the upstream instructions and its glossary/ADR formats to the optional review step by path (`../../../vendor/domain-modeling/SKILL.md`), never by copy.

## In a conversation: write the model now
- **Entities, relationships and glossary are stated in the conversation** (CSV text or plain sentences): write `model.md` **in this reply** in this order — Diagram (Mermaid `erDiagram` with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases `1 to 0+` for 1:N, `1 to 1`, `0+ to 0+`), Entities, Relationships, Invariants (a checklist to confirm: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs), Glossary (`**Term**:` definition, `_Avoid_:` synonyms; supplied definitions kept word for word; any entity without one gets `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`), Open questions (every error and warning, owned by the domain expert). An N:M relationship is drawn through its join entity (e.g. Enrollment between Student and Course).
- **Validate before drawing**: errors E1–E6 — relationship endpoint not a defined entity, entity without identifier, cardinality not `1:1`/`1:N`/`N:M` (e.g. `many`), N:M without `join: <Entity>`, duplicate attribute, bad `required` value; warnings W1–W3 — orphan entity, term without definition, glossary term that is not an entity. Any error means the run fails: say so on line 1, leave invalid relationships out of the diagram, and list each error under Open questions. Never add an undefined entity (e.g. an Instructor that has no entity rows) to make a relationship valid.
- **Existing model plus revised files**: compare and list what is added, removed or changed (entities, attributes, `required`, type changes); every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.
- **The request says files are attached but their contents are not in the conversation**: still write every section now from whatever the request states, with each entity, attribute, cardinality or definition not given shown as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the file it comes from (entities CSV, relationships CSV, glossary CSV, baseline `model.json`). With a review request, also lay out the modeling review per `assets/modeling-review-template.md` — Challenged terms, Edge-case scenarios, Invariants to confirm, ADR candidates — per the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for files.
- **Relationships entirely missing** (entities only, "draw the ER diagram"): ask once for the relationships (`from,to,cardinality,name[,notes]`) instead of guessing how entities relate; definitions and cardinalities are never invented.

## Starting points
- **New** — entities, relationships and glossary become a validated model: Mermaid ER diagram, invariants, glossary, open questions.
- **Existing** — add `baseline` (the `model.json` of today's model): the proposed model is validated the same way and compared with it — what is added, removed or changed — and every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.

## When to use
- Before schema, API or event design: get entities, keys and cardinalities agreed.
- When terms drift ("account" vs "customer"): build the glossary and see which terms lack a definition.
- NOT for: SQL migrations and RLS (`supabase-schema-rls`), tenancy audits (`multi-tenant-saas-patterns`), product requirements (`product-spec-prd`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `entities` | yes | One row per attribute: `entity,attribute,type,required,notes`. Mark the identifier with an `id` / `<entity>_id` name or `PK` in notes; `FK` in notes marks a foreign key. |
| `relationships` | yes | `from,to,cardinality,name[,notes]`; cardinality `1:1`, `1:N`, `N:M`; N:M needs `join: <Entity>` in notes. |
| `glossary` | no | `term,definition[,avoid]`. Entities without a definition get `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`. |
| `title` | no | Bounded-context name (default "Domain model"). |
| `narrative` | no | `true` runs the LLM modeling review. |

## Procedure
1. **Read** the CSVs (`scripts/model.py`); missing columns or files → exit 2 naming them.
2. **Validate** (errors E1–E6): undefined relationship endpoints, entities without identifier, bad cardinality, N:M without join, duplicate attributes, bad `required` values. **Warn** (W1–W3): orphan entities (join entities count as linked), terms without definitions, glossary terms that are not entities.
3. **Render the diagram**: Mermaid `erDiagram` with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases (`1 to 0+` for 1:N, `1 to 1`, `0+ to 0+`). Invalid relationships are left out of the diagram.
4. **Derive invariants**: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs — as a checklist to confirm, not as facts.
5. **Glossary** in the upstream GLOSSARY format (`**Term**:` definition, `_Avoid_:` synonyms).
6. **Open questions**: every error and warning, owned by the domain expert.
7. Optional: with `narrative=true` the LLM fills `assets/modeling-review-template.md`.

## Output
- `model.md` — Diagram, Entities, Relationships, Invariants, Glossary, Open questions.
- `model.json` — entities, relationships, glossary, invariants, errors, warnings; `model.py --check` fails on errors or undefined endpoints.
- `modeling-review.md` (only with `narrative=true`).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every relationship endpoint is a defined entity; every entity has an identifier
- [ ] Every N:M names its join; every cardinality is 1:1, 1:N or N:M
- [ ] The Mermaid block parses; invalid relationships are not drawn
- [ ] No definition was invented: missing ones carry `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`
- [ ] Invariants are presented as a checklist to confirm

## References
- `references/modeling-rules.md` — validation rules, Mermaid mapping, invariant derivation
- `assets/entities-template.csv`, `assets/relationships-template.csv`, `assets/glossary-template.csv` — input layouts
- `assets/modeling-review-template.md` — narrative template for the optional LLM step
- `scripts/model.py` — validator, renderer and contract check (argparse; stdlib)
- Upstream method: `vendor/domain-modeling/` (SKILL.md, GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md, ADR-FORMAT.md)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/domain-modeling-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/domain-modeling-runner`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. # Modeling rules — what the runner checks and renders

The vendored `domain-modeling` skill (mattpocock/skills, pinned in `vendor/pins.json`) is the method: challenge language, sharpen terms, test relationships with scenarios, keep a glossary free of implementation detail, and write ADRs only for hard-to-reverse trade-offs. Read `vendor/domain-modeling/SKILL.md` and its `GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md`; this note documents the runner's deterministic rules.

## Validation
| Code | Kind | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | error | A relationship's `from` or `to` is not an entity in entities.csv (names compared case- and punctuation-insensitively) |
| E2 | error | An entity has no identifier: no attribute named `id` / `<entity>_id`, and no notes containing `PK`, `identifier` or `primary key` |
| E3 | error | Cardinality not `1:1`, `1:N` or `N:M` |
| E4 | error | `N:M` without a join: notes must contain `join: <Name>` or name another defined entity |
| E5 | error | Duplicate attribute within one entity |
| E6 | error | `required` not one of yes/no/true/false/y/n/1/0 |
| W1 | warning | Orphan entity: not an endpoint or join of any relationship |
| W2 | warning | Entity or glossary term without a definition → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]` |
| W3 | warning | Glossary term that is not an entity (attribute, state, or a missing entity?) |

Errors exit 1 but both outputs are written so the gaps are visible. Missing files or columns exit 2. Rows whose first cell starts with `#` are comments.

## Mermaid mapping
| CSV cardinality | erDiagram relationship |
|---|---|
| `1:1` | `A 1 to 1 B` |
| `1:N` | `A 1 to 0+ B` (one A, zero or more B) |
| `N:M` | `A 0+ to 0+ B` (the join entity is drawn as its own entity) |

Text aliases (`1`, `0+`, `to`) are Mermaid ER syntax and avoid the brace markers (`o{`), so the diagram has balanced brackets. A front-matter title block (`---` / `title:` / `---`) names the context. Attribute types are reduced to `[A-Za-z0-9_]` (e.g. `decimal(4,1)` → `decimal_4_1_`); comments drop quotes and brackets. If your relationship is optional on the "one" side, record that in notes; the diagram shows the mandatory form.

## Invariants
Derived, not discovered: each identifier is unique; each required attribute is set; for 1:N every child belongs to exactly one parent; for 1:1 each side has at most one partner; for N:M a pair appears at most once in the join. Present them as a checklist for the domain expert to confirm and for engineering to enforce in schema or code.

## Glossary
Format per the upstream GLOSSARY format: `**Term**:` on one line, the definition on the next, `_Avoid_:` with synonyms. Every entity appears; definitions come only from glossary.csv.

---
name: domain-modeling
description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
---

# Domain Modeling

Actively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `GLOSSARY.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)

## File structure

Most repos have a single context:

```
/
├── GLOSSARY.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/
│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

If a `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:

```
/
├── GLOSSARY-MAP.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
├── src/
│   ├── ordering/
│   │   ├── GLOSSARY.md
│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions
│   └── billing/
│       ├── GLOSSARY.md
│       └── docs/adr/
```

Create files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `GLOSSARY.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

### Challenge against the glossary

When the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `GLOSSARY.md`, call it out immediately. "Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?"

### Sharpen fuzzy language

When the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. "You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things."

### Discuss concrete scenarios

When domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.

### Cross-reference with code

When the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: "Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?"

### Update GLOSSARY.md inline

When a term is resolved, update `GLOSSARY.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md](./GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md).

`GLOSSARY.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `GLOSSARY.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.

### Offer ADRs sparingly

Only offer to create an ADR when all three are true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).

# GLOSSARY.md Format

## Structure

```md
# {Context Name}

{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}

## Language

**Order**:
{A one or two sentence description of the term}
_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction

**Invoice**:
A request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.
_Avoid_: Bill, payment request

**Customer**:
A person or organization that places orders.
_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account
```

## Rules

- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.
- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.
- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.
- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.

## Single vs multi-context repos

**Single context (most repos):** One `GLOSSARY.md` at the repo root.

**Multiple contexts:** A `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:

```md
# Glossary Map

## Contexts

- [Ordering](./src/ordering/GLOSSARY.md): receives and tracks customer orders
- [Billing](./src/billing/GLOSSARY.md): generates invoices and processes payments
- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/GLOSSARY.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping

## Relationships

- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking
- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices
- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`
```

The skill infers which structure applies:

- If `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts
- If only a root `GLOSSARY.md` exists, single context
- If neither exists, create a root `GLOSSARY.md` lazily when the first term is resolved

When multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.

# ADR Format

ADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.

Create the `docs/adr/` directory lazily: only when the first ADR is needed.

## Template

```md
# {Short title of the decision}

{1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}
```

That's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why*, not in filling out sections.

## Optional sections

Only include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.

- **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`): useful when decisions are revisited
- **Considered Options**: only when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering
- **Consequences**: only when non-obvious downstream effects need to be called out

## Numbering

Scan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number and increment by one.

## When to offer an ADR

All three of these must be true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will look at the code and wonder "why on earth did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If a decision is easy to reverse, skip it: you'll just reverse it. If it's not surprising, nobody will wonder why. If there was no real alternative, there's nothing to record beyond "we did the obvious thing."

### What qualifies

- **Architectural shape.** "We're using a monorepo." "The write model is event-sourced, the read model is projected into Postgres."
- **Integration patterns between contexts.** "Ordering and Billing communicate via domain events, not synchronous HTTP."
- **Technology choices that carry lock-in.** Database, message bus, auth provider, deployment target. Not every library: just the ones that would take a quarter to swap out.
- **Boundary and scope decisions.** "Customer data is owned by the Customer context; other contexts reference it by ID only." The explicit no-s are as valuable as the yes-s.
- **Deliberate deviations from the obvious path.** "We're using manual SQL instead of an ORM because X." Anything where a reasonable reader would assume the opposite. These stop the next engineer from "fixing" something that was deliberate.
- **Constraints not visible in the code.** "We can't use AWS because of compliance requirements." "Response times must be under 200ms because of the partner API contract."
- **Rejected alternatives when the rejection is non-obvious.** If you considered GraphQL and picked REST for subtle reasons, record it; otherwise someone will suggest GraphQL again in six months.

# handoff-and-thread-close

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/handoff-and-thread-close --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/handoff-and-thread-close`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Every changed file comes from `git diff --name-status`; copy the result to `docs/HANDOFF.md` (or pass `--write-to-repo` to the script) and commit it so the next run knows where this thread ended.

## Starting points
- **New** — a repo with no `docs/HANDOFF.md` gets its first one from the whole git history: commits, changed files with their why, a next-thread prompt.
- **Existing** — the current `docs/HANDOFF.md` is read: only commits since it was last updated are summarised, and its open items are carried forward.

## When to use
- End of a thread; topic change (rule: one topic per thread); context window filling; before a long pause.
- After any build skill finishes its verify gate.
- NOT for: writing the PR itself (the PR template covers that), changelogs.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Repo with `docs/HANDOFF.md` (create from `assets/HANDOFF.md` if missing) | yes | repo |
| Git state (`git status`, `git diff --stat`, recent commits) | yes | repo |
| What was attempted and what remains (from the thread) | yes | thread |
| Verification results (commands run and outcomes) | yes | thread — if not run, run them now |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md` (HANDOFF contract, rules 5 and 7) and `references/handoff-method.md`.
2. **Collect facts from git, not memory.** `git status --short`, `git diff --stat main...HEAD` (or since last HANDOFF commit), `git log --oneline -10`. Every changed file in the handoff comes from this list.
3. **Verify or declare.** Run lint / typecheck / unit / build if not run in this thread. Record results. If something is red, the state line says so first. *(gate: verify)*
4. **Write HANDOFF.md** per `assets/HANDOFF.md`: State (one line, honest), Done this thread, Changed files (path — why), Open items (owner), Decisions made (with ADR links if any), Next thread starts with (an exact prompt that names the files to read and the first action).
5. **Prune.** Remove items from previous threads that are done; keep the file ≤ 80 lines. Older history lives in git.
6. **Changed-files list** in chat (≤ 15 lines) for commit/PR; flag any file changed that is outside the thread's topic (should it be reverted or split?).
7. **Thread summary** in chat: ≤ 50 words, bottom line first.
8. Offer the commit command (`git add <files> && git commit -m "<type>: <msg>"`) — do not run it unless asked.

## Output
| Artifact | Path / form |
|---|---|
| HANDOFF | `docs/HANDOFF.md` |
| Changed files | chat list |
| Next-thread prompt | inside HANDOFF; also pasted in chat as a code block |
| Commit command | chat |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every changed file came from `git status/diff`, not recollection
- [ ] State line is true (green/red/partial) and first
- [ ] Each open item has an owner
- [ ] Next-thread prompt is copy-paste ready and names files to read first
- [ ] HANDOFF ≤ 80 lines; stale items removed
- [ ] Off-topic changes flagged
- [ ] No secrets, no personal details, no chat transcript pasted

## References
- `references/handoff-method.md` — what goes in, what stays out, prompt-writing rules
- `assets/HANDOFF.md` — the contract template
- `assets/next-thread-prompt.md` — prompt patterns per situation
- `scripts/handoff.py` — fills HANDOFF.md from git (commits, changed files, carried open items); `scripts/make_fixture_repo.py` builds the eval repo
