#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write HANDOFF.md from git facts, not memory.

    python3 -I scripts/handoff.py --target <repo> --state "green — invoices export shipped" \
        [--since <ref|YYYY-MM-DD>] [--project <name>] [--template assets/HANDOFF.md] \
        --out HANDOFF.md [--write-to-repo]

Range: --since <ref> (`<ref>..HEAD`) or --since <date>; otherwise commits after the last commit that
touched docs/HANDOFF.md in the target; otherwise the whole history. Fills the template:
  State                    --state verbatim
  Done this thread         commit subjects in the range (+ "uncommitted changes present" if any)
  Changed files            `git diff --name-status` over the range, each with the subject of the
                           last commit that touched it; uncommitted files from `git status`
  Open items               bullets carried from the previous docs/HANDOFF.md "Open items" section
  Decisions                left for the author (TBD marker)
  Next thread starts with  prompt skeleton naming the files to read; first action is a TBD marker
Keeps the file <= 80 lines (older history lives in git). --write-to-repo also copies the result to
<target>/docs/HANDOFF.md. Exit 1 when the target is not a git repository root or git fails. Stdlib, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DEFAULT_TEMPLATE = HERE.parent / "assets" / "HANDOFF.md"
TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Project owner]"
MAX_LINES = 80
STATUS_WORD = {"A": "added", "M": "modified", "D": "deleted", "R": "renamed", "C": "copied", "T": "type changed"}


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def git(target: Path, *args: str, ok_codes=(0,)) -> str:
    r = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=str(target), capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode not in ok_codes:
        die(f"git {' '.join(args)}: {r.stderr.strip() or 'failed'}")
    return r.stdout


def previous_handoff_commit(target: Path, rel: str) -> str:
    out = git(target, "log", "-1", "--format=%H", "--", rel).strip()
    return out


def section_bullets(text: str, heading: str) -> list[str]:
    lines, out, inside = text.splitlines(), [], False
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.startswith("#"):
            if inside:
                break
            inside = heading.lower() in ln.lower()
            continue
        if inside and ln.strip().startswith("- ") and ln.strip() not in ("- …", "- ..."):
            out.append(ln.strip())
    return out


def replace_section(md: str, heading_startswith: str, body_lines: list[str]) -> str:
    """Replace the body of the first `## <heading…>` section with body_lines (heading kept)."""
    lines, out, i = md.splitlines(), [], 0
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        out.append(ln)
        i += 1
        if ln.startswith("## ") and ln[3:].lower().startswith(heading_startswith.lower()):
            out += body_lines
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith("## "):
                i += 1
            if i < len(lines):
                out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate HANDOFF.md from git history")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="git repo")
    ap.add_argument("--state", required=True, help='one honest line, e.g. "green — export shipped, e2e pending"')
    ap.add_argument("--since", default="", help="ref or YYYY-MM-DD; default: last commit touching docs/HANDOFF.md")
    ap.add_argument("--project", default="", help="project name (default: repo dir name)")
    ap.add_argument("--template", default=str(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE))
    ap.add_argument("--handoff-path", default="docs/HANDOFF.md", help="where the previous handoff lives in the repo")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="HANDOFF.md")
    ap.add_argument("--write-to-repo", action="store_true", help="also copy the result to <target>/<handoff-path>")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    target = Path(a.target)
    if not target.is_dir():
        die(f"target is not a directory: {target}")
    top = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], cwd=str(target), capture_output=True, text=True)
    if top.returncode != 0:
        die(f"not a git repository: {target}")
    if Path(top.stdout.strip()).resolve() != target.resolve():
        die(f"{target} is not a repository root (git root is {top.stdout.strip()}); pass the root directory")
    tmpl_path = Path(a.template)
    if not tmpl_path.is_file():
        die(f"template not found: {tmpl_path}")
    head = git(target, "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD", ok_codes=(0, 1)).strip()
    if not head:
        die("repository has no commits")

    # ---- range
    prev_text = ""
    prev_file = target / a.handoff_path
    if prev_file.is_file():
        prev_text = prev_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if a.since:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", a.since):
            log_args, diff_base, basis = [f"--since={a.since}"], "", f"since {a.since}"
            first = git(target, "log", "--reverse", "--format=%H", f"--since={a.since}").split()
            diff_base = f"{first[0]}~1" if first else ""
        else:
            git(target, "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", a.since + "^{commit}")
            log_args, diff_base, basis = [f"{a.since}..HEAD"], a.since, f"since {a.since}"
    else:
        base = previous_handoff_commit(target, a.handoff_path)
        if base and base != head:
            log_args, diff_base, basis = [f"{base}..HEAD"], base, f"since last HANDOFF commit {base[:7]}"
        elif base == head:
            log_args, diff_base, basis = [f"{base}..HEAD"], base, f"since last HANDOFF commit {base[:7]} (no new commits)"
        else:
            log_args, diff_base, basis = ["HEAD"], "", "whole history (no previous HANDOFF commit)"

    commits = []
    for ln in git(target, "log", "--format=%h%x1f%s", *log_args).splitlines():
        h, _, s = ln.partition("\x1f")
        commits.append((h, s))

    # ---- changed files with why
    why: dict[str, str] = {}
    for h, s in reversed(commits):  # oldest first so the latest subject wins
        for f in git(target, "show", "--name-only", "--format=", h).split():
            why[f] = s
    changed = []
    if diff_base:
        root = git(target, "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", diff_base + "^{commit}", ok_codes=(0, 1)).strip()
        name_status = git(target, "diff", "--name-status", root, "HEAD") if root else ""
    else:
        name_status = git(target, "show", "--name-status", "--format=", *[h for h, _ in commits]) if commits else ""
    seen = set()
    for ln in name_status.splitlines():
        parts = ln.split("\t")
        if len(parts) < 2:
            continue
        status, path = parts[0][0], parts[-1]
        if path in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(path)
        changed.append(f"- `{path}` — {STATUS_WORD.get(status, status)}: {why.get(path, TBD)}")
    uncommitted = [ln[3:].strip() for ln in git(target, "status", "--porcelain").splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    for path in uncommitted:
        if path not in seen:
            changed.append(f"- `{path}` — uncommitted: {TBD}")

    done = [f"- {s} (`{h}`)" for h, s in commits] or [f"- no commits {basis}"]
    if uncommitted:
        done.append(f"- uncommitted changes present ({len(uncommitted)} file(s)) — commit or stash before closing")
    open_items = section_bullets(prev_text, "Open items") or [f"- none carried (no previous {a.handoff_path} open items)"]
    open_items.append(f"- {TBD} new open items from this thread")

    project = a.project or target.resolve().name
    today = dt.date.today().isoformat()
    md = tmpl_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    md = md.replace("{{PROJECT}}", project).replace("{{DATE}}", today)
    md = re.sub(r"^## State:.*$", f"## State: {a.state}", md, count=1, flags=re.M)
    md = replace_section(md, "Done this thread", done)
    md = replace_section(md, "Changed files", changed or ["- none in range"])
    md = replace_section(md, "Open items", open_items)
    md = replace_section(md, "Decisions", [f"- {TBD} (link ADRs if any)"])
    md = replace_section(md, "Tried and rejected", ["- none recorded"])
    files_to_read = ["docs/HANDOFF.md"] + [f for f in ("CLAUDE.md", "docs/SPEC.md") if (target / f).exists()]
    md = replace_section(md, "Next thread starts with", [
        "```", f"Read {', '.join(files_to_read)}.",
        f"Use <skill>. {TBD} first action. Gate: plan→approve before any code.", "```"])
    md = md.replace("- …\n", "")
    lines = md.rstrip("\n").splitlines()
    if len(lines) > MAX_LINES:
        # trim the changed-files list first; older history lives in git
        keep = []
        in_changed, n = False, 0
        for ln in lines:
            if ln.startswith("## "):
                in_changed = ln.startswith("## Changed files")
                n = 0
            if in_changed and ln.startswith("- "):
                n += 1
                if n > 25:
                    if n == 26:
                        keep.append(f"- … {len(changed) - 25} more — see `git diff --name-status {diff_base or 'HEAD'}`")
                    continue
            keep.append(ln)
        lines = keep
    out_text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(out_text, encoding="utf-8")
    if a.write_to_repo:
        prev_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy(out, prev_file)
    print(f"HANDOFF: {len(commits)} commit(s) {basis}, {len(changed)} changed file(s), "
          f"{len(open_items) - 1} open item(s) carried, {len(lines)} lines -> {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a throwaway git repo from a layout of commit folders (evals/demos only).

    python3 -I scripts/make_fixture_repo.py --from evals/fixtures/repo-files --target <dir>

`--from` holds numbered folders (`01-init/`, `02-feature/`, …), each a file tree that is copied over
the target and committed; the subject comes from a `COMMIT_MSG` file in the folder (not copied) or
the folder name. A folder named `uncommitted/` is copied last without committing, to simulate work
in progress. A target this script built earlier is wiped and rebuilt; any other git repo is refused. Exit 1 on bad input. Stdlib.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MARKER = ".fixture-repo"
GIT_ID = ["-c", "user.name=fixture", "-c", "user.email=fixture@example.com", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false"]


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def git(target: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    r = subprocess.run(["git", *GIT_ID, *args], cwd=str(target), capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        die(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed: {r.stderr.strip()}")
    return r.stdout


def copy_tree(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    for p in sorted(src.rglob("*")):
        if p.name == "COMMIT_MSG" or not p.is_file():
            continue
        rel = p.relative_to(src)
        (dst / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy(p, dst / rel)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build a tiny git repo from commit folders")
    ap.add_argument("--from", dest="src", required=True, help="directory of commit folders")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="repo directory to create")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    src, target = Path(a.src), Path(a.target)
    if not src.is_dir():
        die(f"source layout not found: {src}")
    folders = sorted(p for p in src.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and p.name != "uncommitted")
    if not folders:
        die(f"no commit folders under {src}")
    if (target / ".git").exists():
        if not (target / MARKER).exists():
            die(f"target already is a git repo (not one this script built): {target}")
        shutil.rmtree(target)  # rebuild a repo this script made earlier (re-runs into the same out dir)
    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (target / MARKER).write_text("built by make_fixture_repo.py — safe to delete\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git(target, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    for f in folders:
        copy_tree(f, target)
        msg_file = f / "COMMIT_MSG"
        subject = msg_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() if msg_file.is_file() else f.name.split("-", 1)[-1]
        git(target, "add", "-A")
        git(target, "commit", "-q", "-m", subject)
        print(f"committed: {subject}")
    unc = src / "uncommitted"
    if unc.is_dir():
        copy_tree(unc, target)
        print("copied uncommitted changes")
    print(f"fixture repo at {target}: {len(folders)} commit(s)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Handoff Method

Purpose: the next thread (a cold context) resumes in one read with zero re-explanation. Recurring context lives in repo docs, not chat.

## What goes in
| Section | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| State | one line: `green — feature X built and verified, PR open` / `red — unit suite failing in Y` / `partial — T1–T3 done, T4 in progress` | verification run |
| Done this thread | bullets, past tense, outcome not activity ("invoices table + RLS + 6 tests", not "worked on invoices") | thread |
| Changed files | `path — why`, from git | `git status`, `git diff --stat` |
| Open items (owner) | each with an owner and, if known, a date; questions needing a human decision marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` | thread |
| Decisions | one line each; link ADR when one exists | thread |
| Verification | table: check → command → result | thread |
| Next thread starts with | exact prompt (see below) | you |

## What stays out
- Chat transcript, reasoning, dead ends (one line under "tried and rejected" if it saves the next thread time).
- Secrets, env values, personal details.
- Anything already in SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md or an ADR — link instead.
- History older than the previous thread (git has it).

## Next-thread prompt rules
| Rule | Example |
|---|---|
| Names the files to read first | "Read docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/plans/2026-04-01-invoice-export.md" |
| Names the skill to use | "Use spec-to-plan" / "Use safe-fix" |
| Names the first concrete action | "Start at task T4: implement export service" |
| States the gate | "Post the plan and wait for go" / "Repro first" |
| One topic | if two topics remain, write two prompts and say which is first |
| ≤ 8 lines | fits a paste |

## Off-topic drift check
Compare changed files with the thread's topic. Any file outside it: either revert (`git checkout -- path`) or call it out as "split into separate PR: …" in open items. Never silently bundle.

## When the thread ends red
State line first: `red — <what fails>`. Then: repro command, what was tried, hypothesis, and a next prompt that begins with "Use safe-fix. Repro: `<command>`".

## Size discipline
HANDOFF.md ≤ 80 lines. If longer, move detail to the plan file or an ADR and link.

      - {step: policies, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/rbac_to_sql.py {rbac} --out {out}/policies.sql"}
      - {step: audit, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/tenancy_audit.py --migrations {migrations} [--exempt {exempt}] [--tenant-column {tenant_column}] --rbac {rbac} --out {out}/audit.csv --report {out}/audit.md"}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/policies.sql", checks: [exists, contains:"create policy", contains:"-- rollback:"]}
      - {path: "{out}/audit.csv", checks: [exists, csv:[table,file,has_tenant_id,rls_enabled,tenant_index,policies,exempt,status,findings], csv_rows:status~^(ok|finding)$]}
      - {path: "{out}/audit.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Tables","Rules"]]}
    modes:
      new: {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "your first migration; the starter role matrix is used"}
      existing: {case: agent-mode-existing, bring: "your existing migrations folder and current role matrix"}

# multi-tenant-saas-patterns

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/multi-tenant-saas-patterns --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/multi-tenant-saas-patterns`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The audit step exits 1 when a non-exempt table lacks tenant_id, RLS or a tenant-leading index; hand the findings and `policies.sql` to supabase-schema-rls for the migration.

## Starting points
- **New** — your first migration is audited for tenant_id, RLS, policies and a tenant-leading index, and RLS policies are generated from the starter RBAC matrix.
- **Existing** — your whole migrations folder is replayed in order (columns and keys added later by `alter table`, tables dropped later), each table that still exists is audited, your own RBAC matrix is cross-checked against those tables, and policies are generated from it.

## When to use
- "Add organisations/workspaces", "who can do what", "plans and limits", "feature flags per customer", "audit trail", "invite users", "switch tenant".
- Before the first migration of a multi-tenant app; before adding billing.
- NOT for: writing the SQL (`supabase-schema-rls` does that from this design), security verification (`security-review`), single-tenant apps.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tenant concept (org / workspace / account) and whether users belong to many | yes | user — ask once |
| Roles needed and the actions that matter (≤ 20 actions) | yes | `docs/SPEC.md` / user |
| Plans / tiers and the limits/features that differ | yes if billing | user |
| Compliance needs for audit (retention, immutability, export) | no | user; default 1 year, append-only |
| Existing schema | yes if present | repo |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` (Multi-tenant, Auth rows) and `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. **Plan.** Decide the four models with the user using `references/tenant-model.md` decision table: tenancy shape, membership, claims, invitation. Post a one-page design summary; wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Tenant model.** Produce the table list (tenants, tenant_members, invitations), JWT claim strategy (`app_metadata.tenant_id`, `role`; refresh on switch), tenant-switch flow, and the `requireUser()` contract.
4. **RBAC matrix.** Fill `assets/rbac-matrix.csv` (role × action → allow/deny/own) following `references/rbac.md`; define enforcement points: RLS (data), `requireRole()` (actions), UI (hide only). Each action maps to a policy and a service check.
5. **Plans and feature flags.** From `references/plans-and-flags.md`: `plans`, `tenant_subscriptions`, `tenant_features` (overrides), `entitlements` resolution order, limit checks in services (not UI), flag naming `feature.<name>`.
6. **Audit log.** From `references/audit-log.md`: `audit_log` table (append-only, RLS read by admin, no update/delete), `app.audit_row()` trigger, application-level events for non-row actions, retention and export.
7. **Hand off to build.** Produce the migration task list for `supabase-schema-rls` and the service/action list for `nextjs-enterprise-conventions`; include negative tests for `test-strategy-tdd`. *(gate: build via those skills → test)*
8. **Verify.** Walk the checklist: every tenant table has `tenant_id` + RLS; every RBAC action has an enforcement point; every limit is checked in a service; every sensitive action is audited. *(gate: verify)*
9. Record decisions as ADRs (`project-bootstrap/assets/adr-template.md`); update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Design doc | `docs/tenancy.md` (tenant model, claims, flows) |
| RBAC matrix | `docs/rbac-matrix.csv` (from `assets/rbac-matrix.csv`) |
| Plans/flags design | `docs/tenancy.md` §Plans |
| Audit design | `docs/tenancy.md` §Audit |
| ADRs | `docs/adr/NNNN-tenancy.md`, `NNNN-rbac.md` |
| Build task list | for `supabase-schema-rls` / `nextjs-enterprise-conventions` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Tenant id comes only from the JWT (`app_metadata`), never from client input
- [ ] Role change or tenant switch forces a token refresh; stale-claim window stated
- [ ] RBAC matrix: every action has RLS + service enforcement; UI is hide-only
- [ ] Limits enforced in services with a `Result` error code (`PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED`)
- [ ] Audit log append-only; actor, tenant, entity, action, before/after, requestId
- [ ] Cross-tenant unique constraints scoped by `tenant_id`
- [ ] Deleting a tenant: cascade plan + export + retention stated

## References
- `references/tenant-model.md` — tenancy shapes, membership, claims, invitation and switch flows, deletion
- `references/rbac.md` — role design, matrix method, enforcement points, testing
- `references/plans-and-flags.md` — plans, entitlements, overrides, flag lifecycle

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate RLS policies from the RBAC matrix — one policy per action × role.

    python3 -I scripts/rbac_to_sql.py assets/rbac-matrix.csv --out policies.sql [--schema public] [--owner-column created_by]

Input: the assets/rbac-matrix.csv layout — action (`<entity>.<verb>`), resource (table), one column
per role (viewer, member, admin, owner … value allow | deny | own), enforcement_rls (policy name
stem or `n/a …`), enforcement_service, ui, audited. Verb → operation: read/list/view/export/get →
select; create/invite/upload/add → insert; update/change_*/void/toggle/edit/set → update;
delete/remove → delete. Rows whose enforcement_rls starts with `n/a` are emitted as comments
(service-only paths). JWT convention from references/tenant-model.md: tenant and role come from
`auth.jwt() -> 'app_metadata'`; `own` adds `<owner-column> = auth.uid()`. Writes policies.sql with
`-- rollback:` drop statements. Exit 1 on missing file, missing columns or no allow/own cell. Stdlib.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

NON_ROLE = {"action", "resource", "enforcement_rls", "enforcement_service", "ui", "audited"}
OPS = [("select", ("read", "list", "view", "export", "get", "search")),
       ("insert", ("create", "invite", "upload", "add", "import")),
       ("update", ("update", "change", "void", "toggle", "edit", "set", "rename", "archive", "transfer")),
       ("delete", ("delete", "remove"))]
TENANT = "(select (auth.jwt() -> 'app_metadata' ->> 'tenant_id'))::uuid"
ROLE = "(select auth.jwt() -> 'app_metadata' ->> 'role')"


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def op_for(action: str) -> str | None:
    verb = action.split(".", 1)[-1].lower()
    for op, verbs in OPS:
        if any(verb == v or verb.startswith(v + "_") for v in verbs):
            return op
    return None


def ident(s: str) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]+", "_", s.lower()).strip("_")
    return s[:63]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="RBAC matrix CSV -> RLS policies SQL")
    ap.add_argument("matrix", help="rbac-matrix.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="policies.sql")
    ap.add_argument("--schema", default="public")
    ap.add_argument("--owner-column", default="created_by", help="column compared to auth.uid() for `own`")
    ap.add_argument("--tenant-table", default="tenants", help="the tenants table itself, where the tenant column is `id`")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    p = Path(a.matrix)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"matrix not found: {p}")
    rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
            if not (r.get("action") or "").strip().startswith("#")]   # a leading `#` row is a fixture/comment note
    if not rows:
        die("matrix has no rows")
    header = list(rows[0].keys())
    for col in ("action", "resource"):
        if col not in header:
            die(f"matrix lacks column '{col}' (expected the assets/rbac-matrix.csv layout)")
    roles = [h for h in header if h and h not in NON_ROLE]
    if not roles:
        die("matrix has no role columns")

    out = [f"-- policies.sql — generated by multi-tenant-saas-patterns/scripts/rbac_to_sql.py from {p.name}",
           f"-- Convention: tenant and role are read from the JWT app_metadata claims (references/tenant-model.md);",
           f"-- `own` rows compare {a.owner_column} with auth.uid(). One policy per action × role. Review before applying;",
           "-- hand to supabase-schema-rls for the migration (with its rollback block) and rls_lint.py.", ""]
    rollback, n_pol, skipped, unmapped = [], 0, [], []
    for r in rows:
        action, table = r["action"].strip(), ident(r["resource"].strip().split(".")[-1])
        if not action or not table:
            continue
        rls = (r.get("enforcement_rls") or "").strip()
        if rls.lower().startswith("n/a"):
            skipped.append(action)
            out.append(f"-- {action}: no RLS policy ({rls}); enforced in service: {r.get('enforcement_service', '')}")
            continue
        op = op_for(action)
        if not op:
            unmapped.append(action)
            out.append(f"-- {action}: verb not mapped to an operation — write this policy by hand")
            continue
        for role in roles:
            cell = (r.get(role) or "").strip().lower()
            if cell not in ("allow", "own"):
                continue
            name = ident(f"{rls or table + '_' + op}_{role}")
            tcol = "id" if table == ident(a.tenant_table) else "tenant_id"
            pred = f"{tcol} = {TENANT} and {ROLE} = '{role}'"
            if cell == "own":
                pred += f" and {a.owner_column} = (select auth.uid())"
            clause = f"with check ({pred})" if op == "insert" else f"using ({pred})" + (f"\n  with check ({pred})" if op == "update" else "")
            out.append(f"-- {action} / {role}: {cell}" + (f"; audited" if (r.get('audited') or '').strip().lower() == 'yes' else ""))
            out.append(f"create policy {name} on {a.schema}.{table}\n  for {op} to authenticated\n  {clause};")
            out.append("")
            rollback.append(f"-- drop policy if exists {name} on {a.schema}.{table};")
            n_pol += 1
    if n_pol == 0:
        die("no allow/own cells found — nothing to generate")
    out += ["-- rollback:"] + rollback
    outp = Path(a.out)
    outp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    outp.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{n_pol} policies for {len(rows)} action(s) across roles {roles}; {len(skipped)} service-only, "
          f"{len(unmapped)} unmapped -> {outp}")
    if unmapped:
        print(f"warning: unmapped verbs: {unmapped}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Audit migrations for tenant isolation basics: tenant_id column, RLS enabled, tenant-leading index.

    python3 -I scripts/tenancy_audit.py --migrations supabase/migrations --out audit.csv --report audit.md \
        [--exempt tenants,plans,profiles] [--rbac rbac-matrix.csv]

Reads every .sql file (comments stripped) and, per `create table`, checks:
  has_tenant_id   a `tenant_id` column in the column list
  rls_enabled     `alter table <t> enable row level security`
  tenant_index    an index, primary key or unique constraint whose first column is tenant_id
  policies        number of `create policy … on <t>`
Files are read in name order, as they are applied, so an existing migration history is audited as the
schema it builds: `alter table <t> add column tenant_id` in a later file counts as the column,
`alter table <t> add [constraint x] primary key|unique (tenant_id, …)` as the tenant-leading key, and a
`drop table <t>` removes the table from the audit; `changed_in` lists the later files that altered it.
--rbac: the RBAC matrix (assets/rbac-matrix.csv layout) is cross-checked against the audited tables —
matrix resources with no table in the migrations, and tenant-scoped tables no matrix row covers — and
reported under "RBAC coverage" (advisory: the gate is the per-table findings).
Tables listed in --exempt (default: tenants, plans, feature_flags, profiles — global by design) are
reported but not counted as findings. Writes audit.csv (table, file, has_tenant_id, rls_enabled,
tenant_index, policies, exempt, status, findings) and audit.md. Exit 1 on bad input or when any
non-exempt table has a finding (a linter: fix the migration, re-run). Stdlib, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_EXEMPT = "tenants,plans,feature_flags,profiles"
CREATE_TABLE = re.compile(r"create\s+table\s+(?:if\s+not\s+exists\s+)?(?:(\w+)\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?\s*\(", re.I)
ENABLE_RLS = re.compile(r"alter\s+table\s+(?:only\s+)?(?:\w+\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?\s+enable\s+row\s+level\s+security", re.I)
CREATE_INDEX = re.compile(r"create\s+(?:unique\s+)?index\s+(?:concurrently\s+)?(?:if\s+not\s+exists\s+)?\w*\s*on\s+(?:only\s+)?(?:\w+\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?\s*(?:using\s+\w+\s*)?\(\s*\"?(\w+)", re.I)
CREATE_POLICY = re.compile(r"create\s+policy\s+\"?[\w-]+\"?\s+on\s+(?:\w+\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?", re.I)
KEY_IN_TABLE = re.compile(r"(?:primary\s+key|unique)\s*\(\s*\"?(\w+)", re.I)
ALTER_ADD_KEY = re.compile(r"alter\s+table\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?(?:only\s+)?(?:\w+\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?\s+add\s+(?:constraint\s+\"?[\w-]+\"?\s+)?(?:primary\s+key|unique)\s*\(\s*\"?(\w+)", re.I)
ALTER_ANY = re.compile(r"alter\s+table\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?(?:only\s+)?(?:\w+\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?", re.I)
DROP_TABLE = re.compile(r"drop\s+table\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?((?:(?:\w+\.)?\"?\w+\"?\s*,\s*)*(?:\w+\.)?\"?\w+\"?)", re.I)
TENANT_CANDIDATES = ("tenant_id", "workspace_id", "organization_id", "org_id", "account_id", "team_id")


def tenant_col_re(col: str) -> re.Pattern:
    return re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s,(])\"?" + re.escape(col) + r"\"?\s+\w", re.I)


def alter_add_col_re(col: str) -> re.Pattern:
    return re.compile(r"alter\s+table\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?(?:only\s+)?(?:\w+\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?\s+add\s+(?:column\s+)?(?:if\s+not\s+exists\s+)?\"?"
                      + re.escape(col) + r"\"?\s+\w", re.I)


def inline_key_re(col: str) -> re.Pattern:
    """`<col> uuid primary key` / `<col> uuid not null unique …` declared on the column itself."""
    return re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s,(])\"?" + re.escape(col) + r"\"?\s+[\w ()]*?\b(?:primary\s+key|unique)\b", re.I)


def tenant_root(col: str) -> str:
    """workspace_id → workspaces: the tenant table itself, which cannot carry its own tenant key."""
    base = col[:-3] if col.lower().endswith("_id") else col
    return (base + "es" if base.endswith("s") else base + "s").lower()


def detect_tenant_column(files: list[Path]) -> str:
    """The tenancy key this schema actually uses: the candidate column found in the most `create table` bodies
    (ties and no match fall back to tenant_id). Evidence-based, never guessed from names alone."""
    counts = {c: 0 for c in TENANT_CANDIDATES}
    for f in files:
        sql = strip_comments(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        for m in CREATE_TABLE.finditer(sql):
            body = table_body(sql, m.end() - 1)
            for c in TENANT_CANDIDATES:
                if tenant_col_re(c).search(body):
                    counts[c] += 1
    best = max(TENANT_CANDIDATES, key=lambda c: (counts[c], c == "tenant_id"))
    return best if counts[best] > 0 else "tenant_id"


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def strip_comments(sql: str) -> str:
    sql = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", " ", sql, flags=re.S)
    return re.sub(r"--[^\n]*", "", sql)


def table_body(sql: str, start: int) -> str:
    depth, i = 0, start
    while i < len(sql):
        if sql[i] == "(":
            depth += 1
        elif sql[i] == ")":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return sql[start:i + 1]
        i += 1
    return sql[start:]


def audit(files: list[Path], exempt: set[str], col: str = "tenant_id") -> list[dict]:
    """Replay the migrations in order; one row per table that still exists at the end. `col` is the tenancy key."""
    col_l, TENANT_COL, ALTER_ADD_TENANT = col.lower(), tenant_col_re(col), alter_add_col_re(col)
    tables: dict[str, dict] = {}
    rls, idx, pol = set(), set(), {}
    for f in files:
        sql = strip_comments(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        events = [(m.start(), "create", m) for m in CREATE_TABLE.finditer(sql)]
        events += [(m.start(), "drop", m) for m in DROP_TABLE.finditer(sql)]
        for _, kind, m in sorted(events, key=lambda e: e[0]):
            if kind == "drop":
                for raw in m.group(1).split(","):
                    name = raw.strip().split(".")[-1].strip('"').lower()
                    tables.pop(name, None)
                    rls.discard(name)
                    idx.discard(name)
                    pol.pop(name, None)
                continue
            name = m.group(2).lower()
            body = table_body(sql, m.end() - 1)
            t = tables.setdefault(name, {"table": name, "file": f.name, "has_tenant_id": False, "tenant_index": False,
                                         "changed_in": []})
            t["has_tenant_id"] = t["has_tenant_id"] or bool(TENANT_COL.search(body))
            if any(k.group(1).lower() == col_l for k in KEY_IN_TABLE.finditer(body)) or inline_key_re(col).search(body):
                idx.add(name)
        for m in ALTER_ADD_TENANT.finditer(sql):
            if m.group(1).lower() in tables:
                tables[m.group(1).lower()]["has_tenant_id"] = True
        idx |= {m.group(1).lower() for m in ALTER_ADD_KEY.finditer(sql) if m.group(2).lower() == col_l}
        for m in ALTER_ANY.finditer(sql):
            t = tables.get(m.group(1).lower())
            if t and t["file"] != f.name and f.name not in t["changed_in"]:
                t["changed_in"].append(f.name)
        rls |= {m.group(1).lower() for m in ENABLE_RLS.finditer(sql)}
        idx |= {m.group(1).lower() for m in CREATE_INDEX.finditer(sql) if m.group(2).lower() == col_l}
        for m in CREATE_POLICY.finditer(sql):
            pol[m.group(1).lower()] = pol.get(m.group(1).lower(), 0) + 1
    rows = []
    for name, t in sorted(tables.items()):
        t["changed_in"] = ";".join(t["changed_in"])
        t["rls_enabled"] = name in rls
        t["tenant_index"] = name in idx
        t["policies"] = pol.get(name, 0)
        root = tenant_root(col)
        t["exempt"] = name in exempt or name == root or name.endswith("_" + root)
        findings = []
        if not t["has_tenant_id"]:
            findings.append(f"missing {col}")
        if not t["rls_enabled"]:
            findings.append("RLS not enabled")
        if not t["tenant_index"]:
            findings.append(f"no index leading with {col}")
        if t["rls_enabled"] and t["policies"] == 0:
            findings.append("RLS enabled but no policy (table unreachable — intended?)")
        if t["exempt"]:
            findings = [x for x in findings if x not in (f"missing {col}", f"no index leading with {col}")]
        t["findings"] = "; ".join(findings)
        t["status"] = "ok" if not findings else "finding"
        rows.append(t)
    return rows


def rbac_coverage(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Matrix resources without a table, and tenant-scoped tables without a matrix row."""
    if not path.is_file():
        die(f"rbac matrix not found: {path}")
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as fh:
        reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
        if "resource" not in (reader.fieldnames or []):
            die(f"rbac matrix has no 'resource' column: {path}")
        resources = sorted({(r.get("resource") or "").strip().split(".")[-1].lower() for r in reader
                            if (r.get("resource") or "").strip() and not (r.get("action") or "").startswith("#")})
    tables = {r["table"] for r in rows}
    scoped = sorted(r["table"] for r in rows if not r["exempt"])
    return {"matrix": path.name, "resources": resources,
            "resources_without_table": [x for x in resources if x not in tables],
            "tables_without_rbac": [t for t in scoped if t not in resources]}


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Audit migrations for tenant_id, RLS and tenant-leading indexes")
    ap.add_argument("--migrations", required=True, help="directory of .sql files (or one file)")
    ap.add_argument("--exempt", default=DEFAULT_EXEMPT, help=f"comma-separated global tables (default: {DEFAULT_EXEMPT})")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="audit.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--report", default="audit.md")
    ap.add_argument("--rbac", default="", help="RBAC matrix CSV to cross-check against the audited tables")
    ap.add_argument("--tenant-column", default="tenant_id",
                    help=f"the tenancy key column (default tenant_id); 'auto' picks the one the schema uses among {', '.join(TENANT_CANDIDATES)}")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    src = Path(a.migrations)
    if src.is_file():
        files = [src]
    elif src.is_dir():
        files = sorted(src.rglob("*.sql"))
    else:
        die(f"migrations not found: {src}")
    if not files:
        die(f"no .sql files under {src}")
    exempt = {x.strip().lower() for x in a.exempt.split(",") if x.strip()}
    col = a.tenant_column.strip()
    if col == "auto":
        col = detect_tenant_column(files)
    elif not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,62}", col):
        die(f"bad --tenant-column: {col}")
    rows = audit(files, exempt, col)
    if not rows:
        die("no `create table` statements found")
    cov = rbac_coverage(Path(a.rbac), rows) if a.rbac else None
    cols = ["table", "file", "has_tenant_id", "rls_enabled", "tenant_index", "policies", "exempt", "status", "findings",
            "changed_in"]
    out, rep = Path(a.out), Path(a.report)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rep.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with out.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=cols, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            w.writerow({k: (str(v).lower() if isinstance(v, bool) else v) for k, v in r.items()})
    bad = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == "finding"]
    lines = [f"# Tenancy audit — {src.name}", "",
             f"**{len(rows)} table(s) in {len(files)} migration file(s): {len(bad)} with findings. "
             + ("Gate: FAIL." if bad else "Gate: PASS.") + "**", "",
             f"Tenancy key: `{col}`" + (" (detected from the schema)" if a.tenant_column == "auto" else "") + ".", "",
             "## Tables", "", f"| Table | {col} | RLS | tenant-leading index | Policies | Exempt | Findings |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    yn = lambda b: "yes" if b else "no"  # noqa: E731
    for r in rows:
        lines.append(f"| `{r['table']}` | {yn(r['has_tenant_id'])} | {yn(r['rls_enabled'])} | {yn(r['tenant_index'])} | "
                     f"{r['policies']} | {yn(r['exempt'])} | {r['findings'] or '—'} |")
    altered = [r for r in rows if r["changed_in"]]
    if altered:
        lines += ["", "## Altered by later migrations", ""]
        lines += [f"- `{r['table']}` — created in `{r['file']}`, altered in {', '.join(f'`{x}`' for x in r['changed_in'].split(';'))}"
                  for r in altered]
    if cov is not None:
        lines += ["", "## RBAC coverage", "", f"Matrix `{cov['matrix']}`: {len(cov['resources'])} resource(s).", ""]
        lines += [f"- `{x}` is in the matrix but no migration creates it — add the table or drop the rows"
                  for x in cov["resources_without_table"]]
        lines += [f"- `{t}` is tenant-scoped but no matrix row covers it — add its actions before generating policies"
                  for t in cov["tables_without_rbac"]]
        if not cov["resources_without_table"] and not cov["tables_without_rbac"]:
            lines.append("- every matrix resource has a table and every tenant-scoped table has matrix rows")
    lines += ["", "## Rules", "",
              f"- Every tenant-scoped table: `{col} not null`, `enable row level security`, ≥1 policy, composite index leading with `{col}` (shared/stack-conventions.md).",
              f"- Exempt (global) tables: {', '.join(sorted(exempt)) or 'none'} — still need RLS and a policy.",
              "- Hand findings to supabase-schema-rls for the migration; never edit an applied migration."]
    rep.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for r in bad:
        print(f"finding  {r['table']} ({r['file']}): {r['findings']}")
    print(f"{len(rows)} table(s), {len(bad)} with findings -> {out}, {rep}")
    if bad:
        print(f"gate: FAIL — {len(bad)} table(s) need tenancy fixes", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Audit Log

## Requirements
| Requirement | Default |
|---|---|
| What | every insert/update/delete on tenant data tables; every membership, role, billing, settings, flag change; auth events of interest (invite accepted, tenant switch) |
| Who | actor user id (or `system:<job>`), tenant id, `requestId` |
| Immutability | append-only: no update/delete policies; table owned by a role the app cannot alter; optional periodic export to WORM storage |
| Retention | 1 year hot (`[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`), then archive to storage per compliance |
| Access | tenant admins read their tenant's log (RLS); owners export; platform operators via `security definer` function with logging |
| PII | before/after snapshots stored, but redact fields listed in `app.audit_redact_columns` (passwords never exist in tables anyway; emails kept — needed for audit) |

## Schema
```sql
create table public.audit_log (
  id          bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  ts          timestamptz not null default now(),
  tenant_id   uuid not null,
  actor_id    uuid,                         -- null for system
  actor_type  text not null default 'user' check (actor_type in ('user','system','service')),
  request_id  text,
  entity      text not null,                -- table or domain name: 'invoices', 'tenant_members', 'feature_flag'
  entity_id   text,
  action      text not null,                -- 'insert' | 'update' | 'delete' | domain verbs: 'invite.accept', 'role.change'
  before      jsonb,
  after       jsonb,
  diff        jsonb generated always as (app.jsonb_diff(before, after)) stored,
  meta        jsonb                         -- ip, user agent, reason
);
create index audit_log_tenant_ts_idx on public.audit_log (tenant_id, ts desc);
create index audit_log_entity_idx    on public.audit_log (tenant_id, entity, entity_id);

alter table public.audit_log enable row level security;
create policy audit_select_admin on public.audit_log for select to authenticated
  using (tenant_id = (select app.tenant_id()) and (select app.has_role('admin')));
-- no insert/update/delete policies for authenticated: writes happen via trigger (security definer) or service role.
revoke update, delete on public.audit_log from authenticated, anon;
```

## Row trigger (`app.audit_row()`)
```sql
create or replace function app.audit_row() returns trigger
language plpgsql security definer set search_path = '' as $$
declare v_tenant uuid; v_before jsonb; v_after jsonb;
begin
  v_before := case when tg_op in ('UPDATE','DELETE') then to_jsonb(old) end;
  v_after  := case when tg_op in ('INSERT','UPDATE') then to_jsonb(new) end;
  v_tenant := coalesce((v_after->>'tenant_id')::uuid, (v_before->>'tenant_id')::uuid);
  insert into public.audit_log (tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type, request_id, entity, entity_id, action, before, after)
  values (
    v_tenant,
    (select auth.uid()),
    case when (select auth.uid()) is null then 'system' else 'user' end,
    current_setting('request.headers', true)::jsonb->>'x-request-id',
    tg_table_name,
    coalesce(v_after->>'id', v_before->>'id'),
    lower(tg_op), v_before, v_after);
  return coalesce(new, old);
end $$;
```
Attach `after insert or update or delete … for each row execute function app.audit_row()` to every tenant data table (template does this).

## Application events (non-row actions)
`server/services/audit.ts` → `writeAudit({ entity: 'invitation', entityId, action: 'invite.accept', after, meta })` through the admin client (`// rls-lint: allow — audit append only`). Use for: invite sent/accepted, tenant switch, export generated, flag toggled, login anomalies.

## Reading and exporting
- Admin UI: paginated by `(tenant_id, ts desc)`; filter by entity, actor, date.
- Export: owner-only server action → CSV/JSON to private storage path `${tenantId}/audit/<date>.json`; audited itself.
- Operators: `app.audit_search(p_tenant, …)` `security definer` with mandatory reason parameter, which writes its own audit row.

## Retention job
Nightly: move rows older than retention to `audit_log_archive` (or storage), delete from hot table via service role, log counts. Never from the app path.

## Tests
- Trigger: insert/update/delete on a tenant table produce 3 audit rows with correct actor/tenant/diff.
- RLS: admin of tenant A reads only A; member cannot read; nobody can update/delete.
- App event: `acceptInvite` writes `invite.accept`.

# Plans, Entitlements, Feature Flags

## Model
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `plans` | catalogue | `id (free|pro|enterprise), name, limits jsonb, features text[], price_monthly_cents, active` |
| `tenant_subscriptions` | which plan a tenant is on | `tenant_id PK, plan_id, status (trialing|active|past_due|canceled), provider, provider_customer_id, provider_subscription_id, current_period_end, trial_ends_at` |
| `tenant_features` | per-tenant overrides | `tenant_id, feature, enabled, expires_at, reason, set_by`; PK `(tenant_id, feature)` |
| `usage_counters` | enforce limits | `tenant_id, metric, period_start, value`; PK `(tenant_id, metric, period_start)` |

Plan `limits` example: `{"seats": 5, "projects": 10, "storage_mb": 1024, "api_calls_per_day": 10000}`. Plan `features`: `["exports", "sso", "audit_export"]`.

## Entitlement resolution (`server/services/entitlements.ts`)
```
isEnabled(tenant, feature):
  1. tenant_features override (not expired)      → use it
  2. subscription.status in (active, trialing)   → feature ∈ plan.features
  3. past_due                                    → plan features, but write actions limited (grace policy)
  4. canceled / none                             → free plan features
limit(tenant, metric):  override > plan.limits[metric] > default
```
Cache per request (memoise in `AsyncLocalStorage`); never in the JWT (changes too often).

## Enforcement
| Where | Rule |
|---|---|
| Services | `const ent = await entitlements.for(user.tenantId); if (!ent.isEnabled('exports')) return fail('FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE', …)` |
| Limits | check-and-increment in one statement (`update usage_counters … where value < limit returning *`) or a Postgres function — avoids races |
| UI | show upgrade prompts using the same `ent` object passed as props |
| RLS | not for entitlements (business rule, not isolation) — except hard caps enforced by trigger if abuse risk is high |

Error codes: `FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE` (403), `PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED` (409 with `{ metric, limit, current }`).

## Feature flags (release control, separate from entitlements)
| Aspect | Rule |
|---|---|
| Naming | `feature.<area>_<name>` (e.g. `feature.invoice_export`) |
| Source | env `FEATURE_FLAGS` (global kill switch) + `tenant_features` (per-tenant rollout) |
| Default | off in production; on in preview |
| Lifecycle | create with the PR → roll out per tenant → 100% → remove flag and dead code within 2 releases (ticket created at creation) |
| Check | `flags.isOn('feature.x', tenantId)` in services and RSC; never in client bundles for secret features |
| Audit | flag changes written to `audit_log` |

## Billing provider integration (Stripe-shaped)
- Webhook route verifies signature, is idempotent (`provider_event_id` unique), updates `tenant_subscriptions` only; never trusts client-reported plan.
- Checkout/portal sessions created server-side with `tenant_id` in metadata.
- Reconciliation job daily: provider → `tenant_subscriptions` diff → fix + alert.

## Tests
- Entitlement resolution: table-driven unit tests for each (override, status, plan) combination.
- Limit race: integration test with two concurrent increments at the cap → exactly one succeeds.
- Webhook: contract tests with recorded payloads; replay same event twice → one effect.

# RBAC

## Role set (fixed, ordinal)
| Role | Intent | Typical holder |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | billing, delete tenant, transfer ownership; everything below | founder / account owner |
| `admin` | manage members, settings, all data | team lead |
| `member` | create/edit own and shared work | staff |
| `viewer` | read-only | auditor, client guest |

Add roles only when an action set cannot be expressed by the ordinal ladder. Custom per-tenant roles → permissions table (`role_permissions(tenant_id, role, action)`) — defer until required.

## Matrix method (`assets/rbac-matrix.csv`)
Columns: `action, resource, viewer, member, admin, owner, enforcement_rls, enforcement_service, ui, audited`.
Cell values: `allow`, `own` (only rows they created), `deny`.
Rules:
- Every action row has an RLS policy name **and** a service check — UI is hide-only, never the control.
- `own` requires a `created_by`/`user_id` column and a policy with both tenant and owner predicates.
- Mark `audited = yes` for every write to tenant data, membership, billing, settings.

## Enforcement points
| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Database | RLS policies using `app.tenant_id()`, `app.has_role()`, `auth.uid()` | every read/write, including PostgREST, Realtime, direct clients |
| Server | `requireRole('admin')` at the top of actions/routes; service-level checks for business rules (`own`, status transitions) | intent-level authz; clearer errors (`AUTH_FORBIDDEN` vs silent empty) |
| UI | `can(user, 'invoice.delete')` helper → hide/disable | UX only |
| Jobs / edge functions | explicit tenant + role passed in payload, validated; service role used only after validation | background paths |

`can()` is a pure function over the same matrix (generated from the CSV at build time: `scripts/gen-rbac.ts` → `lib/rbac.ts`) so UI and server agree. Server still calls `requireRole`/service checks; `can()` is not a substitute at the boundary.

## Ownership transfer and last-owner rule
- A tenant always has ≥ 1 owner: deny role change/removal that would leave zero (service check + DB constraint via trigger).
- Transfer = promote new owner, then demote old; audited as one event.

## Testing matrix
For each action: one test per role (allow or deny) at the service layer with mocked DB, plus one integration test per RLS policy (positive + negative). Generate the test table from the CSV to avoid drift.

## Common errors
| Error | Fix |
|---|---|
| Role stored only in JWT, not in a table | `tenant_members.role` is the source; JWT is a cache |
| Admin check in layout only | `requireRole` in every action |
| `viewer` can hit a server action because the button is hidden | same |
| Role names compared as strings in many places | ordinal helper (`roleAtLeast`) in `lib/rbac.ts` and `app.has_role()` in SQL, nowhere else |

# Tenant Model

## Decision table
| Question | Options | Default | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isolation | shared schema + RLS (`tenant_id` column) · schema-per-tenant · DB-per-tenant | shared + RLS | one codebase, one migration path; isolation enforced by policy + tests |
| Users ↔ tenants | one tenant per user · many (membership table) | many | `tenant_members` join; active tenant in JWT; switch flow |
| Tenant identity | `tenants.id` uuid + `slug` | both | slug in URLs (`/t/<slug>/…`) or subdomain later |
| Where the active tenant lives | JWT `app_metadata.tenant_id` · cookie · URL | JWT (source of truth) + URL for routing | RLS reads JWT; URL must match JWT or redirect |
| Roles | fixed set (`owner, admin, member, viewer`) · custom per tenant | fixed set | custom roles = permissions table; defer |
| Personal space | personal tenant auto-created per user · none | auto-create | every user always has a tenant; simplifies RLS |

## Core tables (DDL in `assets/tenancy-schema.sql`)
| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `tenants` | the organisation | `id, slug unique, name, plan_id, status (active|suspended|deleting), created_at` |
| `tenant_members` | membership + role | `tenant_id, user_id, role, status (active|invited|removed), invited_by, created_at`; PK `(tenant_id, user_id)` |
| `invitations` | pending invites by email | `id, tenant_id, email, role, token_hash, expires_at, accepted_at, invited_by`; unique `(tenant_id, email)` |
| `profiles` | app-level user data | `user_id PK → auth.users, display_name, default_tenant_id` |

Every other business table: `tenant_id uuid not null references tenants(id) on delete cascade default app.tenant_id()`.

## Claims
| Claim | Set by | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `app_metadata.tenant_id` | server (Auth Hook `custom_access_token` or admin API on switch) | `app.tenant_id()` in RLS; `requireUser()` |
| `app_metadata.role` | same, from `tenant_members.role` for that tenant | `app.has_role()` |
| `app_metadata.tenant_ids` (optional) | same | fast "which tenants can I switch to" without a query |

Custom Access Token Hook (Postgres function) is preferred: claims are computed from `tenant_members` at every token issue, so role changes propagate within the access-token lifetime (default 1 h; set 15 min for admin-sensitive apps). Document the stale-claim window.

## Flows
### Sign-up
1. User signs up → trigger `on auth.users insert` creates `profiles` row and a personal tenant + owner membership (`security definer`, pinned `search_path`).
2. Hook issues token with personal tenant claims.

### Invite
1. Admin creates `invitations` row (token = random 32 bytes; store `sha256` hash only; 7-day expiry) → email with link `/invite/<token>`.
2. Invitee signs in/up → server action `acceptInvite(token)`: hash, look up, check expiry/email match, insert `tenant_members`, mark accepted, trigger token refresh (`supabase.auth.refreshSession()`).
3. Rate-limit invite creation; audit both steps.

### Switch tenant
1. `switchTenant(tenantId)` server action: verify membership (query as the user — RLS on `tenant_members`), update `profiles.default_tenant_id`, call admin API to set `app_metadata.tenant_id/role`, then force refresh so the new JWT carries the claims.
2. Middleware: if URL tenant slug ≠ JWT tenant → redirect to `/t/<jwt-tenant>`.

### Remove member / change role
1. Admin action → update `tenant_members`; audit.
2. Affected user's current token stays valid until expiry → for immediate effect, also maintain a `tenant_members.status` check in RLS helper (`app.is_active_member()`), or shorten token lifetime. State which you chose.

### Delete tenant
1. Owner requests → `status = 'deleting'`, members lose access immediately (helper checks status).
2. Export job writes archive to private storage; retention per policy.
3. After grace period, hard delete cascades (`on delete cascade` everywhere) — verify with a staging drill.

## Routing conventions
- `app/(app)/t/[slug]/…` for tenant pages; layout resolves slug → verifies against JWT.
- Never accept `tenantId` in forms, query strings or bodies for data access; only for the switch action, where it is validated against membership.

## Testing
- Personas per role in two tenants (seed).
- Negative tests: read/write across tenants; removed member; expired invite; slug/JWT mismatch redirect.

# nextjs-enterprise-conventions

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/nextjs-enterprise-conventions --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/nextjs-enterprise-conventions`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The lint step exits 1 on any high-severity finding, so a non-compliant repo fails the run by design; fix the findings in code, then re-run.

## Starting points
- **New** — a new repo is linted against every convention; any high-severity finding fails the gate.
- **Existing** — add `baseline` (the `findings.csv` of an earlier run): each finding is marked known or new, the gate fails only on new high-severity findings, known debt stays listed, and baseline items no longer found are reported as resolved.

## When to use
- Any new or modified file under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `server/`.
- "Review this component", "is this the right place for this query", "add a server action", "add a page".
- Invoked by `spec-to-plan` tasks and `safe-fix` when the diff touches Next.js code.
- NOT for: schema/RLS (`supabase-schema-rls`), security audit (`security-review`), tests design (`test-strategy-tdd`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The task or diff | yes | user / plan |
| Repo (`CLAUDE.md`, `lib/`, `server/`, existing patterns) | yes | repo |
| Next.js major version (`package.json`) | yes | repo |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` and `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`. Read `package.json` for the Next.js version and existing `lib/result.ts`, `lib/logger.ts`, `lib/env.ts` — reuse, never duplicate.
2. **Plan.** For a new feature slice, list files by layer (validator → service → action/route → component → page) with the server/client decision per component. For a review, list the files and the rule IDs you will check. Wait for "go" on anything touching >3 files. *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Framework rules.** If the upstream skills `vercel-react-best-practices` and `vercel-composition-patterns` are installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke them for this step; otherwise follow `references/framework-rules.md` (server/client boundaries, caching, data fetching, server actions, routing).
4. **Layering and errors.** Apply `references/layering.md` (what lives where, import direction) and `references/error-result-pattern.md` (`Result<T,E>`, error codes, no throws across the boundary).
5. **Logging.** Apply `references/logging.md`: `lib/logger` only, correlation id from headers, no PII, no `console.log`.
6. **Build.** Write code in minimal diffs. Each server action: zod parse → auth/tenant check → service call → `Result` → typed response. Each component: server by default; `"use client"` only for interactivity, with the reason in a comment.
7. **Test.** Unit for validators/services; component tests for client components with logic; e2e for the page path. Run lint, typecheck, full unit suite. *(gate: build→test)*
8. **Verify.** Walk `references/conventions-checklist.md`; report as a table (rule → pass/fail/n.a. → file:line). Fix fails before returning. *(gate: test→verify)*
9. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Form |
|---|---|
| Code | minimal diffs in the layered locations |
| Conventions table | chat: rule → status → location |
| Tests | `tests/unit/**`, `tests/e2e/**` |

## Self-check
- [ ] No Supabase call outside `lib/db` / `server/services`
- [ ] Every server action and route handler parses input with zod and checks auth before work
- [ ] Services return `Result<T,E>`; no `throw` crosses server→client; errors have stable codes
- [ ] `"use client"` only where needed, with reason; no secrets or server-only imports in client files
- [ ] Logs structured via `lib/logger`, with `requestId`; no `console.log`, no PII
- [ ] Names and folders match `shared/stack-conventions.md`
- [ ] lint + typecheck + unit green; e2e for touched pages

## References
- `references/framework-rules.md` — server/client components, caching, fetching, actions, routing (fallback for Vercel skills)
- `references/layering.md` — folder/layer rules, import direction, naming
- `references/error-result-pattern.md` — `Result<T,E>`, error codes, boundary mapping
- `references/logging.md` — log schema, correlation id, redaction
- `references/conventions-checklist.md` — rule table used in verify
- `assets/result.ts`, `assets/server-action.example.ts`, `assets/service.example.ts` — starters
- `scripts/lint_conventions.py` — offline linter for NX1–NX5 (Supabase in components, console.log, zod at actions, service-role exposure, raw SQL); exit 1 on high findings

file and snippet match a baseline row (line numbers may move) is `known`; anything else is `new`.
The gate then fails only on new high-severity findings — existing debt stays listed, in the report
and the CSV, but no longer blocks unrelated work — and baseline rows no longer found are reported
as resolved. Without --baseline every finding is `new`. Stdlib, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SKIP_DIRS = {"node_modules", ".next", "out", "dist", "build", "coverage", ".git", "tests", "test", "__tests__"}   # out: next export output
EXTS = {".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs"}   # the conventions apply to JavaScript Next.js apps too
RULES = {
    "NX1": ("supabase-in-component", "high", "No Supabase call outside lib/db or server/services (stack-conventions: Data access)"),
    "NX2": ("console-log", "medium", "Structured logging via lib/logger only; no console.log in committed code"),
    "NX3": ("action-without-zod", "high", "Every server action parses its input with zod before work"),
    "NX4": ("service-role-exposed", "high", "Service-role key only in server-side code; never near the client"),
    "NX5": ("raw-sql-outside-lib-db", "high", "Raw SQL lives in lib/db only"),
}
SUPABASE_CALL = re.compile(r"\.from\(\s*['\"`]|\.rpc\(|\bcreateClient\(")
CONSOLE_LOG = re.compile(r"\bconsole\.log\(")
USE_SERVER = re.compile(r"^\s*['\"]use server['\"]\s*;?\s*$", re.M)
EXPORT_FN = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*export\s+(?:default\s+)?async\s+function\s+(\w+)?\s*\(", re.M)
SERVICE_ROLE = re.compile(r"SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE")
SQL_TAG = re.compile(r"\bsql`")
SERVICE_ROLE_OK = ("server/", "lib/supabase/server", "lib/env.ts")


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def source_files(root: Path):
    for p in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
        if p.suffix not in EXTS or not p.is_file():
            continue
        rel = p.relative_to(root)
        if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in rel.parts[:-1]):
            continue
        yield p, rel.as_posix()


def is_component_surface(rel: str) -> bool:
    return rel.startswith("components/") or "/components/" in rel or \
        (rel.startswith("app/") and rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] in ("page.tsx", "page.ts", "page.jsx", "page.js", "layout.tsx", "layout.jsx", "layout.js"))


def line_no(text: str, pos: int) -> int:
    return text.count("\n", 0, pos) + 1


def body_after(text: str, pos: int) -> str:
    """Text of the `{ … }` block that starts at the first `{` after pos (brace-matched)."""
    start = text.find("{", pos)
    if start < 0:
        return ""
    depth = 0
    for i in range(start, len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return text[start:i + 1]
    return text[start:]


def lint_file(text: str, rel: str) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    lines = text.splitlines()

    def add(rule, ln):
        name, sev, _ = RULES[rule]
        out.append({"rule": rule, "file": rel, "line": ln, "snippet": lines[ln - 1].strip()[:120], "severity": sev})

    if is_component_surface(rel):
        for m in SUPABASE_CALL.finditer(text):
            add("NX1", line_no(text, m.start()))
    for m in CONSOLE_LOG.finditer(text):
        add("NX2", line_no(text, m.start()))
    if USE_SERVER.search(text):
        for m in EXPORT_FN.finditer(text):
            body = body_after(text, m.end())
            if ".parse(" not in body and ".safeParse(" not in body:
                add("NX3", line_no(text, m.start()))
    if not rel.startswith(SERVICE_ROLE_OK):
        for m in SERVICE_ROLE.finditer(text):
            add("NX4", line_no(text, m.start()))
    if not rel.startswith("lib/db/"):
        for m in SQL_TAG.finditer(text):
            add("NX5", line_no(text, m.start()))
    return out


def load_baseline(path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    if not path.is_file():
        die(f"baseline not found: {path}")
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as fh:
        reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
        missing = [c for c in ("rule", "file", "snippet") if c not in (reader.fieldnames or [])]
        if missing:
            die(f"baseline lacks column(s) {missing} (expected a findings.csv from this script)")
        return [((r.get("rule") or "").strip(), (r.get("file") or "").strip(), (r.get("snippet") or "").strip())
                for r in reader if (r.get("rule") or "").strip() and not (r.get("rule") or "").startswith("#")]


def apply_baseline(findings: list[dict], baseline: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Mark each finding known/new (one baseline row matches one finding); return the unmatched (resolved) rows."""
    pool = list(baseline)
    for f in findings:
        key = (f["rule"], f["file"], f["snippet"])
        if key in pool:
            pool.remove(key)
            f["status"] = "known"
        else:
            f["status"] = "new"
    return pool


def write_report(path: Path, findings: list[dict], n_files: int, target: Path,
                 resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None) -> None:
    by_rule = {}
    for f in findings:
        by_rule.setdefault(f["rule"], []).append(f)
    high = sum(1 for f in findings if f["severity"] == "high")
    new_high = sum(1 for f in findings if f["severity"] == "high" and f["status"] == "new")
    based = resolved is not None
    head = f"**{len(findings)} finding(s) in {n_files} file(s): {high} high, {len(findings) - high} medium"
    if based:
        known = sum(1 for f in findings if f["status"] == "known")
        head += f"; {len(findings) - known} new, {known} known from the baseline, {len(resolved)} resolved"
    gate = ("Gate: FAIL (new high-severity findings)." if new_high else
            "Gate: PASS (no new high-severity findings; known debt listed below)." if high else "Gate: PASS.") if based \
        else ("Gate: FAIL (high-severity findings)." if high else "Gate: PASS.")
    lines = [f"# Conventions lint — {target.name}", "", head + ".** " + gate, "",
             "## Summary", "", "| Rule | Name | Severity | Count |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for rule, (name, sev, _) in RULES.items():
        lines.append(f"| {rule} | {name} | {sev} | {len(by_rule.get(rule, []))} |")
    lines += ["", "## Findings", "", "| Rule | File:line | Severity | Status | Snippet |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for f in findings:
        snippet = f["snippet"].replace("|", "\\|")
        lines.append(f"| {f['rule']} | `{f['file']}:{f['line']}` | {f['severity']} | {f['status']} | `{snippet}` |")
    if not findings:
        lines.append("| — | — | — | — | no findings |")
    if based:
        lines += ["", "## Baseline", "",
                  "Known findings are recorded debt: fix them in their own PRs and re-record the baseline. Resolved since the baseline:", ""]
        lines += [f"- {r} `{f_}` — {s_}" for r, f_, s_ in resolved] or ["- none"]
    lines += ["", "## Rules", ""]
    for rule, (name, sev, why) in RULES.items():
        lines.append(f"- **{rule} {name}** ({sev}) — {why}")
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Lint a Next.js repo against the stack conventions")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="repo root")
    ap.add_argument("--findings", default="findings.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--report", default="report.md")
    ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true", help="print only the summary line")
    ap.add_argument("--baseline", default="", help="findings.csv from an earlier run: known debt that does not gate")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    target = Path(a.target)
    if not target.is_dir():
        die(f"target is not a directory: {target}")
    findings, n_files = [], 0
    for p, rel in source_files(target):
        n_files += 1
        findings += lint_file(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), rel)
    if n_files == 0:
        die(f"no .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs source files under {target}")
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: (f["file"], f["line"], f["rule"]))
    resolved = apply_baseline(findings, load_baseline(Path(a.baseline))) if a.baseline else None
    if resolved is None:
        for f in findings:
            f["status"] = "new"
    fp, rp = Path(a.findings), Path(a.report)
    fp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with fp.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["rule", "file", "line", "snippet", "severity", "status"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(findings)
    write_report(rp, findings, n_files, target, resolved)
    high = [f for f in findings if f["severity"] == "high" and f["status"] == "new"]
    if not a.quiet:
        for f in findings:
            print(f"{f['severity']:6} {f['rule']} {f['file']}:{f['line']}  {f['snippet']}"
                  + ("  (known)" if f["status"] == "known" else ""))
    print(f"{len(findings)} finding(s) in {n_files} file(s); {len(high)} {'new ' if resolved is not None else ''}high -> {fp}, {rp}")
    if high:
        print(f"gate: FAIL — {len(high)} {'new ' if resolved is not None else ''}high-severity finding(s)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
