# Error and Result Pattern

## Principle
Expected failures are values; unexpected failures are exceptions. Services return `Result<T, AppError>`; nothing throws across the server→client boundary.

## Types (`lib/result.ts`, see `assets/result.ts`)
```ts
export type Result<T, E = AppError> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E };
export type AppError = {
  code: ErrorCode;            // stable, machine-readable
  message: string;            // safe to show the user
  status: 400|401|403|404|409|422|429|500;
  fieldErrors?: Record<string, string[]>;
  cause?: unknown;            // never serialized to client
};
```

## Error code catalogue (extend per domain)
| Code | Status | When |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | zod parse failed; `fieldErrors` filled |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | no session |
| `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | role/tenant mismatch, RLS denial (`42501`) |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | row missing or filtered by RLS (same response — do not leak existence) |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | unique violation (`23505`), optimistic lock mismatch |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | limiter |
| `UPSTREAM_FAILED` | 502 | external API error after retries |
| `INTERNAL` | 500 | anything unmapped; logged with `requestId`; generic message |

## Mapping Postgres/Supabase errors (`lib/db/errors.ts`)
| PG code | AppError |
|---|---|
| `42501` | `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` (write) / `NOT_FOUND` (read) |
| `23505` | `CONFLICT` |
| `23503` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` (bad reference) |
| `23514` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` (check constraint) |
| `PGRST116` (0 rows with `.single()`) | `NOT_FOUND` |
| other | `INTERNAL` + log |

## Layer behaviour
| Layer | Does |
|---|---|
| `lib/db` | returns `Result`; maps PG errors; never throws for data conditions |
| `server/services` | composes; adds domain codes (`INVOICE_ALREADY_PAID`); logs at `warn` for 4xx, `error` for 5xx |
| `server/actions` | `toActionState(result)` → `{ ok, data?, error?: { code, message, fieldErrors } }` — strips `cause` |
| route handlers | `toResponse(result)` → `NextResponse.json({ error: { code, message } }, { status })` |
| components | render `error.message`; branch on `error.code` for UX (e.g. `CONFLICT` → refresh prompt) |
| `error.tsx` | catches only thrown (unexpected) errors; shows `requestId` for support |

## Rules
- Never `catch (e) { return fail('INTERNAL') }` without logging `e` and the `requestId`.
- Never return raw PG messages to clients.
- `NOT_FOUND` and `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` on reads look identical to the caller.
- Validation errors carry field paths from zod (`error.flatten().fieldErrors`).
- `Result` helpers: `ok(v)`, `fail(code, message, extra?)`, `isOk`, `unwrapOr`, `mapResult`.
- Don't nest `Result` inside `Result`; services flatten.

# Next.js App Router Framework Rules (fallback for vercel-react-best-practices / vercel-composition-patterns)

Target: Next.js 15+ App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict.

## 1. Server vs client components
| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Server by default | Every file under `app/` and `components/` is a server component unless it needs state, effects, browser APIs, or event handlers. |
| `"use client"` is a boundary, not a flag | Put it on the smallest leaf that needs interactivity. Pass server data down as props (serializable only). |
| Reason comment | First line after the directive: `// client: needs useState for dialog open` |
| No server-only imports in client files | `server-only` package in `lib/db/*`, `server/**`, `lib/supabase/server.ts`; `client-only` in browser helpers. |
| No secrets in client | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env in client files; `lib/env.ts` exports `serverEnv` and `publicEnv` separately. |
| Children pattern | Wrap client providers around server children; do not convert a whole subtree to client to use context. |
| Props are serializable | No functions, class instances, Dates (send ISO strings) across the boundary except server actions passed by reference. |

## 2. Data fetching and caching
| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Fetch in server components or services, never in `useEffect` | RSC fetches run on the server with no waterfall to the client. |
| Parallelize | `Promise.all` for independent fetches; `preload` pattern for data needed by children. |
| Explicit caching | Next 15: `fetch` is uncached by default. Opt in with `{ next: { revalidate, tags } }` or `"use cache"`. Document the choice per fetch. |
| Supabase reads are dynamic | They use cookies → the route is dynamic. Do not fight it; cache derived public data with `unstable_cache` / `"use cache"` + tags. |
| Tag invalidation | Mutations call `revalidateTag('<entity>:<tenantId>')`; never blanket `revalidatePath('/')`. |
| Streaming | Wrap slow sections in `<Suspense fallback>`; `loading.tsx` per route segment. |
| No request-time work in layouts that every page pays for | Auth check in `middleware.ts` (cheap cookie check) + per-page `requireUser()`; heavy data in the page. |

## 3. Server actions
| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Location | `server/actions/<domain>.ts`, file starts with `"use server"`. |
| Shape | `export async function createInvoice(prev: ActionState, formData: FormData): Promise<ActionState>` for forms; typed object input for programmatic calls. |
| Order inside | 1 parse (zod) → 2 auth + tenant (`requireUser()`) → 3 rate-limit if public → 4 service call → 5 map `Result` → 6 `revalidateTag` → 7 return serializable state. |
| Never trust `formData` ids | Tenant/user ids come from the session, not the form. Entity ids are re-checked by RLS and the service. |
| No throws for expected failures | Return `{ ok:false, error:{ code, message, fieldErrors } }`. Throw only for programmer errors (caught by `error.tsx`). |
| Actions are public endpoints | Treat like a route handler: authz on every one, even if the UI hides the button. |
| Idempotency | Mutations that can be retried accept an `idempotencyKey` and the service dedupes. |
| `redirect()` after success | Outside try/catch (it throws internally). |

## 4. Route handlers (`app/api/**/route.ts`)
- Only for external callers (webhooks, integrations, health). UI mutations use server actions.
- Verify signatures on webhooks before parsing; respond 2xx fast and enqueue heavy work.
- `export const runtime = 'nodejs'` unless edge is deliberate (Supabase service role needs node).
- Return `NextResponse.json(apiError(...), { status })` using the shared error shape.

## 5. Routing and layout
| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Route groups | `app/(marketing)`, `app/(auth)`, `app/(app)` — `(app)/layout.tsx` enforces session. |
| Files per segment | `page.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx` (client), `not-found.tsx` where it matters. |
| Params | Next 15: `params` and `searchParams` are Promises — `const { id } = await params`. Validate with zod. |
| Metadata | `generateMetadata` for dynamic pages; static `metadata` export otherwise. |
| Middleware | Session refresh + redirect only. No DB calls, no business logic. |

## 6. React rules
| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Hooks | No conditional hooks; custom hooks in `components/features/<domain>/hooks/`. |
| State | Server state lives on the server; client state is UI-only. Avoid duplicating server data in `useState`. |
| Forms | `useActionState` + server action; progressive enhancement (works without JS). `useFormStatus` for pending UI. |
| Lists | Stable `key` from id, never index. |
| Effects | Only for syncing with external systems. Derive, don't effect. |
| Memo | Measure first; React Compiler (if enabled) covers most cases. |
| a11y | Semantic elements, labels for inputs, focus management on dialogs, `aria-live` for async status. |

## 7. Performance
- `next/image` with explicit sizes; `next/font` for fonts; dynamic `import()` for heavy client libs.
- Bundle check: `ANALYZE=true npm run build` on PRs that add client deps > 20 kB.
- No barrel files (`index.ts` re-exporting everything) in `components/` — they defeat tree-shaking.

## 8. TypeScript
- `strict: true`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`. No `any`; `unknown` + narrowing.
- DB types from `lib/db/types.ts` (generated). Domain types in `server/services/<domain>/types.ts`. Never leak `Database['public']['Tables'][...]` rows to components — map to domain DTOs.

# Layering and Naming

## Layers (import direction: top imports from below only)
```
app/ (routes, pages)  ──►  components/  ──►  server/actions/  ──►  server/services/  ──►  lib/db/  ──►  lib/supabase/
                                                 │                      │
                                                 └─► server/validators/ ◄┘
lib/utils, lib/logger, lib/result, lib/env: importable from any layer (pure, no I/O except logger)
```
| Layer | Owns | Must not |
|---|---|---|
| `app/**` | routing, layouts, composing components, calling services in RSC | contain business logic; call Supabase directly |
| `components/ui` | primitives (button, dialog, table) — no domain knowledge | import from `server/` or `lib/db` |
| `components/features/<domain>` | domain UI, hooks, client forms that call actions | call Supabase; contain authz logic |
| `server/actions` | thin: parse → auth → service → map → revalidate | contain queries or business rules |
| `server/services/<domain>` | business rules, orchestration, transactions, audit writes; returns `Result` | know about HTTP, FormData, React |
| `server/validators` | zod schemas + inferred types, shared by actions and services | import services |
| `lib/db` | typed queries (one file per entity), `types.ts` generated | business rules; multiple entities' rules |
| `lib/supabase` | `server.ts` (cookie client), `browser.ts` (anon), `admin.ts` (service role; `server-only`) | be imported by components (except browser.ts for auth UI) |

## Naming
| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Files | kebab-case | `invoice-table.tsx`, `create-invoice.ts` |
| Components | PascalCase, named export, one per file | `export function InvoiceTable()` |
| Server actions | verbObject | `createInvoice`, `voidInvoice` |
| Services | `<domain>.service.ts` exporting an object or functions | `invoiceService.create()` |
| Queries | `<entity>.ts` in `lib/db`, functions `getX / listX / insertX / updateX` | `listInvoicesByTenant()` |
| Validators | `<entity>.ts` exporting `XInput`, `xInputSchema` | `createInvoiceSchema` |
| Error codes | `SCREAMING_SNAKE`, domain-prefixed | `INVOICE_NOT_FOUND`, `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` |
| Env vars | `SCREAMING_SNAKE`; `NEXT_PUBLIC_` only for browser-safe | `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` |
| Tests | mirror path under `tests/unit`, `.test.ts` | `tests/unit/server/services/invoice.test.ts` |
| Feature flags | `feature.<name>` | `feature.invoice_export` |

## Auth helpers (`server/auth.ts`)
```ts
export async function requireUser(): Promise<Result<SessionUser, AppError>>   // 401
export async function requireRole(min: Role): Promise<Result<SessionUser, AppError>> // 403
```
`SessionUser = { id, tenantId, role, email }` built from `app_metadata`. Every action/route starts with one of these.

## Transactions and side effects
- Multi-table writes go through one service function; use a Postgres function (`rpc`) when atomicity is required — Supabase JS has no client-side transactions.
- Side effects (email, webhooks) are enqueued (`jobs` table or queue), never awaited inline in an action.
- Audit log write happens in the service, same call as the mutation.

# Logging Conventions

## Schema (one JSON object per line)
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts` | ISO 8601 | yes | |
| `level` | debug/info/warn/error | yes | |
| `msg` | string | yes | static phrase, no interpolated ids ("invoice created", not `invoice ${id} created`) |
| `requestId` | string | yes (request scope) | from `x-request-id` header or `crypto.randomUUID()`; Vercel sets `x-vercel-id` — include both |
| `userId` | uuid | when known | |
| `tenantId` | uuid | when known | |
| `service` | string | yes | `web`, `edge-fn:<name>`, `job:<name>` |
| `env` | string | yes | `VERCEL_ENV` or `development` |
| `durationMs` | number | for operations | |
| `err` | `{ name, message, stack?, code? }` | on error | stack only in non-prod or at `error` level |
| `...context` | key/values | optional | ids and enums only |

## Rules
| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| `lib/logger` only; `console.*` banned by ESLint (`no-console`) | consistent schema |
| Child loggers per request: `logger.child({ requestId, userId, tenantId })` created in `requireUser()` / middleware | correlation without threading args |
| No PII in logs: no emails, names, free text, tokens, full URLs with query strings | compliance; redaction list in `logger.ts` |
| Level discipline | `debug` dev only; `info` state changes; `warn` expected failures (4xx); `error` unexpected (5xx) |
| One log line per operation outcome, not per step | cost and noise |
| Errors logged once, at the layer that handles them | no duplicate stacks |
| Server actions log `{ action, outcome, durationMs }` | audit of mutations at app level (DB audit covers data) |
| Never log request bodies | secrets and PII |

## Correlation
1. `middleware.ts`: read `x-request-id` or generate; set on request headers and response.
2. `requireUser()`: build child logger with ids; store in `AsyncLocalStorage` (`lib/logger/context.ts`) so services call `log()` without parameters.
3. Client errors (`error.tsx`) display `requestId`; support searches logs by it.

## Where logs go
- Vercel: stdout JSON → Log Drains (to the chosen sink). Configure in `observability-setup`.
- Supabase Edge Functions: `console.log(JSON.stringify(...))` via the same schema (separate tiny logger).
- Local: pretty-print only when `NODE_ENV=development` and `LOG_PRETTY=1`.

# observability-setup

## In a conversation: plan the setup now
- **The request asks for observability on this stack**: answer **in this reply**, in order: (1) one list of questions, asked once — critical user journeys (≤5), error-tracking vendor (Sentry default) and DSN availability, notification channel — each with your default, then carry on with the defaults; (2) the plan table — component → file → add/change → why — covering logger, request context, error tracking, health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard, with a line that nothing changes until "go"; (3) logging: `lib/logger.ts` + `lib/logger/context.ts` (JSON fields `ts, level, msg, service, env, requestId`; redaction of email, token, password, authorization, cookie, key; `requestId` set in `middleware.ts`), `console.*` replaced in minimal diffs, ESLint `no-console: error`; (4) health: `app/api/health/route.ts` (liveness, no dependencies) and `app/api/health/deep/route.ts` (bearer-protected, ≤ 3 s timeout per dependency, 503 when one is down), with tests for both; (5) an alert table — alert → threshold → window → severity tier → runbook → owner → channel — and an SLO table per journey with an error-budget policy; (6) verification on preview: force a synthetic failure (deep health 503) and confirm the alert fires end to end, and confirm a test error reaches the tracker tagged with `requestId`. Thresholds and SLO targets the user has not given are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never reply with only a request for the repo.
- **Part of it already exists** (e.g. "we already have Sentry"): open with an inventory of what is there (Sentry server/client/edge configs, `global-error.tsx`, tags, source maps) and state that it is kept as is; add only what was asked (e.g. health routes and alert rules); add `requestId` as a Sentry tag only if it is missing, as a minimal diff; touch the logger only if `console.*` calls are found.
- **Bare "add observability"**: ask once, in one list, for the critical journeys and the alert channel; meanwhile show the plan skeleton with every SLO target and alert threshold as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never invent SLO numbers.
- **Asked to replace an existing logger or config outright**: decline the overwrite in one line (it loses the team's wiring) and propose the standard file beside it as a `.proposed` twin for a manual merge.

## Starting points
- **New** — point `target` at an empty folder: logger, health routes, alert rules, SLO doc and `.env.example` are written (TypeScript by default).
- **Existing** — point `target` at your repo. **Read before write:** the language flavour is detected first (`tsconfig.json` or any `.ts/.tsx` under `app|lib|components` → TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript) and every file is emitted as `.ts` or `.js` to match — a JavaScript Next.js app gets `lib/logger.js` and `route.js`, never a `.ts` file. A file you already have, **in either extension**, is never overwritten and never gets a conflicting sibling (`route.ts` beside `route.js` is a Next.js routing conflict): an existing health route is reported `exists, kept` with a static gap table (exports `GET`? `force-dynamic`? `no-store`? liveness free of dependency calls?), another existing file in the same flavour gets a `.proposed` twin to merge, one in the other flavour is kept and pointed at the asset. Env vars are appended to `.env.example` only for files written in this run; every `console.*` call in your source is listed. A repo that already has every piece exits 0 with just the gap table; a repo that already holds a conflicting pair (`route.js` **and** `route.ts`) writes nothing, says why in the report, and exits 1.

## When to use
- First production release; after an incident with "we had no idea"; before an SLA commitment.
- Adding a new service/edge function/job that has no logs or health signal.
- NOT for: a specific bug (`safe-fix`), pipeline alerts (`ci-cd-vercel-github`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Critical user journeys (≤5) | yes | `docs/SPEC.md` / user — ask once |
| Error-tracking vendor decision (Sentry default) and DSN availability | yes | user |
| Log sink (Vercel Log Drain target) | no | user; default: vendor's drain |
| On-call / notification channel | yes | user — ask once |
| Existing `lib/logger.ts`, health routes | yes | repo |

Missing facts do not stop the plan: use the stated defaults, mark thresholds and SLO targets `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and ask once at the start. Never invent SLO numbers.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` (Logging, Errors rows) and `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`. Inventory what exists: language flavour (`tsconfig.json` / `.ts` source vs `jsconfig.json` / `.js` only), logger, Sentry, health routes in either extension, deploy platform (Vercel or AWS workflows), Next special files. Every file you add takes the repo's extension; never place a `.ts` route or module beside an existing `.js` one.
2. **Plan.** Table of components to add/change: logger, request context, error tracking (server + client + edge), health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard, runbook links. Post; wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Logging.** Install `assets/logger.ts` (or `assets/logger.js` in a JavaScript repo) as `lib/logger.{ts,js}` (+ `lib/logger/context.{ts,js}` AsyncLocalStorage) per `references/log-schema.md`; wire `requestId` in `middleware.ts`; ESLint `no-console: error`. Replace existing `console.*` in minimal diffs.
4. **Error tracking.** Follow `references/error-tracking.md`: server, client, edge configs; `requestId`/`tenantId` tags; PII scrubbing; source maps in CI; `error.tsx` reporting.
5. **Health.** Add `assets/health-route.ts` (or `.js`) as `app/api/health/route.{ts,js}` (liveness, no deps) and `app/api/health/deep/route.{ts,js}` (DB, auth, storage, queue; bearer-protected) per `references/health-endpoints.md`. If a health route already exists in either extension, keep it, verify it exports `GET`, and list what it is missing versus the standard (see the reference's brownfield table) instead of adding a sibling.
6. **Alerts + SLOs.** From `references/alerts-and-slos.md`, fill `assets/alert-rules.yaml` for the chosen vendor and the SLO table for the critical journeys. Every alert has a runbook link and an owner.
7. **Test.** Unit test logger redaction; integration test both health routes (200 / 503 on simulated DB failure); trigger a test error and confirm it appears in the tracker with `requestId`. Full unit suite green. *(gate: build→test)*
8. **Verify.** Deploy to preview; curl both health routes; confirm Log Drain delivers JSON; confirm an alert fires on a synthetic failure (health 503). *(gate: test→verify)*
9. Write `docs/observability.md` (schema, endpoints, alerts, dashboards, how to find a request by id). Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Logger | `lib/logger.{ts,js}`, `lib/logger/context.{ts,js}` (extension follows the repo) |
| Error tracking | `sentry.{server,client,edge}.config.ts` (or vendor equivalent), `app/global-error.tsx` |
| Health | `app/api/health/route.{ts,js}`, `app/api/health/deep/route.{ts,js}` |
| Alerts / SLOs | `ops/alerts.yaml`, `docs/observability.md` |
| Dashboard spec | `docs/observability.md` §Dashboards |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every log line has `ts, level, msg, service, env`; request-scoped lines have `requestId`
- [ ] Redaction list covers email, token, password, authorization, cookie, key
- [ ] Health liveness has zero dependencies; deep check is auth-protected and times out ≤ 3 s per dependency
- [ ] Every added file matches the repo's flavour (`.js` in a JavaScript repo); no route or module exists in two extensions
- [ ] Every alert: threshold, window, severity, runbook, owner, notification channel
- [ ] SLOs defined for each critical journey with an error-budget policy
- [ ] Synthetic failure produced an alert end-to-end
- [ ] No PII reached the error tracker (checked a real event)

## References
- `references/log-schema.md` — fields, levels, redaction, request context
- `references/error-tracking.md` — Sentry (default) wiring for server/client/edge, scrubbing, source maps
- `references/health-endpoints.md` — liveness vs readiness vs deep; response contract
- `references/alerts-and-slos.md` — alert catalogue, SLO starter, error-budget policy, dashboard panels
- `assets/logger.ts`, `assets/logger-context.ts`, `assets/health-route.ts`, `assets/health-deep-route.ts` (+ the `.js` twins `assets/logger.js`, `assets/logger-context.js`, `assets/health-route.js`, `assets/health-deep-route.js`, functionally identical), `assets/alert-rules.yaml`
- `scripts/install.py` — detects the flavour, installs the matching assets without overwriting or creating `.ts`/`.js` siblings (`exists, kept` + gap table for health routes, `.proposed` twins otherwise), appends env vars for written files to `.env.example`
- `scripts/check_siblings.py` — fails when any route or module exists in two source extensions (used by the eval checks)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/observability-setup --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/observability-setup`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Existing files are never overwritten and never get a `.ts`/`.js` sibling: a health route that exists is kept and gap-checked, a differing file in the same flavour gets a `.proposed` twin listed in the report for a manual merge, and an existing conflicting pair aborts the run (exit 1, nothing written).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Install the observability starter kit into a Next.js repo — read before write, never overwrite.

    python3 -I scripts/install.py --target <repo> [--dry-run] [--project <name>] [--flavour ts|js] \
        --report-json install-report.json --report-md install-report.md

Flavour (read before write): tsconfig.json or any .ts/.tsx under app|lib|components -> TypeScript;
otherwise JavaScript (an empty/new target defaults to TypeScript). The matching asset variant is used:
  assets/logger.{ts,js}            -> lib/logger.{ext}
  assets/logger-context.{ts,js}    -> lib/logger/context.{ext}
  assets/health-route.{ts,js}      -> app/api/health/route.{ext}
  assets/health-deep-route.{ts,js} -> app/api/health/deep/route.{ext}
  assets/alert-rules.yaml          -> ops/alerts.yaml
  assets/slo-starter.md            -> docs/observability.md
Existing files (in ANY source extension: route.js next to a planned route.ts counts) are never
overwritten and never get a conflicting sibling: identical -> skipped; a health route -> "exists, kept"
with a static gap table (exports GET? force-dynamic? no-store? liveness free of dependency calls?);
any other file in the same flavour -> `<file>.proposed` twin for a manual merge; in the other flavour ->
"exists, kept" (merge by hand from the asset). Env vars (`process.env.X`) are appended to .env.example
only for files written in this run. The plan is computed before anything is written: a repo that already
holds a conflicting pair (route.js AND route.ts) makes the run write nothing, report why, and exit 1.
--dry-run writes nothing. The run also lists every `console.*` call in the app's source. Exit 0 when the
repo already has every piece (the report carries the gap table). Exit 1 on bad input or conflict. Stdlib.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ASSETS = HERE.parent / "assets"
# (asset stem, destination without extension, kind); kind: route | module | static
PLAN = [
    ("logger", "lib/logger", "module"),
    ("logger-context", "lib/logger/context", "module"),
    ("health-route", "app/api/health/route", "route"),
    ("health-deep-route", "app/api/health/deep/route", "route"),
    ("alert-rules.yaml", "ops/alerts.yaml", "static"),
    ("slo-starter.md", "docs/observability.md", "static"),
]
SIBLING_EXT = [".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs"]   # any of these at the same stem is "the file"
TS_EXT = {".ts", ".tsx"}
FLAVOUR_DIRS = ("app", "lib", "components", "src")
ENV_RE = re.compile(r"process\.env\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)")
CONSOLE_RE = re.compile(r"\bconsole\.(log|info|warn|error|debug)\s*\(")
SOURCE_EXT = {".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs"}
SKIP_DIRS = {"node_modules", ".next", ".git", "dist", "build", "out", "coverage", ".vercel"}
PLATFORM_VARS = {"NODE_ENV", "VERCEL_ENV", "VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA"}  # set by the platform, not by .env
ENV_DOC = {
    "LOG_LEVEL": "debug|info|warn|error (default: info in production, debug elsewhere)",
    "LOG_PRETTY": "1 to pretty-print logs in local development",
    "SERVICE_NAME": "service label on every log line (default: web)",
    "HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN": "bearer token required by /api/health/deep (generate: openssl rand -hex 32)",
    "NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL": "Supabase project URL",
}
GET_EXPORT_RE = re.compile(r"export\s+(?:async\s+)?function\s+GET\b|export\s+const\s+GET\b|export\s*\{[^}]*\bGET\b[^}]*\}")
# dependency calls a liveness route must not make, most specific first; comments are stripped before matching
DEP_CALL_PATTERNS = [r"\bfetch\s*\(", r"\.rpc\s*\(", r"\.from\s*\(", r"createAdminClient", r"createClient",
                     r"\bsupabase\b", r"\bprisma\b", r"\bmongoose\b", r"\bpg\b", r"\bredis\b"]
LINE_COMMENT_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*//.*$", re.M)
BLOCK_COMMENT_RE = re.compile(r"/\*.*?\*/", re.S)


def _skip(p: Path, target: Path) -> bool:
    return any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in p.relative_to(target).parts)


def detect_flavour(target: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """('ts'|'js', evidence). tsconfig.json or any .ts/.tsx under app|lib|components|src -> ts; else js.
    An empty or missing target has nothing to read and defaults to ts (the greenfield happy path)."""
    if not target.is_dir() or not any(target.iterdir()):
        return "ts", "empty target — default"
    if (target / "tsconfig.json").is_file():
        return "ts", "tsconfig.json present"
    for d in FLAVOUR_DIRS:
        root = target / d
        if not root.is_dir():
            continue
        for p in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix in TS_EXT and not _skip(p, target):
                return "ts", f"{p.relative_to(target).as_posix()} is TypeScript"
    if (target / "jsconfig.json").is_file():
        return "js", "jsconfig.json present, no tsconfig.json or .ts/.tsx source"
    return "js", "no tsconfig.json or .ts/.tsx source under app|lib|components|src"


def siblings(target: Path, stem: str) -> list[Path]:
    """Existing files at <stem>.<ext> for every source extension (the route/module in either flavour)."""
    return [target / f"{stem}{ext}" for ext in SIBLING_EXT if (target / f"{stem}{ext}").is_file()]


def health_gap(text: str, deep: bool) -> list[dict]:
    """Static check of an existing health route against the standard (references/health-endpoints.md)."""
    rows = [{"check": "exports GET", "ok": bool(GET_EXPORT_RE.search(text)),
             "note": "route responds to GET" if GET_EXPORT_RE.search(text) else "no GET export — the route does not respond"}]
    rows.append({"check": "force-dynamic", "ok": "force-dynamic" in text,
                 "note": "" if "force-dynamic" in text else "add `export const dynamic = \"force-dynamic\"`"})
    rows.append({"check": "Cache-Control: no-store", "ok": "no-store" in text,
                 "note": "" if "no-store" in text else "respond with `Cache-Control: no-store`"})
    has_version = bool(re.search(r"\b(version|sha|commit)\b", text))
    rows.append({"check": "build info (version/sha)", "ok": has_version,
                 "note": "" if has_version else "include the deployed commit sha"})
    rows.append({"check": "timestamp (ts)", "ok": bool(re.search(r"\bts\b|toISOString", text)),
                 "note": "" if re.search(r"\bts\b|toISOString", text) else "include `ts`"})
    if deep:
        has_auth = "HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN" in text or re.search(r"\bBearer\b", text) is not None
        rows.append({"check": "bearer-protected (HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN)", "ok": bool(has_auth),
                     "note": "" if has_auth else "require `Authorization: Bearer ${HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN}`"})
        has_timeout = bool(re.search(r"setTimeout|AbortController|timeout", text, re.I))
        rows.append({"check": "per-dependency timeout", "ok": has_timeout,
                     "note": "" if has_timeout else "time out each dependency check at ≤ 3 s"})
        rows.append({"check": "503 when a required dependency is down", "ok": "503" in text,
                     "note": "" if "503" in text else "return 503 on a required dependency failure"})
    else:
        code = LINE_COMMENT_RE.sub("", BLOCK_COMMENT_RE.sub("", text))
        touches = next((m for pat in DEP_CALL_PATTERNS for m in [re.search(pat, code, re.I)] if m), None)
        rows.append({"check": "liveness has no dependency calls", "ok": touches is None,
                     "note": "" if touches is None else
                     f"calls `{touches.group(0).strip()}` — a dependency outage makes the app look dead; move the check to /api/health/deep"})
    return rows


def console_calls(target: Path, ours: set[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """console.* calls in the repo's own source (files this script installs are excluded)."""
    found = []
    if not target.is_dir():
        return found
    for p in sorted(target.rglob("*")):
        rel = p.relative_to(target).as_posix()
        if not p.is_file() or p.suffix not in SOURCE_EXT or rel in ours or rel.endswith(".proposed") or _skip(p, target):
            continue
        for n, ln in enumerate(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1):
            m = CONSOLE_RE.search(ln)
            if m:
                found.append({"path": rel, "line": n, "call": f"console.{m.group(1)}"})
    return found


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def build_plan(target: Path, flavour: str, project: str) -> list[dict]:
    """One decision per asset, computed before any write: written | skipped | proposed | kept | conflict."""
    ext = f".{flavour}"
    plan = []
    for stem, dest_stem, kind in PLAN:
        src = ASSETS / (stem if kind == "static" else f"{stem}{ext}")
        content = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("{{PROJECT}}", project)
        rel = dest_stem if kind == "static" else f"{dest_stem}{ext}"
        item = {"path": rel, "kind": kind, "content": content, "asset": f"assets/{src.name}",
                "env": sorted(set(ENV_RE.findall(content)) - PLATFORM_VARS)}
        existing = siblings(target, dest_stem) if kind != "static" else ([target / rel] if (target / rel).is_file() else [])
        if len(existing) > 1:
            item.update(action="conflict", existing=[p.relative_to(target).as_posix() for p in existing],
                        reason="more than one source file at this path (" + ", ".join(p.name for p in existing)
                        + ") — Next.js resolves one; fix the repo first")
        elif not existing:
            item["action"] = "written"
        else:
            cur = existing[0]
            cur_rel = cur.relative_to(target).as_posix()
            text = cur.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
            item["existing"] = cur_rel
            if cur_rel == rel and text == content:
                item.update(action="skipped", reason="identical")
            elif kind == "route":
                item.update(action="kept", reason="exists, kept — no sibling route created (a route.js/route.ts pair is a Next.js conflict)",
                            gap=health_gap(text, deep=stem == "health-deep-route"))
            elif cur_rel == rel:
                item.update(action="proposed", proposed=rel + ".proposed", reason="exists with different content — merge manually")
            else:
                item.update(action="kept", reason=f"exists, kept — {cur.suffix} file in a {flavour} install; merge by hand from {item['asset']}")
        plan.append(item)
    return plan


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Install logger, health routes, alert rules and SLO starter")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="repo root (created if absent)")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="report only; write nothing")
    ap.add_argument("--project", default="", help="project name for docs/observability.md (default: target dir name)")
    ap.add_argument("--flavour", choices=["ts", "js"], default="", help="override the detected language flavour")
    ap.add_argument("--report-json", default="install-report.json")
    ap.add_argument("--report-md", default="install-report.md")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    target = Path(a.target)
    if target.exists() and not target.is_dir():
        die(f"target is not a directory: {target}")
    missing = [f"{stem}.{e}" for stem, _, kind in PLAN if kind != "static" for e in ("ts", "js") if not (ASSETS / f"{stem}.{e}").is_file()]
    missing += [stem for stem, _, kind in PLAN if kind == "static" and not (ASSETS / stem).is_file()]
    if missing:
        die(f"assets missing: {missing}")
    project = a.project or target.name
    detected, evidence = detect_flavour(target)
    flavour = a.flavour or detected
    if a.flavour:
        evidence = f"--flavour {a.flavour} (detected: {detected}, {evidence})"

    plan = build_plan(target, flavour, project)
    conflicts = [i for i in plan if i["action"] == "conflict"]
    report = {"target": str(target), "dry_run": a.dry_run, "flavour": flavour, "flavour_evidence": evidence,
              "written": [], "skipped": [], "proposed": [], "kept": [], "conflicts": [], "env_added": [], "health_gaps": []}

    for i in plan:
        if i["action"] == "conflict":
            report["conflicts"].append({"path": i["path"], "existing": i["existing"], "reason": i["reason"]})
        elif i["action"] == "skipped":
            report["skipped"].append({"path": i["path"], "reason": "identical"})
        elif i["action"] == "proposed":
            report["proposed"].append({"path": i["path"], "proposed": i["proposed"], "reason": i["reason"]})
        elif i["action"] == "kept":
            report["kept"].append({"path": i["existing"], "planned": i["path"], "reason": i["reason"]})
            if "gap" in i:
                report["health_gaps"].append({"path": i["existing"], "responds": i["gap"][0]["ok"], "checks": i["gap"],
                                              "missing": [g["check"] for g in i["gap"] if not g["ok"]]})
        else:
            report["written"].append(i["path"])

    env_file = target / ".env.example"
    env_existed = env_file.exists()
    existing_env = env_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if env_existed else ""
    present = {m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"^\s*([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\s*=", existing_env, re.M)}
    needed = {v for i in plan if i["action"] == "written" for v in i["env"]}   # only for files this run installs
    to_add = sorted(v for v in needed if v not in present)

    write = not a.dry_run and not conflicts
    if write:
        target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for i in plan:
            if i["action"] == "written":
                dest = target / i["path"]
                dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                dest.write_text(i["content"], encoding="utf-8")
            elif i["action"] == "proposed":
                (target / i["proposed"]).write_text(i["content"], encoding="utf-8")
        if to_add:
            block = ([""] if existing_env else []) + ["# observability (added by observability-setup/scripts/install.py)"]
            block += [f"{v}=  # {ENV_DOC.get(v, 'see docs/observability.md')}" for v in to_add]
            sep = "" if not existing_env or existing_env.endswith("\n") else "\n"
            env_file.write_text(existing_env + sep + "\n".join(block) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if to_add and not conflicts:
        report["env_added"] = to_add
        if not env_existed:
            report["written"].append(".env.example")
    if conflicts:   # nothing is written on a conflict — report the plan that would have run
        report.update(written=[], proposed=[], env_added=[])

    report["console_calls"] = console_calls(target, {i["path"] for i in plan})

    rj, rm = Path(a.report_json), Path(a.report_md)
    rj.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rm.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rj.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    verb = "would be " if a.dry_run else ""
    status = ("**Aborted — nothing written.** The repo already holds a conflicting pair; fix it and re-run." if conflicts else
              f"**{len(report['written'])} file(s) {verb}written, {len(report['skipped'])} skipped (identical), "
              f"{len(report['kept'])} kept (exists), {len(report['proposed'])} proposed for manual merge, "
              f"{len(report['env_added'])} env var(s) {verb}added.**" + (" Dry run — nothing was written." if a.dry_run else ""))
    lines = [f"# Observability install — {project}", "", status, "",
             f"Flavour: **{'TypeScript' if flavour == 'ts' else 'JavaScript'}** (`.{flavour}`) — {evidence}.", ""]
    if conflicts:
        lines += ["## Conflicts (fix before re-running)", ""] + [f"- `{c['path']}` — {c['reason']}" for c in conflicts] + [""]
    lines += ["## Written", ""] + [f"- `{p}`" for p in report["written"]] + (["- none"] if not report["written"] else [])
    lines += ["", "## Kept (exists, kept — no sibling created)", ""]
    lines += [f"- `{k['path']}` — {k['reason']}" for k in report["kept"]] + (["- none"] if not report["kept"] else [])
    if report["health_gaps"]:
        lines += ["", "## Existing health route vs the standard", ""]
        for g in report["health_gaps"]:
            lines += [f"`{g['path']}` — {'responds (exports GET)' if g['responds'] else 'DOES NOT RESPOND (no GET export)'}; "
                      f"missing versus the standard: {', '.join(g['missing']) if g['missing'] else 'nothing'}", "",
                      "| Check | Status | Note |", "|---|---|---|"]
            lines += [f"| {c['check']} | {'ok' if c['ok'] else 'MISSING'} | {c['note']} |" for c in g["checks"]]
            lines += [""]
    lines += ["", "## Skipped (already identical)", ""] + [f"- `{s['path']}`" for s in report["skipped"]] + (["- none"] if not report["skipped"] else [])
    lines += ["", "## Proposed (exists with different content — merge by hand)", ""]
    lines += [f"- `{p['path']}` → review `{p['proposed']}`" for p in report["proposed"]] + (["- none"] if not report["proposed"] else [])
    lines += ["", "## Env vars added to .env.example", "", "Only variables read by files written in this run are added.", ""]
    lines += [f"- `{v}` — {ENV_DOC.get(v, '')}" for v in report["env_added"]] + (["- none"] if not report["env_added"] else [])
    lines += ["", "## Console calls to replace with lib/logger", ""]
    lines += [f"- `{c['path']}:{c['line']}` — `{c['call']}`" for c in report["console_calls"]] or ["- none found"]
    lines += ["", "## Next steps", "",
              f"1. Wire `requestId` in `middleware.{flavour}` and set ESLint `no-console: error`.",
              "2. Replace `console.*` calls with `lib/logger` in minimal diffs.",
              "3. Set `HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN` in the deploy platform's env; curl both health routes on preview.",
              "4. Fill owners and runbook links in `ops/alerts.yaml`; translate to the monitoring vendor.",
              "5. Fill the SLO table in `docs/observability.md` from the critical journeys in SPEC."]
    if report["health_gaps"]:
        lines.append("6. Close the gaps in the existing health route table above (keep the route file; edit in place).")
    rm.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if conflicts:
        print(f"error: conflicting files already in the repo — nothing written: "
              + "; ".join(f"{c['path']} ({', '.join(c['existing'])})" for c in conflicts) + f" -> {rm}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"{'dry-run: ' if a.dry_run else ''}[{flavour}] {len(report['written'])} written, {len(report['skipped'])} skipped, "
          f"{len(report['kept'])} kept, {len(report['proposed'])} proposed, env +{len(report['env_added'])} -> {rj}, {rm}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy an existing repo layout to the run's target before the skill acts on it (evals/demos only).

    python3 -I scripts/seed_repo.py --from evals/fixtures/repo-existing --target <out>/repo

Lets a demo run the brownfield ("existing") path against a copy, so the fixture in the skill folder is
never written to. Every file under --from (dotfiles included) is copied to the same relative path under
--target, and a `.seeded-copy` marker is written. A target this script seeded earlier is wiped and
re-seeded (re-runs into the same out dir); any other non-empty target is refused, so a real repo is
never overwritten. Exit 1 on bad input. Stdlib.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MARKER = ".seeded-copy"


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Copy an existing repo layout to a fresh target (demos only)")
    ap.add_argument("--from", dest="src", required=True, help="directory to copy (the existing repo layout)")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="directory to create")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    src, target = Path(a.src).resolve(), Path(a.target).resolve()
    if not src.is_dir():
        die(f"source layout not found: {src}")
    if target == src or src in target.parents:
        die("target must be outside the source layout")
    if target.exists():
        if not target.is_dir():
            die(f"target is not a directory: {target}")
        if any(target.iterdir()):
            if not (target / MARKER).is_file():
                die(f"target is not empty and was not seeded by this script: {target}")
            shutil.rmtree(target)
    files = sorted(p for p in src.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
    if not files:
        die(f"source layout is empty: {src}")
    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for p in files:
        dest = target / p.relative_to(src)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy(p, dest)
    (target / MARKER).write_text("copied by seed_repo.py from an example layout — safe to delete\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"seeded {target} with {len(files)} file(s) from {src.name}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Error Tracking (Sentry default; adapt names for another vendor)

## Install
```bash
npm i @sentry/nextjs
npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs   # or hand-write the three config files below
```
Env: `SENTRY_DSN` (server/edge), `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (client), `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (CI only, source maps).

## Config files
| File | Runtime | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sentry.server.config.ts` | node | `tracesSampleRate` 0.1 prod / 1.0 preview; `beforeSend` scrubs PII |
| `sentry.client.config.ts` | browser | `replaysOnErrorSampleRate` 0.1 if Replay used; mask all text |
| `sentry.edge.config.ts` | edge | minimal |
| `instrumentation.ts` | — | `register()` loads the right config per `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME` |
| `app/global-error.tsx` | client | `Sentry.captureException(error)` + show `requestId` |
| `next.config.ts` | — | `withSentryConfig(config, { silent: true, widenClientFileUpload: true, hideSourceMaps: true })` |

## Tagging and context
```ts
Sentry.setTag("requestId", ctx.requestId);
Sentry.setTag("tenantId", ctx.tenantId);
Sentry.setUser({ id: ctx.userId });          // id only — never email
Sentry.setTag("release", process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA);
```
Do this in `requireUser()` (server) and after sign-in (client).

## Scrubbing (`beforeSend`)
- Drop `request.cookies`, `request.headers.authorization`, `request.data` (bodies).
- Walk `extra`/`contexts` with the same redaction list as the logger.
- `sendDefaultPii: false`.

## What to capture
| Capture | Don't capture |
|---|---|
| Unhandled exceptions (automatic) | expected `Result` failures (4xx) — those are logs at `warn` |
| `INTERNAL` results in services (`Sentry.captureException(error.cause)`) | validation errors |
| Failed jobs after final retry | each retry |
| Client render errors (`global-error.tsx`) | network errors from ad blockers (`ignoreErrors`) |

## Source maps
CI step in `prod.yml` after build: Sentry plugin uploads with `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`; release = commit sha. Verify one prod event shows de-minified frames.

## Alert integration
Sentry issue alerts: new issue in prod → channel; regression → channel; spike (>10 events/5 min same issue) → page. See `alerts-and-slos.md`.

## Verify
1. Deploy preview; hit `/api/health/deep?simulate=error` (preview only) → event appears with `requestId` tag.
2. Open the event: no email, cookies, or body present.
3. Client: throw in a test button behind `feature.debug` → event with session replay masked.

# Health Endpoints

| Endpoint | Purpose | Auth | Dependencies | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | liveness: process up, build info | none | none | uptime monitor (every 1 min), prod smoke in `prod.yml` |
| `GET /api/health/deep` | readiness: each dependency checked with timeout | `Authorization: Bearer ${HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN}` | DB, auth, storage, queue, critical external | synthetic monitor (every 5 min), post-deploy smoke, on-call |

## Response contract
```json
{
  "status": "ok" | "degraded" | "down",
  "version": "<git sha>",
  "env": "production",
  "ts": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "checks": {
    "db":      { "status": "ok", "latencyMs": 12 },
    "auth":    { "status": "ok", "latencyMs": 40 },
    "storage": { "status": "degraded", "latencyMs": 2900, "detail": "slow" },
    "queue":   { "status": "down", "error": "timeout" }
  }
}
```
HTTP: `200` for `ok`/`degraded`, `503` for `down`. `degraded` = any check slow (> `slowMs`) or an optional dependency down; `down` = any required dependency failed.

## Rules
| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Liveness never touches a dependency | a DB outage must not make the app "dead" to the platform |
| Deep check per-dependency timeout ≤ 3 s, total ≤ 8 s | monitors time out at 10 s |
| Deep check protected | it reveals topology and can be used to load the DB |
| `Cache-Control: no-store`, `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, `runtime = 'nodejs'` | never cached; service role needs node |
| DB check = `select 1` via service role **or** a trivial RLS-safe read; never a heavy query | cost |
| Checks read-only | never write from health |
| `?simulate=error|slow` honoured only when `VERCEL_ENV !== 'production'` | lets alerts be tested on preview |
| Every check logs at `warn` on degraded, `error` on down with `requestId` | correlates with alerts |

## Which dependencies are "required"
| Dependency | Required | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Postgres | yes | `select 1` |
| Supabase Auth | yes | `GET ${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/health` |
| Storage | if uploads are core | `storage.listBuckets()` limit 1 |
| Queue / jobs table | if async flows are core | `select count(*) from jobs where status='pending' and created_at < now() - interval '15 min'` → degraded if > 0 |
| Payment provider | optional | `GET /v1/balance` style lightweight call (cached 60 s) |

## Brownfield: a health route already exists
Keep it — never add `route.ts` beside `route.js` (Next.js resolves one and the other is dead code or a build error). `scripts/install.py` reports the existing route as `exists, kept` and runs this static check; close the gaps by editing the file in place.

| Check | Standard | Typical gap |
|---|---|---|
| exports `GET` | the route responds | missing export → the monitor gets 405 |
| `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` | never prerendered | cached "ok" during an outage |
| `Cache-Control: no-store` | never cached by CDN | stale status |
| build info (`version`/`sha`) | smoke test compares with the released commit | — |
| `ts` | monitors spot a stuck clock | — |
| liveness has no dependency calls (`fetch`, `.rpc(`, Supabase client) | a DB outage must not make the app look dead | existing route probes Supabase → move that probe to `/api/health/deep` |
| deep: bearer-protected, per-dependency timeout, 503 on a required failure | see rules above | unauthenticated deep check exposes topology |

# Log Schema

One JSON object per line to stdout. Vercel captures stdout; Log Drains forward it.

## Fields
| Field | Type | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts` | ISO 8601 UTC | always | logger |
| `level` | `debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error` | always | caller |
| `msg` | string, static phrase | always | caller — "invoice created", never `invoice ${id} created` |
| `service` | `web` / `edge-fn:<name>` / `job:<name>` / `script:<name>` | always | env `SERVICE_NAME` or default `web` |
| `env` | `production` / `preview` / `development` | always | `VERCEL_ENV` ?? `NODE_ENV` |
| `version` | git sha | always | `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` |
| `requestId` | string | request scope | middleware (`x-request-id` or generated) |
| `vercelId` | string | request scope | `x-vercel-id` header |
| `userId` | uuid | when known | `requireUser()` |
| `tenantId` | uuid | when known | `requireUser()` |
| `route` | string | request scope | pathname pattern, not raw URL |
| `action` | string | server actions / jobs | `invoice.create` |
| `outcome` | `ok` / `<ERROR_CODE>` | operations | Result mapping |
| `durationMs` | number | operations | caller |
| `err` | `{ name, message, code?, stack? }` | errors | serializer; stack only at `error` level |
| context | flat key/values | optional | ids, enums, counts only |

## Levels
| Level | Use | Prod volume target |
|---|---|---|
| `debug` | development tracing | off in prod (`LOG_LEVEL=info`) |
| `info` | state changes: created/updated/deleted/sent; request completed | 1–3 lines per request |
| `warn` | expected failures: validation, 401/403/404/409, retry succeeded | — |
| `error` | unexpected: 5xx, upstream down after retries, invariant broken | every one is actionable |

## Redaction (applied by the logger before serialization, case-insensitive key match)
`password, passwd, secret, token, authorization, cookie, set-cookie, apikey, api_key, key, email, phone, ssn, card, iban, dsn` → value replaced by `"[redacted]"`. Nested objects walked to depth 5. Strings > 2 kB truncated with `…[+N]`.

## Request context (`lib/logger/context.ts`)
- `AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId, vercelId, userId?, tenantId?, route }>`.
- `middleware.ts` generates/propagates `x-request-id` and sets it on the response.
- `requireUser()` enriches the store with `userId`, `tenantId`.
- `log.info(ctx, msg)` merges store + ctx automatically; services never pass ids by hand.

## Rules
| Rule | Enforcement |
|---|---|
| `no-console: error` | ESLint |
| No raw request bodies, headers, or URLs with query strings | review; redaction catches common keys |
| Error logged once, at the handling layer | review |
| Log line per outcome, not per step | review |
| Pretty output only when `NODE_ENV=development && LOG_PRETTY=1` | logger |

## Finding a request
1. User reports → ask for `requestId` shown on the error page.
2. Log sink query: `requestId:"<id>"` → all lines across web + edge + jobs.
3. Error tracker: tag `requestId` → event with stack.

# Performance rules PF1–PF10

Static rules implemented in `scripts/perf_review.py`. Each has an id, what the scanner matches, why it matters under load, the fix, and the cases it deliberately does not flag. Severity is **high** when the cost grows with data volume or request count without bound (one bad deploy takes the site down at peak) and **medium** when the cost is real but bounded (slower, heavier, but it stays up).

| Id | Name | Severity | Matches | Why it matters | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PF1 | n-plus-one-query | high | Supabase `.from(`/`.rpc(` or `fetch(` inside a `for`/`while` body or inside a `.map(`/`.forEach(`/`.flatMap(` callback | One round trip per row: 500 rows → 500 queries; latency and connection use scale with the list, and PostgREST/pooler limits are hit first at peak | One query with `.in("fk", ids)`, an embedded select (`select("id, items(sku, qty)")`), or one RPC; then join in memory |
| PF2 | await-in-loop | medium | `await` inside a `for`/`while` body that is not a `for await` loop and is not already a PF1 line | Independent async work runs one after another; total time is the sum instead of the max | Build the promise array and `await Promise.all(...)` (or `Promise.allSettled`); keep a loop only when order or back-pressure is required and say so in a comment |
| PF3 | select-star | high | `.select("*")`, or a select list whose top-level columns include `*` or an embedded `rel(*)` | Every column crosses the wire and is serialised, covering indexes cannot be used, and a later wide column (JSON, text) silently inflates every response | Name the columns the page renders; keep `*` out of embedded selects too |
| PF4 | unbounded-list-read | high | A `.from(…).select(…)` read chain with no `.limit(`, `.range(`, `.single(`, `.maybeSingle(`; writes (`insert/update/delete/upsert`), `head: true` counts and `.eq("id", …)` point reads are exempt | Response size and query time grow with the table; the page that was fine at 2k rows times out at 200k | Paginate with `.range(from, to)` from `searchParams`, or cap with `.limit(n)` and expose "load more" |
| PF5 | fetch-in-use-effect | medium | In a `"use client"` file, a `useEffect(` whose callback body calls `fetch(`, `.from(` or `.rpc(` | The request starts only after hydration: HTML → JS → render → fetch → re-render, a waterfall that doubles time-to-data and bypasses the server cache | Fetch in the server component (page or a server parent) and pass data as props; for client-only interactivity use a server action or a cached route |
| PF6 | heavy-compute-in-render | medium | In a `"use client"` PascalCase component body, `.sort(` or `.filter(` on a destructured prop or `props.x` outside `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`useEffect` | The derived list is recomputed on every render (every keystroke, every parent re-render); sort is O(n log n) and allocates a new array, which also defeats memoised children | `useMemo(() => orders.filter(...).sort(...), [orders, query])`; for very large lists move the sort to the query |
| PF7 | img-instead-of-next-image | medium | `<img` in a `.tsx`/`.jsx` file | No resizing, no modern formats, no lazy loading, no size reservation: large transfers and layout shift (LCP, CLS) | `import Image from "next/image"` with `width`/`height` (or `fill`) and `sizes`; add the remote host to `images.remotePatterns` |
| PF8 | heavy-import-in-page | medium | In `app/**/page.*` or `layout.*`, a static `import … from` one of: recharts, chart.js, react-chartjs-2, plotly.js, react-plotly.js, d3, three, @react-three/fiber, monaco-editor, @monaco-editor/react, codemirror, @codemirror/view, mapbox-gl, leaflet, react-leaflet, pdfjs-dist, react-pdf, jspdf, html2canvas, xlsx, quill, react-quill, @tiptap/react, ag-grid-react, @fullcalendar/react, moment, lodash | The whole library lands in the route's bundle (and a layout's import lands in every route under it), paid on first load even when the widget is below the fold or behind a tab | `const Chart = dynamic(() => import("@/components/charts/RevenueChart"), { ssr: false })` from the page; keep the heavy import inside the client component |
| PF9 | no-store-on-every-fetch | medium | A server page (`app/**/page.*` without `"use client"`) with at least one `fetch(` where every call passes `cache: "no-store"` | The page is fully dynamic: every request re-fetches upstream; no ISR, no CDN hit, upstream rate limits reached first under a spike | `fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 60 } })` or `next: { tags: [...] }` with `revalidateTag` on write; keep `no-store` only for the one truly per-user call |
| PF10 | sync-fs-read-in-handler | medium | In `app/**/route.*`, `readFileSync(`/`readdirSync(` inside an exported `GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|HEAD|OPTIONS` body; module-scope reads are not flagged | The read and the `JSON.parse` run on every request and block the event loop for the whole process | Read and parse once at module scope (cached for the process), or move the data to the database / a KV store |

## Gate
- Exit 1 when any high finding is **new**; exit 0 otherwise. Outputs are always written.
- `--baseline findings.csv`: a finding whose rule, file and snippet match a baseline row is `known` (line numbers may move); unmatched baseline rows are reported as resolved. Known highs do not gate — they are recorded debt with their own PRs.

## Known false positives and limits (say these plainly in a review)
- Static text matching, not a type-checked AST: a `.from(` on a non-Supabase object (e.g. `Array.from(`) is not matched because the scanner requires a string literal argument, but a custom query builder with the same method names is treated as Supabase.
- PF1 also fires on `Promise.all(ids.map(id => supabase.from(...)))` — parallel, but still N queries; the fix is the same (`.in()`), so it stays high.
- PF2 flags a loop that is intentionally sequential (rate-limited upstream, ordered writes). Keep the loop and record it in the baseline with the reason in a code comment.
- PF4 cannot see RLS or a unique filter other than `.eq("id", …)`; a read bounded by a unique business key (`.eq("slug", …)`) without `.single()` is flagged — add `.maybeSingle()`, which is also the correct type.
- PF6 only inspects PascalCase components with parenthesised parameters in `"use client"` files and only `.sort(`/`.filter(` chains whose receiver is a prop; a local `useState` array that is sorted in the body is not flagged (conservative by design).
- PF8's library list is fixed (above); add your own heavy packages by extending `HEAVY_LIBS` in the script and this table together.
- PF9 reads `fetch` options literally; a `no-store` set through a wrapper function or `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` is not seen.
- Nothing is executed or measured: no bundle sizes, no query plans, no latency. Use `observability-setup` for production numbers and confirm each fix with them.

# product-spec-prd

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/product-spec-prd --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/product-spec-prd`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Every brief field the script cannot find becomes `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; the sharpen step may tighten wording but must not invent numbers, users or dates.

## Starting points
- **New** — your brief becomes a PRD on the template (`PRD.md`); the model step sharpens it into `prd-final.md`, or with `draft_only` the checked script draft is the final PRD. Nothing the brief does not say is invented.
- **Existing** — add `existing` (your current PRD): it is redlined section by section against the brief and the review checklist — [KEEP], [SHARPEN], [ADD], and every figure the brief does not back marked [TBD] with an owner — and `prd-final.md` is your PRD with the redline applied, storyline unchanged.

## When to use
- A feature idea, customer ask, or roadmap item needs a definition engineers can plan from.
- Scope disputes ("is X in v1?"), success metrics missing, phased rollout needed.
- NOT for: implementation plans (`spec-to-plan`), tech choices (`project-bootstrap/assets/adr-template.md`), whole-product strategy.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Problem statement or feature idea | yes | user |
| Target users / personas | yes | `docs/SPEC.md` / user — ask once |
| Constraints (deadline, platform, compliance, budget) | no | user |
| Evidence (customer requests, data, support tickets) | no | user — mark absent as assumption |
| Existing product context (`docs/SPEC.md`, related PRDs) | yes if present | repo |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`, `../../../shared/writing-style.md`, then `docs/SPEC.md` and any related PRD.
2. **Frame.** If the upstream skill `product-management:write-spec` is installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke it for steps 2–4 and then apply the template and gates below; otherwise follow `references/prd-method.md`: problem → who → why now → what success looks like. Ask ≤5 questions with defaults, once. *(gate: plan inputs)*
3. **Draft** `docs/prd/<slug>.md` from `assets/prd-template.md`: goals (measurable), non-goals (explicit), user stories with acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), phased scope (v1 / v1.1 / later), metrics with baseline and target, risks, open questions with owners, dependencies.
4. **Challenge.** Run `references/prd-review-checklist.md` against the draft: every goal has a metric; every story has a criterion; every non-goal is something a reader would assume included; v1 is the smallest slice that moves the metric.
5. **Present.** Post the exec summary (≤5 bullets) and the v1 scope table; wait for approval or redlines. Apply redlines per the redline convention (keep storyline, sharpen). *(gate: plan→approve)*
6. **Hand off.** Add a "Engineering handoff" section: acceptance criteria list ready for `spec-to-plan`, data/tenancy implications for `multi-tenant-saas-patterns`, flag name per `plans-and-flags` naming. *(gate: build via spec-to-plan)*
7. **Verify** after build: metrics instrumented (`observability-setup` log `action`/`outcome` events), success review date set. *(gate: verify)*
8. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| PRD | `docs/prd/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.md` |
| Exec summary | chat, ≤5 bullets |
| Engineering handoff | PRD §Engineering handoff → input to `spec-to-plan` |

## Self-check
- [ ] First line of the PRD states the outcome and the metric it moves
- [ ] Every goal measurable; baseline sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Non-goals list ≥ 3 things readers would assume
- [ ] Every user story has Given/When/Then acceptance criteria
- [ ] v1 scope fits one `spec-to-plan` plan (≤ 8 tasks) or is split into phases
- [ ] Open questions have owners and dates
- [ ] No invented numbers, customers, or dates

## References
- `references/prd-method.md` — framing questions, scoping rules, metric design (fallback for write-spec)
- `references/prd-review-checklist.md` — challenge list used before presenting
- `assets/prd-template.md` — PRD template
- `scripts/prd.py` — brief.json → PRD.md on the template; missing arrays become `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` rows
