--draft-only writes --final as the script draft with a label saying the sharpen step did not run.
--existing redlines a PRD the team already has against the brief and the review checklist, keeping its
storyline: every template section is [KEEP] (present and passes), [SHARPEN] (present but fails a check:
goal without a number, < 3 non-goals, metric without baseline/target, story without Given/When/Then,
open question without an owner), or [ADD] (missing: the brief-derived section is added, marked); every
figure in the existing PRD that the brief does not contain is [TBD] with an owner. --redline gets the
table; --final gets the existing PRD with the redline applied (sections untouched except markers).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DEFAULT_TEMPLATE = HERE.parent / "assets" / "prd-template.md"
TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]"


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def as_list(v) -> list:
    if v is None or v == "":
        return []
    return v if isinstance(v, list) else [v]


def replace_section(md: str, heading_startswith: str, body: list[str]) -> str:
    lines, out, i = md.splitlines(), [], 0
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        out.append(ln)
        i += 1
        if ln.startswith("## ") and ln[3:].lower().startswith(heading_startswith.lower()):
            out += body
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith("## "):
                i += 1
            if i < len(lines):
                out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


FROM_BRIEF = {"Exec summary", "Problem", "Users", "Goals", "Non-goals", "Metrics", "Phases", "Engineering handoff"}
REDLINE_SECTIONS = ["Exec summary", "Problem", "Users", "Goals", "Non-goals", "Metrics", "Phases",
                    "User stories", "Risks", "Open questions", "Engineering handoff"]
NUM_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])[$€£]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?%?(?![\w])")
DRAFT_LABEL = "> Script draft — the model sharpen step was not run (draft only); every field comes from the brief."


def split_sections(md: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[tuple[str, list[str]]]]:
    """(preamble lines, [(heading line, body lines)]) on `## ` headings."""
    pre, secs = [], []
    for ln in md.splitlines():
        if ln.startswith("## "):
            secs.append((ln, []))
        elif secs:
            secs[-1][1].append(ln)
        else:
            pre.append(ln)
    return pre, secs


def find_section(secs, name: str):
    n = name.lower()
    for i, (h, _) in enumerate(secs):
        t = re.sub(r"\s*\(.*\)\s*$", "", h[3:]).strip().lower()
        if n in t:
            return i
    return None


def figures(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Figures worth sourcing: with %, a currency sign, or >= 2 digits (ISO dates and section numbers skipped)."""
    text = re.sub(r"\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b", " ", text)
    out = []
    for m in NUM_RE.finditer(text):
        tok = m.group(0)
        digits = re.sub(r"\D", "", tok)
        if tok.endswith("%") or tok[0] in "$€£" or len(digits) >= 2:
            out.append(tok)
    return out


def checks_for(name: str, body: str) -> str:
    """The reason a present section needs sharpening, or '' when it passes."""
    has_tbd = "[TO BE BASELINED" in body
    rows = [ln for ln in body.splitlines() if ln.strip().startswith(("-", "*", "|")) and not re.match(r"^\s*\|[-| ]+\|\s*$", ln)
            and not re.match(r"^\s*\|\s*(#|Non-goal|Metric|Goal|Question|Risk)\b", ln)]
    if not body.strip():
        return "section is empty"
    if name == "Goals" and not figures(body) and not has_tbd:
        return "no goal names a measurable target"
    if name == "Non-goals" and len(rows) < 3:
        return f"{len(rows)} non-goal(s); list at least 3 things a reader would assume are included"
    if name == "Metrics" and not re.search(r"baseline", body, re.I) and not has_tbd:
        return "metrics have no baseline"
    if name == "User stories" and not re.search(r"\bGiven\b.*\bThen\b", body, re.S):
        return "stories have no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria"
    if name == "Open questions" and not re.search(r"owner", body, re.I):
        return "open questions have no owner"
    return ""


def redline(existing: str, draft: str, brief_text: str, source: str) -> tuple[list[dict], str]:
    """Rows for the redline table and the existing PRD with the redline applied."""
    pre, secs = split_sections(existing)
    _, dsecs = split_sections(draft)
    rows, adds = [], []
    for name in REDLINE_SECTIONS:
        i = find_section(secs, name)
        if i is None:
            j = find_section(dsecs, name) if name in FROM_BRIEF else None
            rows.append({"section": name, "verdict": "ADD", "note": "missing — added from the brief" if j is not None
                         else "missing — write it (the brief does not cover it)"})
            body = dsecs[j][1] if j is not None else [TBD, ""]
            adds.append([f"## {name}", f"> [ADD] {rows[-1]['note']}"] + body)
            continue
        reason = checks_for(name, "\n".join(secs[i][1]))
        rows.append({"section": name, "verdict": "SHARPEN" if reason else "KEEP", "note": reason or "passes the checklist"})
        if reason:
            secs[i] = (secs[i][0], [f"> [SHARPEN] {reason}"] + secs[i][1])
    known = set(figures(brief_text))
    unsourced = []
    out_secs = []
    for h, body in secs:
        new_body = []
        for ln in body:
            figs = [f for f in figures(ln) if f not in known and not ln.lstrip().startswith(">")]
            for f in figs:
                unsourced.append({"section": re.sub(r"\s*\(.*\)\s*$", "", h[3:]).strip(), "figure": f})
            if figs:
                ln += " " + " ".join(f"[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner — source for {f}]" for f in figs)
            new_body.append(ln)
        out_secs.append((h, new_body))
    for u in unsourced:
        rows.append({"section": u["section"], "verdict": "TBD", "note": f"figure {u['figure']} is not in the brief — source it or cut it"})
    note = (f"> Redlined against {source} by product-spec-prd (no model step): storyline kept; "
            "[SHARPEN] / [ADD] markers and owned to-be-baselined markers show what to change.")
    lines = list(pre[:1]) + ["", note] + list(pre[1:])
    for h, body in out_secs:
        lines += [h] + body
    for block in adds:
        lines += [""] + block
    return rows, "\n".join(lines).rstrip("\n") + "\n"


def render_redline(rows: list[dict], existing_name: str) -> str:
    counts = {v: sum(1 for r in rows if r["verdict"] == v) for v in ("KEEP", "SHARPEN", "ADD", "TBD")}
    out = [f"# PRD redline — {existing_name}", "",
           f"**{counts['KEEP']} keep, {counts['SHARPEN']} sharpen, {counts['ADD']} add, {counts['TBD']} unsourced figure(s).** "
           "Storyline kept; nothing rewritten.", "", "## Redline table", "", "| Section | Verdict | Note |", "|---|---|---|"]
    out += [f"| {r['section']} | [{r['verdict']}] | {cell(r['note'])} |" for r in rows]
    out += ["", "## Unsourced figures", ""]
    tbd = [r for r in rows if r["verdict"] == "TBD"]
    out += [f"- {r['section']}: {r['note']} (owner: Product owner)" for r in tbd] or ["- none: every figure traces to the brief"]
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def cell(s) -> str:
    return str(s).replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ").strip() or TBD


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="brief.json -> PRD.md on the template")
    ap.add_argument("brief")
    ap.add_argument("--template", default=str(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="PRD.md")
    ap.add_argument("--final", default="", help="final PRD path (written with --draft-only or --existing)")
    ap.add_argument("--draft-only", action="store_true", help="no model step: write --final from the script draft")
    ap.add_argument("--existing", default="", help="the team's existing PRD to redline against the brief")
    ap.add_argument("--redline", default="", help="with --existing: write the redline table here")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.existing and not Path(a.existing).is_file():
        die(f"existing PRD not found: {a.existing}")
    bp, tp = Path(a.brief), Path(a.template)
    if not bp.is_file():
        die(f"brief not found: {bp}")
    if not tp.is_file():
        die(f"template not found: {tp}")
    try:
        brief = json.loads(bp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        die(f"brief is not valid JSON: {e}")
    if not isinstance(brief, dict):
        die("brief must be a JSON object")
    feature = str(brief.get("feature", "")).strip()
    problem = str(brief.get("problem", "")).strip()
    if not feature or not problem:
        die("brief needs non-empty 'feature' and 'problem'")
    users, goals, non_goals = as_list(brief.get("users")), as_list(brief.get("goals")), as_list(brief.get("non_goals"))
    metrics = [m if isinstance(m, dict) else {"name": str(m)} for m in as_list(brief.get("metrics"))]
    phases = [p if isinstance(p, dict) else {"name": str(p)} for p in as_list(brief.get("phases"))]
    evidence = [e if isinstance(e, dict) else {"claim": str(e)} for e in as_list(brief.get("evidence"))]
    constraints = as_list(brief.get("constraints"))
    flag = str(brief.get("flag") or "").strip() or f"feature.{re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', feature.lower()).strip('_')}"
    gaps = []

    md = tp.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("{{TITLE}}", feature)
    m0 = metrics[0] if metrics else {}
    head = (f"**{feature}: {problem.rstrip('.')}. Target {cell(m0.get('name')) if metrics else TBD} "
            f"from {cell(m0.get('baseline')) if m0.get('baseline') else TBD} to "
            f"{cell(m0.get('target')) if m0.get('target') else TBD} by {cell(m0.get('by')) if m0.get('by') else TBD}.**")
    md = re.sub(r"^\*\*\{\{Outcome sentence\}\}.*\*\*$", lambda _: head, md, count=1, flags=re.M)
    md = md.replace("| Flag | `feature.<name>` |", f"| Flag | `{flag}` |")
    exec_summary = [f"- Problem: {problem}",
                    f"- Who: {', '.join(map(str, users)) if users else TBD}",
                    f"- What: {feature}",
                    f"- Success: {'; '.join(f'{cell(m.get('name'))} → {cell(m.get('target')) if m.get('target') else TBD}' for m in metrics) if metrics else TBD}",
                    f"- Scope: v1 = {'; '.join(map(str, as_list(phases[0].get('scope')))) if phases and as_list(phases[0].get('scope')) else TBD}; "
                    f"later = {', '.join(cell(p.get('name')) for p in phases[1:]) if len(phases) > 1 else TBD}"]
    md = replace_section(md, "Exec summary", exec_summary)
    prob = ["| Evidence | Source | Date |", "|---|---|---|"]
    prob += [f"| {cell(e.get('claim'))} | {cell(e.get('source')) if e.get('source') else TBD} | {cell(e.get('date')) if e.get('date') else TBD} |"
             for e in evidence] or [f"| {TBD} (no evidence supplied — assumption) | {TBD} | {TBD} |"]
    if not evidence:
        gaps.append("evidence")
    prob += ["", f"Problem statement: {problem}", "", f"What happens if we do nothing: {TBD}"]
    if constraints:
        prob += ["", "Constraints: " + "; ".join(map(str, constraints))]
    md = replace_section(md, "Problem", prob)
    us = ["| Persona | Role (RBAC) | Job to be done | Today's workaround |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    us += [f"| {cell(u)} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} |" for u in users] or [f"| {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} |"]
    if not users:
        gaps.append("users")
    md = replace_section(md, "Users", us)
    gl = ["| # | Goal | Metric | Baseline | Target | Review date |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for i, g in enumerate(goals, 1):
        m = metrics[i - 1] if i - 1 < len(metrics) else {}
        label = "G1 (primary)" if i == 1 else f"G{i} (leading)"
        gl.append(f"| {label} | {cell(g)} | {cell(m.get('name')) if m else TBD} | "
                  f"{cell(m.get('baseline')) if m.get('baseline') else TBD} | {cell(m.get('target')) if m.get('target') else TBD} | {TBD} |")
    if not goals:
        gl.append(f"| G1 (primary) | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} |")
        gaps.append("goals")
    gl.append(f"| Guardrail | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} |")
    md = replace_section(md, "Goals", gl)
    ng = ["| Non-goal | Reason | Revisit in |", "|---|---|---|"]
    ng += [f"| {cell(n)} | {TBD} | {TBD} |" for n in non_goals] or [f"| {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} |"]
    if not non_goals:
        gaps.append("non_goals")
    md = replace_section(md, "Non-goals", ng)
    mt = ["| Metric | Baseline | Target | Source / instrumentation | Review date |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    mt += [f"| {cell(m.get('name'))} | {cell(m.get('baseline')) if m.get('baseline') else TBD} | "
           f"{cell(m.get('target')) if m.get('target') else TBD} | {cell(m.get('source')) if m.get('source') else TBD} | {TBD} |"
           for m in metrics] or [f"| {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} |"]
    if not metrics:
        gaps.append("metrics")
    md = replace_section(md, "Metrics", mt)
    ph = ["| Phase | Includes | Excludes | Exit criterion |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    ph += [f"| {cell(p.get('name'))} | {'; '.join(map(str, as_list(p.get('scope')))) or TBD} | "
           f"{'; '.join(map(str, as_list(p.get('excludes')))) or TBD} | {cell(p.get('exit')) if p.get('exit') else TBD} |"
           for p in phases] or [f"| v1 | {TBD} | {TBD} | {TBD} |", f"| Later | {TBD} | {TBD} | needs evidence: {TBD} |"]
    if not phases:
        gaps.append("phases")
    md = replace_section(md, "Phases", ph)
    md = replace_section(md, "Engineering handoff", [
        f"- Acceptance criteria: {TBD} (derive from the v1 scope rows above)",
        f"- Entities for supabase-schema-rls: {TBD}",
        f"- RBAC rows to add: {TBD}",
        "- Metrics instrumentation: events `action=<…>` with `outcome`" + (f" for {', '.join(cell(m.get('name')) for m in metrics)}" if metrics else ""),
        f"- Flag: `{flag}`"])
    md = md.replace("{{date}}", dt.date.today().isoformat())
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(md, encoding="utf-8")
    if a.existing:
        ep = Path(a.existing)
        rows, merged = redline(ep.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), md, bp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), bp.name)
        if a.redline:
            Path(a.redline).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            Path(a.redline).write_text(render_redline(rows, ep.name), encoding="utf-8")
        if a.final:
            Path(a.final).write_text(merged, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"redline: {ep.name} — " + ", ".join(f"{sum(1 for r in rows if r['verdict'] == v)} {v.lower()}"
                                                   for v in ("KEEP", "SHARPEN", "ADD", "TBD")))
    elif a.draft_only and a.final:
        lines = md.splitlines()
        Path(a.final).write_text("\n".join(lines[:1] + ["", DRAFT_LABEL] + lines[1:]) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    n_tbd = md.count("[TO BE BASELINED")
    print(f"PRD: {feature}; {len(goals)} goal(s), {len(metrics)} metric(s), {len(phases)} phase(s); "
          f"{n_tbd} marker(s) to baseline" + (f"; brief lacked: {', '.join(gaps)}" if gaps else "") + f" -> {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# PRD Method (fallback for product-management:write-spec)

## 1. Frame (one round of questions, each with a default)
| Question | Why it matters | Default if unanswered |
|---|---|---|
| What problem, for whom, observed how? | prevents solution-first PRDs | mark evidence as assumption |
| What happens if we do nothing? | tests urgency | "status quo acceptable for 1 quarter" |
| What metric moves, from what baseline, to what target, by when? | defines success | baseline `[TO BE BASELINED]`; target = relative (+20%) |
| Who is explicitly not served in v1? | forces non-goals | all personas not named |
| What constraints are fixed? (date, platform, compliance, budget) | shapes phasing | none |

## 2. Scoping rules
| Rule | Practice |
|---|---|
| v1 = smallest slice that moves the metric for the primary persona | cut anything that serves a secondary persona or a secondary metric |
| Non-goals are written as "will not …" with the reason and the phase it may return | ≥ 3 |
| Phases: v1 (ship), v1.1 (fast follow ≤ 4 weeks), later (needs new evidence) | each phase lists its own criteria |
| One PRD = one outcome | two outcomes → two PRDs |
| Dependencies named with owner | integration, data, legal, design |

## 3. User stories
`As a <persona>, I want <capability> so that <outcome>.`
Acceptance criteria per story (Given / When / Then), binary, testable; include the negative/permission case for anything tenant- or role-sensitive.

## 4. Metrics
| Type | Example | Instrumentation |
|---|---|---|
| Outcome (primary, 1) | export adoption: % of active tenants exporting ≥1/month | log event `action=invoice.export outcome=ok` grouped by tenant |
| Leading (≤ 2) | time-to-first-export after enabling | event timestamps |
| Guardrail (≤ 2) | p95 export latency < 5 s; support tickets on exports not up | logs; support tag |

Every metric: name, definition, source, baseline (sourced or TBD with owner), target, review date.

## 5. Risks and open questions
Risk table: risk, likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner. Open questions: question, owner, due date, decision default if unanswered by then.

## 6. Writing
Follow `shared/writing-style.md`: assertions as headings, ≤ 20-word sentences, tables for 3+ items, no banned words, no hedging in the recommendation.

# PRD Review Checklist (run before presenting)

| # | Check | Fail looks like | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | First line states outcome + metric | "This PRD describes…" | rewrite: "Tenant admins export invoices in one click; target: 40% of active tenants export monthly by Q3" |
| 2 | Problem has evidence or is labelled assumption | "Users want…" with no source | cite tickets/data or `[assumption]` |
| 3 | Exactly one primary metric with baseline + target + date | three "key metrics", no baseline | choose one; baseline `[TO BE BASELINED — owner]` |
| 4 | Non-goals ≥ 3 and each is something a reader would assume | "Non-goals: none" | list adjacent features, personas, platforms excluded |
| 5 | Every story has Given/When/Then | "User can export" | add criteria incl. permission-denied case |
| 6 | v1 scope ≤ 8 engineering tasks (sanity) | ten stories in v1 | move to v1.1/later |
| 7 | Tenancy/role implications stated | silent on who can do it | add role row per story; reference RBAC matrix |
| 8 | Data implications stated | new entity not mentioned | list new/changed entities for supabase-schema-rls |
| 9 | Flag name and rollout plan | none | `feature.<name>`, per-tenant rollout |
| 10 | Risks have owner + mitigation | "Risk: adoption" | likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner |
| 11 | Open questions have owner + date + default | list of questions only | add columns |
| 12 | No invented numbers, customers, dates | "Acme asked for this" (not provided) | remove or source |
| 13 | Engineering handoff section complete | missing | criteria list, entities, flag, metrics instrumentation |
| 14 | Readable by a CIO in 3 minutes | 6 pages | body ≤ 2 pages; appendix for detail |

# project-bootstrap

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/project-bootstrap --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/project-bootstrap`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## Starting points
- **New** — an empty folder gets the full skeleton: SPEC, CLAUDE.md, HANDOFF, ADRs, `.env.example`, CODEOWNERS, PR template and the three workflows.
- **Existing** — your repo keeps every file it has; missing skeleton files are added, and each kept SPEC/CLAUDE/HANDOFF is compared with the standard and its missing sections listed as gaps to merge by hand (`bootstrap-report.json`).

## When to use
- "New app", "new repo", "set up the project", "bootstrap", "start from scratch".
- An existing repo has no `docs/SPEC.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `HANDOFF.md` and the user wants it brought to standard.
- NOT for: feature work (`spec-to-plan`), pipeline changes (`ci-cd-vercel-github`), schema (`supabase-schema-rls`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Project name + one-line purpose | yes | user |
| Target directory | yes | user (default: cwd) |
| Stack deviations from `shared/stack-conventions.md` | no | user |
| Tenancy model (single / multi-tenant) | yes | user — ask once |
| Hosting/accounts already provisioned (Vercel, Supabase, GitHub) | no | user |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md`, `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`, `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. **Plan.** List what will be created (see `references/bootstrap-checklist.md`) and what already exists in the target dir. Present as a table: file → create / keep / skip. Wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Build.** Run the scaffold — it never overwrites:
   ```
   python3 -I scripts/scaffold.py --target <dir> --name "<project>" [--multi-tenant]
   ```
   It writes `docs/SPEC.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/HANDOFF.md`, `docs/adr/0000-template.md`, `docs/adr/0001-stack.md`, `.env.example`, `.github/workflows/{ci,preview,prod}.yml`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scaffold.py — write the docs/ADR/CI skeleton into a target directory.

Idempotent: never overwrites an existing file. Re-running reports 0 writes.
Existing repo: every kept Markdown file is read and compared with its template's `##` sections; the
sections it lacks are reported as gaps (`gap    <file>: missing sections — A, B`) for a by-hand merge.
--report writes the same as JSON {target, written[], kept[], gaps[{path, missing[]}]}.
Stdlib only. Run offline: python3 -I scaffold.py --target <dir> --name "<project>" [--multi-tenant] [--dry-run] [--report r.json]

Templates are read from ../assets relative to this script.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as _dt
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ASSETS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "assets"

# (template relative to assets/, destination relative to target)
FILES: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
    ("SPEC.md", "docs/SPEC.md"),
    ("CLAUDE.md", "CLAUDE.md"),
    ("HANDOFF.md", "docs/HANDOFF.md"),
    ("adr-template.md", "docs/adr/0000-template.md"),
    ("env.example", ".env.example"),
    ("CODEOWNERS", ".github/CODEOWNERS"),
    ("pull_request_template.md", ".github/pull_request_template.md"),
    ("workflows/ci.yml", ".github/workflows/ci.yml"),
    ("workflows/preview.yml", ".github/workflows/preview.yml"),
    ("workflows/prod.yml", ".github/workflows/prod.yml"),
]

STACK_ADR = """# ADR-0001: Default stack — Next.js App Router, Supabase, Vercel, GitHub Actions

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted |
| Date | {date} |
| Deciders | [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Tech lead] |

## Context
{name} needs a web application with authenticated users, relational data{tenancy_ctx}, preview environments per change, and a release gate before production. The team standard (shared/stack-conventions.md) is Next.js + Supabase + Vercel + GitHub Actions.

## Decision
Adopt the standard stack without deviation unless listed below.

| Deviation | Reason | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| none | | |

## Options considered
| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard stack (chosen) | team fluency, RLS-based isolation, preview per PR, zero-ops hosting | vendor coupling to Supabase/Vercel | chosen |
| Custom Node API + managed Postgres | full control | ops burden, no RLS by default, slower to first release | rejected |
| Serverless on GCP (Cloud Run + Cloud SQL) | enterprise cloud alignment | more infra code, slower preview envs | rejected for v1; revisit if GCP services are required |

## Consequences
| Type | Consequence | Mitigation (owner) |
|---|---|---|
| Positive | Preview per PR, RLS enforced isolation, tag-gated prod | — |
| Negative | Supabase/Vercel lock-in | Keep data access behind `lib/db`; migrations in repo |
| Neutral | Python for scripts/agents only | ruff + pytest in CI |

## Compliance / verification
- `rls_lint.py` in CI; `.env.example` contract parsed by `lib/env.ts`; prod deploys only via `prod.yml` on tag.
"""


def section_names(markdown: str) -> list[str]:
    """`##` headings with numbering and a trailing parenthetical removed: '## 1. Purpose (one paragraph)' -> 'Purpose'."""
    out = []
    for ln in markdown.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"^##\s+(.*)$", ln)
        if not m:
            continue
        name = re.sub(r"^\d+(\.\d+)*\.?\s+", "", m.group(1)).strip()
        name = re.sub(r"\s*\(.*\)\s*$", "", name).strip()
        if name:
            out.append(name)
    return out


def missing_sections(existing: str, template: str) -> list[str]:
    """Template sections with no matching heading in the existing file (case-insensitive; a match is one name
    containing the other, so '## Users' covers 'Users and jobs to be done')."""
    heads = [h.lower() for h in section_names(existing)]
    return [s for s in section_names(template) if not any(s.lower() in h or (len(h) >= 4 and h in s.lower()) for h in heads)]


def render(text: str, name: str, tenancy: str) -> str:
    today = _dt.date.today().isoformat()
    return (
        text.replace("{{PROJECT_NAME}}", name)
        .replace("{{DATE}}", today)
        .replace("{{TENANCY}}", tenancy)
        .replace("{{PURPOSE}}", "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Tech lead]")
        .replace("{{NUMBER}}", "NNNN")
        .replace("{{TITLE}}", "Title")
    )


def plan(target: Path, name: str, multi_tenant: bool) -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    tenancy = "multi-tenant (tenant_id on every scoped table; RLS)" if multi_tenant else "single-tenant"
    out: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    for src, dst in FILES:
        tpl = ASSETS / src
        if not tpl.exists():
            print(f"error: template missing: {tpl}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(2)
        out.append((target / dst, render(tpl.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), name, tenancy)))
    adr = STACK_ADR.format(
        date=_dt.date.today().isoformat(),
        name=name,
        tenancy_ctx=" with tenant isolation" if multi_tenant else "",
    )
    out.append((target / "docs/adr/0001-stack.md", adr))
    return out


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Idempotent project scaffold (docs/ADR/CI).")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="target project directory")
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="project name")
    ap.add_argument("--multi-tenant", action="store_true", help="mark tenancy as multi-tenant in SPEC/ADR")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="report without writing")
    ap.add_argument("--report", default="", help="also write written/kept/gaps as JSON here")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    target = Path(args.target).resolve()
    if not target.exists():
        if args.dry_run:
            print(f"would create dir {target}")
        else:
            target.mkdir(parents=True)

    written = skipped = 0
    report = {"target": str(target), "dry_run": args.dry_run, "written": [], "kept": [], "gaps": []}
    for path, content in plan(target, args.name, args.multi_tenant):
        rel = path.relative_to(target).as_posix()
        if path.exists():
            skipped += 1
            report["kept"].append(rel)
            print(f"keep   {rel}")
            if path.suffix == ".md":
                miss = missing_sections(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), content)
                if miss:
                    report["gaps"].append({"path": rel, "missing": miss})
                    print(f"gap    {rel}: missing sections — {', '.join(miss)}")
            continue
        written += 1
        report["written"].append(rel)
        print(f"{'would write' if args.dry_run else 'write '} {path.relative_to(target)}")
        if not args.dry_run:
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"\n{'dry-run: ' if args.dry_run else ''}{written} written, {skipped} kept (never overwritten)"
          + (f", {len(report['gaps'])} kept file(s) with section gaps to merge by hand" if report["gaps"] else ""))
    if args.report:
        rp = Path(args.report)
        rp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        rp.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy an existing repo layout to the run's target before the skill acts on it (evals/demos only).

    python3 -I scripts/seed_repo.py --from evals/fixtures/repo-existing --target <out>/repo

Lets a demo run the brownfield ("existing") path against a copy, so the fixture in the skill folder is
never written to. Every file under --from (dotfiles included) is copied to the same relative path under
--target, and a `.seeded-copy` marker is written. A target this script seeded earlier is wiped and
re-seeded (re-runs into the same out dir); any other non-empty target is refused, so a real repo is
never overwritten. Exit 1 on bad input. Stdlib.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MARKER = ".seeded-copy"


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Copy an existing repo layout to a fresh target (demos only)")
    ap.add_argument("--from", dest="src", required=True, help="directory to copy (the existing repo layout)")
    ap.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="directory to create")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    src, target = Path(a.src).resolve(), Path(a.target).resolve()
    if not src.is_dir():
        die(f"source layout not found: {src}")
    if target == src or src in target.parents:
        die("target must be outside the source layout")
    if target.exists():
        if not target.is_dir():
            die(f"target is not a directory: {target}")
        if any(target.iterdir()):
            if not (target / MARKER).is_file():
                die(f"target is not empty and was not seeded by this script: {target}")
            shutil.rmtree(target)
    files = sorted(p for p in src.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
    if not files:
        die(f"source layout is empty: {src}")
    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for p in files:
        dest = target / p.relative_to(src)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy(p, dest)
    (target / MARKER).write_text("copied by seed_repo.py from an example layout — safe to delete\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"seeded {target} with {len(files)} file(s) from {src.name}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

## Commands (verify against package.json before relying on them)
| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `npm ci` |
| Dev | `npm run dev` |
| Lint / typecheck | `npm run lint && npm run typecheck` |
| Unit tests | `npm test` |
| E2E | `npm run test:e2e` |
| Build | `npm run build` |
| Local DB | `supabase start` / `supabase stop` |
| New migration | `supabase migration new <name>` |
| Apply migrations locally | `supabase db reset` |
| Regenerate DB types | `npm run db:types` |
| RLS lint | `python3 -I scripts/rls_lint.py supabase/migrations` |

## Working rules
| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | Plan before build. For anything touching >3 files, schema, auth or CI: write the plan (files, tests, acceptance) and wait for "go". |
| 2 | Minimal diff. Edit the failing lines; never regenerate a file to change a few lines. |
| 3 | Read before writing. Never assume file contents. |
| 4 | Verify before claiming done: lint, typecheck, unit, build. Paste the command output summary. |
| 5 | Never break one thing fixing another. Run the full unit suite after every fix, not just the new test. |
| 6 | Fix in code, not in data. No SQL patches as fixes. |
| 7 | One topic per thread. End every thread by updating `docs/HANDOFF.md`. |
| 8 | Push only changed files. No whole-tree rewrites, no formatter-only churn in feature PRs. |

## Stack conventions (summary; full text in giri-skills `shared/stack-conventions.md`)
- Data access only via `lib/db` or `server/services`. No Supabase calls in components.
- RLS on every table. Service-role key only server-side. Never `NEXT_PUBLIC_` a secret.
- zod at every boundary (`server/validators`). Services return `Result<T, E>`; never throw across server/client.
- Structured JSON logs via `lib/logger`; no `console.log` in committed code.
- One migration per change, forward-only, with `-- rollback:` block. Never edit an applied migration.
- Tests: unit (vitest) for services/validators; integration for `lib/db` against local Supabase; e2e (playwright) for critical paths. Coverage ≥ 80% on `server/`.

## Gates
```
plan → approve → build → test → verify → handoff
```
A step is not done until its gate output exists (plan table, "go", passing test run, HANDOFF entry).

## Where things live
| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/SPEC.md` |
| Decisions | `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md` |
| Thread state | `docs/HANDOFF.md` |
| Env contract | `.env.example` |
| CI | `.github/workflows/{ci,preview,prod}.yml` |

## Do not
- Commit secrets, `.env*` files, or generated types with secrets.
- Add dependencies without stating why in the PR.
- Skip the migration rollback block.
- Use `any` to silence the type checker.

# ci.yml — lint → typecheck → unit → build on every PR and push to main.
# Required status check name: "ci / lint-typecheck-test"
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  NODE_VERSION: "20"

jobs:
  lint-typecheck-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm test -- --coverage
      - name: Coverage gate (server/ >= 80%)
        run: node -e "const s=require('./coverage/coverage-summary.json').total; if (s.lines.pct<80){console.error('coverage',s.lines.pct);process.exit(1)}"
      - name: Build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: http://localhost:54321
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ci-placeholder
          NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: http://localhost:3000
          SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: ci-placeholder
        run: npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: coverage/
          retention-days: 7

  rls-lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: RLS lint (fails on tables without RLS or policies without tenant predicate)
        run: python3 -I scripts/rls_lint.py supabase/migrations --client-dirs app components lib/supabase/browser.ts

  secrets-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Block committed env files
        run: |
          if git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)\.env(\.local|\.production|\.staging)?$'; then
            echo "::error::.env file committed"; exit 1; fi
      - name: Block NEXT_PUBLIC_ service role
        run: |
          if grep -rnE 'NEXT_PUBLIC_[A-Z_]*SERVICE_ROLE' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.env.example' . ; then
            echo "::error::service role key exposed as NEXT_PUBLIC_"; exit 1; fi

# preview.yml — deploy a Vercel preview for the PR and run Playwright e2e against it.
# Required status check name: "preview / e2e"
name: preview

on:
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  deployments: write

env:
  VERCEL_ORG_ID: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
  VERCEL_PROJECT_ID: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }}

jobs:
  deploy-preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    outputs:
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm i -g vercel@latest
      - run: vercel pull --yes --environment=preview --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - run: vercel build --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - id: deploy
        run: |
          URL=$(vercel deploy --prebuilt --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }})
          echo "url=$URL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Comment preview URL
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const url = '${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}';
            const body = `Preview: ${url}`;
            const {data: comments} = await github.rest.issues.listComments({...context.repo, issue_number: context.issue.number});
            const prev = comments.find(c => c.body.startsWith('Preview: '));
            if (prev) await github.rest.issues.updateComment({...context.repo, comment_id: prev.id, body});
            else await github.rest.issues.createComment({...context.repo, issue_number: context.issue.number, body});

  e2e:
    needs: deploy-preview
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Playwright against preview
        env:
          BASE_URL: ${{ needs.deploy-preview.outputs.url }}
          VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET }}
          E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
          E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
        run: npm run test:e2e
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

# prod.yml — production release on tag vX.Y.Z: migrate staging → smoke → migrate prod → deploy → smoke.
# Rollback: see references/rollback.md. Requires GitHub Environments "staging" and "production"
# (production with required reviewers).
name: prod

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]

concurrency:
  group: prod
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  deployments: write

env:
  VERCEL_ORG_ID: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
  VERCEL_PROJECT_ID: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }}

jobs:
  verify-tag:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Tag must point at main
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main || { echo "::error::tag not on main"; exit 1; }

  migrate-staging:
    needs: verify-tag
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1
        with:
          version: latest
      - run: supabase link --project-ref ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF_STAGING }}
        env:
          SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
      - run: supabase db push
        env:
          SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD_STAGING }}

  migrate-prod:
    needs: migrate-staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production   # required reviewers gate lives here
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1
        with:
          version: latest
      - run: supabase link --project-ref ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF_PROD }}
        env:
          SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
      - run: supabase db push
        env:
          SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD_PROD }}

  deploy-prod:
    needs: migrate-prod
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    timeout-minutes: 20
    outputs:
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm i -g vercel@latest
      - run: vercel pull --yes --environment=production --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - run: vercel build --prod --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - id: deploy
        run: |
          URL=$(vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }})
          echo "url=$URL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Smoke — health endpoints
        run: |
          set -e
          curl -fsS "${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}/api/health" | grep -q '"status":"ok"'
          curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN }}" "${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}/api/health/deep" | grep -q '"status":"ok"'
      - name: GitHub release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          generate_release_notes: true

# Bootstrap Checklist (Next.js + Supabase + Vercel)

Every row ends Done, Skipped (reason), or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## A. Repo docs (scaffold writes these)
| # | File | Purpose | Done |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `docs/SPEC.md` | What we are building; scope; NFRs; tenancy | |
| A2 | `CLAUDE.md` | How we work in this repo: commands, conventions, gates | |
| A3 | `docs/HANDOFF.md` | Where we are; next-thread prompt | |
| A4 | `docs/adr/0000-template.md` | ADR template | |
| A5 | `docs/adr/0001-stack.md` | Stack decision + deviations | |
| A6 | `.env.example` | Env contract — every var documented, no values | |
| A7 | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | lint → typecheck → unit → build on PR | |
| A8 | `.github/workflows/preview.yml` | Vercel preview + e2e on PR | |
| A9 | `.github/workflows/prod.yml` | Tag-triggered prod deploy with migrations | |
| A10 | `.github/CODEOWNERS` | Review ownership | |
| A11 | `.github/pull_request_template.md` | PR checklist with gates | |

## B. App skeleton (create with the framework CLI, not by hand)
| # | Item | Command / note | Done |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Next.js app (App Router, TS, ESLint, Tailwind, `src/` off) | `npx create-next-app@latest <name> --ts --eslint --tailwind --app --no-src-dir --import-alias "@/*"` | |
| B2 | Folder layout per `shared/stack-conventions.md` | `mkdir -p components/ui components/features lib/supabase lib/db lib/utils server/actions server/services server/validators supabase/migrations tests/unit tests/e2e tests/fixtures` | |
| B3 | `env.ts` zod parser at boot | `lib/env.ts`; import in `next.config.ts` to fail fast | |
| B4 | Supabase clients | `lib/supabase/server.ts` (cookies), `lib/supabase/browser.ts` (anon only) | |
| B5 | Logger | copy `observability-setup/assets/logger.ts` → `lib/logger.ts` | |
| B6 | Result type | `lib/result.ts` — see `nextjs-enterprise-conventions/references/error-result-pattern.md` | |
| B7 | Vitest + Playwright | copy configs from `test-strategy-tdd/assets/` | |
| B8 | `package.json` scripts | `dev, build, lint, typecheck, test, test:e2e, db:migrate, db:reset, db:types` | |

## C. Supabase
| # | Item | Note | Done |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `supabase init` + `supabase start` locally | local stack before any remote | |
| C2 | Project per environment: dev (local), staging, prod | never share prod DB with preview | |
| C3 | First migration: `0001_init.sql` with tenancy tables + RLS enabled | use `supabase-schema-rls` | |
| C4 | `supabase gen types typescript --local > lib/db/types.ts` wired to `db:types` | | |
| C5 | Service-role key stored only in Vercel server env | never `NEXT_PUBLIC_` | |

## D. Vercel
| # | Item | Note | Done |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Project linked to GitHub repo | `vercel link` | |
| D2 | Env vars per environment (Development / Preview / Production) | match `.env.example` exactly | |
| D3 | Production branch = `main`; prod deploys only from tag workflow | disable auto-prod on push | |
| D4 | Preview protection (Vercel Authentication) on | | |
| D5 | `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_ORG_ID`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` as GitHub secrets | | |

## E. GitHub
| # | Item | Note | Done |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Branch protection on `main` | see `branch-rules.md` | |
| E2 | Required checks: `ci / lint-typecheck-test`, `preview / e2e` | | |
| E3 | Secrets: Vercel trio, `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD`, `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF_STAGING/PROD` | | |
| E4 | Dependabot or Renovate enabled (weekly, grouped) | | |
| E5 | Secret scanning + push protection on | | |

## F. Definition of "bootstrapped"
- `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` passes locally.
- Opening a PR triggers `ci.yml` and `preview.yml`; both green.
- `docs/HANDOFF.md` contains the next-thread prompt for the first feature.

# Branch, PR and Release Rules

## Branch model
| Branch | Purpose | Deploys to | Protected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | Always releasable | Preview (auto) → Production (tag only) | yes |
| `feat/<ticket>-<slug>` | One feature or task | Vercel preview per PR | no |
| `fix/<ticket>-<slug>` | One bug | Vercel preview per PR | no |
| `chore/<slug>` | Deps, CI, docs | preview | no |
| `hotfix/<slug>` | Prod fix branched from the prod tag | preview → tag | no |

No long-lived `develop`/`staging` branches. Staging = the preview deployment of `main`.

## Naming
- Commits: Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`). Scope optional: `feat(auth): …`.
- Tags: `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` on `main` only. Tag = prod release.
- PR title = squash commit message.

## PR rules
| Rule | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| Squash merge only; linear history | branch protection |
| ≥1 approving review; CODEOWNERS review for `supabase/`, `server/`, `.github/` | branch protection + CODEOWNERS |
| Required checks green: `ci`, `preview / e2e` | branch protection |
| PR template checklist completed (tests, migration rollback, env vars, HANDOFF) | review |
| No PR > ~400 changed lines without a stated reason | review |
| Migrations never edited after merge; new migration instead | review + `rls_lint.py` |

## `gh` commands (run after approval; replace `<owner>/<repo>`)
```bash
# Protect main: PR required, 1 review, code-owner review, required checks, linear history, no force-push
gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  --input - <<'JSON'
{
  "required_status_checks": {"strict": true, "contexts": ["ci / lint-typecheck-test", "preview / e2e"]},
  "enforce_admins": true,
  "required_pull_request_reviews": {"required_approving_review_count": 1, "require_code_owner_reviews": true, "dismiss_stale_reviews": true},
  "restrictions": null,
  "required_linear_history": true,
  "allow_force_pushes": false,
  "allow_deletions": false,
  "required_conversation_resolution": true
}
JSON

# Squash-only merges
gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo> -f allow_merge_commit=false -f allow_rebase_merge=false -f allow_squash_merge=true -f delete_branch_on_merge=true

# Secret scanning + push protection
gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo> --input - <<'JSON'
{"security_and_analysis": {"secret_scanning": {"status": "enabled"}, "secret_scanning_push_protection": {"status": "enabled"}}}
JSON

# Required secrets (values from Vercel / Supabase dashboards; never paste into chat)
gh secret set VERCEL_TOKEN
gh secret set VERCEL_ORG_ID
gh secret set VERCEL_PROJECT_ID
gh secret set SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
gh secret set SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD
gh secret set SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF_STAGING
gh secret set SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF_PROD
```

## Release flow
1. Merge PRs to `main` → preview deploy of `main` is staging.
2. Verify staging (smoke e2e in `preview.yml` already ran).
3. `git tag v1.4.0 && git push origin v1.4.0` → `prod.yml` runs migrations then deploys.
4. Rollback: see `ci-cd-vercel-github/references/rollback.md`.

skills/build/safe-fix/SKILL.md:
---
name: safe-fix
description: Use when the user reports a bug or says "fix this" — an error, stack trace, failing test, wrong behaviour, "works in staging not prod". Produces a reproduction, an isolated root cause with evidence, a minimal diff that touches only the failing path, a regression test that fails before and passes after, and full-suite verification — never collateral breakage, never data patches. Wraps superpowers systematic-debugging plus Karpathy-style guardrails when installed. Not for features (use spec-to-plan) or security findings without a repro (use security-review).
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: build
  adlc_stage: improve
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  fits:
    stacks: [any]
    request_kinds: [fix]
  agent:
    inputs:
      - {name: target, type: dir, required: true, from: "repo directory the test command runs in"}
      - {name: cmd, type: string, required: true, from: "the full test command, e.g. \"python3 -m pytest -q\" or \"npx vitest run\""}
      - {name: baseline, type: json, required: false, from: "baseline.json recorded by `safefix.py baseline` before the fix; without it the baseline is taken now (pre-fix state)"}
    run:
      - {step: baseline, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/safefix.py baseline --target {target} --cmd {cmd} --out {out}/baseline.json", skip_if_present: [baseline]}
      - {step: verify, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/safefix.py verify --target {target} --cmd {cmd} [--baseline {baseline}] --out {out}/verify.json"}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/verify.json", checks: [exists, json, contains:"collateral"]}
    modes:
      existing: {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "your repo, its test command and the fix you made"}
---

# safe-fix

## In a conversation: work the fix now
- **The bug report carries a symptom and evidence** (environment, `requestId`, error text, "after yesterday's release"): answer **in this reply** with the fix plan, in order: (1) evidence — what to pull by `requestId` (Vercel logs, Supabase logs, Sentry event) and what each would confirm, plus the release diff to read if it followed a release; (2) the failing reproduction written before any change — the exact test (e.g. an integration test with the affected persona) and why it fails today; (3) the root cause in one sentence with file:line and its evidence, or, until the evidence is in, the ranked hypotheses (e.g. RLS policy predicate, missing JWT claim) and the evidence that settles each; (4) the minimal diff to the failing path only — no renames, no reformatting; (5) the regression test named after the bug (`it('does not <bug> when <condition>')`), seen red on the pre-fix code by stashing the fix; (6) verification — lint, typecheck, full unit suite, affected integration/e2e, build, and a grep of every caller of the changed code; (7) blast radius and rollback (revert the commit or Vercel Instant Rollback; a down-migration if schema changed). Facts you cannot see (paths, log lines) are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, never invented. Never reply with only a request for logs.
- **Asked to change shared code the quick way** (e.g. "just change formatMoney"): grep the callers first and list them; when other callers (e.g. UI) rely on the current behaviour, decline the shared change in one line, fix the failing path instead (a dedicated formatter or a parser option on the export), add a regression test for that path, run the tests that cover the shared function, and state the blast radius explicitly.
- **Too little to reproduce** ("sometimes the save button does nothing"): ask once, in one list, for environment, exact steps, browser, a `requestId` or logs; do not guess-fix. Say what follows if the evidence still gives no repro: targeted, `requestId`-tagged logging at the suspected hops ships first, then the repro and the fix. Never weaken, skip or delete a test to get green.
- **Asked to ship because the one target test passes**: decline in one line — the full suite decides, and any test that was green and is now red is collateral that blocks the fix.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — the test suite is snapshotted before the fix (or your recorded baseline is used), re-run after it, and any test that was green and is now red is reported as collateral damage.
- Only for existing: a fix always lands in code and a test suite that already exist; there is nothing to fix from scratch.

## When to use
- "Fix this bug", an error message, stack trace, failing CI job, "it used to work", production incident follow-up.
- NOT for: new behaviour (`spec-to-plan`), "clean this up" (`nextjs-enterprise-conventions`), pipeline-only failures (`ci-cd-vercel-github` troubleshooting), vulnerability review (`security-review`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Observed behaviour + expected behaviour | yes | user |
| Evidence: error text, stack, failing test name, `requestId`, logs, steps | yes (at least one) | user / logs |
| Environment where it happens (local / preview / prod) and version/sha | yes | user — ask once |
| Repo access | yes | repo |

Missing facts do not stop the fix plan: mark them `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and ask at the end. Only when there is no evidence at all to reproduce from, ask once for it and do not guess-fix.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md` (rules 2, 8, 9, 10 govern this skill) and `references/never-collateral.md`.
2. **Reproduce.** Write the smallest deterministic reproduction: a failing unit/integration test, or an exact command/request. If it cannot be reproduced, stop and gather more evidence (`references/safe-fix-method.md` §Reproduce). No fix without a repro. *(gate: repro exists and fails)*
3. **Isolate.** If the upstream skill `superpowers:systematic-debugging` is installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke it for this step; otherwise follow `references/safe-fix-method.md` §Isolate: trace from symptom to cause with evidence at each hop, bisect (git / inputs / layers), state the root cause in one sentence with file:line. Distinguish root cause from trigger.
4. **Plan the fix.** Post: root cause, the single path to change, files touched (expect 1–3), the regression test, blast radius (who else calls this), rollback. Wait for "go" if the fix touches shared code, schema, auth, or >3 files. *(gate: plan→approve)*
5. **Minimal diff.** Change only the failing path. No renames, no reformatting, no "while I'm here". If the fix needs a refactor, do the refactor as a separate, behaviour-preserving step with the suite green in between.
6. **Regression test.** The repro from step 2 becomes a permanent test named after the bug (`it('does not <bug> when <condition>')`). It must fail on the pre-fix code (verify by stashing the fix once) and pass after. *(gate: build→test)*
7. **Verify the whole, not the part.** Run lint, typecheck, the full unit suite, affected integration/e2e, and build. Re-check every caller of the changed function (grep) for changed assumptions. *(gate: test→verify)*
8. **Fix in code, not data.** If the bug produced bad rows, handle the scenario in code going forward and write a one-off, reviewed migration/backfill for the existing rows — never hand-edit data as the fix.
9. Report with `assets/fix-report.md`; update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Form |
|---|---|
| Root cause statement | one sentence, file:line, evidence |
| Diff | minimal; 1–3 files typical |
| Regression test | `tests/**`, named after the bug |
| Verification | command summary table |
| Fix report | `assets/fix-report.md` filled, in PR description |

## Self-check
- [ ] Repro existed and failed before the change
- [ ] Root cause stated with evidence (not "probably")
- [ ] Diff touches only the failing path; no formatting/renames/unrelated edits
- [ ] Regression test fails on old code, passes on new
- [ ] Full suite green; callers of changed code re-checked
- [ ] No data patched by hand; no `any`, no try/catch swallow, no test skipped or weakened
- [ ] Rollback stated

## References
- `references/safe-fix-method.md` — reproduce → isolate → minimal diff → regression test → verify, with techniques
- `references/never-collateral.md` — the guardrails (what a fix may never do)
- `references/common-bugs-stack.md` — recurring causes in Next.js/Supabase/Vercel apps
- `assets/fix-report.md` — report template
- `scripts/safefix.py` — `baseline` / `verify`: snapshots the test suite before a fix and fails (exit 1) on any newly failing test

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/safe-fix --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/safe-fix`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Typical flow: run once before the fix (writes `baseline.json`), apply the fix, run again with `--input baseline=<dir>/baseline.json`; any newly failing test is collateral and the run exits 1.
# Fix — {{TITLE}} — {{DATE}}

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Symptom | |
| Environment / version | prod / preview / local · sha |
| Evidence | error text · requestId · failing test |
| Root cause | `<file:line>` does X when Y because Z |

# Never-Collateral Rules

Adopted from the token-efficiency rules (fix-don't-redo, verify-before-done, fix-in-code) and Karpathy-style guardrails (no assumptions, minimal diffs, verify before claiming).

| # | Rule | Violation looks like | Instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No fix without a reproduction | "I think this is it, try now" | failing test or command first |
| 2 | Read before writing | editing a file from memory of its contents | open it; read callers |
| 3 | One root cause, one diff | fixing three "suspicious" things at once | confirm the cause; change that one thing |
| 4 | Touch only the failing path | reformatting, renaming, moving code, upgrading deps in the fix PR | separate PR with suite green between |
| 5 | Never weaken a test to pass | `.skip`, loosened assertions, widened types, `any`, `// @ts-ignore`, `catch {}` | fix the code the test guards |
| 6 | Never fix in data | SQL `update` in prod console; hand-edited rows | code handles the scenario; reviewed backfill migration |
| 7 | Run the whole suite, not the one test | "the new test passes" | lint + typecheck + full unit + build; affected e2e |
| 8 | Re-check every caller of changed code | changing a function signature/semantics without grepping | grep; read; adjust or add tests |
| 9 | Don't change behaviour you weren't asked to | "also made it faster", "also handles nulls now" | note it under "parked"; separate PR |
| 10 | No new dependency to fix a bug | adding a library for one guard | stdlib / existing utils |
| 11 | No silent fallbacks | `?? defaultValue` that hides the failure | fail loudly with a typed error; log with requestId |
| 12 | Say what you verified, exactly | "should work now" | command + result table |
| 13 | Stashed-fix check for the regression test | test written after fix, never seen failing | stash, run, see red, pop |
| 14 | Rollback stated | none | redeploy previous tag / flag off / revert migration |
| 15 | Stop when the fix grows | diff > 3 files or > ~60 lines | back to plan gate; it may be a feature or refactor |

## The "would this break something else?" check (run before claiming done)
1. What else calls this? (grep) — read each caller's expectation.
2. What else reads this data/shape? (types, DB columns, API consumers)
3. What was the old behaviour relied on by a test or a UI branch? (run sibling tests)
4. Is there a feature flag, env, or tenant branch that takes the other path? (test that path too)
5. Does the change alter a migration, policy, or env contract? (if yes → supabase-schema-rls / security-review gates apply)
If any answer is "not sure", find out before returning.

# Safe-Fix Method (fallback for superpowers:systematic-debugging)

## 1. Reproduce
| Technique | When |
|---|---|
| Failing unit test with the exact input | logic bugs; preferred form |
| Integration test against local Supabase with seed persona | RLS, query, auth bugs |
| `curl` / Playwright script with recorded request | route handlers, actions, prod-only |
| Replay from logs by `requestId` | prod incidents — pull the log lines, rebuild inputs |
| Env parity check | "works locally": diff `.env.example` vs Vercel env; node version; `VERCEL_ENV` branches in code |

Rules: deterministic (fixed time, seed, ids); minimal (strip inputs until it stops failing, then add the last one back); recorded (the test file or the command is in the report).
If no repro after 30 min: write down what was tried, add targeted logging (`log.debug` with ids, behind `LOG_LEVEL`), ship that, wait for the next occurrence. Do not guess-fix.

## 2. Isolate
| Step | Do |
|---|---|
| Read the error literally | the message names the file:line and the value. Read that line and its inputs before theorising. |
| Trace backwards | from the failing line to where the bad value was produced; cite file:line at each hop |
| Bisect | `git bisect run <repro>` between last-good tag and HEAD; or bisect inputs; or bisect layers (replace service with stub → does page still fail?) |
| Differential | what differs between working and failing case: env, role, tenant, data shape, time, concurrency |
| Confirm | change one thing that your hypothesis says will fix it (even a temporary hack) → repro passes → hypothesis confirmed. Then revert the hack and do the real fix. |

Root cause sentence: "`<file:line>` does X when Y because Z; the symptom appears at `<file:line>`." Trigger ≠ cause: "deploy on Tuesday" is the trigger; "unawaited promise in service" is the cause.

## 3. Minimal diff
| Allowed | Not allowed |
|---|---|
| change the broken expression / branch / guard | reformat the file |
| add a missing `await`, null check, tenant filter, `with check` | rename variables "for clarity" |
| add a zod rule | restructure the module |
| add one helper if the fix needs it twice | move code between files |
| extend an existing test file | delete or `.skip` tests |

Litmus: every changed line is explained by the root cause sentence. If not, it is a separate PR.

## 4. Regression test
- Name after the bug: `it('keeps tenant filter when status filter is empty (#412)')`.
- Place next to existing tests for that unit.
- Verify it fails on old code: `git stash` the fix → run → fails → `git stash pop` → run → passes. Say so in the report.
- For prod incidents, also add the e2e if the path is critical.

## 5. Verify the whole
| Check | Command |
|---|---|
| lint | `npm run lint` |
| typecheck | `npm run typecheck` |
| full unit | `npm test` |
| integration (if db/rls touched) | `npm test -- --project integration` |
| e2e for touched path | `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/<flow>.spec.ts` |
| build | `npm run build` |
| callers | `grep -rn "<changedFn>(" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx .` → read each |
| behaviour of adjacent branches | run the sibling tests of the unit; manual check of the opposite case |

Paste the summary table in the report. "Tests pass" without the command is not verification.

## 6. Data produced by the bug
1. Fix the code (above).
2. Quantify: `select count(*) …` of affected rows (read-only).
3. Write a reviewed backfill migration (idempotent, batched) per `supabase-schema-rls/references/migration-format.md`.
4. Test on staging with a copy; apply via release.
Never: `update` from a SQL console as "the fix".

## 7. Report
Use `assets/fix-report.md`. Keep it to one screen.

# security-review

## In a conversation: review now
- **The change is described or pasted** (a PR summary, a diff, a route handler, "takes tenantId from the query string and uses the admin client"): write the review **in this reply**. Start with the **surface inventory** (changed files grouped by surface: route handlers, server actions, middleware, policies, client components, env, external calls, and what each trusts), then the **findings table, worst first**: severity (reachability × impact, e.g. Critical = R2 × I3), title, trace entry → sink with file:line at each hop (`route.ts:12 → services/x.ts:30 → admin client → invoices`), impact, fix, test. For each Critical/High add a short exploit sketch and the fix in code: tenant from the session, the cookie-bound (RLS) client instead of the admin client, an authz guard, plus a negative regression test that fails before the fix. State "Report written from `assets/review-report.md` → `docs/security/<date>-<scope>.md`" and lay the reply out on its sections: Findings (worst first) · Threat model record · Surfaces reviewed · Verification · Out of scope / parked.
- **The diff lands in an existing repo and the user wants the surrounding code checked**: review the diff and, in the same table, the callers, handlers and components it touches — name each file reviewed so the threat-model record shows full coverage; existing issues (e.g. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on content from the database) are rated like new ones and marked "existing".
- **Nothing security-relevant changed** (CSS, README, copy): line 1 "No security-relevant surface changed." then the surface inventory table that proves it (`| File | Surface | Trusts | Security-relevant? |`, every surface category listed as "none"). Do not invent generic findings (rate limiting, headers) the change does not touch.
- **No diff, PR or scope at all** ("is our app secure?", "review my change"): ask once for the diff or PR and the trust model (roles, tenancy, public endpoints). Do not produce a generic checklist.
- **A diff file is attached**: name the command and outputs first — `python3 -I scripts/scan.py --diff change.patch [--target <repo>] --findings findings.csv --report review.md --final security-review.md` — then the result: findings by severity (or "no critical/high findings"), the gate line (`scan.py --gate findings.csv`: "gate passes (exit 0)" or "gate fails (exit 1): critical/high remains"), and the review filled from the findings (surfaces scanned, threat model, verification). A clean diff (validated server action, parameterised query) is not padded with findings.
- **Asked to approve with a known secret or bypass left in** ("the token is fine to keep in code"): the finding stays Critical/High and the review is not approved; give the fix (move the secret to server env, rotate it).

## Starting points
- **New** — the diff of a new feature is scanned on its added lines; the model step writes the traced review, or with `draft_only` the review record is written from the scan alone, labelled as a draft.
- **Existing** — add `target` (the repo the change lands in): the existing code is scanned in full as well, so callers, handlers and components around the change are covered, and each file appears in the threat-model record.

## When to use
- "Review this before merge", "is this safe", PR touching auth, tenancy, server actions, route handlers, migrations, env, file upload, external calls.
- Release gate: every tag.
- NOT for: writing policies (`supabase-schema-rls`), general code quality (`nextjs-enterprise-conventions`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Diff / PR / file list | yes | user / `git diff main...HEAD` |
| Trust model: roles, tenancy, public endpoints | yes | `docs/SPEC.md`, RBAC matrix — ask once if absent |
| Repo access for reading callers and policies | yes | repo |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` (Auth, Secrets, Multi-tenant rows), `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`, and `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. **Scope.** List changed files grouped by surface: server actions, route handlers, middleware, migrations/policies, client components, env/CI, external calls. Note what each surface trusts. *(gate: plan)*
3. **Threat model per change.** If the upstream skill `security-review` is installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke it for this step with the stack context from `references/stack-specifics.md`; otherwise follow `references/review-method.md`: for each change ask who can reach it, what they control, what it touches, what the worst outcome is, which control stops it, and whether that control is actually in the diff or only assumed.
4. **Trace, don't pattern-match.** For every finding, follow the data from entry point to sink and cite file:line at each hop. A finding without a trace is a question, not a finding.
5. **Rate** each finding with `references/severity-rubric.md` (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info) using reachability × impact. Post the findings table; agree fixes with the user before changing code. *(gate: plan→approve)*
6. **Fix in code** — minimal diffs, following `safe-fix` rules; add a regression test per Critical/High (negative case that fails before the fix). *(gate: build→test)*
7. **Verify.** Re-run the trace for each fixed finding, run `rls_lint.py`, full unit suite, lint. Confirm no new surface was opened by the fix. *(gate: test→verify)*
8. Report with `assets/review-report.md`; update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Form |
|---|---|
| Findings table | severity, title, trace (entry → sink), impact, fix, test |
| Fixes | minimal diffs |
| Regression tests | `tests/**` |
| Report | `docs/security/<date>-<scope>.md` from `assets/review-report.md` |

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/security-review --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/security-review`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. The scan always writes its findings and the review step reasons on them; the gate check then fails the run (exit 1) when any critical/high finding remains, so a risky diff is reported, never waved through.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every finding has an entry→sink trace with file:line
- [ ] Every server action and route handler in scope: input parsed, authz checked, tenant from session
- [ ] RLS: new/changed tables have policies; `with check` on writes; no `user_metadata` claims
- [ ] No secret in client bundle, logs, or repo; `NEXT_PUBLIC_` audit done
- [ ] External calls: allow-listed hosts, timeouts, no user-controlled URLs (SSRF)
- [ ] Critical/High have a failing-then-passing regression test
- [ ] Fix diffs touched only the vulnerable path (no collateral)

## References
- `references/review-method.md` — threat-model questions per change type, trace discipline (fallback for sentry)
- `references/stack-specifics.md` — Next.js server actions, Supabase RLS/service-role, Vercel env pitfalls
- `references/severity-rubric.md` — rating rules and SLA
- `assets/review-report.md` — report template
- `scripts/scan.py` — diff/repo scanner for SEC1–SEC6 (auth, injection, secrets, SSRF, XSS, RLS bypass) → findings.csv; `--gate` fails on critical/high
