#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scan a diff or a repo for the stack's security pitfalls; findings feed the reasoning step.

    python3 -I scripts/scan.py --diff change.patch --findings findings.csv --report review.md
    python3 -I scripts/scan.py --target <repo> --findings findings.csv --report review.md
    python3 -I scripts/scan.py --gate findings.csv        # exit 1 if any critical/high finding
    ... --final security-review.md --draft-only           # no model step: the review record from the scan

Detectors (file:line evidence; secrets are redacted in the evidence column):
  SEC1 action-without-auth      high      "use server" file exporting async functions with no
                                          auth.getUser / getSession / requireUser / requireRole anywhere in the file
  SEC2 raw-sql-interpolation    critical  sql`…${plain}` (a ${helper(x)} call is treated as parameterised),
                                          query(`…${…}`), "select … " + variable
  SEC3 secret-in-code           critical  sk-…, JWT (eyJ….), AWS AKIA… literals
  SEC4 ssrf-user-url            high      fetch(<identifier>) — URL is a variable, not a literal (heuristic)
  SEC5 dangerous-html           medium    dangerouslySetInnerHTML
  SEC6 rls-bypass-in-handler    high      service-role client used in a route handler or server action
With --diff only added lines are scanned (--target adds a full-repo scan) (context lines count for the auth check). Writes
findings.csv (id, category, severity, file, line, evidence, recommendation) and review.md.
Exit 0 after writing (findings or not); the gate is a separate call so an LLM step can reason on
the findings first. Exit 1 on bad input or in --gate mode when critical/high findings exist. Stdlib.
--draft-only --final <path>: writes the review record on the assets/review-report.md sections (Findings,
Threat model record, Surfaces reviewed, Verification) from the scan alone, labelled as a draft: findings
are scanner candidates (not traced entry → sink), and every judgement the scan cannot make — trust model,
trace, regression test — is an owned to-be-baselined marker.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

EXTS = {".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".sql"}
SKIP_DIRS = {"node_modules", ".next", "dist", "build", "coverage", ".git"}
SEV_ORDER = {"critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 3}

USE_SERVER = re.compile(r"^\s*['\"]use server['\"]")
EXPORT_FN = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*export\s+(?:default\s+)?async\s+function\b|^[ \t]*export\s+const\s+\w+\s*=\s*async\b")
AUTH_CHECK = re.compile(r"auth\.getUser\(|getSession\(|requireUser\(|requireRole\(|getClaims\(")
RAW_SQL = re.compile(r"sql`[^`]*\$\{\s*[^}(]*\}|\.(?:query|execute|raw|unsafe)\(\s*`[^`]*\$\{|"
                     r"['\"]\s*(?:select|insert|update|delete)\b[^'\"]*['\"]\s*\+\s*[A-Za-z_]", re.I)
SECRETS = [re.compile(r"\bsk-(?:ant-|live_|test_|proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}"),
           re.compile(r"\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{5,}"),
           re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")]
FETCH_VAR = re.compile(r"\bfetch\(\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$.]*)\s*[,)]")
DANGEROUS_HTML = re.compile(r"dangerouslySetInnerHTML")
SERVICE_ROLE = re.compile(r"SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE|createServiceClient\(|createAdminClient\(|serviceRoleClient|service_role")
HTTP_EXPORT = re.compile(r"^\s*export\s+(?:async\s+)?function\s+(GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)\b|"
                         r"^\s*export\s+const\s+(GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)\s*=", re.M)
RECOMMEND = {
    "SEC1": "Call requireUser()/requireRole() (or supabase.auth.getUser()) before any work; derive tenant from the session, never from input.",
    "SEC2": "Use parameterised queries (sql`… ${sql(param)}` tagged helper or the query builder); never concatenate user input into SQL.",
    "SEC3": "Remove the literal, rotate the credential, load it from env (Vercel/Supabase secrets) and add a secrets-scan CI step.",
    "SEC4": "Allow-list hosts, build the URL from a constant base + validated path, set a timeout; never fetch a user-supplied URL.",
    "SEC5": "Sanitise with a vetted library or render as text; if HTML is unavoidable, restrict to trusted authors and sanitise server-side.",
    "SEC6": "Use the RLS-scoped user client in request handlers; service-role only in jobs/webhooks after explicit validation.",
}
CATEGORY = {"SEC1": "authz", "SEC2": "injection", "SEC3": "secrets", "SEC4": "ssrf", "SEC5": "xss", "SEC6": "rls-bypass"}
SEVERITY = {"SEC1": "high", "SEC2": "critical", "SEC3": "critical", "SEC4": "high", "SEC5": "medium", "SEC6": "high"}


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ inputs

def parse_diff(text: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """{path: {"added": [(line_no, text)], "all": [text]}} from a unified diff."""
    files, cur, new_ln = {}, None, 0
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if raw.startswith("+++ "):
            path = raw[4:].strip()
            path = path[2:] if path.startswith("b/") else path
            cur = files.setdefault(path, {"added": [], "all": []}) if path != "/dev/null" else None
            continue
        if raw.startswith("--- ") or raw.startswith("diff ") or raw.startswith("index "):
            continue
        if raw.startswith("@@"):
            m = re.search(r"\+(\d+)", raw)
            new_ln = int(m.group(1)) if m else 1
            continue
        if cur is None:
            continue
        if raw.startswith("+"):
            cur["added"].append((new_ln, raw[1:]))
            cur["all"].append(raw[1:])
            new_ln += 1
        elif raw.startswith("-"):
            continue
        else:
            cur["all"].append(raw[1:] if raw.startswith(" ") else raw)
            new_ln += 1
    return files


def walk_repo(root: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    files = {}
    for p in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
        if not p.is_file() or p.suffix not in EXTS:
            continue
        rel = p.relative_to(root)
        if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in rel.parts[:-1]):
            continue
        lines = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
        files[rel.as_posix()] = {"added": list(enumerate(lines, 1)), "all": lines}
    return files


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ detectors

def redact(s: str) -> str:
    return s[:8] + "…[redacted]" if len(s) > 8 else "…[redacted]"


def is_handler(path: str, full: str) -> bool:
    name = path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return (path.startswith("app/") and name.startswith("route.")) or "/actions/" in path or \
        path.startswith("server/actions/") or bool(USE_SERVER.search(full)) or bool(HTTP_EXPORT.search(full))


def scan_file(path: str, info: dict) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    full = "\n".join(info["all"])
    ext = Path(path).suffix

    def add(rule, ln, evidence):
        out.append({"id": "", "category": CATEGORY[rule], "rule": rule, "severity": SEVERITY[rule], "file": path,
                    "line": ln, "evidence": evidence.strip()[:140], "recommendation": RECOMMEND[rule]})

    server_action = bool(USE_SERVER.search(full)) and not AUTH_CHECK.search(full)
    handler = is_handler(path, full) if ext != ".sql" else False
    for ln, text in info["added"]:
        if server_action and EXPORT_FN.search(text):
            add("SEC1", ln, text)
        if RAW_SQL.search(text):
            add("SEC2", ln, text)
        for rx in SECRETS:
            for m in rx.finditer(text):
                add("SEC3", ln, text.replace(m.group(0), redact(m.group(0))))
        if ext != ".sql":
            m = FETCH_VAR.search(text)
            if m and not m.group(1).startswith("process.env"):
                add("SEC4", ln, text)
            if DANGEROUS_HTML.search(text):
                add("SEC5", ln, text)
            if handler and SERVICE_ROLE.search(text):
                add("SEC6", ln, text)
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ outputs

def write_outputs(findings: list[dict], fpath: Path, rpath: Path, scope: str, n_files: int) -> None:
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: (SEV_ORDER.get(f["severity"], 9), f["file"], f["line"]))
    for i, f in enumerate(findings, 1):
        f["id"] = f"F{i:02d}"
    fpath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rpath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with fpath.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "category", "severity", "file", "line", "evidence", "recommendation"],
                           extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(findings)
    counts = {s: sum(1 for f in findings if f["severity"] == s) for s in SEV_ORDER}
    gate = "BLOCK" if counts["critical"] or counts["high"] else "MERGE (no critical/high findings from the scanner)"
    lines = [f"# Security scan — {scope}", "",
             f"**{len(findings)} finding(s) across {n_files} file(s): "
             f"{counts['critical']} critical, {counts['high']} high, {counts['medium']} medium, {counts['low']} low. "
             f"Scanner verdict: {gate}.**", "",
             "## Findings", "", "| # | Sev | Category | File:line | Evidence | Recommendation |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for f in findings:
        ev = f["evidence"].replace("|", "\\|")
        lines.append(f"| {f['id']} | {f['severity']} | {f['category']} ({f['rule']}) | `{f['file']}:{f['line']}` | `{ev}` | {f['recommendation']} |")
    if not findings:
        lines.append("| — | — | — | — | no findings | — |")
    lines += ["", "## Surfaces scanned", "", "| Surface | Files |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in surfaces(findings, n_files).items()]
    lines += ["", "## Method and limits", "",
              "- Pattern scan on added lines (diff mode) or all source lines (repo mode); every finding carries file:line.",
              "- Findings are candidates: the review step must trace entry → sink before rating them final.",
              "- SEC1 checks the whole visible file for an auth call; a helper in another file is not seen — confirm manually.",
              "- SEC4 is a heuristic (fetch of a variable); confirm whether the variable is user-controlled.",
              "- Not covered: IDOR, mass assignment, missing RLS policies (run supabase-schema-rls/rls_lint.py), logic flaws."]
    rpath.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def write_final(findings: list[dict], fpath: Path, scope: str, n_files: int, file_names: list[str]) -> None:
    """Deterministic review record (no model step) on the review-report template's sections."""
    tbd = lambda role: f"[TO BE BASELINED — owner: {role}]"  # noqa: E731
    counts = {s_: sum(1 for f in findings if f["severity"] == s_) for s_ in SEV_ORDER}
    verdict = "BLOCK" if counts["critical"] or counts["high"] else "MERGE (scanner candidates only — trace before sign-off)"
    lines = [f"# Security Review — {scope}", "",
             "> Script draft — the model review step was not run (draft only): findings are scanner candidates, "
             "not traced entry → sink; owned markers show what a reviewer must still decide.", "",
             "| Field | Value |", "|---|---|",
             f"| Scope | {scope} ({n_files} file(s)) |", f"| Reviewer | {tbd('Security reviewer')} |",
             f"| Trust model | {tbd('Tech lead')} |", f"| Verdict | {verdict} |", "",
             "## Findings (worst first)", "",
             "| # | Sev | Confidence | Title | Trace (entry → sink) | Fix | Test | Status |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for f in findings:
        lines.append(f"| {f['id']} | {f['severity']} | candidate (scanner) | {f['category']} ({f['rule']}) | "
                     f"`{f['file']}:{f['line']}` → {tbd('Security reviewer')} | {f['recommendation']} | "
                     f"{tbd('Developer')} | open |")
    if not findings:
        lines.append("| — | — | — | no scanner findings | — | — | — | — |")
    lines += ["", "## Threat model record", "",
              "| Change | Who reaches | Control in diff? | Findings |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    by_file: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for f in findings:
        by_file.setdefault(f["file"], []).append(f["id"])
    for name in file_names:
        ids = by_file.get(name, [])
        lines.append(f"| `{name}` | {tbd('Tech lead')} | {'no → ' + ', '.join(ids) if ids else 'no scanner finding'} | "
                     f"{', '.join(ids) or '—'} |")
    lines += ["", "## Surfaces reviewed", "", "| Surface | Files |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in surfaces(findings, n_files).items()]
    lines += ["", "## Verification", "", "| Check | Result |", "|---|---|",
              f"| `scan.py --gate findings.csv` | {'BLOCK — ' + str(counts['critical'] + counts['high']) + ' critical/high' if counts['critical'] or counts['high'] else 'pass — no critical/high'} |",
              f"| `rls_lint.py` (supabase-schema-rls) | not run by this skill — {tbd('Developer')} |",
              f"| Regression tests for Critical/High | {tbd('Developer') if counts['critical'] or counts['high'] else 'none required by the scan'} |",
              f"| Re-trace after fix | {tbd('Security reviewer')} |", "",
              "## Out of scope / parked", "",
              "- IDOR, mass assignment, missing RLS policies and logic flaws are not detected by the scan."]
    fpath.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fpath.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def surfaces(findings: list[dict], n_files: int) -> dict:
    cats = {}
    for f in findings:
        cats.setdefault(f["category"], set()).add(f["file"])
    out = {"files scanned": n_files}
    for c, fs in sorted(cats.items()):
        out[c] = ", ".join(sorted(fs))
    return out


def gate(fpath: Path) -> int:
    if not fpath.is_file():
        die(f"findings file not found: {fpath}")
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(fpath.open(encoding="utf-8")))
    blocking = [r for r in rows if r.get("severity") in ("critical", "high")]
    if blocking:
        print(f"gate: BLOCK — {len(blocking)} critical/high finding(s):", file=sys.stderr)
        for r in blocking:
            print(f"  {r['id']} {r['severity']} {r['file']}:{r['line']} ({r['category']})", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"gate: pass — {len(rows)} finding(s), none critical/high")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Scan a diff or repo for stack security pitfalls")
    ap.add_argument("--diff", help="unified diff file (git diff main...HEAD > change.patch)")
    ap.add_argument("--target", help="repo root to scan in full (may be combined with --diff)")
    ap.add_argument("--gate", metavar="FINDINGS_CSV", help="exit 1 if the findings file has critical/high rows")
    ap.add_argument("--findings", default="findings.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--report", default="review.md")
    ap.add_argument("--final", default="", help="review record path (written with --draft-only)")
    ap.add_argument("--draft-only", action="store_true", help="no model step: write --final from the scan")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.gate:
        return gate(Path(a.gate))
    if not a.diff and not a.target:
        die("give --diff <patch> and/or --target <repo>")
    files, scopes = {}, []
    if a.diff:
        p = Path(a.diff)
        if not p.is_file():
            die(f"diff not found: {p}")
        files.update(parse_diff(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")))
        if not files:
            die(f"no file hunks found in {p} (expected a unified diff with +++ b/<path> headers)")
        scopes.append(p.name)
    if a.target:
        root = Path(a.target)
        if not root.is_dir():
            die(f"target is not a directory: {root}")
        repo = walk_repo(root)
        if not repo:
            die(f"no source files under {root}")
        files.update(repo)
        scopes.append(root.name)
    scope = " + ".join(scopes)
    findings = []
    for path, info in files.items():
        if Path(path).suffix in EXTS:
            findings += scan_file(path, info)
    write_outputs(findings, Path(a.findings), Path(a.report), scope, len(files))
    if a.draft_only and a.final:
        write_final(findings, Path(a.final), scope, len(files), sorted(files))
    for f in findings:
        print(f"{f['id']} {f['severity']:8} {f['rule']} {f['file']}:{f['line']}")
    print(f"{len(findings)} finding(s) in {len(files)} file(s) -> {a.findings}, {a.report}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Security Review Method — reasoning, not checklist (fallback for security-review)

A checklist finds what it lists. A threat model finds what the change actually enables. Do the model first; use the category table only to make sure nothing was skipped.

## Step 1 — Inventory the change by surface
| Surface | Trusts | Typical sinks |
|---|---|---|
| Server action | session cookie; nothing in `formData` | DB write, revalidate, redirect, email |
| Route handler | nothing (public) unless signature/API key verified | DB, queue, external call |
| Middleware | cookie only | redirect, header set |
| RSC page / layout | session; `params`/`searchParams` are untrusted | DB read, render |
| Client component | nothing; it runs on attacker's machine | action call, fetch |
| Migration / policy | — | data exposure across tenants |
| Edge function / job | service role — highest privilege | everything |
| Env / CI | repo contributors | secret exposure |

## Step 2 — Six questions per change
| # | Question | What a weak answer looks like |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Who can reach this? (anon, any user, tenant member, admin, internal only) | "The UI hides the button" |
| 2 | What do they control? (body, params, headers, files, timing, order) | "The id comes from our own page" |
| 3 | What does it touch? (tables, buckets, external systems, other tenants' rows) | "Just reads" (reads leak) |
| 4 | Worst realistic outcome? (cross-tenant read, privilege escalation, data loss, RCE, DoS, money) | "Nothing sensitive" (ids, emails, counts are sensitive) |
| 5 | Which control stops it, and where is it in this diff? | "RLS will catch it" (is RLS enabled on that table? does the service-role path bypass it?) |
| 6 | How would we know it happened? (log, audit, alert) | "We'd notice" |

Write the answers for each change in the report. Findings come from questions 4–5 having a gap.

## Step 3 — Trace discipline
For every candidate finding:
1. Entry: file:line where untrusted data enters.
2. Each transformation: file:line (parse? validate? authorize?).
3. Sink: file:line where it hits DB/FS/network/response.
4. Control gap: the hop where the needed check is missing or bypassable.
5. Exploit sketch: one concrete request that demonstrates it.

If step 5 cannot be written, downgrade to "question for the author".

## Step 4 — Category sweep (after the model, to catch omissions)
| Category | Key questions | Stack hot spots |
|---|---|---|
| Authorization (authz) | Is the role check on the server? Is it per request? Does it check tenant AND role? | server actions without `requireRole`; RSC pages relying on layout checks; API routes |
| IDOR | Is the id scoped to the tenant/user at the DB (RLS) and in the query? | `.eq('id', id)` without tenant filter on a non-RLS table; service-role queries |
| Mass assignment | Is the whole `formData`/body spread into an insert/update? | `update(parsed)` where schema allows `tenant_id`, `role`, `status` |
| Injection | SQL (raw `rpc` with string concat), command, template, header, log injection | `.rpc()` with interpolated SQL; `sql` template misuse; `JSON.parse` of untrusted |
| RLS bypass | Service role in reachable code? Policies missing `with check`? `security definer` without checks? Views without `security_invoker`? | `lib/supabase/admin.ts` imports; migrations |
| Secrets | `NEXT_PUBLIC_` on a secret; secret in logs; `.env` committed; secret in client bundle via import | `lib/env.ts` split; `next.config` env; logger context |
| SSRF | User-controlled URL fetched server-side (webhooks, image proxies, import-by-URL) | route handlers; `fetch(url)` with url from body |
| Open redirect | `redirect(searchParams.next)` unvalidated | sign-in flows |
| File upload | Type/size validated? Path from user? Bucket public? Served with correct content-type? | Storage policies; `storage.from().upload(userPath)` |
| CSRF | Server actions are POST with origin checks by Next; custom route handlers accepting cookies need CSRF token or same-site checks | `app/api/**` with cookie auth |
| Rate limiting / DoS | Public actions (sign-up, password reset, contact) limited? Expensive queries bounded (`limit`)? | route handlers; search endpoints |
| Crypto / tokens | Tokens random (`crypto.randomUUID`/`randomBytes`), hashed at rest, expiring, single-use? | invite links, API keys |
| Logging / privacy | PII or secrets in logs? Audit for sensitive actions? | logger context; audit trigger coverage |
| Dependency / supply chain | New deps? Postinstall scripts? Lockfile changed unexpectedly? | `package.json` diff |
| Error handling | Stack traces or PG messages to client? Different responses for exists/not-exists? | `toResponse`; `NOT_FOUND` vs `FORBIDDEN` |
| Next.js specifics | See `stack-specifics.md` | server-action exposure, `params` trust, middleware bypass |

## Step 5 — Write the finding
```
[HIGH] Cross-tenant invoice read via export endpoint
Trace: app/api/export/route.ts:14 (searchParams.tenantId) → server/services/export.ts:22 (passes tenantId) → lib/supabase/admin.ts (service role) → invoices
Gap: tenantId taken from query, service-role client bypasses RLS; no comparison to session tenant.
Exploit: GET /api/export?tenantId=<other> with any valid session.
Fix: drop tenantId param; use session.tenantId; use cookie client so RLS applies; add negative test.
```

## Anti-patterns in reviews
- Reporting "consider adding rate limiting" without identifying the endpoint and the abuse.
- Rating by category ("injection = critical") instead of reachability × impact.
- Listing 30 Low/Info items that hide the 2 Highs. Lead with the worst.
- Fixing by adding a client-side check.

# Severity Rubric

Severity = reachability × impact, judged for this application, not the category's reputation.

## Reachability
| Level | Who can trigger |
|---|---|
| R3 | Unauthenticated internet |
| R2 | Any authenticated user (any tenant) |
| R1 | Privileged user (tenant admin/owner) or requires another vuln |
| R0 | Internal only (CI, operators) |

## Impact
| Level | Outcome |
|---|---|
| I3 | Cross-tenant data read/write, auth bypass, RCE, secret exposure, money movement |
| I2 | Own-tenant privilege escalation, bulk PII of own tenant, data integrity loss, persistent DoS |
| I1 | Limited info leak (existence, counts), single-record integrity, temporary DoS |
| I0 | Hardening, defence in depth, hygiene |

## Matrix
| | I3 | I2 | I1 | I0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R3 | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
| R2 | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
| R1 | High | Medium | Low | Info |
| R0 | Medium | Low | Info | Info |

## Handling
| Severity | Action | SLA |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Block merge/release; fix now; regression test; notify owner | same day |
| High | Block merge; fix in this PR; regression test | before merge |
| Medium | Fix in this PR if ≤1 h, else ticket with owner + date | ≤ 2 weeks |
| Low | Ticket or fix opportunistically | next cycle |
| Info | Note in report | — |

## Confidence
Attach `confirmed` (exploit sketch works by trace), `likely` (trace complete, exploit untested), or `question` (gap suspected, needs author input). Only `confirmed`/`likely` carry severity.

# Stack-Specific Pitfalls — Next.js App Router · Supabase · Vercel

## Next.js server actions
| Pitfall | Why it matters | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Every exported function in a `"use server"` file is a public POST endpoint | "helper" functions become callable by anyone with the action id | only actions exported; helpers in non-`use server` modules |
| Closure-captured values are serialized to the client (encrypted, but present) | leaking server data; stale authz decisions captured at render | no secrets/ids in closures; re-check authz inside the action |
| `formData` ids trusted | IDOR / tenant hop | ids re-validated; tenant/user from session |
| Authz done in the layout/page, not the action | action callable directly without UI | `requireRole` inside every action |
| `redirect()` inside `try/catch` | swallowed `NEXT_REDIRECT` | redirect after try block |
| Returning full DB rows / `cause` | leaks internal fields, stack | `toActionState` strips; DTO mapping |
| Action does heavy work synchronously | DoS surface | enqueue; limit |
| `allowedOrigins` / `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` unset for multi-domain | CSRF-like cross-origin calls; large bodies | set in `next.config` when using custom domains/proxies |

## Next.js routing / RSC
| Pitfall | Check |
|---|---|
| `params`/`searchParams` used unvalidated in queries | zod parse; uuid check |
| Middleware as the only auth gate — can be bypassed by direct RSC/`_next/data` fetches or misconfigured matcher | per-page `requireUser()` too |
| `error.tsx` exposing `error.message` from server | show `requestId` + generic text in prod |
| Route handler with `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` caching user data | explicit `dynamic`/`revalidate` per route |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` used for anything secret; `process.env.X` referenced in client component (inlined at build) | grep client files for `process.env` |
| `next.config.images.remotePatterns: '**'` | SSRF-ish image proxy; restrict hosts |
| `rewrites`/`proxy` to user-controlled destinations | allow-list |

## Supabase
| Pitfall | Check |
|---|---|
| Table without RLS reachable via anon key (PostgREST exposes every `public` table) | `rls_lint.py`; `select * from pg_tables where rowsecurity=false and schemaname='public'` |
| Policies without `with check` → row can be moved across tenants | lint RLS004 |
| Claims from `user_metadata` (user-editable via `auth.updateUser`) | only `app_metadata`, set server-side |
| Service-role key in client bundle / edge middleware / `NEXT_PUBLIC_` | lint RLS009; grep |
| `security definer` without `set search_path = ''` | lint RLS006 |
| Functions `grant execute to public` by default → anon can call RPC | explicit revoke |
| Storage bucket public or object path user-chosen | bucket private; path = `${tenantId}/${uuid}`; policies on `storage.objects` |
| Realtime channel on table lacking policies | RLS covers Realtime only via policies |
| `auth.users` email enumeration via sign-up/reset responses | uniform responses; rate limit |
| Supabase Auth hooks / Edge Functions use service role — input trusted | validate payload; verify hook secret |
| `.single()` errors leaking "0 rows" vs "forbidden" | map both to `NOT_FOUND` |
| Direct `SUPABASE_DB_URL` in app runtime | migrations/CI only |

## Vercel
| Pitfall | Check |
|---|---|
| Preview deployments unprotected with prod-like data | Vercel Authentication on previews; separate staging DB |
| Preview env vars pointing at prod Supabase | env matrix review |
| `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET` in client or logs | CI secret only |
| Cron routes (`vercel.json` crons) without auth | check `Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}` |
| Log Drains to third party containing PII | logger redaction |
| Env var marked non-sensitive that is sensitive | mark "Sensitive" in Vercel so it cannot be read back |
| Build-time env inlined into client (`NEXT_PUBLIC_`) rotated without redeploy | rotation runbook includes redeploy |

## Python scripts / agents (when present)
- `subprocess` with `shell=True` and user input; `eval`; pickle from untrusted; `requests` without timeout; secrets in argv.

# spec-to-plan

## In a conversation: write the plan now
- **The request names the feature** (SPEC section, ticket, scope): answer **in this reply** with, in order: (1) the context read first — `docs/SPEC.md` (the named section), `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/HANDOFF.md` — and what each contributes, or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` where their contents are not in the conversation; (2) at most 5 clarifying questions in one round, each with your default answer, then plan on the defaults; (3) the plan for `docs/plans/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.md`: file table (path → create/modify → why); ordered tasks, each with files, acceptance criterion, test(s), size S/M/L and rollback; a risk table (risk → mitigation → owner); a concrete rollback (revert tag, flag off, down-migration). Cross-cutting work the SPEC implies gets its own task — an audit-log write when the feature must be audited, an RLS negative test (another tenant's user gets nothing) when data is tenant-scoped, a `security-review` task when auth or RLS changes; (4) a closing line: no code is written until you reply "go". Never reply with only a request for the SPEC.
- **Too big for one thread** (more than ~8 tasks, or several sub-systems such as plans, Stripe, invoices, dunning, admin UI): do not write one long plan. Split it into separate plans, one per thread; list them in build order with the dependency that sets the order, say which plan comes first and why, and give only that first plan's outline. Do not start building.
- **No feature named** ("make a plan for the new feature"): ask once which feature or SPEC section, and stop; do not invent scope or tasks.
- **Asked to fill in tests or rollbacks a thin SPEC does not state**: decline in one line (invented acceptance criteria are not the team's), still list the tasks, and mark their acceptance, tests and rollback `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Tech lead]`.

## Starting points
- **New** — the SPEC section becomes a task-gated plan: tasks with acceptance, tests, rollback, files and size; anything the SPEC does not say is an owned TBD.
- **Existing** — add `repo`: every file a task names is looked up and marked modify or create, a task that edits an applied migration or numbers a new one out of order is flagged in a "Repo check" section before approve.

## When to use
- "Plan this feature", "how should we build X", a ticket or SPEC section is handed over for implementation.
- Any change touching >3 files, schema, auth, CI, or billing — the plan gate is mandatory.
- NOT for: bugs (`safe-fix`), product definition (`product-spec-prd`), repo setup (`project-bootstrap`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Feature description or SPEC section / ticket | yes | user / `docs/SPEC.md` |
| Repo access (to read current structure) | yes | repo |
| Constraints (deadline, no-schema-change, flag-gated, etc.) | no | user |
| `docs/HANDOFF.md` state | yes if exists | repo |

Missing facts do not stop the plan: mark them `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and ask at the end. Only when no feature or SPEC section is named, ask once which one and stop.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`, `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md`, `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`, then `docs/SPEC.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/HANDOFF.md` in the repo.
2. **Clarify (brainstorm).** If the upstream skill `superpowers:brainstorming` is installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke it for this step; otherwise follow `references/brainstorm-fallback.md`. Output: ≤5 open questions, each with your default answer. Ask once. *(gate: plan inputs)*
3. **Map the change.** Read every file the change touches. Produce the file table: path → create/modify → why. Flag anything that violates `shared/stack-conventions.md`.
4. **Write the plan.** If `superpowers:writing-plans` is installed, invoke it and then apply the gates below; otherwise use `assets/plan-template.md` directly and follow `references/plan-method.md`. Every task has: files, acceptance criterion, test(s), estimate (S/M/L), rollback.
5. **Risk and rollback.** Fill the risk table (schema, auth, data migration, external API). Each risk: mitigation + owner. Rollback must be concrete (revert tag, disable flag, down-migration).
6. **Present and stop.** Post the plan summary (≤10 lines + link to `docs/plans/<slug>.md`). Wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
7. **Execute in task order** after approval. Per task: build → run its tests → run the full unit suite → mark done in the plan file. If `superpowers:executing-plans` is installed, invoke it for the loop. *(gates: build→test→verify)*
8. **Verify.** All acceptance criteria checked, lint/typecheck/unit/build green, e2e for touched critical paths. Paste the command summary.
9. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md` (changed files, open items, next-thread prompt).

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Plan | `docs/plans/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.md` (from `assets/plan-template.md`) |
| Plan summary | chat, ≤10 lines |
| Post-build verification | chat, command output summary |
| HANDOFF | `docs/HANDOFF.md` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every task has files, acceptance criterion, test, rollback
- [ ] No code written before "go"
- [ ] File table came from reading the repo, not memory
- [ ] Schema changes route to `supabase-schema-rls`; auth/RLS changes get `security-review` as a task
- [ ] Plan fits one thread; if not, split and say so
- [ ] Unknowns marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`

- `references/plan-method.md` — task decomposition rules, sizing, gate definitions

- `assets/plan-template.md` — plan file template

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/spec-to-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/spec-to-plan`). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn one SPEC.md section into a task-gated plan.

    python3 -I scripts/plan.py SPEC.md --section "Invoice export" [--template assets/plan-template.md] \
        --out plan.md --tasks tasks.csv [--slug invoice-export]

The section (first heading containing --section, case-insensitive; body up to the next heading of
the same or higher level) is read for tasks: every top-level `-`/`*` bullet or `1.` item is a task.
Sub-bullets fill its fields when they start with a recognised key (case-insensitive):
  accept | acceptance | ac   -> acceptance criterion
  test | tests               -> test to write
  rollback | revert          -> rollback
  files | file               -> files to touch
  size                       -> S | M | L
Inline `(accept: …; test: …; rollback: …)` after the task text works too. A field the spec does not
give is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Tech lead]` — never invented. Writes plan.md on the template (Tasks,
Gates, Rollback filled) and tasks.csv (id, task, acceptance, test, rollback, files, size). More than
8 tasks is reported as a split warning. Exit 1 when the file, the section or any task is missing. Stdlib.

Existing codebase (--repo DIR): every file a task names is looked up in the repo and marked `modify`
(exists) or `create` (new); the plan gets a "Repo check" section and tasks.csv a repo_check column.
Migrations get two extra checks, because an applied migration is never edited: a task that names an
existing file under supabase/migrations is flagged (add a new migration instead), and a new migration
whose number is not after the highest one in the repo is flagged as out of order.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DEFAULT_TEMPLATE = HERE.parent / "assets" / "plan-template.md"
TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Tech lead]"
KEYS = {"accept": "acceptance", "acceptance": "acceptance", "ac": "acceptance", "test": "test", "tests": "test",
        "rollback": "rollback", "revert": "rollback", "files": "files", "file": "files", "size": "size"}
ITEM_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+(.*)$")
GATES = [("plan", "spec section + repo read", "this file: file table, tasks, risks, rollback"),
         ("approve", "plan posted", "explicit \"go\" from the user"),
         ("build", "task N started", "diff limited to task N's file list"),
         ("test", "task N code done", "task N tests pass AND full unit suite passes"),
         ("verify", "all tasks done", "lint + typecheck + unit + build green; e2e on touched paths; criteria ticked")]


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def find_section(md: str, heading: str) -> list[str]:
    lines, out, level = md.splitlines(), [], None
    for ln in lines:
        m = re.match(r"^(#+)\s+(.*)$", ln)
        if m:
            if level is None:
                if heading.lower() in m.group(2).lower():
                    level = len(m.group(1))
                continue
            if len(m.group(1)) <= level:
                break
        elif level is not None:
            out.append(ln)
    if level is None:
        die(f"section not found: {heading!r}")
    return out


def split_fields(text: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    """'Export CSV (accept: …; test: …)' -> ('Export CSV', {...})."""
    fields = {}
    m = re.search(r"\(([^()]*\b(?:accept|acceptance|ac|tests?|rollback|revert|files?|size)\s*:[^()]*)\)\s*$", text, re.I)
    if m:
        for part in re.split(r";\s*", m.group(1)):
            k, _, v = part.partition(":")
            key = KEYS.get(k.strip().lower())
            if key and v.strip():
                fields[key] = v.strip()
        text = text[:m.start()].strip()
    return text.strip(), fields


def parse_tasks(lines: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    tasks, base_indent = [], None
    for ln in lines:
        m = ITEM_RE.match(ln)
        if not m:
            continue
        indent, text = len(m.group(1).expandtabs(4)), m.group(2).strip()
        if base_indent is None:
            base_indent = indent
        if indent <= base_indent:
            title, fields = split_fields(text)
            tasks.append({"task": title, **fields})
        elif tasks:
            k, _, v = text.partition(":")
            key = KEYS.get(k.strip().lower().lstrip("*_").rstrip("*_"))
            if key and v.strip():
                tasks[-1][key] = v.strip()
    for i, t in enumerate(tasks, 1):
        t["id"] = f"T{i}"
        for key in ("acceptance", "test", "rollback", "files"):
            t.setdefault(key, TBD)
        size = str(t.get("size", "")).upper()[:1]
        t["size"] = size if size in ("S", "M", "L") else "M"
    return tasks


MIGRATIONS_DIR = "supabase/migrations/"


def task_paths(files: str) -> list[str]:
    if files == TBD:
        return []
    return [p.strip().strip("`").lstrip("./") for p in re.split(r"[,;]", files) if p.strip().strip("`")]


def repo_check(tasks: list[dict], repo: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Mark each named file modify/create; flag edits to existing migrations and out-of-order numbers.
    Sets t['repo_check'] per task and returns the problems (one line each)."""
    mig_dir = repo / MIGRATIONS_DIR
    nums = [int(m.group(1)) for f in (mig_dir.glob("*.sql") if mig_dir.is_dir() else [])
            if (m := re.match(r"^(\d+)", f.name))]
    latest = max(nums) if nums else None
    problems = []
    for t in tasks:
        notes = []
        for rel in task_paths(t["files"]):
            exists = (repo / rel).exists()
            notes.append(f"{rel}: {'modify' if exists else 'create'}")
            if rel.startswith(MIGRATIONS_DIR):
                m = re.match(r"^(\d+)", rel[len(MIGRATIONS_DIR):])
                if exists:
                    problems.append(f"{t['id']}: `{rel}` is an existing migration — never edit an applied one; add a new migration")
                elif m and latest is not None and int(m.group(1)) <= latest:
                    problems.append(f"{t['id']}: new migration `{rel}` is numbered at or before the latest existing one "
                                    f"({latest:04d}) — renumber it after it")
        t["repo_check"] = "; ".join(notes) if notes else "no files named"
    return problems


def replace_section(md: str, heading_startswith: str, body: list[str]) -> str:
    lines, out, i = md.splitlines(), [], 0
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        out.append(ln)
        i += 1
        if ln.startswith("## ") and ln[3:].lower().startswith(heading_startswith.lower()):
            out += body
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith("## "):
                i += 1
            if i < len(lines):
                out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="SPEC section -> task-gated plan")
    ap.add_argument("spec", help="SPEC.md")
    ap.add_argument("--section", required=True, help="heading text of the section to plan")
    ap.add_argument("--template", default=str(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="plan.md")
    ap.add_argument("--tasks", default="tasks.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--slug", default="", help="plan slug (default: from the section heading)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default="", help="existing repo root: mark each file modify/create and check migrations")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    spec = Path(a.spec)
    if not spec.is_file():
        die(f"spec not found: {spec}")
    tmpl = Path(a.template)
    if not tmpl.is_file():
        die(f"template not found: {tmpl}")
    body = find_section(spec.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), a.section)
    tasks = parse_tasks(body)
    if not tasks:
        die(f"section {a.section!r} has no bullet or numbered items to plan from")
    problems = None
    if a.repo:
        if not Path(a.repo).is_dir():
            die(f"repo not found: {a.repo}")
        problems = repo_check(tasks, Path(a.repo))
    else:
        for t in tasks:
            t["repo_check"] = ""
    slug = a.slug or re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", a.section.lower()).strip("-")
    today = dt.date.today().isoformat()

    task_blocks = []
    for t in tasks:
        task_blocks += [f"### {t['id']} — {t['task']} ({t['size']})",
                        f"- Files: {t['files']}", f"- Acceptance: {t['acceptance']}", f"- Tests: {t['test']}",
                        f"- Rollback: {t['rollback']}", "- Status: ☐ built ☐ tests pass ☐ full suite pass", ""]
    task_blocks.pop()  # trailing blank
    if len(tasks) > 8:
        task_blocks.insert(0, f"> **Split warning:** {len(tasks)} tasks exceed the 8-task limit — split into two plans (two threads).\n")
    md = tmpl.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("{{SLUG}}", slug).replace("{{DATE}}", today)
    md = md.replace("| Source | SPEC §__ / ticket __ |", f"| Source | SPEC §{a.section} |")
    sizes = "".join(t["size"] for t in tasks)
    md = md.replace("| Size | S / M / L (sum of tasks) |", f"| Size | {sizes} ({len(tasks)} tasks) |")
    md = replace_section(md, "Tasks", task_blocks)
    gates = ["| Gate | Entry | Exit evidence |", "|---|---|---|"] + [f"| {g} | {e} | {x} |" for g, e, x in GATES]
    gates += ["", "A gate without its exit evidence is not passed. Order: plan → approve → build → test → verify."]
    md = md.replace("## Risks", "## Gates\n" + "\n".join(gates) + "\n\n## Risks", 1)
    if problems is not None:
        check = [f"Files looked up in `{Path(a.repo).resolve().name}`:", ""]
        check += [f"- {t['id']}: {t['repo_check']}" for t in tasks]
        check += ["", "Problems to resolve before approve:" if problems else "No problems found.", ""]
        check += [f"- {p_}" for p_ in problems]
        md = md.replace("## Gates\n", "## Repo check\n\n" + "\n".join(check).rstrip() + "\n\n## Gates\n", 1)
    rollback = [f"- {t['id']}: {t['rollback']}" for t in tasks]
    rollback.append(f"- Whole feature: {TBD} (revert tag / disable flag / down-migration)")
    md = replace_section(md, "Rollback", rollback)
    out, tasks_path = Path(a.out), Path(a.tasks)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tasks_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(md, encoding="utf-8")
    with tasks_path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "task", "acceptance", "test", "rollback", "files", "size", "repo_check"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(tasks)
    n_tbd = sum(1 for t in tasks for k in ("acceptance", "test", "rollback", "files") if t[k] == TBD)
    print(f"plan: {len(tasks)} task(s) from SPEC §{a.section}, {n_tbd} field(s) to be baselined"
          + (f", {len(problems)} repo problem(s)" if problems else "") + f" -> {out}, {tasks_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Brainstorm Fallback (when superpowers:brainstorming is not installed)

Goal: surface the questions whose answers change the plan, with a default for each, in one round.

## Method
1. Restate the request in one sentence as an outcome ("Users can export invoices as CSV per tenant").
2. Walk the dimension list below; for each, decide: known from SPEC/repo, assumed (state the default), or must ask.
3. Ask only the "must ask" items, max 5, each with your default so the user can reply "defaults".
4. Record answers at the top of the plan file under "Decisions".

## Dimensions
| Dimension | Question shape | Typical default |
|---|---|---|
| Users / roles | Who can do this? Which roles are excluded? | tenant admin + member; viewer read-only |
| Data | New tables or columns? Tenant-scoped? Retention? | new table with `tenant_id`, RLS, 90-day retention |
| Boundaries | Server action, route handler, or edge function? | server action for UI; route handler for external callers |
| Volume | Expected rows / requests / file sizes? | ≤10k rows per export; ≤5 MB |
| Failure | What happens on partial failure? Retry? Idempotent? | fail whole op, Result<E>, idempotency key on writes |
| Visibility | Flag-gated? Rollout per tenant? | flag `feature.<name>`, default off in prod |
| Audit | Must the action be in the audit log? | yes for any write to tenant data |
| Non-functional | Latency, a11y, i18n needs? | p95 ≤ 300 ms API; WCAG AA |
| Out of scope | What will reviewers assume is included but is not? | list explicitly |

## Anti-patterns
- Asking questions whose answer does not change the file table.
- Asking without a default (forces a round-trip).
- More than one round of questions.
skills/build/spec-to-plan/references/pla:
# Plan Method — from spec to task-gated plan

## Gate definitions
| Gate | Entry | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|
| plan | spec/ticket + repo read | `docs/plans/<slug>.md` with file table, tasks, risks, rollback |
| approve | plan posted | explicit "go" from the user (or "go with changes: …") |
| build | task N started | diff limited to task N's file list |
| test | task N code done | task N tests pass AND full unit suite passes |
| verify | all tasks done | lint + typecheck + unit + build green; e2e on touched paths; acceptance criteria ticked |
| handoff | verify done | HANDOFF.md updated with changed files + next prompt |

A gate without its exit evidence is not passed. "Should work" is not evidence.

## Task decomposition rules
| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| One task = one vertical slice that can be tested alone | keeps diffs reviewable, lets a thread stop safely mid-plan |
| Order: schema → validators → services → actions/routes → UI → e2e | each layer tests against the one below |
| Max 8 tasks per plan; more → split into two plans (two threads) | token budget and review quality |
| Size S (≤1 h), M (≤half day), L (≤1 day). No XL — split it | estimate honesty |
| Schema tasks delegate to `supabase-schema-rls`; auth-touching tasks add a `security-review` task | specialist skills own their domain |
| Every task names its rollback | no task is "unrevertable" |

## File table format
| Path | Action | Why | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supabase/migrations/0007_invoices.sql` | create | invoices table + RLS | schema |
| `server/validators/invoice.ts` | create | zod schema | — |
| `server/services/invoice.ts` | create | create/list; Result<T,E> | — |
| `app/(app)/invoices/page.tsx` | create | server component list | — |

Read every "modify" file before listing it. If a file is listed from memory, the plan is wrong.

## Acceptance criteria rules
- Observable, binary, written as "Given / When / Then" or "Returns X when Y".
- Mapped 1:1 to at least one test. A criterion with no test is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
- Non-functional criteria (latency, RLS, a11y) are stated per task when relevant, not deferred to "later".

## Test list rules
| Layer | Tool | When mandatory |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | vitest | every service, validator, util |
| Integration | vitest + local Supabase | every `lib/db` query, every RLS policy (positive and negative case) |
| E2E | playwright | every user-visible critical path the task adds or changes |
| Contract | zod parse tests | every external payload |

## Risk table
| Risk | Likelihood (L/M/H) | Impact (L/M/H) | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Migration locks large table | M | H | add column nullable, backfill in batches | ___ |

Always consider: schema change, data backfill, auth/RLS, external API, feature flag default, env var, breaking type change.

## Rollback patterns
| Change type | Rollback |
|---|---|
| Code only | redeploy previous tag (`vercel rollback` or re-run prod.yml on previous tag) |
| Additive migration | leave schema; redeploy previous code; schedule drop migration |
| Destructive migration | forbidden without a two-step (expand → migrate → contract) plan across two releases |
| Flag-gated feature | set flag off; no deploy needed |
| External integration | disable integration via env; queue retries |

## Plan summary (what goes in chat)
```
Plan: <slug> — <N> tasks, est <S/M/L total>, touches <k> files
Schema: yes/no   Auth: yes/no   Flag: <name or none>
Risks: <top 2 with mitigation>
Rollback: <one line>
Full plan: docs/plans/<file>
Reply "go" to build, or "go with changes: …".
```

# supabase-schema-rls

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/supabase-schema-rls --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/supabase-schema-rls`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## Starting points
- **New** — your first migrations are linted against every rule (RLS on, policies present, tenant predicate, `with check`, roles, rollback block).
- **Existing** — the whole history is replayed in order: policies later dropped or replaced and tables later dropped are judged by what is live now, columns added later count, client code is scanned for the service role, and migrations already applied (`applied_through`) are not asked for a rollback block they can no longer get.

## When to use
- "Add a table", "add a column", "who can see X", "set up RLS", "new role", "migration", "seed".
- Any task from `spec-to-plan` tagged risk = schema or auth.
- NOT for: application authz in server actions (`nextjs-enterprise-conventions`), full review (`security-review`), tenant/RBAC design (`multi-tenant-saas-patterns` — design first, then come here).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Entity description: columns, relationships, tenant-scoped? owner column? | yes | user / plan |
| Access rules per role (who reads / writes / deletes) | yes | user / RBAC matrix |
| Existing schema (`supabase/migrations/`, `lib/db/types.ts`) | yes | repo |
| JWT claim layout (`tenant_id`, `role` in `app_metadata`?) | yes | repo (`auth.jwt()` usage) — ask once if absent |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md` (Migrations, Auth, Multi-tenant rows) and `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`. Read the latest 3 migrations and `lib/db/types.ts` for naming and claim conventions.
2. **Plan.** Table: entity → columns → indexes → policies (per role × operation) → rollback. Mark destructive changes and propose expand/contract across two releases. Post the table; wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
3. **Build the migration** with `supabase migration new <name>` and `references/migration-format.md`. Rules: `enable row level security` on every table; `tenant_id` first in composite indexes; `updated_at` trigger; `-- rollback:` block at the end.
4. **Write policies** from `references/rls-patterns.md` — one policy per operation per role; `using` for read/delete, `with check` for insert/update; wrap `auth.*` calls in `(select …)` for performance. Use `assets/rls-policies.sql` snippets.
5. **Lint.** `python3 -I scripts/rls_lint.py supabase/migrations --client-dirs app components lib/supabase/browser.ts`. Zero findings or each one justified in the plan.
6. **Test.** `supabase db reset` locally; run integration tests from `references/rls-testing.md`: for each policy a positive case and a negative case (other tenant / other owner / lower role). Run the full unit suite. *(gate: build→test)*
7. **Types + seed.** `npm run db:types`; update `supabase/seed.sql` with minimal rows for two tenants so negative tests have data.
8. **Verify.** Diff `lib/db/types.ts`; confirm no `service_role` client in `app/`, `components/`, or browser client; confirm `security definer` functions have `set search_path = ''`. *(gate: test→verify)*
9. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`; if an applied migration was wrong, write a new migration — never edit the applied one.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Migration | `supabase/migrations/<ts>_<name>.sql` (with rollback block) |
| Policies | inside the migration; snippets from `assets/rls-policies.sql` |
| Lint result | chat, from `scripts/rls_lint.py` |
| Integration tests | `tests/integration/rls/<table>.test.ts` |
| Types | `lib/db/types.ts` regenerated |
| Seed | `supabase/seed.sql` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every new table: `enable row level security` + at least one policy, or an explicit "no access by design" comment
- [ ] Every tenant table: `tenant_id not null` + policy predicate on it + index leading with it
- [ ] `with check` present on every insert/update policy (not only `using`)
- [ ] No `service_role` in client code; `security definer` functions pin `search_path`
- [ ] Rollback block reverses every statement in reverse order
- [ ] Positive + negative integration test per policy, all green
- [ ] Applied migrations untouched

## References
- `references/rls-patterns.md` — tenant, owner, role-based, public-read patterns; bypass mistakes
- `references/migration-format.md` — file layout, naming, rollback block, expand/contract
- `references/rls-testing.md` — integration test method with JWT impersonation
- `assets/rls-policies.sql` — copy-paste policy snippets
- `assets/migration-template.sql` — migration skeleton

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""rls_lint.py — offline linter for Supabase migrations and client code.

Checks (all static, stdlib only; run with: python3 -I rls_lint.py supabase/migrations):
  RLS001  table created without `enable row level security` anywhere in the migration set
  RLS002  table has RLS enabled but zero policies — unless a migration acknowledges it as intentional with
          `-- rls-lint: deny-all <schema.>table <reason>` (server-only tables; the reason is required)
  RLS003  policy on a tenant-scoped table (has tenant_id column) whose predicate lacks `tenant_id`
  RLS004  insert/update policy without `with check`
  RLS005  policy granted `to public` (or no `to` clause → defaults to public)
  RLS006  `security definer` function without `set search_path`
  RLS007  migration file without a `-- rollback:` block
  RLS008  policy reads claims from `user_metadata` (user-editable)
  RLS009  service-role usage in client directories (--client-dirs)
  RLS010  `using (true)` on a non-select policy, or on select without `to anon` being intentional (warn)

Existing migration history: files are replayed in name order, as they are applied — `drop policy`
withdraws the findings of the policy it drops (the replaced policy is judged, not the old one), `drop
table` removes the table, and `alter table … add column tenant_id` makes a table tenant-scoped.
--applied-through <file>: migrations up to and including that file name are already applied; RLS007
is not raised for them (an applied migration is never edited, so its missing rollback cannot be fixed
there) — every other finding still stands, because it describes the schema as it is.

Exit 1 if any error-level finding. Use --warn-only to downgrade everything to warnings.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

CREATE_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"create\s+table\s+(?:if\s+not\s+exists\s+)?(?:(?P<schema>\w+)\.)?\"?(?P<name>\w+)\"?\s*\((?P<body>.*?)\)\s*;",
    re.I | re.S,
)
ENABLE_RLS_RE = re.compile(
    r"alter\s+table\s+(?:only\s+)?(?:(?P<schema>\w+)\.)?\"?(?P<name>\w+)\"?\s+enable\s+row\s+level\s+security",
    re.I,
)
POLICY_RE = re.compile(
    r"create\s+policy\s+\"?(?P<pname>\w+)\"?\s+on\s+(?:(?P<schema>\w+)\.)?\"?(?P<table>\w+)\"?"
    r"(?P<rest>.*?);",
    re.I | re.S,
)
FOR_RE = re.compile(r"\bfor\s+(select|insert|update|delete|all)\b", re.I)
TO_RE = re.compile(r"\bto\s+((?:\w+\s*,\s*)*\w+)", re.I)
USING_RE = re.compile(r"\busing\s*\(", re.I)
WITH_CHECK_RE = re.compile(r"\bwith\s+check\s*\(", re.I)
SECDEF_FN_RE = re.compile(
    r"create\s+(?:or\s+replace\s+)?function\s+(?P<fn>[\w.\"]+)\s*\(.*?\)(?P<tail>.*?)(?:\$\$|\bas\s+')",
    re.I | re.S,
)
ROLLBACK_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*--\s*rollback:", re.I | re.M)
USER_META_RE = re.compile(r"user_metadata", re.I)
USING_TRUE_RE = re.compile(r"\busing\s*\(\s*true\s*\)", re.I)
SERVICE_ROLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY|service_role|serviceRoleKey|createAdminClient|supabaseAdmin",
)
DROP_POLICY_RE = re.compile(
    r"drop\s+policy\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?\"?(?P<pname>\w+)\"?\s+on\s+(?:(?P<schema>\w+)\.)?\"?(?P<table>\w+)\"?",
    re.I,
)
DROP_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"drop\s+table\s+(?:if\s+exists\s+)?(?P<names>(?:(?:\w+\.)?\"?\w+\"?\s*,\s*)*(?:\w+\.)?\"?\w+\"?)",
    re.I,
)
COMMENT_RE = re.compile(r"--[^\n]*|/\*.*?\*/", re.S)

IGNORE_TABLES = {"schema_migrations", "supabase_migrations"}


@dataclass
class Finding:
    code: str
    level: str  # error | warn
    file: str
    line: int
    msg: str


@dataclass
class Table:
    name: str
    schema: str
    file: str
    line: int
    tenant_scoped: bool
    rls_enabled: bool = False
    policies: list = field(default_factory=list)


DENY_ALL_ACK_RE = re.compile(r"--[ \t]*rls-lint:[ \t]*deny-all[ \t]+(?:(?P<schema>\w+)\.)?(?P<table>\w+)[ \t]+[^\s][^\n]{2,}", re.I)   # reason on the same line


def strip_comments(sql: str) -> str:
    # keep newlines so line numbers hold
    return COMMENT_RE.sub(lambda m: "\n" * m.group(0).count("\n"), sql)


def line_of(text: str, pos: int) -> int:
    return text.count("\n", 0, pos) + 1


def _key(schema, name) -> str:
    return f"{(schema or 'public').lower()}.{name.lower()}"


def lint_migrations(mig_dir: Path, findings: list[Finding], applied_through: str = "") -> None:
    files = [mig_dir] if mig_dir.is_file() else sorted(mig_dir.glob("*.sql"))
    if not files:
        findings.append(Finding("RLS000", "warn", str(mig_dir), 0, "no .sql migrations found"))
        return

    tables: dict[str, Table] = {}
    all_sql: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    deny_all_ok: set[str] = set()   # tables a migration explicitly acknowledges as deny-all (server-only), with a reason

    for f in files:
        raw = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        applied = bool(applied_through) and f.name <= applied_through
        if not ROLLBACK_RE.search(raw) and not applied:
            findings.append(Finding("RLS007", "error", str(f), 1, "missing `-- rollback:` block"))
        for m in DENY_ALL_ACK_RE.finditer(raw):
            deny_all_ok.add(f"{(m.group('schema') or 'public').lower()}.{m.group('table').lower()}")
        sql = strip_comments(raw)
        all_sql.append((f, sql))
        events = [(m.start(), "create", m) for m in CREATE_TABLE_RE.finditer(sql)]
        events += [(m.start(), "drop", m) for m in DROP_TABLE_RE.finditer(sql)]
        for _, kind, m in sorted(events, key=lambda e: e[0]):
            if kind == "drop":
                for raw_name in m.group("names").split(","):
                    parts = raw_name.strip().replace('"', "").split(".")
                    tables.pop(_key(parts[0] if len(parts) == 2 else None, parts[-1]), None)
                continue
            name = m.group("name").lower()
            if name in IGNORE_TABLES:
                continue
            schema = (m.group("schema") or "public").lower()
            body = m.group("body").lower()
            tenant_scoped = bool(re.search(r"\btenant_id\b", body))
            tables[f"{schema}.{name}"] = Table(name, schema, str(f), line_of(sql, m.start()), tenant_scoped)
        # columns added later
        for m in re.finditer(r"alter\s+table\s+(?:only\s+)?(?:(\w+)\.)?\"?(\w+)\"?\s+add\s+(?:column\s+)?(?:if\s+not\s+exists\s+)?\"?tenant_id\"?", sql, re.I):
            key = f"{(m.group(1) or 'public').lower()}.{m.group(2).lower()}"
            if key in tables:
                tables[key].tenant_scoped = True

    pending: dict[tuple[str, str], list[Finding]] = {}   # (table, policy) -> its findings, withdrawn on drop policy
    for f, sql in all_sql:
        for m in ENABLE_RLS_RE.finditer(sql):
            key = f"{(m.group('schema') or 'public').lower()}.{m.group('name').lower()}"
            if key in tables:
                tables[key].rls_enabled = True
            elif m.group("schema") is None or m.group("schema").lower() == "public":
                # table created outside this migration set; still fine
                tables.setdefault(key, Table(m.group("name").lower(), "public", str(f), line_of(sql, m.start()), False)).rls_enabled = True

        events = [(m.start(), "create", m) for m in POLICY_RE.finditer(sql)]
        events += [(m.start(), "drop", m) for m in DROP_POLICY_RE.finditer(sql)]
        events += [(m.start(), "drop_table", m) for m in DROP_TABLE_RE.finditer(sql)]
        for _, kind, m in sorted(events, key=lambda e: e[0]):
            if kind == "drop_table":                # its policies go with it: withdraw their findings
                for raw_name in m.group("names").split(","):
                    parts = raw_name.strip().replace('"', "").split(".")
                    gone = _key(parts[0] if len(parts) == 2 else None, parts[-1])
                    for pk in [pk for pk in pending if pk[0] == gone]:
                        for fd in pending.pop(pk):
                            findings.remove(fd)
                        if gone in tables and pk[1] in tables[gone].policies:
                            tables[gone].policies.remove(pk[1])   # a re-created table starts without them
                continue
            key = f"{(m.group('schema') or 'public').lower()}.{m.group('table').lower()}"
            if kind == "drop":
                pname = m.group("pname")
                for fd in pending.pop((key, pname), []):
                    findings.remove(fd)
                if key in tables and pname in tables[key].policies:
                    tables[key].policies.remove(pname)
                continue
            before = len(findings)
            rest = m.group("rest")
            ln = line_of(sql, m.start())
            op = (FOR_RE.search(rest).group(1).lower() if FOR_RE.search(rest) else "all")
            to = TO_RE.search(rest)
            roles = [r.strip().lower() for r in to.group(1).split(",")] if to else ["public"]
            has_using = bool(USING_RE.search(rest))
            has_check = bool(WITH_CHECK_RE.search(rest))
            tbl = tables.get(key)
            if tbl is not None:
                tbl.policies.append(m.group("pname"))
            if "public" in roles:
                findings.append(Finding("RLS005", "error", str(f), ln, f"policy {m.group('pname')} applies `to public` (name roles: authenticated / anon)"))
            if op in ("insert", "update", "all") and not has_check:
                findings.append(Finding("RLS004", "error", str(f), ln, f"policy {m.group('pname')} ({op}) lacks `with check`"))
            if tbl is not None and tbl.tenant_scoped and tbl.schema == "public" and not re.search(r"\btenant_id\b", rest, re.I):
                findings.append(Finding("RLS003", "error", str(f), ln, f"policy {m.group('pname')} on tenant table {key} has no tenant_id predicate"))
            if USER_META_RE.search(rest):
                findings.append(Finding("RLS008", "error", str(f), ln, f"policy {m.group('pname')} reads user_metadata (user-editable); use app_metadata"))
            if USING_TRUE_RE.search(rest):
                lvl = "warn" if op == "select" else "error"
                findings.append(Finding("RLS010", lvl, str(f), ln, f"policy {m.group('pname')} uses `using (true)` on {op}"))
            pending[(key, m.group("pname"))] = pending.get((key, m.group("pname")), []) + findings[before:]

        for m in SECDEF_FN_RE.finditer(sql):
            tail = m.group("tail")
            if re.search(r"security\s+definer", tail, re.I) and not re.search(r"set\s+search_path", tail, re.I):
                findings.append(Finding("RLS006", "error", str(f), line_of(sql, m.start()), f"security definer function {m.group('fn')} without `set search_path`"))

    for key, t in tables.items():
        if t.schema != "public":
            continue
        if not t.rls_enabled:
            findings.append(Finding("RLS001", "error", t.file, t.line, f"table {key} created without `enable row level security`"))
        elif not t.policies and key not in deny_all_ok:
            findings.append(Finding("RLS002", "error", t.file, t.line, f"table {key} has RLS enabled but no policies (deny-all; if intentional add `-- rls-lint: deny-all {key} <reason>`)"))


def lint_client_dirs(paths: list[str], root: Path, findings: list[Finding]) -> None:
    exts = {".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs"}
    for p in paths:
        base = root / p
        if not base.exists():
            continue
        files = [base] if base.is_file() else [x for x in base.rglob("*") if x.suffix in exts]
        for f in files:
            if "node_modules" in f.parts or ".next" in f.parts:
                continue
            text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
            for i, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
                if SERVICE_ROLE_RE.search(line) and "// rls-lint: allow" not in line:
                    findings.append(Finding("RLS009", "error", str(f), i, "service-role reference in client-side directory"))


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Offline RLS linter for Supabase migrations.")
    ap.add_argument("migrations", nargs="?", default="supabase/migrations", help="migrations directory, or a single .sql file")
    ap.add_argument("--client-dirs", nargs="*", default=[], help="dirs/files that must not reference service role (e.g. app components)")
    ap.add_argument("--root", default=".", help="repo root for --client-dirs")
    ap.add_argument("--warn-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true", help="print only the summary line")
    ap.add_argument("--applied-through", default="", metavar="FILE",
                    help="migration file name up to which the history is already applied (no RLS007 for those)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    findings: list[Finding] = []
    mig = Path(args.migrations)
    if not (mig.is_dir() or (mig.is_file() and mig.suffix.lower() == ".sql")):
        print(f"error: not a migrations directory or a .sql file: {mig}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    lint_migrations(mig, findings, Path(args.applied_through).name if args.applied_through else "")
    lint_client_dirs(args.client_dirs, Path(args.root), findings)

    findings.sort(key=lambda x: (x.file, x.line, x.code))
    errors = 0
    for fd in findings:
        lvl = "warn" if args.warn_only else fd.level
        if lvl == "error":
            errors += 1
        if not args.quiet:
            print(f"{fd.file}:{fd.line}: {lvl.upper()} {fd.code} {fd.msg}")
    print(f"rls_lint: {len(findings)} findings, {errors} errors")
    return 1 if errors else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
