# Relocation / Cost-of-Living Adjustment Method

## Inputs (user-supplied, always)
| Input | Example format | Source the user should cite |
|---|---|---|
| COL index per location | `Columbus OH=100, Austin TX=108` | A named COL calculator or survey, with date |
| Base location | The user's current city | — |
| Housing share (optional) | 0.35 | User's own budget; default 0.30 if the user accepts |
| State income tax (optional) | Effective % per state | User-supplied |

The skill and script carry **no built-in indices**. If the user cannot supply one, mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]` and compare nominal figures only.

## Method
1. Normalize indices to the base location: `rel_index = index_target / index_base`.
2. Adjust only recurring, location-spent dollars: `adjusted_recurring = annual_recurring / rel_index`.
3. Do not COL-adjust: sign-on, relocation, equity (portable value), 401k match (portable).
4. Optional housing-weighted variant when the user supplies a housing index separately:
   `blended = housing_share × housing_rel + (1 − housing_share) × non_housing_rel`.
5. Optional tax step when the user supplies rates: `after_tax = recurring × (1 − effective_rate)` applied to every option.
6. Report nominal and adjusted side by side; the decision matrix uses adjusted.

## Remote roles
- Remote with the user staying put: rel_index = 1.0; note any geo-pay band the company applies.
- Remote with planned move: use the destination index and flag the company's geo-pay policy as a risk.

## Relocation logistics checklist (ask, do not assume)
| Item | Ask |
|---|---|
| Relocation package | Lump sum vs. managed; gross-up; repayment clause |
| Timing | Must move by when; temporary housing covered? |
| Home sale / lease break | Covered? |
| Family | School-year timing, spouse employment support |
| Travel before move | Covered trips, cadence |

## Output table
| Option | Location | Index (source, date) | Annual recurring (nominal) | Rel index | Annual recurring (adjusted) | Delta vs current |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

# Decision Matrix

Default weights (sum = 100). The user may override; record the weights used.

| # | Criterion | Default weight | What a 5 looks like | What a 1 looks like |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | COL-adjusted total compensation | 25 | ≥ 15% above current adjusted | Below current |
| D2 | Role scope and authority | 15 | Owns budget, org, roadmap; reports to CIO/CTO | Dotted-line, no budget |
| D3 | Career trajectory | 15 | Clear path to VP/CIO; visible to execs | Lateral, capped |
| D4 | Company health and stability | 10 | Growing, funded, low layoff risk | Restructuring, losses |
| D5 | Location / remote / travel fit | 10 | Matches user's constraints | Requires unwanted move or travel |
| D6 | Manager and culture signals | 10 | Clear mandate, decision rights, candor in interviews | Vague, high churn |
| D7 | Family and personal timing | 10 | Fits school year, family plans | Conflicts |
| D8 | Learning and domain interest | 5 | Industry and problems the user wants | Industry on avoid-list |

## Scoring
- Scale 1–5 per criterion; cite the evidence for each score in one phrase.
- `weighted = Σ (weight × score) / 5` → 0–100.
- Show the table for every option, including "stay in current role" where applicable.
- A difference under 5 points is a tie; break it on D1 after negotiation or on D7.

## Output table
| Criterion | Weight | Option A score (evidence) | Option B score (evidence) | Current score (evidence) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| … | | | | |
| **Weighted total** | 100 | | | |

## Kill criteria (fail any → do not accept regardless of score)
- Written title/reporting line differs from what was discussed.
- Non-compete would block the user's realistic next move.
- Relocation required before the user's stated earliest date.
- Comp below the user's stated floor after negotiation.

# Negotiation Levers (executive IT roles)

Rank by expected value = (likely gain) × (probability of yes). Ask for the user's judgement on probability; do not assume.

| # | Lever | When it works | Justification to offer | Typical trade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Base salary | Offer below band midpoint; competing offer; user's current base higher | Market band (cite source), scope vs. title, current base | Smallest flexibility at large companies; largest at mid-size |
| L2 | Sign-on bonus | Forfeited bonus/equity at current employer; base is capped | Document the forfeited amount | Easiest yes; one-time |
| L3 | Equity / LTI grant | Public or late-stage private; exec level | Peer grants, retention | Often more flexible than base |
| L4 | Target bonus % | Bonus % below peers at level | Level parity | Rare; usually plan-defined |
| L5 | Title / level | Scope matches a higher level | JD scope, team size, budget | Changes band; ask early |
| L6 | Review timing | Base cannot move now | "Review at 6 months against band midpoint" | Low cost to them |
| L7 | Relocation package | Moving | Actual cost estimate | Easy if a policy exists |
| L8 | Remote / travel terms | Role allows | Productivity, retention | Get in writing |
| L9 | Start date | User needs transition time or a break | Current obligations | Usually flexible |
| L10 | Severance / change-of-control | Exec level, company in flux | Standard exec protection | Ask via counsel if large |
| L11 | Budget / headcount commitments | Role is a turnaround | Mandate clarity | Non-cash, high value |
| L12 | PTO carry-in | Losing accrued PTO | Parity with tenure | Moderate |

## Sequencing
1. Thank, confirm enthusiasm, ask for a call (never negotiate by email only).
2. Lead with the single biggest lever (usually L1 or L3). State the number.
3. Hold L2 (sign-on) as the bridge if L1 stalls.
4. Bundle non-cash items (L6, L8, L9, L11) in the same call; they are cheap for them and valuable for you.
5. Close with a written summary of what was agreed; request the revised letter.

## Rules
- One counter, well justified. A second counter only if they move and a real gap remains.
- Never cite a competing offer that does not exist.
- Ask for the band before anchoring if it was not disclosed.
- Silence after your number; let them respond.
- Decide the walk-away number before the call and write it down.

## Negotiation plan table
| Order | Lever | Ask | Justification (source) | Fallback | Probability (user est.) | Expected gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

# Total Compensation Components

| Component | How to value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Base salary | As stated | Annual |
| Target bonus | base × target % | Show target; note the historical payout % if the user has it (ask) |
| Sign-on bonus | As stated, year 1 only | Note clawback period |
| Equity (RSU) | user-stated grant value ÷ vesting years, per year within horizon | Private company: use user's stated valuation; flag illiquidity |
| Equity (options) | user-stated (strike, FMV, count); value only if the user supplies a number | Otherwise `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user]` |
| Retention / LTI | annualized over vesting period | Often exec-level; ask |
| 401k / pension match | base × match % (cap per plan) | User supplies plan terms |
| Health premiums | employer-paid annual amount if known; else difference in employee cost vs. current | Not a hardcoded value |
| PTO | (days − current days) × daily base rate | Only if the user wants it counted |
| Relocation | lump sum or covered costs, year 1 | Note tax gross-up status |
| Car / phone / stipends | annual stated | |
| Deferred comp / ESPP | only if the user quantifies | |

## Calculations
```
year1_cash      = base + bonus_target + sign_on + relocation
annual_recurring = base + bonus_target + equity_per_year + retirement_match + benefits_value + stipends
annualized_total = annual_recurring + (sign_on + relocation) / horizon_years
```
Show all three. Negotiation targets `annual_recurring`; the decision considers `annualized_total`.

## What not to do
- Do not assume bonus pays at target; ask for payout history or label as target.
- Do not value equity at a hoped-for price.
- Do not net taxes unless the user supplies state rates; if they do, apply the same method to every option.
- Do not count "unlimited PTO" as a number.

## Executive-level items to ask about
Severance terms, change-of-control, non-compete scope, bonus proration in year 1, review timing (6 vs 12 months), title and reporting line in writing, budget and headcount commitments, relocation timing flexibility.

# Outreach and Follow-up

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/outreach-and-followup --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/outreach-and-followup`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## Starting points
- **New** — a first message: the type's variants filled only from your facts, every missing slot listed, and the follow-up cadence dated; the model polishes it, or with `draft_only` the filled skeleton is final.
- **Existing** — add the thread so far: the touches you already sent are counted, only the follow-ups still due are dated (or the stop rule is reported), a reply is flagged, and facts you already used are marked so the next touch adds something new.

## When to use
- "Write a note to X asking for a referral", "reply to this recruiter", "thank-you after my panel", "it's been 10 days, nudge them", "decline this politely", "open the comp conversation".
- "When should I follow up?" → cadence table.
- NOT for: résumé content (`resume-tailor`), interview answers (`interview-prep`), offer math (`offer-evaluator`), logging the touch (`application-tracker`, but remind the user to log it).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Message type (one of six) | yes | user |
| Recipient: name, title, relationship, channel (LinkedIn / email / text) | yes | user |
| Role and company | yes | user |
| Context: last contact date, what was said, interview details, deadline | yes for follow-ups | user or tracker row |
| Facts to cite (1–2 outcomes from master résumé / story bank, with IDs) | no | user file |
| Goal of this message (one sentence) | yes | user; ask once if missing |

No recipient name or context → ask once. Never guess names, dates, titles, or what was discussed.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Identify message type and load its rules from `references/message-types.md` (goal, length, tone, must-include, must-avoid).
3. Draft 2–3 variants that differ in **strategy**, not tone (e.g., "Direct ask" vs "Soft ask via advice"; "Hold firm" vs "Open the door"). Label each with the goal it serves and the trade-off.
4. Pull structure from `assets/message-templates.md`; fill only from supplied facts. Any `<placeholder>` left unfilled is listed for the user.
5. Add a subject line for email. Keep LinkedIn connection notes ≤300 characters; InMail ≤150 words; email ≤180 words; thank-you ≤120 words.
6. Attach the cadence row from `references/cadence.md`: next touch date, channel, stop rule.
7. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact; drafts are the artifact.

## Output
```
Type: <message type> | Channel: <x> | Goal: <one line>

### Variant A — <strategy label>  (prioritizes …; trades off …)
Subject: …
<body>

### Variant B — <strategy label>
…

Cadence: next touch <date / +N business days> via <channel>; stop after <n> touches or on <event>.
Log: add a row to tracker.csv (stage, touch date, next action).
Unfilled placeholders: <list or "none">
```

## Self-check
- [ ] No name, date, title, or interview detail that the user did not supply
- [ ] Any résumé fact cited carries its `[MR-…]` / `[SB-…]` ID
- [ ] Variants differ in strategy, each labelled with what it prioritizes and trades off
- [ ] Length limits respected; one ask per message; no banned words; no flattery
- [ ] Cadence row present with a stop rule
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

## References
- `scripts/fill.py` — fills the type's variants from context.json only (unfilled slots become owned markers) and dates the cadence in business days (stdlib, offline)
- `assets/message-final-template.md` — the llm step polishes into this; every fact and id from message.md is kept
- `references/message-types.md` — rules per type
- `references/cadence.md` — timing, channels, stop rules, escalation ladder
- `assets/message-templates.md` — skeletons with placeholders
skills/career/outreach-and-followup/scri:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fill a message skeleton from supplied facts and compute the follow-up cadence — no invented facts.

    python3 -I scripts/fill.py --type thank-you --context context.json \
        --templates assets/message-templates.md --cadence-ref references/cadence.md \
        --message message.md --cadence cadence.csv

context.json: {"recipient": "Dana Okafor", "company": "...", "role": "...", "last_touch_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
               "specifics": ["slot: text", {"slot": "specific thing they said", "text": "..."}, "free fact"],
               optional: "sender", "channel", "req_id", "timeline_date", "relationship": "warm|cold"}

What it does, deterministically:
  * takes the variants of the message type from assets/message-templates.md (one `## N. Title` section
    per type, `**A — label**` + code block per variant);
  * fills `<placeholders>` only from context.json: recipient / company / role / dates / req id directly,
    anything else from `specifics` whose slot name matches the placeholder. Every other placeholder
    becomes `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Sender]` and is listed, so nothing is silently made up;
  * cadence.csv — touch, date, channel, template, basis, stop_rule: the touches of the matching row of
    references/cadence.md, dated in business days from last_touch_date (or timeline_date where the row
    says so). A touch without a computable date is left for the user with its basis.
Existing thread (--thread thread.md: the conversation so far, one `## YYYY-MM-DD — sent …` or
`## YYYY-MM-DD — received …` heading per message): the touches you already sent are counted, the
cadence is anchored on your first sent message and only the touches still due are listed (or the
stop rule is reported when none remain), a reply from them is noted, and every fact already used in
the thread is marked so the next touch adds a new element instead of repeating it.
--draft-only --final message-final.md: no model step — writes the final message on
assets/message-final-template.md's sections (Message = variant A, Alternate variant = B, Facts used,
Cadence) from the filled skeleton, labelled as a draft; unfilled slots stay owned markers.
Exit 1 on a missing/invalid context, an unknown type, a template section without variants, or a
last_touch_date that is not YYYY-MM-DD. Stdlib only, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Sender]"
TYPES = {
    "referral-ask": {"section": "1", "cadence": "Referral ask (warm contact)", "cold": "Referral ask (cold contact)"},
    "recruiter-reply": {"section": "2", "cadence": "Recruiter inbound"},
    "thank-you": {"section": "3", "cadence": "Post-interview thank-you"},
    "status-check": {"section": "4", "cadence": "Awaiting decision (no timeline)", "timeline": "Awaiting decision (timeline given)"},
    "decline": {"section": "5", "cadence": "After decline (yours or theirs)"},
    "negotiation-open": {"section": "6", "cadence": "Offer received, negotiating"},
}
SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"^## (\d+)\. (.+)$")
VARIANT_RE = re.compile(r"^\*\*([A-Z]) [—–-] (.+?)\*\*")
PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"<([^<>\n`]{1,80})>")
ID_SLOT_RE = re.compile(r"\s*\[(?:SB-nn|MR-Lnn)\]")
ID_RE = re.compile(r"\[(?:SB-\d+|MR-L\d+)\]")
DIRECT = {  # placeholder (normalised) -> context key
    "first name": "recipient_first", "role title": "role", "company": "company", "name": "sender",
    "title line": "sender_title", "req id": "req_id", "date": "last_touch_date", "time zone": "time_zone",
    "window 1": "window_1", "window 2": "window_2", "window": "window_1", "range": "comp_range",
    "timeline": "timeline", "location/remote": "location", "x": "travel_max", "team": "team",
    "their team / with the company": "relationship_note", "level": "level", "scope": "scope",
    "period": "period", "market source": "market_source", "date − 2": "deadline_minus_2",
}


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def read(path: str) -> str:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def norm(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"[^\w\s/−-]", "", s.lower())).strip()


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ context

def load_context(path: str) -> dict:
    try:
        ctx = json.loads(read(path))
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        die(f"context is not valid JSON: {e}")
    if not isinstance(ctx, dict):
        die("context.json must be an object")
    for key in ("recipient", "company", "role", "last_touch_date"):
        if not str(ctx.get(key, "")).strip():
            die(f"context.json needs '{key}' (recipient, company, role, last_touch_date are required)")
    try:
        ctx["_last"] = dt.date.fromisoformat(str(ctx["last_touch_date"]))
    except ValueError:
        die("last_touch_date must be YYYY-MM-DD")
    if ctx.get("timeline_date"):
        try:
            ctx["_timeline"] = dt.date.fromisoformat(str(ctx["timeline_date"]))
        except ValueError:
            die("timeline_date must be YYYY-MM-DD")
    ctx["recipient_first"] = str(ctx["recipient"]).split()[0]
    slots, facts = {}, []
    for item in ctx.get("specifics") or []:
        if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("slot") and item.get("text"):
            slots[norm(str(item["slot"]))] = str(item["text"])
        elif isinstance(item, str) and ":" in item and len(item.split(":", 1)[0]) <= 60:
            slot, _, text = item.partition(":")
            slots[norm(slot)] = text.strip()
            facts.append(item.strip())
        elif isinstance(item, str) and item.strip():
            facts.append(item.strip())
    ctx["_slots"], ctx["_facts"] = slots, facts
    return ctx


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ templates

def load_variants(templates: str, section_no: str) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:
    title, variants, cur, in_block = "", [], None, False
    active = False
    for ln in templates.splitlines():
        m = SECTION_RE.match(ln)
        if m:
            active = m.group(1) == section_no
            if active:
                title = m.group(2).strip()
            continue
        if not active:
            continue
        vm = VARIANT_RE.match(ln.strip())
        if vm:
            cur = {"key": vm.group(1), "label": vm.group(2).strip(), "body": []}
            variants.append(cur)
            continue
        if ln.strip().startswith("```"):
            in_block = not in_block
            continue
        if in_block and cur is not None:
            cur["body"].append(ln)
    if not variants:
        die(f"message-templates has no variants under section {section_no}")
    return title, variants


def fill(body: str, ctx: dict) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    unfilled = []

    def rep(m):
        raw = m.group(1)
        key = norm(raw)
        if key in ctx["_slots"]:
            return ctx["_slots"][key]
        for slot, text in ctx["_slots"].items():
            if slot and slot in key:
                return text
        ck = DIRECT.get(key)
        if ck and str(ctx.get(ck, "")).strip():
            return str(ctx[ck])
        if ck == "deadline_minus_2" and ctx.get("_timeline"):
            return business_days_from(ctx["_timeline"], -2).isoformat()
        unfilled.append(raw)
        return TBD
    out_lines = []
    for ln in PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(rep, body).splitlines():
        if ID_SLOT_RE.search(ln):
            # a `[SB-nn]` / `[MR-Lnn]` note slot: drop it when the fact already carries its id, else flag it
            if ID_RE.search(ln):
                ln = ID_SLOT_RE.sub("", ln)
            else:
                ln = ID_SLOT_RE.sub(" " + TBD, ln)
                unfilled.append("source id (SB-nn / MR-Lnn) for the cited fact")
        out_lines.append(ln)
    return "\n".join(out_lines), unfilled


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ cadence

def business_days_from(start: dt.date, n: int) -> dt.date:
    d, step, left = start, (1 if n >= 0 else -1), abs(n)
    while left:
        d += dt.timedelta(days=step)
        if d.weekday() < 5:
            left -= 1
    return d


def cadence_row(ref: str, situation: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    header = []
    for ln in ref.splitlines():
        if not ln.strip().startswith("|"):
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        if not header:
            header = cells
            continue
        if cells[0].lower() == situation.lower():
            return header, cells
    die(f"cadence.md has no row '{situation}'")
    return [], []


def touch_date(cell: str, prev: dt.date | None, ctx: dict) -> tuple[dt.date | None, str]:
    """-> (date or None, basis). Day N = N business days after the last touch; +N = after the previous touch."""
    c = cell.strip()
    last = ctx["_last"]
    if not c or c == "—":
        return None, ""
    if re.search(r"\bEvery\b", c):
        return None, c
    m = re.search(r"Timeline date \+ (\d+)", c)
    if m:
        if ctx.get("_timeline"):
            return business_days_from(ctx["_timeline"], int(m.group(1))), c
        return None, c + " (timeline_date not supplied)"
    m = re.search(r"Deadline − (\d+)", c)
    if m:
        if ctx.get("_timeline"):
            return business_days_from(ctx["_timeline"], -int(m.group(1))), c
        return None, c + " (timeline_date not supplied)"
    m = re.search(r"\bDay (\d+)", c)
    if m:
        return business_days_from(last, int(m.group(1))), c
    m = re.search(r"Within (\d+)\s*(h|hour|hours|business day|business days|day|days)", c)
    if m:
        n = 1 if m.group(2).startswith("h") else int(m.group(1))
        return business_days_from(last, n), c
    m = re.search(r"^\+\s*(\d+)", c)
    if m:
        return business_days_from(prev or last, int(m.group(1))), c
    if re.search(r"Immediately|Reply within 1", c):
        return last, c
    return None, c


def channel_of(cell: str, default: str) -> str:
    c = cell.lower()
    if "linkedin or email" in c:
        return default
    if "inmail" in c:
        return "LinkedIn InMail"
    if "linkedin" in c or "connection note" in c:
        return "LinkedIn"
    if "email" in c:
        return "email"
    if "different channel" in c:
        return "LinkedIn" if default.lower() == "email" else "email"
    if "call" in c:
        return "call"
    return default


def build_cadence(ref: str, msg_type: str, ctx: dict, template_label: str) -> list[dict]:
    spec = TYPES[msg_type]
    situation = spec["cadence"]
    if msg_type == "referral-ask" and str(ctx.get("relationship", "")).lower() == "cold":
        situation = spec["cold"]
    if msg_type == "status-check" and ctx.get("_timeline"):
        situation = spec["timeline"]
    header, cells = cadence_row(ref, situation)
    stop = cells[header.index("Stop rule")] if "Stop rule" in header else ""
    default_channel = str(ctx.get("channel") or "email")
    rows, prev = [], None
    for i, col in enumerate(header):
        if not col.lower().startswith("touch"):
            continue
        cell = cells[i] if i < len(cells) else ""
        if not cell.strip() or cell.strip() == "—":
            continue
        date, basis = touch_date(cell, prev, ctx)
        prev = date or prev
        rows.append({"touch": col, "date": date.isoformat() if date else "",
                     "channel": channel_of(cell, default_channel),
                     "template": template_label if col == "Touch 1" else "new element (see cadence.md timing rules)",
                     "basis": f"{situation}: {basis}" + ("" if date else " — date needs the user"),
                     "stop_rule": stop})
    return rows


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ existing thread

THREAD_HEAD_RE = re.compile(r"^##\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*[—–-]\s*(sent|received)\b(.*)$", re.I)


def read_thread(text: str) -> dict:
    msgs, cur = [], None
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        m = THREAD_HEAD_RE.match(ln.strip())
        if m:
            try:
                d = dt.date.fromisoformat(m.group(1))
            except ValueError:
                die(f"thread heading has an invalid date: {ln.strip()}")
            cur = {"date": d, "dir": m.group(2).lower(), "note": m.group(3).strip(" ()—-"), "body": []}
            msgs.append(cur)
        elif cur is not None:
            cur["body"].append(ln)
    sent = [m_ for m_ in msgs if m_["dir"] == "sent"]
    if not sent:
        die("thread has no '## YYYY-MM-DD — sent' message")
    return {"messages": msgs, "sent": sent, "received": [m_ for m_ in msgs if m_["dir"] == "received"],
            "text": norm(" ".join(" ".join(m_["body"]) for m_ in msgs))}


def used_in_thread(fact: str, thread: dict) -> bool:
    words = [w for w in norm(fact.split(":", 1)[-1]).split() if len(w) > 3]
    if not words:
        return False
    hits = sum(1 for w in words if w in thread["text"].split())
    return hits / len(words) >= 0.6


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ output

def write_message(path: Path, msg_type: str, title: str, variants, ctx: dict, cadence: list[dict],
                  thread: dict | None = None, stop_note: str = "") -> list[dict]:
    L = [f"# {title} — {ctx['role']}, {ctx['company']}", "",
         f"Type: {msg_type} | Recipient: {ctx['recipient']} | Channel: {ctx.get('channel') or 'email'} | "
         f"Last touch: {ctx['last_touch_date']}", "",
         "Facts come only from context.json. Every unfilled slot is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Sender]` and listed "
         "below; the polish step fills a slot only when a listed fact supports it.", ""]
    if thread is not None:
        sent, recv = thread["sent"], thread["received"]
        L += ["## Thread so far", "",
              f"{len(sent)} message(s) sent (first {sent[0]['date']}, last {sent[-1]['date']}); "
              + (f"{len(recv)} reply(ies), last {recv[-1]['date']} — answer it before following up." if recv
                 else "no reply yet."), ""]
        if stop_note:
            L += [f"**{stop_note}**", ""]
    all_unfilled, filled = [], []
    for v in variants:
        text, unfilled = fill("\n".join(v["body"]), ctx)
        all_unfilled += [f"{v['key']}: {u}" for u in unfilled]
        filled.append({"key": v["key"], "label": v["label"], "text": text.strip()})
        L += [f"## Variant {v['key']} — {v['label']}", "", text.strip(), ""]
    L += ["## Facts to work in (from context.json)", ""]
    L += [f"- {f}" + (" — already used in the thread; add a new element instead" if thread and used_in_thread(f, thread) else "")
          for f in ctx["_facts"]] or ["(none supplied — nothing specific can be cited)"]
    L += ["", "## Unfilled placeholders", ""]
    L += [f"- {u}" for u in dict.fromkeys(all_unfilled)] or ["none"]
    L += ["", "## Cadence", "", "| Touch | Date | Channel | Basis |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {r['touch']} | {r['date'] or TBD} | {r['channel']} | {r['basis']} |" for r in cadence]
    L += [f"", f"Stop rule: {cadence[0]['stop_rule'] if cadence else '—'}",
          "Log: add a row to tracker.csv (stage, touch date, next action).", ""]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text("\n".join(L), encoding="utf-8")
    return filled


def write_final(path: Path, title: str, msg_type: str, ctx: dict, filled: list[dict], cadence: list[dict],
                thread: dict | None, stop_note: str) -> None:
    """message-final.md without a model step: the filled variants on the final template's sections."""
    L = [f"# {title} — {ctx['role']}, {ctx['company']}", "",
         "> Script draft — the model polish step was not run (draft only): the filled skeleton, facts from "
         "context.json only; unfilled slots stay owned markers.", ""]
    if stop_note:
        L += [f"**{stop_note}**", ""]
    a, b = filled[0], (filled[1] if len(filled) > 1 else None)
    L += ["## Message", f"Variant: {a['key']} — {a['label']}", "", a["text"], ""]
    if b:
        L += ["## Alternate variant", f"Variant: {b['key']} — {b['label']}", "", b["text"], ""]
    L += ["## Facts used", "| Fact | Source |", "|---|---|"]
    facts = [f for f in ctx["_facts"] if not (thread and used_in_thread(f, thread))]
    L += [f"| {f.replace('|', '/')} | context.json" + (f" / {', '.join(ID_RE.findall(f))}" if ID_RE.search(f) else "") + " |"
          for f in facts] or [f"| none supplied | {TBD} |"]
    L += ["", "## Cadence", "| Touch | Date | Channel | Basis |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {r['touch']} | {r['date'] or TBD} | {r['channel']} | {r['basis']} |" for r in cadence]
    L += ["", f"Stop rule: {cadence[0]['stop_rule'] if cadence else '—'}",
          "Log: add a row to tracker.csv (stage, touch date, next action).", ""]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text("\n".join(L), encoding="utf-8")


def write_cadence(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["touch", "date", "channel", "template", "basis", "stop_rule"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Fill a job-search message skeleton from context.json and date the cadence")
    ap.add_argument("--type", required=True, choices=sorted(TYPES))
    ap.add_argument("--context", required=True, help="context.json")
    ap.add_argument("--templates", default="assets/message-templates.md")
    ap.add_argument("--cadence-ref", default="references/cadence.md")
    ap.add_argument("--message", required=True, help="output message.md")
    ap.add_argument("--cadence", required=True, help="output cadence.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--thread", default="", help="the conversation so far (## YYYY-MM-DD — sent|received headings)")
    ap.add_argument("--final", default="", help="final message path (written with --draft-only)")
    ap.add_argument("--draft-only", action="store_true", help="no model step: write --final from the filled skeleton")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    ctx = load_context(a.context)
    thread = read_thread(read(a.thread)) if a.thread else None
    if thread is not None:
        ctx["_last"] = thread["sent"][0]["date"]      # cadence days count from the first message sent
        ctx["last_touch_date"] = thread["messages"][-1]["date"].isoformat()
    title, variants = load_variants(read(a.templates), TYPES[a.type]["section"])
    rows = build_cadence(read(a.cadence_ref), a.type, ctx, f"{TYPES[a.type]['section']}{variants[0]['key']} {variants[0]['label']}")
    if not rows:
        die("no touches found for this message type in cadence.md")
    stop_note = ""
    if thread is not None:
        done = len(thread["sent"])
        remaining = rows[done:]
        if not remaining:
            stop_note = f"Cadence exhausted after {done} touch(es) — stop rule: {rows[0]['stop_rule']}. Do not send another."
            remaining = [{**rows[-1], "touch": "Stop", "date": "", "template": "none",
                          "basis": f"{done} touch(es) already sent — {rows[0]['stop_rule']}"}]
        rows = remaining
    filled = write_message(Path(a.message), a.type, title, variants, ctx, rows, thread, stop_note)
    write_cadence(Path(a.cadence), rows)
    if a.draft_only and a.final:
        write_final(Path(a.final), title, a.type, ctx, filled, rows, thread, stop_note)
    print(f"{a.type}: {len(variants)} variants, {len(rows)} cadence touches; wrote {a.message}, {a.cadence}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Follow-up Cadence

Business days. "Stop" means stop initiating; respond if they reach out.

| Situation | Touch 1 | Touch 2 | Touch 3 | Stop rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Referral ask (warm contact) | Day 0 LinkedIn or email | Day 5 same channel, add one new detail | Day 12 different channel | Stop after 3; thank and move on |
| Referral ask (cold contact) | Day 0 connection note | Day 7 InMail if accepted | — | Stop after 2 |
| Recruiter inbound | Reply within 1 business day | — | — | Not applicable |
| Applied, no response | Day 7 referral or recruiter nudge | Day 14 hiring-manager LinkedIn note | — | Stop after 2; mark "Ghosted" at day 30 |
| Post-interview thank-you | Within 24 h | — | — | One per interviewer |
| Awaiting decision (timeline given) | Timeline date + 2 | +7 | — | Stop after 2; move to "Stalled" |
| Awaiting decision (no timeline) | Day 5 ask for timeline | Day 12 | Day 20 | Stop after 3 |
| Competing offer in hand | Immediately, state the deadline | Deadline − 2 | — | Decide at deadline |
| Offer received, negotiating | Within 2 days: thank + request call | Call | Written confirmation same day | — |
| After decline (yours or theirs) | Day 0 clean close | Day 90 light touch (article, congratulations) | Every 90–120 days | Keep as network contact |

## Escalation ladder (applied, no response)
1. Recruiter who posted the role.
2. Referrer, asking them to ping internally.
3. Hiring manager on LinkedIn with a 2-sentence value note.
4. Stop. Log in tracker as "Ghosted" with date.

## Timing rules
- Send Tue–Thu, 7:30–9:30 a.m. recipient local time, or within 10 minutes of their last message.
- Never follow up on a Monday morning or Friday afternoon.
- Each follow-up adds one new element (news, availability change, relevant insight). Never resend the same note.
- Count touches across channels, not per channel.

## Tracker integration
After each touch, update tracker.csv: `last_touch`, `next_action`, `next_action_date`. The `application-tracker` aging rules read these fields.

# Message Types — Rules

Universal tone rules: peer-to-peer, direct, specific, warm without flattery. One ask per message. First sentence states why you are writing. No "I hope this finds you well", no "just checking in", no exclamation marks, no apologizing for writing.

| Type | Goal | Length | Must include | Must avoid | Variant strategies |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Referral ask | Get a named insider to refer or introduce | LinkedIn ≤300 chars (connect) / email ≤150 words | Specific role + req ID, why you (1 sourced outcome), the exact ask, easy out ("if it's not a fit, no worries") | Attaching résumé unasked, multiple roles, guilt | **Direct ask** (fast, risks a no) · **Advice-first** (15-min call about the team; slower, builds relationship) · **Mutual-contact bridge** (via shared connection) |
| Recruiter reply | Advance to a screen with your constraints on record | ≤120 words | Interest level, 2 availability windows, comp expectation as a range or request for their band, location/travel constraint in one line | Over-explaining tenure, listing all skills, enthusiasm inflation | **Lead with fit** (strong role match) · **Qualify first** (ask band/location before committing time) · **Redirect** (not this role; what you would consider) |
| Post-interview thank-you | Reinforce one point, fix one gap, keep momentum | ≤120 words, within 24 h, one per interviewer | Reference one specific thing they said, one value point you bring to it, next step as you understand it | Generic gratitude, restating résumé, new asks | **Reinforce** (strongest point) · **Repair** (clarify a weak answer in 2 sentences) · **Bridge** (connect their stated priority to your 90-day thinking) |
| Status check | Get a decision or a date without seeming anxious | ≤90 words | Date of last contact, the timeline they gave, a reason to write now (new info, competing timeline, availability), explicit question | "Just following up", pressure, ultimatums (except the competing-offer variant) | **Light touch** (new information + question) · **Timeline** (competing process, need a date) · **Value add** (share a relevant article/insight, then ask) |
| Decline | Exit cleanly and keep the door open | ≤100 words | Thank specific person, one honest reason category (role scope, comp, timing, location), willingness to stay in touch | Detailed critique, bluffing, negotiation disguised as decline | **Clean close** · **Door open** (specific future scenario) · **Refer** (suggest a contact if appropriate) |
| Negotiation open | Start the comp conversation from a position of partnership | ≤150 words | Enthusiasm for the role, the gap stated as a number or lever, market/context justification, a proposed next step (call) | Ultimatums, multiple asks at once, apologizing for asking | **Base first** (single biggest lever) · **Package** (base + sign-on + start date bundled) · **Non-cash** (title, scope, remote, review timing) |

## Channel rules
| Channel | Use for | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn connection note | Cold or warm first touch | 300 characters |
| LinkedIn InMail / message | Known contacts, recruiters | 150 words |
| Email | Anything after first contact; thank-yous; negotiation | 180 words |
| Text | Only if they texted first; scheduling only | 2 sentences |

## Level signals (Sr Director / VP)
- Cite scale once (team, budget, outcome) — not a list.
- Speak about their business problem before your background.
- Offer time windows; do not ask "when works for you?".
- Sign with name and one-line title; no inspirational quotes.

# Résumé Tailor (truth-locked)

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/resume-tailor --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/resume-tailor`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## Starting points
- **New** — the JD's keywords are mapped to your master résumé (gaps go to you, never into the résumé); the model writes the tailored résumé, or with `draft_only` it is assembled from verbatim master lines; either way every bullet must trace to a master line.
- **Existing** — add a résumé you already tailored: it is kept word for word, every bullet is traced against the master, and the supported JD keywords it does not cite yet are added as verbatim, cited bullets under "Additions for this JD".

## When to use
- "Tailor my résumé for this JD", "make this ATS-friendly", "rewrite my summary for a VP role", "which keywords am I missing".
- After `jd-fit-scorer` returns GO / LEAN GO.
- NOT for: scoring fit (use `jd-fit-scorer`), cover letters or recruiter messages (use `outreach-and-followup`), interview stories (use `interview-prep`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Master résumé (full, untailored, with line numbers or stable bullet IDs) | yes | user file; format in `assets/master-resume.example.md` |
| JD full text | yes | user paste |
| Target title and level | no | JD; default Sr Director |
| Fit output from `jd-fit-scorer` | no | prior step; speeds keyword mapping |
| Page limit and format (2-page, ATS plain, LinkedIn) | no | user; default 2-page ATS plain |

If the master résumé is missing, stop and ask for it. Do not build from memory, LinkedIn recollection, or prior conversations.

## TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)
1. The master résumé is the only source of facts: employers, titles, dates, team sizes, budgets, metrics, technologies, awards.
2. Every tailored bullet carries a source reference `[MR-L<line>]` or `[MR-<bullet-id>]`.
3. Allowed transformations: reorder, reword, merge two source bullets, drop detail, change emphasis, swap synonyms for JD keywords **when the master résumé supports the underlying fact**.
4. Not allowed: new metrics, inflated numbers, new technologies, new scope, new titles, implied certifications, "led" where the source says "contributed to".
5. If the user asks to add a claim with no source line, refuse that claim, explain why in one sentence, and offer two options: (a) add the fact to the master résumé first with their confirmation it is true, or (b) phrase the adjacent true fact instead. Continue with the rest of the tailoring.
6. The output must include a traceability table. A bullet with no source row is a defect; remove it before returning.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Number the master résumé lines if not already numbered (`MR-L1`…). Do not alter content.
3. Build the ATS keyword map per `references/ats-keyword-mapping.md`: JD keyword → exact/synonym → master résumé evidence line → placement (summary, core competencies, bullet, skills).
4. Flag JD keywords with no evidence as **UNSUPPORTED**. These go in the gap note to the user, never into the résumé.
5. Rewrite the executive summary (≤4 lines) using only supported keywords; structure per `references/executive-resume-structure.md`.
6. Rewrite bullets with the formula in `references/bullet-formula.md`. Prioritize the 8–12 bullets most relevant to the JD's must-haves; demote the rest. Patterns (not facts) are in `assets/bullet-bank.md`.
7. Produce the before/after diff per `references/diff-format.md`.
8. Produce the traceability table: tailored bullet → `[MR-Lxx]` → transformation type.
9. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

## Output
Markdown file `resume-<company>-<role>.md` containing, in order:
1. Keyword map table (JD keyword | status | evidence | placement)
2. Tailored résumé (ATS plain: no tables, no columns, no graphics, standard headings)
3. Before/after diff
4. Traceability table
5. Unsupported-claims note (what the JD wants that the master résumé cannot support, and what to do about it)

## Self-check
- [ ] Every tailored bullet has a `[MR-…]` source and appears in the traceability table
- [ ] No number, employer, title, date, or technology appears that is absent from the master résumé
- [ ] Any user-requested unsupported claim was refused with an explanation and alternatives
- [ ] Summary ≤4 lines; bullets ≤2 lines each; action verb first; metric present where the source has one
- [ ] ATS plain formatting: standard section names, no tables inside the résumé body, dates as `Mon YYYY – Mon YYYY`
- [ ] Banned words from `writing-style.md` absent (leverage, synergy, robust, seamless, cutting-edge)
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; everything comes from the supplied master résumé

## References
- `scripts/tailor.py` — JD keyword → master-line evidence map, gap list, verbatim candidate bullets (stdlib, offline)
- `scripts/check_traceability.py` — the TRUTH LOCK gate: exit 1 on an uncited bullet, an unknown id, or a number absent from its cited lines
- `assets/tailored-resume-template.md` — the llm step fills this; every bullet ends with `[MR-Lnn]`
- `references/ats-keyword-mapping.md` — mapping method, synonym rules, density limits
- `references/bullet-formula.md` — action + scope + metric + outcome, exec verbs, anti-patterns
- `references/executive-resume-structure.md` — section order, length, what to cut at exec level
- `references/diff-format.md` — before/after and traceability table layouts
- `assets/master-resume.example.md` — EXAMPLE master résumé format (fictional)
- `assets/bullet-bank.md` — reusable bullet patterns (no facts)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prove every bullet of a tailored résumé traces to the master résumé — the TRUTH LOCK gate.

    python3 -I scripts/check_traceability.py --resume tailored-resume.md --master master-resume.md \
        --out traceability.csv

Units checked ("bullets"): every list item (`- `, `* `, `1. `) anywhere in the résumé, plus every prose
line under the `## Summary` heading. Headings, tables, blockquotes, HTML comments and blank lines are
not checked (role headers `### Employer — Title (dates)` are copied from the master's own headers).

For each bullet, traceability.csv records: bullet (first 80 chars), cited_ids, all_ids_exist (yes/no),
numbers_in_bullet_found_in_cited_lines (yes/no). Exit 1 — and the run halts — when any bullet
  * carries no `[MR-Lnn]` citation,
  * cites an id that is not a line of the master résumé, or
  * contains a number, percentage or dollar figure that none of its cited lines contains.
A file carrying `<!-- dry-run: template unfilled -->` (the runner's dry provider) has no bullets to
check: the CSV is written with its header only and the gate passes with evidence "dry-run template".
Exit 1 on a missing file or a master without MR-L ids. Stdlib only, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

DRY_MARKER = "<!-- dry-run: template unfilled -->"
MR_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(MR-L\d+)\s*\|\s*(.*)$")
CITE_RE = re.compile(r"\[(MR-L\d+(?:\s*,\s*MR-L\d+)*)\]")
BULLET_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*•]|\d+[.)])\s+(.*)$")
# a number not glued to a letter or slash on the left (so S/4HANA's 4 is not a number) — $, %, M/K suffixes allowed
NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9/.])\$?(\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)")
FIELDS = ["bullet", "cited_ids", "all_ids_exist", "numbers_in_bullet_found_in_cited_lines"]


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def read(path: str) -> str:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_master(path: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    lines = {}
    for raw in read(path).splitlines():
        m = MR_LINE_RE.match(raw)
        if m:
            lines[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
    if not lines:
        die("master résumé has no `MR-Lnn | text` lines (see assets/master-resume.example.md)")
    return lines


def numbers(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return [n.replace(",", "") for n in NUMBER_RE.findall(text)]


def units(resume: str) -> list[str]:
    """Bullets anywhere + prose lines under '## Summary'."""
    out, in_summary = [], False
    for raw in resume.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip()
        if line.startswith("#"):
            in_summary = line.lstrip("#").strip().lower().startswith("summary")
            continue
        s = line.strip()
        if not s or s.startswith(("<!--", "|", ">", "_", "```")):
            continue
        m = BULLET_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            out.append(m.group(1).strip())
        elif in_summary:
            out.append(s)
    return out


def check(resume: str, master: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[str]]:
    rows, problems = [], []
    for u in units(resume):
        ids = []
        for m in CITE_RE.finditer(u):
            ids += [i.strip() for i in m.group(1).split(",")]
        text = CITE_RE.sub("", u).strip()
        label = text[:80]
        if not ids:
            rows.append({"bullet": label, "cited_ids": "", "all_ids_exist": "no",
                         "numbers_in_bullet_found_in_cited_lines": "no"})
            problems.append(f"no citation: {label}")
            continue
        missing = [i for i in ids if i not in master]
        cited_text = " ".join(master.get(i, "") for i in ids)
        cited_nums = set(numbers(cited_text))
        untraced = sorted({n for n in numbers(text) if n not in cited_nums})
        rows.append({"bullet": label, "cited_ids": ";".join(ids), "all_ids_exist": "no" if missing else "yes",
                     "numbers_in_bullet_found_in_cited_lines": "no" if untraced else "yes"})
        if missing:
            problems.append(f"unknown id(s) {missing}: {label}")
        if untraced:
            problems.append(f"number(s) {untraced} not in cited lines {ids}: {label}")
    return rows, problems


def write_csv(rows: list[dict], path: Path) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=FIELDS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="TRUTH LOCK gate: every résumé bullet cites existing MR-L lines "
                                             "and introduces no number they do not contain")
    ap.add_argument("--resume", required=True, help="tailored résumé (Markdown)")
    ap.add_argument("--master", required=True, help="master résumé with MR-Lnn | line ids")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="traceability.csv")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    resume = read(a.resume)
    master = load_master(a.master)
    out = Path(a.out)
    if DRY_MARKER in resume:
        write_csv([], out)
        print(f"0 bullets checked (dry-run template); wrote {out}")
        return 0
    rows, problems = check(resume, master)
    write_csv(rows, out)
    if not rows:
        print("TRUTH LOCK: the résumé has no bullets or summary lines to check", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    n_ok = sum(1 for r in rows if r["all_ids_exist"] == "yes" and r["numbers_in_bullet_found_in_cited_lines"] == "yes")
    if problems:
        for pr in problems:
            print(f"TRUTH LOCK: {pr}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"{len(rows)} bullets checked, {len(rows) - n_ok} fail the truth lock; wrote {out}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"{len(rows)} bullets checked, all trace to the master résumé; wrote {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Map JD keywords to master-résumé evidence lines — the deterministic half of the TRUTH LOCK.

    python3 -I scripts/tailor.py --jd jd.txt --master master-resume.md \
        --keyword-map keyword-map.csv --gap-list gap-list.md --bullets candidate-bullets.md

master-resume.md: every fact line is numbered `MR-Lnn | text` (layout: assets/master-resume.example.md).

What it does, deterministically:
  * extracts keywords from the JD's requirement lines — proper nouns and acronyms (SAP S/4HANA, FinOps,
    MBA), noun phrases with a known head (ERP consolidation, API gateway, vendor management), scale
    markers ($25M budget, 10+ years) — and weights each `must` or `nice` from the line's own wording;
  * looks for literal support in the master résumé: every content token of the keyword (crudely
    stemmed) on one MR line, or a scale marker that the MR meets or exceeds. No synonym guessing;
  * keyword-map.csv  — jd_keyword, present_in_master (yes/no), master_line_ids, weight;
  * gap-list.md      — keywords with no support. They go to the user, never into the résumé;
  * candidate-bullets.md — for every supported JD must-have (then nice-to-have), the supporting
    master lines quoted VERBATIM with their ids. The script rewrites nothing; the llm step does, and
    scripts/check_traceability.py proves every bullet it writes still traces.
--draft-only --final tailored-resume.md: no model step — the tailored résumé is assembled from master lines
quoted verbatim with their ids (Summary = the master's summary lines; Selected experience = the lines
that support JD keywords, must-haves first, under the master's own role headers; Skills = supported JD
keywords without figures, each citing its lines; Education = the master's education lines), so
check_traceability.py passes by construction. Labelled as a draft.
--existing tailored.md --final tailored-resume.md: a résumé you already tailored is kept verbatim and
extended — every supported JD keyword whose master lines it does not cite yet gets one verbatim, cited
bullet under "Additions for this JD" — so the trace gate checks your text and the additions together.
Exit 1 on a missing/empty file or a master résumé without MR-L ids. Stdlib only, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MR_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(MR-L\d+)\s*\|\s*(.*)$")
TBD_RESUME = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Candidate]"
NICE_RE = re.compile(r"nice[- ]to[- ]have|preferred|a plus|is a plus|ideally|bonus|desirable|nice to", re.I)
MUST_RE = re.compile(r"\bmust\b|\brequired\b|\brequire[sd]?\b|\bminimum\b", re.I)
LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"^(must[- ]haves?|nice[- ]to[- ]haves?|required|preferred|requirements?|qualifications?|"
                      r"responsibilities|you (?:will|have)|what you(?:'ll)? bring)\s*[:\-–]\s*", re.I)
PAREN_RE = re.compile(r"\(([^()]{2,60})\)")
MONEY_RE = re.compile(r"\$\s?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([MBK])\b", re.I)
YEARS_RE = re.compile(r"(\d+)\s*\+?\s*years?", re.I)
HEADS = ("consolidation", "modernization", "modernisation", "migration", "management", "integration",
         "integrations", "gateway", "program", "programs", "platform", "platforms", "leadership", "governance",
         "transformation", "architecture", "engineering", "strategy", "roadmap", "optimization", "operations",
         "security", "compliance", "analytics", "automation", "delivery", "negotiation", "committee",
         "re-platform", "replatform", "remediation", "certification", "payer", "payers", "domain")
# single words that stand as keywords on their own (industries, platforms-as-words, functions)
STANDALONE = {"insurance", "healthcare", "claims", "enrollment", "manufacturing", "retail", "banking", "payer",
              "vendor", "vendors", "outsourcing", "procurement", "cybersecurity", "privacy", "audit"}
TEAM_RE = re.compile(r"team of (\d+)|(\d+)\s*\+?\s*(?:people|engineers|staff|fte|direct reports|employees)", re.I)
STOP = {"a", "an", "the", "and", "or", "of", "with", "in", "for", "to", "on", "at", "by", "is", "are", "be",
        "have", "has", "must", "required", "preferred", "experience", "strong", "proven", "demonstrated",
        "ability", "plus", "nice", "ideally", "years", "year", "more", "least", "minimum", "including",
        "across", "within", "large", "scale", "we", "you", "our", "your", "as", "that", "this", "such",
        "etc", "e.g", "eg", "ie", "i.e", "value", "role", "candidate", "team", "teams", "working", "own",
        "owned", "owning", "leading", "lead", "led", "managing", "manage", "managed", "building", "build",
        "track", "record", "hands", "deep", "solid", "relevant", "equivalent", "comparable", "similar",
        "exposure", "end", "or", "and", "related"}
GENERIC_CAPS = {"Must", "Nice", "Required", "Preferred", "Experience", "Strong", "Proven", "Ability", "We",
                "You", "Our", "The", "A", "An", "Location", "Travel", "Requirements", "Responsibilities",
                "Bachelor", "Master", "Degree", "Minimum", "Plus", "Senior", "Director", "Vice", "President",
                "Manager", "Lead", "Head", "Chief", "Reports", "Reporting", "Hybrid", "Remote", "Onsite",
                "Up", "Yes", "No", "Title", "Company", "Team", "Role", "About", "What", "Who", "How", "Led",
                "Lead", "Leading", "Managed", "Owned", "Own", "Delivered", "Built", "Drive", "Driven", "Track",
                "Demonstrated", "Deep", "Hands", "Familiarity", "Knowledge", "Understanding", "Excellent",
                "Exceptional", "Partner", "Collaborate", "Develop", "Define", "Ensure", "Oversee", "Establish",
                "Champion", "Serve", "Act", "Work", "Provide", "Support", "Maintain", "Create", "Set", "Shape",
                "Run", "Cloud", "Enterprise", "Comparable", "Must-have", "Nice-to-have"}


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def read(path: str) -> str:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if not text.strip():
        die(f"file is empty: {p}")
    return text


def stem(tok: str) -> str:
    t = tok.lower().strip("'\"“”.,;:()")
    for suf in ("ations", "ation", "ating", "ated", "ities", "ity", "ness", "ments", "ment", "ings", "ing",
                "ies", "ers", "er", "ed", "es", "s"):
        if len(t) > len(suf) + 3 and t.endswith(suf):
            return t[: -len(suf)]
    return t


def content_tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    toks = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+#./-]*", text)
    return [stem(t) for t in toks if t.lower() not in STOP and len(t) > 1]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ master résumé

def load_master(path: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    lines = []
    for raw in read(path).splitlines():
        m = MR_LINE_RE.match(raw)
        if m:
            lines.append((m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()))
    if not lines:
        die("master résumé has no `MR-Lnn | text` lines (see assets/master-resume.example.md)")
    return lines


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ JD keywords

def clean_phrase(p: str) -> str:
    p = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", p).strip(" ,;:.-–—")
    p = re.sub(r"\b(?:is )?(?:strongly )?(?:preferred|required|a plus|desirable|ideally|nice to have)\b", "", p, flags=re.I)
    return p.strip(" ,;:.-–—")


def caps_runs(clause: str) -> list[str]:
    """Runs of capitalised / acronym / versioned tokens, e.g. 'SAP S/4HANA', 'FinOps', 'MBA'."""
    out, run = [], []
    toks = clause.split()
    for i, tok in enumerate(toks):
        bare = tok.strip("“”\"'(),.;:")
        is_cap = bool(re.match(r"^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9+#./-]*$", bare)) and bare not in GENERIC_CAPS and not (
            i == 0 and bare.lower() in STOP)
        has_inner_cap = bool(re.search(r"[a-z][A-Z]", bare)) or bool(re.search(r"[A-Z]{2}", bare)) or \
            bool(re.search(r"\d", bare))
        keep = bare and (is_cap or (has_inner_cap and bare[0].isalpha() and bare not in GENERIC_CAPS))
        nxt = toks[i + 1].lower() if i + 1 < len(toks) else ""
        verb_like = bare.istitle() and not has_inner_cap and (bare.lower().endswith(("ed", "ing"))
                                                              or nxt in STOP and nxt != "")
        if keep and not (i == 0 and verb_like):
            run.append(bare)
        else:
            if run:
                out.append(" ".join(run))
            run = []
        if tok.endswith((",", ";", ".", ")", ":")) and run:
            out.append(" ".join(run))
            run = []
    if run:
        out.append(" ".join(run))
    return [r for r in out if len(r) >= 2 and not re.fullmatch(r"\d+[%+]?", r)]


def head_phrases(clause: str) -> list[str]:
    """'cloud cost management', 'API gateway', 'ERP consolidation' — up to 3 content words + a head noun."""
    out = []
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+#./-]*", clause)
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        wl = w.lower()
        if wl in HEADS:
            pre = []
            for prev in reversed(words[max(0, i - 3): i]):
                if prev.lower() in STOP or prev.lower() in HEADS:
                    break
                pre.insert(0, prev)
            if pre:
                out.append(" ".join(pre + [w]))
            elif wl in STANDALONE:
                out.append(w)
        elif wl in STANDALONE:
            out.append(w)
    return out


def scale_markers(line: str) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    out = []
    for m in MONEY_RE.finditer(line):
        label = f"${m.group(1)}{m.group(2).upper()}" + (" budget" if re.search(r"budget|p&l|portfolio", line, re.I) else "")
        out.append((label, {"money": float(m.group(1)), "unit": m.group(2).upper()}))
    for m in YEARS_RE.finditer(line):
        out.append((f"{m.group(1)}+ years", {"years": int(m.group(1))}))
    for m in TEAM_RE.finditer(line):
        n = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
        out.append((f"team of {n}", {"team": int(n)}))
    return out


def extract_keywords(jd_text: str) -> list[dict]:
    """[{keyword, weight, line}] in JD order, deduplicated case-insensitively."""
    found, seen = [], set()
    section_nice = False
    for raw in jd_text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        header = re.match(r"^(nice[- ]to[- ]haves?|preferred(?: qualifications)?|bonus|desirable)\s*:?\s*$", line, re.I)
        if header:
            section_nice = True
            continue
        if re.match(r"^(must[- ]haves?|required|requirements|responsibilities|qualifications)\s*:?\s*$", line, re.I):
            section_nice = False
            continue
        is_req = bool(re.match(r"^[-*•\d.)]+\s+", line)) or MUST_RE.search(line) or NICE_RE.search(line)
        if not is_req:
            continue
        body = re.sub(r"^[-*•\d.)]+\s+", "", line)
        body = LABEL_RE.sub("", body)
        stripped = PAREN_RE.sub(" ", body)
        weight = "nice" if (NICE_RE.search(stripped) or section_nice) and not re.search(r"\bmust\b", stripped, re.I) \
            else "must"
        cands: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        for m in PAREN_RE.finditer(body):
            w = "nice" if NICE_RE.search(m.group(1)) else weight
            cands += [(clean_phrase(x), w) for x in re.split(r",|/(?!\d)| or ", m.group(1))]
        for clause in re.split(r",|;| and | or |/(?!\d)|\bwith\b|\bincluding\b", stripped):
            cands += [(c, weight) for c in caps_runs(clause)]
            cands += [(c, weight) for c in head_phrases(clause)]
        for label, _ in scale_markers(body):
            cands.append((label, weight))
        for c, w in cands:
            c = clean_phrase(c)
            if not c or len(c) < 2 or c.lower() in STOP:
                continue
            key = c.lower()
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            found.append({"keyword": c, "weight": w, "line": body})
    # drop a one-word keyword that is merely a token of a longer keyword from the same line
    keep = []
    for k in found:
        longer = [o for o in found if o is not k and o["line"] == k["line"] and k["keyword"].lower() in o["keyword"].lower()
                  and len(o["keyword"]) > len(k["keyword"])]
        if longer and " " not in k["keyword"]:
            continue
        keep.append(k)
    return keep


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ matching

def money_in(text: str) -> list[tuple[float, str]]:
    return [(float(m.group(1)), m.group(2).upper()) for m in MONEY_RE.finditer(text)]


def supports(keyword: str, text: str) -> bool:
    kl, tl = keyword.lower(), text.lower()
    if re.search(r"(?<![a-z0-9])" + re.escape(kl) + r"(?![a-z0-9])", tl):
        return True
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\$(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)([MBK])(?: budget)?", keyword)
    if m:
        want, unit = float(m.group(1)), m.group(2)
        return any(u == unit and v >= want for v, u in money_in(text))
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)\+ years", keyword)
    if m:
        return any(int(y) >= int(m.group(1)) for y in YEARS_RE.findall(text))
    m = re.fullmatch(r"team of (\d+)", keyword)
    if m:
        return any(int(a or b) >= int(m.group(1)) for a, b in TEAM_RE.findall(text))
    toks = content_tokens(keyword)
    if not toks:
        return False
    ttoks = set(content_tokens(text))

    def present(t: str) -> bool:
        return t in ttoks or (len(t) >= 5 and any(t in x for x in ttoks))
    return all(present(t) for t in toks)


def map_keywords(keywords: list[dict], master: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for k in keywords:
        ids = [mid for mid, text in master if supports(k["keyword"], text)]
        rows.append({"jd_keyword": k["keyword"], "present_in_master": "yes" if ids else "no",
                     "master_line_ids": ";".join(ids), "weight": k["weight"], "jd_line": k["line"]})
    return rows


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ outputs

def write_map(rows: list[dict], path: Path) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["jd_keyword", "present_in_master", "master_line_ids", "weight"],
                           extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def write_gaps(rows: list[dict], path: Path) -> None:
    gaps = [r for r in rows if r["present_in_master"] == "no"]
    lines = ["# Gap list — JD keywords with no support in the master résumé", "",
             "Rule (TRUTH LOCK): nothing on this list goes into the résumé. If the master résumé supports a "
             "keyword under another name, add the JD term to that master line first (SYNONYM rule in "
             "`references/ats-keyword-mapping.md`), then re-run. Otherwise the gap is addressed in the "
             "interview or accepted.", ""]
    if not gaps:
        lines += ["None — every extracted JD keyword has at least one supporting master line.", ""]
    else:
        lines += ["| JD keyword | Weight | JD line | Option |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
        for g in gaps:
            lines.append(f"| {g['jd_keyword']} | {g['weight']} | {g['jd_line'][:90]} | "
                         f"Add to master résumé only if true (user confirms), else omit |")
        lines.append("")
    n_must = sum(1 for g in gaps if g["weight"] == "must")
    lines += [f"Unsupported: {len(gaps)} of {len(rows)} keywords ({n_must} must-have).", ""]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")


def write_bullets(rows: list[dict], master: list[tuple[str, str]], path: Path) -> None:
    by_id = dict(master)
    lines = ["# Candidate bullets — supporting master lines, quoted verbatim", "",
             "Each JD keyword below has literal support in the master résumé. The lines are the ONLY raw "
             "material for the tailored résumé; every tailored bullet must end with the `[MR-Lnn]` id(s) it "
             "came from, and `scripts/check_traceability.py` fails the run otherwise.", ""]
    for weight, title in (("must", "JD must-haves"), ("nice", "JD nice-to-haves")):
        sel = [r for r in rows if r["weight"] == weight and r["present_in_master"] == "yes"]
        lines += [f"## {title} with support ({len(sel)})", ""]
        if not sel:
            lines += ["(none)", ""]
        for r in sel:
            lines += [f"### {r['jd_keyword']}", ""]
            for mid in r["master_line_ids"].split(";"):
                lines.append(f"- [{mid}] {by_id[mid]}")
            lines.append("")
    unsupported = [r["jd_keyword"] for r in rows if r["present_in_master"] == "no"]
    lines += ["## Unsupported keywords (see gap-list.md)", "",
              ("- " + "\n- ".join(unsupported)) if unsupported else "(none)", ""]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")


def master_layout(path: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]:
    """id -> enclosing '## ' section title, id -> enclosing '### ' role header (or '')."""
    section, role, sec_of, role_of = "", "", {}, {}
    for raw in read(path).splitlines():
        if raw.startswith("## "):
            section, role = raw[3:].strip(), ""
        elif raw.startswith("### "):
            role = raw[4:].strip()
        m = MR_LINE_RE.match(raw)
        if m:
            sec_of[m.group(1)], role_of[m.group(1)] = section, role
    return sec_of, role_of


CITED_RE = re.compile(r"\[(MR-L\d+(?:\s*,\s*MR-L\d+)*)\]")
DRAFT_LABEL = ("<!-- Script draft: the model step was not run (draft only). Every line is a master-résumé line quoted "
               "verbatim with its id; reword it yourself, keeping the [MR-Lnn] ids. -->")


def assemble_draft(rows: list[dict], master: list[tuple[str, str]], master_path: str, jd_title: str) -> str:
    by_id = dict(master)
    sec_of, role_of = master_layout(master_path)
    L = [f"# Tailored résumé — {jd_title}", "", DRAFT_LABEL, "", "## Summary", ""]
    summary = [mid for mid, _ in master if sec_of.get(mid, "").lower().startswith("summary")]
    L += [f"- {by_id[mid]} [{mid}]" for mid in summary] or [f"- {TBD_RESUME}"]
    picked: list[str] = []
    for weight in ("must", "nice"):
        for r in rows:
            if r["weight"] == weight and r["present_in_master"] == "yes":
                for mid in r["master_line_ids"].split(";"):
                    if mid not in picked and role_of.get(mid):
                        picked.append(mid)
    L += ["", "## Selected experience", ""]
    roles = list(dict.fromkeys(role_of[m] for m, _ in master if m in picked))
    for role in roles:
        L += [f"### {role}", ""] + [f"- {by_id[m]} [{m}]" for m, _ in master if m in picked and role_of[m] == role] + [""]
    if not roles:
        L += [f"- {TBD_RESUME}", ""]
    L += ["## Skills", ""]
    skills = [r for r in rows if r["present_in_master"] == "yes" and not re.search(r"\d", r["jd_keyword"])]
    L += [f"- {r['jd_keyword']} [{', '.join(r['master_line_ids'].split(';')[:2])}]" for r in skills] or [f"- {TBD_RESUME}"]
    edu = [mid for mid, _ in master if sec_of.get(mid, "").lower().startswith("education")]
    L += ["", "## Education and certifications", ""] + ([f"- {by_id[m]} [{m}]" for m in edu] or [f"- {TBD_RESUME}"])
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def extend_existing(existing: str, rows: list[dict], master: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    by_id = dict(master)
    cited = set()
    for m in CITED_RE.finditer(existing):
        cited |= {i.strip() for i in m.group(1).split(",")}
    adds, keys = [], []
    for weight in ("must", "nice"):
        for r in rows:
            if r["weight"] != weight or r["present_in_master"] != "yes":
                continue
            ids = r["master_line_ids"].split(";")
            if cited & set(ids):
                continue
            mid = ids[0]
            if mid not in {a[0] for a in adds}:
                adds.append((mid, r["jd_keyword"]))
            keys.append(r["jd_keyword"])
    out = existing.rstrip("\n") + "\n"
    if adds:
        out += ("\n## Additions for this JD\n\n<!-- Verbatim master lines for JD keywords your résumé does not cite yet; "
                "move each into place and reword, keeping the id. -->\n\n")
        out += "\n".join(f"- {by_id[mid]} [{mid}]" for mid, _ in adds) + "\n"
    return out, keys


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="JD keyword → master-résumé evidence map (truth-locked, no rewriting)")
    ap.add_argument("--jd", required=True, help="job description text file")
    ap.add_argument("--master", required=True, help="master résumé with MR-Lnn | line ids")
    ap.add_argument("--keyword-map", required=True, help="output CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--gap-list", required=True, help="output Markdown")
    ap.add_argument("--bullets", required=True, help="output Markdown (verbatim supporting lines)")
    ap.add_argument("--final", default="", help="tailored résumé path (written with --draft-only or --existing)")
    ap.add_argument("--draft-only", action="store_true", help="no model step: assemble --final from verbatim master lines")
    ap.add_argument("--existing", default="", help="a résumé you already tailored, to check and extend for this JD")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    jd = read(a.jd)
    master = load_master(a.master)
    keywords = extract_keywords(jd)
    if not keywords:
        die("no requirement lines found in the JD (expected bullets or lines with must/required/preferred)")
    rows = map_keywords(keywords, master)
    write_map(rows, Path(a.keyword_map))
    write_gaps(rows, Path(a.gap_list))
    write_bullets(rows, master, Path(a.bullets))
    if a.existing and a.final:
        text, missing = extend_existing(read(a.existing), rows, master)
        Path(a.final).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"existing résumé kept; {len(missing)} supported JD keyword(s) it did not cite: {', '.join(missing) or 'none'}")
    elif a.draft_only and a.final:
        title = next((ln.strip() for ln in jd.splitlines() if ln.strip()), "role")[:100]
        Path(a.final).write_text(assemble_draft(rows, master, a.master, title), encoding="utf-8")
    n_yes = sum(r["present_in_master"] == "yes" for r in rows)
    print(f"{len(rows)} JD keywords: {n_yes} supported, {len(rows) - n_yes} unsupported; "
          f"{len(master)} master lines; wrote {a.keyword_map}, {a.gap_list}, {a.bullets}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

skills/career/resume-tailor/references/a:
# ATS Keyword Mapping Method

## Step 1 — Extract JD keywords
| Type | How to spot | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Hard skills / platforms | Proper nouns, acronyms, product names | Apigee, SAP S/4HANA, ServiceNow, Snowflake |
| Competencies | Verb + object phrases in responsibilities | "manage vendor contracts", "own technology roadmap" |
| Scope markers | Numbers and scale words | "$30M budget", "team of 80", "multi-region" |
| Credentials | Degree, certification, clearance | MBA, PMP, TOGAF, CISSP |
| Title words | Exact title and adjacent titles | "Senior Director, Enterprise Applications" |

Rank by frequency × placement (title > requirements > responsibilities > about-us).

## Step 2 — Map to master résumé evidence
| Status | Rule |
|---|---|
| EXACT | Keyword string appears in the master résumé |
| SYNONYM | Master résumé states the same fact under a different name (e.g., JD "API management platform", MR "Apigee"). Use the JD term **and** keep the MR term in parentheses once |
| ADJACENT | Related but not the same (JD "Boomi", MR "MuleSoft"). Do not claim the JD term; state the MR term and the category ("iPaaS") |
| UNSUPPORTED | No evidence. Goes to the gap note only |

Synonym substitution requires the underlying fact to be true in the MR. "Led" ≠ "supported". "Architected" ≠ "implemented".

## Step 3 — Placement
| Placement | What goes there | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Title line | Exact JD title if the MR history supports that level | 1 |
| Executive summary | Top 5–7 keywords, in prose | ≤4 lines |
| Core competencies | 9–12 keyword phrases, pipe- or comma-separated (ATS-safe) | 2 lines |
| Experience bullets | Keywords inside outcome bullets | natural density |
| Skills / Technology | Platforms and tools | 3–5 lines |

## Density rules
- Each top-10 keyword appears 2–3 times across the document; never more than 4.
- No keyword stuffing lines ("Keywords: …"), no white text, no hidden sections.
- Use the exact JD spelling for the first occurrence (e.g., "Generative AI" not "GenAI") if the MR fact supports it.

## ATS formatting rules
- Standard headings: Summary, Core Competencies, Professional Experience, Education, Certifications.
- One column, no tables, no text boxes, no headers/footers for contact info.
- Dates: `Jan 2021 – Jun 2024`. Employer, title, location on separate lines or a single line with `|`.
- File name: `Firstname-Lastname-Senior-Director-Role.docx/pdf`.

## Output table format
| JD keyword | Priority | Status | Evidence | Placement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apigee | 1 | EXACT | MR-L22 | Summary, bullet, skills |
| Vendor management | 2 | SYNONYM (SOW negotiation) | MR-L31 | Competencies, bullet |
| Boomi | 3 | ADJACENT (MuleSoft) | MR-L22 | Gap note |
| SOX compliance | 4 | UNSUPPORTED | — | Gap note |
skills/career/resume-tailor/references/b:
# Bullet Formula

```
<Action verb> <what> <scope: team / budget / users / geography> → <metric> <outcome / business consequence>
```
Target ≤ 2 lines (≤ 32 words). Metric where the master résumé has one; otherwise the outcome only. Never add a metric.

| Element | Rule | Executive-level examples |
|---|---|---|
| Action verb | Past tense, leadership scale | Led, Directed, Built, Transformed, Consolidated, Negotiated, Launched, Owned, Restructured, Scaled |
| What | The initiative, platform or org | "the enterprise integration platform", "a 70-person application org" |
| Scope | At least one of: people, dollars, users, sites, regions | "$20M portfolio", "90,000 learners", "12 countries" |
| Metric | Percentage, dollars, time, volume — exactly as in MR | "cut cycle time 70%", "$5M run-rate savings" |
| Outcome | Business consequence, not activity | "enabling same-day disbursement", "retiring 3 legacy systems" |

## Transformation types (for the traceability table)
| Code | Meaning | Allowed? |
|---|---|---|
| REWORD | Same facts, new phrasing or JD keyword | Yes |
| MERGE | Two MR bullets into one | Yes, cite both |
| SPLIT | One MR bullet into two | Yes |
| REORDER | Moved for relevance | Yes |
| TRIM | Detail dropped | Yes |
| EMPHASIZE | Metric or scope moved to front | Yes |
| NEW | Fact not in MR | **No — refuse** |

## Anti-patterns
| Anti-pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| "Responsible for…" | Start with the verb |
| Activity without outcome ("Managed vendors") | Add the MR outcome or drop |
| Stacked adjectives ("robust, scalable, seamless") | Delete; keep the number |
| Three metrics in one bullet | Split |
| Inflating "participated" to "led" | Keep the MR verb |
| Vague scale ("large team") | Use MR number or omit |

## Verb ladder by level
| Level | Verbs |
|---|---|
| Manager | Delivered, Implemented, Coordinated |
| Director | Led, Built, Launched, Owned, Standardized |
| Sr Director / VP | Directed, Transformed, Consolidated, Restructured, Negotiated, Scaled, Set strategy for |
Use the ladder only where the MR supports that scope.

# Before / After Diff and Traceability Formats

## Before / after diff
One block per changed unit (summary, scope line, bullet). Unchanged units are listed once under "KEEP" by MR line.

```
### <Role or section>
[SHARPEN] MR-L18
- BEFORE: Managed the integration team and delivered APIs for multiple business units.
- AFTER:  Directed a 12-person integration team delivering 240+ APIs on MuleSoft for 6 business units, cutting partner onboarding from 6 weeks to 9 days. [MR-L18, MR-L19]
- WHY:    JD must-have "API program leadership"; metric moved forward.

[CUT] MR-L27 — pre-2010 technical detail, no JD relevance
[REORDER] MR-L22 → position 1 — JD title keyword
[KEEP] MR-L20, MR-L21, MR-L24
```

Tags follow the repo redline convention: `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]`. `[ADD]` is permitted only for structural elements (headings, competency section) — never for facts.

## Traceability table (mandatory)
| # | Tailored text (first 60 chars) | Source | Transformation | Metric unchanged? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Directed a 12-person integration team delivering 240+ APIs… | MR-L18, MR-L19 | MERGE + REWORD | Yes |
| 2 | Negotiated iPaaS renewal, cutting run-rate $1.1M/yr… | MR-L31 | EMPHASIZE | Yes |

Rules:
- One row per bullet and per summary sentence.
- "Metric unchanged?" must be Yes. "No" or "N/A (no metric in source)" only.
- A row with Source empty or "NEW" fails the self-check.

## Unsupported-claims note
| JD wants | Why not included | Option |
|---|---|---|
| SOX audit ownership | Not in MR | Add to MR if true (user confirms), else omit |
| Boomi | MR shows MuleSoft | State "iPaaS (MuleSoft)"; address Boomi in interview |
