# Executive Résumé Structure (Sr Director / VP / CxO IT)

## Section order and length
| # | Section | Length | Content rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Header | 2 lines | Name, target title line, city/state (or "Remote"), phone, email, LinkedIn. No street address. |
| 2 | Executive summary | ≤4 lines | Level, domain, scale (people/$), 2–3 signature outcomes with numbers from MR, 1 line on what you bring to this JD. No adjectives. |
| 3 | Core competencies | 9–12 phrases | JD-mapped keyword phrases. ATS-safe separators. |
| 4 | Selected achievements (optional) | 3–4 bullets | Only if the MR has 3+ headline metrics; otherwise skip |
| 5 | Professional experience | 1.3 pages | Reverse chronological. Last 15 years detailed; older roles as one line each. Each role: 1-line scope statement (team, budget, reporting line) + 3–6 bullets. |
| 6 | Education & certifications | 2–4 lines | Degree, institution; certifications with year if in MR |
| 7 | Board / advisory / speaking (optional) | ≤3 lines | Only if in MR |

Total: 2 pages. Three pages only for CxO with 25+ years and board roles.

## What to cut at executive level
- Technical minutiae older than 10 years (languages, versions)
- "References available on request"
- Objective statements
- Soft-skill lists ("team player", "excellent communicator")
- Every role before year 15 reduced to `Title, Employer, Years`

## Scope statement template (per role)
`<Title> reporting to <CIO/CTO/SVP>. <N> direct / <M> total staff, $<X>M budget, <portfolio description>. [MR-Lxx]`
All values must come from the MR; omit the element if the MR does not state it.

## Level signals the reader looks for
| Signal | Where to show it |
|---|---|
| Budget ownership | Scope statement, summary |
| Org size and structure | Scope statement |
| Reporting line | Scope statement |
| Multi-year transformation | First bullet of the relevant role |
| Vendor / contract outcomes | One bullet per role where MR supports |
| Executive stakeholder exposure | Summary and one bullet |
| Business outcome (revenue, cost, risk, speed) | Every bullet's tail |

---
name: account-plan
description: Use when the user asks to build or refresh a quarterly or annual account plan, account strategy, or account review for an existing or target client — including weighting the account's pipeline (win probabilities, deal values the CRM lacks) or setting the account target. Produces a one-page-first account plan — account snapshot, relationship and stakeholder map with coverage gaps, white-space map (our services × their business units/platforms), pipeline table, risks to the account, and 90-day plays with owners and dates — with every revenue, pipeline, or stakeholder fact sourced to the user's inputs or marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]. Do not use for pre-pitch research on a new logo (client-research-brief) or for a single-pursuit battle card (competitive-positioning).
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: presales
  adlc_stage: opportunity
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    inputs:
      - {name: stakeholders, type: csv, required: true, from: "stakeholders.csv: name, role, stance -2..2, influence 1-5, last_contact, departure_risk (layout: evals/fixtures/stakeholders.csv)"}
      - {name: pipeline, type: csv, required: true, from: "pipeline.csv: opportunity, stage, value, close_date, owner, next_step (CRM export; layout: evals/fixtures/pipeline.csv)"}
      - {name: services, type: csv, required: true, from: "services.csv: service, status_at_account in active|proposed|none (layout: evals/fixtures/services.csv)"}
      - {name: client, type: string, required: false, default: "<Client>"}
      - {name: as_of, type: string, required: false, from: "yyyy-mm-dd; enables stale-contact (90 days) detection"}
      - {name: previous_plays, type: csv, required: false, from: "last quarter's plays.csv (optional status column: done | open | dropped) for the refresh"}
      - {name: previous_pipeline, type: csv, required: false, from: "last quarter's pipeline.csv, for the pipeline delta"}
    run:
      - {step: plan, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/account_plan.py {stakeholders} {pipeline} {services} --out {out}/account-plan.md --plays {out}/plays.csv --client {client} [--as-of {as_of}] [--previous-plays {previous_plays}] [--previous-pipeline {previous_pipeline}]"}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/account-plan.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Stakeholder map","White-space matrix","Pipeline","90-day plays"]]}
      - {path: "{out}/plays.csv", checks: [exists, csv:[play_id,play,addresses,owner,date,success_measure], csv_rows:owner!empty]}
    modes:
      new: {case: agent-happy-path, bring: "stakeholder list, CRM pipeline export and service coverage"}
      existing: {case: agent-mode-existing, bring: "this quarter's exports plus last quarter's plays and pipeline"}
---

# account-plan

## In a conversation: write the plan now
The reply **is the plan**: its first line is `Posture: <Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter> — <the facts that drove it>`, never a question or a request for files. Questions for missing facts go at the end.
- **The request carries account facts** (engagements, end dates, pipeline, stakeholders, events such as a sponsor leaving), or says the CRM export, stakeholder list, catalog or prior plan are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the full account plan **in this reply** from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order, page 1 standing alone:
  1. **Posture on line 1** (Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter) with the two or three facts that drove it (e.g. sponsor departure, nearest engagement end date).
  2. **Snapshot** — revenue, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles; each cell sourced ("CRM export, <date>") or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Weighted pipeline only when the CRM supplies probabilities, and say so.
  3. **Top risks** and **90-day plays** (3–6), each with owner, date and success measure: at least one coverage play (e.g. the successor to a departing sponsor) and one renewal/defense play for the nearest engagement end.
  4. Detail: **stakeholder map** (role, influence, disposition — unknown stays `unknown` —, our owner, last contact) with departures flagged as exposure and **coverage gaps** computed; **white-space matrix** (our services × their units) using `current / qualified / hypothesis / no fit / unknown`, each hypothesis citing its signal and confirming action; **pipeline table**; **risk register**; **change log vs the prior plan** on a refresh (achieved, carried, dropped and why).
  Mark every value the request does not give `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the source it will come from, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
- **No account facts at all** ("write an account plan for X"): ask once, in one list, for account facts (engagements, revenue, stakeholders, pipeline), our service catalog and the quarter. Do not estimate current spend, wallet share or stakeholder dispositions. Offer the **Enter** posture template with every cell marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` if the account is a target with no history.
- **Asked to invent win probabilities or a target** ("assign 60% / 30%", "put the target at what we usually aim for"): say in one line that probabilities and targets are not invented, because leadership will treat them as forecast. Show the **unweighted** pipeline only; offer to add probabilities if the user records them in the CRM as their own sales judgment, labelled as such. Show the target as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` until the user confirms the official target and its source, and report gap-to-target as a marker until target and weighting are confirmed. Never print the requested percentages or target figure as plan values.

## Starting points
- **New** — stakeholders, pipeline and service coverage become a 90-day plan: stakeholder map, white space, pipeline, risks and plays with owned TBDs.
- **Existing** — add last quarter's plays and pipeline: the refresh says which plays were done, carried over (with last quarter's owner to confirm), dropped or closed by events, which plays are new, and how each opportunity moved since the last plan.

## When to use
- "Build the Q<n> account plan for <client>."
- "Refresh the account strategy — we just lost the renewal / won the assessment."
- "Prepare the quarterly account review for leadership."
- NOT for: new-logo research (`client-research-brief`), one pursuit (`competitive-positioning`, `proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Account facts: current engagements (scope, value, end dates), revenue history, contract vehicles, team on the account | yes | user / CRM export / prior plan |
| Stakeholder list with titles, our relationship owner, last contact | yes (any subset; rest TBD) | user / CRM |
| Client business context: strategy, initiatives, org changes, budget cycle (from `client-research-brief` or user) | no | brief / user |
| Pipeline: opportunities, stage, value, close date, next step | yes or "none" | CRM / user |
| Our service catalog (for white space) | yes | file / user |
| Prior plan (for refresh) | no | file |
| Quarter and planning horizon | yes | user |

If the request carries no account facts at all, ask once. Individual facts missing from a request that has some (catalog, revenue, a stakeholder's last contact) do not stop the draft: they are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never estimate the client's spend with us or wallet share from memory.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Snapshot**: fill the account snapshot table (`assets/account-plan-template.md` §1) from inputs only: revenue by period, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles, NPS/health signals if provided. Each cell sourced (CRM export date, prior plan version, user statement) or marked.
2. **Stakeholder map** per `references/account-planning-method.md` §2: for each stakeholder — role, influence (decision / influencer / gatekeeper / user), disposition toward us (advocate / neutral / skeptic / unknown), our relationship owner, last meaningful contact, next contact plan. Compute coverage gaps: decision-makers with no owner or no contact in 90 days; business units with no relationship. Unknown disposition is `unknown`, never assumed neutral.
3. **White-space map** (§3): matrix of our service lines × the client's business units or platforms. Cells: `current` (sourced engagement), `qualified` (pipeline), `hypothesis` (signal from brief or discovery with the signal cited), `no fit` (reason), `unknown`. Hypotheses carry the confirming action. Count the cells; the plan's growth plays come from `hypothesis` cells with the strongest signals.
4. **Pipeline table**: each opportunity with stage (use the user's stage names), value (from CRM or marked), close date, win probability only if the user's CRM supplies it (no invented probabilities), next step with owner and date, and the blocker if any. Reconcile the sum with the snapshot.
5. **Decision point — account posture.** Per §4: Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter, from the facts (renewal exposure, relationship coverage, competitive threat, white-space signal strength). State the posture on line 1 and the two or three facts that drove it.
6. **Risks to the account** (§5): renewal risk, stakeholder departure, competitive entry, delivery issues, budget cut, concentration risk; each with likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner.
7. **90-day plays**: 3–6 plays, each with objective, actions, owner, date, success measure, and which white-space cell or risk it addresses. Plays without an owner are not plays. Include at least one relationship play (coverage gap) and one delivery-quality play if any engagement is active.
8. **Targets** only from the user: if a revenue target exists, show gap-to-target = target − (booked + weighted pipeline, if probabilities are supplied) and the plays that close it. If no target, `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
9. **One-page view first**, detail behind. Refresh mode: diff against the prior plan (what changed, what was achieved, what was dropped and why).
10. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `account-plan-<client>-<quarter>.md` per `assets/account-plan-template.md`
- Page 1: posture and bottom line · snapshot · top risks · 90-day plays. Following pages: stakeholder map and gaps · white-space matrix · pipeline · risk register · change log (refresh)

## Self-check
- [ ] Posture stated on line 1 with the driving facts
- [ ] Every revenue, pipeline, and target figure sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] No invented win probabilities; weighted pipeline only if the CRM supplies probabilities
- [ ] Stakeholder dispositions sourced; unknowns marked unknown
- [ ] Coverage gaps computed and addressed by at least one play
- [ ] White-space hypotheses cite a signal and a confirming action
- [ ] Every play has owner, date, success measure
- [ ] Risks have likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner
- [ ] Internal document; no content copied into client-facing material without review

## References
- `references/account-planning-method.md` — snapshot, stakeholder mapping, white-space logic, posture decision, risk patterns, play design, review cadence
- `assets/account-plan-template.md` — plan template (one page first)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/account-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/account-plan`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Account plan from stakeholder, pipeline and service-coverage CSVs.

    python3 -I scripts/account_plan.py stakeholders.csv pipeline.csv services.csv \
        --out account-plan.md --plays plays.csv [--client "Acme"] [--as-of 2026-10-01]

stakeholders.csv: name, role, stance (-2..2), influence (1-5), last_contact (yyyy-mm-dd or blank), departure_risk
pipeline.csv:     opportunity, stage, value, close_date, owner, next_step
services.csv:     service, status_at_account (active | proposed | none)

Produces account-plan.md: stakeholder map (influence × stance grid), white-space matrix, pipeline
table with total, risks (departure risk, stale contacts when --as-of is given), and 90-day plays:
one per service with status none, one per stakeholder with stance <= 0 and influence >= 4, one per
stakeholder flagged departure_risk. Play owner and date are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Account owner]` (the
plan never assigns people it was not told about); plays.csv carries the same rows. Blank pipeline
values become the marker and are excluded from the total, which then says so.
Quarterly refresh (existing plan): --previous-plays last quarter's plays.csv (optional `status` column:
done | open | dropped; blank = open) and/or --previous-pipeline last quarter's pipeline.csv. The plan
then gains "Since last plan": each previous play is done, carried over (its trigger still fires — the
new play is marked "carried from <id>"), dropped, or closed by events (still open but no longer
triggered — confirm with the account team; a carried play keeps last quarter's owner, marked to confirm);
new plays are listed as new; and the pipeline delta lists
opportunities added, removed, and stage / value / close-date changes. Rows whose first cell starts
with `#` are notes and are skipped.
Exit 1 on missing columns, stance/influence out of range, non-numeric values or an unknown
status. Stdlib only, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Account owner]"
STATUSES = ("active", "proposed", "none")
STALE_DAYS = 90


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def read_csv(path: str, cols: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    with p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        rows = [{k: (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k} for r in csv.DictReader(f)]
    if not rows:
        die(f"{p.name}: no data rows")
    missing = [c for c in cols if c not in rows[0]]
    if missing:
        die(f"{p.name}: missing columns {missing}")
    return rows


def read_previous(path: str, cols: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Last quarter's CSV; `#` note rows skipped; may be empty."""
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    with p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        missing = [c for c in cols if c not in (reader.fieldnames or [])]
        if missing:
            die(f"{p.name}: missing columns {missing}")
        rows = [{k: (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k} for r in reader]
    return [r for r in rows if r.get(cols[0]) and not r[cols[0]].startswith("#")]


def since_last(plays: list[dict], prev_plays: list[dict] | None, pipe: list[dict], prev_pipe: list[dict] | None) -> list[str]:
    L = ["", "## Since last plan", ""]
    if prev_plays is not None:
        current = {p["play"]: p for p in plays}
        rows = []
        for pp in prev_plays:
            status = (pp.get("status") or "open").lower()
            if status not in ("done", "open", "dropped"):
                die(f"previous plays {pp['play_id']}: status must be done | open | dropped, got {status!r}")
            now = current.get(pp["play"])
            if status in ("done", "dropped"):
                outcome = status
            elif now:
                outcome = f"carried over as {now['play_id']}"
                now["addresses"] += f" (carried from {pp['play_id']}, last quarter)"
                now["carried"] = True
                if pp.get("owner"):
                    now["owner"] = f"{pp['owner']} (last quarter's owner — confirm)"
            else:
                outcome = "closed by events — trigger no longer fires; confirm with the account team"
            rows.append(f"| {pp['play_id']} | {pp['play']} | {outcome} |")
        L += ["| Last quarter | Play | Outcome |", "|---|---|---|"] + (rows or ["| — | none recorded | |"])
        new = [p for p in plays if not p.get("carried") and p["play"] not in {pp["play"] for pp in prev_plays}]
        L += ["", f"New this quarter: {', '.join(p['play_id'] for p in new) or 'none'}.", ""]
    if prev_pipe is not None:
        before = {p["opportunity"]: p for p in prev_pipe}
        after = {p["opportunity"]: p for p in pipe}
        rows = [f"| {o} | added | {after[o]['stage'] or TBD} |" for o in after if o not in before]
        rows += [f"| {o} | removed (won, lost or merged — confirm) | was {before[o]['stage'] or TBD} |" for o in before if o not in after]
        for o in after:
            if o in before:
                ch = [f"{col} {before[o].get(col) or '—'} → {after[o].get(col) or '—'}" for col in ("stage", "value", "close_date")
                      if (before[o].get(col) or "") != (after[o].get(col) or "")]
                if ch:
                    rows.append(f"| {o} | changed | {'; '.join(ch)} |")
        L += ["| Opportunity | Change | Detail |", "|---|---|---|"] + (rows or ["| — | no change since last plan | |"])
    return L


def int_in(row: dict, col: str, lo: int, hi: int, where: str) -> int:
    raw = row.get(col, "")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"-?\d+", raw) or not lo <= int(raw) <= hi:
        die(f"{where}: {col} must be an integer {lo}..{hi}, got {raw!r}")
    return int(raw)


def money(raw: str, where: str):
    if raw == "":
        return None
    try:
        return float(raw.replace(",", "").replace("$", ""))
    except ValueError:
        die(f"{where}: non-numeric value {raw!r}")


def date_or_none(raw: str, where: str):
    if not raw:
        return None
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(raw)
    except ValueError:
        die(f"{where}: date must be yyyy-mm-dd, got {raw!r}")


def truthy(raw: str) -> bool:
    return raw.strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "y", "high", "h")


def fmt(x) -> str:
    return TBD if x is None else (f"{int(round(x)):,}" if abs(x - round(x)) < 0.005 else f"{x:,.2f}")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="stakeholders + pipeline + services -> account-plan.md + plays.csv")
    ap.add_argument("stakeholders"); ap.add_argument("pipeline"); ap.add_argument("services")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True); ap.add_argument("--plays", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--client", default="<Client>")
    ap.add_argument("--as-of", default="", help="yyyy-mm-dd; enables stale-contact detection")
    ap.add_argument("--previous-plays", default="", help="last quarter's plays.csv (optional status: done|open|dropped)")
    ap.add_argument("--previous-pipeline", default="", help="last quarter's pipeline.csv, for the pipeline delta")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    as_of = date_or_none(a.as_of, "--as-of")
    stk = read_csv(a.stakeholders, ["name", "role", "stance", "influence", "last_contact", "departure_risk"])
    pipe = read_csv(a.pipeline, ["opportunity", "stage", "value", "close_date", "owner", "next_step"])
    svc = read_csv(a.services, ["service", "status_at_account"])
    for i, s in enumerate(stk, 1):
        w = f"stakeholders row {i}"
        s["stance_i"] = int_in(s, "stance", -2, 2, w)
        s["infl_i"] = int_in(s, "influence", 1, 5, w)
        s["last"] = date_or_none(s["last_contact"], w)
        s["risk"] = truthy(s["departure_risk"])
        s["stale"] = bool(as_of and (s["last"] is None or (as_of - s["last"]).days > STALE_DAYS))
    for i, p in enumerate(pipe, 1):
        p["value_f"] = money(p["value"], f"pipeline row {i}")
    for i, s in enumerate(svc, 1):
        if s["status_at_account"].lower() not in STATUSES:
            die(f"services row {i}: status_at_account must be one of {STATUSES}, got {s['status_at_account']!r}")
        s["status"] = s["status_at_account"].lower()

    plays = []
    for s in svc:
        if s["status"] == "none":
            plays.append({"play": f"Open white space: {s['service']}", "addresses": f"white-space cell {s['service']} (none)",
                          "type": "white-space"})
    for s in stk:
        if s["stance_i"] <= 0 and s["infl_i"] >= 4:
            plays.append({"play": f"Move {s['name']} ({s['role']}) from stance {s['stance_i']} to +1",
                          "addresses": f"stakeholder {s['name']}: influence {s['infl_i']}, stance {s['stance_i']}", "type": "stakeholder"})
        if s["risk"]:
            plays.append({"play": f"Cover departure risk: {s['name']} ({s['role']})",
                          "addresses": f"departure risk on {s['name']}", "type": "risk"})
        elif s["stale"]:
            plays.append({"play": f"Re-establish contact with {s['name']} ({s['role']})",
                          "addresses": f"no contact in {STALE_DAYS} days (last: {s['last_contact'] or 'never'})", "type": "coverage"})
    if not plays:
        plays.append({"play": "Confirm posture, target and coverage with the account team",
                      "addresses": "no gap triggered by the inputs; validate the inputs are complete", "type": "posture"})
    for i, p in enumerate(plays, 1):
        p.update({"play_id": f"P{i}", "owner": TBD, "date": TBD, "success_measure": TBD})

    refresh = []
    if a.previous_plays or a.previous_pipeline:
        prev_plays = read_previous(a.previous_plays, ["play_id", "play"]) if a.previous_plays else None
        prev_pipe = read_previous(a.previous_pipeline, ["opportunity", "stage", "value", "close_date"]) if a.previous_pipeline else None
        refresh = since_last(plays, prev_plays, pipe, prev_pipe)
    known = [p for p in pipe if p["value_f"] is not None]
    total = sum(p["value_f"] for p in known)
    L = [f"# Account Plan — {a.client} — 90-day plan" + (f" (as of {as_of})" if as_of else ""), "",
         "**INTERNAL.** Sources: stakeholders.csv, pipeline.csv, services.csv as supplied; nothing else.", "",
         "## Bottom line",
         f"{len(stk)} stakeholders ({sum(1 for s in stk if s['stance_i'] <= 0 and s['infl_i'] >= 4)} influential and not yet supportive, "
         f"{sum(1 for s in stk if s['risk'])} at departure risk) · pipeline {fmt(total)}"
         + (f" across {len(known)} of {len(pipe)} opportunities ({len(pipe) - len(known)} unvalued)" if len(known) != len(pipe) else f" across {len(pipe)} opportunities")
         + f" · {sum(1 for s in svc if s['status'] == 'none')} white-space cells · {len(plays)} plays. Posture: {TBD}.", "",
         "## Stakeholder map (influence × stance)", "| Influence \\ Stance | −2 blocker | −1 sceptic | 0 neutral | +1 supporter | +2 champion |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for infl in (5, 4, 3, 2, 1):
        cells = []
        for st in (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2):
            names = [s["name"] + (" ⚠" if s["risk"] else "") for s in stk if s["infl_i"] == infl and s["stance_i"] == st]
            cells.append(", ".join(names) or "—")
        L.append(f"| {infl} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    L += ["", "⚠ = departure risk flagged", "", "| Name | Role | Stance | Influence | Last contact | Departure risk | Coverage |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {s['name']} | {s['role']} | {s['stance_i']} | {s['infl_i']} | {s['last_contact'] or TBD} | "
          f"{'yes' if s['risk'] else 'no'} | {'stale' if s['stale'] else ('n/a' if not as_of else 'ok')} |" for s in stk]
    L += ["", "## White-space matrix", "| Service | Status at account | Play |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for s in svc:
        play = next((p["play_id"] for p in plays if p["type"] == "white-space" and s["service"] in p["play"]), "—")
        L.append(f"| {s['service']} | {s['status']} | {play} |")
    L += ["", "## Pipeline", "| Opportunity | Stage | Value | Close date | Owner | Next step |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {p['opportunity']} | {p['stage'] or TBD} | {fmt(p['value_f'])} | {p['close_date'] or TBD} | {p['owner'] or TBD} | {p['next_step'] or TBD} |"
          for p in pipe]
    L.append(f"| **Total** | | {fmt(total)}" + (f" (excludes {len(pipe) - len(known)} unvalued)" if len(known) != len(pipe) else "") + " | | | |")
    L += ["", "## Risks to the account", "| Risk | Early signal | Mitigation (play) | Owner |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| Departure of {s['name']} ({s['role']}) | departure_risk flagged | {next((p['play_id'] for p in plays if p['type'] == 'risk' and s['name'] in p['play']), '—')} | {TBD} |"
          for s in stk if s["risk"]]
    L += [f"| Coverage gap: {s['name']} | no contact in {STALE_DAYS} days | {next((p['play_id'] for p in plays if p['type'] == 'coverage' and s['name'] in p['play']), '—')} | {TBD} |"
          for s in stk if s["stale"] and not s["risk"]]
    if L[-1].startswith("|---"):
        L.append("| none identified from inputs | | | |")
    L += refresh
    L += ["", "## 90-day plays", "| # | Play | Addresses | Owner | Date | Success measure |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {p['play_id']} | {p['play']} | {p['addresses']} | {p['owner']} | {p['date']} | {p['success_measure']} |" for p in plays] \
        or ["| — | no play triggered by the inputs | | | | |"]
    Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(a.out).write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    with Path(a.plays).open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["play_id", "play", "type", "addresses", "owner", "date", "success_measure"],
                           extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader(); w.writerows(plays)
    print(f"account plan: {len(stk)} stakeholders, {len(pipe)} opportunities, {len(plays)} plays -> {a.out}, {a.plays}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Account Planning Method

## 1. Snapshot
| Field | Source | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue by period (last 4–8 quarters) | CRM/finance export with date | Never from memory |
| Active engagements: scope, value, end date, delivery health | Engagement list; delivery lead statement | End dates drive renewal risk |
| Contract vehicles (MSA, rate card validity, preferred-supplier status) | Legal/commercial | Expiry dates are risks |
| Health signals (NPS, escalations, reference status) | Delivery / client statements | Cite the source and date |
| Our team on the account (roles, allocation) | User | — |

## 2. Stakeholder mapping
| Field | Values | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Influence | Decision-maker · Influencer · Gatekeeper · User · Unknown | From org knowledge or discovery; not inferred from title alone where it matters |
| Disposition | Advocate · Neutral · Skeptic · Unknown | Requires evidence (statement, behavior); default is Unknown |
| Relationship owner (ours) | Named | Every decision-maker needs one |
| Last meaningful contact | Date | "Meaningful" = two-way conversation, not a newsletter |
| Next contact plan | Action, date | — |

Coverage gaps (computed):
| Gap | Rule |
|---|---|
| Uncovered decision-maker | No relationship owner, or no contact in 90 days |
| Single-threaded | Only one of our people knows the stakeholder |
| Uncovered business unit | No stakeholder mapped in a BU with white-space signal |
| Skeptic without plan | Disposition skeptic and no play addresses it |
| Departure exposure | Advocate rumored or announced leaving; no successor relationship |

## 3. White-space map
Matrix: rows = our service lines (from the catalog); columns = client business units, platforms, or programs (from the brief/account facts).

| Cell value | Meaning | Required content |
|---|---|---|
| `current` | Active engagement | Engagement ID |
| `qualified` | Opportunity in pipeline | Opportunity ID |
| `hypothesis` | Signal suggests a need | Signal (source) + confirming action + owner |
| `no fit` | Not a plausible need or blocked | Reason (e.g., incumbent locked, policy) |
| `unknown` | No information | Discovery action |

Signal strength for hypotheses: H (client stated a need or a dated forcing event), M (public signal: posting, filing, program), L (pattern inference). Only H and M hypotheses become 90-day plays.

## 4. Account posture
| Posture | Conditions (from facts) | Plan emphasis |
|---|---|---|
| Grow | Delivery healthy; advocates in ≥2 BUs; H/M white-space signals; no renewal exposure in the quarter | Expansion plays, executive access, reference development |
| Defend | Renewal within 2 quarters; competitive entry evidenced; delivery issue or skeptic in decision chain | Renewal plan, delivery recovery, stakeholder re-coverage |
| Harvest | Client strategy moving away from our services; low white-space; relationships thin | Protect margin, minimal investment, graceful exit planning |
| Enter | Target account with no active engagement | Access plays, assessment offer, reference-led introduction |

State the posture and the two or three facts that drove it. A posture without facts is a wish.

## 5. Risk patterns
| Risk | Early signal | Typical mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Renewal loss | RFP issued for current scope; procurement engaged early; rate challenge | Value review with sponsor; independent baseline of outcomes delivered; renewal proposal 2 quarters out |
| Sponsor departure | Announcement, org change, reduced access | Multi-thread now; introduce successor early |
| Competitive entry | New vendor logos in client comms; "benchmark" exercises; vendor-shaped RFP language | Battle card; seed evaluation criteria; executive outreach |
| Delivery issue | Escalations, missed milestones, change requests disputed | Recovery plan with dates; executive sponsor call; do not hide |
| Budget cut | Hiring freeze, program pauses, earnings commentary | Re-scope to cost-out plays; phase; protect run work |
| Concentration | One engagement > 60% of account revenue | Diversify BUs; smaller parallel engagements |

## 6. Play design
| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Objective | One sentence with a measurable outcome in 90 days |
| Actions | 2–5 with owner and date |
| Success measure | Observable (meeting held, proposal submitted, renewal signed, stakeholder disposition moved with evidence) |
| Addresses | White-space cell ID or risk ID |
| Investment | Hours or cost if any; sourced |

Minimum plays: one coverage play, one growth play (if posture is Grow/Enter), one defense play (if Defend), one delivery-quality play (if active engagements). Maximum six; more means none get done.

## 7. Review cadence
| Review | Cadence | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Play check | Bi-weekly | Actions done / slipped; blockers |
| Pipeline | Monthly | Stage movement; next steps; forecast changes (from CRM) |
| Plan refresh | Quarterly | Change log: achieved, dropped (why), new; posture reassessed |

Refresh output includes a change log table: `Item | Prior plan | Now | Reason`.

---
name: client-research-brief
description: Use when the user asks to research a company, account, or prospect before a pitch, discovery call, or proposal ("research <company> before the meeting", "build me a brief on <account>"). Produces a sourced one-page brief — business snapshot, filings and financial signals, technology-stack signals, leadership, recent news, likely initiatives, and hypotheses for the call — with every claim carrying a source and every unknown marked. Includes a no-network script that turns a notes/links file into the brief skeleton. Do not use for competitor battle cards (competitive-positioning) or for synthesizing a call (discovery-interview).
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: presales
  adlc_stage: opportunity
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    inputs:
      - {name: notes, type: file, required: true, from: "notes/links file the user collected (.md or .txt); nothing is fetched"}
      - {name: company, type: string, required: true}
      - {name: purpose, type: string, required: false, default: "discovery", from: "discovery | proposal | exec-meeting | pitch"}
      - {name: previous, type: md, required: false, from: "the brief written last time for this client; new material is marked and dropped sources listed"}
      - {name: draft_only, type: flag, required: false, flag: "--draft-only", from: "true to skip the model step: brief.md is written from the notes, every item cited, labelled as a draft"}
    run:
      - {step: skeleton, kind: script, cmd: "python3 -I scripts/brief_skeleton.py --notes {notes} --company {company} --purpose {purpose} [--previous {previous}] --out {out}/brief-skeleton.md --final {out}/brief.md {draft_only}"}
      - {step: brief, kind: llm, template: assets/brief-template.md, context: ["{out}/brief-skeleton.md", "{notes}", "references/research-method.md"], out: "{out}/brief.md", skip_if_present: [draft_only]}
    outputs:
      - {path: "{out}/brief-skeleton.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Bottom line","Sources"]]}
      - {path: "{out}/brief.md", checks: [exists, sections:["Bottom line","Snapshot","Technology signals","Questions for the call","Sources"], no_unowned_tbd, cites_source_ids:"{out}/brief-skeleton.md"]}
    modes:
      new: {case: agent-mode-new, bring: "your notes and links on the company"}
      existing: {case: agent-mode-existing, bring: "fresh notes plus the last brief on this client"}
---

# client-research-brief

## In a conversation: write the brief now
- **The request names the company and the purpose** (the angle is optional — when it is missing, the brief is still written and the angle shows `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; with or without a notes file — if the notes are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation, work from what the request states): write the brief **in this reply**, applying the skeleton script's classification by hand (sort each note item — filing link, job posting, announcement — into its section and number it as a source `[S1]…`). Never reply with only a request for the file. In template order (`assets/brief-template.md`):
  1. **Bottom line** — three facts the reader must walk in knowing, each with its source.
  2. **Snapshot** — each cell sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
  3. **Financial signals** — each number cites the filing and its section/page (e.g. "10-K, Item 7, p. __"); figures not quoted in the request stay `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the filing section to read.
  4. **Technology signals table** — signal, source and tier, confidence (High / Med / Low per the playbook), and the confirming question for the call.
  5. **Leadership** — public-record facts only (title, since, prior employer, quoted priorities); no personality inference.
  6. **Recent news** (≤6, dated) · **Likely initiatives** labelled *Hypothesis*, each with the signal and its tier and the confirming question · **Risks and landmines** · **Questions for the call**.
  7. **Sources** — every URL or document with date accessed and tier.
  Keep the reply to about one page (≈700 words) so the Sources list is always complete.
- **Company or purpose missing or ambiguous** ("a brief on Apex"): ask once which company (legal name, HQ country, ticker if listed) and the purpose and date of the meeting. Do not produce a brief for a guessed company and do not invent a notes file or sources.
- **Asked to fill revenue, IT spend or other figures that no source gives** (private company, "use what you think it is"): say in one line that private-company figures are not estimated without a cited public source. Show those cells as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` — never print an estimate anywhere, and never cite aggregator revenue estimates. Use only the user's notes as sources, rate a fact resting on a single signal **Low**, and give the specific discovery question that would baseline each figure (e.g. "What is the annual run cost of your WMS and integration estate?").

## Starting points
- **New** — your notes and links are sorted into the brief's sections with every source numbered; the model step writes the brief, or with `draft_only` the brief is your notes verbatim, each item cited, the so-what left as owned markers.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (the last brief on this client): material already in it is carried, new material is marked NEW, and sources it cited that your notes no longer carry are listed to re-check or drop.

## When to use
- "Research <company> before the pitch on <date>."
- "What is <account> likely to be spending on in the next 12 months?"
- "Build a brief on the new CIO at <company>."
- NOT for: competitor analysis (`competitive-positioning`), quarterly account strategy (`account-plan`), call synthesis (`discovery-interview`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Company legal/common name, HQ country | yes | user |
| Purpose: pitch / discovery / proposal / exec meeting, and date | yes | user |
| Our angle: the service line or initiative we are positioning | yes | user |
| Notes/links file (`notes.md` or `.txt`: URLs, pasted excerpts, prior-contact notes) | no | file |
| Named stakeholders to profile | no | user |
| Network access available? (yes/no) | yes | environment |

If company name or purpose is missing, ask once. A missing notes file or angle does not stop the brief: unsourced cells are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never guess which company is meant when names collide (ask "Acme Corp (NYSE: ACM) or Acme Ltd (UK)?").

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Scope the brief to the purpose.** A discovery brief emphasizes initiatives and pains; a proposal brief emphasizes procurement, incumbents, and financial capacity; an exec-meeting brief emphasizes the individual and their public positions. Use `references/research-method.md` §1 to pick the emphasis weights.
2. **Build the source plan** from `references/research-method.md` §2 (source tiers: filings > investor materials > regulator/press releases > reputable press > job postings > vendor case studies > social). Decide which tiers are reachable: if no network, only the notes file and user-provided excerpts count as sources; everything else is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
3. **Run the skeleton script** when a notes file exists: `python3 -I scripts/brief_skeleton.py --notes notes.md --company "<name>" --out brief.md`. It classifies links and excerpts into the brief sections and lists what is still empty. Then fill each section by reading the sources (the script does not fetch).
4. **Extract tech-stack signals** using `references/tech-signal-playbook.md`: job postings (platform names, team sizes), engineering blogs, case studies by vendors, conference talks, open-source repos, status pages, DNS/MX hints if provided. Record each signal with confidence (High / Med / Low) per the playbook rubric; never upgrade confidence without a second independent source.
5. **Decision point — financial capacity.** If public: pull revenue, operating margin trend, capex/opex guidance, and any stated cost-out or transformation program from the latest annual/quarterly filing (cite the document and page). If private: state ownership (PE / founder / family), last funding or acquisition event if public, and mark capacity `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Do not estimate revenue for a private company.
6. **Profile leadership** limited to the roles that matter for our angle (CIO/CTO/CDO, the business sponsor, CFO, CISO where security gates apply). Tenure, prior employer, public statements, and what they have changed since arrival. Public-record facts only; no inference about personality or politics.
7. **Derive likely initiatives** as hypotheses, not facts: each row cites the signal(s) behind it and states what question on the call would confirm it. Feed these to `discovery-interview`.
8. **Write the brief** on `assets/brief-template.md`. One page. Bottom line first: the three facts the reader must walk in knowing. Sources appendix lists every URL/document with the date accessed.
9. Run the self-check. Delete any sentence you cannot trace to a source line or to the user's notes.

## Output
- File: `client-brief-<company-slug>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections (template order): Bottom line · Snapshot · Financial signals · Technology signals (table with confidence) · Leadership · Recent news (≤6 items, dated) · Likely initiatives and hypotheses · Risks and landmines · Questions for the call · Sources
- Length: ≤ 1 page body plus sources. If longer, move detail to an appendix.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every number carries a source (document + page/section, or URL + date)
- [ ] No revenue, headcount, or spend estimate for a private company unless from a cited public source
- [ ] Tech signals carry a confidence rating; no "they use X" at Low confidence
- [ ] Leadership section contains only public-record facts; no personal characterizations
- [ ] Likely initiatives are labeled hypotheses with the confirming question
- [ ] No content from other clients or from the author's own history
- [ ] Bottom line is three facts, first lines of the document

## References
- `references/research-method.md` — emphasis by purpose, source tiers, financial-signal extraction, writing rules
- `references/tech-signal-playbook.md` — where tech-stack signals live and how to rate confidence
- `assets/brief-template.md` — one-page brief template
- `scripts/brief_skeleton.py` — notes/links file → brief skeleton with empty-section report (no network)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/client-research-brief --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/client-research-brief`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.
skills/presales/client-research-brief/sc:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a client-brief skeleton from a notes/links file. No network access.

Reads a plain-text or Markdown notes file containing URLs, pasted excerpts,
and free-form notes. Classifies each line into a brief section using keyword
and URL-pattern heuristics, writes a Markdown skeleton in the layout of
assets/brief-template.md, and reports which sections received no material.

The script never fetches anything. It organizes what the user already has so
the brief can be completed by reading the cited sources. Every classified item
is listed with its origin line number so it can be traced back.

Usage:
    python3 -I brief_skeleton.py --notes notes.md --company "Acme Corp" --out brief.md
    python3 -I brief_skeleton.py --notes notes.txt --company "Acme" --purpose proposal
    ... --previous last-brief.md                       # refresh: what is new since the last brief
    ... --final brief.md --draft-only                  # no model step: a cited brief from the notes

--previous: the brief written last time for this client. Each note line already in it is carried, the
rest is marked NEW in the To-do column, and "Changes since the last brief" lists the new items and the
previous brief's sources that the notes no longer carry (not re-confirmed: re-check or drop them).
--draft-only --final: writes the brief on the template's sections with every item cited by its [Sn]
source id (items without a URL cite "notes Ln"); the bottom line is the first three cited items, verbatim,
with the "so what" left as an owned marker — labelled as a draft (the model step was not run).

Exit codes: 0 success; 2 input file not found or empty.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import re
import sys
from collections import OrderedDict
from pathlib import Path

URL_RE = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s)>\]]+", re.IGNORECASE)

# Section -> (URL host/path patterns, keyword patterns). Order matters: first match wins.
RULES: "OrderedDict[str, tuple[list[str], list[str]]]" = OrderedDict(
    [
        (
            "Financial signals",
            [
                r"sec\.gov", r"edgar", r"10-k", r"10-q", r"20-f", r"annual[- ]report",
                r"investor", r"earnings", r"proxy", r"bond", r"audited",
            ],
        ),
        (
            "Technology signals",
            [
                r"careers", r"jobs?\.", r"greenhouse", r"lever\.co", r"workday\.com",
                r"github\.com", r"developer\.", r"/api", r"status\.", r"engineering",
                r"job posting", r"posting", r"tech stack", r"platform", r"migrat",
                r"mulesoft", r"apigee", r"boomi", r"informatica", r"kafka", r"salesforce",
                r"sap", r"oracle", r"workday", r"aws", r"azure", r"gcp", r"snowflake",
                r"databricks", r"kubernetes",
            ],
        ),
        (
            "Leadership",
            [
                r"linkedin\.com/in/", r"\bcio\b", r"\bcto\b", r"\bcdo\b", r"\bcfo\b",
                r"\bciso\b", r"chief", r"appointed", r"joins? as", r"named .* officer",
                r"vice president", r"\bvp\b", r"provost",
            ],
        ),
        (
            "Recent news",
            [
                r"prnewswire", r"businesswire", r"reuters", r"bloomberg", r"wsj\.com",
                r"ft\.com", r"techcrunch", r"news", r"press[- ]release", r"announce",
                r"acqui", r"partnership", r"outage", r"breach", r"lawsuit",
            ],
        ),
        (
            "Snapshot",
            [
                r"wikipedia", r"about[- ]us", r"/about", r"headquarter", r"founded",
                r"employees", r"revenue", r"locations", r"stores", r"plants", r"campuses",
            ],
        ),
        (
            "Likely initiatives (hypotheses)",
            [
                r"initiative", r"program", r"roadmap", r"transformation", r"modern",
                r"strategy", r"priority", r"hypothes",
            ],
        ),
        (
            "Risks and landmines",
            [r"risk", r"landmine", r"incumbent", r"competitor", r"avoid", r"sensitive"],
        ),
        (
            "Questions for the call",
            [r"\?$", r"^q[:\d]", r"ask them", r"question"],
        ),
    ]
)

SECTION_ORDER = [
    "Bottom line",
    "Snapshot",
    "Financial signals",
    "Technology signals",
    "Leadership",
    "Recent news",
    "Likely initiatives (hypotheses)",
    "Risks and landmines",
    "Questions for the call",
    "Sources",
]

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Account owner]"


def classify(line: str) -> str:
    """Return the section name for a line, or 'Unclassified'."""
    low = line.lower()
    for section, patterns in RULES.items():
        for pat in patterns:
            if re.search(pat, low):
                return section
    return "Unclassified"


def parse_notes(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, list[tuple[int, str]]], list[tuple[int, str]]]:
    """Split notes into classified items and a list of (line_no, url) sources."""
    buckets: dict[str, list[tuple[int, str]]] = {s: [] for s in SECTION_ORDER}
    buckets["Unclassified"] = []
    sources: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
    current_heading: str | None = None

    for n, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        # Explicit user headings override heuristics: "## Leadership" or "[leadership]"
        m = re.match(r"^(?:#+\s*|\[)([A-Za-z /()]+?)\]?\s*$", line)
        if m:
            name = m.group(1).strip().lower()
            matched = next((s for s in SECTION_ORDER if s.lower().startswith(name[:8])), None)
            current_heading = matched
            continue
        for url in URL_RE.findall(line):
            sources.append((n, url))
        section = current_heading or classify(line)
        buckets.setdefault(section, []).append((n, line))
    return buckets, sources


def norm_line(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s.strip().lstrip("-*#> ").strip()).lower()


def compare_previous(prev_text: str, buckets: dict, sources: list) -> dict:
    """Which note lines are new since the previous brief, and which previous sources the notes dropped."""
    prev_norm = norm_line(prev_text.replace("\\|", "|"))
    prev_urls = list(OrderedDict.fromkeys(URL_RE.findall(prev_text)))
    new_lines = set()
    for items in buckets.values():
        for n, line in items:
            urls = URL_RE.findall(line)
            text_seen = norm_line(URL_RE.sub("", line)) and norm_line(URL_RE.sub("", line)) in prev_norm
            if not (text_seen or (urls and all(u in prev_urls for u in urls))):
                new_lines.add(n)
    now_urls = {u for _, u in sources}
    return {"new_lines": new_lines, "dropped_sources": [u for u in prev_urls if u not in now_urls]}


def changes_section(delta: dict, buckets: dict) -> list[str]:
    out = ["## Changes since the last brief", ""]
    new = [(n, line, sec) for sec, items in buckets.items() for n, line in items
           if n in delta["new_lines"] and not line.startswith("#")]
    out += [f"- NEW (L{n}, {sec}): {line.replace('|', chr(92) + '|')}" for n, line, sec in sorted(new)] or \
           ["- No new material since the last brief."]
    out += [f"- Not re-confirmed: {u} was cited last time and is not in the notes — re-check or drop it ({TBD})"
            for u in delta["dropped_sources"]]
    return out + [""]


def render(company: str, purpose: str, buckets: dict, sources: list, today: str, delta: dict | None = None) -> str:
    out: list[str] = []
    out.append(f"# Client Brief — {company} — for {purpose} on {TBD}")
    out.append("")
    out.append(f"Prepared: {today} · Angle: {TBD} · Network used: no (skeleton from notes)")
    out.append("")
    # every item has a citable id: one per URL in the notes, plus one for the notes themselves (user-supplied, unverified)
    sid: dict[str, str] = {}
    for _, url in sources:
        sid.setdefault(url, f"S{len(sid) + 1}")
    notes_id = f"S{len(sid) + 1}"
    out.append("## Bottom line")
    out.append(f"1. {TBD}")
    out.append(f"2. {TBD}")
    out.append(f"3. {TBD}")
    out.append("")

    for section in SECTION_ORDER[1:-1]:
        out.append(f"## {section}")
        items = buckets.get(section, [])
        if items:
            out.append("| # | Material from notes (line) | Source | Confidence | To do |")
            out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|")
            for i, (n, line) in enumerate(items, start=1):
                urls = URL_RE.findall(line)
                src = f"{sid[urls[0]]} {urls[0]}" if urls and urls[0] in sid else f"{notes_id} (notes)"
                cell = line.replace("|", "\\|")
                todo = "NEW since last brief — verify and cite" if delta and n in delta["new_lines"] else "verify and cite"
                out.append(f"| {i} | {cell} (L{n}) | {src} | {TBD} | {todo} |")
        else:
            out.append(f"_No material in notes._ {TBD}")
        out.append("")

    if delta is not None:
        out += changes_section(delta, buckets)
    out.append("## Sources")
    out.append("| # | Source | Section / page | Date accessed | Tier |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|")
    listed = set()
    for n, url in sources:
        if url not in listed:
            listed.add(url)
            out.append(f"| {sid[url]} | {url} | (notes L{n}) | {TBD} | {TBD} |")
    out.append(f"| {notes_id} | Account notes supplied by the user (unverified until cited to a public source) | line numbers as given | {TBD} | user notes |")
    out.append("")

    unclassified = buckets.get("Unclassified", [])
    if unclassified:
        out.append("## Unclassified notes (place manually)")
        out.append("| Line | Text |")
        out.append("|---|---|")
        for n, line in unclassified:
            out.append(f"| L{n} | {line.replace('|', '\\|')} |")
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out)


def render_final(company: str, purpose: str, buckets: dict, sources: list, today: str, delta: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """The brief on the template's sections, every item cited by source id; no model step."""
    sid: dict[str, str] = {}
    for _, url in sources:           # same ids as the skeleton's Sources table
        sid.setdefault(url, f"S{len(sid) + 1}")

    def cite(n: int, line: str) -> str:
        ids = [sid[u] for u in URL_RE.findall(line) if u in sid]
        return " ".join(f"[{x}]" for x in dict.fromkeys(ids)) or f"notes L{n}"

    def text(line: str) -> str:
        return URL_RE.sub("", line).strip(" —-:").replace("|", "\\|") or line.replace("|", "\\|")

    out = [f"# Client Brief — {company} — for {purpose} on {TBD}", "",
           f"Prepared: {today} · Angle: {TBD} · Network used: no (brief from the user's notes)", "",
           "> Script draft — the model step was not run (draft only): items are the user's notes, verbatim and cited; "
           "inferences and the so-what are owned markers.", "", "## Bottom line"]
    cited = [(n, line) for sec in ("Financial signals", "Technology signals", "Leadership", "Recent news", "Snapshot")
             for n, line in buckets.get(sec, []) if URL_RE.search(line)]
    for i, (n, line) in enumerate(cited[:3], start=1):
        out.append(f"{i}. {text(line)} {cite(n, line)} — so what: {TBD}")
    if not cited:
        out.append(f"1. {TBD} (no cited material in the notes)")
    out.append("")
    for section in SECTION_ORDER[1:-1]:
        out += [f"## {section}", ""]
        items = buckets.get(section, [])
        if items:
            out += ["| # | Item (verbatim from notes) | Source | Confidence |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
            out += [f"| {i} | {text(line)} | {cite(n, line)} | {TBD} |" for i, (n, line) in enumerate(items, start=1)]
        else:
            out.append(f"_No material in notes._ {TBD}")
        out.append("")
    if delta is not None:
        out += changes_section(delta, buckets)
    out += ["## Sources", "", "| # | Source | Section / page | Date accessed | Tier |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    listed = set()
    for n, u in sources:
        if u not in listed:
            listed.add(u)
            out.append(f"| {sid[u]} | {u} | (notes L{n}) | {TBD} | {TBD} |")
    if not sources:
        out.append(f"| — | {TBD} | | | |")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def coverage_report(buckets: dict) -> str:
    rows = []
    for section in SECTION_ORDER[1:-1]:
        count = len(buckets.get(section, []))
        status = "EMPTY — needs research" if count == 0 else f"{count} item(s)"
        rows.append(f"  {section:<34} {status}")
    rows.append(f"  {'Unclassified':<34} {len(buckets.get('Unclassified', []))} item(s)")
    return "\n".join(rows)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--notes", required=True, help="Path to notes/links file (.md or .txt)")
    p.add_argument("--company", required=True, help="Company name for the brief title")
    p.add_argument("--purpose", default="discovery", help="discovery | proposal | exec-meeting | pitch")
    p.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="Output Markdown path (default: stdout)")
    p.add_argument("--previous", default=None, help="the last brief for this client (refresh: new vs carried)")
    p.add_argument("--final", default=None, help="final brief path (written with --draft-only)")
    p.add_argument("--draft-only", action="store_true", help="no model step: write --final from the notes")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)

    path = Path(args.notes)
    if not path.is_file():
        print(f"error: notes file not found: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if not text.strip():
        print(f"error: notes file is empty: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    buckets, sources = parse_notes(text)
    today = dt.date.today().isoformat()
    delta = None
    if args.previous:
        pp = Path(args.previous)
        if not pp.is_file():
            print(f"error: previous brief not found: {pp}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        delta = compare_previous(pp.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), buckets, sources)
    md = render(args.company, args.purpose, buckets, sources, today, delta)
    if args.draft_only and args.final:
        Path(args.final).write_text(render_final(args.company, args.purpose, buckets, sources, today, delta), encoding="utf-8")

    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(md, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {args.out}")
    else:
        print(md)
    print("\nCoverage:", file=sys.stderr)
    print(coverage_report(buckets), file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Research Method

## 1. Emphasis by purpose
Weights are the share of the one page each section should take. Cut sections below 5% to a single line.

| Section | Discovery call | Proposal / RFP | Exec meeting (1:1) | Pitch (competitive) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Snapshot | 10% | 10% | 5% | 10% |
| Financial signals | 10% | 20% | 10% | 15% |
| Technology signals | 25% | 20% | 10% | 20% |
| Leadership | 10% | 10% | 35% | 15% |
| Recent news | 10% | 10% | 15% | 10% |
| Likely initiatives / hypotheses | 25% | 15% | 15% | 15% |
| Risks and landmines | 5% | 10% | 5% | 10% |
| Questions for the call | 5% | 5% | 5% | 5% |

## 2. Source tiers
Use the highest tier available. Cite tier in the Sources appendix so the reader can judge reliability.

| Tier | Source type | Use for | Caution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regulatory filings (10-K/10-Q/20-F, annual report, proxy), audited accounts | Revenue, margin, segment data, stated strategy, risk factors, named programs, executive comp drivers | Public companies only; dates lag 1–3 months |
| 2 | Investor materials: earnings transcripts, investor-day decks | Initiatives with executive ownership, capex guidance, cost-out targets, timeline statements | Forward-looking; quote exact wording |
| 3 | Company press releases, regulator notices, court filings | Leadership changes, acquisitions, partnerships, enforcement | Spin; corroborate with Tier 1–2 |
| 4 | Reputable business and trade press | Context, analyst reaction, program status | Verify numbers against Tier 1 |
| 5 | Job postings, engineering blogs, conference talks, vendor case studies | Technology stack, team size, platform migrations, pain areas | Signals, not facts; rate confidence |
| 6 | LinkedIn/public profiles, social posts, review sites | Leadership tenure and background, culture signals | Public-record facts only; no inference |
| 7 | Our prior notes and relationship history (from the notes file) | Context, prior conversations, known incumbents | Internal; never appears in client-facing material |

Rules:
- A number without a Tier 1–3 source is labeled "reported" with its Tier 4–5 source, or is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
- Private companies: ownership structure and public events only. No revenue estimates from aggregator sites (they are frequently wrong and cannot be defended in a meeting).
- Date every source. A 2023 job posting is a weak signal for 2026 stack.

## 3. Financial-signal extraction (public companies)
Pull exactly these from the latest annual filing and most recent quarterly; cite page or section.

| Signal | Where in the filing | Why it matters to us |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue and trend (3 years) | Selected financial data / MD&A | Size of opportunity; growth or cost-out mode |
| Operating margin trend | MD&A | Margin pressure → cost-out programs → migration/TCO plays |
| Capex and technology spend commentary | MD&A, cash-flow discussion | Funding shape (capex vs opex) |
| Named programs ("transformation", "modernization", "simplification") | MD&A, CEO letter, earnings transcript | Sponsor language to mirror in the proposal |
| Risk factors mentioning technology, cyber, legacy systems, integration, vendors | Item 1A (10-K) | Board-visible pain; quote verbatim |
| Restructuring charges | Notes to financials | Headcount reductions → capacity gaps → partner demand |
| Acquisitions / divestitures | Notes, press releases | Integration programs; platform consolidation |
| Segment reporting | Notes | Which business unit the sponsor sits in and its share |
| Auditor or control weaknesses | Item 9A | Compliance-driven urgency |

For higher-ed and public institutions: use audited financial statements, bond offering documents (very detailed on strategy and risk), accreditation reports, and board minutes where public.

## 4. Leadership profiling rules
| Include | Exclude |
|---|---|
| Title, start date, prior employer and role, public talks, quoted priorities, programs announced under them | Age, family, personal social media, speculation about internal politics or performance, anything from private sources |
| Changes since arrival (reorgs, vendor changes, hires) from Tier 3–5 sources | Characterizations ("hands-on", "political") |
| Reporting line if stated publicly | Inferred reporting line |

Format: one row per person. `Role | Name | Since | Prior | Public priorities (quoted, sourced) | Relevance to our angle`.

## 5. Likely initiatives — hypothesis format
| Initiative (hypothesis) | Signals (with tier) | Confidence | Confirming question for the call | Our angle |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Confidence: High = Tier 1–2 source names it; Med = two independent Tier 3–5 signals; Low = one Tier 5 signal. Do not list Low-confidence initiatives in the Bottom line.

## 6. Risks and landmines
Things that could embarrass us or kill the conversation if unknown:
- Recent outage, breach, or regulatory action (do not reference unprompted; be prepared if they do)
- Litigation with a vendor we might name
- Incumbent partners with a long relationship (check case studies and press releases)
- Executive departures in the last 90 days
- Public commitments (dates, savings targets) that any proposal must respect

## 7. Writing the brief
- Bottom line = three facts, each sourced, each with a "so what" for our angle.
- One page. The reader is walking into a meeting; they will not read page two.
- Tables for leadership, tech signals, initiatives, news.
- No adjectives about the company ("innovative", "struggling"). State the fact and the metric.
- Sources appendix: numbered, with URL or document name, section/page, date accessed, tier.

# Technology-Signal Playbook

Goal: infer the client's platform estate, integration approach, cloud posture, and team shape from public signals, with honest confidence ratings.

## 1. Where signals live
| Signal source | What it reveals | Typical confidence | How to read it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Job postings (careers page, aggregators) | Named platforms (ERP, iPaaS, API gateway, cloud, data stack), team size (number of similar reqs), seniority mix, locations (onshore/offshore), migration language ("experience migrating from X to Y") | Med (High if 3+ postings over 6 months agree) | Required skills = current stack; "nice to have" or "experience with" = target stack. A posting for "Platform X migration lead" is a program signal |
| Engineering / tech blog, conference talks | Architecture decisions, platform choices, scale figures, team names | High for what is stated; dates matter | Quote the talk title and date |
| Vendor case studies and press releases | Confirmed vendor relationships, scope of use, go-live year | High for relationship; Med for current scope | Vendors overstate; check the date |
| Open-source repos / GitHub org | Languages, frameworks, CI tooling, API styles | Med | May be side projects |
| Public API developer portals | API gateway product (visible in URL patterns, headers, portal branding), API maturity, versioning | High for gateway product | Look at docs footer, auth flow, base URLs |
| Status pages, incident posts | Platform components, cloud provider regions, outage patterns | Med | Dates of incidents feed urgency |
| DNS / MX / TLS (only if user provides lookup output) | Email provider, CDN, hosting | Med | Do not run lookups from this skill; use provided data |
| Earnings calls / filings | Named transformation programs, cloud commitments, platform consolidations | High | Tier 1–2 |
| Partner ecosystem pages (vendor "customers" lists) | Vendor relationships | Med | Lists go stale |
| Analyst reports (if provided) | Strategy context | Med–High | Cite the report |
| LinkedIn titles of staff (public) | Team structure, platform specialists on staff | Low–Med | Titles lag reality |

## 2. Confidence rubric
| Rating | Rule |
|---|---|
| High | Stated by the company itself (filing, blog, talk, developer portal) or confirmed by two independent Tier 3–5 sources within 18 months |
| Med | One Tier 3–5 source within 18 months, or two older sources |
| Low | One source older than 18 months, or inferred from indirect evidence (e.g., a single job posting) |

Never write "they use X" at Low confidence. Write "signal suggests X (Low: single posting, 2024)".

## 3. Signal-to-hypothesis patterns
| Signal pattern | Likely situation | Our angle |
|---|---|---|
| Postings for both legacy iPaaS and a newer API gateway | Migration under way or planned; licensing-cost driver | Migration factory, TCO case (`integration-migration-assessor`) |
| Many postings for integration developers over 12 months, no architect postings | Sprawl without governance; key-person risk | Integration assessment, platform standards |
| ERP upgrade posting + "data migration" + "testing" roles | ERP program in flight; integration re-platform rides along | Integration workstream, test automation |
| "AI engineer" postings but no data-engineering postings | AI ambition ahead of data readiness | Data foundation first, use-case canvas |
| Multiple cloud providers in postings | Multi-cloud by acquisition; consolidation opportunity | Platform rationalization |
| Offshore locations appearing in postings for the first time | Building captive offshore; partner competition or opportunity to run it | Managed service / build-operate-transfer |
| Status page shows repeated incidents on one component | Operational pain with a visible date trail | Resilience, observability, modernization |
| Developer portal on a known gateway product with few APIs | Platform bought, not adopted | API program acceleration |

## 4. Recording signals
Table columns in the brief:
`Area | Signal (what you saw) | Source (URL/doc, date) | Confidence | Inference | Confirming question`

Areas to cover: ERP/core, integration/API platform, cloud and infrastructure, data and analytics, AI/ML, security/compliance, customer-facing digital, engineering practices (CI/CD, SRE), sourcing model (captive, partners named).

## 5. What not to do
- Do not scrape, log in, or access anything non-public. Public pages and user-provided material only.
- Do not infer vendor relationships from a logo on a slide at a conference.
- Do not assume a posting means a funded program; it may be backfill.
- Do not present a stack diagram as fact. Label it "inferred from public signals; to be confirmed in discovery".
