# effort-estimator

## In a conversation: build the estimate now
The reply **is the estimate**, about 1,000 tokens: compact tables (WBS ≤ 12 rows), one line per point, no preamble — all seven parts must fit, so never spend the reply on one part. Never claim a Monte Carlo figure you did not compute: P50/P80/P90 come from the `estimate.py` run (quote them exactly when its output is in the conversation, else `[from estimate.py run — owner: Estimation lead]`); never write only a command.
- **The request carries scope counts** (e.g. "118 interfaces: 60 simple, 40 medium, 18 complex"), even when it says the actuals, WBS or rate card are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the estimate **in this reply**, in this order. Never reply with only a request for files.
  1. **WBS** in the `assets/wbs-template.csv` columns (`task_id, phase, work_package, task, role, driver_group, count, unit_o, unit_m, unit_p, …, basis, predecessors, notes`): parametric rows per band (count × unit effort, basis `PAR`, citing the prior actuals as the unit source), plus explicit PM, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare and KT packages. Unit efforts not in the conversation are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the attached actuals as source.
  2. **Model**: the exact command — `python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md` — and a results table P50 / P80 / P90 effort and cost with **contingency = P80 − P50** as its own column; figures not yet computed read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead, from the estimate.py run]`.
  3. **Confidence quoted** per `references/estimation-method.md` §4, and why: fixed price, inventory known → P80; fixed price, inventory unconfirmed → P90 or assessment first; T&M → P50 with P80 as NTE.
  4. **Staffing table** by role and phase with onshore/offshore split, allocations between 20% and 100%, leverage ratio.
  5. **Price and margin**: price only from the supplied rate card (effort × bill rate), margin at P50 and at P80; rates not visible are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, never typical rates.
  6. **Assumptions**: every count and unit effort as a row with its source.
  7. **Memo** in the `assets/estimate-summary-template.md` sections: Bottom line, Basis of estimate (basis mix ANA/PAR/JUD %), Assumptions, Exclusions, Risks to the estimate and de-risking, Sensitivity, Staffing, Price-to-win.
- **WBS given (or said to be attached), no rate card** ("here is the WBS, give me the price"): ask once for the rate card with its columns (`role, grade, location, cost_rate, bill_rate, currency, valid_until`), and in the same reply produce the **effort-only output**: `| | P50 | P80 | P90 | Contingency (P80 − P50) |` effort row (from the WBS run, or `[from estimate.py run]` when the WBS content is not visible), the staffing table by role and phase, and a price row that reads exactly **`Price: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] — no rate card supplied; no rates assumed`**.
- **No WBS and no scope** ("give me the price for Acme"): ask once for the WBS (`assets/wbs-template.csv`) — `estimate.py` cannot run without it — and the rate card; invent no tasks.
- **WBS and rate card attached**: line 1 the command — `python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rates.csv --iterations 20000 --seed 7 --out estimate.md --memo estimate-memo.md --client <client> [--previous estimate-previous.json] [--draft-only]` (+ `--json` → `estimate.json`) — then P50/P80/P90 with contingency = P80 − P50, staffing, price and margin, and the memo in the template sections (Bottom line, Basis of estimate, Assumptions, Risks). `draft_only` / "no LLM": the memo is written from the run's figures, **labelled as a draft**, every figure tracing to `estimate.md`.
- **Re-estimate with a previous `estimate.json`**: a change table `| Item | Previous | Now | Change |` for P80 effort, each phase (a phase absent before is "new"), and price at P80 — previous values copied exactly from the file, current values from this run — and the memo repeats that table.
- **No scope or WBS at all**: ask once, in one list, for the scope counts, phases, commercial model and rate card; say no counts, unit efforts or rates will be invented.
- **Asked to use an "industry-standard" unit effort or quote fixed price at P50**: decline in one line (there is no sourced industry standard; a P50 fixed price carries no contingency, so it loses money half the time). Do not supply an industry figure. Use the user's own figure (e.g. 3 days per interface) only if they confirm it as their assumption, labelled `JUD`, with the anchor source `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Flag that `JUD` > 30% of effort makes the estimate low-confidence and recommend an assessment phase or per-unit pricing with a count band. Do not stop at asking — show, in this reply: `| Unit effort | 3 days/interface — user's figure, basis JUD | anchor source [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] |`; `Basis mix: JUD 100% > 30% → low confidence → recommend an assessment phase, or per-unit pricing with a count band`; `| | P50 | P80 | Contingency (P80 − P50) |` side by side; and the recommendation P80/P90 fixed or T&M with a P80 NTE.

## Starting points
- **New** — your WBS (and rate card) is modelled: P10–P90 effort, phases, variance contributors, staffing, cost and price; the model step writes the memo, or with `draft_only` the memo is written from the run's figures, every number traceable.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (the earlier run's `estimate.json`): the re-estimate shows what changed — totals, each phase and price at P80, previous → now — in the report and the memo.

## When to use
- "Size the <initiative> engagement."
- "Give me P50/P80 for this WBS."
- "What team do we need and what is the onshore/offshore split?"
- "Does this price hold margin?"
- NOT for: benefits and ROI (`value-case-builder`), interface-level complexity scoring (`integration-migration-assessor` feeds this skill), narrative (`proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Scope definition: deliverables, counts (interfaces, components, sites, users), phases | yes | discovery synthesis / architecture doc / assessor output |
| Rate card CSV (role, location, cost rate, bill rate, currency) | yes for cost/price; else effort-only | user file (`assets/rate-card.example.csv` shows the layout) |
| Constraints: deadline, team-size cap, onshore/offshore policy, client-side availability | no | user |
| Target margin or price-to-win (if known) | no | user |
| Prior actuals for similar work (if any) | no | user file |

If scope counts are missing, ask once; otherwise estimate per unit and mark counts `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` so the total scales. If the rate card is missing, produce effort and staffing only; never invent rates.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Decompose to a WBS** per `references/estimation-method.md` §1: phases → work packages → tasks sized 2–15 person-days. Each task carries a driver (count × unit effort) or a fixed effort, a role mix, and a dependency. Keep management, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, and knowledge transfer as explicit packages; they are the most frequently omitted.
2. **Assign 3-point estimates** (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic) per task using the calibration rules in §2. Pessimistic is the "things go wrong but not catastrophic" case, typically 1.5–3× most-likely. Record the basis for each: analogy (prior actual), parametric (count × unit), or expert judgment. Expert judgment on >30% of effort is a flag in the output.
3. **Run the model**: `python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md`. Outputs P50/P80/P90 effort and cost, per-phase distribution, staffing table, and a sensitivity list (tasks contributing most variance). Without `--rates`, the script outputs effort only. Rates match on role AND location (add a WBS `location` column when a role is priced onshore and offshore); a mixed-currency card needs `--currency` and sourced `--fx CUR=rate`, otherwise the script stops. The script does not compute duration; the memo derives it from the critical path and staffing plan or marks it `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead]`.
4. **Decision point — confidence level to quote.** Per §4: fixed-price → P80 minimum, P90 for migrations with unknown inventories; T&M → P50 as the estimate with P80 as the not-to-exceed; assessments → fixed at P80 with a short duration. State which was used and why.
5. **Build the staffing pyramid** per `references/staffing-and-rates.md`: roles, grades, allocation by phase, onshore/offshore split against policy and client constraints, ramp-up and ramp-down, leverage ratio. Check span of control and that no role is allocated above 100% or below a useful minimum (20%).
6. **Cost and margin**: cost = effort × cost rate; price = effort × bill rate or target-margin markup; contingency = (P80 − P50) shown explicitly, not buried in rates. Compare with price-to-win if given; if the gap exceeds 15%, list scope or mix levers rather than cutting the estimate.
7. **Write the estimate memo** on `assets/estimate-summary-template.md`: bottom line (P80 effort, duration, team, price or "price pending rate card"), basis of estimate, assumptions (every count and rate), exclusions, risks to the estimate, sensitivity.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File |
|---|---|
| WBS with 3-point estimates | `wbs-<client>-<initiative>.csv` (layout: `assets/wbs-template.csv`) |
| Model output | `estimate-<client>-<initiative>.md` (from script) |
| Estimate memo | `estimate-memo-<client>-<initiative>.md` (template: `assets/estimate-summary-template.md`) |

## Self-check
- [ ] WBS includes PM, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, KT packages
- [ ] Every task has basis (analogy / parametric / judgment); judgment share reported
- [ ] Confidence level chosen and justified against the commercial model
- [ ] Contingency shown explicitly as P80 − P50
- [ ] Rates only from the supplied rate card; no rates if none supplied
- [ ] Every count is an assumption row with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` where unconfirmed
- [ ] Staffing allocations between 20% and 100%; leverage ratio stated
- [ ] Totals reconcile across WBS, model output, and memo

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/effort-estimator --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/effort-estimator`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## References
- `references/estimation-method.md` — WBS rules, 3-point calibration, PERT/Monte Carlo, confidence selection, sensitivity
- `references/staffing-and-rates.md` — pyramid design, onshore/offshore, leverage, margin sanity, rate-card contract
- `assets/wbs-template.csv` — WBS input layout
- `assets/rate-card.example.csv` — rate-card layout with EXAMPLE placeholder rows (replace with real rates; never ship)
- `assets/estimate-summary-template.md` — memo template
- `scripts/estimate.py` — PERT + Monte Carlo, staffing table, cost roll-up
skills/presales/effort-estimator/scripts:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PERT + Monte Carlo effort model over a WBS CSV, with staffing and cost roll-up.

Input WBS CSV columns (see assets/wbs-template.csv):
  task_id, phase, work_package, task, role, driver_group, count,
  unit_o, unit_m, unit_p, optimistic, most_likely, pessimistic, basis, predecessors, notes

Per task, effort in person-days is either:
  * parametric: count * unit_{o,m,p}   (used when count and unit_* are numeric), or
  * fixed:      optimistic / most_likely / pessimistic.
Rows whose count is non-numeric (e.g. "[TO BE BASELINED]") are reported as
unresolved and excluded from the totals, so the output never contains a figure
that was not in the input.

Model: Beta-PERT sampling per task (lambda = 4). Tasks sharing a non-empty
driver_group receive a common multiplier per iteration (log-normal, sigma 0.15)
to represent correlated uncertainty. Outputs P10/P50/P80/P90 totals, per-phase
statistics, variance contributors, basis mix, and (with --rates) a cost roll-up
and margin at P50 and P80.

Rate card CSV columns (see assets/rate-card.example.csv):
  role, grade, location, cost_rate, bill_rate, currency, valid_until, notes
Rates match on role AND location. A role priced at one location matches WBS rows
without a location; a role priced at several locations needs the optional WBS
`location` column (otherwise exit 2). Duplicate (role, location) rows are rejected.
Costs are never summed across currencies: a mixed-currency card needs --currency
plus a sourced --fx CUR=rate per other currency, else exit 2. Expired or unreadable
valid_until dates are flagged. Roles absent from the rate card are listed and
excluded from cost; no rate is ever assumed.

Effort cells must be numbers >= 0; blank or [TO BE BASELINED] marks the task
unresolved; negative, non-finite or other non-numeric values exit 2, as do
duplicate task_id rows. Duration is not computed (effort only) and is reported
as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead]. CSVs may carry a UTF-8 BOM.

Usage:
    python3 -I estimate.py wbs.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md
    python3 -I estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --seed 7
    python3 -I estimate.py wbs.csv --json          # machine-readable summary
    python3 -I estimate.py wbs.csv --rates card.csv --currency USD --fx INR=0.012

Existing estimate (re-estimate): --previous <estimate.json from the earlier run> adds "Change vs previous
estimate" to the report — P50/P80/P90 and each phase, old → new with the delta, and price at P80 when
both runs were costed in the same currency — so a revised WBS is explained, not just re-quoted.
--draft-only --memo <path>: writes the estimate memo on assets/estimate-summary-template.md's sections
(Bottom line, Basis of estimate, Assumptions, Risks, …) from this run alone, every figure exactly as in
the Markdown report, labelled as a draft (the model step was not run); what the model cannot know is an
owned to-be-baselined marker.

Standard library only. Exit 0 ok; 2 input error.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import random
import statistics
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

PERT_LAMBDA = 4.0
GROUP_SIGMA = 0.15


@dataclass
class Task:
    task_id: str
    phase: str
    work_package: str
    name: str
    role: str
    driver_group: str
    o: float
    m: float
    p: float
    basis: str
    predecessors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    unresolved_reason: str = ""
    location: str = ""

    @property
    def pert_mean(self) -> float:
        return (self.o + PERT_LAMBDA * self.m + self.p) / (PERT_LAMBDA + 2)

    @property
    def pert_sd(self) -> float:
        return (self.p - self.o) / 6.0


TBD_EST = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead]"
TBD_FIN = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Finance lead]"
PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS = ("TO BE BASELINED", "TBD")


def _num(v: str) -> float | None:
    try:
        x = float(str(v).strip())
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return x if math.isfinite(x) else None


def _effort_value(raw: str | None, where: str, col: str) -> float | None:
    """Parse one effort cell.

    Blank or an explicit placeholder ("[TO BE BASELINED]", "TBD") -> None (the task is
    reported as unresolved). Any other non-numeric, non-finite or negative value is an
    input error: effort cannot be negative and garbage must not be silently dropped.
    """
    s = (raw or "").strip()
    if not s or any(mk in s.upper() for mk in PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS):
        return None
    try:
        v = float(s.replace(",", ""))
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: {col} is not a number: {s!r} "
                         "(use a number >= 0, leave it blank, or write [TO BE BASELINED])") from None
    if not math.isfinite(v):
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: {col} is not a finite number: {s!r}")
    if v < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: {col} must be >= 0 (effort cannot be negative), got {s!r}")
    return v


def _open_csv(path: Path):
    # utf-8-sig strips the BOM Excel writes on "CSV UTF-8" exports; without it the first
    # header becomes "\ufeffrole" and every lookup on that column silently misses.
    return open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig")


def load_wbs(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Task], list[Task]]:
    tasks: list[Task] = []
    unresolved: list[Task] = []
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    with _open_csv(path) as fh:
        rdr = csv.DictReader(fh)
        required = {"task_id", "phase", "task", "role"}
        missing = required - set(rdr.fieldnames or [])
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"WBS missing columns: {sorted(missing)}")
        for row in rdr:
            tid = (row.get("task_id") or "").strip()
            if not tid:
                continue
            line = rdr.line_num
            if tid in seen:
                raise ValueError(f"WBS: duplicate task_id '{tid}' (lines {seen[tid]} and {line}); "
                                 "task ids must be unique")
            seen[tid] = line
            where = f"WBS task {tid} (line {line})"
            count = _effort_value(row.get("count"), where, "count")
            uo, um, up = (_effort_value(row.get(k), where, k) for k in ("unit_o", "unit_m", "unit_p"))
            fo, fm, fp = (_effort_value(row.get(k), where, k)
                          for k in ("optimistic", "most_likely", "pessimistic"))
            reason = ""
            if count is not None and None not in (uo, um, up):
                o, m, p = count * uo, count * um, count * up  # type: ignore[operator]
            elif None not in (fo, fm, fp):
                o, m, p = fo, fm, fp  # type: ignore[assignment]
            elif (row.get("count") or "").strip() and None not in (uo, um, up):
                reason = f"count not numeric: '{row.get('count')}'"
                o = m = p = 0.0
            else:
                reason = "no numeric three-point values"
                o = m = p = 0.0
            if not reason and not (o <= m <= p):
                reason = f"three-point values not ordered (O<=M<=P): {o}, {m}, {p}"
            t = Task(
                task_id=tid,
                phase=(row.get("phase") or "").strip(),
                work_package=(row.get("work_package") or "").strip(),
                name=(row.get("task") or "").strip(),
                role=(row.get("role") or "").strip(),
                driver_group=(row.get("driver_group") or "").strip(),
                o=o, m=m, p=p,
                basis=(row.get("basis") or "JUD").strip().upper() or "JUD",
                predecessors=[x.strip() for x in (row.get("predecessors") or "").split(";") if x.strip()],
                unresolved_reason=reason,
                location=(row.get("location") or "").strip(),
            )
            (unresolved if reason else tasks).append(t)
    return tasks, unresolved


def _key(s: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(s.split()).casefold()


def load_rates(path: Path, as_of: date | None = None) -> dict[str, dict[str, dict]]:
    """Rate card keyed by role, then location (both case-insensitive).

    A role may have one row per location (onshore/offshore/...). Two rows for the same
    role AND location are an input error: the previous implementation kept the last one
    silently.
    """
    as_of = as_of or date.today()
    rates: dict[str, dict[str, dict]] = {}
    with _open_csv(path) as fh:
        rdr = csv.DictReader(fh)
        if "role" not in (rdr.fieldnames or []):
            raise ValueError(f"rate card missing column 'role' (found: {rdr.fieldnames})")
        for row in rdr:
            role = (row.get("role") or "").strip()
            if not role:
                continue
            loc = (row.get("location") or "").strip()
            line = rdr.line_num
            by_loc = rates.setdefault(_key(role), {})
            if _key(loc) in by_loc:
                prev = by_loc[_key(loc)]
                raise ValueError(
                    f"rate card: duplicate rows for role '{role}' at location '{loc or '(blank)'}' "
                    f"(lines {prev['line']} and {line}); keep one row per role and location")
            vu = (row.get("valid_until") or "").strip()
            validity = ""
            if vu:
                try:
                    if date.fromisoformat(vu) < as_of:
                        validity = f"expired {vu}"
                except ValueError:
                    validity = f"valid_until not an ISO date: '{vu}'"
            rate = {
                "role": role,
                "location": loc,
                "line": line,
                "cost_rate": _num(row.get("cost_rate", "")),
                "bill_rate": _num(row.get("bill_rate", "")),
                "currency": (row.get("currency") or "").strip().upper(),
                "valid_until": vu,
                "validity_issue": validity,
                "example": "EXAMPLE" in (row.get("notes") or "").upper() or "EXAMPLE" in (row.get("grade") or "").upper(),
            }
            for col in ("cost_rate", "bill_rate"):
                raw = (row.get(col) or "").strip()
                if raw and (rate[col] is None or rate[col] < 0):
                    raise ValueError(f"rate card line {line} ({role}): {col} must be a number >= 0, got {raw!r}")
            by_loc[_key(loc)] = rate
    return rates


def parse_fx(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """--fx INR=0.012 means 1 INR = 0.012 units of the reporting currency."""
    fx: dict[str, float] = {}
    for it in [x for item in (items or []) for x in item.split(",") if x.strip()]:  # repeatable and/or comma list
        cur, sep, val = it.partition("=")
        rate = _num(val) if sep else None
        if not cur.strip() or rate is None or rate <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"--fx must look like CUR=rate with rate > 0 (1 CUR = rate reporting currency), got {it!r}")
        fx[cur.strip().upper()] = rate
    return fx


def pert_sample(rng: random.Random, o: float, m: float, p: float) -> float:
    if p <= o:
        return m
    a = 1 + PERT_LAMBDA * (m - o) / (p - o)
    b = 1 + PERT_LAMBDA * (p - m) / (p - o)
    return o + rng.betavariate(a, b) * (p - o)


def percentile(sorted_vals: list[float], q: float) -> float:
    if not sorted_vals:
        return 0.0
    k = (len(sorted_vals) - 1) * q
    f = math.floor(k)
    c = min(f + 1, len(sorted_vals) - 1)
    return sorted_vals[f] + (sorted_vals[c] - sorted_vals[f]) * (k - f)


def simulate(tasks: list[Task], iterations: int, seed: int | None) -> dict:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    groups = sorted({t.driver_group for t in tasks if t.driver_group})
    totals: list[float] = []
    phase_totals: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
    task_samples: dict[str, list[float]] = {t.task_id: [] for t in tasks}
    for _ in range(iterations):
        mult = {g: math.exp(rng.gauss(0.0, GROUP_SIGMA)) for g in groups}
        total = 0.0
        per_phase: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
        for t in tasks:
            v = pert_sample(rng, t.o, t.m, t.p)
            if t.driver_group:
                v *= mult[t.driver_group]
            task_samples[t.task_id].append(v)
            total += v
            per_phase[t.phase] += v
        totals.append(total)
        for ph, v in per_phase.items():
            phase_totals[ph].append(v)
    totals.sort()
    out = {
        "iterations": iterations,
        "total": {q: percentile(totals, q / 100) for q in (10, 50, 80, 90)},
        "mean": statistics.fmean(totals) if totals else 0.0,
        "phases": {},
        "variance": [],
    }
    for ph, vals in phase_totals.items():
        vals.sort()
        out["phases"][ph] = {q: percentile(vals, q / 100) for q in (50, 80, 90)}
    for t in tasks:
        s = sorted(task_samples[t.task_id])
        out["variance"].append({
            "task_id": t.task_id, "task": t.name, "phase": t.phase,
            "p10": percentile(s, 0.10), "p90": percentile(s, 0.90),
            "spread": percentile(s, 0.90) - percentile(s, 0.10),
            "variance": statistics.pvariance(s) if len(s) > 1 else 0.0,
        })
    out["variance"].sort(key=lambda r: r["variance"], reverse=True)
    return out


def staffing(tasks: list[Task]) -> dict:
    by_role_phase: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))
    phases: list[str] = []
    for t in tasks:
        if t.phase not in phases:
            phases.append(t.phase)
        label = f"{t.role} ({t.location})" if t.location else t.role
        by_role_phase[label][t.phase] += t.pert_mean
    return {"phases": phases, "roles": {r: dict(p) for r, p in by_role_phase.items()}}


def resolve_rate(task: Task, rates: dict[str, dict[str, dict]]) -> dict | None:
    """Match a task to exactly one rate row on role AND location.

    - task has a location: that (role, location) row, else no match;
    - task has no location: the role's only row; if the role has rows for several
      locations the match is ambiguous and raises (never pick one silently).
    """
    by_loc = rates.get(_key(task.role))
    if not by_loc:
        return None
    if task.location:
        return by_loc.get(_key(task.location))
    if len(by_loc) == 1:
        return next(iter(by_loc.values()))
    locs = sorted(r["location"] or "(blank)" for r in by_loc.values())
    raise ValueError(
        f"rate card has rows for role '{task.role}' at several locations ({', '.join(locs)}) and "
        f"WBS task {task.task_id} does not say which: add a 'location' column to the WBS "
        "(one task row per role and location) so the rate matches on role AND location")


def cost_rollup(tasks: list[Task], rates: dict[str, dict[str, dict]], sim: dict,
                fx: dict[str, float] | None = None, report_currency: str = "") -> dict:
    fx = dict(fx or {})
    groups: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = defaultdict(float)
    rate_for: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    missing: list[str] = []
    for t in tasks:
        r = resolve_rate(t, rates)
        if r is None:
            label = f"{t.role} ({t.location})" if t.location else t.role
            if label not in missing:
                missing.append(label)
            continue
        k = (r["role"], r["location"])
        groups[k] += t.pert_mean
        rate_for[k] = r
    all_mean = sum(t.pert_mean for t in tasks) or 1.0
    scale50 = sim["total"][50] / all_mean
    scale80 = sim["total"][80] / all_mean

    used = list(rate_for.values())
    blank_cur = [f"{r['role']} ({r['location'] or 'no location'}), line {r['line']}" for r in used if not r["currency"]]
    if blank_cur:
        raise ValueError("rate card rows used by the WBS have no currency: " + "; ".join(blank_cur)
                         + " — fill the currency column (ISO code)")
    currencies = sorted({r["currency"] for r in used})
    report = (report_currency or "").strip().upper()
    if not report and len(currencies) == 1:
        report = currencies[0]
    if report:
        fx[report] = 1.0
    unconverted = [c for c in currencies if c not in fx]
    if len(currencies) > 1 and not report:
        raise ValueError(
            f"rate card mixes currencies ({', '.join(currencies)}); costs in different currencies are "
            "never summed under one label. Pass --currency <ISO> plus --fx CUR=rate for each other "
            f"currency from a sourced FX rate, or split the rate card. FX: {TBD_FIN}")
    if unconverted:
        raise ValueError(
            f"no FX rate supplied for {', '.join(unconverted)} into reporting currency {report}; "
            f"pass --fx {unconverted[0]}=<rate> (1 {unconverted[0]} = <rate> {report}). FX: {TBD_FIN}")

    rows, example_flag, validity = [], False, []
    cost50 = price50 = cost80 = price80 = 0.0
    for k in sorted(groups):
        r, pd = rate_for[k], groups[k]
        example_flag = example_flag or r["example"]
        if r["validity_issue"]:
            validity.append(f"{r['role']} ({r['location'] or 'no location'}): {r['validity_issue']}")
        conv = fx[r["currency"]]
        cr, br = r["cost_rate"], r["bill_rate"]
        row = {"role": r["role"], "location": r["location"], "pd_p50": pd * scale50, "pd_p80": pd * scale80,
               "cost_rate": cr, "bill_rate": br, "rate_currency": r["currency"], "fx_to_report": conv,
               "valid_until": r["valid_until"], "validity_issue": r["validity_issue"]}
        if cr is not None:
            row["cost_p50"], row["cost_p80"] = pd * scale50 * cr * conv, pd * scale80 * cr * conv
            cost50 += row["cost_p50"]; cost80 += row["cost_p80"]
        if br is not None:
            row["price_p50"], row["price_p80"] = pd * scale50 * br * conv, pd * scale80 * br * conv
            price50 += row["price_p50"]; price80 += row["price_p80"]
        rows.append(row)
    def margin(price: float, cost: float) -> float | None:
        return (price - cost) / price if price else None
    fx_used = {c: fx[c] for c in currencies if c != report}
    return {"rows": rows, "missing_roles": missing, "currency": report, "fx_used": fx_used,
            "example_rates": example_flag, "rate_validity_issues": validity,
            "cost_p50": cost50, "cost_p80": cost80, "price_p50": price50, "price_p80": price80,
            "margin_p50": margin(price50, cost50), "margin_p80": margin(price80, cost80)}


def predecessor_issues(tasks: list[Task], unresolved: list[Task]) -> list[str]:
    known = {t.task_id for t in tasks} | {t.task_id for t in unresolved}
    out = []
    for t in tasks + unresolved:
        for pr in t.predecessors:
            if pr not in known:
                out.append(f"{t.task_id} -> unknown predecessor '{pr}'")
    return out


def basis_mix(tasks: list[Task]) -> dict[str, float]:
    tot = sum(t.m for t in tasks) or 1.0
    mix: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    for t in tasks:
        mix[t.basis] += t.m / tot
    return dict(mix)


def render_md(tasks, unresolved, sim, staff, cost, mix, pred_issues=None) -> str:
    L: list[str] = []
    tot = sim["total"]
    L.append("# Estimate model output")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Bottom line")
    L.append("| Statistic | Person-days |")
    L.append("|---|---|")
    for q in (10, 50, 80, 90):
        L.append(f"| P{q} | {tot[q]:,.0f} |")
    L.append(f"| Contingency (P80 − P50) | {tot[80]-tot[50]:,.0f} ({(tot[80]-tot[50])/tot[50]*100 if tot[50] else 0:.0f}%) |")
    L.append(f"| Iterations | {sim['iterations']:,} |")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Duration")
    L.append(f"Not computed by this model: figures here are effort in person-days. Duration: {TBD_EST} — "
             "derive it from the critical path (task predecessors) and the staffing plan; "
             "duration is not effort divided by team size.")
    for msg in pred_issues or []:
        L.append(f"- Dependency check: {msg}")
    L.append("")
    jud = mix.get("JUD", 0.0)
    L.append("## Basis mix (share of most-likely effort)")
    L.append("| Basis | Share |")
    L.append("|---|---|")
    for k, v in sorted(mix.items()):
        L.append(f"| {k} | {v*100:.0f}% |")
    if jud > 0.30:
        L.append("")
        L.append(f"**Flag:** expert judgment covers {jud*100:.0f}% of effort (>30%). Treat as low-confidence; recommend an assessment phase before fixed pricing.")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## By phase")
    L.append("| Phase | P50 | P80 | P90 |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|---|")
    for ph in staff["phases"]:
        s = sim["phases"].get(ph, {50: 0, 80: 0, 90: 0})
        L.append(f"| {ph} | {s[50]:,.0f} | {s[80]:,.0f} | {s[90]:,.0f} |")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Top variance contributors")
    L.append("| Task | Phase | P10 | P90 | Spread |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for r in sim["variance"][:8]:
        L.append(f"| {r['task_id']} {r['task']} | {r['phase']} | {r['p10']:,.0f} | {r['p90']:,.0f} | {r['spread']:,.0f} |")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Staffing (PERT-mean person-days by role and phase)")
    hdr = "| Role | " + " | ".join(staff["phases"]) + " | Total |"
    L.append(hdr)
    L.append("|" + "---|" * (len(staff["phases"]) + 2))
    for role, per in sorted(staff["roles"].items()):
        cells = [f"{per.get(ph, 0.0):,.0f}" for ph in staff["phases"]]
        L.append(f"| {role} | " + " | ".join(cells) + f" | {sum(per.values()):,.0f} |")
    L.append("")
    if cost is not None:
        cur = cost["currency"] or ""
        L.append("## Cost and price (from supplied rate card)")
        if cost["example_rates"]:
            L.append("**Warning:** rate card contains EXAMPLE placeholder rows. Figures below are not usable; replace with real rates.")
        for v in cost["rate_validity_issues"]:
            L.append(f"**Warning:** rate validity — {v}. Refresh the rate before quoting; {TBD_FIN}")
        if cost["fx_used"]:
            L.append("FX applied (supplied via --fx; 1 unit = rate in " + cur + "): "
                     + ", ".join(f"{c} {v:g}" for c, v in sorted(cost["fx_used"].items())))
        L.append(f"| Role | Location | Rate currency | PD @P50 | PD @P80 | Cost @P80 ({cur}) | Price @P80 ({cur}) |")
        L.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
        for r in cost["rows"]:
            L.append(f"| {r['role']} | {r['location']} | {r['rate_currency']} | {r['pd_p50']:,.0f} | {r['pd_p80']:,.0f} | "
                     f"{r.get('cost_p80', 0):,.0f} | {r.get('price_p80', 0):,.0f} |")
        L.append("")
        L.append("| Metric | @P50 | @P80 |")
        L.append("|---|---|---|")
        L.append(f"| Cost ({cur}) | {cost['cost_p50']:,.0f} | {cost['cost_p80']:,.0f} |")
        L.append(f"| Price ({cur}) | {cost['price_p50']:,.0f} | {cost['price_p80']:,.0f} |")
        m50 = cost["margin_p50"]; m80 = cost["margin_p80"]
        L.append(f"| Gross margin | {'n/a' if m50 is None else f'{m50*100:.0f}%'} | {'n/a' if m80 is None else f'{m80*100:.0f}%'} |")
        if cost["missing_roles"]:
            L.append("")
            L.append("Roles with no rate-card match (excluded from cost; fix the mapping): " + ", ".join(cost["missing_roles"]))
        L.append("")
    else:
        L.append("## Cost and price")
        L.append("No rate card supplied — effort only. Price: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead]")
        L.append("")
    if unresolved:
        L.append("## Unresolved tasks (excluded from totals)")
        L.append("| Task | Reason |")
        L.append("|---|---|")
        for t in unresolved:
            L.append(f"| {t.task_id} {t.name} | {t.unresolved_reason} — [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Estimation lead] |")
        L.append("")
    L.append(f"Modeled tasks: {len(tasks)}; unresolved: {len(unresolved)}.")
    return "\n".join(L)


def load_previous(path: Path) -> dict:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get("total"), dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name} is not an estimate.json from this script (no 'total')")
    tot = {int(k): float(v) for k, v in data["total"].items()}
    phases = {ph: {int(k): float(v) for k, v in vals.items()} for ph, vals in (data.get("phases") or {}).items()}
    cost = data.get("cost") or None
    return {"total": tot, "phases": phases, "cost": cost}


def change_lines(prev: dict, sim: dict, staff: dict, cost) -> list[str]:
    def row(label, old, new):
        if old is None:
            return f"| {label} | — | {new:,.0f} | new |"
        if new is None:
            return f"| {label} | {old:,.0f} | — | removed |"
        d = new - old
        return f"| {label} | {old:,.0f} | {new:,.0f} | {'+' if d >= 0 else '−'}{abs(d):,.0f} |"
    L = ["## Change vs previous estimate", "| Item | Previous | Now | Change |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for q in (50, 80, 90):
        L.append(row(f"Total P{q} (pd)", prev["total"].get(q), sim["total"][q]))
    for ph in list(staff["phases"]) + [ph for ph in prev["phases"] if ph not in staff["phases"]]:
        old = prev["phases"].get(ph, {}).get(80)
        new = sim["phases"].get(ph, {}).get(80) if ph in staff["phases"] else None
        L.append(row(f"{ph} P80 (pd)", old, new))
    pc = prev.get("cost")
    if cost is not None and pc and pc.get("currency") == cost.get("currency") and pc.get("price_p80") is not None:
        L.append(row(f"Price @P80 ({cost['currency']})", float(pc["price_p80"]), cost["price_p80"]))
    else:
        L.append(f"| Price @P80 | not compared | | {TBD_EST} (both runs need a rate card in the same currency) |")
    L.append("")
    return L


def render_memo(sim, staff, cost, mix, unresolved, change: list[str] | None, client: str = "") -> str:
    """Estimate memo (no model step): every figure exactly as render_md prints it."""
    tot = sim["total"]
    cont = tot[80] - tot[50]
    cur = (cost or {}).get("currency") or ""
    jud = mix.get("JUD", 0.0)
    L = [f"# Estimate Memo — {client or TBD_EST} — draft", "",
         "> Script draft — the model step was not run (draft only): figures are copied from `estimate.md`; "
         "judgements are owned markers.", "",
         "## Bottom line", "| Item | Value | Basis |", "|---|---|---|",
         f"| Effort quoted | {tot[80]:,.0f} person-days at P80 (P50 {tot[50]:,.0f}, P90 {tot[90]:,.0f}) | "
         f"`scripts/estimate.py`, {sim['iterations']:,} iterations |",
         f"| Confidence level used | {TBD_EST} | commercial model not supplied |",
         f"| Duration | {TBD_EST} | the model computes effort only |",
         f"| Price | " + (f"{cost['price_p80']:,.0f} {cur} at P80" if cost is not None else f"pending rate card — {TBD_EST}")
         + " | supplied rate card |",
         f"| Contingency | P80 − P50 = {cont:,.0f} person-days ({cont / tot[50] * 100 if tot[50] else 0:.0f}%) | shown as a line |",
         "| Basis mix | " + " · ".join(f"{k} {v * 100:.0f}%" for k, v in sorted(mix.items())) + " | "
         + ("flag: judgment above 30%" if jud > 0.30 else "within the 30% judgment limit") + " |", "",
         "## Basis of estimate", "| Phase | P50 (pd) | P80 (pd) | P90 (pd) |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for ph in staff["phases"]:
        s_ = sim["phases"].get(ph, {50: 0, 80: 0, 90: 0})
        L.append(f"| {ph} | {s_[50]:,.0f} | {s_[80]:,.0f} | {s_[90]:,.0f} |")
    L += [f"| **Total** | {tot[50]:,.0f} | {tot[80]:,.0f} | {tot[90]:,.0f} |", ""]
    if change:
        L += change
    L += ["## Assumptions", "| ID | Assumption | Source |", "|---|---|---|",
          "| A-01 | Driver counts and unit efforts are as in the WBS | WBS basis and notes columns |",
          f"| A-02 | Client SME availability | {TBD_EST} |",
          f"| A-03 | Environments ready before the build phase | {TBD_EST} |",
          "| A-04 | Rates as on the supplied rate card | " + ("rate card valid_until column" if cost is not None else TBD_EST) + " |", "",
          "## Risks to the estimate and de-risking", "| Risk | Effect on estimate | De-risk action | Owner |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in sim["variance"][:3]:
        L.append(f"| {r['task_id']} {r['task']} | spread {r['spread']:,.0f} pd (P10 {r['p10']:,.0f} → P90 {r['p90']:,.0f}) | "
                 f"{TBD_EST} | {TBD_EST} |")
    if jud > 0.30:
        L.append(f"| Expert judgment covers {jud * 100:.0f}% of effort | low confidence in the totals | "
                 f"assessment phase before fixed pricing | {TBD_EST} |")
    if unresolved:
        L.append(f"| Unresolved WBS rows excluded from totals | totals are understated | baseline the rows | {TBD_EST} |")
    L += ["", "## Exclusions", f"{TBD_EST}", ""]
    return "\n".join(L)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("wbs", help="WBS CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--rates", help="Rate card CSV (optional)")
    ap.add_argument("--iterations", type=int, default=10000)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="Write Markdown report here (default stdout)")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Print JSON summary instead of Markdown")
    ap.add_argument("--currency", default="", help="Reporting currency when the rate card mixes currencies")
    ap.add_argument("--fx", action="append", default=[], metavar="CUR=RATE",
                    help="Sourced FX rate into the reporting currency (1 CUR = RATE); repeatable")
    ap.add_argument("--as-of", default="", help="Date (YYYY-MM-DD) for rate validity checks; default today")
    ap.add_argument("--previous", default="", help="estimate.json of the earlier run, for the change section")
    ap.add_argument("--memo", default="", help="estimate memo path (written with --draft-only)")
    ap.add_argument("--draft-only", action="store_true", help="no model step: write --memo from this run")
    ap.add_argument("--client", default="", help="client name for the memo title")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    wbs_path = Path(args.wbs)
    if not wbs_path.is_file():
        print(f"error: WBS not found: {wbs_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        tasks, unresolved = load_wbs(wbs_path)
    except UnicodeDecodeError:  # subclass of ValueError: must come first
        print(f"error: {wbs_path} is not a UTF-8 CSV file (save it as 'CSV UTF-8')", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    except (ValueError, csv.Error) as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not tasks:
        print("error: no modelable tasks (all rows unresolved or empty)", file=sys.stderr)
        for t in unresolved:
            print(f"  - {t.task_id}: {t.unresolved_reason}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if args.iterations < 1000:
        print("warning: fewer than 1000 iterations gives unstable percentiles", file=sys.stderr)

    sim = simulate(tasks, args.iterations, args.seed)
    staff = staffing(tasks)
    mix = basis_mix(tasks)
    cost = None
    if args.rates:
        rp = Path(args.rates)
        if not rp.is_file():
            print(f"error: rate card not found: {rp}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        try:
            as_of = date.fromisoformat(args.as_of) if args.as_of else None
            fx = parse_fx(args.fx)
            cost = cost_rollup(tasks, load_rates(rp, as_of), sim, fx, args.currency)
        except UnicodeDecodeError:  # subclass of ValueError: must come first
            print(f"error: {rp} is not a UTF-8 CSV file (save it as 'CSV UTF-8')", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        except (ValueError, csv.Error) as e:
            print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        for v in cost["rate_validity_issues"]:
            print(f"warning: rate validity — {v}", file=sys.stderr)
    preds = predecessor_issues(tasks, unresolved)
    for msg in preds:
        print(f"warning: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    change = None
    if args.previous:
        pp = Path(args.previous)
        if not pp.is_file():
            print(f"error: previous estimate not found: {pp}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        try:
            change = change_lines(load_previous(pp), sim, staffing(tasks), cost)
        except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as e:
            print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"total": sim["total"], "phases": sim["phases"], "basis_mix": mix,
                          "unresolved": [t.task_id for t in unresolved],
                          "duration": TBD_EST, "dependency_issues": preds,
                          "cost": cost}, indent=2, default=float))
        return 0
    md = render_md(tasks, unresolved, sim, staff, cost, mix, preds)
    if change:
        md = md.replace("## Duration", "\n".join(change) + "\n## Duration", 1)
    if args.draft_only and args.memo:
        Path(args.memo).write_text(render_memo(sim, staff, cost, mix, unresolved, change, args.client), encoding="utf-8")
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(md, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {args.out}")
    else:
        print(md)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Estimation Method

## 1. WBS rules
| Rule | Practice |
|---|---|
| Hierarchy | Phase → work package → task. Three levels; a fourth only for programs > 5,000 person-days |
| Task size | 2–15 person-days. Larger tasks hide uncertainty; smaller tasks create false precision |
| Drivers | Prefer parametric tasks: `count × unit effort`. The count is an assumption; the unit effort is calibrated from actuals or the complexity scoring in `integration-migration-assessor` |
| Completeness | Mandatory packages: project management (8–15% of delivery effort), QA/test (20–35% for integration), environments and DevOps, data/test-data preparation, cutover and rehearsal, hypercare, knowledge transfer and documentation, governance and reporting. Add them explicitly even if "included" in rates elsewhere |
| Dependencies | Record predecessor task IDs; the critical path drives duration, not total effort |
| Exclusions | List what the WBS does not cover (licenses, client effort, third-party fees) |

## 2. Three-point calibration
| Point | Definition | Calibration guidance |
|---|---|---|
| Optimistic (O) | Everything goes right; experienced team; no rework | Rarely below 0.7× most likely |
| Most likely (M) | Normal conditions for this client; typical rework | Anchor on actuals when available |
| Pessimistic (P) | Known risks materialize (unclear requirements, access delays, defect-heavy legacy); not a disaster scenario | 1.5× M for well-understood work; 2–3× M for legacy migration, data-heavy, or first-of-a-kind tasks |

Basis codes: `ANA` analogy to a prior actual (cite the reference ID), `PAR` parametric (count × unit, cite the unit source), `JUD` expert judgment. Report the share of total M-effort by basis. If `JUD` > 30%, flag the estimate as low-confidence and recommend an assessment phase before fixed pricing.

Unit-effort anchors must come from the user's prior actuals or the assessor's complexity bands. Do not supply "industry" unit efforts; if none exist, mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and run the model on judgment with the flag raised.

## 3. PERT and Monte Carlo
PERT mean per task: `(O + 4M + P) / 6`; standard deviation: `(P − O) / 6`.
Monte Carlo: sample each task from a Beta-PERT distribution (shape from O, M, P), sum per phase and total, repeat N ≥ 10,000 times. Report:
| Statistic | Use |
|---|---|
| P50 | Expected effort; T&M estimate |
| P80 | Fixed-price quote floor; contingency = P80 − P50 |
| P90 | Fixed-price for high-uncertainty migrations; board-level commitment |
| Phase P50/P80 | Milestone pricing |
| Variance contributors | Top tasks by variance; targets for de-risking (assessment, spike, prototype) |

Correlation: tasks sharing a driver (same count) move together. The script applies a shared multiplier per `driver_group` so that correlated uncertainty is not understated. Independent sampling of correlated tasks under-states P80.

## 4. Confidence selection
| Commercial model | Quote | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed price, inventory known | P80 | Contingency covers normal variance |
| Fixed price, inventory unconfirmed | P90, or assessment first | Count uncertainty dominates |
| T&M | P50 estimate, P80 as NTE | Client holds risk; NTE protects budget |
| Assessment (fixed) | P80, short duration | Scope is bounded by time |
| Managed service transition | P80 | Transition risk is supplier's |

## 5. Duration
Duration ≠ effort ÷ team size. Compute from the critical path with realistic allocation (a 100%-allocated person yields ~80% productive days). Apply client-side constraints: freeze windows, SME availability, approval latency (assume 5 business days per gate unless the client states otherwise). Ramp-up: first two weeks of any new team member at 50%.

## 6. Sensitivity and de-risking
From the variance contributors, propose de-risking actions:
| Variance source | De-risk by |
|---|---|
| Unconfirmed counts | Inventory in an assessment phase; price per unit with a count band |
| Legacy complexity unknown | Spike on the 3 most complex items; re-score |
| Client dependency latency | Dependency register with dates; day-for-day clause in SOW |
| New technology for the team | Prototype in phase 0; training line in WBS |
| Data quality | Profiling task before build; data remediation as client responsibility or separate package |

## 7. Estimate memo structure
1. Bottom line: P80 effort (person-days), duration (weeks), team shape, price (if rate card) or "price pending rate card", confidence level used and why.
2. Basis of estimate: WBS summary table by phase (P50/P80), basis mix (ANA/PAR/JUD %).
3. Assumptions: counts, unit efforts, allocations, rates validity — each with source or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
4. Exclusions.
5. Risks to the estimate and de-risking plan.
6. Sensitivity: top 5 variance contributors.
7. Staffing table (from `staffing-and-rates.md`).
8. Price-to-win comparison and levers (if a target was given).

# Staffing and Rates

## 1. Pyramid design
| Layer | Roles | Typical share of effort (delivery engagements) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead | Engagement manager, lead architect | 10–15% | Part-time EM below ~2,000 person-days |
| Senior | Technical leads, senior developers, test lead, business analyst | 25–35% | One tech lead per 4–6 developers |
| Core | Developers, integration engineers, test engineers | 45–60% | Largest layer; offshore-heavy where policy allows |
| Support | DevOps, data, PMO, documentation | 5–10% | Often shared across engagements |

Shares are design targets, not a basis for estimating effort. Effort comes from the WBS; the pyramid allocates it.

Leverage ratio = (senior + core + support effort) ÷ lead effort. Record it; compare with the user's own norms if provided. Do not assert a "standard" ratio.

## 2. Onshore / offshore mix
| Factor | Pushes onshore | Pushes offshore |
|---|---|---|
| Client-facing work (workshops, design, stakeholder management) | ↑ | |
| Data residency / security restrictions | ↑ | |
| Overlap requirement with client time zone | ↑ | partial (shifted hours) |
| Well-specified build and test work | | ↑ |
| Run / support with follow-the-sun | | ↑ |
| Price-to-win pressure | | ↑ |
| First engagement with client (trust) | ↑ initially | ↑ after wave 1 |

Rules:
- State the mix by phase, not one number. Design phases run onshore-heavy; build and test offshore-heavy; cutover mixed.
- Each offshore team needs a named onshore counterpart for escalation.
- Overlap hours per day with the client are an assumption row.
- The mix is a lever against price-to-win; moving it changes risk, which goes in the risk register.

## 3. Allocation rules
| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Max allocation | 100% (reality: ~80% productive) |
| Min useful allocation | 20% (below that, context-switching dominates) |
| EM allocation | 25–50% for mid-size; 100% above ~3,000 person-days |
| Architect allocation | High in design, tapering to 20–30% in build, up in cutover |
| Test lead | From design phase, not from test phase |
| Ramp | New joiners at 50% for two weeks |

## 4. Rate-card contract
The skill never invents rates. The rate card is supplied as CSV with this layout (see `assets/rate-card.example.csv`):

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `role` | Must match `role` values used in the WBS |
| `grade` | Optional; for pyramid reporting |
| `location` | `onshore` / `offshore` / `nearshore` / a named country |
| `cost_rate` | Internal daily cost (used for margin) |
| `bill_rate` | Daily rate charged (used for price) |
| `currency` | ISO code |
| `valid_until` | Date; the estimate notes rate validity |

Rates match on role AND location. A role priced at several locations needs the optional WBS `location` column (one task row per role and location); duplicate (role, location) rows and ambiguous matches stop the script (exit 2). Costs are never summed across currencies: a mixed-currency card needs `--currency <ISO>` and a sourced `--fx CUR=rate` per other currency, else exit 2 with FX `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Finance lead]`. Expired or unreadable `valid_until` dates are flagged in the output. If `cost_rate` is absent, margin cannot be computed and the memo says so. If a WBS role has no rate-card match, the script lists it and excludes it from cost; fix the mapping rather than guessing.

## 5. Margin sanity
| Check | Rule |
|---|---|
| Gross margin | (price − cost) ÷ price, computed at P80 effort and at P50 effort; show both |
| Contingency placement | Contingency (P80 − P50) is a line, not a rate uplift |
| Price-to-win gap | If price > PTW by >15%, list levers: scope phasing, mix shift, automation assets, client-side responsibilities, duration change. Do not cut the estimate to fit |
| Discount | Any discount is applied to price and shown as a line; margin recalculated |
| Expenses | Travel estimated separately from stated trip counts; never folded into rates |

## 6. Staffing table layout
| Role | Location | Phase 1 (%) | Phase 2 (%) | Phase 3 (%) | … | Total person-days | Named? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Followed by a phase × month heat table (FTE per month) to check feasibility against the team-size cap and hiring lead times.

# exec-deck-redline

## In a conversation: redline now
- **The request carries the audience, the decision and the slot** — including when the deck and source documents are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: produce the redline **in this reply**. Never reply with only a request for the file. In this order:
  1. **Storyline as found** in ≤6 bullets, preserved; no new narrative (where slide text is not in the conversation, mark each bullet `[confirm against slide n]` rather than inventing content).
  2. **Decision test** — what the audience must believe after slide 1 and approve by the last slide.
  3. **Rubric score before and after** (`assets/redline-rubric.md`).
  4. **Redline table** — every slide gets a verdict `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]`; each `[SHARPEN]` row has the full rewritten title (an assertion, ≤12 words) and body.
  5. **Numbers check** against the named sources (e.g. the estimate memo, the discovery synthesis); every unsourced number, role or date becomes `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
  6. **Time fit** — about one body slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck (30 minutes → ~15 body slides); overflow to the appendix and a **parked list** with destinations.
  7. **Executive summary slide** — the decision, three reasons (numbers or markers), next steps with owners and dates.
  8. **Speaker notes** ≤60 words per kept or sharpened slide, aligned to slide content · **Open items** with owners.
- **No decision, audience or slot** ("tidy up these slides"): ask once, in one list, for the audience, the decision the deck must obtain and the time slot. Do not begin slide rewrites without the decision test. Offer a **density-only pass** (titles, one point per slide, tables for lists) as the fallback if the user has no decision in mind, labelled "density-only — not a decision redline".
- **Asked to put an invented savings figure, go-live date or assumed sponsor on a slide**: say in one line that the redline marks unknowns rather than inventing figures, roles or dates, because the CFO will hold the team to them. Keep the slide (e.g. the business-case slide stays in the storyline as `[SHARPEN]`/`[TBD]`, not cut) and show: savings `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` with a note naming the source that would confirm it (the value case); go-live `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` tied to the estimate's critical path, not a chosen quarter; sponsor `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, no assumed name or role. Never print the requested figure, quarter or person anywhere.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — your deck is read slide by slide into a ledger with every unsourced figure listed; the model step writes the redline (storyline kept, [KEEP]/[SHARPEN]/[CUT]/[ADD]/[TBD]), or with `draft_only` a mechanical redline flags unsourced figures, label titles and dense slides; the verdicts are applied back to the ledger.
- Only for existing: a redline always starts from a deck that already exists; to build a deck from nothing, start with proposal-writer or value-case-builder.

## When to use
- "Redline this steering-committee deck."
- "Sharpen these slides for the CIO — keep the story."
- "Review the board pack before Friday."
- NOT for: building a new deck (produce content with the domain skill, then this skill for the pass), documents (`proposal-writer`, `sow-drafter`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The deck (PPTX, PDF, or slide text export) | yes | file |
| Audience and the decision the deck must obtain | yes | user |
| Time slot (minutes) | yes | user |
| Source documents behind the numbers (if any) | no | files |
| Constraints: template, slide limit, mandated sections | no | user |

If the audience or the decision is missing, ask once; a deck without a decision cannot be sharpened, only tidied. Missing source documents or slot constraints do not stop the redline: unsourced numbers are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` (redline convention) and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. The user's standing instruction applies: stay close to the original storyline and sharpen it; do not replace the narrative; no invented dollar figures, roles, or dates.

1. **Read the whole deck before touching any slide.** Write the storyline as it stands in ≤6 bullets (situation → complication → decision asked → options → recommendation → next steps, or whatever the author used). If the storyline is coherent, it stays. If it has a gap (e.g., no decision slide), that is an `[ADD]`, not a rewrite.
2. **Set the decision test.** From the audience and decision input: what must the reader believe after slide 1, and what must they approve by the last slide? Every slide is judged against this.
3. **Score the deck** with `assets/redline-rubric.md` (storyline, titles, evidence, so-what, density, numbers discipline, time fit). Record the score before and after; the after score is the self-check.
4. **Redline slide by slide** per `references/redline-method.md`:
   - `[KEEP]` unchanged.
   - `[SHARPEN]` rewrite the title as an assertion; cut to the one point; convert prose to a table or a single chart spec; state the "so what" in the first line of the body. Provide the rewritten text in full.
   - `[CUT]` with reason (duplicates, no decision relevance, appendix material) and where the content moves.
   - `[ADD]` only for storyline gaps; state source for any content added.
   - `[TBD]` for every number, role, date without a source in the provided materials: `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
5. **Decision point — time fit.** Count body slides vs time slot using the rule in the method (§4): roughly one slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck, less for discussion. Over the limit → move to appendix, do not shrink fonts.
6. **Write speaker notes** for every kept/sharpened body slide: ≤60 words, the spoken point, the number to say, the transition. Notes never contain content absent from the slide or the sources.
7. **Produce the executive summary slide** if missing (one slide: decision asked, three reasons with numbers or `[TBD]`, next steps with owners and dates). Place it as slide 2 (after title) or 1 if there is no title slide.
8. **Deliver**: redline table, rewritten slide text in order, speaker notes, parked list (content cut with destination), and the before/after rubric score. If the user supplied a PPTX and asks for the file edited, apply changes with the pptx tooling available in the session; otherwise deliver text ready to paste.
9. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `deck-redline-<client-or-topic>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections: Storyline as found (≤6 bullets) · Decision test · Rubric score before/after · Redline table (slide #, original title, verdict, reason, new title, body change summary) · Rewritten slides (full text, in order) · Speaker notes · Parked content · Open items (`[TBD]` list with owners)

## Self-check
- [ ] Storyline preserved; changes are sharpening, not replacement
- [ ] Every title is an assertion with a number or consequence
- [ ] Every number, role, date has a source or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] No slide carries more than one point; 3+ items are tables
- [ ] Slide count fits the time slot; overflow in appendix
- [ ] Speaker notes ≤60 words, aligned to slide content
- [ ] Executive summary slide present with decision, reasons, next steps
- [ ] No banned words; no author or other-client references

## References
- `references/redline-method.md` — storyline preservation, title assertions, slide patterns, density rules, time fit, speaker-note rules
- `assets/redline-rubric.md` — scoring rubric and redline table layout
- `assets/storyline-checklist.md` — storyline integrity checklist by deck type

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/exec-deck-redline --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/exec-deck-redline`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

    python3 -I scripts/redline.py --apply redline.md --ledger ledger.csv

Inputs: a .pptx (needs python-pptx: `pip install python-pptx`; see requirements-optional.txt) or a
.md/.txt export with `--- slide N ---` separators (first non-empty line of each block = title).
ledger.csv: slide, title, text, verdict, reason, numbers_found   (verdict/reason blank until applied)
unsourced-numbers.csv: slide, number, context — every number (>= 3 significant digits or carrying
$ / %) on a line that names no source (`source`, `per <doc>`, `[Sn]`, `(… 20xx)` count as sources).
--apply reads the redline table in redline.md (| Slide # | Original title | Verdict | Reason | …)
and fills verdict/reason for the matching slides; rows without a bracketed verdict are ignored.
--draft-only --redline-out redline.md (build mode): no model step — writes a mechanical redline on the
template's sections from the ledger alone: one row per slide, [TBD] + [SHARPEN] for slides with
unsourced figures (each figure becomes an owned to-be-baselined marker in the rewritten slide),
[SHARPEN] for a label title (<= 4 words, no figure, no verb of decision) or a body over 60 words,
[KEEP] otherwise; a missing decision ask in slides 1-2 is listed under "Slides to add". Labelled as a
draft; storyline untouched; the --apply step then fills the ledger from it.
Nothing is invented; the ledger is the deck's own text. Exit 1 on a missing file, an unsupported
extension, a text export without separators, or a pptx without python-pptx. Stdlib only, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])([$€£]?)(-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)(%?)(?![\w])")
SOURCE_RE = re.compile(r"(?i:\bsources?\b)|\bper\s+[A-Z(]|\[S\d+\]|\(\s*[^()]*20\d\d\s*\)|(?i:\bsrc:)")
SEP_RE = re.compile(r"^---\s*slide\s+(\d+)\s*---\s*$", re.I)
DATE_RE = re.compile(r"\b\d{4}-\d{2}(-\d{2})?\b")
FOOTNOTE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(source|sources)\s*[:—-]", re.I)
VERDICT_RE = re.compile(r"\[(KEEP|SHARPEN|CUT|ADD|TBD)\]")
LEDGER_COLS = ["slide", "title", "text", "verdict", "reason", "numbers_found"]


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def sig_digits(num: str) -> int:
    return len(num.replace(",", "").replace("-", "").replace(".", "").lstrip("0"))


def numbers_in(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Numbers worth tracing (>= 3 significant digits or $ / %); ISO dates are not numbers."""
    out = []
    for m in NUMBER_RE.finditer(DATE_RE.sub(" ", text)):
        sym, num, pct = m.groups()
        if sym or pct or sig_digits(num) >= 3:
            out.append(f"{sym}{num}{pct}")
    return out


def slides_from_text(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
    slides, cur, buf = [], None, []
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        m = SEP_RE.match(ln.strip())
        if m:
            if cur is not None:
                slides.append((cur, buf))
            cur, buf = int(m.group(1)), []
        elif cur is not None:
            buf.append(ln.rstrip())
    if cur is not None:
        slides.append((cur, buf))
    if not slides:
        die("text export has no '--- slide N ---' separators")
    out = []
    for n, lines in slides:
        body = [ln for ln in lines if ln.strip()]
        title = body[0].lstrip("# ").strip() if body else ""
        out.append((n, title, "\n".join(body)))
    return out


def slides_from_pptx(path: Path) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore
    except ImportError:
        die("reading .pptx needs python-pptx: pip install python-pptx  (or export the deck to "
            "deck.md with '--- slide N ---' separators)")
    prs = Presentation(str(path))
    out = []
    for n, slide in enumerate(prs.slides, 1):
        lines, title = [], ""
        try:
            if slide.shapes.title is not None and slide.shapes.title.has_text_frame:
                title = slide.shapes.title.text_frame.text.strip()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            title = ""
        for shape in slide.shapes:
            if getattr(shape, "has_text_frame", False) and shape.has_text_frame:
                for para in shape.text_frame.paragraphs:
                    t = "".join(r.text for r in para.runs).strip()
                    if t:
                        lines.append(t)
            if getattr(shape, "has_table", False) and shape.has_table:
                for row in shape.table.rows:
                    cells = [c.text.strip() for c in row.cells]
                    if any(cells):
                        lines.append(" | ".join(cells))
        if getattr(slide, "has_notes_slide", False) and slide.has_notes_slide:
            notes = slide.notes_slide.notes_text_frame.text.strip() if slide.notes_slide.notes_text_frame else ""
            if notes:
                lines.append(f"[notes] {notes}")
        if not title and lines:
            title = lines[0]
        out.append((n, title, "\n".join(lines)))
    if not out:
        die("pptx has no slides")
    return out


def build(deck: Path, ledger: Path, unsourced: Path, redline_out: Path | None = None) -> None:
    if not deck.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {deck}")
    ext = deck.suffix.lower()
    if ext == ".pptx":
        slides = slides_from_pptx(deck)
    elif ext in (".md", ".txt"):
        slides = slides_from_text(deck.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
    else:
        die(f"unsupported deck format {ext!r}: use .pptx, .md or .txt")
    rows, uns = [], []
    for n, title, text in slides:
        nums = []
        footnote = any(FOOTNOTE_RE.match(ln) for ln in text.splitlines())
        for ln in text.splitlines():
            found = numbers_in(ln)
            nums += found
            if found and not SOURCE_RE.search(ln) and not footnote:
                uns += [{"slide": n, "number": x, "context": ln.strip()[:160]} for x in found]
        rows.append({"slide": n, "title": title, "text": text, "verdict": "", "reason": "",
                     "numbers_found": "; ".join(nums)})
    ledger.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with ledger.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=LEDGER_COLS); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
    with unsourced.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["slide", "number", "context"]); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(uns)
    if redline_out is not None:
        redline_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        redline_out.write_text(draft_redline(rows, uns, deck.name), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"ledger: {len(rows)} slides, {sum(len(r['numbers_found'].split('; ')) for r in rows if r['numbers_found'])} "
          f"numbers, {len(uns)} unsourced -> {ledger}, {unsourced}")


DECK_TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Deck owner]"
DECISION_RE = re.compile(r"\b(decision|approve|approval|decide|ask)\b", re.I)


def draft_redline(rows: list[dict], uns: list[dict], deck_name: str) -> str:
    """Mechanical redline (no model step): checks from the rubric that the ledger alone can decide."""
    by_slide: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}
    for u in uns:
        by_slide.setdefault(int(u["slide"]), []).append(u)
    table, rewrites = [], []
    for r in rows:
        n, title, text = int(r["slide"]), r["title"], r["text"]
        body = text.splitlines()[1:] if text.splitlines() and text.splitlines()[0].lstrip("# ").strip() == title else text.splitlines()
        words = len(re.findall(r"\w+", " ".join(body)))
        verdicts, reasons = [], []
        figs = by_slide.get(n, [])
        if figs:
            verdicts += ["SHARPEN", "TBD"]
            reasons.append(f"{len(figs)} figure(s) without a source")
        if len(title.split()) <= 4 and not numbers_in(title) and not DECISION_RE.search(title):
            verdicts.append("SHARPEN")
            reasons.append("title is a label, not an assertion")
        if words > 60:
            verdicts.append("SHARPEN")
            reasons.append(f"body has {words} words (limit 60)")
        verdicts = list(dict.fromkeys(verdicts)) or ["KEEP"]
        tbd_items = "; ".join(f"{u['number']} → {DECK_TBD}" for u in figs) or "—"
        table.append(f"| {n} | {title.replace('|', '/')} | {' + '.join(f'[{v}]' for v in verdicts)} | "
                     f"{'; '.join(reasons) or 'passes the mechanical checks'} | {DECK_TBD if 'SHARPEN' in verdicts else '—'} | "
                     f"{'mark unsourced figures' if figs else '—'} | {tbd_items} | — |")
        if verdicts != ["KEEP"]:
            lines = []
            for ln in body:
                hits = [u["number"] for u in figs if u["context"] and ln.strip()[:160] == u["context"]]
                pos, out_ln = 0, ""
                for num in hits:                          # replace each figure once, left to right
                    i = ln.find(num, pos)
                    if i < 0:
                        continue
                    out_ln += ln[pos:i] + DECK_TBD
                    pos = i + len(num)
                lines.append(out_ln + ln[pos:])
            rewrites += [f"Slide {n} — {DECK_TBD if 'title is a label, not an assertion' in reasons else title}",
                         f"So what: {DECK_TBD}", "Body:"] + lines + \
                        [f"Source: {DECK_TBD if figs else 'as on the slide'}", ""]
    ask = any(DECISION_RE.search(r["text"]) for r in rows[:2])
    out = [f"# Deck Redline — {deck_name} — draft", "",
           "> Script draft — the model step was not run (draft only): mechanical checks from the rubric "
           "(sources, title form, density); judgement on storyline and so-what is an owned marker.", "",
           "## Bottom line", f"{DECK_TBD} — the decision the deck asks for, and whether the deck as found earns it.", "",
           "## Redline table",
           "| Slide # | Original title | Verdict | Reason | New title (assertion) | Body change (summary) | Source / `[TBD]` items | Moves to |",
           "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"] + table + ["", "## Rewritten slides", "", "```"] + \
          (rewrites or ["No slide needs a mechanical rewrite."]) + ["```", "", "## Unsourced numbers to baseline",
                                                                  "| Slide | Number | Context | Owner |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    out += [f"| {u['slide']} | {u['number']} | {u['context'].replace('|', '/')} | {DECK_TBD} |" for u in uns] or \
        ["| — | none | every figure names a source | — |"]
    out += ["", "## Slides to add", "| Beat missing (storyline checklist) | Proposed slide | Why |", "|---|---|---|"]
    out.append("| Decision ask | none — slides 1–2 state it | — |" if ask else
               f"| Decision ask | Slide 1: the decision as an assertion, with owner and date | {DECK_TBD} |")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def apply(redline: Path, ledger: Path) -> None:
    if not redline.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {redline}")
    if not ledger.is_file():
        die(f"ledger not found: {ledger}")
    verdicts = {}
    for ln in redline.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        if not ln.startswith("|"):
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        if len(cells) < 3 or not re.fullmatch(r"\d+", cells[0]):
            continue
        vs = VERDICT_RE.findall(ln)
        if not vs:
            continue
        verdict = " + ".join(f"[{v}]" for v in dict.fromkeys(vs))
        reason = cells[3] if len(cells) > 3 else ""
        verdicts[int(cells[0])] = (verdict, reason)
    with ledger.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    n = 0
    for r in rows:
        v = verdicts.get(int(r["slide"])) if r.get("slide", "").isdigit() else None
        if v:
            r["verdict"], r["reason"] = v
            n += 1
    with ledger.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=LEDGER_COLS); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
    missing = [r["slide"] for r in rows if not r["verdict"]]
    print(f"applied {n} verdicts to {ledger}; {len(missing)} slides without verdict"
          + (f": {missing[:10]}" if missing else ""))


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Deck -> slide ledger + unsourced numbers; --apply verdicts from redline.md")
    ap.add_argument("deck", nargs="?", help="deck.pptx, deck.md or deck.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--ledger", required=True, help="ledger.csv (written, or updated with --apply)")
    ap.add_argument("--unsourced", default="", help="unsourced-numbers.csv (build mode)")
    ap.add_argument("--apply", metavar="REDLINE_MD", help="fill verdict/reason in the ledger from redline.md")
    ap.add_argument("--redline-out", default="", help="build mode: draft redline path (written with --draft-only)")
    ap.add_argument("--draft-only", action="store_true", help="no model step: write --redline-out from the ledger")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.apply:
        apply(Path(a.apply), Path(a.ledger))
        return 0
    if not a.deck or not a.unsourced:
        die("build mode needs a deck and --unsourced")
    build(Path(a.deck), Path(a.ledger), Path(a.unsourced),
          Path(a.redline_out) if a.draft_only and a.redline_out else None)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Redline Method

## 1. Preserve the storyline
The author chose a narrative for reasons the reviewer may not see (politics, prior commitments, what the sponsor already said). The redline sharpens that narrative. It does not substitute the reviewer's preferred one.

| Allowed | Not allowed |
|---|---|
| Reorder two adjacent slides to fix a logic gap | Restructure the deck around a new framework |
| Add a missing executive-summary or decision slide | Add a new recommendation the author did not make |
| Merge two slides making the same point | Replace the author's options with different options |
| Move detail to appendix | Delete the author's evidence because "it is weak" (mark `[TBD]` for sourcing instead) |
| Rewrite titles and body for clarity | Change the ask (budget, decision) |

If the reviewer believes the storyline is wrong, that is a separate note to the author ("storyline risk"), not a redline action.

## 2. Title assertions
A title states the slide's conclusion. The body proves it. A reader who reads only titles gets the whole argument.

| Label title (replace) | Assertion title (use) |
|---|---|
| "Current state" | "Three platforms carry 80% of integration incidents" (or `[TBD]` for the figure) |
| "Options" | "Option B reaches first value in 6 months at the lowest delivery risk" |
| "Risks" | "Two risks need sponsor decisions this month" |
| "Timeline" | "Go-live before peak freeze requires a decision by <date>" |
| "Next steps" | "Three decisions today unlock wave 0 on <date>" |

Rules: ≤ 12 words; one claim; a number or a consequence; no question marks; no "overview of".

## 3. Slide patterns
| Pattern | Use when | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| Executive summary | Always, slide 1–2 | Decision asked · three reasons (number each) · next steps (owner, date) |
| Situation-complication | Opening | Left: facts with sources; right: what changed and why it matters now |
| Options comparison | Decision slides | Table: options × criteria, scored; recommendation highlighted |
| Evidence | Proving a claim | One chart or one table; title = the finding; source line |
| Plan | Timeline | Milestones with dates and dependencies; freeze windows shaded |
| Risk | Governance | Table: risk, likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner; top 5 only |
| Ask | Closing | Decisions needed, by whom, by when; what happens if delayed |

One point per slide. If a slide needs two titles, it is two slides or a table.

## 4. Density and time fit
| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Body slides for a decision deck | ≈ minutes ÷ 2 (30-minute slot → ≤ 15 body slides, typically 8–12) |
| Body slides for a discussion deck | ≈ minutes ÷ 4 |
| Words per slide body | ≤ 60 for exec audiences; tables count rows not words |
| Table rows | ≤ 7; more → appendix with a summary row on the body slide |
| Chart | One per slide; title is the finding; axis labels; source line |
| Appendix | Unlimited; referenced from body slides ("detail: A3") |

Overflow handling: move to appendix → merge duplicates → cut non-decision content. Never shrink fonts below the template minimum.

## 5. Numbers discipline
| Case | Action |
|---|---|
| Number with a source in provided materials | Keep; add source line on the slide or in notes |
| Number with no source | `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` in place of the number; note which source would confirm |
| Number that conflicts between slides | Flag both; `[TBD]` until reconciled; name the owner |
| Role or name not in materials | `[TBD — owner]`; never invent an owner |
| Date not in materials | `[TBD — owner]`; never pick a plausible date |
| Percentage without a base | Add the base or `[TBD]` |

The redline never "improves" a number. It either sources it or marks it.

## 6. Speaker notes
| Rule | Practice |
|---|---|
| Length | ≤ 60 words |
| Content | The spoken point in one sentence · the one number to say aloud · the transition to the next slide |
| Alignment | Nothing in the notes that is not on the slide or in the sources |
| Anticipation | Optional one line: "If asked about X, answer: …" (only with sourced answer) |

## 7. Redline output discipline
- Verdict for every slide, including title and appendix slides.
- `[SHARPEN]` always includes the full rewritten title and body; a reason alone is not a redline.
- Parked content lists where it went (appendix slide number or "dropped — reason").
- Before/after rubric scores are shown; the after score is the self-check evidence.
- Chat response stays under 50 words; the artifact carries the detail.
