# integration-migration-assessor

## In a conversation: assess now
- **The request carries the inventory** (or its contents): produce the readout **in this reply**. Report the share of unknown factors and whether the assessment is provisional; list retirement candidates with owners to confirm before effort is discussed; a band distribution table with outliers explained; a wave plan (wave 0 foundation, a representative wave 1, balanced middle waves, dependencies enforced, cutovers outside the client's freeze windows, entry/exit criteria); TCO lines that cite the client's contract for licence cost, with migration cost `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` until the effort estimate exists; handoffs to effort-estimator and solution-architecture-doc.
- **No inventory, only a count**: ask once for the inventory and offer the collection template (`assets/inventory-columns.md`) and the minimum viable column set for a provisional assessment. Never synthesize an inventory or a band distribution from a count.
- **Asked to use list prices, treat blanks as simple, or give a ballpark savings figure**: say in one line why not (blank factors scored simple are the main cause of overrun; vendor list prices from memory are not the client's contract). Score blanks as unknown (mid-band, flagged); show licence cost and savings as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the client contract as the source; state the TCO direction qualitatively at most; give next steps with owners.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — the inventory of your current estate is scored, banded and planned into waves, the TCO is built only from the rate inputs you supply, and the readout is written by the model step or, with `draft_only`, assembled from the two summaries with every figure copied verbatim.
- Only for existing: an assessment always scores an integration estate that already runs; there is nothing to assess from scratch.

## When to use
- "Assess <client>'s MuleSoft/Boomi/ESB/Informatica estate for migration to <target>."
- "Score this interface inventory and give me waves."
- "Build the TCO comparison for staying vs migrating."
- NOT for: drawing the target architecture (`solution-architecture-doc`), P50/P80 effort (`effort-estimator`), full business case with non-platform benefits (`value-case-builder`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Interface inventory CSV (one row per interface/API/flow; columns per `assets/inventory-columns.md`) | yes | client export / discovery / platform admin console export |
| Source and target platforms (or "target to be selected") | yes | user |
| Current platform cost facts: licence, infrastructure, support/run team, contract end | no — TCO is `[TO BE BASELINED]` without them | client / user |
| Constraints: freeze windows, contract end dates, dependent programs (ERP upgrade), compliance | no | discovery |
| Prior migration actuals (unit effort per band) if any | no | user |

If the inventory is missing, ask once; offer `assets/inventory-columns.md` as the collection template. Never synthesize an inventory.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Validate the inventory**: run `python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --validate`. It reports missing columns, blank factor cells, and duplicates. Blank factor cells score as "unknown" (mid-band with a flag), never as "simple". Report the unknown share; above 25% the assessment is provisional and says so.
2. **Score complexity** with `python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --out scored.csv --waves 4`. Factors and weights per `references/complexity-scoring.md` (pattern, transformation logic, protocol/connector availability on target, endpoints, data volume, error handling and orchestration, security, test coverage, documentation, business criticality). Review the band distribution (Simple / Medium / Complex / Very complex) against what discovery said; investigate outliers.
3. **Decision point — migration approach per band.** Apply `references/migration-factory-method.md` §2: Simple → automated/tool-assisted conversion with templated tests; Medium → factory with pattern templates; Complex → design-led with refactor; Very complex → candidates for redesign, retirement, or re-platform outside the factory. Retirement candidates (unused, duplicate, superseded) are identified first; they are the cheapest migration.
4. **Assign waves** (script output, then adjust): wave 0 foundation; wave 1 representative simples; middle waves balance complexity and resolve dependencies; final wave long-tail and decommission. Respect freeze windows and dependent programs from constraints. Each wave gets entry/exit criteria and a rollback approach from §4 of the method.
5. **Build the TCO/ROI layout** on `assets/tco-model-spec.md` (CSV layout spec) and `assets/tco-model.md` (markdown table layout): current run-rate (licence, infra, people, support, incidents) vs target run-rate, one-time migration cost (from `effort-estimator`, or `[TO BE BASELINED]`), timing of savings (only after decommission), 3–5-year view, payback, sensitivity on the two biggest drivers. Every figure sourced to a client document or marked. Licence savings are not realized until the source platform is decommissioned; model that date explicitly.
6. **Risk register for the migration**: dual-run cost, connector gaps on target, skills, endpoint changes during migration, data drift, cutover windows, vendor cooperation; each with likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner.
7. **Write the assessment readout** on `assets/assessment-readout-template.md`: bottom line (inventory size, band mix, approach, waves, TCO direction with confidence, decision asked), evidence, scoring results, wave plan, TCO layout, risks, next steps. Feed interface counts and bands to `effort-estimator` and the wave plan to `solution-architecture-doc`.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File |
|---|---|
| Scored inventory | `inventory-scored-<client>.csv` (script) |
| Wave plan | within readout; CSV wave column in scored inventory |
| TCO model layout | `tco-<client>.csv` per `assets/tco-model-spec.md` + markdown table in readout |
| Assessment readout | `migration-assessment-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Inventory validated; unknown-factor share reported; provisional flag if >25%
- [ ] Band distribution reviewed against discovery; outliers explained
- [ ] Retirement candidates identified before scoring effort
- [ ] Waves have entry/exit criteria, rollback, and respect constraints
- [ ] TCO: every figure sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; savings timed after decommission
- [ ] Sensitivity on the two largest drivers shown
- [ ] No vendor pricing quoted from memory; licence figures from client contracts or marked
- [ ] No other-client specifics; no author history

## References
- `references/complexity-scoring.md` — factors, weights, bands, unknown handling, calibration
- `references/migration-factory-method.md` — approach per band, factory operating model, wave rules, cutover and rollback, decommission
- `assets/inventory-columns.md` — inventory CSV column spec (collection template)
- `assets/tco-model-spec.md` — TCO/ROI CSV layout spec
- `assets/tco-model.md` — TCO markdown table layout
- `assets/assessment-readout-template.md` — readout template
- `scripts/score_inventory.py` — validate, score, band, assign waves

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/integration-migration-assessor --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/integration-migration-assessor`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assessment readout without a model step: the scoring and TCO summaries, assembled on the readout layout.

    python3 -I scripts/readout_draft.py --scoring scoring-summary.md --tco tco-summary.md \
        --client Acme --out readout.md

Used when the LLM readout step is skipped (draft only). Every figure is copied verbatim from the two
summaries this skill's scripts wrote (so `numbers_trace_to` holds by construction); nothing is
computed here. Sections (assets/assessment-readout-template.md): Bottom line (the summaries' own
headline lines), Scoring results (band table, unknown-factor and retirement lines), Wave plan (wave
table), TCO (the TCO summary, headings demoted), Risks and Next steps (owned to-be-baselined markers,
plus a risk line when interfaces carry unknown factors or payback is outside the horizon). Labelled
as a draft. Exit 1 when a summary is missing or lacks its tables. Stdlib only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Migration lead]"


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def tables(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Consecutive `|` lines, as blocks."""
    out, cur = [], []
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        if ln.startswith("|"):
            cur.append(ln)
        elif cur:
            out.append(cur)
            cur = []
    if cur:
        out.append(cur)
    return out


def line_starting(text: str, prefix: str) -> str:
    return next((ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip().startswith(prefix)), "")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="scoring + TCO summaries -> readout.md (no model step)")
    ap.add_argument("--scoring", required=True, help="scoring-summary.md (score_inventory.py --summary)")
    ap.add_argument("--tco", required=True, help="tco-summary.md (tco.py --summary)")
    ap.add_argument("--client", default="<Client>")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    sp, tp = Path(a.scoring), Path(a.tco)
    for p in (sp, tp):
        if not p.is_file():
            die(f"summary not found: {p}")
    scoring, tco = sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), tp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    blocks = tables(scoring)
    bands = next((b for b in blocks if b[0].startswith("| Band")), None)
    waves = next((b for b in blocks if b[0].startswith("| Wave")), None)
    if not bands or not waves:
        die(f"{sp.name} lacks the band and wave tables (expected score_inventory.py --summary output)")
    unknown = line_starting(scoring, "Interfaces with >=1 unknown factor")
    retire = line_starting(scoring, "Retirement candidates")
    payback = line_starting(tco, "Payback:")
    if not payback:
        die(f"{tp.name} lacks the 'Payback:' line (expected tco.py --summary output)")
    tco_body = [re.sub(r"^(#+) ", lambda m: "#" * (len(m.group(1)) + 1) + " ", ln)
                for ln in tco.splitlines() if not ln.startswith("# ")]
    risks = []
    m = re.search(r"unknown factor: (\d+)", unknown)
    if m and int(m.group(1)) > 0:
        risks.append(f"| {unknown} | scores and waves may move once the unknowns are baselined | {TBD} |")
    if "not within horizon" in payback:
        risks.append(f"| {payback} | the business case does not pay back inside the TCO horizon | {TBD} |")
    risks.append(f"| Delivery and cutover risks for the wave plan | {TBD} | {TBD} |")
    out = [f"# Migration Assessment — {a.client} — draft", "",
           "> Script draft — the model step was not run (draft only): figures are copied from the scoring and TCO "
           "summaries; recommendations are owned markers.", "",
           "## Bottom line", f"- {payback}", f"- {retire}" if retire else "", f"- {unknown}" if unknown else "",
           f"- Recommendation: {TBD}", "",
           "## Scoring results"] + bands + ["", unknown, retire, "", "## Wave plan"] + waves + \
          ["", "## TCO"] + tco_body + ["", "## Risks", "| Risk | Effect | Owner |", "|---|---|---|"] + risks + \
          ["", "## Next steps", "| Action | Owner | Date |", "|---|---|---|",
           f"| Validate band and wave assignments with the client architects | {TBD} | {TBD} |",
           f"| Confirm rate inputs and sources | {TBD} | {TBD} |"]
    Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(a.out).write_text("\n".join(x for x in out if x is not None) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"readout draft -> {a.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate, score, band, and wave-assign an integration/API inventory CSV.

Input columns: see assets/inventory-columns.md. Factor columns:
  pattern, transformation, target_connector, endpoint_count, volume_class,
  error_handling, security, test_coverage, documentation, criticality
Optional: calls_90d, endpoint_status, freeze_tag, depends_on.

Scoring (references/complexity-scoring.md): each factor 1-5, weighted,
normalized to 0-100. Blank or unrecognized factor values score 3 and are
counted as unknown; they are never treated as simple. Bands: Simple 0-30,
Medium 31-55, Complex 56-75, Very complex 76-100.

Waves: retirement candidates and decommissioning endpoints are excluded.
Wave 1 takes representative Simple items (one per pattern first, up to the
wave-1 share); remaining items are balanced across middle waves by weighted
score, with depends_on ordering enforced (a dependent never precedes its
prerequisite) and Very complex items kept out of the final wave.

Usage:
    python3 -I score_inventory.py inventory.csv --validate
    python3 -I score_inventory.py inventory.csv --out scored.csv --waves 4
    python3 -I score_inventory.py inventory.csv --out scored.csv --wave1-share 0.15 --summary

Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 input error; 4 validation failed (with --validate).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

FACTORS: list[tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int] | None]] = [
    # (column, factor_id, weight, value->score map or None for numeric endpoint_count)
    ("pattern", "f1", 15, {"sync": 1, "async": 3, "batch": 3, "orchestration": 5}),
    ("transformation", "f2", 15, {"none": 1, "mapping": 2, "moderate": 3, "heavy": 5}),
    ("target_connector", "f3", 15, {"native": 1, "partial": 3, "none": 5}),
    ("endpoint_count", "f4", 10, None),
    ("volume_class", "f5", 10, {"low": 1, "medium": 3, "high": 5}),
    ("error_handling", "f6", 10, {"default": 1, "custom": 3, "compensation": 5}),
    ("security", "f7", 8, {"basic": 1, "oauth-pii": 3, "regulated": 5}),
    ("test_coverage", "f8", 7, {"automated": 1, "manual": 3, "none": 5}),
    ("documentation", "f9", 5, {"current": 1, "partial": 3, "none": 5}),
    ("criticality", "f10", 5, {"low": 1, "medium": 3, "high": 5}),
]
TOTAL_WEIGHT = sum(w for _, _, w, _ in FACTORS)
REQUIRED = ["interface_id", "name", "source_system", "target_system"]
BANDS = [(30, "Simple"), (55, "Medium"), (75, "Complex"), (100, "Very complex")]


def band_of(score: float) -> str:
    for upper, name in BANDS:
        if score <= upper:
            return name
    return "Very complex"


def score_factor(col: str, raw: str, mapping: dict[str, int] | None) -> tuple[int, bool, bool]:
    """Return (score, unknown, review_flag)."""
    v = (raw or "").strip().lower()
    if not v:
        return 3, True, False
    if mapping is None:  # endpoint_count numeric
        try:
            n = int(float(v))
        except ValueError:
            return 3, True, True
        return (1 if n <= 2 else 3 if n <= 4 else 5), False, False
    if v in mapping:
        return mapping[v], False, False
    return 3, True, True  # unrecognized value: unknown + review


def validate(rows: list[dict], fieldnames: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    problems: list[str] = []
    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED if c not in fieldnames]
    if missing:
        problems.append(f"missing required columns: {missing}")
    missing_factors = [c for c, *_ in FACTORS if c not in fieldnames]
    if missing_factors:
        problems.append(f"missing factor columns (will score as unknown): {missing_factors}")
    ids = Counter((r.get("interface_id") or "").strip() for r in rows)
    dups = [k for k, n in ids.items() if k and n > 1]
    if dups:
        problems.append(f"duplicate interface_id: {dups[:10]}{' ...' if len(dups) > 10 else ''}")
    blanks = sum(1 for r in rows if not (r.get("interface_id") or "").strip())
    if blanks:
        problems.append(f"{blanks} rows with blank interface_id")
    return problems


def score_rows(rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    for r in rows:
        total = 0.0
        unknown = 0
        review = False
        for col, fid, w, mapping in FACTORS:
            s, unk, rev = score_factor(col, r.get(col, ""), mapping)
            r[f"{fid}_score"] = s
            total += s * w
            unknown += int(unk)
            review = review or rev
        # conflict check: pass-through sync with no connector but 'none' transformation is plausible; flag heavy+sync
        r["weighted_score"] = round(total / TOTAL_WEIGHT / 5 * 100, 1)
        r["unknown_factors"] = unknown
        r["band"] = band_of(r["weighted_score"])
        calls = (r.get("calls_90d") or "").strip()
        retire = False
        try:
            retire = calls != "" and float(calls) <= 0
        except ValueError:
            pass
        if (r.get("endpoint_status") or "").strip().lower() == "decommissioning":
            retire = True
        r["retire_candidate"] = "Y" if retire else "N"
        r["review_flag"] = "Y" if review else "N"


def assign_waves(rows: list[dict], waves: int, wave1_share: float) -> None:
    candidates = [r for r in rows if r["retire_candidate"] == "N"]
    for r in rows:
        r["wave"] = "retire" if r["retire_candidate"] == "Y" else ""
    if not candidates or waves < 2:
        for r in candidates:
            r["wave"] = "1"
        return
    by_id = {r["interface_id"]: r for r in candidates}
    # Wave 1: representative simples, one per pattern first
    simples = sorted((r for r in candidates if r["band"] == "Simple"), key=lambda r: r["weighted_score"])
    if not simples:  # no Simple band: prove the factory on the lowest-scored items instead
        simples = sorted(candidates, key=lambda r: r["weighted_score"])
    n_w1 = max(1, int(round(len(candidates) * wave1_share)))
    wave1: list[dict] = []
    seen_patterns: set[str] = set()
    for r in simples:
        p = (r.get("pattern") or "").lower()
        if p not in seen_patterns and len(wave1) < n_w1:
            wave1.append(r); seen_patterns.add(p)
    for r in simples:
        if r not in wave1 and len(wave1) < n_w1:
            wave1.append(r)
    for r in wave1:
        r["wave"] = "1"
    remaining = [r for r in candidates if r["wave"] == ""]
    middle = list(range(2, waves + 1))
    # Balance by weighted score across middle waves; Very complex never in the last wave
    loads = {w: 0.0 for w in middle}
    for r in sorted(remaining, key=lambda r: -r["weighted_score"]):
        allowed = middle[:-1] if (r["band"] == "Very complex" and len(middle) > 1) else middle
        w = min(allowed, key=lambda k: loads[k])
        r["wave"] = str(w); loads[w] += r["weighted_score"]
    # Enforce dependencies: dependent wave >= prerequisite wave (iterate to fixpoint)
    changed = True
    guard = 0
    while changed and guard < 50:
        changed = False; guard += 1
        for r in candidates:
            deps = [d.strip() for d in (r.get("depends_on") or "").split(";") if d.strip()]
            for d in deps:
                pre = by_id.get(d)
                if pre is None or pre["wave"] in ("", "retire"):
                    continue
                if int(r["wave"]) < int(pre["wave"]):
                    r["wave"] = pre["wave"]; changed = True


def summary(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    L = []
    bands = Counter(r["band"] for r in rows)
    total = len(rows)
    L.append("| Band | Count | Share |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|")
    for _, name in BANDS:
        L.append(f"| {name} | {bands.get(name, 0)} | {bands.get(name, 0)/total*100 if total else 0:.0f}% |")
    unk = sum(1 for r in rows if r["unknown_factors"] > 0)
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"Interfaces with >=1 unknown factor: {unk} ({unk/total*100 if total else 0:.0f}%)"
             + ("  — PROVISIONAL (>25%)" if total and unk / total > 0.25 else ""))
    L.append(f"Retirement candidates: {sum(1 for r in rows if r['retire_candidate']=='Y')}; review flags: {sum(1 for r in rows if r['review_flag']=='Y')}")
    L.append("")
    L.append("| Wave | Count | Σ score | Simple | Medium | Complex | Very complex |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    wv: dict[str, list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
    for r in rows:
        wv[r["wave"]].append(r)
    for w in sorted(wv, key=lambda k: (k == "retire", int(k) if k.isdigit() else 0)):
        rs = wv[w]
        c = Counter(r["band"] for r in rs)
        L.append(f"| {w} | {len(rs)} | {sum(r['weighted_score'] for r in rs):.0f} | {c.get('Simple',0)} | {c.get('Medium',0)} | {c.get('Complex',0)} | {c.get('Very complex',0)} |")
    return "\n".join(L)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("inventory", help="Inventory CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="Scored CSV output path")
    ap.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=4, help="Number of business waves (excluding wave 0)")
    ap.add_argument("--wave1-share", type=float, default=0.15, help="Share of interfaces in wave 1 (0.10-0.20)")
    ap.add_argument("--validate", action="store_true", help="Validate only; exit 4 on problems")
    ap.add_argument("--summary", action="store_true", help="Print band and wave summary (Markdown)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    path = Path(args.inventory)
    if not path.is_file():
        print(f"error: inventory not found: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rdr = csv.DictReader(fh)
        fieldnames = list(rdr.fieldnames or [])
        rows = [dict(r) for r in rdr]
    if not rows:
        print("error: inventory has no rows", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    problems = validate(rows, fieldnames)
    for p in problems:
        print(f"validation: {p}", file=sys.stderr)
    if args.validate:
        hard = [p for p in problems if p.startswith("missing required") or p.startswith("duplicate") or "blank interface_id" in p]
        print("validation: " + ("OK" if not hard else "FAILED"), file=sys.stderr)
        return 4 if hard else 0
    if any(p.startswith("missing required") for p in problems):
        return 2

    score_rows(rows)
    assign_waves(rows, args.waves, args.wave1_share)

    if args.out:
        extra = [f"{fid}_score" for _, fid, _, _ in FACTORS] + ["unknown_factors", "weighted_score", "band", "retire_candidate", "review_flag", "wave"]
        out_fields = fieldnames + [c for c in extra if c not in fieldnames]
        with open(args.out, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=out_fields, extrasaction="ignore")
            w.writeheader()
            for r in rows:
                w.writerow(r)
        print(f"wrote {args.out} ({len(rows)} rows)")
    if args.summary or not args.out:
        print(summary(rows))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""TCO table from a scored inventory + user-supplied rate inputs. No default prices.

Inputs
  scored inventory CSV (from score_inventory.py): needs `band` (Simple / Medium / Complex /
    Very complex); `retire_candidate` (true/false) rows are excluded from migration counts.
  rates CSV: key,value[,unit,source,notes] — every amount is annual unless stated. Keys:
    currency                         ISO code (default USD)
    current_licence                  current platform licence per year
    current_infrastructure           current hosting per year
    current_run_team                 current run/support team per year
    current_support_contract         vendor support per year
    target_licence, target_infrastructure, target_run_team, target_support_contract
    unit_cost_simple, unit_cost_medium, unit_cost_complex, unit_cost_very_complex
                                     one-time migration cost per interface by band
    training_one_time, decommission_one_time
    dual_run_months                  months both platforms run (target pays both run-rates)
    decommission_month               month (from start) the current platform is switched off;
                                     current-platform costs in `target` stop after it
    horizon_years                    default 3 (max 5)
  A key that is absent or blank makes every line that needs it
  `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Integration architect]`; a derived total that touches such a line is reported the
  same way, never as a number (assets/tco-model-spec.md).

Outputs
  --out tco.csv        one row per scenario x category x line x year
                       (scenario, category, line, year, amount, currency, source, basis, confidence)
  --summary tco.md     run-rate comparison, one-time cost, net benefit and payback tables
  --json tco.json      machine-readable totals

Usage:
    python3 -I tco.py scored.csv --rates rates.csv --out tco.csv --summary tco.md --json tco.json

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bad input (missing file/columns, non-numeric value). Stdlib only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Integration architect]"
BANDS = [("Simple", "unit_cost_simple"), ("Medium", "unit_cost_medium"),
         ("Complex", "unit_cost_complex"), ("Very complex", "unit_cost_very_complex")]
RUN_CATS = [("licence", "licence"), ("infrastructure", "infrastructure"),
            ("run_team", "run team"), ("support_contract", "support contract")]


def load_rates(path: Path) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"error: rates file not found: {path}")
    vals, src = {}, {}
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rdr = csv.DictReader(f)
        if not rdr.fieldnames or "key" not in rdr.fieldnames or "value" not in rdr.fieldnames:
            sys.exit("error: rates CSV needs columns key,value")
        for r in rdr:
            k, v = (r.get("key") or "").strip(), (r.get("value") or "").strip()
            if not k or not v:
                continue
            if k == "currency":
                vals[k] = v
            else:
                try:
                    vals[k] = float(v.replace(",", ""))
                except ValueError:
                    sys.exit(f"error: non-numeric value for {k}: {v!r}")
            src[k] = (r.get("source") or "").strip() or "rates CSV"
    return vals, src


def load_inventory(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"error: inventory not found: {path}")
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    if not rows:
        sys.exit("error: inventory has no rows")
    if "band" not in rows[0]:
        sys.exit("error: inventory has no `band` column (run score_inventory.py first)")
    return rows


def money(v, cur: str) -> str:
    return TBD if v is None else f"{v:,.0f} {cur}"


def build(rows: list[dict], rates: dict, src: dict):
    cur = str(rates.get("currency", "USD"))
    horizon = int(min(max(rates.get("horizon_years", 3), 1), 5))
    dual_months = rates.get("dual_run_months")
    decom_month = rates.get("decommission_month")
    lines = []  # scenario, category, line, year, amount(None=TBD), source

    def add(scn, cat, line, year, key_or_amount, source, basis="budget", conf="M"):
        if isinstance(key_or_amount, str):
            amt, s = rates.get(key_or_amount), src.get(key_or_amount, f"missing key {key_or_amount}")
        else:
            amt, s = key_or_amount, source
        lines.append({"scenario": scn, "category": cat, "line": line, "year": year,
                      "amount": amt, "currency": cur, "source": s, "basis": basis, "confidence": conf})

    # run-rate, both scenarios
    for year in range(1, horizon + 1):
        for cat, label in RUN_CATS:
            add("current", cat, f"current {label}", year, f"current_{cat}", None)
            # target: new platform costs
            add("target", cat, f"target {label}", year, f"target_{cat}", None)
        # dual run: current platform costs continue inside the target scenario until decommission
        if decom_month is None:
            add("target", "dual_run", "current platform until decommission", year, None,
                "decommission_month missing", "assumption", "L")
        else:
            months_in_year = max(0.0, min(12.0, decom_month - 12 * (year - 1)))
            if months_in_year > 0:
                share = months_in_year / 12.0
                total = 0.0
                missing = False
                for cat, _ in RUN_CATS:
                    v = rates.get(f"current_{cat}")
                    if v is None:
                        missing = True
                    else:
                        total += v * share
                add("target", "dual_run", f"current platform {months_in_year:.0f} months (decommission month {decom_month:.0f})",
                    year, None if missing else round(total, 2),
                    "current_* keys x months before decommission", "estimate", "M")
    # one-time migration, by band
    counts = {}
    for r in rows:
        if str(r.get("retire_candidate", "")).strip().lower() in ("true", "1", "yes"):
            continue
        counts[r.get("band", "")] = counts.get(r.get("band", ""), 0) + 1
    for band, key in BANDS:
        n = counts.get(band, 0)
        if n == 0:
            continue
        unit = rates.get(key)
        add("target", "migration_one_time", f"migrate {n} {band} interfaces @ {key}", 0,
            None if unit is None else round(n * unit, 2),
            f"{src.get(key, 'missing ' + key)}; count from scored inventory", "estimate", "M")
    add("target", "training", "training / enablement", 0, "training_one_time", None, "estimate", "M")
    add("target", "decommission", "decommission", 0, "decommission_one_time", None, "estimate", "M")
    if dual_months is not None and decom_month is None:
        lines.append({"scenario": "target", "category": "dual_run", "line": "dual_run_months given but decommission_month missing",
                      "year": 0, "amount": None, "currency": cur, "source": "rates CSV", "basis": "assumption", "confidence": "L"})
    return lines, cur, horizon, counts


def summarize(lines, cur, horizon):
    def total(scn, year, exclude_one_time=True):
        sel = [l for l in lines if l["scenario"] == scn and l["year"] == year]
        if exclude_one_time:
            sel = [l for l in sel if l["year"] != 0]
        if any(l["amount"] is None for l in sel):
            return None
        return sum(l["amount"] for l in sel)

    run = {scn: {y: total(scn, y) for y in range(1, horizon + 1)} for scn in ("current", "target")}
    one_time_lines = [l for l in lines if l["year"] == 0]
    one_time = None if any(l["amount"] is None for l in one_time_lines) else sum(l["amount"] for l in one_time_lines)
    cum = {"current": {}, "target": {}}
    net_year, net_cum, payback = {}, {}, None
    cc, ct = 0.0, (one_time if one_time is not None else None)
    cum["current"][0], cum["target"][0] = 0.0, ct
    net_year[0] = None if ct is None else -ct
    net_cum[0] = net_year[0]
    broken = ct is None
    for y in range(1, horizon + 1):
        c, t = run["current"][y], run["target"][y]
        if broken or c is None or t is None:
            broken = True
            cum["current"][y] = None if c is None else (cc := cc + c)
            cum["target"][y] = None
            net_year[y] = net_cum[y] = None
            continue
        cc += c
        ct += t
        cum["current"][y], cum["target"][y] = cc, ct
        net_year[y] = c - t
        net_cum[y] = cc - ct
        if payback is None and net_cum[y] >= 0:
            payback = y
    return {"currency": cur, "horizon_years": horizon, "run_rate": run, "one_time_total": one_time,
            "cumulative": cum, "net_benefit_by_year": net_year, "net_cumulative": net_cum,
            "payback_year": payback if not broken else None,
            "net_3yr": net_cum.get(min(3, horizon)) if not broken else None,
            "tbd_lines": [l["line"] for l in lines if l["amount"] is None]}


def render_md(lines, s, counts):
    cur, H = s["currency"], s["horizon_years"]
    yrs = list(range(1, H + 1))
    L = [f"# TCO — scored inventory x rate inputs", "",
         f"Currency: {cur} · Basis: undiscounted · Horizon: {H} years · "
         f"Lines marked TBD: {len(s['tbd_lines'])}", "",
         "## Run-rate comparison",
         "| Category | " + " | ".join(f"Current Y{y}" for y in yrs) + " | " + " | ".join(f"Target Y{y}" for y in yrs) + " | Source |",
         "|---|" + "---|" * (2 * H) + "---|"]
    cats = []
    for l in lines:
        if l["year"] != 0 and l["category"] not in cats:
            cats.append(l["category"])
    for cat in cats:
        cells, srcs = [], set()
        for scn in ("current", "target"):
            for y in yrs:
                sel = [l for l in lines if l["scenario"] == scn and l["category"] == cat and l["year"] == y]
                if not sel:
                    cells.append("—")
                elif any(l["amount"] is None for l in sel):
                    cells.append(TBD)
                else:
                    cells.append(f"{sum(l['amount'] for l in sel):,.0f}")
                srcs.update(l["source"] for l in sel)
        L.append(f"| {cat.replace('_', ' ')} | " + " | ".join(cells) + f" | {'; '.join(sorted(srcs))[:80]} |")
    L.append("| **Annual total** | " + " | ".join(
        money(s["run_rate"][scn][y], cur) for scn in ("current", "target") for y in yrs) + " | |")
    L += ["", "## One-time migration cost", "| Line | Amount | Source | Confidence |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {l['line']} | {money(l['amount'], cur)} | {l['source']} | {l['confidence']} |"
          for l in lines if l["year"] == 0]
    L.append(f"| **Total one-time** | {money(s['one_time_total'], cur)} | | |")
    L += ["", "## Net benefit and payback",
          "| Year | Current cumulative | Target cumulative (incl. one-time) | Net benefit (year) | Net cumulative |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for y in range(0, H + 1):
        L.append(f"| {y} | {money(s['cumulative']['current'].get(y), cur)} | {money(s['cumulative']['target'].get(y), cur)} | "
                 f"{money(s['net_benefit_by_year'].get(y), cur)} | {money(s['net_cumulative'].get(y), cur)} |")
    pb = s["payback_year"]
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"Payback: {('year ' + str(pb)) if pb else ('not within horizon' if s['net_3yr'] is not None else TBD)} · "
             f"3-year net: {money(s['net_3yr'], cur)}")
    L += ["", "## Inventory counts used (non-retirement)", "| Band | Count |", "|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {b} | {counts.get(b, 0)} |" for b, _ in BANDS]
    if s["tbd_lines"]:
        L += ["", "## Lines awaiting input (owner: Integration architect)"]
        L += [f"- {t}" for t in s["tbd_lines"]]
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("inventory", type=Path, help="scored inventory CSV (with band column)")
    ap.add_argument("--rates", type=Path, required=True, help="rate inputs CSV (key,value,...)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True, help="TCO lines CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--summary", type=Path, help="Markdown summary")
    ap.add_argument("--json", type=Path, help="JSON totals")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    rows = load_inventory(a.inventory)
    rates, src = load_rates(a.rates)
    lines, cur, horizon, counts = build(rows, rates, src)
    s = summarize(lines, cur, horizon)
    a.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with a.out.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["scenario", "category", "line", "year", "amount", "currency",
                                          "source", "basis", "confidence"])
        w.writeheader()
        for l in lines:
            w.writerow({**l, "amount": TBD if l["amount"] is None else f"{l['amount']:.2f}"})
    if a.summary:
        a.summary.write_text(render_md(lines, s, counts), encoding="utf-8")
    if a.json:
        a.json.write_text(json.dumps({**s, "band_counts": counts}, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(lines)} TCO lines ({len(s['tbd_lines'])} TBD) -> {a.out}; "
          f"3-yr net: {money(s['net_3yr'], cur)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Interface Inventory — Column Specification (collection template)

One row per interface / API / flow. Send to the client platform team as the collection template; most columns can be exported from the platform console or repository. Factor columns accept the listed values; blank = unknown (scored mid-band with a flag).

| # | Column | Required | Values / format | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `interface_id` | yes | Unique ID (client's or `INT-nnn`) | Platform export |
| 2 | `name` | yes | Human name | Platform export |
| 3 | `source_system` | yes | System name | Platform export |
| 4 | `target_system` | yes | System name (semicolon list if fan-out) | Platform export |
| 5 | `owner` | no | Team / person | Platform team |
| 6 | `pattern` | factor F1 | `sync` / `async` / `batch` / `orchestration` | Platform export / review |
| 7 | `transformation` | factor F2 | `none` / `mapping` / `moderate` / `heavy` | Code review |
| 8 | `target_connector` | factor F3 | `native` / `partial` / `none` | Target platform catalog |
| 9 | `endpoint_count` | factor F4 | Integer | Platform export |
| 10 | `volume_class` | factor F5 | `low` / `medium` / `high` | Metrics |
| 11 | `error_handling` | factor F6 | `default` / `custom` / `compensation` | Code review |
| 12 | `security` | factor F7 | `basic` / `oauth-pii` / `regulated` | Security review |
| 13 | `test_coverage` | factor F8 | `automated` / `manual` / `none` | Repo |
| 14 | `documentation` | factor F9 | `current` / `partial` / `none` | Repo / wiki |
| 15 | `criticality` | factor F10 | `low` / `medium` / `high` | Business owner |

| 18 | `freeze_tag` | no | Label for a constraint (e.g., `erp-go-live`) | PMO |
| 19 | `depends_on` | no | Semicolon list of `interface_id` that must migrate first | Architecture |
| 20 | `notes` | no | Free text | — |

Value mapping to factor scores (1 / 3 / 5): first value → 1, middle → 3, last → 5; `endpoint_count`: ≤2 → 1, 3–4 → 3, ≥5 → 5. `transformation`: none → 1, mapping → 2, moderate → 3, heavy → 5.

Minimum viable inventory for a provisional assessment: columns 1–4, 6–8. Everything else improves confidence.

# TCO / ROI Model — CSV Layout Specification

Two CSV files. Every `amount` cell carries a `source` cell; an empty source is invalid — write `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]` in `amount` instead.

## File 1: `tco-lines.csv` (one row per cost line per scenario per year)
| # | Column | Type | Allowed values / format |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scenario` | enum | `current` (stay) · `target` (migrate) |
| 2 | `category` | enum | `licence` · `infrastructure` · `run_team` · `support_contract` · `incident_cost` · `migration_one_time` · `dual_run` · `training` · `decommission` · `other` |
| 3 | `line` | text | Specific item (e.g., "Core licence — 4 vCores", "L2 support team — 3 FTE") |
| 4 | `year` | int | 0 (one-time, at start) … 5 |
| 5 | `amount` | number or marker | Currency amount or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]` |
| 6 | `currency` | text | ISO code |
| 7 | `source` | text | Document + page/section, or the client role who stated it, or `estimate-memo vX` |
| 8 | `basis` | enum | `contract` · `invoice` · `budget` · `estimate` · `assumption` |
| 9 | `confidence` | enum | `H` · `M` · `L` |
| 10 | `timing_rule` | text | e.g., "starts after decommission date D", "ends at contract end 2027-06-30" |
| 11 | `notes` | text | — |

Rules:
- Licence and infrastructure savings in `target` appear only from the year after the decommission date; until then, `dual_run` lines carry both.
- `migration_one_time` amounts come from `effort-estimator` output (P80 unless stated) and cite the memo version.
- Vendor list prices are never used from memory; only client contracts, quotes, or marked.

## File 2: `tco-assumptions.csv`

| 6 | `sensitivity` | `H` / `M` / `L` (effect on NPV if ±20%) |
| 7 | `used_by_lines` | semicolon list of `line` values |

Mandatory assumption rows: decommission date; discount rate (if NPV used; else "undiscounted"); contract end dates; growth in interface count; run-team cost per FTE (client-provided); migration cost source and confidence level; inflation/uplift; currency.

| Annual run-rate by scenario | Σ amounts by scenario, year (excluding one-time) |
| Cumulative cost by scenario | Running Σ across years incl. one-time |

| Payback | First year where cumulative net benefit ≥ 0 |
| 3-year / 5-year net | Σ net benefit through year 3 / 5 |
| NPV (optional) | Σ net benefit ÷ (1 + r)^year, r from assumptions |
| Sensitivity | Recompute 3-year net with the two highest-sensitivity assumptions at ±20% |

Any derived output computed from a line marked `[TO BE BASELINED]` is itself reported as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`, not as a number.

# Complexity Scoring

## 1. Factors, scales, weights
Each factor is scored 1 (simplest) to 5 (hardest) from the inventory columns. Weighted total 0–100. Weights are defaults; adjust to the source/target pair and state the adjustment in the readout.

| # | Factor | Column | 1 | 3 | 5 | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Integration pattern | `pattern` | Sync request/response pass-through | Async/event, batch with scheduling | Orchestration, long-running saga, compensations | 15 |
| F2 | Transformation logic | `transformation` | None / field mapping | Moderate mapping with lookups and conditionals | Heavy custom code, scripting, stateful logic | 15 |
| F3 | Connector / protocol availability on target | `target_connector` | Native connector or standard HTTP | Partial (adapter or minor custom) | No connector; custom build (e.g., legacy protocol, proprietary adapter) | 15 |
| F4 | Endpoints and systems touched | `endpoint_count` | 2 | 3–4 | ≥5 or fan-out | 10 |
| F5 | Data volume and payload | `volume_class` | Low (<10k msgs/day, small payloads) | Medium | High (>1M/day) or large payloads/files | 10 |
| F6 | Error handling and orchestration | `error_handling` | Default retry | Custom retry, DLQ, notification | Compensation, manual intervention workflows, SLA-bound recovery | 10 |
| F7 | Security and compliance | `security` | Basic auth/API key internal | OAuth2/mTLS, PII | Regulated data, tokenization, residency, audit obligations | 8 |
| F8 | Test coverage available | `test_coverage` | Automated tests exist | Manual test cases documented | None | 7 |
| F9 | Documentation and ownership | `documentation` | Current docs, named owner | Partial | None / owner unknown | 5 |
| F10 | Business criticality | `criticality` | Low | Medium | Revenue/compliance-critical, peak-sensitive | 5 |

Weighted score = Σ (factor score × weight) ÷ 5 → 0–100.

## 2. Bands
| Band | Score | Typical approach | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simple | 0–30 | Automated / tool-assisted conversion, templated tests | Volume play; the factory's bread and butter |
| Medium | 31–55 | Factory with pattern templates; developer completes | Majority in most estates |
| Complex | 56–75 | Design-led; refactor into target patterns; dedicated tests | Senior developers; architecture review |
| Very complex | 76–100 | Redesign, retire, or re-platform outside factory; spike first | Candidates for business process review |

Band thresholds are calibrated against prior actuals when available; otherwise stated as defaults.

## 3. Unknown handling
| Situation | Rule |
|---|---|
| Blank factor cell | Score 3 with `unknown` flag; the script lists the interface |
| >25% of interfaces with ≥1 unknown factor | Assessment is provisional; the readout says so on line 1 and the next step is inventory completion with an owner |
| Conflicting inputs (e.g., "no connector" but pattern "pass-through") | Flag `review`; analyst resolves |

Never default unknowns to 1 (Simple). Under-scoring is the primary cause of migration overrun.

## 4. Retirement screening (before scoring effort)
| Signal | Column | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Zero or near-zero traffic in 90 days | `calls_90d` | Retirement candidate; confirm with owner |
| Duplicate of another interface (same source, target, purpose) | analyst | Merge; migrate once |
| Endpoint system being decommissioned | `endpoint_status` | Retire with the system; exclude from waves |
| Superseded by a newer API | analyst | Retire; redirect consumers |

Retirement candidates are reported as a separate count with the owner who must confirm. Savings from retirement are real only after confirmation.

## 5. Calibration
If prior migration actuals exist (effort per interface by band), compare predicted bands against actual effort distribution; adjust weights or thresholds and record the adjustment. Without actuals, keep defaults and flag unit efforts in `effort-estimator` as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## 6. Output columns added by scoring
`f1_score … f10_score`, `unknown_factors` (count), `weighted_score`, `band`, `retire_candidate` (Y/N), `review_flag`, `wave`.

# Migration Factory Method

## 1. Principles
| Principle | Practice |
|---|---|
| Inventory before estimate | No effort or price without a scored inventory |
| Retire before migrate | Cheapest interface is the one you delete |
| Patterns before interfaces | Build target-pattern templates (sync API, async event, batch, file) in wave 0; interfaces then follow templates |
| Prove the factory on simples | Wave 1 validates tooling, tests, and cutover before complexity arrives |
| Parallel run governs cutover | Legacy and target run side by side; variance log decides go/no-go |
| Decommission is a deliverable | Savings start when the old platform is switched off, not when the new one is switched on |

## 2. Approach by band
| Band | Approach | Team | Test | Review |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Simple | Tool-assisted conversion (spec extraction → target config generation); developer verifies | Core engineers, high leverage | Templated contract tests, auto-generated from spec; parallel-run comparison | Peer |
| Medium | Factory: template selection, mapping completion, custom logic ported | Core + senior | Contract + integration tests; parallel run | Tech lead |
| Complex | Design-led: re-express orchestration/transformation in target patterns; may split into several interfaces | Senior + architect | Full integration and NFR tests; extended parallel run | Architect |
| Very complex | Spike first (time-boxed); decide redesign / retire / keep on legacy longer / re-platform | Architect + business owner | Per decision | ARB and business sponsor |

## 3. Factory operating model
| Station | Input | Output | Exit check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intake | Scored inventory row, source artifacts | Migration ticket with pattern template assigned | Owner confirmed; test data available |
| Convert | Ticket | Target implementation in repo | Lint/build passes; config generated |
| Test | Implementation | Contract + integration test results | Pass thresholds met |
| Parallel run | Deployed to target in shadow | Variance log over N days | Variance within tolerance; sign-off |
| Cutover | Sign-off | Traffic switched; legacy route disabled | Monitoring green for hypercare window |
| Decommission | Cutover complete for all interfaces on a legacy component | Component removed; licence/infra released | Finance confirms cost release |

Throughput is measured per station; bottlenecks (usually test data and client sign-off) are managed as dependencies with dates.

## 4. Wave rules
| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Wave 0 | Target platform foundation, CI/CD, observability, security baseline, pattern templates, conversion tooling, test harness, parallel-run comparison tool. No business cutovers |
| Wave 1 | 10–20% of interfaces, Simple band, covering each pattern at least once; proves the factory |
| Middle waves | Mixed bands; dependencies resolved within or before the wave; the most complex items in a middle wave with the most attention, never last |
| Final wave | Long tail, stragglers, decommission |
| Sizing | Balance by weighted score sum, not by count |
| Dependencies | Interfaces sharing an endpoint under change migrate together; consumers after providers |
| Constraints | Freeze windows exclude cutovers; dependent programs (ERP go-live) fix wave boundaries |
| Entry criteria | Wave scope frozen; test data ready; owners confirmed; environments available |
| Exit criteria | All interfaces cut over; hypercare complete; no open P1; variance logs signed; runbooks delivered |
| Rollback | Per interface: route switch back to legacy within <n> minutes; legacy retained until wave exit + buffer |

## 5. Cutover and parallel run
| Element | Default | Adjust when |
|---|---|---|
| Parallel-run duration | 5 business days (Simple/Medium), 10 (Complex) | Monthly batch → one full cycle |
| Variance tolerance | 0 functional variance; timing within SLA | Known legacy defects documented as accepted variance |
| Cutover window | Off-peak, outside freeze | Client calendar |
| Hypercare | 10 business days per wave | Peak proximity |
| Go/no-go | Variance log, test results, rollback rehearsed, owner sign-off | — |

## 6. Decommission
| Step | Owner | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm no traffic on legacy routes (30 days) | Platform team | Metrics |
| Remove legacy deployments | Platform team | Change record |
| Terminate licences / infrastructure | Client procurement | Contract notice |
| Release run team capacity | Client IT | Org change |
| Record savings start date | Finance | Ledger |

TCO savings lines reference these dates. Without a decommission date, savings are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## 7. Risks specific to migration
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Connector gaps on target discovered late | F3 scoring; spike in wave 0 for any F3 = 5 |
| Endpoint systems change during migration | Change freeze on in-flight endpoints; or re-score and re-wave |
| Dual-run cost longer than planned | Decommission as milestone with owner; licence notice dates tracked |
| Test data unavailable | Data provisioning as client dependency with date |
| Skills on target platform | Wave 0 enablement; pairing; named onshore leads |
| Unknown-heavy inventory | Provisional assessment; inventory completion phase |

# orals-prep

## In a conversation: prepare the team now
- **The request carries the format and the team** (duration, presentation vs Q&A split, evaluators, presenters) — including when the proposal, deck, compliance matrix or battle card are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the orals pack **in this reply** from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
  1. **Evaluation map** — each stated criterion (or, if criteria are unknown, the proposal's structure) → slide(s) → speaker.
  2. **Timed script** fitting the presentation slot — segments with start/end minute, speaker, slide, point, proof (number with source or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`), transition; **opening ≤90 s and close ≤60 s written verbatim**; scripted handoffs; **airtime check** (every speaker ≥1 segment, none >40%).
  3. **Likely-questions bank** (table) — one question per compliance partial (e.g. each security partial), per `[TBD]`, per estimate assumption, plus the battle card's objections and the standard evaluator set; each answer ≤75 words with the answerer, evidence pointer and "do not say" line.
  4. **The hard three** (typically price, the known gaps, incumbent continuity) with honest answers that state the gap and the mitigation.
  5. **Red-team protocol** and **rehearsal plan** — three dry runs (content and timing, Q&A only, full with red team), each with a date or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and the rubric (`assets/orals-rubric.md`).
  6. **Number sheet** — every figure the team may say, with its proposal page · **Logistics and risks** · **Open items** with owners.
  No competitor is named in any answer.
- **No format or team** ("help us get ready for the pitch"): ask once, in one list, for the format (duration, presentation/Q&A split, attendees, evaluation criteria), the presenting team and the proposal and deck. Do not produce a timed script without the duration and the team. If the proposal is available, offer to generate the question bank from it as a parallel first step.
- **Asked to script new numbers, uncleared client claims or a competitor attack** ("say we are 30% faster", "our last clients saw 40% savings", "name the incumbent's failed upgrade"): say in one line that new numbers and competitor naming in orals create credibility and compliance risk. Rewrite the answer around the proposal's basis of estimate, P80 contingency and a like-for-like comparison; use cleared references only, in their cleared form, or omit them; replace the competitor mention with a ghost line in consequence language (the risk the client should weigh, and how we remove it). Never print the requested percentages in the answer, unless the user shows they are in the proposal with a source.

## Starting points
- **New** — from the submitted proposal: a timed script skeleton with speakers, an airtime check, a number sheet every presenter keeps in front of them, and likely evaluator questions.
- **Existing** — add your team's current talk track: every figure it says that the proposal does not contain is flagged, each speaker's spoken length is compared with their slot, and people with lines but no slot are listed (`talk-track-check.md`).

## When to use
- "We are shortlisted; orals are Thursday — prepare us."
- "Run a red-team on our pitch."
- "Build the Q&A bank for the steering-committee readout."
- NOT for: fixing the slides (`exec-deck-redline`), building the battle card (`competitive-positioning`), writing the proposal (`proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The proposal or readout document (final) | yes | file |
| The deck to be presented (final or near-final) | yes | file |
| Format rules: duration, presentation vs Q&A split, attendees (names/roles if known), evaluation criteria, allowed presenters | yes | RFP / client / user |
| Our presenting team (names, roles on the engagement) | yes | user |
| Battle card (if a competitive pursuit) | no | competitive-positioning output |
| Compliance matrix and clarification answers (RFP pursuits) | no | rfp-compliance-matrix output |

If format rules or the team are missing, ask once; a script cannot be timed or assigned without them. Missing files (proposal, deck, compliance matrix, battle card) or unknown evaluation criteria do not stop the pack when the format and team are stated: the gaps are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Decode the evaluation**: from the format rules, list what is scored and by whom. If the evaluation criteria are unknown, mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and assume the proposal's structure is the scoring frame. Map each scored criterion to the slide(s) and speaker that will prove it (`references/orals-method.md` §1).
2. **Build the timed script** on `assets/script-template.md`: segments with start/end minute, speaker, slide, the point (one sentence), the proof (number with source), the transition line. Reserve ≥35% of total time for Q&A unless the format fixes it. Opening ≤90 seconds: their situation, the outcome, what they will hear. Close ≤60 seconds: the ask and the next step.
3. **Assign speakers by credibility**, not seniority: the person who will do the work speaks to the approach; the engagement lead to governance and commitments; the executive sponsor opens and closes. Every speaker has ≥1 segment and ≤40% of airtime. Note handoffs explicitly.
4. **Generate the likely-questions bank** (`references/question-bank-and-red-team.md` §1): from the proposal's weak spots (every `P`/`N` in the compliance matrix, every `[TBD]`, every assumption), from the evaluation criteria, from the battle card's objections, and from the standard evaluator set. For each: question, who answers, the answer (≤75 words, number + source, no new claims), the evidence slide/page, and the "do not say" line.
5. **Decision point — the hard three.** Identify the three questions the team most fears (price, a gap, a credibility challenge). Write the answers with the engagement lead; rehearse these first and most. If an honest answer exposes a real gap, the answer states the gap and the mitigation; it does not spin.
6. **Red-team** (§2): assign one person to play the skeptical evaluator and one the incumbent-friendly evaluator; run the objections in the bank plus three unscripted; score with `assets/orals-rubric.md`; log every answer that exceeded 90 seconds, invented a number, or contradicted the proposal.
7. **Rehearsal plan**: dry run 1 (content and timing), dry run 2 (Q&A only), dry run 3 (full, with red team), each with a date and the rubric scores. Fix list after each.
8. **Logistics and risk**: room/virtual setup, backups (PDF of deck, offline), who speaks if someone drops, name pronunciation for attendees, prohibited content (other clients' names without clearance, pricing details if sealed).
9. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `orals-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections: Evaluation map (criterion → slide → speaker) · Timed script · Speaker assignments and handoffs · Likely questions bank (table) · The hard three · Red-team log · Rehearsal plan · Logistics and risks · Open items
- Companion: `assets/orals-rubric.md` scored per dry run

## Self-check
- [ ] Every scored criterion mapped to a slide and a speaker
- [ ] Script timed to the format; Q&A ≥35% unless fixed by the client
- [ ] Every number in the script and answers traces to the proposal/sources; none new
- [ ] Hard three identified with honest answers that state gaps and mitigations
- [ ] Each answer ≤75 words with a named answerer and evidence pointer
- [ ] No competitor named in any answer; no uncleared client references
- [ ] Rehearsal plan has dates and rubric scores recorded
- [ ] Logistics and backups listed

## References
- `references/orals-method.md` — evaluation decoding, script structure, speaker assignment, answer discipline, delivery rules
- `references/question-bank-and-red-team.md` — standard evaluator questions by theme, question-generation sources, red-team protocol
- `assets/script-template.md` — timed script layout
- `assets/orals-rubric.md` — dry-run scoring rubric

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/orals-prep --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/orals-prep`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Orals prep from a proposal: timed script skeleton, number registry, likely questions.

    python3 -I scripts/orals.py proposal.md --minutes 60 --speakers "Giri,Priya,Alex" \
        --question-bank references/question-bank-and-red-team.md \
        --script orals-script.md --registry number-registry.csv --questions likely-questions.md

Timing: 70% presentation / 30% Q&A; a fixed opening (1.5 min) and close (1 min) bracket the
sections, which get presentation time proportional to their word count in proposal.md (minimum
one minute each). Speakers are assigned round-robin in proposal order; the opening goes to the
first speaker and the close to the last. number-registry.csv lists every number in the proposal
(>= 3 significant digits or carrying $ / %) with its section and context, plus the computed timing
and airtime numbers (section "orals timing"), so every number in orals-script.md traces to it.
likely-questions.md = the standard evaluator questions from the question bank, one question per
`[TO BE BASELINED` marker in the proposal ("what is the number?"), and one per assumption row.
No proof line is written for a section that holds no number; it reads `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Bid manager]`.
Existing talk track (--talk-track track.md --check out.md): the team's current script, one line per
speaker turn (`Name: …` or `**Name:** …`), is checked against the proposal and the timing: every figure
it says that the proposal does not contain is flagged (cut it or source it in the proposal first),
each speaker's spoken minutes (at 150 words per minute) are compared with the allocated airtime, and
lines from people not in --speakers are listed. Written to --check; the generated script is unchanged.
Exit 1 when proposal.md is missing / has no sections, --minutes < 10, or --speakers is empty.
Stdlib only, offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Bid manager]"
NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])([$€£]?)(-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)(%?)(?![\w])")
DATE_RE = re.compile(r"\b\d{4}-\d{2}(-\d{2})?\b")
OPEN_MIN, CLOSE_MIN, QA_SHARE = 1.5, 1.0, 0.30


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def sig(num: str) -> int:
    return len(num.replace(",", "").replace("-", "").replace(".", "").lstrip("0"))


def numbers_in(text: str):
    """Numbers worth tracing (>= 3 significant digits or $ / %); ISO dates are not numbers."""
    for m in NUMBER_RE.finditer(DATE_RE.sub(" ", text)):
        sym, num, pct = m.groups()
        if sym or pct or sig(num) >= 3:
            yield f"{sym}{num}{pct}"


def sections_of(md: str) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    out, cur = [], None
    for ln in md.splitlines():
        if ln.startswith("## "):
            cur = (re.sub(r"^\d+\.\s*", "", ln[3:].strip()), [])
            out.append(cur)
        elif cur is not None:
            cur[1].append(ln)
    return out


def mmss(minutes: float) -> str:
    total = int(round(minutes * 60))
    return f"{total // 60}:{total % 60:02d}"


def bank_questions(path: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """(theme, question, answer pattern) rows from the '### <theme>' tables of the question bank."""
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        return []
    rows, theme = [], ""
    for ln in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        if ln.startswith("## "):
            theme = ""
            continue
        if ln.startswith("### "):
            theme = ln[4:].strip()
            continue
        if theme and ln.startswith("| \""):
            c = [x.strip() for x in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
            if len(c) >= 2:
                rows.append((theme, c[0].strip('"'), c[1]))
    return rows


WPM = 150
SPOKEN_NUM_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])[$€£]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?(?:%|[kKmMbB]\b)?")


def spoken_figures(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Figures as said, suffix kept ('$2.1M', '6.2%'); same threshold as numbers_in plus k/M/B amounts."""
    out = []
    for m in SPOKEN_NUM_RE.finditer(DATE_RE.sub(" ", text)):
        tok = m.group(0)
        core = tok.lstrip("$€£").rstrip("%kKmMbB")
        if tok[0] in "$€£" or tok[-1] in "%kKmMbB" or sig(core) >= 3:
            out.append(tok)
    return out


TURN_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*]\s*)?\**([A-Z][\w .'-]{0,40}?)\**\s*:\**\s*(.+)$")


def check_talk_track(track: str, registry: list[dict], airtime: dict, speakers: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    known = {r["number"] for r in registry if r["section"] != "orals timing"}
    words: dict[str, int] = {}
    untraced, strangers = [], []
    for n, ln in enumerate(track.splitlines(), 1):
        m = TURN_RE.match(ln)
        if not m or ln.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        who, said = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
        words[who] = words.get(who, 0) + len(said.split())
        if who not in speakers and who not in strangers:
            strangers.append(who)
        untraced += [(n, who, x) for x in spoken_figures(said) if x not in known]
    L = ["# Talk track check", "", f"Checked against the proposal's number registry and the timed script ({WPM} words per minute).", "",
         "## Figures not in the proposal", "| Line | Speaker | Figure | Action |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {n} | {who} | {x} | cut it, or source it in the proposal first ({TBD}) |" for n, who, x in untraced] or \
         ["| — | — | — | every figure traces to the proposal |"]
    L += ["", "## Airtime vs spoken length", "| Speaker | Allocated min | Spoken min | Verdict |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for s_ in speakers:
        spoken = words.get(s_, 0) / WPM
        alloc = airtime.get(s_, 0.0)
        verdict = "no lines in the track" if not words.get(s_) else \
            ("over — cut" if spoken > alloc * 1.1 else "under — room to add proof" if spoken < alloc * 0.5 else "fits")
        L.append(f"| {s_} | {round(alloc, 1)} | {round(spoken, 1)} | {verdict} |")
    L += ["", "## Speakers not in the line-up", ""]
    L += [f"- {w}: has lines in the track but is not in --speakers — add them or reassign the lines" for w in strangers] or ["- none"]
    return L


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="proposal.md -> orals-script.md + number-registry.csv + likely-questions.md")
    ap.add_argument("proposal")
    ap.add_argument("--minutes", type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--speakers", required=True, help="comma list in speaking order")
    ap.add_argument("--question-bank", default="references/question-bank-and-red-team.md")
    ap.add_argument("--script", required=True); ap.add_argument("--registry", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--questions", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--talk-track", default="", help="the team's existing talk track to check")
    ap.add_argument("--check", default="", help="with --talk-track: write the check here")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.talk_track and not Path(a.talk_track).is_file():
        die(f"talk track not found: {a.talk_track}")
    if a.minutes < 10 or a.minutes > 240:
        die("--minutes must be 10..240")
    speakers = [s.strip() for s in a.speakers.split(",") if s.strip()]
    if not speakers:
        die("--speakers is empty")
    p = Path(a.proposal)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    md = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    secs = sections_of(md)
    if not secs:
        die("proposal has no '## ' sections")
    title = next((ln[2:].strip() for ln in md.splitlines() if ln.startswith("# ")), p.stem)

    registry = []
    for name, lines in secs:
        for ln in lines:
            for n in numbers_in(ln):
                ctx = re.sub(r"\s*\|\s*", " / ", ln.strip().strip("|")).strip(" /")
                registry.append({"number": n, "section": name, "context": ctx[:140]})
    present = a.minutes * (1 - QA_SHARE)
    qa = a.minutes - present
    body_min = max(present - OPEN_MIN - CLOSE_MIN, len(secs) * 1.0)
    weights = [max(len(" ".join(lines).split()), 1) for _, lines in secs]
    tot_w = sum(weights)
    alloc = [max(1.0, round(body_min * w / tot_w * 2) / 2) for w in weights]
    scale = body_min / sum(alloc)
    alloc = [round(x * scale * 2) / 2 for x in alloc]
    alloc = [max(0.5, x) for x in alloc]

    rows, t = [], 0.0
    rows.append((t, t + OPEN_MIN, "Opening", speakers[0], "1–2", "Their situation in their words; the outcome we commit to", TBD))
    t += OPEN_MIN
    airtime = {s: 0.0 for s in speakers}
    airtime[speakers[0]] += OPEN_MIN
    for i, ((name, lines), m) in enumerate(zip(secs, alloc)):
        spk = speakers[i % len(speakers)]
        nums = [r["number"] for r in registry if r["section"] == name]
        proof = ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(nums)) if nums else TBD
        rows.append((t, t + m, name, spk, TBD, TBD, proof))
        airtime[spk] += m
        t += m
    rows.append((t, t + CLOSE_MIN, "Close", speakers[-1], "last", "The ask; next step with date; one memorable sentence", TBD))
    airtime[speakers[-1]] += CLOSE_MIN
    t += CLOSE_MIN
    rows.append((t, t + qa, "Q&A", "all (per likely-questions.md)", "—", "", ""))
    t_end = t + qa
    for lab, val in (("total minutes", a.minutes), ("presentation minutes", round(present, 1)), ("Q&A minutes", round(qa, 1)),
                     ("body minutes", round(body_min, 1))):
        registry.append({"number": str(val), "section": "orals timing", "context": lab})
    for s, m in airtime.items():
        share = round(100 * m / present)
        registry.append({"number": f"{share}%", "section": "orals timing", "context": f"airtime share {s}"})
        registry.append({"number": str(round(m, 1)), "section": "orals timing", "context": f"airtime minutes {s}"})
    registry.append({"number": mmss(t_end).replace(":", ""), "section": "orals timing", "context": "end of slot"})

    L = [f"# Orals Script — {title}", "",
         f"Format: {a.minutes} min total · {mmss(present)} presentation · {mmss(qa)} Q&A · Speakers: {', '.join(speakers)} · "
         f"Attendees: {TBD} · Evaluation criteria: {TBD}", "",
         "## Timed script", "| Start | End | Segment | Speaker | Slide | The point (one sentence) | Proof (numbers from proposal; see number-registry.csv) |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {mmss(s)} | {mmss(e)} | {seg} | {spk} | {slide} | {point} | {proof} |" for s, e, seg, spk, slide, point, proof in rows]
    L += ["", "## Airtime check", "| Speaker | Minutes | Share of presentation |", "|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {s} | {round(m, 1)} | {round(100 * m / present)}% |" for s, m in airtime.items()]
    L += ["", "## Opening (verbatim, ≤90 s)", TBD, "", "## Close (verbatim, ≤60 s)", TBD, "",
          "## Number sheet (in front of every presenter)", "| Number | Context | Section |", "|---|---|---|"]
    seen = set()
    for r in registry:
        if r["section"] != "orals timing" and (r["number"], r["section"]) not in seen:
            seen.add((r["number"], r["section"]))
            L.append(f"| {r['number']} | {r['context']} | {r['section']} |")
    if not seen:
        L.append(f"| none in proposal | every claim needs a number — {TBD} | |")
    L += ["", "## Handoffs", "| From | To | Line |", "|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {rows[i][3]} | {rows[i + 1][3]} | {TBD} |" for i in range(len(rows) - 2) if rows[i][3] != rows[i + 1][3]]
    L += ["", "## Logistics", "| Item | Status | Owner |", "|---|---|---|",
          f"| PDF + offline deck | | {TBD} |", f"| Attendee names/pronunciation | | {TBD} |",
          f"| Timekeeper and signals (−5, −2) | | {TBD} |", f"| Backup presenter per segment | | {TBD} |"]
    Path(a.script).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(a.script).write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    with Path(a.registry).open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["number", "section", "context"]); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(registry)

    Q = [f"# Likely questions — {title}", "", "| # | Question | Theme | Answerer | Answer (≤75 words) | Evidence | Confidence |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    k = 0
    for theme, q, pattern in bank_questions(a.question_bank):
        k += 1
        Q.append(f"| {k} | {q} | {theme} | {TBD} | pattern: {pattern} | {TBD} | |")
    for name, lines in secs:
        for ln in lines:
            if "[TO BE BASELINED" in ln:
                k += 1
                Q.append(f"| {k} | What is the number for: {re.sub(r'[|`*]', '', ln).strip()[:100]}? | Unbaselined ({name}) | {TBD} | how and when it will be baselined | {name} | |")
            if re.match(r"\|\s*A-\d+\s*\|", ln):
                k += 1
                cells = [c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
                Q.append(f"| {k} | What if \"{cells[1] if len(cells) > 1 else ln}\" is wrong? | Assumptions | {TBD} | impact and change-control trigger | {name} | |")
    if k == 0:
        Q.append(f"| 1 | {TBD} | | | | | |")
    Path(a.questions).write_text("\n".join(Q) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if a.talk_track and a.check:
        C = check_talk_track(Path(a.talk_track).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), registry, airtime, speakers)
        Path(a.check).write_text("\n".join(C) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"orals: {len(secs)} sections in {a.minutes} min, {len(speakers)} speakers, "
          f"{len(seen)} proposal numbers registered, {k} likely questions -> {a.script}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Orals Dry-Run Rubric

Score each presenter and the team 0–3 per criterion after every dry run. Target before the real session: no criterion below 2; team total ≥ 24/30.

## Team criteria
| # | Criterion | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Timing | >20% over or under | 10–20% off | Within 10% | On time; close delivered in full |
| T2 | Evaluation coverage | Criteria missed | Some covered | All covered | All covered with a proof each, in the evaluators' terms |
| T3 | Opening and close | Missing or generic | Present, weak | Clear ask | Their situation + outcome + ask; memorable sentence |
| T4 | Handoffs | Confused | Awkward | Clean | Scripted and natural; each speaker's credibility set up |
| T5 | Number discipline | New or contradicting numbers | One slip | Clean | Clean; sources cited aloud where it matters |
| T6 | Q&A answers | Rambling, defensive | Mixed | ≤75 words mostly | Direct, proof, stop; unknowns handled with "we will send by <date>" |
| T7 | Hard three | Avoided or spun | Partial | Honest with mitigation | Honest, concise, mitigation with owner; lands with evaluators |

skills/presales/orals-prep/references/or:
# Orals Method

## 1. Decode the evaluation
| Input | What to extract | If absent |
|---|---|---|
| RFP / invitation | Scored criteria and weights; who scores; format; what may be presented; whether pricing is discussed | `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; ask the client contact; assume the proposal structure |
| Attendee list | Roles → what each cares about (CFO: price, risk; CIO: approach, team; procurement: compliance; operator: day-to-day) | Prepare for the four archetypes |
| Shortlist context | Number of bidders, order of presentation, time between bidders | Assume we are not last; make the close memorable |

Evaluation map: `Criterion (weight) | Slide(s) | Speaker | Proof (number, source) | Risk if challenged`.

## 2. Script structure
| Segment | Share of presenting time | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Opening | ≤90 s | Their situation (their words, one number), the outcome we commit to, what they will hear in the next <n> minutes |
| Understanding and approach | 35% | How we get to the outcome; gates; what we need from them |
| Team and governance | 20% | Who shows up, how decisions get made, continuity commitments |
| Proof | 25% | Win themes with cleared evidence; ghost lines |
| Commercial and risks | 15% | Structure, basis of estimate, top risks with mitigations (price detail only if the format allows) |
| Close | ≤60 s | The ask; next step with date; one sentence they will remember |

Rules:
- Q&A share ≥35% of total time unless the client fixes it. Evaluators remember answers more than slides.
- One speaker per segment; handoffs scripted ("<Name> will take you through how we do that").
- Every number spoken has a source in the proposal. No new numbers in the room.
- Never read slides. The slide holds the evidence; the speaker gives the "so what".

## 3. Speaker assignment
| Role on the engagement | Speaks to | Not to |
|---|---|---|
| Executive sponsor | Opening, commitments, close | Technical detail |
| Engagement lead | Approach, governance, risks, commercial structure | Deep technical |
| Lead architect | Solution, migration approach, NFRs | Pricing |
| Delivery / test lead | Factory, quality, cutover | Strategy |

Credibility rule: the person who will do the work answers questions about the work. If the proposed lead cannot attend, say so and explain who will cover; do not substitute silently.

Airtime: each presenter ≥1 segment; none >40%.

## 4. Answer discipline
| Rule | Practice |
|---|---|
| Length | ≤75 words spoken (~30 seconds). Longer answers lose the room and invite follow-ups into weak ground |
| Structure | Direct answer first → one proof (number + source) → stop. Offer detail: "Happy to go deeper if useful." |
| Unknowns | "We do not have that figure in the room; we will send it by <date>." Never guess |
| Gaps | State the gap and the mitigation. Evaluators have the compliance matrix; spin is detected |
| Competitors | Never named. Consequence language only (ghost lines) |
| Other clients | Only cleared references, in the form cleared (named or anonymized) |
| Contradictions | If an answer would contradict the proposal, the proposal wins; say "as in section <n>" |
| Pricing | Only if the format allows; otherwise "pricing is in the sealed submission; we can walk through the basis of estimate" |
| Hostile question | Acknowledge the concern; answer the underlying criterion; do not debate the premise |

## 5. Delivery rules
| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Arrive with a PDF and an offline copy | Projector/network failures |
| Names and titles of evaluators on a card | Address by name |
| One person tracks time; signals at −5 and −2 minutes | Overruns cut the close |
| Parking lot visible | Questions deferred are captured and answered in writing after |
| Silence after an answer | Do not fill it; let them ask the next question |
| Follow-up within 24 hours | Parked questions, requested figures, thank-you with the one-sentence close |

## 6. Common failure modes
| Failure | Prevention |
|---|---|
| Executive presents technical content poorly | Reassign; credibility over hierarchy |
| Script runs 40% over | Dry run 1 with timer; cut slides, not speaking pace |
| Team disagrees on an answer in the room | Hard-three rehearsal; one owner per question theme |
| New number invented under pressure | Number sheet in front of every presenter; "we will send it" rule |
| Reading the deck | Notes contain the point and the number only; no sentences |
| No close | Script the close; sponsor owns it; practice it three times |
