# Question Bank and Red Team

## 1. Question-generation sources
| Source | Produces |
|---|---|
| Compliance matrix `P`/`N`/`Q` rows | "How will you meet <requirement>?" — one per row |
| Every `[TO BE BASELINED]` in the proposal | "What is the number?" — answer: how and when it will be baselined |
| Every assumption in the estimate | "What if <assumption> is wrong?" |
| Evaluation criteria | One question per criterion from each evaluator archetype |
| Battle card objections | The alternative's strengths as questions |
| Discovery divergent views | "Your proposal assumes X; our operations team says Y" |
| Standard evaluator set (below) | Baseline coverage |

## 2. Standard evaluator questions by theme
### Understanding and approach
| Question | Answer pattern | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| "What is the biggest risk to this program, and what would you do about it?" | Name the top risk from the register, its early signal, the mitigation, the owner | Risk register |
| "Why this phasing? Why not faster?" | Gate logic; what each gate de-risks; what faster would cost in risk | Approach section |
| "What do you need from us, and what happens if we cannot provide it?" | Dependency list with dates; day-for-day consequence; alternatives | Dependencies table |
| "What would make you walk away?" | Honest conditions (access, decision latency); shows judgment | Assumptions |

### Team
| Question | Answer pattern | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| "Will the people in this room be on the engagement?" | Named commitments; continuity clause; what happens on departure | Team section |
| "How much of the work is offshore and how do you manage it?" | Mix by phase; onshore counterparts; overlap hours; security model | Team and governance |
| "What happens if your lead leaves?" | Succession named; knowledge in repo; continuity commitment | Governance |

### Proof
| Question | Answer pattern | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| "Have you done exactly this before?" | Cleared reference with scale and outcome; what was different; what we learned | Why-us |
| "Can we speak to that client?" | Only if cleared-contactable; otherwise anonymized reference and offer written case | Reference register |
| "What went wrong on a similar program?" | One honest example (anonymized), the cause, the change we made | Lessons |

### Commercial and risk
| Question | Answer pattern | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| "Why are you more expensive than <alternative>?" | Basis of estimate (scored inventory, P80 contingency explicit); invite like-for-like; levers with risk effects | Pricing basis |
| "What is not included?" | Exclusions list; why; how handled if needed | Pricing exclusions |
| "What triggers a change request?" | Assumption register; threshold; process | SOW assumptions |
| "Will you share risk / fixed price?" | Which phases fixed, which not, and why (inventory confidence) | Commercial model |

### Technical
| Question | Answer pattern | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| "Why this architecture over <alternative>?" | Options table and scoring; the deciding criterion | ADR-001 |
| "How do you handle cutover and rollback?" | Parallel run, variance tolerance, rollback window, hypercare | Migration method |
| "How do you secure <data class> offshore?" | Residency design, access model, certifications in scope | Security view |
| "What are your NFR commitments?" | Targets with measurement; what is to be baselined with them | NFR table |

### Closing / relationship
| Question | Answer pattern | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| "Why should we choose you?" | Three win themes, one sentence each, with a number | Exec summary |
| "What would you do in the first 30 days?" | Wave 0 / mobilization plan with dates and what they will see | Plan |
| "Is there anything you want to change in your proposal now?" | Only clarifications; no new scope or price; "we stand by it; we would welcome a clarification on <X>" | — |

## 3. Question bank layout
| # | Question | Theme | Likely asker | Answerer | Answer (≤75 words) | Evidence (slide/page) | Do not say | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 4. The hard three
| # | Question | Why it is hard | Honest answer | Mitigation stated | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 5. Red-team protocol
| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| Roles | Skeptical evaluator (challenges every number); incumbent-friendly evaluator (defends the status quo); timekeeper/scorer |
| Rounds | Round 1: scripted bank. Round 2: three unscripted questions per red-teamer. Round 3: interrupt mid-presentation |
| Scoring | `assets/orals-rubric.md` per answer and per presenter |
| Log | Every answer >90 s, every new number, every contradiction, every competitor mention, every uncleared reference |
| Fix list | Owner and date per item; re-run the failed items in the next dry run |

## 6. Red-team log layout
| Dry run | Question | Answerer | Time (s) | Issue (long / new number / contradiction / competitor / uncleared / weak) | Fix | Owner | Re-tested (Y/N) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

skills/presales/proposal-writer/SKILL.md:
---
name: proposal-writer
description: Use when the user asks to write, assemble, structure, or redline a client proposal, RFP response narrative, executive summary, or statement of qualifications — including assembling it from a win-themes.json (themes, proof, so_what) with a discovery pack and estimate memo, wording the outcome claims in a proposal's executive summary, or being asked to "fill in typical numbers so it reads well". Produces an on-template proposal — executive summary, understanding of needs, approach, solution, team, timeline, governance, risks, assumptions, pricing placeholders, why-us — built on win themes and ghosting the competition, with every figure sourced or marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]. In redline mode it keeps the existing storyline and sharpens it section by section. Do not use for compliance matrices (rfp-compliance-matrix), SOWs (sow-drafter), pricing math (effort-estimator), building the ROI/benefits model itself (value-case-builder) or competitor battle cards (competitive-positioning).
license: MIT
metadata:
  domain: presales
  adlc_stage: opportunity
  version: 0.2.0
  author: giri-skills
  agent:
    inputs:
      - {name: win_themes, type: json, required: true, from: "win-themes.json: {client, initiative, themes:[{theme, proof, so_what}]} (layout: evals/fixtures/win-themes.json)"}
      - {name: discovery, type: md, required: false, from: "discovery pack from discovery-interview (pain matrix is quoted into section 2)"}
      - {name: estimate, type: md, required: false, from: "estimate memo from effort-estimator (bottom line is quoted into pricing)"}
      - {name: value_case, type: md, required: false, from: "value-case.md from value-case-builder (bottom line is quoted into objectives)"}
      - {name: existing, type: md, required: false, from: "a proposal draft the team already wrote; redlined against the win themes and inputs (storyline kept), no model step"}
      - {name: draft_only, type: flag, required: false, flag: "--draft-only", from: "true to skip the model sharpen step: the assembled draft becomes proposal-final.md"}

# proposal-writer

## In a conversation: write the proposal now
The reply **is the proposal (or its redline)**, never only a command or a request for files. About 1,000 tokens: tables, one-line section bodies, no preamble.

**Never**
- Never state a benefit percentage or outcome number the user "wants because it reads stronger" or calls "typical" (e.g. "reduce run cost by 40%, recovery time by 75%"). Decline in one line: *outcome numbers must come from the value case (value-case-builder) or the client's own baseline*. Show the outcome table with Baseline and Target `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, and offer the compliant alternative: **state the outcome as a hypothesis, with baselining as a phase-1 deliverable and the measurement method named**. The numbers appear nowhere else in the reply.
- Never fill a slot "with typical numbers": every unfilled slot is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
- Never write "understanding of needs" from imagination; never name the incumbent or competitor in client text (ghost them).
- Never keep a figure in a team draft that no input backs (e.g. an unsourced "40% cost cut") — replace it with an owned marker; keep figures an input backs (e.g. a price the estimate memo states).

**Which reply**
1. **No problem statement / evidence** (e.g. "draft a proposal for a retail client, make it compelling"): ask once, one list — problem statement with evidence (discovery synthesis, RFP or notes), scope/solution outline, estimate output (or confirmation to use pricing placeholders). Write no needs section. Close with: "Once these arrive I start from the win-theme worksheet (`assets/win-theme-worksheet.md`)."
2. **Win-themes file missing** when assembling ("Write the proposal." with only a discovery pack): ask once for **`win-themes.json`** (`{client, initiative, themes:[{theme, proof, so_what}]}`); `scripts/assemble.py` stops (exit 1) without it.
3. **Write** (inputs described or attached), in this order:
   a. **Win-theme worksheet first** (internal): `| # | Client hot button ("quoted" from their evidence, or [quote — discovery §, owner: ___]) | Discriminator | 4 tests: relevance · uniqueness · provability · consequence | Proof (cleared) | Ghost line |`. A theme without proof is cut.
   b. **Executive summary (≤1 page)**: first sentence = the outcome in the client's KPI terms; 3–5 bullets each tied to a theme; what it takes — duration, team and onshore/offshore split copied exactly from the estimate; price `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` unless a price is supplied.
   c. **Sections in `assets/section-library.md` order** (Understanding of your needs · Objectives and success measures · Approach and methodology · Proposed solution · Scope and deliverables · Timeline · Team and governance · Risks and assumptions · Pricing · Why us · Compliance appendix), each heading an assertion, one "so what" line; lists of 3+ items as tables.
   d. **Ghost** the incumbent (e.g. a vendor's services arm) by the capability it lacks, never by name.
   e. **Risks** `| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner |`; **Assumptions** `| Assumption | Consequence if false (change-control trigger) |`.
   f. **Submission checklist — internal, do not ship** (page limit, forms, file naming).
4. **Assemble from files** (win-themes.json ± discovery pack ± estimate memo): name the command and outputs, then show the result:
   `python3 -I scripts/assemble.py win-themes.json --library assets/section-library.md [--discovery …] [--estimate …] --out proposal.md --placeholders placeholders.csv --sources sources.md --final proposal-final.md [--draft-only] [--existing draft.md --redline proposal-redline.md]`.
   - Win themes threaded into the executive summary as T1..Tn and the why-us table; estimate "Bottom line" quoted into Pricing; pain matrix into section 2.
   - **Every `<slot>` not filled by an input is registered** in `placeholders.csv` (placeholder, section, owner) as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Bid manager]`; say so. A thin theme (no proof, no estimate) → its proof, so-what and every number stay markers, listed in placeholders.csv; no numbers invented.
   - `draft_only` / "no model step": **`proposal-final.md` is the assembled draft, labelled "draft — sharpen step not run"; every number traces to `sources.md`.**
5. **Redline an existing draft** (keep our storyline): table `| Section | [KEEP]/[SHARPEN]/[ADD]/[TBD] | Note |` — present sections kept (e.g. team), missing library sections [ADD]ed, the executive summary [SHARPEN]ed for each win theme it lacks (name them), every figure in no input [TBD] and replaced by `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Bid manager]` in proposal-final.md, figures an input backs kept and say which input (e.g. "USD 1,472,000 kept — estimate memo"). Then the sharpened executive summary.

## Starting points
- **New** — win themes (and the discovery pack, estimate memo, value case when you have them) are assembled into a proposal on the section library; the model step sharpens it, or with `draft_only` the assembled draft is final. Every number traces to an input.
- **Existing** — add `existing` (your team's draft): it is redlined against the library and the win themes — sections kept, missing ones added from the inputs, the executive summary sharpened where a theme is missing — and every figure no input backs is replaced by an owned marker in `proposal-final.md` and listed in `proposal-redline.md`.

## When to use
- "Write the proposal for <client> based on the discovery synthesis and estimate."
- "Draft the executive summary and approach sections for the <RFP> response."
- "Redline this proposal draft — keep the story, make it sharper."
- NOT for: requirement inventory (`rfp-compliance-matrix`), contract terms (`sow-drafter`), effort numbers (`effort-estimator`), deck rework (`exec-deck-redline`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Mode: `write` or `redline` | yes | user |
| Problem statement with evidence (discovery synthesis, RFP, or user notes) | yes | file |
| Scope and solution outline (architecture doc or user description) | yes | file / user |
| Estimate output (effort, team, duration) or "pricing placeholders" | yes | file / user |
| Client format constraints (page limit, mandated sections, forms) | no | RFP / user |
| Competitive context (incumbent, likely bidders) | no | user / competitive-positioning |
| Existing draft (redline mode) | yes in redline | file |
| Reference projects we are cleared to name | no | user |

If the problem statement or scope is missing, ask once. Do not write an "understanding of needs" from imagination.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. The redline convention in quality-bar.md governs redline mode.

### Mode A — write
1. **Build the win-theme worksheet** (`assets/win-theme-worksheet.md`) before any prose. For each of 3–4 themes: client hot button (quoted from their evidence) → our discriminator → proof (named, cleared) → ghost (what the alternative cannot do, stated without naming them). A theme without proof is cut. See `references/win-themes-and-ghosting.md`.
2. **Decision point — proposal shape.** Choose per `references/proposal-method.md` §1: Assessment (short, fixed-fee, decision-oriented), Delivery (phased, milestone-priced), Managed service (SLA-led, run-rate priced), or Hybrid. The shape sets section emphasis and the pricing structure placeholder.
3. **Write the executive summary last, but outline it first**: ≤1 page, four moves — their situation in their numbers, the outcome we commit to, how (three to five bullets, each tied to a win theme), what it takes (duration, team shape, price placeholder). No company history, no "we are pleased to submit".
4. **Draft sections from `assets/section-library.md`** in the client's mandated order if one exists; otherwise the library order. Each section opens with its "so what" sentence. Pull evidence verbatim from the discovery synthesis; cite RFP clause IDs where the client gave them. Compliance-driven responses: every mandatory requirement is answered where the compliance matrix points, using the "requirement → response → evidence" micro-structure.
5. **Numbers discipline.** Effort, duration, team, and price come only from the estimate file. Benefits come only from `value-case-builder` output or client statements. Anything else is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never round a placeholder into a number to "make it read better".
6. **Risks and assumptions**: use the registers in `references/proposal-method.md` §4. Every risk has likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner. Every assumption states what changes if it fails (it becomes a change-control trigger in the SOW).
7. **Team section**: roles, responsibilities, allocation, onshore/offshore split from the estimate. Named individuals only if the user supplies them. No biographies of the author or of people not confirmed for the engagement.
8. **Why-us and proof**: only cleared references, with the client's permission status noted internally. Ghost competitors via the win themes, never by naming them in the document.
9. **Compliance and format pass**: page limits, fonts, forms, signature pages, file naming from the RFP. Build the submission checklist.

### Mode B — redline
1. Read the whole draft once. Write the storyline as it stands in five bullets. If it holds, keep it; the job is to sharpen.
2. Redline every section with `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]` and a reason. `[SHARPEN]` includes the rewritten text. Headings become assertions. Remove banned words. Convert prose lists of 3+ items to tables.
3. Check every number against its source; unsourced numbers become `[TBD — owner]` with a note on where the source should come from.
4. Deliver the redline table and the clean rewritten version.

### Both modes
10. Run the self-check. Strip anything that references other clients without clearance, internal rates, or the author's own history.

## Output
| Mode | File | Format |
|---|---|---|
| write | `proposal-<client>-<initiative>-v0.1.md` | Sections per `assets/section-library.md`; win-theme worksheet in an internal appendix (not shipped); submission checklist |
| redline | `proposal-<client>-redline-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` | Redline table (section · verdict · reason · rewritten text) followed by the clean v+1 draft |

## Self-check
- [ ] Executive summary ≤1 page; first sentence states the outcome in the client's terms
- [ ] Every win theme has quoted hot button, discriminator, proof, ghost
- [ ] Every number traceable to estimate, value case, or client evidence; else `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Mandatory RFP requirements each answered where the compliance matrix points
- [ ] Risks: likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner. Assumptions: consequence if false
- [ ] No banned words; headings are assertions; 3+ items are tables
- [ ] No other-client specifics without clearance; no author résumé content
- [ ] Format constraints met; submission checklist complete

## References
- `references/proposal-method.md` — proposal shapes, section intent, evidence rules, risk/assumption registers, review gates
- `references/win-themes-and-ghosting.md` — theme construction, discriminator tests, ghosting rules, proof standards
- `assets/section-library.md` — section-by-section templates with "so what" openers
- `assets/win-theme-worksheet.md` — worksheet

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/proposal-writer --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/proposal-writer`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`proposal.md`, `placeholders.csv`, `sources.md`, `proposal-final.md`, `proposal-redline.md`).

skills/presales/proposal-writer/referenc:
# Proposal Method

## 1. Proposal shapes
| Shape | When | Emphasis | Pricing structure placeholder | Typical length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Assessment | Client needs a decision (migrate? which platform? how much?) before committing | Method, deliverables, decision criteria, speed | Fixed fee; `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` | 8–12 pages |
| Delivery | Scope is known; client wants it built or migrated | Approach, phases, team, quality, risk | Phase or milestone pricing; T&M with cap or fixed by wave | 20–40 pages |
| Managed service | Client wants run responsibility transferred | SLAs, operating model, transition, continuous improvement | Monthly run-rate with tiers; transition fee | 20–30 pages |
| Hybrid (assess → deliver → run) | Large modernization with unknowns | Gated phases; exit criteria per gate | Fixed assessment + estimated delivery range + indicative run-rate | 30–50 pages |

Decision rule: if discovery left the gaps list with volumes unknown, the first phase is an assessment regardless of what the client asked for. Price the assessment firmly and the rest as a range with named drivers.

## 2. Section intent (what each must achieve)
| Section | Must achieve | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| Executive summary | Decision-maker can approve from this page alone | Starts with our history; no numbers; longer than a page |
| Understanding of needs | Client reads it and says "they listened" | Paraphrases the RFP back; no quotes, no numbers, no consequence |
| Objectives and success measures | Agreed definition of done | Vague outcomes ("improved efficiency") with no metric or baseline owner |
| Approach and methodology | Client sees the path and the gates | Generic methodology slide; no decision points; no exit criteria |
| Solution | Technical credibility for the architect reviewer | Product pitch; no fit to their estate; no NFRs |
| Scope and deliverables | No ambiguity about what is in and out | Deliverables without acceptance criteria; out-of-scope list missing |
| Timeline | Dates the client can plan around | Gantt without dependencies on the client; no freeze windows |
| Team and governance | Confidence the right people show up and decisions get made | Org chart without allocation percentages; escalation path missing |
| Risks and assumptions | Honest; every assumption a change-control trigger | Boilerplate risks; assumptions hidden in footnotes |
| Pricing | Clear structure, clear basis, clear exclusions | Numbers without basis; unclear what triggers change |
| Why us / proof | Evidence for each win theme | Logo wall; uncleared references; claims without numbers |
| Compliance appendix | Every mandatory requirement answered | Cross-references that do not resolve |

## 3. Evidence rules
| Claim type | Acceptable evidence | Not acceptable |
|---|---|---|
| Client situation | Their words (discovery quotes), their documents, their filings | Our assumption about their pain |
| Outcome commitment | Value case with sourced baseline; or outcome stated as hypothesis with baselining as phase-1 deliverable | Invented percentage improvement |
| Our capability | Cleared reference with outcome numbers; certification with scope; product feature | "Extensive experience"; uncleared client names |
| Effort/price | Estimate output (P50/P80), rate card | Round numbers chosen to look good |
| Timeline | Estimate critical path + client dependency dates | Dates picked to match the RFP without checking feasibility |

Reference clearance states: `cleared-named` · `cleared-anonymized` · `not-cleared`. Only the first two may appear; the matrix is internal.

## 4. Registers
### Risk register
| ID | Risk | Likelihood (H/M/L) | Impact (H/M/L) | Mitigation | Owner (ours / client) | Trigger / early signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Minimum coverage: client-side availability, data quality, environment access, third-party vendor dependency, scope growth, key-person, security/compliance approvals, cutover windows.

### Assumption register
| ID | Assumption | Basis (source) | If false → consequence | Change-control trigger (Y/N) | Owner to confirm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Every quantity in the estimate (interface count, user count, environments, sites) is an assumption row.

## 5. Review gates
| Gate | When | Reviewer | Pass criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pink (storyline) | After win themes and exec-summary outline | Pursuit lead | Themes proven; shape chosen; exec summary outline approved |
| Red (draft) | Full draft | Independent reviewer not on the writing team | Scores each section against §2; every number sourced; compliance cross-refs resolve |
| Gold (final) | After pricing and legal | Partner / sponsor | Price-to-win check; risk register signed; format compliance; submission checklist complete |

Red-team scoring per section (0–3): 0 missing · 1 generic · 2 specific but unproven · 3 specific, proven, in client's terms. Sections at ≤1 go back to the author.

## 6. Writing rules specific to proposals
- Client's name appears more often than ours. Count it.
- Each section opens with the "so what" for the evaluator, then the detail.
- Mirror the client's terminology (their program names, their KPI names, their org names). Do not rename their initiatives.
- Benefits precede features. "Cuts term-start incident recovery from days to hours by …" not "We use event-driven architecture".
- Active voice, present tense for approach, future tense for commitments.
- Avoid "we understand that" openers; state the fact and cite its source.
- Length: shorter beats longer at equal evidence. Evaluators score, they do not read.

# Win Themes and Ghosting

## 1. What a win theme is
A win theme is a client benefit, tied to something they care about, that we can prove and the alternative cannot match. Three to four per proposal. Each one appears in the executive summary, is developed in one or more sections, and is proven in the why-us section.

| Element | Test | Example (illustrative only) |
|---|---|---|
| Hot button | Quoted or cited from client evidence (discovery, RFP, filing). If we cannot quote it, it is our hot button, not theirs | "We re-key every order over $50k by hand." — VP Ops |
| Discriminator | Something we do that the alternative does not, or does worse, and that the client would value | Migration factory with automated interface conversion and parallel-run harness |
| Proof | Cleared reference with an outcome number; certification; demonstrable asset | Reference R-07 (cleared-anonymized): 240 interfaces migrated in 11 months, zero P1 incidents in parallel run |
| Ghost | The weakness of the alternative, stated as a client risk without naming anyone | "Approaches that migrate interface by interface without a parallel-run harness carry cutover risk into peak season." |

## 2. Discriminator tests
Apply all four. A discriminator failing any one is a feature, not a theme.
| Test | Question |
|---|---|
| Relevance | Does it map to a hot button the client stated? |
| Uniqueness | Can the incumbent or likely competitors say the same sentence? If yes, it is table stakes |
| Provability | Do we have a cleared proof point with a number? |
| Consequence | Can we state what the client loses without it, in their terms? |

Common false discriminators: "experienced team", "proven methodology", "customer-centric", "partnership approach", "global delivery". Every bidder claims them.

## 3. Ghosting rules
Ghosting sets evaluation criteria that favor us by raising the client's attention to risks the alternative carries.
| Do | Do not |
|---|---|
| State the risk as a general truth about approaches | Name the competitor or their product |
| Tie it to the client's own stated consequence | Invent a consequence they did not state |
| Follow immediately with how we remove the risk | Leave the ghost hanging as fear |
| Use in exec summary, approach, and risk sections | Use in the pricing section (reads as excuse) |

Ghost patterns by situation:
| Situation | Ghost line pattern |
|---|---|
| Incumbent with long tenure | "Continuity has value; it also carries the cost of the current run-rate and the assumptions built into it. The approach should include a baseline the client can audit." |
| Larger competitor | "Programs staffed from a bench rather than from the proposed team see leadership change mid-flight. Named leads and continuity commitments reduce that." |
| Cheaper competitor | "Estimates built without an interface inventory and complexity scoring tend to grow after award. We price from a scored inventory and state the drivers." |
| Product vendor bidding services | "A platform vendor's services team optimizes for platform adoption. An independent team optimizes for the client's outcome across platforms." |

## 4. Proof standards
| Proof type | Minimum content | Clearance |
|---|---|---|
| Reference project | Scope shape, scale numbers, outcome numbers, duration, role we played | Named or anonymized per client agreement; stored in the internal reference register |
| Certification | Standard, scope, issuing body, expiry | Public |
| Asset / accelerator | What it does, measurable effect (time, defects, cost), where it was used | Internal; outcome number cleared |
| Team credential | Role-relevant certifications and years; no personal narrative | Individual's consent for named use |

No proof → no theme. Drop it or downgrade it to a supporting claim without a proof line.

## 5. Theme-to-section map
| Theme | Exec summary bullet | Developed in | Proven in | Ghost placed in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | | | | |
| T2 | | | | |
| T3 | | | | |

Fill before drafting. Themes that do not land in at least two sections are too weak to carry.

# rfp-compliance-matrix

## In a conversation: build the matrix now
- **The request carries the RFP and the capability source** — including when the RFP PDF and catalog are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: produce the bid review **in this reply** from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
  1. **Bid call on line 1** — `BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID` (provisional where the gate tests are open) with its three drivers.
  2. **Requirement inventory** — apply `scripts/extract_requirements.py`'s rules by hand: numbered clauses and shall/must/required sentences, wrapped lines merged, boilerplate moved to Administrative, items from tables and appendices added, client IDs kept with our `REQ-nnn` alongside.
  3. **Classification** — every requirement by category (`FUN TEC SEC COM DEL ADM`) and `M/D/O` per `references/requirement-taxonomy.md`; hidden mandatories flagged.
  4. **Compliance matrix** in the column order of `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` (`req_id, client_id, section, page, text, category, mdo, weight, flags, compliance, evidence, gap_condition, mitigation, owner, response_section, status, clarification_id`). No `C` without an evidence citation from the capability catalog; no evidence → `P` or `Q`.
  5. **Gaps and risks** — every `P`/`N` with mitigation, risk if unmitigated and owner.
  6. **Clarification questions** — one per item, neutral, citing the clause ID, revealing no gap.
  7. **Deadlines** (Q&A, submission) with the RFP page, or page `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` · **Response plan** (section, owner, due).
  Rows the request cannot fill show `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; end with the few questions that close them.
- **No RFP at all**: ask once for the document. **No capability source**: ask once for the capability statement or service catalog, and still produce the requirement inventory and taxonomy classification now; if the user declines, mark every compliance cell `Q` with `owner: ___` rather than guessing `C`.
- **Asked to mark items Comply without evidence** ("we are basically SOC 2 ready, ISO 27001 next quarter", "no partials in front of the client"): say in one line that `C` requires current, in-scope certification evidence. Score those requirements `P` with mitigation `roadmap` and the expected date `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` (never the hoped-for date); flag the mandatory items in gaps-and-risks with an owner; offer client-facing wording that presents the roadmap commitment without misrepresenting current status.

## Starting points
- **New** — the RFP is split into requirements, each scored against your capability inventory (C/P/Q with evidence and owner), with mandatory gaps, clarification questions and a provisional bid gate.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (your reviewed matrix from the last round): unchanged clauses keep their reviewed answer, changed clauses are re-scored and flagged for re-review, new clauses are flagged, and withdrawn ones are listed to drop from the response.

## When to use
- "We received an RFP from <client>; break it down."
- "Build the compliance matrix for this RFI."
- "Should we bid on this?"
- "What clarification questions do we send before the deadline?"
- NOT for: proposal prose (`proposal-writer`), pricing (`effort-estimator`), SOW (`sow-drafter`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| RFP document(s): .pdf / .docx / .md / .txt, including appendices | yes | file |
| Submission deadline, Q&A deadline, format rules (page limits, forms) | yes (extract or ask) | document / user |
| Our capability statement or service catalog (what we can claim) | yes | file / user |
| Named owners for response sections (or "assign later") | no | user |
| Known incumbent / competitive context | no | user |

If the RFP file is missing, ask once. If the capability source is missing, ask once and still produce the inventory and classification; if it stays missing, mark every compliance cell `Q` (Clarify) with `owner: ___` rather than guessing what we comply with. Missing deadlines or owners do not stop the matrix: they are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Extract the requirement inventory.** Run `python3 -I scripts/extract_requirements.py <rfp-file> --out requirements.csv`. The script captures numbered clauses (1.2.3, (a), R-014), and sentences with shall / must / required / will provide, with section context and page. Review the CSV: merge split sentences, drop boilerplate (definitions, instructions to bidders go in a separate "Administrative" category), and add any requirements the script missed from tables and appendices. Never renumber the client's IDs; add our `REQ-nnn` alongside.
2. **Classify every requirement** using `references/requirement-taxonomy.md`: Category (Functional / Technical / Security-Compliance / Commercial / Delivery-PM / Administrative), Mandatory vs Desirable (per RFP wording), and Evaluation weight if the RFP states scoring. Flag "hidden mandatories" — requirements phrased softly but located in pass/fail sections.
3. **Score compliance** per `references/compliance-scoring.md`: `C` Comply · `P` Partial · `N` Non-comply · `Q` Clarify. The rule: `C` requires evidence we can cite (project, certification, product feature, named capability in our catalog). No evidence → `P` or `Q`, never `C`. Each row gets an owner and the proposal section that will carry the response.
4. **Decision point — bid/no-bid.** Apply the gate in `references/compliance-scoring.md` §3: any `N` on a mandatory is a hard stop unless a clarification can convert it; compute `C` share on mandatories; check deadline feasibility against the response effort (count of sections × owners available). Output `BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID` with the three facts that drove it. Do not soften a NO-BID.
5. **Draft clarification questions** for every `Q`, ambiguous mandatory, and scoring-rule gap. Use the question format in `references/compliance-scoring.md` §4: neutral wording, no capability reveal, one question per item, reference the clause ID. Group by theme; cap at the count the RFP allows.
6. **Build the gaps-and-risks list**: every `P` and `N` with the mitigation (partner, roadmap commitment, alternative approach, exception request) and the risk if unmitigated.
7. **Assemble the matrix** on `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` (column spec) — export as CSV/XLSX for the response team, plus a Markdown summary for the bid review. Totals by category and by compliance level must reconcile with the inventory count.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Requirement inventory | `rfp-<client>-requirements.csv` | Script output, reviewed |
| Compliance matrix | `rfp-<client>-compliance-matrix.csv` (or `.xlsx` if openpyxl available) | Columns per `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` |
| Bid review summary | `rfp-<client>-bid-review.md` | Bottom line (BID call) · Totals table · Mandatory non-compliances · Gaps and risks · Clarification questions · Response plan (section, owner, due) · Administrative checklist |

## Self-check
- [ ] Inventory count = matrix row count; totals by category reconcile
- [ ] No `C` without a cited evidence item
- [ ] Every mandatory `N` or `P` appears in gaps-and-risks with a mitigation and owner
- [ ] Clarification questions reference clause IDs and reveal no capability gaps
- [ ] Bid/no-bid call on line 1 of the summary with its three drivers
- [ ] Deadlines (Q&A, submission) stated with source page
- [ ] No other-client names or internal rate information in any artifact that could ship

## References
- `references/requirement-taxonomy.md` — categories, mandatory detection, hidden-mandatory patterns, evaluation weighting
- `references/compliance-scoring.md` — C/P/N/Q rules, evidence standard, bid/no-bid gate, clarification-question format
- `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` — column specification for CSV/XLSX
- `scripts/extract_requirements.py` — .txt/.md/.docx/.pdf → requirements CSV

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/rfp-compliance-matrix --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/rfp-compliance-matrix`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract numbered and obligation-bearing requirements from an RFP into CSV.

Supports .txt, .md, .docx (python-docx if installed), and .pdf (pypdf if
installed). When an optional library is missing, the script says so and exits
with code 3 rather than failing silently. No network access is used.

Detection:
  * Numbered clauses:  1.2.3 / 4.3 / R-014 / REQ 12 / (a) / (ii) / A.1
  * Obligation words:  shall, must, is required to, required, will provide,
                       mandatory, should, expected to, preferred  (M/D classification)
  * Tables in .docx are read row by row; the first cell is used as the client ID
    when it looks like an identifier.

Output columns (match assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md, cols 1-9 subset):
  req_id, client_id, section, page, text, mdo_hint, keyword, source_file

Usage:
    python3 -I extract_requirements.py rfp.pdf --out requirements.csv
    python3 -I extract_requirements.py rfp.docx appendix-b.docx --out reqs.csv --min-words 4
    python3 -I extract_requirements.py rfp.md --dry-run

Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 file not found/unsupported; 3 missing optional library.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

CLAUSE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:"
    r"(?P<num>\d+(?:\.\d+){0,4})[.)]?\s+"          # 1.2.3 or 4.3
    r"|(?P<req>(?:REQ|R|FR|NFR|TR|SR)[-\s]?\d+[A-Za-z]?)[:.)]?\s+"  # R-014, REQ 12
    r"|\((?P<alpha>[a-z]{1,2}|[ivx]{1,5})\)\s+"      # (a) (ii)
    r"|(?P<letnum>[A-Z]\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*)[.)]?\s+"     # A.1.2
    r")"
)
HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)*[.)]?\s+)?([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 ,&/()-]{3,80})\s*$")
MANDATORY_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required to|are required to|required|will provide|mandatory|minimum requirement)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
DESIRABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(should|expected to|preferred|desirable|where possible|advantageous)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)
OPTIONAL_RE = re.compile(r"\b(may|optional|nice to have|could)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
BOILERPLATE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(table of contents|page \d+|confidential|copyright|all rights reserved)", re.IGNORECASE
)


@dataclass
class Req:
    client_id: str
    section: str
    page: str
    text: str
    mdo_hint: str
    keyword: str
    source_file: str


def read_txt(path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return list of (page_label, text) blocks. Plain text has one block."""
    return [("1", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))]


def read_docx(path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    try:
        import docx  # type: ignore
    except ImportError:
        print("error: python-docx not installed; convert the .docx to .txt or install python-docx", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(3)
    d = docx.Document(str(path))
    lines: list[str] = []
    for para in d.paragraphs:
        t = para.text.strip()
        if t:
            style = (para.style.name or "").lower() if para.style is not None else ""
            lines.append(("## " + t) if style.startswith("heading") else t)
    for ti, table in enumerate(d.tables, start=1):
        for row in table.rows:
            cells = [c.text.strip() for c in row.cells]
            cells = [c for c in cells if c]
            if not cells:
                continue
            if len(cells) >= 2 and re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]{0,4}[-\s]?\d+(\.\d+)*[A-Za-z]?$", cells[0]):
                lines.append(f"{cells[0]} {' '.join(cells[1:])}")
            else:
                lines.append(" ".join(cells))
    return [("docx", "\n".join(lines))]


def read_pdf(path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    try:
        from pypdf import PdfReader  # type: ignore
    except ImportError:
        print("error: pypdf not installed; export the PDF to text or install pypdf", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(3)
    reader = PdfReader(str(path))
    blocks: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages, start=1):
        try:
            txt = page.extract_text() or ""
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - report and continue
            txt = ""
            print(f"warning: page {i} text extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        blocks.append((str(i), txt))
    if not any(t.strip() for _, t in blocks):
        print("warning: no extractable text (scanned PDF?). OCR is out of scope for this script.", file=sys.stderr)
    return blocks


READERS = {".txt": read_txt, ".md": read_txt, ".docx": read_docx, ".pdf": read_pdf}


def mdo_hint(text: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    m = MANDATORY_RE.search(text)
    if m:
        return "M", m.group(1).lower()
    m = DESIRABLE_RE.search(text)
    if m:
        return "D", m.group(1).lower()
    m = OPTIONAL_RE.search(text)
    if m:
        return "O", m.group(1).lower()
    return "", ""


def join_wrapped_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Merge PDF-wrapped lines into sentences: a line that does not end a sentence
    and whose successor does not start a clause is appended to the previous line."""
    out: list[str] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip()
        if not line.strip():
            out.append("")
            continue
        if out and out[-1] and not re.search(r"[.;:]\s*$", out[-1]) and not CLAUSE_RE.match(line) \
                and not line.startswith("## ") and not HEADING_RE.match(line):
            out[-1] = out[-1] + " " + line.strip()
        else:
            out.append(line)
    return out


def extract(blocks: list[tuple[str, str]], source: str, min_words: int, numbered_only: bool) -> list[Req]:
    reqs: list[Req] = []
    section = ""
    for page, text in blocks:
        for line in join_wrapped_lines(text):
            s = line.strip()
            if not s or BOILERPLATE_RE.match(s):
                continue
            if s.startswith("## "):
                section = s[3:].strip()
                continue
            cm = CLAUSE_RE.match(s)
            client_id = ""
            body = s
            if cm:
                client_id = next(g for g in (cm.group("num"), cm.group("req"), cm.group("alpha"), cm.group("letnum")) if g)
                body = s[cm.end():].strip()
                # A short numbered line with no obligation word is a heading, not a requirement.
                if len(body.split()) <= 8 and not MANDATORY_RE.search(body) and not DESIRABLE_RE.search(body):
                    section = f"{client_id} {body}"
                    continue
            elif HEADING_RE.match(s) and len(s.split()) <= 10 and not MANDATORY_RE.search(s):
                section = s
                continue
            hint, kw = mdo_hint(body)
            if numbered_only and not client_id:
                continue
            if not client_id and not hint:
                continue
            if len(body.split()) < min_words:
                continue
            reqs.append(Req(client_id, section, page, body, hint, kw, source))
    return reqs


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("files", nargs="+", help="RFP files (.txt .md .docx .pdf)")
    p.add_argument("--out", default="requirements.csv", help="Output CSV path")
    p.add_argument("--min-words", type=int, default=5, help="Ignore candidate lines shorter than this")
    p.add_argument("--numbered-only", action="store_true", help="Keep only lines with a clause identifier")
    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Print summary; do not write CSV")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)

    all_reqs: list[Req] = []
    for f in args.files:
        path = Path(f)
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"error: file not found: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        reader = READERS.get(path.suffix.lower())
        if reader is None:
            print(f"error: unsupported file type: {path.suffix} (use .txt .md .docx .pdf)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        blocks = reader(path)
        all_reqs.extend(extract(blocks, path.name, args.min_words, args.numbered_only))

    # De-duplicate exact text repeats (headers/footers repeated per page)
    seen: set[str] = set()
    unique: list[Req] = []
    for r in all_reqs:
        key = r.text.lower()
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        unique.append(r)

    m = sum(1 for r in unique if r.mdo_hint == "M")
    d = sum(1 for r in unique if r.mdo_hint == "D")
    o = sum(1 for r in unique if r.mdo_hint == "O")
    print(f"candidates: {len(unique)}  (M={m} D={d} O={o} unclassified={len(unique)-m-d-o})", file=sys.stderr)

    if args.dry_run:
        for i, r in enumerate(unique[:25], start=1):
            print(f"REQ-{i:03d} | {r.client_id or '-'} | {r.mdo_hint or '-'} | {r.text[:90]}")
        if len(unique) > 25:
            print(f"... {len(unique) - 25} more")
        return 0

    with open(args.out, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh)
        w.writerow(["req_id", "client_id", "section", "page", "text", "mdo_hint", "keyword", "source_file"])
        for i, r in enumerate(unique, start=1):
            w.writerow([f"REQ-{i:03d}", r.client_id, r.section, r.page, r.text, r.mdo_hint, r.keyword, r.source_file])
    print(f"wrote {args.out} ({len(unique)} rows). Review: merge split sentences, drop boilerplate, add table/appendix items.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score an extracted requirements CSV against a capability inventory -> compliance matrix.

Inputs
  requirements CSV (from extract_requirements.py; columns used):
    req_id, client_id, section, page, text, mdo_hint [, keyword, source_file]
  capabilities CSV (our inventory; one row per capability):
    capability_id, keywords, status, evidence, owner [, gap_condition, mitigation, category]
      keywords  : `||`-separated words/phrases matched against the requirement text
      status    : C (comply) or P (partial). A `C` with empty evidence is downgraded to P
                  (references/compliance-scoring.md §1). N is never produced by this script:
                  an unmatched requirement is Q (clarify) with a CQ id, so a human decides.
      owner     : named person who answers for this capability

Outputs
  --out matrix.csv   17 columns per assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md
  --gaps gaps.md     bottom line, mandatory gaps, clarification questions, bid gate
  --summary x.json   counts, mandatory C share, bid gate verdict and the open gate tests

Bid gate (references/compliance-scoring.md §3), computed only for the tests this script can
see: mandatory N count (always 0 here), mandatory C share, Q count. The other gate tests
(hidden mandatories, deadline feasibility, weighting, incumbent, strategic fit) are reported
as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: bid manager]`; the verdict is therefore "provisional".

Usage:
    python3 -I score_matrix.py requirements.csv --capabilities caps.csv \
        --out matrix.csv --gaps gaps.md --summary bid-score.json [--min-overlap 0.5]

Existing matrix (--previous matrix.csv from the earlier round, e.g. before an addendum): a requirement
with the same clause (client_id, else req_id) and the same text keeps the reviewed answer — compliance,
evidence, gap, mitigation, owner, response section and status — flagged `carried`; a clause whose text
changed is re-scored and flagged `changed (was <C/P/N/Q>)`; a clause not in the previous matrix is
flagged `new`; previous clauses no longer in the RFP are listed as withdrawn. gaps.md gains "Changes
since the previous matrix". Rows whose req_id starts with `#` are notes and are skipped.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bad input (missing file, missing columns, no rows). Stdlib only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MATRIX_COLS = ["req_id", "client_id", "section", "page", "text", "category", "mdo", "weight",
               "flags", "compliance", "evidence", "gap_condition", "mitigation", "owner",
               "response_section", "status", "clarification_id"]
REQ_COLS = {"req_id", "text"}
CAP_COLS = {"capability_id", "keywords", "status", "owner"}
TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: bid manager]"
WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+\-/.]*")


def read_csv(path: Path, required: set[str], label: str) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"error: {label} not found: {path}")
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    if not rows:
        sys.exit(f"error: {label} has no rows: {path}")
    missing = required - set(rows[0].keys())
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"error: {label} missing columns: {sorted(missing)}")
    return rows


def tokens(text: str) -> set[str]:
    return set(WORD_RE.findall(text.lower()))


def match(req_text: str, caps: list[dict], min_overlap: float):
    """Best capability by share of its keyword phrases found in the requirement."""
    rt = req_text.lower()
    rtoks = tokens(req_text)
    best, best_score = None, 0.0
    for cap in caps:
        kws = [k.strip().lower() for k in cap.get("keywords", "").split("||") if k.strip()]
        if not kws:
            continue
        hits = 0
        for kw in kws:
            if " " in kw:
                hits += kw in rt
            else:
                hits += kw in rtoks
        score = hits / len(kws)
        if score > best_score:
            best, best_score = cap, score
    if best is not None and best_score >= min_overlap:
        return best, best_score
    return None, best_score


def mdo_of(row: dict) -> str:
    v = (row.get("mdo_hint") or row.get("mdo") or "").strip().upper()[:1]
    return v if v in ("M", "D", "O") else "D"


def score(reqs: list[dict], caps: list[dict], min_overlap: float):
    matrix, cq_n = [], 0
    for r in reqs:
        cap, s = match(r.get("text", ""), caps, min_overlap)
        row = {c: "" for c in MATRIX_COLS}
        row.update({k: r.get(k, "") for k in ("req_id", "client_id", "section", "page", "text")})
        row["mdo"] = mdo_of(r)
        row["weight"] = r.get("weight") or TBD
        row["status"] = "drafted"
        if cap is None:
            cq_n += 1
            row["compliance"] = "Q"
            row["clarification_id"] = f"CQ-{cq_n:03d}"
            row["gap_condition"] = "no matching capability in inventory — confirm scope and intent"
            row["owner"] = TBD
            row["flags"] = "UNQ" if not re.search(r"\d", r.get("text", "")) else ""
        else:
            status = (cap.get("status") or "P").strip().upper()[:1]
            evidence = (cap.get("evidence") or "").strip()
            if status == "C" and not evidence:
                status = "P"
                row["gap_condition"] = "evidence not cited — C downgraded to P (scoring §1)"
            if status not in ("C", "P"):
                status = "P"
            row["compliance"] = status
            row["evidence"] = evidence
            row["owner"] = cap.get("owner") or TBD
            row["category"] = cap.get("category", "")
            if status == "P":
                row["gap_condition"] = row["gap_condition"] or cap.get("gap_condition") or TBD
                row["mitigation"] = cap.get("mitigation") or TBD
            row["flags"] = f"match={s:.2f}"
        matrix.append(row)
    return matrix


CARRY = ("compliance", "evidence", "gap_condition", "mitigation", "owner", "response_section", "status",
         "clarification_id", "category")


def _clause(r: dict) -> str:
    return (r.get("client_id") or r.get("req_id") or "").strip()


def _norm(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(WORD_RE.findall((text or "").lower()))


def apply_previous(matrix: list[dict], prev: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Carry reviewed answers for unchanged clauses; flag changed/new; return the change summary."""
    before = {_clause(r): r for r in prev if _clause(r) and not (r.get("req_id") or "").startswith("#")}
    seen, changes = set(), {"carried": [], "changed": [], "new": [], "withdrawn": []}
    for row in matrix:
        key = _clause(row)
        old = before.get(key)
        if old is None:
            row["flags"] = (row["flags"] + "; " if row["flags"] else "") + "new"
            changes["new"].append(key)
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        if _norm(old.get("text", "")) == _norm(row["text"]):
            for c in CARRY:
                if c in ("owner", "category"):            # keep the inventory's value when the old cell is blank
                    if (old.get(c) or "").strip():
                        row[c] = old[c].strip()
                elif c in old:                            # the reviewed answer wins, blanks included (a resolved Q has no CQ)
                    row[c] = (old.get(c) or "").strip()
            if row["compliance"] != "Q":
                row["clarification_id"] = ""              # an answered clarification no longer needs a CQ
            row["flags"] = "carried"
            changes["carried"].append(key)
        else:
            row["flags"] = (row["flags"] + "; " if row["flags"] else "") + f"changed (was {old.get('compliance', '?')})"
            changes["changed"].append((key, old.get("compliance", "?"), row["compliance"]))
    changes["withdrawn"] = [(k, r.get("text", "")) for k, r in before.items() if k not in seen]
    return changes


def render_changes(ch: dict) -> list[str]:
    L = ["", "## Changes since the previous matrix",
         f"{len(ch['carried'])} carried with their reviewed answer · {len(ch['changed'])} changed · "
         f"{len(ch['new'])} new · {len(ch['withdrawn'])} withdrawn.", "",
         "| Clause | Change | Detail |", "|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {k} | changed | text differs — re-scored {now} (was {was}); re-review the answer |" for k, was, now in ch["changed"]]
    L += [f"| {k} | new | not in the previous matrix — review the drafted answer |" for k in ch["new"]]
    L += [f"| {k} | withdrawn | {t[:100].replace('|', '/')} — drop it from the response |" for k, t in ch["withdrawn"]]
    if not (ch["changed"] or ch["new"] or ch["withdrawn"]):
        L.append("| — | none | every clause carried |")
    return L


def gate(matrix: list[dict]) -> dict:
    mand = [r for r in matrix if r["mdo"] == "M"]
    m_c = sum(r["compliance"] == "C" for r in mand)
    m_n = sum(r["compliance"] == "N" for r in mand)
    m_q = sum(r["compliance"] == "Q" for r in mand)
    share = (m_c / len(mand)) if mand else None
    if m_n >= 1:
        verdict = "NO-BID"
    elif share is None:
        verdict = "BID-WITH-CONDITIONS"
    elif share >= 0.8 and m_q == 0:
        verdict = "BID"
    elif share >= 0.6:
        verdict = "BID-WITH-CONDITIONS"
    else:
        verdict = "NO-BID"
    return {
        "verdict": verdict + " (provisional)",
        "mandatory_total": len(mand), "mandatory_C": m_c, "mandatory_N": m_n, "mandatory_Q": m_q,
        "mandatory_C_share": round(share, 3) if share is not None else None,
        "open_gate_tests": {k: TBD for k in ("hidden_mandatories", "deadline_feasibility",
                                              "evaluation_weighting", "incumbent_signal",
                                              "strategic_fit")},
    }


def render_gaps(matrix: list[dict], g: dict) -> str:
    counts = {k: sum(r["compliance"] == k for r in matrix) for k in "CPNQ"}
    L = ["# Compliance gaps and bid gate", "",
         "## Bottom line",
         f"**{g['verdict']}** — {len(matrix)} requirements: C {counts['C']} · P {counts['P']} · "
         f"N {counts['N']} · Q {counts['Q']}. Mandatory C share: "
         f"{g['mandatory_C_share'] if g['mandatory_C_share'] is not None else 'n/a (no M rows)'} "
         f"({g['mandatory_C']}/{g['mandatory_total']}).",
         "", "Open gate tests (not computable from the matrix):",
         "| Test | Status |", "|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {k.replace('_', ' ')} | {v} |" for k, v in g["open_gate_tests"].items()]
    L += ["", "## Mandatory gaps", "| req_id | client_id | compliance | gap | mitigation | owner |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    gaps = [r for r in matrix if r["mdo"] == "M" and r["compliance"] in ("P", "N", "Q")]
    L += [f"| {r['req_id']} | {r['client_id']} | {r['compliance']} | {r['gap_condition']} | "
          f"{r['mitigation']} | {r['owner']} |" for r in gaps] or ["| — | | | none | | |"]
    L += ["", "## Clarification questions",
          "| CQ | Clause | Requirement (verbatim) | Why it matters (internal) |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    qs = [r for r in matrix if r["compliance"] == "Q"]
    L += [f"| {r['clarification_id']} | {r['client_id'] or r['req_id']} | "
          f"{r['text'][:120].replace('|', '/')} | {r['gap_condition']} |" for r in qs] or ["| — | | none | |"]
    L += ["", "## Partials (all)", "| req_id | mdo | evidence | gap | owner |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    L += [f"| {r['req_id']} | {r['mdo']} | {r['evidence']} | {r['gap_condition']} | {r['owner']} |"
          for r in matrix if r["compliance"] == "P"] or ["| — | | | none | |"]
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("requirements", type=Path, help="requirements CSV from extract_requirements.py")
    ap.add_argument("--capabilities", type=Path, required=True, help="capability inventory CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True, help="matrix CSV path")
    ap.add_argument("--gaps", type=Path, help="gaps/bid-gate Markdown path")
    ap.add_argument("--summary", type=Path, help="bid score JSON path")
    ap.add_argument("--previous", type=Path, help="matrix.csv from the earlier round (addendum / re-bid)")
    ap.add_argument("--min-overlap", type=float, default=0.5,
                    help="share of a capability's keywords that must hit (default 0.5)")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    reqs = read_csv(a.requirements, REQ_COLS, "requirements CSV")
    caps = read_csv(a.capabilities, CAP_COLS, "capabilities CSV")
    matrix = score(reqs, caps, a.min_overlap)
    changes = apply_previous(matrix, read_csv(a.previous, {"req_id", "text", "compliance"}, "previous matrix")) \
        if a.previous else None
    g = gate(matrix)
    a.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with a.out.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=MATRIX_COLS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(matrix)
    if a.gaps:
        text = render_gaps(matrix, g)
        if changes is not None:
            text = text.rstrip("\n") + "\n" + "\n".join(render_changes(changes)) + "\n"
        a.gaps.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    if a.summary:
        counts = {k: sum(r["compliance"] == k for r in matrix) for k in "CPNQ"}
        summary = {"requirements": len(matrix), "counts": counts, "gate": g}
        if changes is not None:
            summary["changes"] = {k: len(v) for k, v in changes.items()}
        a.summary.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(matrix)} requirements scored -> {a.out}; gate: {g['verdict']}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Compliance Matrix — Column Specification

Use this exact column order for the CSV/XLSX. Columns 1–9 come from the extraction and taxonomy pass; 10–17 from scoring. Freeze header row; filter on every column.

| # | Column | Type | Allowed values / format | Filled by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `req_id` | text | `REQ-001` … sequential, never reused | script |
| 2 | `client_id` | text | RFP clause number verbatim (e.g., `4.3.2`, `R-014`, `(b)(ii)`) | script |
| 3 | `section` | text | RFP section heading | script |
| 4 | `page` | int/text | Page number or location label | script |
| 5 | `text` | text | Verbatim requirement; no paraphrase | script, reviewed |
| 6 | `category` | enum | `FUN` `TEC` `SEC` `COM` `DEL` `ADM` | analyst |
| 7 | `mdo` | enum | `M` `D` `O` | analyst (per taxonomy §2) |
| 8 | `weight` | text | Stated score/percent or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]` | analyst |
| 9 | `flags` | text | Semicolon list from `AMB DUP CON UNQ OOS INC` | analyst |
| 10 | `compliance` | enum | `C` `P` `N` `Q` | owner, reviewed |
| 11 | `evidence` | text | Catalog ref / cert (expiry) / project ref ID / product feature. Required when `C` | owner |
| 12 | `gap_condition` | text | Required when `P` or `N` | owner |
| 13 | `mitigation` | enum+text | `partner` `roadmap` `custom-build` `exception` `alternative` + note | owner |
| 14 | `owner` | text | Named person | bid manager |
| 15 | `response_section` | text | Proposal section number | bid manager |
| 16 | `status` | enum | `not-started` `drafted` `reviewed` `final` | owner |
| 17 | `clarification_id` | text | `CQ-nnn` when `compliance = Q` or flag `AMB`/`CON`/`UNQ` | analyst |

## Validation rules (apply before bid review)
| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| Completeness | Row count = inventory count |
| Evidence | `compliance = C` ⇒ `evidence` non-empty |
| Gaps | `compliance ∈ {P, N}` ⇒ `gap_condition` and `mitigation` non-empty |
| Clarify | `compliance = Q` ⇒ `clarification_id` non-empty |
| Mandatory N | `mdo = M` and `compliance = N` ⇒ appears in bid review §3 |
| Owner | Every row with `mdo ∈ {M, D}` has an `owner` |

## Summary pivots for the bid review
- Category × Compliance (count)
- Mandatory only: Compliance (count and %)
- Owner × Status (count) — response progress
- Flags (count) — quality of the RFP itself

# Compliance Scoring

## 1. Levels
| Code | Level | Rule | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|---|
| C | Comply | We meet the requirement as written today, with no caveat | Cite one of: a named capability in our catalog, a certification (with expiry), a delivered project of the same shape (internal reference ID only; never the client name in the matrix unless cleared), a product feature |
| P | Partial | We meet part of it, or meet it with a condition, a partner, or a roadmap commitment | State exactly what is met, what is not, and the mitigation |
| N | Non-comply | We do not meet it and no credible mitigation exists within the response window | State why and whether an exception will be requested |
| Q | Clarify | The requirement is ambiguous, conflicting, or depends on information we do not have | Clarification question ID |

Rules that prevent optimistic scoring:
- A `C` with the evidence cell empty is a `P`. The reviewer changes it; the author does not argue.
- "We can build it" is a `P` with mitigation "custom build — estimated in pricing", not a `C`.
- Certifications count only if current and in the correct scope (entity, region, service).
- A partner's capability is `P` until the partner has confirmed in writing; then `C` with the partner named as evidence.
- Commercial terms: `N` on "accept T&Cs without exception" if legal has any redline. Record redlines as the mitigation.

## 2. Row fields added by scoring
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Compliance | C / P / N / Q |
| Evidence | Cited item (catalog ref, cert, project ref, product feature) |
| Gap / condition | For P and N: what is missing |
| Mitigation | Partner · roadmap · custom build · exception request · alternative approach |
| Owner | Named person responsible for the response text |
| Response section | Where in the proposal the answer lives (section number) |
| Status | Not started · Drafted · Reviewed · Final |
| Clarification ID | CQ-nnn for Q rows |

## 3. Bid / no-bid gate
Compute after scoring. State the call on line 1 of the bid review.

| Test | BID | BID-WITH-CONDITIONS | NO-BID |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mandatory `N` count | 0 | 1–2, each with a credible clarification or exception path | ≥1 with no path |
| Mandatory `C` share | ≥ 80% | 60–79% | < 60% |
| Hidden mandatories (qualification thresholds, certifications, T&Cs) | All met | One open, resolvable before Q&A deadline | Any unmet |
| Deadline feasibility | Response effort ≤ 70% of available owner-days | 70–100% | > 100% |
| Evaluation weighting known | Yes | Clarification sent | Unknown and price-dominant with an incumbent |
| Incumbent signal (INC flags) | None or few | Several, wedge identified | RFP reads as written for the incumbent and no wedge |
| Strategic fit (our angle, vertical, reference value) | Strong | Moderate | Weak |

Decision rule: any NO-BID column hit on Mandatory N, Hidden mandatories, or Deadline feasibility → NO-BID. Two or more CONDITIONS → BID-WITH-CONDITIONS, conditions listed with owner and date.

Response effort estimate: `sections × average hours per section (default 6 for narrative, 2 for tabular) + 20% review`. Compare with owner availability stated by the user. If availability is unknown, mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and flag feasibility as unassessed.

## 4. Clarification-question format
Questions are read by the client and often by competitors (answers are typically shared with all bidders). Write accordingly.

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| One question per item, referencing the clause ID | Traceability; forces a specific answer |
| Neutral wording; ask for the client's intent, not confirmation of our approach | Do not reveal gaps or strategy |
| Never ask something answered elsewhere in the RFP | Signals poor reading; wastes a question slot |
| Prefer questions whose answers change scope, price, or compliance | Slots are limited |
| Ask for scoring criteria and weights if absent | Shapes the whole response |
| Ask for volumes and counts whenever a requirement is unquantified | Feeds the estimate |

Template: `CQ-nnn | Clause <id> (p. <n>) | "<Question>" | Why it matters to us (internal) | Scope/price impact (internal)`

Examples of good wording:
- "Clause 4.3.2 references 'all existing integrations'. Can the Authority provide the count and list of integrations in scope, by system?"
- "Section 7 states data must reside in-region. Does this apply to backup and disaster-recovery copies as well as primary storage?"
- "Please confirm whether the evaluation applies weighted scoring, and if so, the relative weights of technical, commercial, and delivery criteria."

Examples of bad wording:
- "Would a solution based on <our platform> be acceptable?" (reveals approach)
- "Is SOC 2 Type I sufficient?" (reveals we lack Type II)

## 5. Bid review summary layout
1. Bottom line: `BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID` + three drivers.
2. Totals: table by category × compliance level; mandatory subset shown separately.
3. Mandatory non-compliances and partials: ID, text, gap, mitigation, owner.
4. Gaps and risks: full list.
5. Clarification questions: ordered by scope/price impact.
6. Response plan: section, owner, draft due, review due.
7. Administrative checklist: format, forms, signatures, references, delivery method, deadlines with page references.

# Requirement Taxonomy

## 1. Categories
| Category | Code | Contains | Typical response owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Functional | FUN | What the solution must do for users and the business | Solution architect |
| Technical | TEC | Architecture, platforms, integration, performance, data, environments | Technical architect |
| Security & Compliance | SEC | Certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI, HIPAA, FERPA, GDPR), data residency, access control, audit | CISO delegate / compliance |
| Commercial | COM | Pricing structure, payment terms, liability, insurance, IP, warranties, SLAs with credits | Commercial / legal |
| Delivery & PM | DEL | Methodology, timeline, team, governance, reporting, transition, training | Delivery lead |
| Administrative | ADM | Submission format, page limits, forms, signatures, references, deadlines | Bid manager |

Administrative items are tracked, not scored for compliance; they are pass/fail on submission.

## 2. Mandatory vs desirable detection
| Wording | Treat as |
|---|---|
| shall, must, is required to, will provide, mandatory, minimum requirement | Mandatory (M) |
| should, is expected to, preferred, desirable, where possible, would be advantageous | Desirable (D) |
| may, could, optional, nice to have | Optional (O) |
| Located in a section titled "Pass/Fail", "Minimum qualifications", "Mandatory criteria", "Gate" | Mandatory regardless of wording |

Hidden mandatories — check explicitly:
- Qualification thresholds in the introduction ("bidders must have delivered three comparable programs")
- Insurance, bonding, and financial-standing tests in the commercial section
- Certifications named in an appendix form rather than the body
- Reference-customer counts and recency requirements
- Local-presence, language, or working-hours requirements
- Data-residency or sovereign-cloud statements buried in security annexes
- Acceptance of terms and conditions "without exception" (an N here is a hard stop)

## 3. Evaluation weighting
If the RFP publishes scoring, record it against each requirement or section:
| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| Weight | Points or percentage as stated; sum must equal the stated total |
| Scoring method | Pass/fail · scored 0–5 · lowest price · best value — record verbatim |
| Price weight | Note separately; drives how aggressive the estimate must be |

If the RFP does not publish scoring, do not invent weights. Record `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and add a clarification question asking for the evaluation criteria and relative weights.

## 4. Requirement quality flags
| Flag | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| AMB | Ambiguous: could be read two ways | Clarification question |
| DUP | Duplicate or overlapping with another ID | Cross-reference; respond once, point both |
| CON | Conflicts with another requirement or with terms | Clarification question; note risk |
| UNQ | Unquantified ("high performance", "scalable") | Ask for the number or propose one in the response as an assumption |
| OOS | Likely out of our scope / needs a partner | Gaps list; partner decision |
| INC | Incumbent-shaped (specifies the incumbent's product or process) | Competitive flag; see competitive-positioning |

## 5. Inventory record
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| REQ-ID | Our sequential ID (REQ-001 …) |
| Client ID | The RFP's own clause number, verbatim |
| Section | RFP section heading |
| Page | Page or location |
| Text | Verbatim requirement text (do not paraphrase) |
| Category | FUN / TEC / SEC / COM / DEL / ADM |
| M/D/O | Mandatory / Desirable / Optional |
| Weight | Stated score or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` |
| Flags | AMB / DUP / CON / UNQ / OOS / INC |

# Request for Proposal — Integration Platform Modernization (fictional)

## 3. Technical requirements
3.1 The Supplier shall migrate all existing integrations from the incumbent iPaaS to an API gateway platform.
3.2 The Supplier must provide an API developer portal with self-service onboarding for internal teams.
3.3 The solution shall support OAuth 2.0 and mutual TLS for all external APIs.

## 5. Commercial requirements
