# solution-architecture-doc

## In a conversation: write the document now
- **The request carries facts** (systems, interfaces, constraints, NFRs, dates, audience): write the architecture document **in this reply**. Do not ask for a file or JSON first, and never answer with only questions. Use what is given; mark each missing fact `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`; end with the few questions that would close those gaps.
- **The request carries no client facts at all**: ask once, in one list, for current-state facts, drivers and constraints, NFR expectations and the audience. Do not draw a current state from assumptions. You may offer a generic pattern catalogue, labelled "not client-specific".
- **Asked to invent NFR numbers or to "just pick" products**: say in one line why not (unsourced targets and undecided products become contractual and credibility risk). Show each target as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` with its measurement method and the discovery question that would set it; show products as role placeholders with `proposed` ADRs naming the client decision owner; offer the scored options table as the way to decide.

The document, in this order (CIO depth: 6–10 pages, the bottom line stands alone; ARB depth adds component, deployment and security views):
1. **Bottom line** — the target state in one paragraph, the top 3 decisions, the waves, the biggest risk, what is still open.
2. **Drivers and constraints** — each with its source.
3. **Current state** (context + container, Mermaid) from evidence only; every box source-tagged; unknown integrations dashed and listed as gaps.
4. **Options and recommendation** — at least two options scored on weighted criteria (show the arithmetic); the choice is ADR-001.
5. **Target state** (context + container, Mermaid C4) — undecided products as placeholders.
6. **Integration map** — interfaces grouped by pattern, with protocol, data, volume/SLA (sourced or marked) and wave.
7. **NFRs** — target, measurement method, source, design response; constraints such as data residency become NFRs.
8. **Security and data**, **operability and environments**.
9. **Migration waves** — goal, scope, entry and exit criteria, rollback, aligned to the stated dates.
10. **Decision log** (ADRs with owner and status), **risks** (likelihood × impact, owner, mitigation), **open items** with owners, **sources**.

## Starting points
- **New** — the target design becomes a decision-ready architecture document: bottom line, drivers, C4 context, container and deployment diagrams, integration map, migration waves (entry, exit, rollback), NFRs, security, scored options with ADRs, risks, decision log, open items and sources.
- **Existing** — add `current` (the estate as it runs today, same layout): the document gains a change view — containers kept, added, retired or re-platformed, integrations added, retired or re-patterned — and a decision-log row for every retirement and re-platform.

## When to use
- "Produce the target architecture for <client>'s <initiative>."
- "Draw the C4 context and container views for the proposal."
- "Write the NFRs and decision log for this design."
- "Review this architecture document before it goes to the client."
- NOT for: effort (`effort-estimator`), interface scoring and TCO (`integration-migration-assessor`), proposal prose (`proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Current-state facts: systems, platforms, integration inventory, environments, hosting | yes | discovery synthesis / assessor output / client docs |
| Drivers and constraints: objectives, compliance regimes, vendor decisions already made, budget shape, dates | yes | discovery synthesis / RFP |
| Stated NFR expectations (volumes, latency, availability, RPO/RTO, security) or "none stated" | yes | client docs / user |
| Audience: CIO deck-level vs architecture-review-board level | yes | user |
| Existing draft (review mode) | yes in review | file |

Missing facts never stop the draft: write what is evidenced, mark the rest `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, and ask for it at the end. Never draw a current-state diagram from assumptions.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Fix the audience and depth** per `references/architecture-method.md` §1. CIO-level: context view + container view + decisions + waves, 6–10 pages. ARB-level: add component views for the critical containers, full NFR table, deployment view, security view.
2. **Draw the current state first** (context + container) from evidence only. Every box carries a source tag (document, slide, interview). Unknown integrations are drawn dashed with a `?` label and listed as gaps. This diagram is the baseline the client will correct; invite correction explicitly.
3. **Decision point — architecture options.** Identify the 2–3 options that the drivers permit (e.g., strangler migration vs big-bang; single API gateway vs federated; event backbone vs point-to-point API). Score each against the weighted criteria in §3 of the method (fit to drivers, risk, cost shape, time to value, operability, lock-in). Record the chosen option as ADR-001 using `assets/adr-template.md`; the others become the "alternatives considered" section. Never present a single option as inevitable.
4. **Draw the target state** (context, container; component for critical containers at ARB depth) with the Mermaid C4 templates in `assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md`. Name every container with technology placeholders only where a product decision is still open; mark those `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
5. **Build the integration map**: table of interfaces (source, target, pattern, protocol, data, volume, SLA, owner, wave) from the assessor output or the inventory; group by pattern (sync API, async event, batch file, managed-file transfer). Volumes and SLAs come from sources or are marked.
6. **Write the NFRs** with `assets/nfr-checklist.md`: every applicable NFR gets a measurable target, a measurement method, a source for the target (client statement, regulation, SLA), and a design response. "High availability" is not an NFR; "99.9% monthly, measured at the gateway, excluding planned windows ≤4h/month" is.
7. **Log every significant decision** as an ADR (context, options, decision, consequences, status, owner, date). Significant = changes cost, risk, vendor lock-in, or operating model. Decisions the client must make are ADRs in `proposed` status with the client owner named.
8. **Plan migration waves** per §5 of the method: wave criteria (risk, dependency, business value, freeze windows), per-wave scope, entry/exit criteria, rollback approach, parallel-run strategy. Wave membership for interfaces comes from the assessor's wave assignment when it exists.
9. **Security, data, and operability views** at the depth the audience needs: identity and access model, data classification and residency, secrets, observability, environments and promotion path, DR.
10. **Review mode**: read the draft fully; check each section against the review rubric in `references/architecture-review-rubric.md`; produce `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]` findings with rewritten content; deliver the clean version.
11. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `architecture.md` (Mermaid blocks inline, for Git and Confluence) and `architecture.html` (the same document, printable, diagrams inline; Print → Save as PDF)
- `diagrams/context.svg`, `diagrams/container.svg`, `diagrams/deployment.svg` (C4 pictures for slides) and `architecture.drawio` (every view, editable in diagrams.net / Confluence)
- `adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md` per decision, with the weighted option scores; `nfr.csv`
- Sections: Bottom line (target state in one paragraph + top 3 decisions) · Drivers and constraints · Current state (diagrams + gaps) · Options and recommendation (scored table) · Target state (diagrams) · Integration map · NFRs · Security and data · Operability and environments · Migration waves · Decision log (ADR index) · Risks · Open items with owners
- Appendices: `adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md` per decision (template `assets/adr-template.md`)

## Self-check
- [ ] Current-state boxes each carry a source; unknowns dashed and listed as gaps
- [ ] ≥2 options scored on stated criteria before the recommendation
- [ ] Every NFR has target, measurement method, source, design response
- [ ] Every significant decision has an ADR with owner and status
- [ ] Every volume, SLA, count sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Waves have entry/exit criteria and rollback
- [ ] Product names appear only where decided; otherwise placeholders marked
- [ ] Diagrams render (valid Mermaid); each has a one-line caption stating what it shows
- [ ] No other-client architecture details, no author history

## References
- `references/architecture-method.md` — depth by audience, current-state evidence rules, option scoring, wave planning, views
- `references/architecture-review-rubric.md` — review criteria and scoring for existing documents
- `assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md` — Mermaid C4 context/container/component/deployment templates
- `assets/nfr-checklist.md` — NFR categories with target patterns and measurement methods
- `assets/adr-template.md` — ADR template

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. When you can run commands, put the facts into `components.json` (layout: `evals/fixtures/northwind-order-hub.json`) and run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/solution-architecture-doc --input components=<file> --input client=<name> --out <dir>`; report `run.json` and hand over the deliverables it writes (below) instead of re-typing them.
When you cannot run commands, **write the document yourself** following the Procedure — never answer a request that already carries facts with only a question. Draft from what is given, mark every gap `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, and ask for the missing facts at the end.

# Architecture Method

## 1. Depth by audience
| Audience | Views | NFR depth | ADRs | Length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CIO / steering committee | Context, container, wave plan | Top 6 NFRs as a table | Top 3 decisions summarized; index to the rest | 6–10 pages |
| Architecture review board | + component (critical containers), deployment, security, data | Full checklist | All, with alternatives | 15–30 pages |
| Delivery team | + sequence diagrams for critical flows, environment matrix, interface specs by reference | Full + test approach per NFR | All | As needed |

Produce the CIO version first; the ARB version extends it. Never produce ARB depth for a CIO audience.

## 2. Current-state evidence rules
| Rule | Practice |
|---|---|
| Source every box | Tag each system/container with `[src: doc/slide/interview]` |
| Draw only what is evidenced | Unknown integrations are dashed with `?`; listed in a gaps table with the client owner who can confirm |
| No inferred products | If the discovery said "an ESB", draw "ESB `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`", not a product name |
| Invite correction | Caption: "Baseline from <sources>; to be validated with <client role> on <date>" |
| Count what you can | Interface counts, environments, regions — from inventory; otherwise marked |

## 3. Option scoring
Criteria and default weights; adjust weights to the client's stated drivers and show the adjustment.
| Criterion | Weight (default) | 1 | 3 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fit to drivers (objectives, constraints) | 25 | Meets few | Meets most | Meets all incl. constraints |
| Delivery risk | 20 | Big-bang, unproven in this estate | Phased with some unknowns | Incremental, reversible, proven patterns |
| Cost shape (capex/opex, run-rate direction) | 15 | Raises run-rate | Neutral | Lowers run-rate; fits budget shape |
| Time to first value | 15 | > 12 months | 6–12 months | < 6 months |
| Operability (skills, observability, support) | 15 | New skills, thin tooling | Partial | Existing skills, mature tooling |
| Lock-in / exit | 10 | Proprietary, hard to exit | Moderate | Open standards, portable |

Score table: `Option | per-criterion score × weight | Total | Key risk | Key benefit`. The recommendation references the table; the ADR records it. If two options score within 10%, say so and name the deciding qualitative factor.

Typical option sets:
| Decision | Options |
|---|---|
| Migration approach | Strangler by wave · Big-bang cutover · Hybrid (core big-bang, periphery strangler) |
| API layer | Single gateway · Federated gateways by domain · Gateway + service mesh |
| Integration style | Sync REST/GraphQL · Event backbone (Kafka/pub-sub) · Hybrid by interaction type |
| Hosting | Single cloud · Multi-cloud by workload · On-prem + cloud burst |
| Identity | Central IdP with federation · Per-platform · Hybrid with brokered SSO |
| Data integration | ELT to warehouse · CDC streaming · Virtualization |

## 4. Views
| View | Shows | Mermaid template |
|---|---|---|
| Context (C1) | System, users, external systems | `C4Context` |
| Container (C2) | Deployable units, data stores, protocols | `C4Container` |
| Component (C3) | Inside a critical container | `C4Component` |
| Deployment | Environments, regions, zones, scaling | `C4Deployment` |
| Integration map | Table + optional flow diagram | `flowchart` |
| Critical flows | Sequence of calls for 2–3 key journeys | `sequenceDiagram` |
| Security | Trust boundaries, identity flows, secrets, data classes | Annotated container view |

Every diagram: title, caption (what it shows and as-of date), legend if non-standard notation.

## 5. Migration wave planning
| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| Wave criteria | Dependency order (foundations first), risk (low-risk early to prove the pattern, highest-risk in a middle wave with max attention, never last), business value, freeze windows, team ramp |
| Wave 0 | Platform foundation: landing zone, CI/CD, observability, security baseline, reference implementation, test harness. No business interfaces |
| Wave 1 | 10–20% of scope, low-complexity, representative of patterns; proves the factory |
| Middle waves | Balanced by complexity; dependencies resolved within or before the wave |
| Final wave | Long-tail and deprecations; legacy decommission |
| Per wave | Scope list (IDs), entry criteria, exit criteria, rollback approach, parallel-run period, cutover window, hypercare |
| Decommission | Explicit tasks and dates; licensing savings only after decommission |

Wave table: `Wave | Scope (IDs, count) | Complexity mix | Dependencies | Entry criteria | Exit criteria | Rollback | Window`.

## 6. Decision log
Significant decisions get an ADR; the document carries an index: `ADR | Title | Status (proposed/accepted/superseded) | Owner | Date | Impact`. Decisions the client must make stay `proposed` with the client owner named and a decision-by date; they feed the dependency register in the SOW.

## 7. Security, data, operability minimums (any audience)
| Area | Minimum content |
|---|---|
| Identity and access | IdP, protocols (OIDC/SAML/OAuth2), service identity, RBAC model, admin access path |
| Data | Classification levels, residency, encryption at rest/in transit, retention, PII handling, backup and DR (RPO/RTO) |
| Secrets | Vault/KMS, rotation, no secrets in code or config repos |
| Observability | Logs, metrics, traces; correlation ID; dashboards; alert routing; SLO reporting |
| Environments | Dev/test/UAT/perf/prod; promotion path; data masking; IaC |
| Resilience | Failure modes per container, retries, circuit breakers, idempotency, DLQ for async |

# Architecture Review Rubric

Score each criterion 0–3. Anything at ≤1 is a `[SHARPEN]` or `[ADD]` finding with rewritten content. Report the scored table first, then findings in document order.

| # | Criterion | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Drivers stated and traceable | Absent | Generic ("modernize") | Specific, unsourced | Specific, sourced, each mapped to a design decision |
| 2 | Current state evidenced | Absent or invented | Diagram without sources | Sourced, gaps unmarked | Sourced, gaps marked with owners |
| 3 | Options considered | Single option | Options named, not scored | Scored, weights unexplained | Scored against weighted criteria tied to drivers |
| 4 | Target-state clarity | No diagram | Diagram without technology or responsibility | Clear containers and protocols | + ownership, data stores, trust boundaries |
| 5 | Integration map | Absent | List without patterns | Patterns and protocols | + volumes, SLAs, owners, waves (sourced or marked) |
| 6 | NFRs measurable | Absent | Adjectives | Targets without measurement method | Targets, method, source, design response |
| 7 | Decisions logged | None | Implicit in prose | ADRs without alternatives | ADRs with alternatives, consequences, owners, status |
| 8 | Migration plan | None | Phases without criteria | Waves with scope | + entry/exit, rollback, parallel run, decommission |
| 9 | Security and data | Absent | Mentioned | Identity and encryption covered | + classification, residency, secrets, DR with RPO/RTO |
| 10 | Operability | Absent | "Monitoring will be in place" | Tooling named | + SLOs, alert routing, environments and promotion, IaC |
| 11 | Numbers discipline | Invented figures | Unsourced figures | Mostly sourced | All sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` |
| 12 | Audience fit | Wrong depth | Mixed depth | Right depth, uneven | Right depth throughout; exec summary stands alone |
| 13 | Diagram quality | Do not render | Render, no captions | Captions | + legends, as-of dates, consistent naming with text |
| 14 | Risks and open items | Absent | Listed | With mitigations | With likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner, date |

## Common findings and rewrites
| Finding | Rewrite pattern |
|---|---|
| "The solution will be highly available and scalable." | NFR rows: availability 99.9% monthly at gateway, excluding ≤4h planned; horizontal scaling to 2× peak (peak = `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`) within 10 minutes |
| "We recommend <product> as the integration platform." with no alternatives | Add options table and ADR with the two alternatives and the scoring; keep the recommendation |
| Current-state diagram with 30 named products from memory | Reduce to evidenced systems; dash the rest; add gaps table |
| "Migration will be done in phases." | Wave table with scope IDs, criteria, rollback |
| Security section listing controls without data classification | Add classification table and map controls to classes |
| Product names for undecided components | Replace with role names and `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` |

2. Findings in document order: `Section | Verdict ([KEEP]/[SHARPEN]/[CUT]/[ADD]/[TBD]) | Reason | Rewritten content or action`.
3. Clean revised document.

Every figure comes from the proposal or estimate or is marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]. Do not use for proposal narrative (proposal-writer) or effort math (effort-estimator); legal terms are flagged for counsel, not drafted.

# sow-drafter

## In a conversation: draft the SOW now
- **The request carries the approved proposal, the estimate and the commercial model** — including when the proposal and estimate are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: draft the SOW **in this reply** on `assets/sow-template.md` from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
  1. **Scope** — numbered `S-nn` statements (verb + object + boundary, with appendix references) and mirrored `O-nn` out-of-scope items where ambiguity is likely.
  2. **Deliverables and acceptance** — table with ID, format, objective acceptance criteria, method, review window, approver (client role), milestone; plus a **deemed-acceptance clause**.
  3. **Milestones and payment** tied to accepted deliverables per the stated model (e.g. fixed price per wave → one milestone per wave on acceptance); amounts from the proposal pricing or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
  4. **Assumptions** — every estimate quantity as an assumption with basis, consequence if false, change-control trigger = Y, and who confirms by when.
  5. **Client dependencies** with due dates and a delay-consequence clause.
  6. **Governance and RACI** with exactly one A per row; **change-control procedure** with a minor-change threshold.
  7. **Legal flags** — topics (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance) referenced to the MSA clause and marked "confirm with counsel", not drafted.
  8. Separately, internal (not shipped): **proposal → SOW traceability table** and **scope-ambiguity register**.
  Mark every value the request does not give `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming its source, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
- **No proposal, or no commercial model** ("turn this proposal into an SOW"): ask once, in one list, for the commercial model (fixed / T&M / milestone / run-rate) and the estimate file (and the proposal if absent). Say in one line that acceptance-payment linkage depends on the model. Do not draft the commercial section on an assumed model; you may offer to draft scope and deliverables meanwhile.
- **Asked for subjective acceptance or an unsourced price** ("to the client's reasonable satisfaction", "put roughly what we discussed on the call"): say in one line that subjective acceptance invites disputes over sign-off and payment. Rewrite the criteria as objective, testable ones per `references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md`. Show the total as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` with a note that it must come from the estimate/proposal pricing — never print the discussed figure anywhere. Offer a **deemed-acceptance clause** (accepted unless written rejection with reasons within the review window) as the flexibility mechanism instead.

## Starting points
- **New** — the approved proposal becomes a SOW on the template: scope in and out, deliverables with acceptance criteria, milestones, team, every assumption carried, the change-control clause verbatim.
- **Existing** — add `existing_sow` (the client's paper or an earlier version): it is reconciled against the proposal — deliverables missing or added, subjective acceptance criteria, assumptions not carried, clauses absent — in `sow-reconciliation.md`, next to the SOW drafted from the proposal.

## When to use
- "Turn the approved proposal into an SOW."
- "Redline this SOW — the scope is too loose."
- "Write acceptance criteria for these deliverables."
- NOT for: proposal narrative (`proposal-writer`), estimate (`effort-estimator`), MSA/legal clauses (flag for counsel).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Approved proposal (final version) | yes | file |
| Estimate output: phases, effort, team, milestones | yes | file |
| Commercial model decided: fixed / T&M / milestone / run-rate | yes | user |
| Governing agreement (MSA) reference and any mandated SOW template | no | user / file |
| Client-side named roles for RACI | no | user |
| Existing SOW draft (redline mode) | yes in redline | file |

If the proposal or commercial model is missing, ask once. A missing estimate figure, MSA reference or client role name does not stop the draft: it is marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. An SOW without a decided commercial model cannot define acceptance and payment linkage.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. Redline convention applies in redline mode.

1. **Extract the scope baseline** from the proposal: objectives, phases, deliverables, team, timeline, assumptions, risks. Build a traceability table: proposal section → SOW clause. Anything in the proposal that is not scope, deliverable, assumption, or commercial term (marketing language, win themes) is dropped from the SOW.
2. **Write scope as numbered statements** per `references/sow-method.md` §2: each in-scope item is a verb + object + boundary ("Migrate the 42 interfaces listed in Appendix A from platform X to platform Y, including unit and integration test"). Mirror every in-scope item with an explicit out-of-scope statement where ambiguity is likely. Run the scope-ambiguity scan (§3) and register each ambiguity with its resolution.
3. **Define deliverables with acceptance criteria** using `references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md`. Each deliverable: ID, description, format, acceptance criteria (objective, testable), acceptance method (review / test / demonstration), review window (days), deemed-acceptance rule, approver (client role).
4. **Decision point — commercial linkage.** Per `references/sow-method.md` §5: fixed-price → milestones tied to accepted deliverables; T&M → monthly invoicing against approved timesheets with a not-to-exceed; milestone → payment on acceptance with a percentage schedule; run-rate → service levels with credits. Amounts come from the estimate/proposal pricing or are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never place a number without a source.
5. **Convert every assumption into a change-control trigger**: assumption → basis → what happens if false (effort, schedule, price) → who confirms by when. Client dependencies get a due date and a consequence clause ("delay of client dependency D3 by more than 5 business days shifts dependent milestones day for day").
6. **Governance and RACI**: forums, cadence, decision rights, escalation path, and a RACI across the deliverables with one A per row. Client roles named if supplied, else role titles with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
7. **Change-control procedure**: request → impact assessment (effort, schedule, price, risk) → approval authority and threshold → documentation. Include a minor-change threshold to avoid paperwork for trivial items.
8. **Legal flags**: list every clause that counsel must confirm against the MSA (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance). Do not draft these; reference the MSA or mark for counsel.
9. **Redline mode**: read the draft fully; score each clause against the ambiguity scan and acceptance patterns; produce `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]` with rewritten text; deliver the clean version.
10. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `sow-<client>-<initiative>-v0.1.md` (or `-redline-<date>.md` in redline mode)
- Template: `assets/sow-template.md`
- Companion: `assets/assumptions-checklist.md` completed as Appendix C
- Internal (not shipped): proposal→SOW traceability table; scope-ambiguity register; legal-flags list

## Self-check
- [ ] Every in-scope item is numbered, bounded, and has a matching out-of-scope statement where ambiguity exists
- [ ] Every deliverable has objective acceptance criteria, method, review window, approver, deemed-acceptance rule
- [ ] Every assumption states consequence if false and is a change-control trigger
- [ ] Client dependencies have due dates and delay consequences
- [ ] Payment schedule links to accepted deliverables/milestones; all amounts sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] RACI has exactly one A per deliverable
- [ ] Legal clauses referenced to MSA or flagged for counsel; none drafted here
- [ ] No proposal marketing language, no other-client references, no author history

## References
- `references/sow-method.md` — scope statements, ambiguity scan, commercial linkage, change control, governance
- `references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md` — patterns by deliverable type with examples
- `assets/sow-template.md` — SOW template
- `assets/assumptions-checklist.md` — assumptions and dependencies checklist by engagement type

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/sow-drafter --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/sow-drafter`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.
skills/presales/sow-drafter/scripts/sow_:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Draft a Statement of Work from an approved proposal.

    python3 -I scripts/sow_from_proposal.py proposal.md --template assets/sow-template.md \
        --out SOW.md --deliverables deliverables.csv --assumptions-check assumptions-check.csv

Reads from proposal.md (Markdown produced by proposal-writer or on its section library):
  * "Scope and deliverables" table rows  -> deliverables (D-nn) and in-scope statements (S-nn)
  * "Out of scope" line                   -> out-of-scope statements (O-nn)
  * "Assumption register" table rows      -> SOW assumptions (A-nn), every one carried over
  * "Timeline" milestone rows             -> milestones (M-nn)
  * "Team" role rows                      -> team table
  * H1 "<Client> — <Initiative> — Proposal" -> SOW header
Writes SOW.md on the template (scope in/out, deliverables with acceptance criteria, assumptions,
RACI stub, the template's change-control clause verbatim), deliverables.csv (id, deliverable,
acceptance, phase, format) and assumptions-check.csv listing proposal assumptions NOT carried
over (header only when the SOW is complete). Any missing acceptance criterion, date or amount is
`[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Delivery lead]`; nothing is invented. Exit 1 when proposal.md is missing or has
no scope/deliverables table. Stdlib only, offline.

Existing SOW (--existing-sow SOW-v2.md --reconcile reconciliation.md): a SOW draft already in play (the
client's paper or an earlier version) is reconciled against the approved proposal — every proposal
deliverable is found in it or listed missing, acceptance criteria that are absent or subjective
("reasonable satisfaction", "to be agreed", "best efforts") are flagged, deliverable ids the proposal
does not have are flagged as scope added, proposal assumptions it does not carry are listed, and the
change-control, acceptance and assumptions clauses are checked for presence. SOW.md is still drafted
from the proposal, so the two can be compared side by side.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TBD = "[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Delivery lead]"


def die(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def read(path: str) -> str:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        die(f"file not found: {p}")
    return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def section(md: str, heading: str) -> list[str]:
    lines, out, level = md.splitlines(), [], None
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.startswith("#"):
            lvl = len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip("#"))
            if level is None:
                if heading.lower() in ln.lower():
                    level = lvl
                continue
            if lvl <= level:
                break
        elif level is not None:
            out.append(ln)
    return out


def cells(row: str) -> list[str]:
    return [c.strip() for c in row.strip().strip("|").split("|")]


def table_after(lines: list[str], header_startswith: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Data rows of the first table whose header line starts with the given text."""
    rows, inside = [], False
    for ln in lines:
        if not inside:
            if ln.startswith(header_startswith):
                inside = True
            continue
        if not ln.startswith("|"):
            break
        body = ln.replace("|", "").strip()
        if set(body) <= set("-: "):
            continue
        c = cells(ln)
        if any(c):
            rows.append(c)
    return rows


def val(c: list[str], i: int) -> str:
    v = c[i].strip("`").strip() if i < len(c) else ""
    return v if v and not v.startswith("[TO BE BASELINED") else ""


SUBJECTIVE = re.compile(r"reasonable satisfaction|to be agreed|\btbd\b|best efforts|as required|sole discretion", re.I)
CLAUSES = [("Change control", r"change control|change request"), ("Acceptance", r"acceptance"),
           ("Assumptions", r"assumption")]


def reconcile(existing: str, deliverables: list[dict], assumptions: list[dict], name: str) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
    """Reconciliation of an existing SOW against the proposal; returns (lines, number of issues)."""
    rows: dict[str, str] = {}          # deliverable id -> acceptance cell, from tables with a Deliverable column
    header: list[str] | None = None
    for ln in existing.splitlines():
        if not ln.startswith("|"):
            header = None
            continue
        c = cells(ln)
        if header is None:
            header = [h.lower() for h in c]
            continue
        if set("".join(c)) <= set("-: "):
            continue
        if any("deliverable" in h for h in header) and c and re.fullmatch(r"D-\d+", c[0].strip("` ")):
            acc_i = next((i for i, h in enumerate(header) if "acceptance" in h), None)
            rows.setdefault(c[0].strip("` "), c[acc_i] if acc_i is not None and acc_i < len(c) else "")
    issues = 0
    L = [f"# SOW reconciliation — {name} vs the approved proposal", "", "## Deliverables",
         "| ID | Proposal deliverable | In this SOW | Acceptance in this SOW | Finding |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for d in deliverables:
        c = rows.get(d["id"])
        if c is None:
            issues += 1
            L.append(f"| {d['id']} | {d['deliverable']} | no | — | missing — add it with the proposal's acceptance: {d['acceptance']} |")
            continue
        acc = "" if c.startswith("[TO BE BASELINED") else c
        if not acc:
            issues += 1
            finding = f"no acceptance criterion — use the proposal's: {d['acceptance']}"
        elif SUBJECTIVE.search(acc):
            issues += 1
            finding = f"subjective acceptance — replace with the proposal's: {d['acceptance']}"
        else:
            finding = "ok"
        L.append(f"| {d['id']} | {d['deliverable']} | yes | {acc or '—'} | {finding} |")
    extra = [k for k in rows if k not in {d['id'] for d in deliverables}]
    for k in extra:
        issues += 1
        L.append(f"| {k} | — | yes | {rows[k] or '—'} | scope added: not in the approved proposal — "
                 f"change request or remove ({TBD}) |")
    L += ["", "## Assumptions", "| ID | Proposal assumption | In this SOW |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for s_ in assumptions:
        hit = s_["assumption"] in existing
        issues += not hit
        L.append(f"| {s_['id']} | {s_['assumption']} | {'yes' if hit else 'no — carry it over'} |")
    if not assumptions:
        L.append("| — | the proposal carries no assumption register | — |")
    L += ["", "## Clauses", "| Clause | Present |", "|---|---|"]
    heads = "\n".join(ln for ln in existing.splitlines() if ln.startswith("#"))
    for label, rx in CLAUSES:
        ok = re.search(rx, heads, re.I) is not None
        issues += not ok
        L.append(f"| {label} | {'yes' if ok else 'no — add the section from assets/sow-template.md'} |")
    L.insert(2, f"**{issues} issue(s) to resolve before signature.**\n")
    return L, issues


def marker_or(v: str) -> str:
    return v or TBD


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="proposal.md -> SOW.md + deliverables.csv + assumptions-check.csv")
    ap.add_argument("proposal")
    ap.add_argument("--template", required=True, help="assets/sow-template.md")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="SOW.md")
    ap.add_argument("--deliverables", required=True, help="deliverables.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--assumptions-check", required=True, help="assumptions-check.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--existing-sow", default="", help="a SOW draft already in play, to reconcile with the proposal")
    ap.add_argument("--reconcile", default="", help="with --existing-sow: write the reconciliation here")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    prop, tmpl = read(a.proposal), read(a.template)
    m = re.search(r"^# (.+?) — (.+?) — Proposal\s*$", prop, re.M)
    client, initiative = (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else (TBD, TBD)

    scope = section(prop, "Scope and deliverables")
    drows = table_after(scope, "| ID | Deliverable |")
    if not drows:
        die("proposal has no 'Scope and deliverables' table with rows (header '| ID | Deliverable |')")
    deliverables = []
    for i, c in enumerate(drows, 1):
        deliverables.append({"id": val(c, 0) or f"D-{i:02d}", "deliverable": marker_or(val(c, 1)),
                             "description": marker_or(val(c, 2)), "acceptance": marker_or(val(c, 3)),
                             "phase": marker_or(val(c, 4)), "format": marker_or(val(c, 5))})
    out_of_scope = []
    for ln in scope:
        if ln.lower().startswith("out of scope"):
            body = ln.split(":", 1)[1] if ":" in ln else ""
            out_of_scope = [s.strip(" .") for s in re.split(r";|\n|(?<=[a-z0-9\)])\.\s", body) if s.strip(" .")]
            if body.strip().startswith("[TO BE BASELINED"):
                out_of_scope = []
    arows = table_after(section(prop, "Risks and assumptions"), "| ID | Assumption |")
    assumptions = [{"id": val(c, 0) or f"A-{i:02d}", "assumption": marker_or(val(c, 1)), "basis": marker_or(val(c, 2)),
                    "if_false": marker_or(val(c, 3)), "cc": val(c, 4) or "Y", "confirm_by": marker_or(val(c, 5))}
                   for i, c in enumerate(arows, 1)]
    mrows = table_after(section(prop, "Timeline"), "| Milestone |")
    milestones = [{"id": f"M{i}", "name": marker_or(val(c, 0)), "when": marker_or(val(c, 1)),
                   "dep": marker_or(val(c, 2))} for i, c in enumerate(mrows, 1)]
    trows = table_after(section(prop, "Team and governance"), "| Role |")
    team = [{"role": marker_or(val(c, 0)), "resp": marker_or(val(c, 1)), "alloc": marker_or(val(c, 2)),
             "loc": marker_or(val(c, 3)), "named": val(c, 4) or "—"} for c in trows]

    exec_lines = [ln for ln in section(prop, "Executive summary") if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("|")]
    background = exec_lines[0] if exec_lines else TBD
    for n, d in enumerate(deliverables, 1):
        d["milestone"] = milestones[min(n, len(milestones)) - 1]["id"] if milestones else "M1"

    # ---- build the SOW on the template: keep every template section, fill the tables we own
    L = (tmpl.replace("<Client>", client).replace("<Initiative>", initiative)
         .replace("| Client | <legal entity> |", f"| Client | {client} (legal entity {TBD}) |")
         .replace("<Two to four sentences from the approved proposal: situation and objective. No marketing language.>",
                  f"From the approved proposal: {background}")).splitlines()
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(L):
        ln = L[i]
        if ln.startswith("| S-01 |"):
            for n, d in enumerate(deliverables, 1):
                out.append(f"| S-{n:02d} | Deliver {d['deliverable']} ({d['phase']}) | Appendix D |")
            i += 1; continue
        if ln.startswith("| O-01 |"):
            if out_of_scope:
                for n, s in enumerate(out_of_scope, 1):
                    out.append(f"| O-{n:02d} | {s} | S-{min(n, len(deliverables)):02d} |")
            else:
                out.append(f"| O-01 | {TBD} | S-01 |")
            i += 1; continue
        if ln.startswith("| D-01 | A | R |"):
            for d in deliverables:
                out.append(f"| {d['id']} | A | R | R | I | C | C |")
            i += 1; continue
        if ln.startswith("| D-01 |"):
            for d in deliverables:
                out.append(f"| {d['id']} | {d['deliverable']} | {d['description']} | {d['format']} | "
                           f"{d['acceptance']} | review | 5 | {TBD} | {d['milestone']} |")
            i += 1; continue
        if ln.startswith("| M1 |"):
            if milestones:
                for ms in milestones:
                    dels = ", ".join(d["id"] for d in deliverables if d["milestone"] == ms["id"]) or "—"
                    out.append(f"| {ms['id']} | {ms['name']} | {ms['when']} | {dels} | {ms['dep']} |")
            else:
                out.append(f"| M1 | {TBD} | {TBD} | {', '.join(d['id'] for d in deliverables)} | DEP-01 |")
            i += 1; continue
        if ln.startswith("| A-01 |"):
            if assumptions:
                for s in assumptions:
                    out.append(f"| {s['id']} | {s['assumption']} | {s['basis']} | {s['if_false']} | {s['cc']} | {s['confirm_by']} |")
            else:
                out.append(f"| A-01 | {TBD} (proposal carries no assumption register) | | | Y | |")
            i += 1; continue
        if ln.startswith("| Role | Responsibilities |") and team:
            out.append(ln); out.append(L[i + 1])
            for t in team:
                out.append(f"| {t['role']} | {t['resp']} | {t['alloc']} | {t['loc']} | {t['named']} |")
            i += 2; continue
        out.append(re.sub(r"<[^<>\n`]{1,200}>", TBD, ln))
        i += 1
    sow = "\n".join(out).rstrip("\n") + "\n"
    sow = sow.replace("| Version | 0.1 — draft |", "| Version | 0.1 — draft (generated from proposal.md) |")
    Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(a.out).write_text(sow, encoding="utf-8")

    with Path(a.deliverables).open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["id", "deliverable", "description", "acceptance", "phase", "format", "milestone"])
        w.writeheader(); w.writerows(deliverables)
    # every proposal assumption must appear in the SOW text; list the ones that do not
    missing = [s for s in assumptions if s["assumption"] not in sow]
    with Path(a.assumptions_check).open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["id", "assumption", "status"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows([{"id": s["id"], "assumption": s["assumption"], "status": "NOT IN SOW"} for s in missing])
    if a.existing_sow:
        rec, n_issues = reconcile(read(a.existing_sow), deliverables, assumptions, Path(a.existing_sow).name)
        if a.reconcile:
            Path(a.reconcile).write_text("\n".join(rec) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"reconciliation: {Path(a.existing_sow).name} — {n_issues} issue(s)")
    n_tbd = sum(1 for d in deliverables if d["acceptance"] == TBD)
    print(f"SOW: {len(deliverables)} deliverables ({n_tbd} acceptance criteria to baseline), "
          f"{len(assumptions)} assumptions carried, {len(missing)} not carried, {len(out_of_scope)} out-of-scope -> {a.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Acceptance-Criteria Patterns

Acceptance criteria are objective, testable, and tied to the deliverable. "Client satisfaction" is not a criterion. Use the pattern for the deliverable type; combine where needed.

## 1. Document deliverables (assessment report, architecture, plan, runbook)
| Criterion type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Completeness | Contains sections listed in Appendix <n> | "Contains all 9 sections of the target-architecture outline in Appendix D" |
| Traceability | Every <item> maps to <source> | "Every migration wave lists its interfaces by ID from the inventory in Appendix A" |
| Review | Reviewed by <role>; comments resolved or logged | "Reviewed by the client Enterprise Architect; all comments classified material/non-material; material comments resolved" |
| Format | Delivered as <format> in <repository> | "Delivered as PDF and Markdown in the client's project SharePoint" |

Acceptance method: review. Window: 5–10 business days. Deemed acceptance applies.

## 2. Software / integration deliverables (interfaces, services, components)
| Criterion type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Functional | Passes test cases in <test plan> with <threshold> | "Passes 100% of P1 and ≥95% of P2 test cases in the wave test plan; no open P1 defects" |
| Non-functional | Meets NFR-nn under <test> | "Sustains 200 requests/second with p95 latency ≤ 400 ms for 30 minutes in the client UAT environment (NFR-04)" |
| Parallel run | Output parity with legacy for <period> | "Produces identical outputs to the legacy interface for 5 consecutive business days of parallel run, variance log reviewed and signed" |
| Operability | Monitoring, alerts, runbook in place | "Dashboards and alert rules deployed; runbook entry delivered per interface" |
| Code quality | Static analysis and review gate | "No critical or high findings in <tool>; peer review recorded in the repository" |
| Security | Scan results | "No critical/high vulnerabilities in dependency and container scans at delivery date" |

Acceptance method: test execution witnessed or evidence package. Window: 5 business days after evidence delivery.

## 3. Migration / cutover deliverables (wave cutover, data migration)
| Criterion type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Cutover completion | <n> interfaces live, legacy disabled, rollback not invoked within <period> | "All 12 wave-2 interfaces live in production; legacy routes disabled; no rollback within 10 business days" |
| Data reconciliation | Record counts and control totals match within <tolerance> | "Migrated record counts match source 100%; control totals match within 0.01%" |
| Stability | Incident threshold during hypercare | "No P1 incidents attributable to migrated interfaces during the 10-day hypercare window; P2 incidents resolved within SLA" |

Acceptance method: cutover report with evidence. Window: hypercare period + 3 business days.

## 4. Service / run deliverables (managed service months)
| Criterion type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| SLA attainment | Monthly service report shows SLAs met or credits applied | "Monthly report delivered by the 5th business day; SLA table per Appendix F; credits computed per schedule" |
| Volume bands | Actual volumes within contracted band or change request raised | "Transaction volume within Band B; above Band B triggers CR per clause 9" |

Acceptance method: monthly report review. Window: 5 business days.

## 5. Training and knowledge transfer
| Criterion type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery | Sessions delivered, attendance recorded | "Two sessions delivered; attendance sheet signed; recordings and materials in repository" |
| Competency (optional) | Participants complete exercise | "At least 80% of participants complete the hands-on lab" |

## 6. Assessment and advisory outputs (recommendation, roadmap, business case)
| Criterion type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Decision readiness | Contains options, criteria, recommendation, costs with basis | "Presents ≥2 options scored against the agreed criteria (Appendix E), a recommendation, and cost ranges with stated assumptions" |
| Baseline sourced | Every baseline figure sourced or marked | "Every baseline figure carries a source or a `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` marker agreed with the sponsor" |
| Presentation | Presented to steering committee | "Presented at steering committee; decisions and actions minuted" |

## 7. Anti-patterns
| Avoid | Because | Replace with |
|---|---|---|
| "To the client's satisfaction" | Subjective; unlimited rework | Objective criteria above |
| "Industry best practice" | Undefined | Named standard, version |
| "Fully tested" | Undefined threshold | Test-plan pass rates and open-defect limits |
| "Production-ready" | Undefined | NFR pass + operability + security criteria |
| Criteria that depend on a client action without a dependency row | Supplier cannot control acceptance | Add DEP-nn with date and consequence |

# SOW Method

## 1. Purpose of the SOW
The proposal persuades; the SOW protects both parties. Everything in the SOW must be enforceable: numbered, bounded, testable, dated, owned. If a sentence cannot be the subject of a dispute, it does not belong.

## 2. Scope statements
Pattern: `S-nn | <Verb> <object> <boundary/quantity> <quality standard> <reference to appendix>`.

| Weak | Enforceable |
|---|---|
| "Migrate integrations to the new platform." | "S-03: Migrate the 42 interfaces listed in Appendix A from <platform X> to <platform Y>, including unit tests, integration tests against the client's UAT environment, and runbook entries per interface." |
| "Provide training." | "S-09: Deliver two 4-hour remote training sessions for up to 12 client developers on the platform operating model, with recorded sessions and slide decks delivered as D-11." |
| "Support go-live." | "S-12: Provide hypercare for 10 business days after each wave cutover, 08:00–18:00 client local time, with a named lead and a 2-hour response target for P1 issues." |

Out-of-scope mirror: for each S-nn where a reader could reasonably assume more, add `O-nn`. Standard O items: data cleansing, licenses, hardware/cloud consumption costs, third-party vendor fees, business process redesign, end-user training beyond stated sessions, environments provisioning, historical data migration unless listed, 24×7 support unless listed.

## 3. Scope-ambiguity scan
Run against every S-nn and D-nn. Register each hit with the resolution.
| Ambiguity | Question to resolve | Typical resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Unquantified noun ("the interfaces", "users", "reports") | How many, listed where? | Appendix list; count becomes an assumption and change trigger |
| "Including but not limited to" | What is the limit? | Remove the phrase; enumerate |
| Quality undefined ("production-ready", "best practice") | Which standard, tested how? | Reference the client's standard or ours by name; acceptance criterion |
| Environment unstated | Which environments, who provides them, by when? | Dependency with date |
| Time window unstated ("support", "hypercare") | Hours, days, response targets? | Explicit window and targets |
| Owner unstated ("will be reviewed") | By whom, in how many days? | Approver role and review window |
| Reuse implied ("existing assets") | Which assets, who owns them, licensed how? | IP clause reference; appendix |
| Dependency implied ("once access is granted") | By whom, by when, consequence? | Dependency register |

## 4. Deliverables vs activities
Deliverables are things that can be accepted; activities are work. Only deliverables carry acceptance and payment. Each deliverable row: `D-nn | Name | Description | Format | Acceptance criteria | Acceptance method | Review window | Approver | Deemed-acceptance rule | Milestone`.

Deemed acceptance: "If the client does not provide written acceptance or a documented, material deficiency list within <n> business days of delivery, the deliverable is deemed accepted." Material deficiency = failure against a stated acceptance criterion, not a preference.

## 5. Commercial linkage
| Model | Payment trigger | What the SOW must contain | Risk held by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed price | Accepted milestone | Milestone table with deliverables per milestone, percentage schedule, acceptance rules; assumptions as change triggers | Supplier (scope), client (dependencies) |
| T&M | Monthly approved timesheets | Rate card by role, not-to-exceed, estimate as guidance, change control for NTE increase | Client |
| Milestone T&M (hybrid) | Monthly actuals capped per milestone | Both of the above | Shared |
| Run-rate / managed service | Monthly fee | Service catalog, SLAs, service credits, baseline volumes, volume bands, transition plan | Supplier (SLA), client (volume) |

All amounts: from the proposal pricing or estimate, cited by section; otherwise `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Rate cards referenced from `effort-estimator`'s rate-card file by name, never retyped.

## 6. Assumptions and dependencies
Assumption pattern: `A-nn | Statement | Basis (source) | If false: effort / schedule / price impact | Change control trigger: Y | Confirmed by (client role) by (date)`.
Dependency pattern: `DEP-nn | Client provides <what> | By <date or "T-n days before milestone"> | Consequence of delay: <day-for-day shift / re-plan / change request>`.

Rule: every number in the estimate is an assumption. Every item the client must provide is a dependency with a date.

## 7. Governance
| Forum | Cadence | Attendees | Decisions | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daily stand-up | Daily | Delivery team | Blockers | Delivery lead |
| Project status | Weekly | PM both sides, workstream leads | Risks, issues, change requests < threshold | Engagement manager ↔ client PMO |
| Steering committee | Monthly or per gate | Sponsor, engagement partner, PMs | Gates, change requests ≥ threshold, priority conflicts | Executive sponsor both sides |

RACI: one A per deliverable; R may be several; C and I by role. Client roles with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` if not named.

## 8. Change control
| Step | Content |
|---|---|
| Request | Either party; written; CR-nn; description, reason |
| Impact assessment | Supplier within 5 business days: effort, schedule, price, risk, affected deliverables |
| Approval | Below threshold (e.g., ≤ 2 person-days and no price change): PMs; above: steering committee; price changes: signatory authority per MSA |
| Documentation | Signed CR appended; baseline updated; assumptions register updated |
| Minor change | Clarifications with no effort/schedule/price impact: recorded in status report, no CR |

## 9. Legal flags (do not draft)
IP ownership and license-back of pre-existing materials · limitation of liability and caps · warranties and remedy period · termination for convenience and fees · data protection and processing roles · confidentiality · non-solicitation · insurance · export control · dispute resolution · order of precedence (MSA vs SOW). List each with the MSA clause reference and "confirm with counsel".

Do not use for platform-only TCO (integration-migration-assessor feeds this) or for effort (effort-estimator). Not for wording outcome claims in a proposal's executive summary (proposal-writer) or synthesizing discovery call notes (discovery-interview).

# value-case-builder

## In a conversation: build the case now
- **The request carries baselines** (volumes, costs, rates from client sources): write the value case **in this reply**. A benefits tree tracing each lever to the client's statements and cost drivers; baselines cited with confidence (H/M/L); unbaselined benefits kept out of the headline and listed; targets as low/base/high with mechanisms and ramps tied to delivery milestones; costs including delivery (at the estimate's P80), run, dual-run and decommission timing; NPV only at a discount rate the client's finance supplied, on their fiscal year; sensitivity on the top three assumptions with break-even values; a benefits-realization plan with client owners (unowned benefits flagged); a double-counting check.
- **The request says files are attached but their contents are not in the conversation**: still build the whole case now from the facts the request states (who said what, which sources exist, the discount rate, the fiscal year). Lay out every section in full — benefits tree, baselines table, targets, costs, NPV, sensitivity, realization plan, double-counting check — with each value the request does not give shown as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the attached source it will come from. Never reply with only a request for the files.
- **No client baselines**: ask once for scope, outcomes, at least one baseline fact and the audience. If none are available, say on line 1 that this is not a business case yet, give a hypothesis map (benefits tree with every baseline `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`) and the specific data requests with their likely holders.
- **Asked to use an industry benchmark or put a big multiple on page one**: decline in one line (a CFO-grade case is built from the client's baselines and mechanisms; an unsourced multiple will not survive finance review). Show the headline as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` — never print the requested multiple or percentage anywhere, not even beside that marker — list the unbaselined benefits, and offer the path to a defensible number: data requests with owners and a short baselining phase. A benchmark the user supplies with a source is recorded at confidence L and kept out of the headline.

## Starting points
- **New** — sourced benefits and costs become a CFO-grade value case: yearly cash flows, NPV, payback, P80 cost and sensitivity, with unbaselined rows kept out of the headline.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (the earlier case's `value-model.json`): the refresh shows how benefits, costs, net, NPV, P80 cost and payback moved, and which benefits were added, removed, re-estimated or newly baselined.

## When to use
- "Build the business case for <initiative>."
- "What is the ROI on this program, and how confident are we?"
- "Review the client's draft business case before the steering committee."
- NOT for: platform TCO alone (`integration-migration-assessor`), effort and price (`effort-estimator`), the proposal narrative (`proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Initiative scope and outcomes (objectives, success measures) | yes | discovery synthesis / proposal |
| Baseline facts: current cost, volumes, cycle times, headcount on the process, error/incident rates, revenue levers | yes (any subset; rest is TBD) | client documents / statements |
| Cost of the initiative: one-time (from `effort-estimator`) and run (from TCO or client) | yes or `[TO BE BASELINED]` | estimate memo / TCO |
| Finance conventions: currency, horizon (3/5 yr), discount rate, capex/opex treatment, fiscal year | no — defaults stated as assumptions | client finance / user |
| Audience: CFO-grade vs sponsor-level | yes | user |

If scope and at least one baseline fact are missing, ask once. A value case with no client baseline is a hypothesis map, and the output says so on line 1.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Build the benefits tree** per `references/value-method.md` §1: strategic driver → value lever → operational metric → financial value. Each leaf must trace to an outcome the client stated. Classify each benefit: hard (cash, cost avoided with a named budget line), soft-quantifiable (productivity hours with a conversion rule), strategic (unquantified; listed, not summed).
2. **Baseline every metric**: value, source (document/page or client role and date), confidence (H/M/L). No source → `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and the metric is excluded from the headline number until baselined. Do not borrow benchmarks from memory; if the user supplies an external benchmark, cite it and rate confidence L.
3. **Set improvement targets** as ranges (low / base / high) with the mechanism that produces them (automation of step X removes Y hours; decommission removes licence line Z). A target without a mechanism is not admissible. Ramp realization over time per §3 (benefits rarely start at 100% on go-live).
4. **Model costs**: one-time (delivery at P80 from the estimate memo, licences, change management, decommission), run (new platform, support, subscriptions), and the cost of delay for the status quo if evidenced. Cite sources; mark unknowns.
5. **Decision point — headline metric.** With the finance conventions in hand choose: simple payback and multi-year net (sponsor-level) or NPV/IRR (CFO-grade). State the discount rate as an assumption with owner. Never present NPV if the discount rate is not from the client's finance team; use undiscounted net and say so.
6. **Compute and lay out** on `assets/value-model-spec.md` (CSV layout) and `assets/value-case-template.md` (markdown). Any output depending on a `[TO BE BASELINED]` input is itself marked, not computed from a placeholder.
7. **Sensitivity**: identify the three assumptions with the largest effect on 3-year net; show ±20% (or the realistic range) and the break-even value of each. If the case flips sign within the realistic range, say so on line 1.
8. **Benefits-realization plan**: each benefit with a KPI, baseline, target, measurement method, owner (client), review cadence, and the realization start date tied to a delivery milestone. Benefits without a client owner are listed as unowned risks.
9. **Risks to the case**: adoption, dependency on other programs, data quality, timing of decommission, double counting (check overlap between levers).
10. Review mode: apply the rubric in `references/value-case-review-rubric.md`, redline per convention, deliver clean version.
11. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File |
|---|---|
| Value model (CSV layout) | `value-model-<client>-<initiative>.csv` per `assets/value-model-spec.md` |
| Value case document | `value-case-<client>-<initiative>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` per `assets/value-case-template.md` |

Sections: Bottom line (headline metric with confidence and what is unbaselined) · Benefits tree · Baselines and sources · Targets and mechanisms · Costs · Model (yearly table, payback, net) · Sensitivity · Benefits-realization plan · Risks · Assumptions register · Decision asked

## Self-check
- [ ] Every benefit traces to a client-stated outcome and has a mechanism
- [ ] Every baseline has source and confidence or is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Headline number excludes unbaselined benefits; the exclusion is stated
- [ ] Strategic benefits listed, not summed
- [ ] Costs include run and decommission timing; delivery cost cites the estimate memo
- [ ] Sensitivity on top three assumptions with break-even values
- [ ] Every benefit has a client owner or is flagged unowned
- [ ] No double counting across levers; no benchmarks from memory

## References
- `references/value-method.md` — benefits tree, classification, baselining, targets and ramps, finance conventions, double-counting checks
- `references/value-case-review-rubric.md` — review criteria for an existing business case
- `assets/value-model-spec.md` — CSV layout specification
- `assets/value-case-template.md` — markdown document template

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/value-case-builder --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/value-case-builder`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.
